contradicted.title: FixedColorLight.Color() decodes the COLOR descriptor index as a FixedColor ordinal
contradicted.ourValue: FixedColor ordinal BLACK=0, RED=1, GREEN=2, YELLOW=3, BLUE=4, PURPLE=5, TURQUOISE=6, WHITE=7 (color.go:451-458), applied to the raw descriptor index by Color() at color.go:581
contradicted.firmwareValue: COLOR index order BLACK=0, BLUE=1, GREEN=2, TURQUOISE=3, RED=4, PURPLE=5, YELLOW=6, WHITE=7
contradicted.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColor (enum constants BLACK(0), BLUE(1), GREEN(2), TURQUOISE(3), RED(4), PURPLE(5), YELLOW(6), WHITE(7)); the COLOR StateParameter is built from it via HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createColorSelectionParameter, whose VALUE_LIST is SimpleRGBColor#getNames(false); the same first-eight order via HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColorOpticalSignal#getNames. Independently, Tier 1 WebUI: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/opticalsignalreceiver.fn:64-65 and :72-78 (`! string listColor = "black\tblue\tgreen\tturquoise\tred\tpurple\tyellow\twhite"`, then `<option value=#loop#>` for loop=0..7 with `setDpState(oColor.ID(), this.value)` and read-back `jQuery(...).val(#oColor.Value()#)`), ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/dimmer.fn:179, and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/getColorElement.tcl:10-17 (options(0)=BLACK … options(7)=WHITE).
contradicted.finding:
The firmware's COLOR ordinal is the RGB bit pattern (bit0=blue, bit1=green, bit2=red), not the order FixedColor enumerates. Four of eight slots differ: index 1 is BLUE (we say RED), index 3 is TURQUOISE (we say YELLOW), index 4 is RED (we say BLUE), index 6 is YELLOW (we say TURQUOISE). BLACK/GREEN/PURPLE/WHITE coincide by accident.

The ordinal is what actually arrives on the wire. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue replaces an ENUM's logical label with its index in VALUE_LIST when the flag replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal is set, and the CCU's shipped HmIP config sets it: ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true`. So every COLOR event and getValue on HmIP-BSL / HmIP-MP3P ch2-5 / HmIPW-WGC delivers the RGB-bit index, and generic.Select.Value() hands it to Color() verbatim.

Consequences on our side: ColorName(), the MQTT fixed_color field and ChannelHsColor's index leg all mislabel four of eight colours; ChannelHsColor's sibling read via custom.EnumLabelValue (label-driven) disagrees with Color(); and SoundPlayerLED writes `colorLabel := fixedColorNames[color]` (sound_led.go:337) into the put_paramset, so a mis-decoded slot is written back to the device. SetColor's optimistic `l.color.OnEvent(int32(c))` (color.go:606) also stores our ordinal, which is not the one the CCU will echo.

The write path is correct and its comment (color.go:610-613) is exactly right: a label write is accepted. Only the read path substitutes the convention.

Scope note: the `RfDimmer_Color_Fixed` profile also routes through newFixedColorConstructor for DeviceType `hbw-lc-rgbww-in6-dr` (profiles.go:210-241). That is not a firmware-shipped device — no XML under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/ declares it — so its COLOR ordering is not decidable from these sources. It does not change the verdict: the decode is shared, and it is contradicted on every device the firmware does describe.

Witness (Tier 3, explains provenance, not authority): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:63-75 declares FixedColor as a StrEnum whose members are the labels; the Python reference never carries a numeric ordinal at all, so our integer ordering is a Go-side invention with no upstream source.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had FixedColor matched the CCU, all three independent Tier-1 orderings would have read BLACK, RED, GREEN, YELLOW, BLUE, PURPLE, TURQUOISE, WHITE. Each of them instead reads BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE, so the check does separate the two hypotheses rather than returning the same answer either way.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld, and every quote re-verified against the source. The firmware's COLOR ordinal is the index into a VALUE_LIST ordered BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE. Four of eight slots differ from ours: index 1 is BLUE (we say RED), 3 is TURQUOISE (we say YELLOW), 4 is RED (we say BLUE), 6 is YELLOW (we say TURQUOISE). BLACK/GREEN/PURPLE/WHITE coincide. I additionally confirmed the two links the previous grounding left implicit: (a) COLOR really is a StringEnumToInteger ENUM, which is the precondition for the ordinal substitution in convertParameterValue, and (b) the outbound branch returns the list index rather than SimpleRGBColor's own value field — so the extended VALUE_LIST (RANDOM/OLD_VALUE/DO_NOT_CARE appended) does not shift the first eight either. Our own code already states the correct order in a comment at color.go:610-613 while Color() contradicts it.

One correction to the previous consequence list, which overstates by one item: ChannelHsColor (color.go:676-690) is entirely label-driven — it calls custom.EnumLabelValue(l.channelColor) and matches the returned CCU name against fixedColorNames, never touching an index. It is therefore correct, and it is the sibling that will visibly disagree with Color()/ColorName() on the four wrong slots. The genuinely affected surfaces are Color(), ColorName() (color.go:640-649) and everything downstream of them, plus SetColor's optimistic l.color.OnEvent(int32(c)) (color.go:606), which seeds the store with our ordinal rather than the one the CCU will echo. sound_led.go:337 (`colorLabel := fixedColorNames[color]`) is only a write-back hazard for a caller that round-trips a value it read from Color().

Scope note verified, not changed: RfDimmer_Color_Fixed also routes through newFixedColorConstructor (internal/model/custom/light/init.go:71) for DeviceType hbw-lc-rgbww-in6-dr (internal/model/custom/profiles.go:210-215). No XML under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/ or rftypes/ mentions rgbww, so that device's COLOR ordering is not decidable here — but the decode is shared and is contradicted on every device the firmware does describe.

contradicted.title: BATTERY_STATE > 10 is used as the test for "this reading is a percentage, not a voltage"
contradicted.ourValue: BATTERY_STATE is surfaced as a 0-100 battery percentage when its value is > 10 (availability.go:234, rationale comment at :28-31)
contradicted.firmwareValue: BATTERY_STATE is `<logical type="float" min="1.5" max="4.6" unit="V"/>` — a cell voltage in volts, docu brief "Batteriespannung" ("battery voltage"); physical integer, `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="10.0" offset="-1.5"/>`
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2350-2359 (parameter id="BATTERY_STATE", operations="read,event", logical float min=1.5 max=4.6 unit="V"; declared inside `<channel index="4" type="CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER">` at :2309); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml:2313-2319; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:5211-5220. Those three files are the complete set: `grep -aln BATTERY_STATE ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/*.xml` returns exactly them. The HmIP side never declares it — no occurrence of BATTERY_STATE anywhere in HMIPServer or HMServer.
contradicted.finding:
The descriptor answers this without a threshold and answers it the other way. BATTERY_STATE is a cell voltage in volts on every device that declares it — HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM and HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU, all three with the identical logical block min=1.5 max=4.6 unit="V". No device XML in the firmware declares BATTERY_STATE as a percentage, in millivolts, or with any unit but V. HmIP has no BATTERY_STATE at all (it carries OPERATING_VOLTAGE plus OPERATING_VOLTAGE_STATUS instead — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory, ParameterMapKey("OPERATING_VOLTAGE","highRes") and ("OPERATING_VOLTAGE_STATUS")).

So `f > 10` cannot be satisfied by any firmware-declared BATTERY_STATE: the declared maximum is 4.6. The branch at availability.go:234 is dead code, not a mis-scaling risk — the bundle's "3000 %" / "12 %" damage scenario has no device behind it. What it does cost is the opposite of what the comment claims: for the three thermostats that do report BATTERY_STATE, no battery level is surfaced at all.

A second, independent reason the branch never fires: BATTERY_STATE is declared on channel 4 (CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER) on HM-CC-RT-DN, while channel0Float (availability.go:179-180) looks only at `<address>:0`. So even a hypothetical percentage-valued BATTERY_STATE would not be found where the code looks.

The honest replacement is the declared UNIT: the descriptor carries unit="V" together with MIN/MAX, and Channel.ParameterFloatRange already exposes it. Note this is a Tier-2 grounding — the rfd firmware itself carries no BATTERY_STATE semantics; the device XMLs are what the daemon reads at runtime, so they are the right authority for this question, and they and the runtime descriptor cannot disagree here (they are the same document).
contradicted.negativeControl: Had BATTERY_STATE been a percentage on any family, at least one `<parameter id="BATTERY_STATE">` block would carry unit="%" with a 0..100 logical range — the pattern the same files use for VALVE_STATE (`<logical type="integer" min="0" max="99" default="0" unit="%"/>`, rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2365). All three BATTERY_STATE declarations instead carry unit="V" min="1.5" max="4.6", so the check distinguishes the two cases.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld and strengthened. Every one of the three device XMLs declares BATTERY_STATE identically as a cell voltage, min 1.5, max 4.6, unit V — no device XML in the firmware declares it as a percentage, in millivolts, or with any other unit. `f > 10` cannot be satisfied by any firmware-declared BATTERY_STATE, so the branch at availability.go:234 is dead code, not a mis-scaling risk; the bundle's "3000 %" damage scenario has no device behind it. The cost runs the other way: on the three thermostats that do report BATTERY_STATE, no battery level is surfaced at all.

Two additions to the previous grounding. First, the channel argument generalises: the previous agent named channel 4 for HM-CC-RT-DN only, and I confirmed the other two — HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM is also channel 4, and HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU is channel 2 (THERMALCONTROL_TRANSMIT). None of the three is on `:0`, and channel0Float looks only at `<address>:0`, so the branch is unreachable for a second, independent reason on every declaring device. Second, an independent Tier-2 corpus (pydevccu) is silent on BATTERY_STATE, which removes the possibility that some non-shipped descriptor carries a percentage form.

Tier is 2 and correctly labelled: the rfd firmware source carries no BATTERY_STATE semantics of its own; the device type XMLs are what the daemon reads at runtime, and here the shipped XML and the runtime descriptor are the same document, so they cannot disagree. The honest replacement remains the declared UNIT, which the descriptor carries together with MIN/MAX and which Channel.ParameterFloatRange already exposes.

contradicted.title: HM-CC-VG-1 SET_TEMPERATURE bounds 4.5 / 30.5 overwrite the CCU-declared MIN/MAX
contradicted.ourValue: MIN rewritten to 4.5, MAX rewritten to 30.5 on HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE (VALUES), unconditionally at paramset ingest; Reason string "CCU returns invalid MIN/MAX bounds for virtual heating groups (0/0 or string)"
contradicted.firmwareValue: min="5.0" max="30.0" default="20.0" unit="°C" type="FLOAT" operations="7" control="HEATING_CONTROL.SETPOINT" aggregation="LAST"
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml:504-505 — `<status_parameter aggregation="LAST" control="HEATING_CONTROL.SETPOINT" default="20.0" max="30.0" min="5.0" name="SET_TEMPERATURE" operations="7" tab_order="4" type="FLOAT" unit="°C">`, inside `<channel id="1" type="CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER">` (:433) of the file's single `<group>` (:3), whose `<virtual_device_type>` is HM-CC-VG-1 (:8113). The runtime paramset description is built from those attributes verbatim by HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.GroupDeviceHandler#createParamsetDescriptions -> #createHashMapFromParameterValues, which puts parameter.getMax() / parameter.getMin() into the RpcStruct; those accessors are declared String-typed on HMServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.bidcos.BidCosVirtualChannelParameter. Comparison value: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2392-2395 — HM-CC-RT-DN's own SET_TEMPERATURE is `<logical type="float" min="4.5" max="30.5" default="20.0" unit="°C">`.
contradicted.finding:
The firmware does declare bounds for this parameter, and they are not the ones we write. HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE is declared min=5.0, max=30.0, default=20.0, unit=°C. Our patch replaces that with 4.5 / 30.5 — which are exactly HM-CC-RT-DN's own logical bounds (rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2395), i.e. the member device's range substituted for the group's. The group is deliberately narrower than its members.

Direction of the error: the patch widens the range on both ends. A setpoint of 4.5 or 30.5 now passes our validation and the SPA slider now offers it, and both are outside the range the CCU declares for the group.

Half of the patch's Reason is corroborated and half is not:
- "or string" is confirmed. GroupDeviceHandler copies parameter.getMin()/getMax() straight into the description, and both accessors are String-typed on BidCosVirtualChannelParameter, so the CCU really does report MIN and MAX for this parameter as XML-RPC strings rather than doubles. A patch that coerces the string form to a number is well founded.
- "0/0" is not. Nothing in the group definition or in the description-building path produces 0/0 for SET_TEMPERATURE; the declared values are "5.0" and "30.0". If a real CCU was observed returning 0/0, that observation is unaccounted for by these sources and should be re-measured before the numbers are changed.

What the patch should carry, on this evidence: keep the string→number coercion, and use 5.0 / 30.0. Note also that DEFAULT (20.0) and UNIT (°C) are declared and currently untouched by the patch.

One scope caveat, stated as unverified: HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.rfd.legacy.VirtualDefinitionFactory#fillChannelParameter can build a channel parameter's min/max from a member device's ParameterDescription instead of from the shipped XML. I did not establish which of the two paths serves a runtime HM-CC-VG-1, so I cannot exclude a configuration in which the group inherits HM-CC-RT-DN's 4.5/30.5. The shipped group definition is unambiguous and is the authority I can cite; if the inheriting path is live, the answer would be 4.5/30.5 and our patch would be right for the wrong stated reason. Settling that needs a getParamsetDescription capture from a real CCU with a heating group.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the firmware genuinely left this parameter's bounds unset or at 0/0, the `<status_parameter>` element would carry no min/max attributes or min="0" max="0", and GroupDeviceHandler would have put null or "0" into the description. It carries min="5.0" max="30.0" — and the neighbouring ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE in the same channel carries min="-10.0" max="50.0", showing the attributes are populated per parameter rather than boilerplate.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld, and the one caveat the previous grounding left open is now closed in its favour. HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE is declared min=5.0, max=30.0, default=20.0, unit=°C. Our patch replaces that with 4.5 / 30.5 — the member device's range substituted for the group's — widening the accepted range by 0.5 K at each end, so a setpoint of 4.5 or 30.5 now passes our validation and the SPA slider offers it.

Resolving the open caveat: VirtualDefinitionFactory#fillChannelParameter, the path that could have made the group inherit a member's ParameterDescription bounds, is called only from HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.rfd.legacy.RFD2VirtualDeviceConverter — which is a developer-side generator, not a runtime path: it carries a `public static void main` and hard-coded source paths of the form D:/SVN/HomeMatic/devicetypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml. The live path is the shipped file, named in Constants and HMServerConfiguration as above. So the inheriting configuration the previous agent could not exclude is not live, and 5.0 / 30.0 is what a real CCU serves.

A second, independent reason the answer cannot be 4.5/30.5: BidCosVirtualChannelParameter's own field initialisers are min "5.0", max "30.0", default "20.0". Whether the group-definition parser fills those attributes or leaves them at the class defaults, SET_TEMPERATURE comes out 5.0 / 30.0 either way.

Provenance, stated as unverified as to intent: the shipped group values do not match what the generator would produce from today's device XML — HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU channel 2 SET_TEMPERATURE is 4.5/30.5, and MANU_MODE (4.5/30.5) and ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE (-10.0/50.0) in the same group channel did carry through from the device, while the four ACTION parameters (AUTO_MODE, BOOST_MODE, COMFORT_MODE, LOWERING_MODE) all carry a nonsensical min 5.0 / max 30.0, i.e. the class defaults. So 5.0/30.0 for SET_TEMPERATURE may be a class-default leftover rather than a deliberate narrowing. That does not change what the CCU serves, and it is what our patch must not contradict.

The Reason string splits as the previous agent found. "or string" is confirmed — getMin/getMax are String-typed and copied verbatim into the description, so MIN and MAX really do arrive as XML-RPC strings; the coercion half of the patch is well founded, and DEFAULT ("20.0") and UNIT ("°C") arrive the same way and are currently untouched. "0/0" is not corroborated anywhere in the group definition or the description-building path and should be re-measured before the numbers are trusted.

contradicted.title: The per-model MASTER channel whitelist encodes 30 devices' channel layouts with no firmware citation
contradicted.citation: Tier 2 (deciding): ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-DRDI3.json — MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is declared on VCU6948166:1,:2,:3,:4,:8,:12. At :4/:8/:12 the declared fields are TYPE=ENUM, VALUE_LIST=['OFF','ON'], DEFAULT='ON', MIN='OFF', MAX='ON', OPERATIONS=3, FLAGS=1; at :1/:2/:3 they are VALUE_LIST=['INACTIVE','KEY_BEHAVIOR','SWITCH_BEHAVIOR','BINARY_BEHAVIOR'], DEFAULT='KEY_BEHAVIOR'. ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-DRDI3.json gives channel TYPE=MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER for 1/2/3 and DIMMER_TRANSMITTER for 4/8/12. Tier 1 (shape, not the numbers): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory registers CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE once per channel-specification subtype key (distinct value lists per key: an {OFF,ON} variant, an {OFF,ON,ON_LED} variant, {INACTIVE,KEY_BEHAVIOR,SWITCH_BEHAVIOR,BINARY_BEHAVIOR}, {SHUTTER,BLIND}, {NORMAL_MODE,SILENT_MODE}, the HEAT_DEMAND_* set, the SENSOR_ES_* set, …) — never per model plus channel number. Tier 1 for the descriptor's own reach: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config carries no CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE entry at all (it maps only Control/Unit/TabOrder metadata), so that file cannot settle this question.
contradicted.finding:
Contradicted at HmIP-DRDI3. Our value: Channels {1,2,3} (rules.go:79-82). Firmware/descriptor value: {1,2,3,4,8,12}. Channels 4, 8 and 12 are the DIMMER_TRANSMITTER channels and their CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is the {OFF,ON} channel-enable flavour, a different knob from the {INACTIVE,KEY_BEHAVIOR,…} input mode on 1/2/3 — but it is declared, writable (OPERATIONS=3) and today never becomes a data point, because decider.go step 3 default-skips every MASTER parameter without a whitelist hit.

Everything else in the table that the corpus can reach is confirmed exactly: HmIP-DRBLI4 {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,13,17,21}; HmIP-MIO16-PCB {13,14,15,16}; HmIP-DRSI1 {1}; HmIP-DRSI4 {1,2,3,4}; HmIP-DSD-PCB {1}; HmIP-FCI1 {1}; HmIP-FSI16 {1}; HmIP-MOD-RC8 channelRange(1,9)={1..8}; HmIPW-DRBL4 {1,5,9,13}; HmIPW-DRI32 channelRange(1,33)={1..32}; HmIPW-FIO6 channelRange(1,7)={1..6}; ELV-SH-TACO {2}; HmIP-RGBW ch0 DEVICE_OPERATION_MODE. Climate side confirmed too: HmIP-BWTH {1,8} (ch1 = MIN_MAX_VALUE_NOT_RELEVANT_FOR_MANU_MODE/OPTIMUM_START_STOP/TEMPERATURE_{MAXIMUM,MINIMUM,OFFSET}, ch8 = HEATING_VALVE_TYPE); key "HmIP-WGT" prefix-matches the real model HmIP-WGTC, whose climate MASTER sits at 8 and 14 — {8,14} correct; HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU / HM-CC-VG-1 carry theirs on the device-level MASTER, which the empty-Channels wildcard covers.

The structural half: because the firmware attaches CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE to a channel specification, not to a (model, channel) pair, a per-model channel table cannot be complete by construction. Thirteen further models in the 399-device descriptor corpus declare MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE and get no entry and no prefix hit — HmIP-DLP {2,3,12}, HmIP-ESI {1}, HmIP-SAM {1}, HmIP-SMO230-A {4}, HmIP-SPDR {2,3,4}, HmIP-STV {1}, HmIP-SWO-B/-PL/-PR {2}, HmIP-UDI-SMI55 {3,6}, HmIPW-DRD3 {1,5,9} — plus HmIP-eTRV-2/-C-2/-F, which do match the "HmIP-eTRV" key but whose Parameters set is climateMasterParameters, so their CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE ({NORMAL_MODE,SILENT_MODE} per the factory) is withheld; same for HmIP-HEATING:1, which declares both the climate set and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE. Not verifiable from these sources: HmIP-FCI6 channelRange(1,7), HmIP-FSI6 {1} and HmIPW-DRI16 channelRange(1,17) — those three models are absent from the descriptor corpus and from the shipped BidCos XMLs.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the table been right, the per-model channel sets extracted from paramset_descriptions/*.json would have matched every entry the corpus can reach, and no model outside the table would have declared MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE. The extraction did produce a different answer in both directions — one exact mismatch (DRDI3, three extra channels) and thirteen uncovered models — while returning byte-for-byte agreement on the other twelve entries, so the check discriminates rather than agreeing by construction.
contradicted.ourValue: HmIP-DRDI3 → Channels {1, 2, 3}
contradicted.firmwareValue: HmIP-DRDI3 → MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE on channels {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12}
contradicted.challengeNote: UPHELD as contradicted, and strengthened from Tier 2 to Tier 1 on the operator surface — but the prior agent's completeness claim is wrong and I widened the boundary. Corpus re-measured over all 399 paramset_descriptions: 29 models declare MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE (the prior report listed 28 — it omitted 'HmIP-eTRV-2 I9F'). Every channel-operation-mode entry it called confirmed does check out exactly: DRBLI4 {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,13,17,21}, MIO16-PCB {13,14,15,16}, DRSI1 {1}, DRSI4 {1,2,3,4}, DSD-PCB {1}, FCI1 {1}, FSI16 {1}, MOD-RC8 {1..8}, HmIPW-DRBL4 {1,5,9,13}, HmIPW-DRI32 {1..32}, HmIPW-FIO6 {1..6}, ELV-SH-TACO {2}. The claim 'Climate side confirmed too' is NOT sound: I re-ran the same measurement over the climate MASTER set and found six further models that declare a whitelisted climate parameter and get no entry and no prefix hit — HmIP-FAL230-C10 ch0 and HmIPW-FAL230-C6 ch0 (HEATING_VALVE_TYPE), HmIPW-SCTHD ch1 and HmIPW-WTH ch1 (the key 'HmIP-WTH' does not prefix 'HmIPW-WTH' — the 'W' falls where the '-' is), HmIP-SCTH230 ch4 and ELV-SH-CTH ch1 (TEMPERATURE_OFFSET) — plus ELV-SH-TACO ch1 TEMPERATURE_OFFSET, which the model's own entry (ch2, CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE only) actively withholds. HmIP-STE2-PCB ch1/ch2 is also uncovered but is named as deliberate in decider.go's own comment. Where I demote the framing rather than the verdict: the descriptor settles which channels DECLARE the parameter and the WebUI settles which the CCU EXPOSES, but neither carries our data-point policy, so 'contradicted' is exact as a channel-layout claim and is not a firmware statement about what should be whitelisted. Damage is also smaller than the bundle's damage clause says: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is in hiddenParameters, so even a whitelisted hit is marked NoCreate for UI/MQTT — the missing entries deny applyChannelOperationModeGating an input, they do not withhold a rendered knob.

contradicted.title: The 10 s CONFIG_PENDING settle delay is a comment-claim about CCU internals with a duty-cycle consequence
contradicted.site: internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:20-28 (configPendingSettleDelay) and the doc block at :45-63 that repeats the rationale
contradicted.citation: Tier 1, the HmIP path our hook is actually gated to: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getParameterSet maps getParamset(address, "MASTER") to BackendCommandType.DEVICE_CONFIG_GET; de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.BackendCommandHandler routes that to de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleGetConfigCommand, whose whole body issues PersistenceCommandType.PERSISTENCE_COMMAND_LOAD_DEVICE_CONFIGURATION on the persistence bus; de.eq3.cbcs.persistence.kryo.KryoPersistenceWorker#loadSpecificDevice answers it by deserialising the device's persisted config file (with the .new/.old rename dance). The over-the-air read is a different command entirely — DEVICE_CONFIG_ASK → DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleAskConfigCommand → TransactionSubsystemCommandType.DYNAMIC_TRANSACTION_COMMAND_START_CONFIG — and getParamset never reaches it. Ordering: de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.task.TransactionTaskFactory#createDeviceConfigurationTransaction appends the tasks in the order SendFrame(setParameterByIndex…) → SendFrame(commitParameterSetting) → PersistenceTask(PERSISTENCE_COMMAND_SAVE_DEVICE_CONFIGURATION) → CyclicTimeoutUpdateTask → NotifyDeviceConfigurationPendingChangedTask; de.eq3.cbcs.persistence.kryo.KryoPersistenceWorker#saveDevice is a synchronous write-then-rename. contradicted.finding:
The firmware does not round float echoes to two decimals, and it does not use a fixed precision at all.

What it does: on a write, the logical float is quantised to `round((v + offset) * factor)` — half away from zero, the `dval += 0.5` branch — and on every read or event the echo is exactly `physical_int / factor - offset`. The quantum is therefore 1/factor, a per-parameter constant declared in the device-type XML. Over XML-RPC the double is serialised with `%f`, six decimals; over BIN-RPC as mantissa/2^30 with an exponent. Neither is two decimals.

A survey of every FLOAT parameter carrying a float_integer_scale across ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/*.xml gives these factors and counts: 2 (873), 200 (533), 10 (281), 1 (40), 100 (38), 10.0 (19), 1000 (6), 62.5 (6), 3.38983050847 (2), 1.0 (1), 31.25 (1), 50 (1). 625 further FLOAT parameters carry no float_integer_scale at all. So the quantum ranges from 1.0 down to 0.001, straddling roundTo2's 0.01 bucket in both directions, and both failure modes are reachable on real read/write/event parameters:

- False reject, factor=2 (SET_TEMPERATURE, the single most common factor). Write 20.3 → physical round(40.6)=41 → echo 20.5. roundTo2 gives 20.3 vs 20.5, no match, WaitForStateChangeOrTimeout blocks the full 60 s and write_options.go:189 turns that into an error from SetValueWithOptions even though the wire write succeeded and the device is at the nearest representable setpoint. Any FLOAT write not already on the device's grid behaves this way whenever factor <= 100.
- False confirm, factor=200 (LEVEL/LEVEL_SLATS, blinds). Physical 23 → 0.115 and physical 24 → 0.12 are two distinct blind positions half a percent apart; roundTo2 maps both to 0.12 (0.115*100 is exactly 11.5 in binary64, and Go's math.Round is half-away-from-zero). An echo of 0.115 confirms an expected write of 0.12.

The cross-check the reader asked for comes out negative: the paramset description cannot supply the right tolerance. HSSLogicalTypeFloat::GetDescription returns TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL only — no step, no precision, no factor. The factor lives solely in the device-type XML that rfd loads at startup and never exposes over XML-RPC. So replacing 2 decimals with a descriptor-derived quantum is not performable from the runtime descriptor; the honest options are to compare the echo against the value the CCU would quantise to (requires the factor, which we do not have), or to accept any echo for the key and stop calling it a value match.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the CCU echoed the written value verbatim, PhysicalToLogical would not exist on this path and getParamset/event would return the stored double unchanged; instead the value makes a documented round trip through an int. Had two decimals been the CCU's own precision, `_doubleFormat` would be "%.2f" rather than "%f", and the float logical type's GetDescription would carry a step or precision field to justify it — it carries neither. And had the collision cases been artefacts of my arithmetic rather than of the rule, roundTo2(0.12) and roundTo2(0.115) would have differed; computed on the same binary64 grid Go uses, they are equal (0.12), while roundTo2(20.3) and roundTo2(20.5) differ — the check discriminates in both directions.
contradicted.missingInput: The per-parameter conversion factor (`<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="…"/>`). It is not carried by getParamsetDescription — HSSLogicalTypeFloat::GetDescription emits TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL only — so a correct per-parameter tolerance cannot be computed from anything the daemon reads at runtime.
contradicted.ourValue: Confirmed iff math.Round(expected*100)/100 == math.Round(actual*100)/100 — a fixed 2-decimal bucket for every FLOAT.
contradicted.firmwareValue: echo = round((written + offset) * factor) / factor - offset, quantum 1/factor per parameter (observed factors 1, 1.0, 2, 3.38983050847, 10, 10.0, 31.25, 50, 62.5, 100, 200, 1000); serialised over XML-RPC with `%f` = 6 decimals.

The contradiction stands, and I rebuilt it rather than accepting it. I re-ran the factor survey over ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/*.xml independently and reproduced the previous agent's histogram exactly, count for count: 2426 float parameters, 1801 with a float_integer_scale spread over 12 distinct factors, 625 with none. The quantum therefore ranges from 1.0 down to 0.001 and straddles roundTo2's 0.01 bucket in both directions. Every cited line transcribes verbatim, including the truncating `(int)dval` after the half-away-from-zero bias.

I checked the one route that would have rescued the rule and the previous agent did not. HSSParameter::SetValue can echo a write back through `inst->ReportEvent(id, log_temp, …)` — and `log_temp` is the logical value *before* LogicalToPhysical, i.e. the un-quantised 20.3, not 20.5. Had SET_TEMPERATURE carried loopback="true", their false-reject example would have collapsed. It does not: the attribute is absent, the parser default is false, no float parameter in any of the 127 rftypes declares loopback="true", and SET_TEMPERATURE's echo is declared to come from `<event frame="INFO_LEVEL"/>` and `<event frame="ACK_STATUS"/>` — both from_device frames carrying the 6-bit physical integer. So the compared value really is the quantised one: write 20.3 → physical round(40.6)=41 → echo 20.5 → roundTo2 mismatch.

I also checked their false-confirm arithmetic, which rests on an exactness claim: 23/200 = 0.115 and 0.115*100 == 11.5 exactly in binary64, so Go's half-away-from-zero math.Round lifts it to 12 and roundTo2(0.115) == roundTo2(0.12) == 0.12. Verified numerically; two blind positions half a percent apart collapse into one bucket. Their 'not performable from the runtime descriptor' conclusion is also right — GetDescription for FLOAT emits TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL over a base that adds only UNIT; the factor never leaves the device-type XML that rfd loads at startup.

One correction to the stated consequence, which the previous agent asserted as if it were live. valuesMatch is reachable only through WaitForStateChangeOrTimeout, and both call sites are gated on `opts.WaitForCallback`. Grepping the tree, `WaitForCallback: true` appears in internal/client/write_options_test.go and write_options_waitforcallback_doc_test.go and nowhere else — no production caller enables it (internal/config/timeouts.go carries only the timeout, not the flag). So the false reject and the false confirm are latent in an opt-in path, not defects a running daemon is hitting today. The rule is still contradicted; the severity is 'wrong tolerance waiting to be switched on', not 'writes are failing now'.

contradicted.title: Timer.Max publishes 16343 as a maximum in seconds, though 16343 is DURATION_VALUE's per-unit INTEGER maximum
contradicted.ourValue: Max() returns 16343 with the doc-comment "the upper-bound seconds threshold" — i.e. 4 h 32 min 23 s presented as the data point's maximum in seconds
contradicted.firmwareValue: DURATION_VALUE is INTEGER, default 0, min 0, max 16343 *counts*, paired with DURATION_UNIT ∈ {S, M, H} (older channels) or {S, M, H, 10MS} (default S). The count's seconds meaning is value × {1, 60, 3600, 0.01}. The legacy surface's own seconds-domain limits are different numbers again: DURATION_UNIT=H with DURATION_VALUE ≥ 31 is rewritten to 16383 (0x3FFF, the 'infinite' marker) on the way in, and on the read-back path any unit×value ≥ 111600 s is reported as ON_TIME = 8580000 s.
contradicted.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDurationValueParameter (LogicalType.INTEGER, default 0, min 0, max 16343 — the single factory used for DURATION_VALUE on the withColor, uniLight, siren and withRoom groups and for RAMP_TIME_VALUE / RAMP_TIME_TO_OFF_VALUE / MANUAL_SELF_CALIBRATION_DURATION_VALUE) and #createDurationUnitParameter (LogicalType.ENUM over {"S","M","H"} or {"S","M","H","10MS"}, default "S"); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createDurationValueParameter (same literal 16343); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#correctInfiniteDuration and #migrateDurations.
contradicted.finding: I read our site: Max() hands out float64(timerUpperBoundSeconds) unconditionally, and the constant's own comment two files over (timer.go:25-27) correctly calls it "the threshold above which seconds are re-expressed as minutes" — so the package already contradicts itself, and the firmware sides with timer.go and projection.go against data_point.go. 16343 is the wire integer's maximum per unit, not a duration. Three consequences worth separating. (1) The uniformity claim in internal/model/custom/mixins.go:115-120 is confirmed: 16343 is a single literal in one factory method that every DURATION_VALUE-bearing channel goes through, so no channel declares a different max. (2) projection.go's "~678 days at the hours unit" is arithmetically right about the integer but is not a reachable duration: the CCU coerces DURATION_UNIT=H with value ≥ 31 to the infinite marker before dispatch, so at the hours unit the largest *finite* duration is 30 h. (3) There is therefore no single seconds number to publish — the honest Max() is unit-dependent, and if one number is wanted, the reachable finite ceiling below the infinity coercion is 111600 s (31 h), not 16343 s and not 678 days. Also worth recording: the CCU's own encoder promotes seconds→minutes at 16000 s and minutes→hours at 960000 s (DeviceUtil#migrateDurations), whereas our RecalcUnit promotes at 16343 and 16343 min. Both stay inside the declared integer max, so both are legal writes; the divergence is not a defect but it is a divergence. reachesDevice is false for Max() itself (a read-side metadata accessor that only over-restricts a slider or validator), though the same constant does drive RecalcUnit on the write path.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had 16343 been a seconds cap, the firmware would have had to enforce it in the seconds domain — a check on unit×value against 16343, or a DURATION_VALUE max that varied with the unit. It does neither: the max is a constant argument in one factory that never sees the unit, and the only seconds-domain thresholds in the legacy surface are 111600 and 8580000. The check reacts: the same reading located real seconds-domain limits (111600 / 8580000) and the real unit enum, so it would have surfaced a seconds cap had one existed.
contradicted.challengeNote: UPHELD on the headline and re-verified two ways: 16343 is DURATION_VALUE's per-unit INTEGER maximum (Tier 1 factory literal, Tier 2 descriptor MAX with TYPE INTEGER and a paired unit ENUM), so Max()'s doc-comment 'upper-bound seconds threshold' is wrong and the package already contradicts itself — timer.go:25-27 correctly calls the same constant a unit-promotion threshold. The uniformity claim is confirmed: 16343 is one literal in one factory method per server and nothing else in the corpus carries it. BUT three of the bundle's supporting statements are WRONG SURFACE and must not be used as the fix. (1) 'on the read-back path any unit x value >= 111600 s is reported as ON_TIME = 8580000 s'. That code is in DeviceUtil#migrateDurations, whose only caller is DeviceUtil#convertCombinedParameter — the COMBINED_PARAMETER decoder on the way IN. It is not a read-back path at all, and the branch fires only when the target channel declares an ON_TIME state parameter. Our Timer writes DURATION_VALUE/DURATION_UNIT directly, so this clamp never touches it. (2) Consequently 'the reachable finite ceiling below the infinity coercion is 111600 s (31 h)' is wrong twice over: the number comes from a surface we do not use, and it is self-inconsistent — correctInfiniteDuration coerces at value >= 31.0, so 31 h is precisely the first coerced value, making 30 h the largest finite hours-unit duration. On the path we actually write, the coercion applies only at unit H, so the largest finite duration reachable through a direct DURATION_* write is 16343 minutes (about 11.35 days), not 111600 s. Whether the device accepts it is valve/actuator firmware and is not readable here. (3) 'the CCU's own encoder promotes seconds->minutes at 16000 s and minutes->hours at 960000 s, whereas our RecalcUnit promotes at 16343 — a divergence'. Same wrong surface: those thresholds live in the else-branch of migrateDurations, which runs only when a caller sends ON_TIME inside a COMBINED_PARAMETER to a channel that declares no ON_TIME. Our RecalcUnit emits DURATION_VALUE/DURATION_UNIT directly and never passes through that encoder, so there is no divergence to record. What survives on our path: correctInfiniteDuration is genuinely on it (it runs at the head of validateAndConvertValues for every VALUES write), so unit=H with value >= 31 becomes 16383/infinite whether we intended it or not. FURTHER DEMOTION the bundle did not make: the title says Timer.Max 'publishes' 16343. I could find no production call site of Max() on a Timer anywhere in the repo — the method exists to satisfy a data-point interface and nothing in internal/north or internal/payload invokes it; the HA number bound comes from projection.go's independent timerMaxSeconds = 86400. So today this is a wrong constant and a wrong doc-comment in an unconsumed accessor, not a published value. Severity accordingly low.

contradicted.finding:
The doc claim at :42-44 ("substring-matching replacements") describes a normalisation strategy the CCU does not use, and the corpus it is applied to contains the exact counterexamples the candidate predicted.

Compound units exist and we mangle them. `unit="m3/Imp."` is declared on METER_CONSTANT_GAS in two BidCos device XMLs, and the HmIP legacy parameter definition declares GAS_FLOW as `m3/h`. Both contain "m3", so CleanupUnit returns "m³" for both — a meter constant in cubic metres per impulse and a flow in cubic metres per hour both come out naming a plain volume. The firmware does the opposite: getUnit never matches on a substring; it reaches the per-impulse spelling by keying on the *parameter* (METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME → "m³/Imp"), which is a reading our unit-keyed table structurally cannot produce.

The "degree" entry is a second, independent contradiction, and it is worse than a lost suffix: we map it to "°C" (Celsius) while the firmware maps it to "°" (programs.fn:611-614 sets °, and getUnit maps HmIP's "_Grad_" to ° likewise). The only two parameters that declare unit="degree" are WIND_DIRECTION and WIND_DIRECTION_RANGE — angles. We are saved from shipping that today only because fixUnitByParam:38-39 overrides both to "°" before the replace table is consulted, so the entry is unreachable for the parameters that trigger it. That is a latent trap, not a correct rule: any future parameter declaring a unit containing "degree" would be labelled a temperature.

The damage extends past presentation, because CleanupUnit's output is also a *lookup key*: quantity.go:54 and :86 feed it into parameter.MetadataByUnit to derive Quantity and ValueBehavior. A meter constant collapsed to "m³" is therefore not only mislabelled but classified as a volume measurement.

On the map-iteration nondeterminism the candidate also raises: I could not reproduce it from the firmware's unit corpus. Across all 148 rftypes/hs485types XMLs and the HmIP legacy config, no declared unit string contains two of our six table keys (the only near-miss, `Unit=""` in the legacy config, matches the `"` key alone). So the ordering hazard is real in the code but currently unreachable from firmware-declared data — I am reporting that as measured, not as safe by design.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the firmware normalised units by substring, getUnit would be built from `string match`/`regsub` rather than a chain of `==` tests, and it would not need the two per-parameter escapes (METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME, METER_CONSTANT_ENERGY) that exist precisely because whole-string matching cannot reach a compound spelling. Had no compound unit containing a table key existed, the grep over every declared unit= attribute and every .Unit= line would have returned only atomic spellings; it returned m3/Imp., m3/h, L/min, 1/cm, m3/h and x 200Hz among others.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Contradiction upheld, but on a cleaner counterexample than the candidate's, and with its damage claim cut back.

What I checked. getUnit really is equality-only — I read all 43 lines; every test is `==` or `string equal`, on the unit or on the parameter name. The compound units really exist, in both stacks. And I reproduced the candidate's non-collision claim properly rather than trusting it: I enumerated the complete distinct unit corpus on both sides — 40 distinct `unit="..."` strings across all rftypes + hs485types XMLs, and 30 distinct `.Unit=` values in the HmIP legacy config — and confirmed no declared unit contains two of our six table keys. The map-iteration hazard in CleanupUnit is therefore real in code but unreachable from firmware-declared data. Measured, not safe by design.

Where I improve on the candidate. Its headline example relates two differently-named parameters: getUnit keys on METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME, but the parameter that actually declares `unit="m3/Imp."` is METER_CONSTANT_GAS. METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME and METER_CONSTANT_ENERGY appear in no rftypes/hs485types XML and in no legacy-config line — they are HmIP names. The stronger reading needs no such bridge: METER_CONSTANT_GAS matches none of getUnit's branches, so the firmware renders `m3/Imp.` verbatim, while we return `m³`. Same for GAS_FLOW (`m3/h`), which no firmware surface normalises at all — programs.fn only handles "100%" and "degree".

Where the candidate overstates. "A meter constant collapsed to m³ is not only mislabelled but classified as a volume measurement" is false. sensorMetadataByUnit (internal/parameter/metadata.go:266-271) has exactly four keys — "%", "bar", "°C", "g/m³". "m³" is not among them, so the collapsed unit yields QuantityNone / ValueBehaviorNone, identical to what the raw string would yield. And GAS_FLOW never reaches the unit fallback at all: it is classified one stage earlier by parameter (metadata.go:77, QuantityVolumeFlowRate). The damage is a wrong displayed unit, not a wrong classification.

Reachability, which I checked because a presentation-only defect still has to reach a surface: CleanupUnit is called from MQTT discovery (internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:753 and :820) for VALUES parameters — that is where m3/h lands — and from internal/central/adapter/uischema_adapter.go:456 for the config-UI schema, which is where METER_CONSTANT_GAS, a MASTER parameter, lands. Both are live.

The "degree" -> "°C" entry is a second, independent contradiction and I confirm the candidate's reading including the shadowing: the only four parameters declaring unit="degree" are WIND_DIRECTION and WIND_DIRECTION_RANGE, and fixUnitByParam:38-39 overrides both to "°" before the replace table is consulted, so the wrong entry is unreachable today. Latent, not shipped. One gap the candidate named in its summary column but did not pursue: HmIP declares `_Grad_` (and `Grad`) as units and getUnit maps `_Grad_` to °; we have no entry, so `_Grad_` reaches the operator literally. `${lblReadings}` is another declared HmIP unit we pass through raw.

contradicted.finding:
Five sub-claims, three outcomes.

CONTRADICTED — astro offset. Every one of the 47 models in the descriptor corpus declares 01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET as INTEGER MIN -128 MAX 127. We accept and emit -720..+720. The CCU's own editor does not carry a constant at all: HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1128-1134 reads ASTRO_OFFSET_MIN/MAX out of the paramset description (hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:39-46 fills them from `$psDescr(01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET)` MIN/MAX) and clamps the input field to them. So the firmware answer is "whatever the channel declares", and what every channel declares is ±128, not ±720. rawconvert.go:832-835 lets anything in ±720 through to the wire, so a value between 128 and 720 is written and the device either rejects the putParamset or stores a clipped switching time. The unit is confirmed as minutes (`'ASTRO_OFFSET_UNIT' : 'min'`).

CONTRADICTED — the 24-slot comment at rest_contract.go:361. It contradicts SlotNo 1..75 three lines below and both the firmware and the descriptors: `_getMaxEntries` returns 69 or 75, and every model in the corpus declares NN_WP_* keys up to exactly 69 or 75. The 75/69 constant at simple.go:329 and its existing citation to `_getMaxEntries` are verbatim correct, including the 69-model list (HmIP-MP3P, HmIPW-WRC6(-A), WRC6-230, water switches, HmIP-BSL fw 2.x); the descriptors add HmIP-HDM1/HDM2 to the 69 group. `default: return -1` means the switch does not bound a lock / access-transmitter channel — for those the descriptor is the only bound, which is what the SlotNo comment already says.

NARROWED — target channels. The firmware field is not an "X_Y" grammar at all: it is an integer bitmask, MAX 16777215 = 2^24-1, addressed by the device's own virtual-receiver channel number minus one (the derivation at internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:940-985 already cites HmIPWeeklyProgram.js correctly and takes the bit from the device, so the write path is sound). What is narrowed is the DTO's grammar: HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-LSC and HmIP-RGBW declare TARGET_CHANNELS as STRING with MAX '281474976710655' = 2^48-1, i.e. 48 addressable bit positions. `channelPattern` `^[1-8]_[123]$` can express at most 24 keys and rejects anything past `8_3`, and internal/central/adapter/week_profile_filter.go:237-247 mints keys as `<group index+1>_<member index+1>` with no upper bound, so a device with more than 8 schedule-relevant groups produces a key its own validator rejects. Separately, those three models declare the field STRING while rawconvert.go:840 writes a Go int — I did not establish what the legacy API does with an int for a STRING-typed config parameter, so that part is unverified.

CONFIRMED with a naming correction — the lock DURATION pair. DURATION_BASE index 7 is BASE_1_H and DURATION_FACTOR's max and default are both 31, so (7, 31) is the CCU's own "maximum duration" encoding. That the wire value of an ENUM is the VALUE_LIST index is read from HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:96-110, not assumed. The name "HOUR_1" in the comment is not a CCU name — it appears nowhere in the descriptors or the CCU editor; it is the Python reference's enum (../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:2550 `HOUR_1 = 7`, a witness). The CCU calls it BASE_1_H.

CONFIRMED — the colour field. NN_WP_HUE_SATURATION_COLOR_TEMPERATURE_EFFECT_VALUE declares MAX 1048575 = 2^20-1 on all three universal-light models, so "packed 20-bit" is exact; the TYPE discriminator declares MAX 2, so the acceptance set {0,1,2} is exact for these devices. One caveat: the CCU's own editor offers five options for that select — 0 hue/saturation, 1 colour temperature, 2 effect, 3 Switch, 4 Dimmer (HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1676-1682) — so 3 and 4 exist in the editor but exceed every shipped device's declared MAX. Because we carry the field as an opaque int, the round-trip is lossless either way; the comment's enumeration is simply not the editor's full list.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had ±720 been the real astro bound, at least one of the 47 models in the descriptor corpus would declare MIN/MAX beyond ±128 — none does, all 47 declare exactly -128/127 — and the CCU editor would have carried a literal rather than reading psDescr. Had 24 been the slot bound, no channel would declare an NN_WP_* key above 24 and `_getMaxEntries` would return 24; every model declares up to 69 or 75 and the function returns 69 or 75. Had (7,31) been wrong, DURATION_BASE's VALUE_LIST would put a different symbol at index 7 or DURATION_FACTOR's MAX would not be 31. Had the colour field not been 20 bits, its declared MAX would not be exactly 2^20-1.
contradicted.challengeNote:
EVERY SUB-CLAIM REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY. I re-derived the descriptor corpus myself rather than trusting the candidate's counts: 01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET is INTEGER -128..127 DEFAULT 0 on all 44 files that carry it (candidate said 47 — an overcount, substance unaffected); max NN_WP_WEEKDAY index is 69 on exactly {HmIP-BSL, HmIP-HDM1, HmIP-HDM2, HmIP-MP3P, HmIPW-WRC6} and 75 on the other 40; 01_WP_TARGET_CHANNELS is INTEGER 0..16777215 on 42 files and STRING '0'..'281474976710655' on exactly {HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-LSC, HmIP-RGBW} (candidate said 43/3); DURATION_BASE VALUE_LIST is the 8-element list ending BASE_1_H on 38 files, DURATION_FACTOR INTEGER 0..31 DEFAULT 31 on 38; colour VALUE 0..1048575 and TYPE 0..2 on 3. The two contradictions therefore stand, and the write path is the right surface (rawconvert.go:801 mints `%02d_WP_`, i.e. the HmIP MASTER keys the editor edits).

ONE CITATION DEMOTED — WRONG SURFACE. The candidate grounded "an ENUM's wire value is the VALUE_LIST index" on ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:96-110. That code is verbatim as quoted, but libhsscomm is the BidCos stack (rfd / hs485d); 01_WP_DURATION_BASE is an HmIP MASTER parameter served by HMIPServer's legacy XML-RPC surface. The two demonstrably differ: HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDescription emits MIN=int(0), MAX=int(size-1), DEFAULT=int, whereas the captured HmIP descriptor for 01_WP_DURATION_BASE emits MIN="BASE_100_MS", MAX="BASE_1_H", DEFAULT="BASE_1_H" — strings. The cited code is not the code that produced this descriptor.

I FOUND THE RIGHT-SURFACE GROUNDING AND IT REACHES THE SAME ANSWER, WITH A NEW CAVEAT. On the HmIP legacy surface the ordinal substitution is a configuration-gated behaviour: DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue converts an ENUM value to its VALUE_LIST ordinal outbound and back to the string inbound ONLY when `replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal` is set; the field defaults to false in code (set from property `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal`, default false, in both LocalServer and HMIPServer startup), and the shipped CCU config turns it ON at crRFD.conf:47. So (7, 31) is correct on a stock CCU — but it is correct BECAUSE of a config line, not because the protocol says so. On a deployment where that property is false the legacy surface passes ENUM values as strings, and rawconvert.go's `toInt(val)` read would yield 0 while its int write would hand an Integer to a String-typed parameter. That conditionality is not stated anywhere in our code or in the candidate's finding; it is a real, previously-unnamed fragility. The "HOUR_1" naming correction is upheld: HOUR_1 appears nowhere in the firmware tree or the descriptors, and is aiohomematic's enum name at const.py:2550 (verified). The CCU calls it BASE_1_H.

TARGET-CHANNELS NARROWING UPHELD AND SHARPENED. `channelPattern` `^[1-8]_[123]$` (simple.go:158) admits at most 24 keys, while internal/central/adapter/week_profile_filter.go:246-248 mints keys as `fmt.Sprintf("%d_%d", actorIdx+1, subIdx+1)` with no upper bound on either index — verified verbatim — so a device with more than 8 schedule-relevant groups, or more than 3 members in one, produces a key its own validator rejects. The three STRING-typed models declare 48 addressable bit positions. Whether the legacy API accepts a Go int for a STRING-typed config parameter remains unverified in those words; the DeviceUtil path I read converts only ENUM and LONG, and leaves other types untouched, which suggests but does not establish that an Integer would reach the parameter unconverted.

There is no "Test-Alarm" action, button or string anywhere in the CCU's HmIP siren surface: the only alarm-firing control is iseAlarmSirenHMIP.activateAlarm, whose dialog title translates as "Alarm auslösen" and which writes DURATION_UNIT / DURATION_VALUE / ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION / OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION as a single Interface.putParamset to VALUES. Grepping the German language files for Testalarm / Test-Alarm returns nothing alarm-related. So the comment's parity claim is unsupported as written.

The number itself is nevertheless the CCU's own: 3 s is the first and shortest of the five fixed durations that dialog offers (3_S / 10_S / 30_S / 2_M / 10_M), i.e. what an operator gets by opening the dialog and firing without changing the duration. That is a real firmware-offered value and a defensible source for a short bounded activation — it is simply not "the Test-Alarm duration". The descriptor default is not a source either: HmIP-ASIR DURATION_VALUE declares DEFAULT 0 with DURATION_UNIT DEFAULT 'S', so the device default is 0 s, which cannot be an audible test.

Same file, one Tier 1 mapping worth having on the record because our own EncodeTimerDuration depends on it: the CCU writes DURATION_UNIT as an int with oUnit.S = 0, M = 1, H = 2, D = 3 (iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js:85), while the ASIR descriptor's VALUE_LIST is only ['S','M','H'] — the WebUI carries a fourth code the ASIR channel does not declare.

Recommendation for the comment, if it is rewritten: cite the dialog's duration list, not a Test-Alarm.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the CCU shipped a fixed test duration, iseAlarmSirenHMIP would write a constant instead of the dialog's selection, or a separate test action would exist — and the check does distinguish the two cases: the same file shows the CCU writing constants elsewhere (oUnit's fixed 0/1/2/3 codes) and reading the dialog for the duration. contradicted.title: The COLOR-integer hue round-trip is asymmetric: read divides by 200, write multiplies by 199
contradicted.citation: Read (CCU's own control page): ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/rgbw.fn:30-31 — verbatim: `WriteLine( "if (colorVal > 199) {colorVal = 200; saturation = '0%'}");` / `WriteLine( "var convertedValue = parseInt(colorVal / 199 * 360); " );`. Same arithmetic in two further independent CCU paths: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/RGBW_Controller.js:52,55 (`var hsvVal = parseInt(this.curValue / 199 * 360);` … `if (this.showWhite && this.curValue == 200) { saturation = "0%"; hsvVal = 0; }`) and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/webui.js:18210-18215,18254. Write: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/extern/spectrum.js:1383-1386 — `toHMString: function() { var hsv = rgbToHsv(this._r, this._g, this._b); var h = mathRound(hsv.h * 360) … return parseInt(h / 360 * 199); }`, selected by `preferredFormat: "convert360To200"` (spectrum.js:1490-1493; set at rgbw.fn:37, RGBW_Controller.js:65, webui.js:18219). White sentinel on write: spectrum.js:959-964 `convertWhiteValue` returns 200 only when `(preferredFormat == "convert360To200") && (currentHue == 0) && (currentSaturation == 0) && (currentValue == 1)`. Descriptor (Tier 2, firmware-shipped): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_rgbw.xml:279-292 — `<parameter id="COLOR" operations="read,write,event" control="RGBW_COLOR.COLOR">` with `<logical type="integer" min="0" max="255" default="0"/>`, physical integer value_id="LEVEL", no SPECIAL entries and no `<conversion>`. Witness (Tier 3): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:456 `return color / 200 * 360, _MAX_SATURATION` and :472 `color = 200 if saturation < 0.1 else int(round(max(min(hue, 1), 0) * 199))` — the Python family carries the identical asymmetry, which is where ours came from.
contradicted.firmwareValue: read hue = parseInt(COLOR / 199 * 360); write COLOR = parseInt(hue / 360 * 199); white ⟺ COLOR > 199 (read) / hue==0 && sat==0 && value==1 → 200 (write); descriptor COLOR is integer 0..255 with no SPECIAL
contradicted.ourValue: read hue = trunc(COLOR / 200 * 360); write COLOR = round(hue / 360 * 199); white ⟺ COLOR >= 200 (read) / saturation < 10 → 200 (write)
contradicted.finding: The comment's model is right and the arithmetic is not. Firmware confirms the hue circle is 0..199 with 200 as the white point: the write factor is 199 (spectrum.js toHMString), the read divisor is also 199, and the white test is `colorVal > 199` — matching our `c >= 200` exactly. But our read divides by 200 where all three CCU paths divide by 199, so the pair is asymmetric on our side and symmetric on the CCU's. Concretely: 135 of the 200 in-circle COLOR values decode to a different hue than the CCU's own UI reports — first divergence at COLOR=26 (ours 46°, firmware 47°), maximum 2°, and at the top COLOR=199 ours reads 358° where the firmware reads 360°. A second, smaller difference on the write half: the firmware truncates (`parseInt`) where we round (`math.Round`), so for 180 of the 360 hues we send one COLOR step more than the CCU's picker would (hue=1° → ours 1, firmware 0). Fixing the read divisor to 199 makes our round-trip converge and matches the CCU; matching the write to truncation would additionally make our writes byte-identical to the WebUI's. Note also that the descriptor declares COLOR up to 255 with no SPECIAL — 200..255 are simply undefined, and both we and the firmware fold the whole tail to white, so that half is already right. One caveat on scope: rfd applies no conversion to COLOR (physical is a plain integer), so the integer's meaning is defined only by the operator layer — the WebUI paths above are the authority here, and they are unanimous.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our read been right, rgbw.fn:31 and RGBW_Controller.js:52 and webui.js:18215 would read `/ 200 * 360`; all three read `/ 199 * 360`. Had the circle been 0..200 with 201 as white, toHMString would multiply by 200 and the white tests would compare against 200 rather than 199. Had the descriptor reserved 200 as a documented sentinel I would have found a SPECIAL block in rf_rgbw.xml; there is none, which is why the sentinel is a WebUI convention and had to be read there.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld as contradicted. I opened every cited file and every quote is exact, including the two truncation-vs-rounding details that carry the finding.

Surface check (the attack this project keeps catching, and it fails here): this is the same parameter, not a look-alike. rgbw.fn resolves its datapoint by `cObj.DPByControl("RGBW_COLOR.COLOR")`, and rf_rgbw.xml:279 declares COLOR with exactly `control="RGBW_COLOR.COLOR"` on the channel our profile maps. The device XML applies no conversion and declares only an opaque integer 0..255, so the CCU's operator layer is the only place the hue span is stated at all — and it is unanimous across three files written at different times, in both directions.

Patch check (which the prior finding did not do): rgbw.fn is patched twice by the distribution. I read both patched copies; neither touches lines 30-31. The /199 read is what ships.

Arithmetic reproduced independently: read divergences 135 of the 200 in-circle values, first at COLOR=26 (ours 46°, firmware 47°), maximum delta 2° (105 values off by 1, 30 by 2), and COLOR=199 → ours 358° vs firmware 360°. Write divergences 180 of 360 hues, ours one step higher (hue=1° → ours 1, firmware 0), because math.Round is half-away-from-zero where parseInt truncates. The prior finding's numbers are exactly right.

The defect is also internal, independent of which authority one picks: our write uses span 199 and our read uses divisor 200, so our own round-trip is unstable — write(270°)=149, read(149)=268°; write(359°)=198, read(198)=356°. Fixing the read divisor to 199 makes it converge AND matches all three CCU paths; matching the write to truncation would make our writes byte-identical to the WebUI's.

Scope, per notes/parity/by_design.md:3400 and :3449: RfDimmer_Color is registered for exactly one model, HM-LC-RGBW-WM (COLOR on VCU3747418:2), so the divergence reaches one device family. That narrows the blast radius but not the verdict.

One caveat I will state rather than paper over: what a given COLOR integer physically renders is decided inside the device, and the CCU applies no conversion. The WebUI is therefore the authority on the CCU's stated interpretation, not on the LED's response curve. There is no descriptor-level statement of the hue span anywhere; the operator layer is the strongest source available, and it is consistent in both directions.

contradicted.finding: The CCU's own PROGRAM selector is on exactly our surface — rgbw.fn resolves the datapoint by `DPByControl("RGBW_AUTOMATIC.PROGRAM")`, the same VALUES parameter our EffectLight writes — so this is a like-for-like comparison, not the LINK-paramset ACT_COLOR_PROGRAM one step away (that surface, KEY.tcl, carries the same seven labels anyway). contradicted.title: Optimistic-write confirmation compares floats after half-up rounding to two decimals
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger.cpp:56-66 `double dval=((double&)in+offset)*factor; if(dval>=0)dval+=0.5; else dval-=0.5; ((int&)*out)=(int)dval;` and :69-77 `((double&)*out)=(((double)((int&)in))/factor)-offset;` — every FLOAT parameter with a `float_integer_scale` conversion is quantised to 1/factor on write and echoed back from that quantised integer. The factors are per parameter, from ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/: rf_cc_rt_dn.xml `<parameter id="SET_TEMPERATURE"><logical type="float" min="4.5" max="30.5" default="20.0" unit="°C"/>…<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="2"/>` (step 0.5 °C) and `<parameter id="ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE">…factor="10.0"` (step 0.1); rf_dim_2t_644_le_v2_4.xml LEVEL `factor="200"` (step 0.005) and ON_TIME / RAMP_TIME `factor="10"` (step 0.1). The HmIP side names the quantity outright: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.DoubleToInteger#getStepGranularity returns 1.0/factor, and #convertLogicalToPhysical applies the same ±0.5 half-away-from-zero rounding. The step is NOT on the wire we read: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:205-218 exports ID, OPERATIONS, FLAGS, TAB_ORDER, CONTROL; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeFloat.cpp:105-119 adds TYPE, MIN, MAX, DEFAULT, SPECIAL; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalType.cpp:53-61 adds UNIT. No factor, no step, no precision.
contradicted.firmwareValue: Quantisation is per parameter, step = 1/factor: 0.5 °C for SET_TEMPERATURE, 0.1 for ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE / ON_TIME / RAMP_TIME, 0.005 for LEVEL, 1.0 for factor=1 parameters. The echo is the round-tripped quantised value, so it may differ from the written value by up to half a step.
contradicted.ourValue: A fixed two-decimal comparison for every float parameter — effectively a ±0.005 tolerance, regardless of the parameter
contradicted.finding: The firmware does quantise, and it does echo the quantised value, so the comment's worry is real — but the amount it allows is wrong in both directions and wrong most often in the dangerous one. Two decimals is a ±0.005 window. On a SET_TEMPERATURE write (factor 2) the CCU snaps to the nearest 0.5 °C: a written 20.3 comes back as 20.5, and valuesClose compares round(20.3,2)=20.30 against round(20.5,2)=20.50 and reports a mismatch — precisely the 'tracker cleared as CCU-authoritative, user-visible value flips' failure the comment names, on the single most commonly written float in the product. The same holds for every factor-10 parameter (ON_TIME, RAMP_TIME, ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE): step 0.1, tolerance 0.005, twenty times too tight. In the other direction it is too loose for factor-200 LEVEL, whose step is 0.005 — there a real 0.005 refusal is inside the window. So the fixed constant is not a conservative choice; it is unrelated to what the firmware does. The right driver is the parameter's own step granularity — the HmIP stack calls it exactly that — but that value is NOT PERFORMABLE from what we read: getParamsetDescription carries TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL/UNIT/OPERATIONS/FLAGS/TAB_ORDER/CONTROL and nothing about the physical scaling, on both the BidCos and HmIP legacy surfaces. Deriving a step from MIN/MAX, or from the unit string, would be exactly the convention-substitution this audit exists to catch. The honest options are to widen the tolerance deliberately and say why, or to carry a per-parameter step table sourced from the device XMLs — not to leave a two-decimal constant with a Python citation behind it.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had a uniform two-decimal quantisation been the firmware's rule, every float parameter would carry `factor="100"`. Across firmware/rftypes the factors are 200, 100, 10, 2 and 1 on different parameters of the same device, and the HmIP converter exposes 1/factor under the name getStepGranularity — a different answer, and a specific one. Had the step been readable at runtime, it would appear in HSSLogicalTypeFloat::GetDescription alongside MIN/MAX/DEFAULT; that function assigns five keys and none of them is it.
contradicted.missingInput: The per-parameter step granularity (1/factor). It exists in the firmware's device XML and in the HmIP converter, but is not exported by getParamsetDescription on either transport, so the daemon cannot measure it from the CCU.
contradicted.challengeNote: Verdict UPHELD as contradicted; the not-performable pillar is now verified more completely than the candidate verified it; the failure narrative needs correcting. Formulas quoted character-exact; all factors opened in the XMLs and matched. STRENGTHENED: the candidate listed three files as proof that the step is not exported, but stopped before HSSParameter::GetDescription's last line, which delegates to an arbitrary key-value block from the device XML. I inventoried every `<field id=…>` across firmware/rftypes/*.xml — one id, `AutoconfRoles`, 12 occurrences. Nothing resembling a step, precision or factor is exported on either surface, so deriving a per-parameter tolerance from getParamsetDescription is genuinely not performable, and deriving it from MIN/MAX or the unit string would be convention-substitution. CORRECTED consequence: the candidate's SET_TEMPERATURE story — 'tracker cleared as CCU-authoritative, user-visible value flips' — overstates the damage on the confirmation path. datapoint.go:1043 assigns `d.value = v` unconditionally before the tracker is consulted, and both branches at :1088-1098 announce v; the mismatch branch only clears the tracker sooner. The reachable defect is on the OTHER caller the candidate did not open: IsStateChange (datapoint.go:1997-2009) and WithValue (:2054-2059) use the same valuesClose to decide whether a write is sent at all. For a factor-200 LEVEL the ±0.005 window swallows real device steps — a confirmed 0.500 and a commanded 0.503 quantise to 100 and 101, a genuine step the device can execute, yet round(x,2) makes them equal and the write is suppressed. That is reachable from any caller finer than whole percent (a Matter LevelControl 0..254 mapping lands on ~0.004 increments). In the other direction the window is twenty times too tight for factor-10 parameters and ten times too tight for SET_TEMPERATURE, which only costs a redundant radio send. CORRECTED fact: 'step 0.1 for ON_TIME / RAMP_TIME' holds only in the lowest exponent range — the XML chains integer_tinyfloat (11-bit mantissa, 5-bit exponent) after the factor-10 scale, and HSSParameter.cpp:385-387 applies conversions in order, so the step grows with magnitude above roughly 204.7 s. Both corrections push the same way: the two-decimal constant is unrelated to what the firmware does, and the honest options remain widening it deliberately with a stated reason, or carrying a per-parameter step table sourced from the device XMLs.

contradicted.firmwareValue: Parameters that CAN cause a device request on a getValue: BidCos — only those whose <physical> uses interface="command" AND declares a <get request=…> child; HmIP — exactly INSTALL_TEST and CURRENT_ILLUMINATION. SPECIAL ids that exist: NOT_USED, OLD_LEVEL, PERMANENT, LOCKED, ACT_LEVEL, NO_MODIFICATION, VENT_OPEN — never OPTIONAL.
contradicted.ourValue: ignoreOnInitialLoadExact = {DUTY_CYCLE, DUTYCYCLE, LOW_BAT, LOWBAT, OPERATING_VOLTAGE} + prefixes ERROR_/RSSI_ + suffix _ERROR, justified as 'wakes battery-powered devices unnecessarily and may exceed duty-cycle limits'
contradicted.finding: Both halves are contradicted, on different grounds. (1) IgnoreOnInitialLoad's rationale is false for every member of its own set. I scanned all 130 rftypes plus 18 hs485types for the <physical interface> of each targeted parameter: DUTYCYCLE(59) internal, RSSI_DEVICE(126) internal, RSSI_PEER(126) internal, LOWBAT 89 internal + 22 command, and every ERROR_* / *_ERROR occurrence (65 across 12 names) command. I then checked whether any of the command-interface ones carries a <get request=…> child, which per RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.cpp:152 is the only thing that lets GetData build a frame: NOT ONE of them does — all 87 are 'no-get'. So on BidCos every parameter in our skip list is served from the local store with zero radio traffic, and even a hypothetical get-capable one on a wakeup device would be queued rather than transmitted (`QueueAfterWakeupFrame`, :168-172), so getValue cannot wake a sleeping device on this transport at all. OPERATING_VOLTAGE does not appear in the BidCos XMLs; on the HmIP side it is served from the device model like everything else. (2) The two parameters that DO reach the device on a getValue — INSTALL_TEST and CURRENT_ILLUMINATION on the HmIP legacy surface, via DeviceUtil#askValue — are ABSENT from the skip list. INSTALL_TEST is in our OptionalParameters set instead, i.e. we marked the one genuinely expensive read as merely optional. (3) The 'CCU sends an empty string for LEVEL_2' rationale answers a surface the firmware does not have: getValue on a non-readable parameter faults with code -1, getParamset silently omits non-readable parameters and faults outright if a readable one fails — there is no path that yields an empty string for a FLOAT. What our code actually does with IsOptional is allowsNoneValue (whether an unobserved DP still counts valid), not empty-value decoding, so both the bundle's summary and our own comment describe a mechanism that does not exist. (4) The descriptor CAN replace part of the list but not all of it. OPERATIONS (Tier-1 bits at HSSParameter.h:53-59) already marks DURATION_UNIT(2), EFFECT(2), ON_TIME(2 on 432 of 435 declarations), RAMP_TIME(2), RAMP_TIME_UNIT(2), RAMP_TIME_TO_OFF_UNIT(2) and INSTALL_TEST(2/4/6) as non-readable, so those are derivable. OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createfloat.tcl:21 `sv.ValueType( ivtFloat );` (SysVar.createFloat is the only JSON-RPC creator of a NUMBER sysvar). OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:464 `boolean bNumber = ( (iVT==ivtFloat) && (iST==istGeneric) );` and :1488-1497 the NUMBER renderer `sSysVarVal = cObjTmp.Value().ToString(2);`. contradicted.ourValue: NUMBER → FLOAT when the scanned value string contains '.', else INTEGER.
contradicted.firmwareValue: NUMBER is unconditionally ivtFloat + istGeneric. There is no integer NUMBER sysvar in the CCU's object model, and SysVar.getAll's `type` field is derived from ValueSubType() alone — ValueType() is never emitted, so the payload carries no int/float distinction to recover.
contradicted.finding: Our code re-derives a distinction the CCU does not make. Two Tier-1 facts settle it independently. (1) `getall.tcl` computes `type` exclusively from `ValueSubType()`; `ValueType()` appears nowhere in the getAll/get scripts, so the reader's premise that the payload might already carry ivtFloat/ivtInteger is false — it does not, and cannot be made to without changing the script. (2) Every sysvar-creation path in the firmware pairs istGeneric with ivtFloat (system.fn:832, createfloat.tcl:21, bin/hm_autoconf:338); `ivtInteger` appears in exactly one pairing, with istEnum (LIST). A repo-wide grep for `ValueType( ivt` across OpenCCU-Base returns no ivtInteger+istGeneric anywhere. The WebUI confirms the reading operationally: it classifies a variable as NUMBER only when `(iVT==ivtFloat) && (iST==istGeneric)` (system.fn:464) and renders it with `.ToString(2)` (:1497), i.e. always with decimals. So the correct mapping is NUMBER → FLOAT, always; the INTEGER branch of inferSysvarType is unreachable in the firmware's model and every integer-looking NUMBER value that hits it is a misclassification. Consequences beyond the reader's summary: model/hub/sysvar.go:754 routes a HubValueTypeInteger sysvar through intToWire, so a write of 21.5 to a float sysvar the daemon classified INTEGER is truncated to 21 before it reaches the CCU — a wrong value written into CCU state, not merely a lost bound. The rule is a faithful port of the Python sibling's heuristic (json_rpc.py:2482), which is a witness to where our rule came from, not evidence that it is right.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our rule been correct, the CCU would have to distinguish the two, and I would have found either (a) `getall.tcl` emitting `sv.ValueType()` next to `ValueSubType()`, or (b) at least one creation path setting `ValueType(ivtInteger)` together with `ValueSubType(istGeneric)`. The check can produce that answer — it did produce the ivtInteger form, at system.fn:840, but paired with istEnum. Both searches returned the opposite of our rule.
contradicted.challengeNote: Upheld on the firmware side; I re-read every citation and all four transcribe exactly. Surface checked and correct: our consumer really is SysVar.getAll (hub_wiring.go:1139 `jc.Call(ctx, "SysVar.getAll", ...)`, type+value taken at :1190), so getall.tcl is the script whose output we parse — not a different sysvar method. The firmware model has no integer NUMBER: every creation path pairs istGeneric with ivtFloat, and the WebUI's own classifier requires (ivtFloat && istGeneric) to call a variable NUMBER. TWO CORRECTIONS to the previous finding. (1) The stated consequence is wrong about our own code: intToWire (internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:826-852) guards the float branch with `v.Float >= math.MinInt32 && v.Float <= math.MaxInt32 && v.Float == math.Trunc(v.Float)`, so a write of 21.5 to a sysvar misclassified INTEGER is REJECTED with `sysvar %q: value %s is not an integer`, not truncated to 21. No wrong value reaches CCU state by this path; the operator's write silently fails instead. The string branch is the same (ParseInt("21.5") fails). (2) A defect the previous finding missed: inferSysvarType runs inside the scan loop, so the declared kind FLIPS between refreshes as the live value crosses an integral boundary — a variable reading 21.0 is INTEGER this scan and FLOAT the next, and toWire reads whichever Meta() the last scan left. BOUNDARY on severity: whether the INTEGER branch fires at all depends on how ReGa stringifies a float Value(), and that is not in Tier 1 — ReGaHss is a closed binary; only its Tcl/HTML consumers are in the tree. system.fn:1497 forcing `.ToString(2)` for display and system.fn:1491 handling `Value() == ""` both indicate the raw rendering is neither fixed-decimal nor guaranteed non-empty (an empty value has no '.', so it classifies as INTEGER), but I cannot measure the rendering from Tier 1. The mapping is contradicted; the firing rate is unverified.

Tier 1, semantics of the last entry: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:30 "stringTableAlarmConfirmingSignal2" : "Confirmation signal 2 - long short short" (:25 "Alternating slow flashing", :26 "Simultaneous slow flashing", :36 "Simultaneous fast flashing", :41 "Simultaneous short flashing"). contradicted.finding: The firmware fixes the order and it is stable across HmIP-ASIR, HmIP-ASIR-2 and HmIP-ASIR-O (identical 8-entry VALUE_LIST, identical MIN/MAX). Our rule therefore resolves deterministically to the last entry, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2 — the third of three one-shot confirmation signals ("long short short"), not an alarm pattern. Every repeating optical alarm pattern the device offers is one of the four *_REPEATING entries at indices 1-4; the three CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_* entries at indices 5-7 are the only members whose names do not carry REPEATING, and the firmware's own LINK-paramset defaults for a signalling optical link pick index 1 and index 4. So the positional convention picks the entry furthest from what an optical alarm needs: an optical-only activation or optical test fire writes a confirmation blink pattern, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE goes true, the watchdog is satisfied, and the sustained alarm flash never happens. HmIP-ASIR-B1 is not present in the descriptor corpus; the HmIP-side enum is device-independent, so its VALUE_LIST can only be a prefix/subset of the same order. The sound fix is the one the acoustic half already uses: answer it in the model from the descriptor, choosing a declared *_REPEATING member (or refusing when none exists), not from a position in the flattened projection.
