Upheld as contradicted, and the original's damage assessment survives a harder look — which is the part I most expected to break, since "the wrong constant is harmless" is exactly the claim that usually turns out to be optimistic.

Eight of nine labels are verbatim correct: CLOSED, OPEN, VENTILATION_POSITION on DOOR_STATE, and NOP, OPEN, STOP, CLOSE, PARTIAL_OPEN on DOOR_COMMAND. The ninth is wrong — ours is "UNKNOWN", the firmware's is "POSITION_UNKNOWN".

It is genuinely dead, and I established that from the read path rather than by grepping for the constant. DOOR_STATE arrives as an ordinal and is resolved to a label through custom.EnumLabelValue before OnState sees it (garage.go:365-366: `if label, ok := custom.EnumLabelValue(g.doorStateDp); ok { g.OnState(DoorState(label)) }`). So a real drive in that state produces DoorState("POSITION_UNKNOWN"), which is unequal to DoorStateUnknown and falls to the default arm everywhere. The two arms it could have reached both already return the same thing: closureStateFor's `case DoorStateUnknown: return nil` sits immediately above `default: return nil`, and Position() has no case for it and returns (zero, false) either way. The whole-repo usage set is three sites — the declaration, that one Matter case, a nolint comment — plus internal/model/custom/cover/matter_test.go:268, which drives a label no device can send and will therefore stay green whatever the constant says. A textbook bracketing test.

The write path cannot carry the wrong spelling either: command() writes string(c) where c is a DoorCommand, and the doorMode EnumSelect (garage.go:184-188) lists only CLOSED / VENTILATION_POSITION / OPEN, all correct.

It should still be corrected before something starts comparing it, and the fix is a one-token rename with no behavioural surface.

Two facts worth recording while the source is open, both of which I confirmed independently. (a) The physical byte for POSITION_UNKNOWN is 7 and for PARTIAL_OPEN is 8, but what the daemon sees is the ordinal into the value list (3 and 4), because the two-array StringEnumToInteger maps physical→label and DeviceUtil then maps label→position; so custom.EnumLabelValue's positional resolution is on the correct surface, and a client decoding the physical value directly would be wrong. (b) On a drive without the ventilation option the list is three long and PARTIAL_OPEN does not exist at all, so Vent() must stay gated on Capabilities.SupportsVent as it is. I also checked for an RF-side counterpart that would narrow the rule: there is none — DOOR_STATE and DOOR_COMMAND appear nowhere in src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}, so this is HmIP-only, and the descriptor corpus confirms the parameter pair exists on exactly two device types.

Dispatch: :1589-1601 `cgi_input; set action "put_page"; catch { import action }; if {[session_requestisvalid 8] > 0} then action_$action`. Newer OCCU stand that ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0163-WebUI-ImprovedFileUploadButton.patch:133 carries as unchanged context: `form "/config/fileupload.ccc?sid=$sid&action=backup_upload&url=$env(SCRIPT_NAME)" name=backup_form … { file_button backup_file … }`.

contradicted.firmwareValue: POST to cp_security.cgi?sid=@<sid>@ with `action=backup_upload` as a POST field and the payload in field `backup_file` (older stand), or POST /config/fileupload.ccc?sid=@<sid>@&action=backup_upload&url=/config/cp_security.cgi with field `backup_file` (newer stand). `restore_backup` occurs nowhere in either tree.
contradicted.finding: Four points, three of them wrong. (1) Endpoint /config/cp_security.cgi — correct on the older stand; on the OCCU stand the OpenCCU distribution patches, the upload form already posts to /config/fileupload.ccc and passes the CGI back as `url=`, so the endpoint is version-dependent. (2) `@`-wrapping of the sid — CORRECT and required: the canonical session id literally contains the delimiters (session.tcl:464 `set sid "@$sid@"`), and the query parser only accepts an @-wrapped value (:312), so a bare sid is rejected. (3) The action value is wrong: the firmware verb is `backup_upload`; `restore_backup` does not appear anywhere in OpenCCU-Base or in the ~200 OpenCCU patches. Because the CGI dispatches by string concatenation (`action_$action`, :1601) an unknown action raises a Tcl "invalid command name action_restore_backup" rather than a clean error. (4) The file field is wrong: the firmware reads `import_file -client backup_file`, i.e. the field must be named `backup_file`, not `file`. Two further contract facts our code does not model: the CGI requires user level 8 (`session_requestisvalid 8`), and upload is only step one of three — `backup_upload` merely stores /tmp/new_config.tar; `backup_restore_check` validates the archive signature and `backup_restore_go` performs the restore and needs the system security key. So even with the field and action fixed, a single POST would upload and never restore, which is exactly the silent-acceptance failure the candidate feared. Sending `action` in both the query and the body is not itself fatal (cgi_input merges both), but it is redundant — the firmware sends it once, as a POST field on the older stand and as a query parameter on the newer one.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had `restore_backup` and `file` been the firmware's names, a tree-wide grep for those literals would have hit in cp_security.cgi or in the patch set. It returns nothing for `restore_backup` anywhere, while `backup_upload` hits at cp_security.cgi:1027 and :1510 and in 0007/0163 of the patch set, and `backup_file` hits at :1027 and :1515. Had the sid needed to be bare, session.tcl:312's regexp would not require the @ delimiters and :464 would not add them.
contradicted.challengeNote: Upheld as contradicted; every cited line verifies verbatim, and I re-ran the decisive negative search myself. `restore_backup` appears exactly once anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base plus ../OpenCCU, in an unrelated file — the recovery-system's own upload form (../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/package/recovery-system/external/package/hm-platform/rootfs-overlay/www/index.cgi:74, `action="cgi-bin/restore_backup.cgi"`), which is the separate recovery boot mode, not the CCU's config CGI our restorer posts to. So: the action verb is wrong (firmware: `backup_upload`), the multipart field name is wrong (firmware: `backup_file`, read by `import_file -client backup_file`), and the endpoint is stand-dependent (cp_security.cgi on the OpenCCU-Base stand, /config/fileupload.ccc on the newer OCCU stand the distribution patches — fileupload.ccc does not exist in OpenCCU-Base, so the newer stand's receiver cannot be read here). The one point our code has right is the `@`-wrapping: the canonical sid literally contains the delimiters and the query parser only accepts an @-wrapped value. Two claims in the previous pass I could NOT confirm and am demoting to inference: (a) "the CGI requires user level 8" — `session_requestisvalid` has no definition anywhere in either tree, only call sites, whose arguments are 0 and 8; the literal is there, the meaning of 8 is not read from any source; (b) "an unknown action raises a Tcl 'invalid command name' rather than a clean error", and by extension that the CCU answers HTTP 200 — `cgi_eval` is likewise not defined in this tree, so the status code an undefined `action_*` produces cannot be established here. What IS readable and sufficient: no `action_restore_backup` proc exists, so the upload is never processed. Additional defect on the same surface that the previous pass did not name: the doc comment at backup_restorer.go:36-39 ("The CCU runs the restore asynchronously and reboots when done; the HTTP response only confirms that the upload was accepted") is false in a second way — even a correctly-formed backup_upload only writes /tmp/new_config.tar; the restore requires backup_restore_check and then backup_restore_go with the system security key, neither of which our code sends.

contradicted.title: The RF profile pointer is read as 0-based only when it arrives as a string
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:72-94 (EnforceConstraints), :96-112 (GetDescription), :115-118 (GetDefault); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:381-401; HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createActiveProfileParameter; Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU.json and HM-CC-VG-1.json (WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER), HmIP-BWTH.json / HmIP-eTRV-B1.json (ACTIVE_PROFILE)

contradicted.firmwareValue: WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER is TYPE=ENUM, MIN=0, MAX=2, DEFAULT=0, VALUE_LIST=["WEEK PROGRAM 1","WEEK PROGRAM 2","WEEK PROGRAM 3"], in the MASTER paramset (physical `interface="config" list="7" index="16"`), OPERATIONS=3 (READ|WRITE, no EVENT). contradicted.finding: Two halves, one confirmed and one contradicted. (a) 0-based for RF is CORRECT: rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:382-393 documents `<ol start="0">` with `WEEK PROGRAM 1` first, and `<logical type="option">` lists the three options in that order; HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDescription sets `MIN=int(0)`, `MAX=int(options.size()-1)` and `VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i]`, so the VALUE_LIST index IS the wire value. 1-based for ACTIVE_PROFILE is also correct (min 1, default 1). (b) The TYPE discriminator is WRONG. For an option-typed parameter the CCU returns an int: `GetDefault()` returns `(int&)default_option`, and `EnforceConstraints` (:78-91) takes any incoming string, matches it against the option labels and REPLACES it with `*val=(int)i`, falling back to `atoi(s_val.c_str())` otherwise. So WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER never reaches us as a numeric string; it reaches us as an int and hits our 1-based branch, mapping firmware 0 -> nothing, 1 -> P1 (should be P2), 2 -> P2 (should be P3). Two further mismatches: our string branch accepts 0..5 where the firmware declares MAX=2 (three programs on both devices that carry the parameter), and the parameter is MASTER/no-EVENT, so `Channel.Parameter` (internal/model/device/channel.go:392-396, VALUES-only) returns nil and `subscribeProfilePointer` never installs the subscription at all — the defect is latent, not live, which is why no round-trip has caught it. The separate climate path (internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:1936, resolveWeekProgramPointer + toInt + MasterParameter walk) is correct and matches the firmware.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the CCU exposed the RF pointer as a string, HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDefault would return a std::string and EnforceConstraints would leave the string form intact rather than overwriting it with `(int)i`; and the descriptor TYPE would be STRING rather than ENUM with a VALUE_LIST. Both checks read differently in that world.
contradicted.challengeNote: Contradiction upheld and strengthened; one sub-claim narrowed. What I checked. (a) The 0-based half is right and the source carries the ordinal explicitly: InitFromXml stores options[index]=id (honouring an explicit index= attribute when present, sequential otherwise — WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER declares none), and GetDescription sets MIN=int(0), MAX=int(options.size()-1), VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i]. rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:381-401 is verbatim as cited, including <ol start="0"> and <physical type="integer" interface="config" list="7" index="16" size="1.0"/>. (b) The type discriminator is contradicted, and I closed a hole in the previous citation. EnforceConstraints alone does not say which direction it runs; HSSParameter::GetValue:220-249 does — the read path goes physical_type->Get, PhysicalToLogical, then EnforceConstraints(inst, &log_temp, OP_READ). Physical type is integer, so log_temp enters the TypeInt branch, which only clamps. The value handed to getParamset is TypeInt. There is no read path on which the CCU emits this parameter as a numeric string, so our `case string` branch is unreachable and an RF pointer would take the 1-based branch: firmware 0 -> nothing, 1 -> P1 (should be P2), 2 -> P2 (should be P3). The 0..5 acceptance range also exceeds the declared MAX=2. (c) Latency confirmed independently: subscribeProfilePointer (week_profile_filter.go:538, reached only from :455) is the sole production caller of SyncProfilePointer, and it resolves DPs through Channel.Parameter, which reads c.valuePoints — VALUES only (channel.go:392-396). Tier 2 shows WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER in MASTER only with OPERATIONS=3 on both carrying devices, so the DP is never found and the branch never executes. (d) The ACTIVE_PROFILE citation is verbatim: IntegerToInteger(1.0, -1.0), min 1, max 3 for subtype "default" and 6 for "wth2". (e) New: the ORIGIN of the wrong rule is a Tier-3 witness read as fact. aiohomematic week_profile_data_point.py:512 and :539 carry exactly the comments 'RF: WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER is str ("0", "1", ...)'. That is a Python implementation's reading, ported into our code as a wire fact. Tier inflation at source. NARROWING of the previous finding: its blanket 'it reaches us as an int' is proven only for the rfd/BidCos path. HM-CC-VG-1 is a virtual heating group served by HMServer (address INT0000001), and its descriptor declares MIN/MAX/DEFAULT as the STRINGS "0"/"2"/"0" where HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU declares ints — a different description path. WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER does not occur anywhere in the HMServer tree I could read, so whether that virtual-group path returns a string VALUE is unverified. It does not change the verdict (still MASTER-only, still unreachable through Channel.Parameter), but the claim should be scoped to rfd.

contradicted.challengeNote:

I replace the prior finding's provenance guess for the 189. Concretely, ConvertFlashTimeToOnTimeList returns "600MS" for any input in 551..650 ms, "800MS" for 751..850, "900MS" for 851..950 and "4S" for 3501..4500 — none of these is in the device's VALUE_LIST, and the string goes straight into the atomic turn-on put_paramset at sound_led.go:341-352. It is also absent from the Python family, so it did not even come in with the port; it is invented. pkg/hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go is right and the registry rows are wrong. Consequence today: none behavioural. With IDLE_ON struck, the SMOKE_ALARM row's On∪Off is [PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM] ∪ [IDLE_OFF, INTRUSION_ALARM] = the complete four-entry VALUE_LIST, and the INTRUSION_ALARM row's union is complete too — so no real label falls through classify() and no derived sensor sticks at a stale value. The entry is inert dead data. What it does prove is the bundle's concern: half of that row sources its OnValues from hmenum.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatusSmokeLabels() while the OffValues are hand-written literals that were never read from the descriptor, and the two halves of the same row now disagree about what the vocabulary is. contradicted.negativeControl: Had IDLE_ON been a real label, the firmware enum would declare it as a constant (the VALUE_LIST is generated from the enum's own constants, so there is no path by which a real label is absent from it) and a grep for the token would hit in at least one tree. The grep is demonstrably able to hit: run for IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM and SECONDARY_ALARM over the same paths it returns matches in both the firmware component and the descriptor corpus. contradicted.title: The HmIP-RF firmware install gate (READY_FOR_UPDATE family) is a port, not a firmware reading
contradicted.ourValue: IsFirmwareUpdateReady = {READY_FOR_UPDATE, DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE}; IsFirmwareUpdateInProgress = {DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE}; BidCos-RF/BidCos-Wired = availability only, no state gate; every other interface = no update ever.
contradicted.firmwareValue: The CCU's own install precondition is `installable = updateState == READY_FOR_UPDATE || liveServerUpdateState == NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE || liveServerUpdateState == DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE` — DO_UPDATE_PENDING and PERFORMING_UPDATE are NOT installable. The base state machine is UP_TO_DATE(1), NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE(2), DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE(3), READY_FOR_UPDATE(4), PERFORMING_UPDATE(5), DO_UPDATE_PENDING(6), BACKGROUND_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED(7); the live-update state machine is UP_TO_DATE(1), NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE(2), DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE(3), LIVE_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED(6). The reported FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE string is the base state unless it is BACKGROUND_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED/absent, in which case it is "LIVE_" + the live state. BidCos (rfd/hs485d) reports FIRMWARE, AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE and UPDATABLE and carries no FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE field at all.
contradicted.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#isUpdateInstallable; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#installFirmware; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#translateFirmwareUpdateState; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicemanagement.HMIPDeviceFirmwareUpdateState; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicemanagement.HMIPDeviceFirmwareLiveUpdateState; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi:135 (BidCos gate), :146 (PERFORMING_UPDATE), :150-151 (NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE / DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE), :162-166 (DO_UPDATE_PENDING / READY_FOR_UPDATE), :168-188 (LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:246-256; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Device.cpp:294-298
contradicted.finding:
Three separate divergences, all settled at Tier 1.

(a) MISSING STATE — LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE / LIVE_DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE. The firmware's installability predicate accepts a liveServerUpdateState of NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE or DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE, and those surface on the legacy XML-RPC wire as the strings "LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE" / "LIVE_DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE" (translateFirmwareUpdateState prefixes "LIVE_" when the base state is BACKGROUND_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED). The WebUI's device-firmware overview renders an Update button for LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE (ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi:168-188), with a device-type carve-out only for HmIP-HAP/HmIPW-DRAP below firmware 2.1 and for HmIP-HAP2. Our set contains neither string, so GatedLatestFirmware returns info.Current: a genuinely installable live update on an access point is hidden forever. This is the bundle's "too narrow hides an installable update" damage, realised.

(b) OVER-WIDE STATES — DO_UPDATE_PENDING and PERFORMING_UPDATE are in our ready-set but are not installable per isUpdateInstallable, and the WebUI shows a status text rather than an Update button for them (:146, :162 renders the button only for DO_UPDATE_PENDING/READY_FOR_UPDATE — note that DO_UPDATE_PENDING IS offered by the WebUI but rejected by installFirmware, so the firmware itself is inconsistent between its UI and its RPC guard; the RPC guard is the one our POST hits). Our update entity therefore offers an install that installFirmware answers with `false`.

(c) The `false` return is not detected. internal/client/backends/ccu.go:223-226 treats a successful XML-RPC call as success and only falls back to updateFirmware on a *fault*; installFirmware returns a plain boolean false when not installable, so a rejected install is reported to the operator as a started install.

BidCos branch: CONFIRMED. RFDevice.cpp:246-256 and HS485Device.cpp:294-298 populate FIRMWARE / AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE / UPDATABLE and never FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE, and the WebUI's non-HmIP branch gates purely on `AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE != "0.0.0" && AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE != FIRMWARE`. So "BidCos reports installability directly with no state gate" is exactly what the firmware does. InProgress()'s hard gate to HmIP-RF is also correct — there is no BidCos in-progress phase to miss.

One unit-in-the-last-place divergence on the zero-version rule: our isZeroVersion also rejects "0.0" and "0"; the WebUI's BidCos action panel compares only against "0.0.0" (:135), while its display helper suppresses both "0.0" and "0.0.0" (:107). Ours is the safer superset, not a defect, but it is not what the install gate does.

Also worth recording: the WebUI picks the RPC by interface, not by device — updateFirmware for everything except HmIP-RF and HmIP-Wired, installFirmware for those two (ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368). Our try-installFirmware-then-fall-back-on-fault ordering reaches the same place for the interfaces we model (there is no InterfaceHmIPWired in pkg/hmenum/interface.go).
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our ready-set been right, isUpdateInstallable would have read `updateState == READY_FOR_UPDATE || DO_UPDATE_PENDING || PERFORMING_UPDATE` with no live-state clause, and the WebUI switch would have had no LIVE_* case that renders an Update button. It reads the opposite in both places: DO_UPDATE_PENDING/PERFORMING_UPDATE absent from the predicate, two LIVE_ states present. For the BidCos half, had a state gate existed I would have found FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE written into dev_desc in RFDevice.cpp / HS485Device.cpp next to AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE; the key is absent from both.
contradicted.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted at Tier 1. Every citation checked and every quote present verbatim: both firmware enums, isUpdateInstallable's three-term disjunction, translateFirmwareUpdateState's "LIVE_" prefix rule, installFirmware's plain `return false` on a non-installable device, and all six WebUI switch arms at the exact cited lines. The BidCos half is confirmed the hard way — FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE occurs nowhere in src/rfd, src/hs485d or src/devicetypes (zero grep hits), so "BidCos reports installability directly with no state gate" is what the firmware does, and InProgress()'s hard gate to HmIP-RF is right because BidCos has no in-progress phase.

Finding (a) MISSING STATE stands and is the one that matters. LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE is installable per the RPC guard AND gets a real Update button in the WebUI (:168-188; the only carve-outs are HmIP-HAP/HmIPW-DRAP below fw 2.1 and HmIP-HAP2, which show an info message instead). Our enum already carries the constant; IsFirmwareUpdateReady simply omits it, so GatedLatestFirmware returns info.Current and an installable access-point update is hidden. Confirmed.

Finding (b) OVER-WIDE STATES: the set-width divergence is real against both firmware surfaces, but the stated damage is NOT reachable and I demote it. DeriveDeviceUpdateStatus (pkg/hmenum/device.go:68-70) tests IsFirmwareUpdateInProgress FIRST, and both over-wide members (DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE) are in that set — so the update entity reports "installing", never "update_available", and never presents itself as an offer that installFirmware would answer false. The only observable effect is that LatestFirmware()/UpdateAvailable() report the target version while an install runs, which is what the WebUI's PERFORMING_UPDATE row conveys too. Downgrade (b) from "offers an install the CCU rejects" to a latent set-width divergence.

Finding (c) stands and is strengthened: ccu.go:223-231 treats a successful call as success and only retries updateFirmware on an XMLRPCFault, while installFirmware returns a plain boolean. The CCU's OWN client checks it — ic_ifacecmd.cgi:371 reads `if { $result == 1 }` before reporting success. We do not.

Two refinements to the bundle's own text: LIVE_DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE is accepted by isUpdateInstallable but the WebUI renders a status row for it (:189-191), so the two firmware surfaces disagree there — only LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE is unambiguously "offer it" on both. And the firmware carries a third grouping our sets match neither of: UPDATE_PENDING is true for {DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE, READY_FOR_UPDATE}. The isZeroVersion note is right: :135 compares only "0.0.0", the display helper at :107 suppresses "0.0" and "0.0.0"; ours is a safe superset.

contradicted.title: An empty string coerces a boolean data point to false
contradicted.site: internal/model/generic/coerce.go:53-75 (toBool), reached via coerceWire → DataPoint.OnWireValue / RestoreCachedValue / paramDefault
contradicted.ourValue: toBool accepts "true","1","on","yes" → (true,true) and "false","0","off","no","" → (false,true). An empty string is a *confirmed* false.
contradicted.firmwareValue: The CCU's own string→boolean conversion is Tcl_GetBoolean, whose accepted set is {0,1,true,false,yes,no,on,off} (case-insensitive, unambiguous abbreviations allowed) and which returns TCL_ERROR — not false — for the empty string. In the other direction a boolean is marshalled to the string "1" or "0", never "". An unknown value is a fault, not an empty string: rfd's getValue throws XmlRpcException("Failure") and the HmIP side throws an unknown-parameter-value RPC exception when the channel holds no value.
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:119-123 (`}else if(strstr(type, "bool")==type){//bool` … `retval=Tcl_GetBoolean(interp, value, &b);`); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:204-209 (`case XmlRpcValue::TypeBoolean: sval=(bool)v?"1":"0";`); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/getvalue.tcl (Interface.getValue returns that string; Interface.setValue passes `[list $type $value]` straight into the same converter); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:286-300; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getValue
contradicted.finding:
The literal set our code accepts is exactly the firmware's — {true,1,on,yes} / {false,0,off,no} is Tcl_GetBoolean's acceptance set, which is a real and useful grounding for the eight named literals. The empty string is the one member that is not: the firmware's converter returns TCL_ERROR for it, i.e. "this is not a boolean", which is our (false,false), not our (false,true).

And the premise behind including it does not hold on either ingest path. (i) The ReGa seed: our fetch_all_device_data script only emits a data point that has a valid Timestamp(), and for ValueType()==2 it writes the unquoted JSON literals true/false — so a bool arrives as a Go bool, never as a string, and an unknown bool is omitted from the document entirely rather than sent as "". (ii) Direct reads: Interface.getValue hands back the marshalled "1"/"0"; a value the CCU does not have produces an XML-RPC fault, which checkXmlRpcStatus turns into a JSON-RPC error. There is no CCU surface I could find that encodes "unknown boolean" as an empty string.

So the "" case is dead on the seeding path and live only on the REST generic SetValue path, where it is the wrong answer in the damaging direction: a client posting "" gets a confirmed false written toward the device, whereas the CCU would have rejected the same string. Dropping "" from the falsey list makes toBool agree with the firmware exactly and leaves the DP unobserved instead of confidently off.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our rule been right I would have found either "" inside the firmware's boolean acceptance path (Tcl_GetBoolean accepting it, or a guard mapping empty→false before it) or a CCU response shape that emits "" for a BOOL whose value is unknown. Instead the converter errors on "", the marshaller emits only "1"/"0", and both the BidCos and HmIP getValue implementations raise a fault for an absent value — three independent places that would have looked different.
contradicted.challengeNote:
The VERDICT survives but the GROUNDING does not, and I have re-sourced it.

What I broke. (1) The load-bearing input is unreadable. The bundle's central claim — "Tcl_GetBoolean's accepted set is {0,1,true,false,yes,no,on,off} and it returns TCL_ERROR for the empty string" — is not in any Tier-1/2/3 tree. Tcl core is not bundled (find for tclGet*, tclUtil.c, tclInt.h over ../OpenCCU-Base and ../OpenCCU returns nothing). That is external Tcl API documentation presented as a firmware reading. What tclrpc.cpp itself shows is only that a bool-typed value is handed to Tcl_GetBoolean and that a non-OK return propagates as TCL_ERROR rather than as false — the acceptance set is invisible there.
(2) Wrong surface. tclrpc's XmlRpcValueFromString is the CCU acting as an XML-RPC *client*: a ReGa/WebUI script passing `[list bool <string>]` into Interface.setValue. Our toBool decodes values arriving FROM the CCU and values arriving from our own REST clients. Different direction, different consumer.
(3) The supporting claim is refuted outright. "The literal set our code accepts is exactly the firmware's — a real and useful grounding for the eight named literals" is false. On the surface our code is actually on — the CCU's own XmlRpcValue parser — "on", "yes", "off" and "no" appear nowhere. Our set is WIDER than the firmware's, not equal to it. Strike that half of the grounding.

What replaces it, and why the verdict still stands. libXmlRpc is the value library rfd and hs485d link, so boolFromXml/boolFromStream/boolFromText are the CCU's own decoders for exactly the values we decode. All three reject an empty input as a parse failure, and both emitters produce non-empty tokens, so no CCU surface encodes an unknown boolean as "". Independently, the seeding premise holds in our own repo: fetch_all_device_data.fn emits bare JSON true/false for ValueType()==2 and omits any DP without a valid Timestamp(), so a bool never reaches coerceWire as a string on that path. The "" branch is therefore dead on ingest and live only on the REST generic SetValue path, where a client posting "" gets a confirmed false written toward the device that the CCU itself would have rejected. Dropping "" leaves the DP unobserved instead of confidently off.

Tier 2, the descriptor: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json carries 38 LOWBAT declarations on channels 1..5 across 18 models; HM-Sec-Sir-WM VCU0000261:4 declares LOWBAT with CONTROL "DEVICE.LOWBAT", FLAGS 1, OPERATIONS 5, TYPE BOOL, and HM-MOD-EM-8Bit VCU0000127:3 with CONTROL "BATTERIE.LOWBAT" — exactly the two CONTROL strings the two WebUI fragments look up. Tier 3 witness for where our rule came from: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/store/visibility/rules.py:308-311 `ACCEPT_PARAMETER_ONLY_ON_CHANNEL = {Parameter.LOWBAT: 0}` under the comment "Some devices have parameters on multiple channels, but we want to use it only from a certain channel" — a de-duplication preference, never a device fact.
contradicted.finding: The rule as written is contradicted by the firmware. LOWBAT is not a channel-0-only parameter: 18 BidCos models declare it additionally on channels 1..5, with read+event operations and (unlike the channel-0 copy) a visible, non-service flag set. For two of them the CCU's own control pages bind the non-zero-channel copy by CONTROL name — the siren arming control reads DEVICE.LOWBAT off HM-Sec-Sir-WM channel 4, the digital-state control reads BATTERIE.LOWBAT off HM-MOD-EM-8Bit channel 3 — so the firmware's operator surface treats the off-channel copy as the battery display for that channel, while the channel-0 copy is the service-message parameter (FLAGS 9). Our rule suppresses exactly the datapoints the CCU renders. contradicted.title: 'Some CCU firmware variants reject a raw setValue' is an uncited comment steering a write path
contradicted.ourValue: "Some CCU firmware variants reject a raw setValue for parameters they accept inside put_paramset — HmIP CONTROL_MODE=0 (AUTO) is the canonical case."
contradicted.firmwareValue: The asymmetry is real, unconditional and channel-type-driven (not variant-driven): setValue gates on checkRequiredValues, putParameterSet does not. But on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER the gated key is SET_POINT_MODE, not CONTROL_MODE — a bare setValue of CONTROL_MODE passes the gate and is dispatched.
contradicted.citation: Tier 1 — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#setValue builds a DeviceChannelValuesCommandDTO for the single key and then guards the dispatch with `if (!DeviceUtil.checkRequiredValues(device, channelIndex, valueKey, commandDTO)) { return false; }` — no event-bus send, no fault, and the incomplete DTO is parked in the class's `storedDeviceChannelValuesCommandDTO` static to be merged into the next setValue on the same device+channel. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#putParameterSet has no such call: for parameterSetType "VALUES" it goes straight from #validateAndConvertValues to the event-bus send. #checkRequiredValues builds a per-channel-type required set and decides with `if (paramSet.size() > 0 && (!paramSet.contains(valueKey) || paramSet.contains(valueKey) && paramSet.size() == commandDTO.getValues().size())) { ret = true; }`. Its HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER branch adds SET_POINT_MODE only when the write already carries it, then unconditionally adds SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE. Parameter shape: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createControlModeParameter — `byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE;` and a StateParameter("CONTROL_MODE", LogicalType.INTEGER, PhysicalType.INTEGER, IOOperations(ops), null, 0, 0, 3, ...), i.e. write-only, default 0, range 0..3; IOOperations values are READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4 (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations). Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M.json, channel :1 VALUES — CONTROL_MODE `"OPERATIONS": 2, "MIN": 0, "MAX": 3, "DEFAULT": 0, "TYPE": "INTEGER"`; SET_POINT_MODE `"OPERATIONS": 7`; ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M.json gives channel :1 TYPE = HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER. BidCos side for contrast: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:318-330 forwards setValue straight to RFManager::SetValue with no companion-parameter gate at the RPC layer.
contradicted.finding: The mechanism the comment gestures at exists and is exactly the shape claimed — the CCU's HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface really does accept inside put_paramset writes it refuses as a bare setValue, and the refusal is the worst kind: setValue returns false with no XML-RPC fault and no frame sent, so the caller sees success-shaped silence. PutParamsetForce is therefore defensible. But three parts of the sentence are wrong or wider than the firmware. (1) "Some CCU firmware variants" — it is not a variant question. checkRequiredValues is an unconditional branch on the channel's ChannelType, present on every build of this surface; the outcome is deterministic per (channel type, key set). (2) CONTROL_MODE is the wrong canonical case. On HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER the required set is {SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE} (plus SET_POINT_MODE when the write already carries it), and the final predicate short-circuits to ret=true for any valueKey NOT in that set — CONTROL_MODE is not in it, so a bare setValue(CONTROL_MODE, 0) is dispatched normally. The key on that channel that setValue actually refuses alone is SET_POINT_MODE: it lands in the required set, the set has 2 entries against a 1-entry write, the predicate fails, and nothing is sent. That is a striking result because the neighbouring comment in setIPMode (climate.go:1493-1499) already claims writing SET_POINT_MODE "has no effect on most CCU firmwares" — that claim is the one the firmware backs, and it backs it through this gate rather than through read-only-ness (SET_POINT_MODE is declared OPERATIONS 7, fully writable). The two comments have the right facts attached to the wrong parameters. (3) The genuinely gated cases on other channel types are worth naming instead of a vague "some parameters": DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE and RAMP_TIME_UNIT/RAMP_TIME_VALUE (each pair required whole, on any channel type); IDENTIFY_TARGET_LEVEL with IDENTIFY_DURATION and the IDENTIFICATION_MODE_* pair; WEEK_PROGRAM_TARGET_CHANNEL_LOCK(S); STATE on SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER/WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER; LEVEL on SERVO_/DIMMER_/BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and SHADING_RECEIVER (which also injects LEVEL=1.01 when only LEVEL_2 is given); the COLOR/COLOR_BEHAVIOUR pair; the DISPLAY_DATA_* set on ACOUSTIC_DISPLAY_RECEIVER; and on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the four-way {DURATION_UNIT, DURATION_VALUE, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION} — which is directly relevant to the siren path and means a bare setValue of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION alone is silently dropped. Net effect on our code: PutParamsetForce is not needed for the CONTROL_MODE-only ModeAuto write it was justified by, and is needed for cases the comment does not mention. Nothing is broken today — PutParamsetForce is strictly safe, and the two multi-key ModeHeat/ModeOff writes would take put_paramset regardless — but the justification should be rewritten around checkRequiredValues and the ALARM_SWITCH/siren cases, not around CONTROL_MODE and "firmware variants".
contradicted.negativeControl: Had CONTROL_MODE genuinely been gated, it would have had to appear inside the HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER branch of checkRequiredValues (the way SET_POINT_MODE and SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE do) or in isLegacyParameterDisabled; it appears in neither, and the final predicate's `!paramSet.contains(valueKey)` clause explicitly lets an unlisted key through. Conversely, had there been no asymmetry at all, putParameterSet would have called the same guard — it does not, which is what makes the general claim survive while the example fails.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Demoted from `narrowed` to `contradicted`, because both load-bearing assertions in the comment are false against Tier 1 and I verified each by opening the method.

"Some CCU firmware variants" — #checkRequiredValues is an unconditional branch on the channel's ChannelType. The outcome is a pure function of (channel type, key set); there is no build flag, no version gate. A reader who believes "variants" will conclude the risk is probabilistic and untestable, which is the opposite of true.

"CONTROL_MODE=0 (AUTO) is the canonical case" — I traced the predicate by hand for the exact write our code makes. For a bare {CONTROL_MODE} on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER, paramSet = {SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE}: size > 0 and `!paramSet.contains("CONTROL_MODE")` is true, so ret = true and the DTO is sent. For a bare {SET_POINT_MODE}: paramSet = {SET_POINT_MODE, SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE}, valueKey IS contained and 2 != 1, so the condition fails, ret stays false, the DTO is parked and setValue returns false. So `PutParamsetForce` at internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:1530 is not needed for the ModeAuto write it is justified by, and the ModeHeat/ModeOff writes carry two keys and would take put_paramset regardless. Nothing is broken — PutParamsetForce is strictly safe — but the comment's example is the one case that does not need it.

One narrowing of the prior report, which I checked because it read as too clean. It says SET_POINT_MODE is "declared OPERATIONS 7, fully writable", making the gate the whole story for the neighbouring comment at climate.go:1493 ("writing SET_POINT_MODE has no effect on most CCU firmwares — the value is read-only on the wire"). ClimateStateParameterFactory registers two SET_POINT_MODE variants; the "READ_ONLY" one really is READ|EVENT. So the old comment's read-only claim is correct for channels bound to that variant and wrong for those bound to "default" (the eTRV-B-2 R4M shows 7), where the gate is the operative mechanism. Which variant a given channel gets is a per-channel-type binding I did not enumerate, so "the gate, not read-only-ness" is right for the devices in the corpus and not proven in general.

The siren consequence the prior report surfaced is real and I confirm it verbatim: on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the branch adds all four of DURATION_UNIT, DURATION_VALUE, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION as soon as any one is present, so a bare setValue of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION is dropped silently. That, not CONTROL_MODE, is what the comment should point at.

contradicted.title: The actuator-feedback exclusion list decides which parameters can never raise an alarm, from seven literals
contradicted.ourValue: "Every entry is a parameter the alarm engine or an operator *writes* — reading it back as a cause turns the domain's own output into an input" — asserted over all seven entries
contradicted.firmwareValue: Only three of the seven are writable. ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION and SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND are OPERATIONS 2 (write-only). ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE and EMERGENCY_OPERATION are OPERATIONS 5 (read+event) — device-reported, never written. INTRUSION_ALARM is not a parameter identifier on any CCU surface.
contradicted.citation: Tier 1 — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory registers ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE and OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE through #createReadEventBooleanParameter, whose body is `byte ops = GeneralStateParameterFactory.getReadEventIOOperation();` — no WRITE bit. The same class's #createAcousticAlarmSelectionParameter, #createOpticalAlarmSelectionParameter and #createSmokeDetectorCommandParameter each open with `byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE;` (SELECTION parameters are ENUMs over SignalAcoustic/SignalOptical names, SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND over SmokeDetectorCommand names). EMERGENCY_OPERATION is registered through HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory#createReadEventBooleanIntegerParameter, whose body is `byte ops = IOOperations.READ; ops = (byte)(ops | IOOperations.EVENT);`. Bit values: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations — READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4. INTRUSION_ALARM appears in the firmware only as an enum MEMBER, never as a parameter id: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.SmokeDetectorCommand (alongside INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF), SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus, and SmokeDetectorEvent (ordinal 2); the only INTRUSION_ALARM-prefixed parameter is the SERVICE parameter INTRUSION_ALARM_COUNTER (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.serviceparameter.StatisticParameterFactory). None of the seven appears in any ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml — they are HmIP-only. Tier 2 confirmation across the whole descriptor corpus (../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json joined to channel TYPE from ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json): ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER VALUES carries ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE OPERATIONS 5, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION 2, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE 5, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION 2, DURATION_UNIT 2, DURATION_VALUE 2 — and nothing else; SMOKE_DETECTOR VALUES carries SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND 2 and, read-only at 5 or 4, DIRT_LEVEL, ERROR_ALARM_TEST, ERROR_CODE, ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER, INSTALL_TEST, LOWBAT, SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS, SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEST_RESULT, SMOKE_LEVEL, STATE; EMERGENCY_OPERATION appears only on CLIMATECONTROL_FLOOR_TRANSCEIVER / _PUMP_TRANSCEIVER / _DIRECT_TRANSMITTER at OPERATIONS 5; and no paramset anywhere declares a parameter named INTRUSION_ALARM.
contradicted.finding: The list's stated rationale is false for four of its seven entries, which matters because that rationale is what a future reader will use to decide whether a new entry belongs. ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE and EMERGENCY_OPERATION are read+event on every surface that declares them — the device reports them and nothing in the system can write them, so they are not "the domain's own output" in the sense the comment claims. They are feedback the device produces, which is a perfectly good reason to exclude them from causal classification (a siren reporting that it is sounding is not evidence of an intrusion) but a different reason, and the comment states the wrong one. EMERGENCY_OPERATION is doubly mis-scoped: it lives on the underfloor-heating actuator channels (CLIMATECONTROL_FLOOR_*), so the entry has nothing to do with the siren/smoke families the block is organised around. The fourth is inert rather than wrong: "INTRUSION_ALARM" is keyed as an `hmenum.Parameter`, but the CCU has no parameter by that name — it is a VALUE of SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS and of the SmokeDetectorCommand enum, which our own contract tests already treat correctly as a value (tests/contract/safety_classifier_test.go:214 asserts it is excluded from ActiveValues, not from parameters). The map entry can never match a lookup key and is dead. On the bundle's second question — write-capable VALUES parameters on the siren/smoke channel types the list omits — the answer is short and reassuring: on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the only writable parameters beyond the two SELECTIONs are DURATION_UNIT and DURATION_VALUE (the siren's own on-time, which nothing would classify as a fault cause anyway, though note from candidate c009 that the firmware requires all four to be written together); on SMOKE_DETECTOR there is nothing beyond SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND. There is no channel type literally named SIREN — the HmIP siren channel is ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, and the adjacent ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (HmIP-MP3P) carries a much larger writable set (LEVEL 7, SOUNDFILE 7, STOP 2, REPETITIONS 2, OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE 2, SOUNDFILE_LIST_1..12 at 2) that the list does not cover at all. Impact today is nil: none of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE or EMERGENCY_OPERATION appears in byParameter or byChannelAndParameter (they occur nowhere else in classify.go), so the exclusions are belt-and-braces and removing them would change no output. The defect is entirely in the recorded reason, which is the load-bearing part of a hand-maintained list whose completeness the file says rests on the comment.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had all seven genuinely been written parameters, each factory would have opened with `byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE;` the way the three SELECTION/COMMAND ones do, and the descriptor corpus would have reported OPERATIONS 2 (or a value with bit 2 set) for all seven instead of 5 for three of them; a real INTRUSION_ALARM parameter would have surfaced as a key in some paramset or as a StateParameterIdentifier constant. The scan reports 2 for exactly three, 5 for exactly three, and no key at all for the seventh — three distinguishable outcomes from one mechanism, so the check is tethered.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld as contradicted. I re-ran every leg rather than accepting it, including the negative Tier-1 claim, because the same tree's ISO-8859-1 encoding produced a false negative elsewhere in this bundle — here the absence is real.

The recorded rationale is false for four of seven entries, and the rationale is the load-bearing part: the file's own comment tells a future reader to keep the list ahead of every lookup, so the stated reason is the admission test for new entries. ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE and EMERGENCY_OPERATION are read+event on every surface that declares them — nothing in this system or any other can write them, so they are not "the domain's own output". They are device-reported feedback, which is a good reason to exclude them (a siren reporting that it is sounding is not evidence of an intrusion) but a different one. EMERGENCY_OPERATION is doubly mis-scoped: the Tier-2 join puts it only on underfloor-heating actuator channels, so it has nothing to do with the siren/smoke families the block is organised around, and its inline comment ("a fallback mode an actuator enters on command loss") is the accurate description sitting under the wrong heading.

The fourth entry is inert rather than wrong: "INTRUSION_ALARM" is keyed as an hmenum.Parameter but the CCU has no parameter by that name, so the map entry can never match a lookup key. Our own tests already treat it correctly as a *value* (internal/model/safety/classify_test.go:111 asserts it is absent from ActiveValues; :118 asserts Classify(SMOKE_DETECTOR, INTRUSION_ALARM) is not ok — which passes via this dead entry rather than via absence from the tables).

I confirm the impact assessment independently: none of the seven appears anywhere else in internal/model/safety/classify.go, so all seven exclusions are belt-and-braces and removing them changes no output today. The defect is entirely in the recorded reason.

One addition the prior report gestured at without pinning: there is no channel type literally named SIREN, and the adjacent ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (HmIP-MP3P) carries a large writable set the list does not cover. That is a completeness gap in the list, not a defect in the entries present.

contradicted.title: The allow-list of INTERNAL-flagged parameters that may still surface
contradicted.citation: HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter — the FLAGS assignment is a single if/else chain: UNREACH → 25; ERROR_CODE and service-message parameters → 1 or 9; `parameter.getName().equals("REPETITIONS") || parameter.getName().equals("OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE") || parameter.getName().startsWith("COLOR_LIST_") || parameter.getName().startsWith("ON_TIME_LIST_") || parameter.getName().startsWith("SOUNDFILE_LIST_")` → setFlags(2); everything else → setFlags(1). DeviceUtil#fillLegacyParameter, the only later mutator, sets TAB_ORDER, UNIT and CONTROL only — never FLAGS. CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is a configuration parameter (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.ConfigurationParameterIdentifier#CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE, built by GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory#createEnumeration) and matches no branch above, so it takes the else → FLAGS=1. BidCos: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/ declares DIRECTION 12 times, every one of them `<parameter id="DIRECTION" operations="read,event" ui_flags="internal">` (e.g. rf_d.xml:274, rf_winmatic.xml:198, rf_dim_1l_644.xml:360); rfd emits FLAGS from HSSParameter.cpp:210 `(*val)["FLAGS"]=flags;`. ON_TIME_LIST_*, REPETITIONS and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE do not appear in rftypes/ or hs485types/ at all — they are HmIP-only. Tier 2 corroboration, ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json (FLAGS as actually declared at runtime): CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE FLAGS=1 TYPE=ENUM in 105 descriptors (e.g. HmIP-STV.json, VCU3432945:1 MASTER); DIRECTION FLAGS=3 TYPE=ENUM in 124 (e.g. HMW-LC-Bl1-DR.json, VCU0000011:3 VALUES); REPETITIONS FLAGS=2 in 5 (HmIP-WRCD.json, VCU4243444:3 VALUES); ON_TIME_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 in 3 (HmIP-MP3P.json, VCU1543608:6 VALUES); plus COLOR_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 (3), SOUNDFILE_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 (1), OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE FLAGS=2 (4).
contradicted.ourValue: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE listed as an INTERNAL-flagged parameter needing an exemption to surface
contradicted.firmwareValue: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE carries FLAGS=1 (VISIBLE, no INTERNAL bit) — the firmware never flags it internal, on either transport
contradicted.finding: Three of the four entries are grounded; the fourth is not, and it is precisely the one the comment presents as the Go-side addition. DIRECTION, REPETITIONS and ON_TIME_LIST_1 do carry the INTERNAL bit (DIRECTION: ui_flags="internal" in all 12 BidCos declarations, FLAGS=3 = VISIBLE|INTERNAL at runtime; REPETITIONS and ON_TIME_LIST_* : the HmIP legacy surface sets FLAGS=2 by name-match), so exempting them is doing real work. CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE does not: the HmIP FLAGS chain has no branch for it and the else yields FLAGS=1, and 105 real descriptors agree. The entry is therefore inert — the exemption at internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:401 and reason.go:206 can never fire for it, because the guard those sites sit behind only asks about INTERNAL-flagged parameters. That is harmless in behaviour but wrong as documentation: the comment asserts a property of the descriptor ('their Flags field includes FLAG.INTERNAL') that the firmware contradicts for that name, and the stated reason for the entry ('the operation-mode gating pipeline reads it directly') is a claim about our pipeline, not about the CCU. Second, smaller result: the firmware's INTERNAL-by-name set is wider than our allow-list — OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE, COLOR_LIST_* and SOUNDFILE_LIST_* are also FLAGS=2. That is a deliberate difference in the safe direction (an allow-list is what we want visible), not a gap, but it means 'ported verbatim from the Python sibling's field map' is not the same set the firmware flags, and the two should not be conflated.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE claim been true I would have found either a name-match for it in the DeviceUtil FLAGS chain (the chain is exhaustive — every parameter takes exactly one branch, so an INTERNAL classification could not come from anywhere else in that method), a later FLAGS mutation in fillLegacyParameter, or descriptors carrying FLAGS 2/3/6 for it. The same scan that returned FLAGS=1 for CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE returned FLAGS=2 for REPETITIONS/ON_TIME_LIST_1 and FLAGS=3 for DIRECTION in the same pass, so the check demonstrably distinguishes the two outcomes.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Contradiction upheld, verified independently on both tiers rather than accepted.

What I checked. I opened the FLAGS chain and transcribed it rather than trusting the summary — it is a single if/else with four arms, and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE matches none of them, so it lands on the else and takes FLAGS=1. I then closed the escape the prior pass asserted without showing: fillLegacyParameter really does touch only TabOrder, Unit and Control, and the properties file it reads from carries no FLAGS key anywhere in its 1092 lines and no entry for this parameter at all, so nothing downstream can set the bit. I confirmed the parameter is absent from every BidCos device XML in both trees, and I re-ran the descriptor census myself: 105 real descriptors report FLAGS=1 for it. The three genuine entries hold up: DIRECTION carries ui_flags="internal" in all 31 BidCos declarations and comes back FLAGS=3 at runtime, and REPETITIONS / ON_TIME_LIST_1 are set to 2 by the name-match arm, so exempting those three is doing real work.

One count corrected. The prior finding said DIRECTION appears 12 times in rftypes; it appears 31 times across src/devicetypes/rftypes and firmware/rftypes together. All 31 carry ui_flags="internal", so the conclusion is unchanged, but the number should not be repeated as given.

Why this is documentation and not behaviour. I read both consumers. Each tests Flags.IsInternal() before consulting the map — reason.go:205-209 and operation_mode.go:397-401 — so a FLAGS=1 parameter never reaches the allow-list and the entry can never fire. The cost is entirely in what the comment claims: it asserts a property of the descriptor ('their Flags field includes FLAG.INTERNAL') that the firmware contradicts for that one name, and it justifies the entry with a claim about our own pipeline ('the operation-mode gating pipeline reads it directly') rather than about the CCU. The prior finding's second result also stands and is worth keeping: the firmware's INTERNAL-by-name set is wider than our allow-list — OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE, COLOR_LIST_* and SOUNDFILE_LIST_* are FLAGS=2 as well — so the comment's provenance line, that this set was ported verbatim from the Python sibling's field map, describes a different set from the one the firmware flags. Leaving them out is the safe direction for an allow-list; conflating the two sets is not.

On HmIP nothing clamps at all: a caller-supplied 3600 really does open a one-hour pairing window, while the same request against BidCos-RF silently becomes ten minutes. That comment is the stated reason the writer does not validate, which is what makes it load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

If the daemon keeps not clamping, the contract should say the CCU truncates to 600 s on BidCos-RF and does not bound HmIP at all, and a duration above 600 s should not be reported back as honoured. Our own lower guard — duration <= 0 -> ErrInstallModeInvalidDuration at install_mode.go:225 — diverges from the firmware's 0-means-off, but in the safe direction; I would keep it.

contradicted.finding:
Both premises of the patch comment fail, in opposite ways.

(1) "the CCU declares MAX=21 … [wrongly]" is contradicted. 21 is not a stale or generic bound the CCU got wrong: the firmware registers CODE_ID three times under distinct channel-type keys, and the HmIP-FWI variant is deliberately (1, 21) — narrower than the generic (0, 30) and wider than the keypad (1, 8). The WebUI then gives 21 a name: on the FWI maintenance control, CODE_ID == 21 renders as the bell button, i.e. 1..20 are the twenty finger codes and 21 is the doorbell. So MAX=21 is the firmware's considered answer for exactly this device.

(2) "5-bit field" is confirmed — CODE_ID is the low five bits of the CODE_STATUS byte (`valueData[0] & 0x1F`), CODE_STATE the top three (`>> 5`) — so the wire can indeed carry 0..31 and a 31 observation is physically possible. But nothing in the firmware names 31 as an idle/no-active-code sentinel; that half of the comment is Tier-1 silent. The firmware's idle indicator is a different parameter: CODE_STATE = 0 = CodeState.IDLE, and the WebUI reads CODE_ID *only* when CODE_STATE == 1 (KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED), ignoring it in every other state.

Consequence for our code: the patch widens a bound the firmware set on purpose, and does so with a sentinel meaning the firmware does not assign. CODE_ID carries read|write|event on the fwi variant, so the widened MAX also admits writes of 22..31 that the declared range rejects. The reported symptom ("the entity never returned to 31 after a recognized code") is better served by following CODE_STATE — which is what the CCU's own operator surface does — than by re-interpreting an out-of-range CODE_ID. If the raw 31 must be kept, the honest framing is "the wire field is 5 bits wide, so values above the declared MAX are observable", not "31 means idle".
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, createCodeId for the "fwi" key would have carried max=31 (or the generic 0..30 registration would have applied to FWI with no fwi-specific override), and either the CODE_STATUS decode or the WebUI control would special-case 31 the way it special-cases 21. Instead the fwi override exists and pins 21, and the only value the WebUI singles out is 21. The check discriminates: the same file proves the mechanism can express per-device bounds (fwi 1..21 vs wkp 1..8 vs generic 0..30), so an idle sentinel or a wider FWI bound would have been visible in the same place I looked.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld, and the case is stronger than the first pass made it, but one link in its stated chain was unread and I close it differently.

Premise 1 — "the CCU declares MAX=21 [wrongly]" — is contradicted. 21 is the firmware's considered answer: the generic registration is (0,30), the keypad one is (1,8), and only the fwi-keyed one is (1,21). The WebUI then gives 21 a meaning on exactly our surface: the FWI maintenance control reads MAINTENANCE.CODE_ID, lists twenty CODE_USED_01..20 slots, and renders CODE_ID == 21 as the bell button. Twenty finger codes plus the doorbell is 21.

Premise 2 — "5-bit field, 31 = no active code" — splits. The bit layout is confirmed verbatim, and I added the leg that makes the observation credible: the event path applies no range check, so a raw 31 is deliverable and the reported symptom is physically consistent. But nothing in the firmware assigns 31 any meaning. The firmware's idle indicator is a different parameter — CODE_STATE = 0 = CodeState.IDLE — and the CCU's own operator surface reads CODE_ID only while CODE_STATE == 1, ignoring it in all seven other states. "31 = no active code" is a convention supplied by us, sitting behind a firmware citation. Under the project's own rule that half of the comment is not confirmable — it is Tier-1 silent, and the honest framing is "the wire field is 5 bits wide, so values above the declared MAX are observable".

Correction to the first pass's reasoning (not its verdict): it asserted that the (CODE_ID, "fwi") registration is the one HmIP-FWI receives. The second element of ParameterMapKey is a parameterSubtypeID, not a channel or device type, and it is assigned from a `subtype` attribute in a channel-type XML that is not readable here. That mapping was presented as read; it was not. It survives by elimination — (1,21) is the only registration in the whole firmware that can produce MAX=21, and our own patch records observing MAX=21 — plus the FWI-specific WebUI evidence above. Conclusion unchanged, chain repaired.

Consequence for our code: the patch widens a deliberate bound on a parameter that carries WRITE on this variant (ops = 7), so it also admits writes of 22..31 that the CCU's declared range rejects — that half is an inference about our validation path, not a firmware measurement. Following CODE_STATE, which is what the CCU's own surface does, addresses the reported symptom without re-interpreting an out-of-range CODE_ID.

There is no path in this firmware by which the CCU emits a SATURATION descriptor without the EVENT bit. SATURATION is registered once, with read|write|event; the legacy XML-RPC descriptor copies that byte unchanged; the one override file that could rewrite a parameter description (legacy-parameter-definition.config, consumed by #fillLegacyParameter) can only set TabOrder, Unit and Control, and carries no RGBW or SATURATION entry at all. The device-side frame handling does deliver SATURATION as a status update, so the event source the patch restores is real — the patch is therefore a no-op against a current CCU (its Apply returns false) rather than a corruption, but its stated condition cannot be reproduced from the firmware.

The patch names neither a firmware version nor a CCU version, so the "sometimes" it rests on is unfalsifiable and the patch can never be retired on evidence. Either it was written against an older HMIPServer build, or the observation had a different cause (e.g. a descriptor read that raced device bring-up, or a channel where SATURATION is absent rather than event-less). Recommendation: either date the observation to a firmware version so it can be re-measured, or drop the patch — the descriptor is the authority here and it already says 7.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, I would have found a second SATURATION registration under a channel-type-qualified ParameterMapKey (the mechanism the same file uses for CODE_ID's "fwi" and "wkp" variants) built from #getReadEventIOOperation-without-EVENT or a write-only factory, or an OPERATIONS override in #fillLegacyParameter / legacy-parameter-definition.config. contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld on every leg, with one addition and one boundary the first pass understated.

Addition: the first pass said the override file can only set TabOrder, Unit and Control. There is a fourth lever — .Disabled — and it is worth knowing because it strengthens the alternative explanation the first pass floated. A disabled parameter is dropped from the descriptor entirely; it never appears with reduced operations. So the two shapes a real CCU can produce for SATURATION are "present with OPERATIONS=7" and "absent". "Present without EVENT" is not among them.

Boundary: the patch names no firmware version, so "sometimes" cannot be falsified for builds not in this tree. What is measured is that the condition cannot arise on this firmware; that older builds behaved differently is neither shown nor excluded. Because Apply returns false against a current CCU the patch is inert rather than harmful, but it can never be retired on evidence as written. Either date the observation to a firmware version so it can be re-measured, or drop it — the descriptor is the authority and it already says 7.

I also checked the thing that would have made this a wrong-surface finding: whether HmIP-RGBW's colour channels are described by a second producer (a virtual universal-light service) rather than by the legacy path cited. They are not.

The actual length lives in the converter constructor (AsciiStringToInteger(16), UnicodeStringToInteger(16), AsciiStringToInteger(127)) and is not published in the paramset description. contradicted.finding: MAX on a STRING parameter is not a length on either transport. On BidCos the CCU publishes MAX as the empty string and its only constraint check is that the value is a string at all. On HmIP the same field carries either a character-class regex whose {n} suffix happens to contain the length, or a maximum lexical value for date- and version-shaped strings; DeviceUtil publishes it verbatim, so that is exactly what arrives on the wire. Neither form is an integer. Traced through textMaxLen, every real descriptor value returns 0: "" yields 0, "[0x20-0x7E]{16}" stops on '[', "2255_12_31 23:55" stops on '_', "255.255.255" stops on '.'. So the guard is inert in production — it neither fires falsely nor ever fires, and the comment describes a check that cannot run. The bundle's byte-vs-character concern is real in principle (len(v) counts UTF-8 bytes while the firmware converter counts ISO-8859-1 bytes, so an umlaut costs 2 against a budget measured in 1) but moot while maxLen is always 0. On the second half of the question: the CCU does not refuse an over-long value, it truncates it into the fixed-size byte array, so nothing surfaces as an error either way. Deriving a real cap is not possible from the descriptor — it would need the converter's length argument, which the paramset description never exposes.

contradicted.challengeNote: Upheld, and I widened the enumeration rather than sampling it. On BidCos the STRING logical type writes MAX="" unconditionally and its constraint check is a type test — no length is enforced or published. I additionally checked the shipped device corpus: zero rftypes and zero hs485types XMLs declare a logical_type_string at all, so the BidCos STRING path has no device behind it in the firmware's own device set. On HmIP I enumerated every LogicalType.STRING construction site plus every DISPLAY_DATA_STRING regex actually passed in; each maxValue is "", a regex beginning '[' or '(', or a lexical bound ("2255_12_31 23:55", "255.255.255", "0.0.0").
