So the guard is inert for every descriptor value I can enumerate — it neither fires falsely nor ever fires, and the comment describes a check that cannot run. The truncation half is also upheld verbatim: AsciiStringToInteger allocates a fixed-size array and copies min(length, input) bytes in ISO-8859-1, so the CCU neither rejects nor reports an over-long write. Two boundaries the grounding did not name. (a) HSSDescription::Describe lets a device XML override any published field, MAX included, after the logical type has written "" — no shipped XML does so (0 hits), but "MAX is never numeric" is therefore a property of the shipped corpus, not a firmware invariant. (b) Our Text data point is built from whatever descriptor an interface returns, and CUxD's descriptors are in no reference tree; a CUxD STRING with a numeric MAX would wake the guard, and nothing here says what it would then do. Tier 2 is silent throughout: the pydevccu corpus contains no STRING parameter at all (0 of them), and openccu-data ships translations and semantics, not paramset descriptions.

contradicted.title: The OPERATIONS DETERMINE bit and the FLAGS projection are restated in DTO comments, away from their definition and without a firmware citation
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:54-58 (OP_NONE=0, OP_READ=1, OP_WRITE=2, OP_EVENT=4, OP_DETERMINE=8 — "Werte fuer das Feld OPERATIONS in der Parameterbeschreibung an der XmlRpc-Schnittstelle"), :64-69 (FLG_NONE=0, FLG_VISIBLE=(1<<0), FLG_INTERNAL=(1<<1), FLG_TRANSFORM=(1<<2), FLG_SERVICE=(1<<3), FLG_STICKY=(1<<4)), :91 (IsDeterminable = operations & OP_DETERMINE); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:209-210 ((*val)["OPERATIONS"]=operations; (*val)["FLAGS"]=flags); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFParamset.cpp:251-265 (Determine refuses unless IsDeterminable, then calls DetermineValue on the device); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:258-265 (XML-RPC method "determineParameter"); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/tools/devconfig.cgi:902-903 (renders the "Determine" link exactly when $operations & 8), :950-956 (that link calls determineParameter). HmIP corroboration of the STICKY bit: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter stamps UNREACH with FLAGS 25 = 1|8|16 = VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY. Tier-3 witness for provenance only: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:1243 "STICKY = 10  # This might be wrong. Documentation says 0x10 # not used".
contradicted.firmwareValue: OPERATIONS: READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4, DETERMINE=8. FLAGS: VISIBLE=1, INTERNAL=2, TRANSFORM=4, SERVICE=8, STICKY=16 (1<<4).
contradicted.ourValue: OPERATIONS identical (pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:77-80). FLAGS: FlagVisible=1, FlagInternal=2, FlagTransform=4, FlagService=8 identical — but FlagSticky=10 (pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:113), where the firmware says 16.
contradicted.finding: The two claims the bundle names are both right, and a neighbouring constant in the same definition block is wrong. DETERMINE is 0x08, and its meaning is exactly what the DTO comment says: RFParamset::Determine refuses the request unless IsDeterminable and then reads the value off the device, reachable over XML-RPC as determineParameter. The surface matches too — the CCU's own device-configuration tool renders a "Determine" link on precisely the condition $operations & 8, on any paramset, so our MASTER-editor button is on the same path the firmware is on and not a different surface wearing the same name. VISIBLE/INTERNAL/SERVICE are 1/2/8, so the three-field projection in UISchemaParameterFlags is faithful as far as it goes; the comment "mirrors the OCCU FLAGS bitmask" overstates it, since TRANSFORM (4) and STICKY (16) are dropped and unnamed, leaving a client unable to distinguish "flag absent" from "flag not projected". The contradiction is FlagSticky = 10 against the firmware's (1<<4) = 16. Because Has() requires every bit of the mask, the constant is wrong in both directions: a parameter genuinely carrying FLAGS 16 reports IsSticky() false, and a parameter carrying FLAGS 10 (INTERNAL|SERVICE) reports IsSticky() true. The in-repo comment asserts the opposite of what I found — it calls 0x10 "a known eQ-3 documentation bug" and keeps 10 "for wire parity" — but 0x10 is what eQ-3's own source says, not merely its documentation, and the HmIP server independently emits 25 for UNREACH, which only decomposes as VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY if STICKY is 16. The value traces to aiohomematic, a Tier-3 witness that flags its own uncertainty in the same line. Nothing in production reads FlagSticky or IsSticky today (only bitmask_test.go), so this is latent rather than live — but the test TestFlagStickyKeepsAiohomematicEncoding currently pins the wrong value in place.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our values been right, HSSParameter.h would have shown OP_DETERMINE at some value other than 8 (making the DETERMINE claim fail) and FLG_STICKY at 10 rather than (1<<4). The check reads all nine named constants and compares each: eight agreed and one did not, which is the differential result the control asks for. The independent HmIP confirmation is a second, structurally different check on the same bit — FLAGS 25 for UNREACH decomposes uniquely as 1|8|16 and is impossible if STICKY were 10.
contradicted.challengeNote: Upheld on every point, and I closed the one hole that could have sunk it. DETERMINE is 0x08 and means what the DTO comment says: RFParamset::Determine refuses with fault -6 unless the parameter carries the bit, then reads the value off the device, reachable as determineParameter. The surface matches ours — devconfig.cgi renders its "Determine" link on precisely $operations & 8, on any paramset, and that link invokes determineParameter, so our MASTER-editor button sits on the firmware's own path rather than a different surface wearing the same name. Because that is WebUI behaviour, I checked the distribution patch layer the firmware map warns about: patch 0037-WebUI-DevConfig touches devconfig.cgi but no line mentioning operations or Determine, so the condition survives into the shipped image. VISIBLE/INTERNAL/SERVICE are 1/2/8, so the three-field projection is faithful as far as it goes, while "mirrors the OCCU FLAGS bitmask" overstates it — TRANSFORM (4) and STICKY (16) are dropped unnamed, leaving a client unable to tell "flag absent" from "flag not projected". The contradiction stands: FLG_STICKY is (1<<4) in eQ-3's own header, not 10, so our in-repo comment asserts the opposite of the source — 0x10 is what the firmware's code says, not merely its documentation. Because Has() requires every bit of the mask, FlagSticky=10 is wrong in both directions: a parameter carrying FLAGS 16 reports IsSticky() false, and one carrying FLAGS 10 (INTERNAL|SERVICE) reports it true. The HmIP side corroborates independently: UNREACH is stamped FLAGS 25, whose only decomposition is 1|8|16 = VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY, and STICKY's firmware comment ("a service message that does not reset itself when its cause goes away") is exactly UNREACH's behaviour. Correction to the grounding's blast radius: FlagSticky and IsSticky are read in two test files, not one — pkg/hmenum/bitmask_test.go and tests/contract/hmenum_constants_test.go:48 — and in no production file, so the defect is latent, with TestFlagStickyKeepsAiohomematicEncoding pinning the wrong value in place.

contradicted.title: The two XML-RPC write-formatting rules that reach every device write rest only on a comment claiming fault -5
contradicted.ourValue: "<i4> is silently rejected with xml-rpc fault -5"; "<double>1</double> is rejected with fault -5, <double>1.0</double> is accepted"; both attributed to "the CCU firmware (eQ-3 ReGaHss)"
contradicted.firmwareValue: <i4> and <int> are synonyms in all three CCU-side XML-RPC parsers; <double>1</double> parses fine (strtod / Double.parseDouble); fault -5 in rfd is "Unknown parameter", and the string "Invalid parameter or value" belongs to the HmIP legacy surface and is raised for an unknown parameter or an out-of-domain value, never for a tag or literal form
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:260-261 `else if (typeTag == I4_TAG || typeTag == INT_TAG)\n      result = intFromXml(valueXml, offset);` — and libXmlRpc itself EMITS <i4>: :515-519 `xml += I4_TAG;` in `XmlRpcValue::intToXml`. Double: :577-584 `bool XmlRpcValue::doubleFromXml(...) { ... double dvalue = strtod(valueStart, &valueEnd); if (valueEnd == valueStart) return false; ...}`. Tcl surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:111 `}else if(strstr(type, "int")==type || strstr(type, "i4")==type){//int`. HmIP legacy XML-RPC: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcParser#parseValue — `case 3307: case 104431:` (the hashCodes of "i4" and "int", declared as TYPE_INTEGER_4_BYTE and TYPE_INTEGER) fall through to the same `Integer.parseInt` branch, and the double branch is `Double.parseDouble(this.reader.getText())`. Fault -5 in rfd: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:128,140,163 and :1738 `throw XmlRpcException("Unknown parameter", -5);`. The exact string "Invalid parameter or value" with faultCode -5: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException (cases UNKNOWN_PARAMETER / INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE).
contradicted.finding: Both stated reasons are false on both CCU-side XML-RPC surfaces our transport actually reaches. (1) <i4>: libXmlRpc (rfd, hs485d) dispatches I4_TAG and INT_TAG to the identical intFromXml, and it serialises its OWN integers as <i4> — a client that rejected <i4> could not talk to the CCU at all. tclrpc accepts both. The HmIP legacy parser (HmIP-RF, HmIP-Wired, VirtualDevices) puts "i4" and "int" in the same switch case. (2) <double>1</double>: libXmlRpc converts with strtod and the HmIP parser with Double.parseDouble; both accept "1", and both discard the literal text at that point — the value is a C++ TypeDouble / Java Double before any putParamset type check runs, so NO downstream validator can distinguish "1" from "1.0". (3) The fault attribution is doubly wrong: -5 in rfd reads "Unknown parameter", and the message our comment quotes comes from the HmIP legacy surface (raised when the backend reports UNKNOWN_PARAMETER or INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE — a parameter-identity or value-domain failure), not from ReGaHss and not from value formatting. What our code DOES is harmless: emitting <int> and forcing at least one fractional digit are both accepted everywhere. The defect is the recorded reason — it names a constraint that does not exist, and an operator who "simplifies" the formatter on that basis will change nothing, while one who trusts it will look for -5 in the wrong place. Scope caveat: I checked the three CCU-side parsers only; CUxD is BIN-RPC (no value tags) and Homegear is third-party, so an observation behind the original comment may have come from a non-CCU peer — that possibility is unverified.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the claims been right I would have found a tag whitelist that maps only INT_TAG to the integer branch (each of the three parsers could trivially have done so — they all enumerate tag names explicitly), and a double path that kept the literal string for a later validator. All three parsers accept both integer tags in one branch, and both double paths call strtod/parseDouble immediately — the opposite result in each case.
contradicted.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted. I opened every cited line and each contains what was claimed, transcribed exactly.

The decisive point is one I re-verified independently: libXmlRpc does not merely tolerate <i4>, it EMITS it. `XmlRpcValue::intToXml` at :517 appends I4_TAG. rfd and hs485d serialise every integer they send us as <i4>. A CCU that rejected <i4> on input would be rejecting its own wire form, and our transport — which parses incoming <i4> — could not have worked at all. That single fact settles rule (1) without needing the parser dispatch, and the parser dispatch (:260-261) settles it a second time.

Rule (2) is equally dead. Both surfaces convert the literal before any validator sees it: strtod in C++ (:580-584), Double.parseDouble in the HmIP parser. Neither preserves the text "1" vs "1.0", so no downstream putParamset check can distinguish them — the distinction our comment asserts is not merely unenforced, it is unrepresentable at the point where enforcement would happen.

I add a THIRD independent wrongness the prior pass gestured at but did not state as a finding: the attribution names a peer this transport never addresses. `internal/client/transport/xmlrpc` speaks to the interface processes — rfd, hs485d (both libXmlRpc) and HMIPServer's legacy surface. ReGaHss is reached over JSON-RPC (`internal/client/transport/jsonrpc`), never over this codec. So the comment attributes a constraint to a component that is not on the path, in addition to describing a constraint that does not exist on the components that are.

What our code does is harmless — <int> and a forced fractional digit are accepted everywhere — so this is a documentation defect, not a delivery bug. The cost is directional: an operator debugging a -5 will look in ReGaHss and at value formatting, when -5 from rfd means the parameter name is unknown and -5 from the HmIP legacy surface means unknown parameter or out-of-domain value.

I keep the prior pass's scope caveat and endorse it: only the three CCU-side parsers were read. CUxD is BIN-RPC and carries no value tags at all; Homegear is third-party. Whatever observation originally produced this comment may have come from a non-CCU peer, and that remains unverified — it is not a reason to keep the comment as written, but it is a reason not to assert the comment was invented.

contradicted.title: Interface reachability is inferred from a `connected` field that may not exist
contradicted.ourValue: "one entry per *currently active* interface"; absence = down; optional per-entry `connected` boolean honoured
contradicted.firmwareValue: one entry per CONFIGURED interface, with exactly the members name, port, info; no connected member; entries are read from /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml and cached, never from live process state
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/listinterfaces.tcl — header: "Fuer jedes Interface wird ein Objekt mit den folgenden Feldern angegeben: name [string], port [integer], info [string]"; body: `foreach interfaceName [array names INTERFACE_LIST] { array set interface $INTERFACE_LIST($interfaceName) ... append result "\"name\":[json_toString $interfaceName]" ; append result ",\"port\":$interface(PORT)" ; append result ",\"info\":[json_toString $interface(INFO)]" ... }`. Source of the list: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/homematic.cgi:53 `array set INTERFACE_LIST [ipc_getInterfaces]` and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/ipc.tcl:14,20,25-35,40-72 — `set IPC_INTERFACES_FILE "/etc/config/InterfacesList.xml"`, `set IPC_CACHE_FILE "/var/tmp/api_ipc.cache"`, `proc ipc_getInterfaces` returns the cache when present else parses the XML (name/url/info per <ipc> node, PORT derived from the URL). Where liveness does live: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/listbidcosinterfaces.tcl — "isConnected: [boolean] true, falls das Interface gerade verbunden ist", `append result ",\"isConnected\":[toJSONBoolean $gateway(CONNECTED)]"`, fed by ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:1269 `(bool&) descr["CONNECTED"] = (iface->IsConnected());`.
contradicted.finding: Both halves of the comment are false, and the consequence is the one the reader feared. Interface.listInterfaces is a CONFIGURATION listing: it walks /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml (via a /var/tmp cache), so an interface process that is dead still appears, and no member reports liveness. Concretely, on stock firmware our decoder always takes `reachable := true` (the `connected` lookup at :70-74 is dead code — the response literally appends only three keys), and the Reconciler's membership diff never shrinks, so ConnectivityChangedEvent can never carry an unreachable transition from this probe; a total interface outage reads as fully reachable. The `connected`/`isConnected` field the comment half-remembers belongs to a DIFFERENT method: Interface.listBidcosInterfaces reports address, description, dutyCycle, isConnected, isDefault, fwVersion, type per BidCoS gateway (from rfd's listBidcosInterfaces struct) — i.e. per radio gateway, not per interface process. That method, or Interface.getLGWConnectionStatus, or a per-interface XML-RPC ping/init round trip, is what would actually settle reachability. Tier 2 cannot help here: this is a firmware-generated response, not a device declaration, so Tier 1 is the only authority and it is unambiguous.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our reading been right the tcl would either have appended a fourth member (a `connected` key) or built INTERFACE_LIST from live process state rather than from a file plus a cache. It appends exactly three keys and reads a static XML through ipc_getInterfaces — a different result in both directions.
contradicted.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted, and I found nothing that rescues it.

Every cited line opened and matched. listinterfaces.tcl emits three keys and only three; there is no conditional branch that could add a fourth. The list comes from a file on disk via a cache in /var/tmp, so a dead interface process still appears — and worse, a genuine configuration change does not appear until the cache file is cleared. The `connected` lookup at connectivity_probe.go:70-74 is dead code against stock firmware: `reachable` is always true, so ConnectivityChangedEvent can never carry an unreachable transition from this probe, and a total interface outage reads as fully reachable.

I ran the check the prior pass did not: the firmware map warns that a WebUI/ReGa rule read from the sources may be overridden by the ~200 distribution patches. I grepped all of ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/ for listinterfaces / listInterfaces and got zero hits. So the OCCU source text is what ships on OpenCCU, and there is no patched variant that adds a liveness member. That closes the one escape route the citation had.

The half-remembered field belongs to a different method on a different granularity: Interface.listBidcosInterfaces reports address, description, dutyCycle, isConnected, isDefault, fwVersion and type per BidCoS radio GATEWAY, sourced from rfd's own listBidcosInterfaces struct — not per interface process. That method, Interface.getLGWConnectionStatus, or a per-interface XML-RPC round trip is what would actually settle reachability.

Tier 2 cannot speak here and it is worth being explicit about why: this is a firmware-generated response shape, not something a device declares, so no descriptor corpus is authority over it. Tier 1 is the only witness and it is unambiguous.

contradicted.title: The Homegear-vs-CCU classification rests on three unsourced string signatures and defaults to CCU
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:35 `const char XmlRpcServerConnection::BINARY_SIGNATURE[] = "Bin";` and :98-101 `if((_header.length()>=BINARY_SIGNATURE_SIZE+5) && (strncmp(hp, BINARY_SIGNATURE, BINARY_SIGNATURE_SIZE)==0)){ _isBinary=true; …}` — one listening socket, protocol chosen per request · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/CMakeLists.txt:95 and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/CMakeLists.txt:57 both `target_link_libraries(… XmlRpc …)` · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1206 `XmlRpcMethodPing(XmlRpcServer* s):XmlRpcServerMethod("ping", s){};` and :1274 registers it; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:601 the same · ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/config_templates/InterfacesList.xml:5 `<url>xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001</url>` (BidCos-RF) and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485dLoader/hs485dLoader.cpp:238 `<url>xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:` (BidCos-Wired) — the CCU's own clients address rfd and hs485d over BIN-RPC · Homegear signatures: `grep -rai "homegear"` over ../OpenCCU-Base returns nothing, and no device type in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types} or in ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/ begins with `HG-` (Tier 2).
contradicted.firmwareValue: rfd and hs485d both serve BIN-RPC on their ordinary XML-RPC socket (auto-detected by the 3-byte "Bin" signature) and both implement `ping`; the CCU addresses them as `xmlrpc_bin://…`
contradicted.ourValue: `// Step 1 — try BIN-RPC ping (CUxD uses BIN-RPC exclusively).` → any endpoint that answers a BIN-RPC ping is classified KindCUxD
contradicted.finding: The CUxD half is contradicted outright. BIN-RPC is not a CUxD discriminator on a CCU: libXmlRpc's server sniffs the first three bytes of every request and switches to the binary framing on the same socket, rfd and hs485d both link that library, both register `ping`, and the CCU's own InterfacesList addresses BidCos-RF with `xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001`. rfd's ping handler accepts exactly one string parameter (XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1208-1217), which is precisely the shape we send (`Call(ctx, "ping", cfg.InterfaceID)`), so a BIN-RPC probe pointed at rfd returns success and the endpoint is classified KindCUxD with no further check. The Homegear half is a different result and should not be reported as the same one: whether `TYPE` starting `HG-` or a FIRMWARE string containing `homegear` identifies Homegear is a Homegear question, and the CCU sources are silent on it by construction. What Tier 1 + Tier 2 do settle is the false-positive risk against stock firmware: neither string occurs anywhere in the OCCU sources, in the shipped device-type XMLs, or in the pydevccu descriptor corpus, so stock firmware cannot trip the Homegear branch. Mitigating fact discovered while reading: DetectBackend has no production caller (only detection_test.go), so nothing on a running daemon depends on either branch today.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had 'CUxD uses BIN-RPC exclusively' been right, the CCU's own interface list would address rfd over `xmlrpc://` like it addresses VirtualDevices, and the shared server library would carry no binary path. It addresses it `xmlrpc_bin://` and the library carries the path at XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:98 — a different result from the one the rule predicts. For the Homegear half the control is `grep -rai homegear ../OpenCCU-Base` plus a `HG-` scan of both descriptor corpora: a hit would have shown the sniff can fire against stock firmware; there is none.
contradicted.challengeNote: The CUxD half is contradicted and I confirm it end to end: BIN-RPC is not a CUxD discriminator on a CCU. libXmlRpc switches to binary framing on the same listening socket from the first three bytes, rfd and hs485d both link it, both register `ping`, the handler accepts exactly the one-string shape our probe sends, and the CCU's own InterfacesList addresses BidCos-RF as xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001 - so a BIN-RPC probe pointed at rfd returns success and the endpoint is labelled KindCUxD with no further check. I ALSO BREAK the previous agent's treatment of the Homegear half. It reported that half as Tier-1-silent-by-construction and stopped there, which reads as 'ungrounded but ordinary'. It is worse: the three signatures have no witness at ANY tier. The Python family we ported from does not use them - aiohomematic decides Homegear from the getVersion string (`"homegear" in version_lower`), probed only when system.listMethods advertises getVersion. So sniffHomegear's TYPE-prefix/FIRMWARE rules were invented at the port, not carried over, and the doc comment's confident 'Homegear encodes a TYPE field that starts with HG-' asserts a property of a data source that was read from nowhere - the exact tell this project's rule names. That should be recorded as unverified-with-no-witness, not as Tier-1 silence. The constructive half: the mechanism aiohomematic uses IS groundable against this firmware - rfd implements getVersion and libXmlRpc serves system.listMethods, so a version-string discriminator can be built and negative-controlled against a real CCU, while the listDevices sniff cannot be checked against anything. Two things I upheld from the previous agent, both re-measured: stock firmware cannot trip the Homegear branch (0 hits for "homegear", no HG- type, both with negative controls), and DetectBackend has no production caller - grep over *.go finds it only in internal/client/backends/detection_test.go. One consequence the previous agent did not name: internal/client/interface_client.go:158 and :163 carry comments saying the client 'populates this after [backends.DetectBackend] completes'. Nothing calls DetectBackend, so those two comments are false as well - a comment-claims item, not a wire item.

contradicted.title: The virtual-remote device addresses are bare literals with no cited source
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFCentral.cpp:36-37 `type="HM-RCV-50"; serial="BidCoS-RF";` · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Central.cpp:36-37 `type="HMW-RCV-50"; serial="BidCoS-Wir";` · HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.VirtualRemoteControl — `DEVICE_TYPE = "HmIP-RCV-50"`, `DEVICE_ID_BASE = "HmIP-RCV-"`, a static counter `vrcNr` initialised to 1, and in the constructor `this.id = DEVICE_ID_BASE + vrcNr;` with `createDeviceDescription` calling `setAddress(this.id)` and naming children `this.id + ":" + channelIndex`; the single instance is built in HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler's constructor from `AccessPointUtil.getFirstMasterAccessPoint`, gated by `Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.Enabled` (=true in ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf) with channel indices `Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.ChannelIndex.First`=0 … `.Last`=50.
contradicted.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF → address "BidCoS-RF", TYPE HM-RCV-50 · BidCos-Wired → address "BidCoS-Wir", TYPE HMW-RCV-50 · HmIP-RF → address "HmIP-RCV-1" (HmIP-RCV-<n>, n starts at 1), TYPE HmIP-RCV-50
contradicted.ourValue: InterfaceHmIPRF → "HmIP-RF"; InterfaceBidCosRF → "BidCoS-RF"; every other interface → ("", false)
contradicted.finding: Both halves the reader flagged are wrong, and the third definition in the repo is right. (1) `interface_client.go:1085` returns "HmIP-RF" as the HmIP virtual-remote address. The firmware address is `HmIP-RCV-1` — DEVICE_ID_BASE "HmIP-RCV-" plus a counter that starts at 1, with one instance constructed per LegacyServiceHandler. "HmIP-RF" is the INTERFACE name, not a device address; no device with that address exists. (2) The doc comment at :1079-1081 says wired interfaces have no virtual-remote concept. hs485d constructs one unconditionally: HS485Central.cpp:37 `serial="BidCoS-Wir"`, type HMW-RCV-50. (3) The capitalisation the reader doubted is right: `BidCoS-RF` with a capital S, verbatim from RFCentral.cpp:37. So `internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:38-44` — "BidCoS-RF", "BidCoS-Wir", "HmIP-RCV-1" — matches the firmware on all three entries, and `pkg/hmenum/device_model.go:21-25` — HM-RCV-50, HMW-RCV-50, HmIP-RCV-50 — matches the three TYPE strings exactly. The wrong definition is the one in interface_client.go, and it is the one with no citation. One narrowing on the routingkey entry: `HmIP-RCV-1` is only the first VRC's address; the counter is static and increments per constructed instance, so a second LegacyServiceHandler in one JVM would yield HmIP-RCV-2. On a CCU one handler is built, so HmIP-RCV-1 is correct in our scope. Consequence today: `VirtualRemote()` has no production caller (only interface_client_test.go:186 and interface_client_deep_test.go:559), so the wrong address is latent — but it is a device-addressing datum that would go on the wire the moment it is wired up, and its two neighbours prove the repo already knows the right answer.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had "HmIP-RF" been the HmIP virtual remote's address, the HmIP component would have had a constant carrying it and no `DEVICE_ID_BASE` counter; instead the address is composed from a base plus an instance number and the TYPE is a separate constant. Had BidCos-Wired had no virtual remote, hs485d would have had no HS485Central with a `serial=` assignment, mirroring rfd's RFCentral; it has one, at the same line, with a different literal — the check returns a different string for each of the three families, so it is not echoing our input.
contradicted.challengeNote: Upheld, and I strengthened it in the one place it was thin. All three firmware values are verbatim, and the step the previous agent left implicit - that rfd's `serial` is the XML-RPC ADDRESS - is now cited (RFDevice.cpp:242). interface_client.go:1085 returns "HmIP-RF", which is the INTERFACE name; the firmware address is HmIP-RCV-1, and I closed the one escape route the previous agent did not test: VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching is exact-equality against DEVICE_ID_BASE+vrcNr, so "HmIP-RF" matches nothing and would be resolved as an ordinary device id, raising DeviceNotFound. The doc comment's claim that wired interfaces have no virtual-remote concept is refuted by HS485Central.cpp:36-37, which constructs one unconditionally. The capitalisation the reader doubted is right (`BidCoS-RF`, capital S). The two neighbouring definitions match the firmware exactly on all three entries. ONE CITATION DEFECT I found in the grounding, and it is the kind this audit exists to catch. It writes the VRC channel range as though crRFD.conf carried it - 'gated by Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.Enabled (=true in crRFD.conf) with channel indices Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.ChannelIndex.First=0 ... .Last=50'. crRFD.conf sets only three VRC properties: Enabled, MigrationGate.Enabled, MigrationGate.File (grep over ../OpenCCU-Base/etc and /opt returns exactly those). 0 and 50 are the CODE defaults in VirtualRemoteControl's constructor (ServiceProperties.getInt with fallback 0 and 50) - a firmware default, not a shipped configuration value, and this project's own rule separates those two tiers. It does not change the address, so the verdict stands, but a later reader following that citation into crRFD.conf will not find the numbers. The address narrowing the previous agent gave is correct and I re-derived it: vrcNr is static and increments per constructed instance, so HmIP-RCV-1 is only the first; on a CCU one LegacyServiceHandler is built, so it is the right value in our scope. Consequence today is latent - VirtualRemote() has no production caller - but it is a device-addressing datum that goes on the wire the moment it is used, and its two neighbours already hold the right answer.

contradicted.citation: OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.cpp:147-176 `GetData`: `if(get_request_frame.id.empty()){ return inst->GetStoredValue(value_id, param); }` / `if(inst->GetAge(value_id)<VALUE_CACHE_TIME){ return inst->GetStoredValue(value_id, param); }` / `if(channel->GetDevice()->RxNeedsWakeup()){ if(inst->GetStoredValue(value_id, param))return true; channel->GetDevice()->QueueAfterWakeupFrame(frame); return false; }`. OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParamset.cpp:162-176 (`Get` returns false on the first parameter whose GetValue fails — no partial struct). OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalType.cpp:43-44 (`use_default_on_failure` is a per-parameter XML attribute, default false at :25). OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:228-244 + OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcException.h:29 (`Failure` with the default code -1). Descriptor scan: `grep -rn use_default_on_failure ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/` = 21 hits in 20 of 130 files, every one `<logical type="string" default="" use_default_on_failure="true"/>`. `grep -rho 'id="[A-Z_0-9]*_STATUS"' ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml | sort -u` = ACK_STATUS, LED_STATUS only.
contradicted.ourValue: value_cache.go:314-332: BidCos-RF and VirtualDevices are skipped interface-wide because a per-parameter fallback "cannot return a device-fresh reading — only a CCU-internal placeholder (reported with *_STATUS = NORMAL so the status cannot be used to reject it)" and because "the fallback then returns the paramset default instead of a real reading".
contradicted.firmwareValue: For BidCos-RF: (a) a read that cannot be satisfied does NOT return the paramset default — `HSSParamset::Get` aborts on the first failing readable parameter and the whole getParamset answers fault -1 "Failure". The DEFAULT fallback exists only for parameters whose device XML declares `use_default_on_failure="true"`, which in the shipped rftypes is 21 parameters, all `logical type="string" default=""`. (b) There is no `*_STATUS = NORMAL` sibling convention on BidCos-RF; the only `*_STATUS` ids in the 130 shipped rftypes are ACK_STATUS and LED_STATUS. (c) The suppression is not interface-shaped: the no-active-query branch is gated on `RxNeedsWakeup()`, i.e. on the device's RX_MODE, so a mains BidCos-RF device (RX_ALWAYS) DOES get the get-request frame sent and answered from the device. (d) The CCU already computes the exact flag we want — `undefined`, true from construction and cleared only when a device frame delivered the value — and exposes it through the 3-argument getValue/getParamset (mode==1).
contradicted.finding: The rule's stated firmware basis does not hold for BidCos-RF on any of its three legs. The failure mode is not a plausible-looking default value quietly marked valid; it is a hard fault -1 on the whole paramset, because HSSParamset::Get is all-or-nothing. The `*_STATUS = NORMAL` reasoning is imported from the HmIP surface and has no counterpart in the BidCos-RF descriptors. And the skip keys on the interface while the firmware keys on RX_MODE, which is exactly the over-broad scope the reader flagged: mains-powered BidCos-RF devices are actively queried by rfd and are paying for the battery subset. Most usefully, the input our code is trying to guess at is carried by the source after all — rfd tracks `undefined` per parameter and hands it over on the 3-argument form, so the honest fix is to read that flag rather than to widen or narrow a heuristic. I could not settle the VirtualDevices half: that interface is served by the HMServer group/virtual-device stack, not by rfd, and I did not verify its read path — treat the VirtualDevices leg of this rule as still ungrounded.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had our claim been right, `HSSParamset::Get` would have inserted the logical DEFAULT for an unreadable parameter and continued to the next one, and `use_default_on_failure` would appear on ordinary numeric value parameters across the rftypes corpus rather than on 21 empty-string parameters. It does neither: Get `return false`s on the first failure, and the attribute defaults to false (HSSLogicalType.cpp:25). Had the battery/mains distinction been irrelevant, `RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand::GetData` would have had no RX_MODE branch; it has one, and the branch is the only place the get-request frame is skipped.
contradicted.missingInput: The VirtualDevices read path (HMServer group/virtual-device stack) — not examined; the BidCos-RF findings do not transfer to it.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Contradicted, and I reproduced all three legs myself — but the audited report's own leg (c) is over-broad in the same way it accuses our comment of being.

Confirmed by my reading: (a) the failure mode is a hard fault, not a plausible default. HSSParamset::Get (:162-176) aborts on the first readable parameter whose GetValue fails and XmlRpcMethodGetParamset turns that into -1 "Failure" — there is no partial struct and no silently-substituted default. The DEFAULT fallback exists only behind `use_default_on_failure`, which in the shipped descriptors is 21 empty-string parameters. Our code's fallback path is `loader.GetParamset(..., ParamsetKeyValues)`, so this is the right surface. (b) There is no *_STATUS = NORMAL convention in the RF descriptors; the only ids are ACK_STATUS and LED_STATUS. (d) The firmware does carry the flag we are guessing at — `undefined`, true from construction (:28), cleared only in ProcessIncomingFrame (:355), exposed on the 3-argument getValue/getParamset (mode==1, :252-280). Reading it is the honest fix.

Overstated by the audited report: leg (c), "the suppression is not interface-shaped, it is RxNeedsWakeup-shaped, so mains BidCos-RF devices DO get queried". The RxNeedsWakeup gate at :166 is reached only after the guard at :152 — `if(get_request_frame.id.empty()) return GetStoredValue(...)`. Only 76 parameters across 21 of the 127 shipped RF device XMLs declare a `<get request="..."/>` frame at all. For every other BidCos-RF VALUES parameter no active query is issued regardless of RX_MODE; the read returns the stored value or fails. So the firmware's key is (declares a get frame) AND (RX_ALWAYS or already stored) — not RX_MODE alone. Our interface-wide skip is still wrong, but it is less wrong than the audited report implies, and a fix keyed purely on RX_MODE would be a second guess.

The VirtualDevices half stays ungrounded; the audited report says so and I did not close it either.

contradicted.challengeNote:
Upheld, and I checked the one thing that could have overturned it. Two of the four sets are wrong, both in the direction that sends a call the HmIP daemon refuses: InterfacesSupportingConfigRestore includes HmIP-RF and InterfacesSupportingTeams includes HmIP-RF, and all three of those methods answer with NotImplementedException. The comment's smoke-detector rationale for Teams does not survive — HmIP smoke-detector grouping goes through the HmIP group/virtual-device path, not the legacy team methods.

I verified both method tables line by line rather than trusting the summary; every cited line number was exact, and I confirmed the negative halves directly: rfd contains no searchDevices symbol at all (not just an unregistered class), and hs485d contains no team or config-restore symbol. I also checked ExtendedLegacyServiceHandler's full override list to make sure none of the six is rescued by the subclass, and found the same six throwing in HMServer as well as HMIPServer, so the result does not depend on which server serves a given legacy interface.

The one counter-signal I found, and why it does not overturn: OpenCCU patch 0151-WebUI-Add-DeviceRestoreConfigButton gates the new Restore Config button on `$EASYLINKMODE == "false"` only — it is NOT interface-gated. (The `if {($iface != $HmIPIdentifier) && ($iface != $HmIPWIdentifier)}` line in the same hunk is pre-existing context belonging to the firmware-update block, not the restore gate.) So the OpenCCU WebUI does offer restore-config on HmIP devices. That is a WebUI bug, not evidence of support: the call lands on HMIPServer's throwing method, and devconfig.cgi's own `cmd_restore_config` is written to `catch` the failure and render a "failed" page. The daemon is authority over the button.

contradicted.title: The callback mux answers an unknown CCU probe with the JSON-RPC code -32601 on an XML-RPC surface
contradicted.ourValue: "the CCU treats an absent signature as 'any types accepted' and never inspects the contents" (methodSignature), "the CCU only checks existence, not content" (methodHelp), and -32601 chosen "as the closest standardised codepoint" for a method-not-found probe
contradicted.firmwareValue: The CCU never calls system.methodSignature — the string does not occur anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base. It never calls system.methodHelp on a callback either. It calls system.listMethods exactly once, at callback registration, and inspects the result solely for the presence of "replaceDevice". No CCU code path reads a fault code returned by a callback.
contradicted.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:255 (XmlRpcCallSync("system.listMethods", …) inside PlatformInit — the sole caller in the tree), :256/:263-266 (result scanned only for methname.compare("replaceDevice")), :322 (supportReplaceDevice decides replaceDevice vs deleteDevices), :132-144 (XmlRpcCallSync tests only c.isFault() and logs result->toText(); the code number is never extracted); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:575 (parseResponse sets the boolean _isFault and parses the fault struct as a value, no faultCode branch); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServer.cpp:218-219, :271-277 (listMethods/methodHelp exist only as methods the CCU *offers*; no methodSignature at all). Tree-wide grep for "methodSignature" over ../OpenCCU-Base returns zero files. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyBackendClient exposes exactly event, listDevices, newDevices, deleteDevices, updateDevice, replaceDevice, readdedDevice, multicall and firmwareUpdateStatusChanged toward a registered callback — no system.* probe; and HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.InterfaceInitializer#handle registers an interface via DeviceUtil#synchronizedBackendDevices, which goes straight to listDevices, never to listMethods. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcParser does parse faultCode into an RpcRemoteException, but no caller in the legacy notification path branches on getFaultCode().
contradicted.finding: Both comment claims are contradicted, though the code itself is harmless. (1) -32601 is safe for the stated purpose but not for the stated reason: no CCU path compares a fault code from a callback. rfd/hs485d only test the boolean isFault() and log the fault struct's rendered text; the HmIP side parses faultCode into an exception object that the legacy path never inspects. Any code would do; -32601 is not "what the CCU expects", because the CCU expects nothing. (2) The methodSignature comment asserts a CCU behaviour that does not exist — the CCU never issues that call, on either the BidCos or the HmIP callback surface. Same for methodHelp: it is a method the CCU *implements* on its own surface, never one it calls on ours. (3) The one probe the CCU does make is the one the comments say nothing about, and it has a real consequence: HSSManager::PlatformInit calls system.listMethods on the callback URL during registration and scans the returned array for "replaceDevice"; a missing entry sets supportReplaceDevice=false, after which a replaced device arrives as deleteDevices + newDevices instead of replaceDevice. We do register "replaceDevice" (internal/central/rpcserver/xmlrpc_server.go:415), so this is currently correct — but it is the claim worth pinning, and it is load-bearing in a way -32601 is not. Note the answer must be an array: a fault or any non-array from listMethods silently yields supportReplaceDevice=false and registration continues regardless (HSSManager.cpp:258-270).
contradicted.negativeControl: Had the CCU probed methodSignature, the string would occur somewhere in the CCU sources — the tree-wide grep over ../OpenCCU-Base returns zero files, while the same grep for "system.listMethods" returns exactly two hits and one of them is a live caller. Had a fault code been inspected, XmlRpcCallSync or XmlRpcClient would extract result["faultCode"] and compare it; both only set/inspect a boolean. The check demonstrably distinguishes the two cases: it found the one probe that does exist and the one place the fault is examined, and both fell the other way from our comment.
contradicted.challengeNote:
Contradicted, upheld — and I extended the search past where the prior agent stopped, which strengthened rather than weakened it. Three checks I added:

(a) methodSignature. The prior claim was scoped to ../OpenCCU-Base. I grepped both HmIP server components as well: zero occurrences anywhere. The comment at mux.go:110-111 asserts a CCU behaviour that exists on no surface.

(b) methodHelp. Not merely "implemented, never called" — it IS called, by ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/tools/devconfig.cgi, but toward `$interfaces($iface)`, i.e. the interface daemon's own XML-RPC surface, not toward a registered callback. That is the wrong-surface trap this series keeps catching, and it lands on the prior finding's side: the call exists, it just is not on our path. The comment at mux.go:105 is still contradicted.

(c) A near-miss I chased and cleared: `RpcClient.listMethods()` exists as a client capability in both HmIP components (`new RpcRequest(method, "system.listMethods")`), and `IRegaServer` declares @RpcMethod("system.listMethods") and @RpcMethod("system.methodHelp") as a proxy toward ReGa. Neither is a callback probe: `grep -rn '\.listMethods()'` finds no invocation of the client method anywhere in either tree, and IRegaServer's target is ReGa, not us. Recording this so a later grep does not appear to overturn the finding.

The prior finding's positive claim also holds and is the one worth pinning: HSSManager::PlatformInit probes the callback URL with system.listMethods and scans the array for "replaceDevice"; a fault, a non-array, or a missing entry all silently yield supportReplaceDevice=false, after which a replaced device arrives as deleteDevices + newDevices. We register it (xmlrpc_server.go:415), so this is correct today and is load-bearing in a way -32601 is not.

One shape constraint the prior finding missed: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcParser reads the fault struct as `(Integer) errorStruct.get("faultCode")` with no null guard. The *value* is indeed never inspected — but the *member* must be present and integer-typed or the HmIP side throws while parsing our fault. Our faults always carry an int code, so this is a constraint on the struct shape, not on the number.

contradicted.title: Duty-cycle and transmission-pending recovery windows are ported constants, not measured against the CCU

contradicted.finding: The trigger mapping is contradicted on both codes, and the durations themselves are not derivable. -8: a CCU never rejects a value write with a duty-cycle fault. The only producer is the firmware-update path, gated by an instantaneous airtime-budget test (does the image fit in the remaining 450000-byte allowance with 20 % to spare). So RetryDutyCycleDelay = 40 s cannot fire on the write path its own doc comment describes ("when a CCU rejects a command with a duty-cycle / RF-throttle error"); against a real CCU it is reachable only from `updateFirmware`. -10: real, but HmIP-only (rfd and hs485d never emit it), and it does not mean "the CCU is busy for a moment" — it means the target device is not currently reachable and the command has been persisted as pending configuration for delivery when the device next talks to the access point. It is cleared by that event, so a fixed 5 s wait re-asks a question whose answer cannot have changed; with MaxAttempts = 3 the chain then gives up 10 s later while the CCU still intends to deliver the write. The duration questions themselves are not performable from any source I can read: rfd holds no duty-cycle recovery model at all (it reads a percentage out of the transceiver's HELLO frame and only re-notifies on band crossings), and the HmIP pending window is bounded by the device's own wake-up cycle, which no CCU source carries. contradicted.negativeControl: Had the firmware defined a recovery interval, `DutyCycleForUpdate` or `BidcosInterface::SetDutyCycle` would compute or wait on one; both only compare the instantaneous percentage, and the threshold map is consumed exclusively by `GetDutyCycleLowerBound`/`GetDutyCycleUpperBound` for change notification. contradicted.ourValue: 60 s TTL bounds the window in which an inbound callback still counts as the confirmation of a send
contradicted.firmwareValue: unbounded for a wake-on-radio device — the frame is queued until the device next transmits, with no expiry and a depth-10 queue that silently drops the oldest frame; the synchronous budgets are 1500/4500/12500 ms per BidCos frame (up to 2 tries) and 25 s per HmIP legacy call
contradicted.finding: The firmware places no upper bound on the confirmation latency at all for a wake-up device, so 60 s is a policy choice and the comment's framing of it as sufficient is unsupported. Concretely: for a device whose effective rx mode is WAKEUP, rfd's PutData stores the value in its own volatile store (which emits nothing — ValueStore::SetStoredValue only writes the map), queues the frame, and returns true, so putParamset/setValue answer success without transmitting. The queued frame goes out only when the device itself transmits (SendAfterWakeupFrames is called from the incoming-frame path). There is no timeout on that queue; the only bound is depth 10, and overflow drops the oldest frame with a warning — so the confirming VALUES callback can arrive minutes later or never. 46 of the ~130 shipped RF device types declare a wake-up-only rx mode (rx_modes="CONFIG,WAKEUP" x28, "CONFIG,WAKEUP,LAZY_CONFIG" x15), including rf_cc_tc.xml (HM-CC-TC, a thermostat users write setpoints to), rf_sec_mdir.xml, rf_sc.xml and rf_rhs.xml. Separately, the candidate's duty-cycle framing answers a different surface: RetryDutyCycleDelay = 40 s is our own wait, not a CCU-stated latency; the CCU's duty-cycle rejection is fault -8 and carries no delay. What the firmware does bound is only the synchronous case (1.5/4.5/12.5 s per BidCos frame with up to 2 tries; 25 s per HmIP legacy call), and those all fit inside 60 s comfortably — the TTL is adequate for every non-wake-up path and structurally cannot cover the wake-up path at any value.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had 60 s (or any fixed TTL) been firmware-supported, rfd would carry an expiry on the after-wakeup queue or a delivery deadline after which the queued frame is abandoned and an event or fault raised. It carries neither: the only bound in that code path is a queue depth, and overflow is logged as a dropped frame rather than reported to the caller.

Count correction: rftypes holds 127 XMLs, not ~130, and 45 of them name WAKEUP in an rx_modes attribute, of which 42 declare no BURST and no ALWAYS — so 42 wake-up-only device types, not 46, and the sub-counts are 28 ("CONFIG,WAKEUP") plus 14 ("CONFIG,WAKEUP,LAZY_CONFIG"), not 28 plus 15. Tier 2, the device's own declaration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-WRCD.json, channel VCU4243444:3 VALUES — DISPLAY_DATA_ID {TYPE INTEGER, MIN 1, MAX 5, DEFAULT 1, OPERATIONS 2}; DISPLAY_DATA_STRING {TYPE STRING, MIN "", MAX "[0x20-0x7E]{16}", DEFAULT "", OPERATIONS 2}
contradicted.finding: Our profile is scoped to exactly one device: internal/model/custom/profiles.go:1429-1438 registers IPTextDisplay for DeviceType "hmip-wrcd", channel 3. Within that scope maxDisplayID = 5 is right, and both tiers agree (the WRCD descriptor declares MIN 1 / MAX 5; the firmware's "five" variant is createDisplayDataIDParameter(1, 5)). Note it is right only in that scope — the same parameter is registered with (1,2) and (0,7) for other display channels, so the constant must not be lifted to a fleet-wide rule, and the honest source is the runtime descriptor's MIN/MAX rather than a literal. MaxRowLength = 24 is wrong by 8: firmware and descriptor both cap the row at 16 characters, and additionally restrict the alphabet to 0x20..0x7E (the default variant's converter is the ASCII one). Two consequences, both reaching the device: a 17..24-character row passes our validator and goes out in the put_paramset for the CCU to truncate or reject, and HA is told `max: 24` so operators are invited to type 8 characters that cannot arrive. Our comment cites "the HmIP-SDV* firmware limit" — no HmIP-SDV device appears in the pydevccu descriptor corpus, in ../openccu-data, or in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/, so that attribution is unsourced as well as numerically wrong. Also worth recording: the descriptor's MAX for a STRING parameter is a constraint regex, not a length, so any code that reads MAX numerically will read nothing usable — the 16 has to be parsed out of the regex or kept as a WRCD-scoped constant with this citation. Separately, the doc comment at textdisplay.go:519 ("Validation: ID must be >= 1") understates the code, which enforces an upper bound too.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had maxDisplayID been wrong, the WRCD descriptor would have declared a different pair — 1/2 or 0/7, the two other variants the firmware registers — and rows 3..5 (or row 0) would have been mis-gated; it declares 1/5. Had MaxRowLength = 24 been right, the declared MAX would read `{24}` or a numeric 24 in at least one of the four DISPLAY_DATA_STRING variants the firmware registers; none contains a 24, and the WRCD's own declaration reads `[0x20-0x7E]{16}`.
contradicted.challengeNote: UPHELD on the contradiction, with the consequence narrowed. Right surface established: internal/model/custom/profiles.go:1429-1438 registers IPTextDisplay for DeviceType "hmip-wrcd" channel 3 only, and the WRCD descriptor's channel :3 is exactly where both DISPLAY_DATA_ID and DISPLAY_DATA_STRING live — so the factory's default (non-utf8, non-bwth, non-wgd) variant is the one this profile writes. maxDisplayID = 5 is right and doubly sourced (firmware "five" variant = (1,5); descriptor MIN 1 / MAX 5); it must stay WRCD-scoped, since the same parameter is also registered (1,2) and (0,7). MaxRowLength = 24 is wrong by 8 in both tiers: 16, not 24. The "HmIP-SDV*" attribution in the comment is unsourced — no HmIP-SDV appears in ../pydevccu, ../openccu-data or ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/. THREE CORRECTIONS to the reader. (1) The reader's downstream claim "for the CCU to truncate or reject" is not sourced and I could not source it: the converter bound to this parameter is the no-arg AsciiStringToInteger, whose length field is 0, so #convertLogicalToPhysical allocates `temp.length + 1` bytes and truncates nothing, and I found no length or regex validation of STRING values on the legacy put_paramset path (DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue special-cases only the Unicode/WGD converters and METER_OBIS_SEARCH_STRING). What a 17..24-character row actually does at the device is therefore UNVERIFIED — say that rather than "truncate or reject". (2) The converter's charset is ISO_8859_1, so the 0x20..0x7E alphabet is a DECLARED constraint, not one the conversion enforces. (3) Our validator counts BYTES (`len(r.Text)`) while the declared limit counts characters; inside the declared alphabet these coincide, but a UTF-8 non-ASCII row would be measured wrongly by our check as well. What our code should follow here is the runtime descriptor (MIN/MAX read from the device), not a literal — the firmware's per-variant registration is precisely why a fleet-wide constant is unsafe.

contradicted.title: The com-test completion timestamp is parsed in the daemon's local zone although the CCU's zone is known
contradicted.ourValue: time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02 15:04:05", poll.Completed, time.Local) — the string is interpreted in the DAEMON's zone; the constant's comment attributes the layout to system.Date
contradicted.firmwareValue: The string is the CCU's local wall clock in the CCU's configured zone, carrying no offset; and it comes from LastTestCompletedTime(), not from system.Date. A zone-free Unix-seconds accessor for exactly this value exists: LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds()
contradicted.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/startpage.htm:179 `<% Write(system.Date("%H:%M")); %>` and :184 `Write(system.Date("%d.%m.%Y"))` — system.Date IS the operator-facing wall clock, so it renders CCU local time, not UTC | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/device/startcomtest.tcl:17-18 `Write(system.Date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")); device.DevStartComTest();` and www/api/methods/device/pollcomtest.tcl:19-21 `if (device.LastTestCompletedTime() >= timestamp) { Write(device.LastTestCompletedTime()); }` — the CCU's own Device.startComTest/pollComTest, the exact pattern our scripts reproduce, and it compares the two as STRINGS and never parses them | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:492-494 (LastTestCompletedTime() → TimeStampToString3) with ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/TimeStamp.fn:55-75, whose fixed offsets Substr(0,4)/(5,2)/(8,2)/(11,2)/(14,2)/(17,2) pin the layout to `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` and which renders it verbatim with no zone conversion | ../OpenCCU-Base/bin/{arm-linux-gnueabihf,aarch64-linux-gnu,x86_64-linux-gnu}/ReGaHss — the ReGa script method-name table lists `LastTestCompletedTime` immediately followed by `LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds`, and `DevStartComTest` on the next entry; siblings `LastDPActionTimeSeconds`, `LastTimestampSeconds`, `LastTriggerTimeSeconds`, `AlOccurrenceTimeSeconds`, `ProgramLastExecuteTimeSeconds` follow the same naming convention | our own get_alarm_messages.fn:62 already uses that convention (`oVar.LastTimestampSeconds()`)
contradicted.finding:
Contradicted on two counts.

Zone. `system.Date` is what the CCU prints as its own clock on the WebUI start page (`maintime`, `maindate`), so it renders the CCU's configured local time; there is no UTC path and no format string anywhere in the tree carries %z or an offset. LastTestCompletedTime() is the same wall-clock shape — TimeStamp.fn slices it at fixed offsets and prints the result unchanged, so the operator sees CCU local time. Our code hands that offset-free string to time.ParseInLocation with `time.Local`, which is the *daemon's* zone. A UTC container against a Europe/Berlin CCU therefore reports CompletedAt one or two hours off, and the sign of the error is such that CompletedAt can land *before* StartedAt (StartedAt is a real time.Now()). The rega package already has the correct input: BackendInfo.Timezone carries the CCU's IANA zone (runner.go:368-370), and runner.go:303-306 states the very convention this path breaks.

Surface. The comment at :135-137 attributes the layout to `system.Date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")` "for the start / completed timestamps". Only `started` is system.Date (start_com_test.fn:41). `completed` is `oDev.LastTestCompletedTime()` (poll_com_test.fn:42) — and `completed` is the only one the constant is ever used on, at :194. The layout happens to match, but it is grounded on the wrong accessor; TimeStamp.fn is the source that actually settles the layout of the value we parse.

And the firmware offers the clean way out. `LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds()` exists in ReGaHss's script API, sitting directly beside `LastTestCompletedTime` and `DevStartComTest` in the method-name table, and the repo already uses that naming convention for alarm timestamps. Switching poll_com_test.fn to it removes the parse and the zone question entirely. Note also that the CCU's own pollComTest never converts these strings to a time at all — it only string-compares them, which is exactly what our poll script does at poll_com_test.fn:43; the zone bug is purely on the Go side, in turning the reported string into an absolute instant.
contradicted.negativeControl: Had system.Date rendered UTC, the WebUI start page would be showing UTC as the CCU's clock to the operator, and TimeStamp.fn would have had to apply an offset before display — it applies none, and the check would have surfaced that as a conversion step in the Substr chain. Had no seconds accessor existed, the ReGaHss method-name table would list `LastTestCompletedTime` with no `…Seconds` sibling — which is exactly what the table shows for its neighbours `LastChangeValue`, `LastTriggerID` and `ValueMin`, so the extraction distinguishes presence from absence rather than matching every name. And had our code been right, :194 would have named a zone derived from BackendInfo.Timezone instead of time.Local; the literal `time.Local` is unambiguous in the source.
contradicted.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted on both counts, with one correction to the prior report's reasoning and one demotion of its proposed fix.

Surface, re-checked: the constant is referenced exactly once, at :194, and only on poll.Completed. poll_com_test.fn:42 reads `oDev.LastTestCompletedTime()`; system.Date appears only in start_com_test.fn:41, and `started` is never parsed. So the comment grounds the layout on an accessor that never produces the value the constant is used on. The layout is nevertheless correct, and the source that actually settles it is TimeStamp.fn:55-75: the WebUI slices LastTestCompletedTime() at fixed character offsets 0,4 / 5,2 / 8,2 / 11,2 / 14,2 / 17,2, which can only be `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. One correction to the prior report: TimeStampToString3 does NOT render the value verbatim — it emits only `HH:MM:SS`. What the source proves is the input layout and the absence of any zone conversion, which is what the claim needs; "verbatim" overstates it.

Zone, re-checked and strengthened: the ReGaHss binary carries the literal `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S` and, separately, a logging format `[%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z]`. eQ-3 attaches %Z where they want a zone and omit it here, and the binary links localtime/localtime_r rather than gmtime. Combined with system.Date being the operator clock on the start page and with the test date being rendered straight to the operator, the value is CCU-local wall clock with no offset. Note the contradiction does not even depend on "CCU-local": an offset-free string parsed in the daemon's zone is wrong for any CCU zone that is not the daemon's, and internal/client/rega/runner.go:303-306 already states that convention for the alarm path.

CORRECTION the prior report got wrong: it claims "a UTC container against a Europe/Berlin CCU therefore reports CompletedAt one or two hours off, and the sign of the error is such that CompletedAt can land before StartedAt". The sign is inverted for that example. CCU-local 14:30 CEST is the instant 12:30Z; parsed as UTC it becomes 14:30Z, i.e. roughly two hours in the FUTURE, so CompletedAt lands after StartedAt, not before. CompletedAt precedes StartedAt only in the opposite arrangement (daemon zone ahead of the CCU's — e.g. a Berlin daemon against a UTC CCU). The defect is real either way; the failure mode stated in the report is not the one the common deployment produces. DurationMs is computed from time.Since(startedAt) and is unaffected; the wrong instant is confined to CompletedAt, which is a public DTO field (`completed_at`, pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:781) and therefore reaches REST and WS clients as an RFC3339 stamp with the daemon's offset.

DEMOTION of the proposed fix: `LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds` is proven to EXIST as a symbol, adjacent to two methods that are proven callable (LastTestCompletedTime at system.fn:492, DevStartComTest at startcomtest.tcl:18), on all four shipped architectures; and the *Seconds convention is proven real by four siblings actually invoked in firmware ReGa (system.fn:1222,1227,1232; pda/eq3/program.tcl:8) plus a ReGaHss runtime error message that names LastTimestampSeconds() and LastDPActionTimeSeconds() with call parentheses. But no firmware call site for LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds exists anywhere in www/ or src/webui/. That it is callable and returns Unix seconds is inference from adjacency and naming, not read from a call site — exactly the shape of assumption this audit exists to catch. It is a well-supported hypothesis and the right thing to try, but it must be probed against a live CCU (a read; no write, no approval needed) before poll_com_test.fn is switched to it. The zone-independent fallback that needs no new accessor is to parse with the zone from BackendInfo.Timezone (runner.go:368-370) instead of time.Local.

reachesDevice.title: The door-lock action LEVEL values, including the out-of-range 1.01 'open', rest on nothing
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.CalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createLevelParameter — ConfigurationParameter(LogicalType.FLOAT, PhysicalType.INTEGER, RW, DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0), list, listIndex, 0, 1 /*byte*/, 0, default 0.0, min 0.0, max 1.01). Same factory's #create16BitLevelParameter is identical but 2 bytes with DoubleToInteger(50000.0,0.0) and the same max 1.01. Callers: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.SwitchCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createWeekProfile builds NN_WP_LEVEL / NN_WP_DURATION_BASE / NN_WP_DURATION_FACTOR over lists 12..14 × 25 entries (#getMaxPeriods = 75); BlindCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createWeekProfile builds NN_WP_LEVEL_2 from the same #createLevelParameter. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.DoubleToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical: `d *= factor; d += offset; d = d>=0 ? d+0.5 : d-0.5; (int)d`. Duration encoding: #createTimeFactor declares min 0 / max 31 / default 31; #createTimeBase is a StringEnumToInteger over de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.LinkTimeBase = {BASE_100_MS, BASE_1_S, BASE_5_S, BASE_10_S, BASE_1_M, BASE_5_M, BASE_10_M, BASE_1_H} — index 7 = BASE_1_H. Lock physical scale: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLockTargetLevelParameter declares LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL {LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN} = {0, 200, 255}, and LOCK_STATE {UNKNOWN, LOCKED, UNLOCKED} = {255, 0, 200}. Channel type: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.ChannelType declares SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE(48) and no door-lock week-profile type, matching internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:570-577. Witness (Tier 3): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/schedule_models.py:293-298 carries the same four triplets and names the 1.01 case AUTORELOCK_END, not "open".
reachesDevice.finding: The numbers are right; the label attached to 1.01 is not, and the neighbouring Level2 bound is one ulp too tight. (1) 1.01 IS a legal LEVEL — it is exactly the declared MAX of every calendar WP_LEVEL parameter, so simple.go:200's `e.Level > 1.01` bound reproduces the firmware maximum verbatim rather than admitting an out-of-range value. (2) 0.0 → physical 0 and 1.0 → physical 200 under DoubleToInteger(200,0); on a door lock those are exactly the declared LOCKED and UNLOCKED codes of LOCK_STATE / LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL, so the locked/unlocked mapping is grounded. (3) The 'open / latch release' reading of 1.01 is NOT supported: 1.01×200+0.5 → physical 202, whereas the firmware's OPEN sentinel is 255 (logical 1.275, above the WP_LEVEL max and unreachable through this parameter). Our code does not in fact claim 'open' on the wire — LockActionOpen's string value is "autorelock_end" (simple.go:98), matching the Python witness; only the Go identifier and the reader's summary say 'open'. What the device does with WP_LEVEL=202 is decided by the lock's own firmware, which is not in any tree here — that part stays unverified. (4) CONTRADICTION on the same site: simple.go:202 rejects Level2 > 1.0, but WP_LEVEL_2 is created by the identical #createLevelParameter with max 1.01. A CCU-reported cover slot at LEVEL_2=1.01 fails our validator on a read→validate→write round-trip. (5) Corroborated in passing: durBase 7 = BASE_1_H and durFactor 31 = the declared factor max/default; our comment calling 31 a "sentinel 'always'" is our interpretation, the firmware declares it only as the maximum.
reachesDevice.ourValue: Level bound 0..1.01; Level2 bound 0..1.0; 1.01 identified as 'open'/latch release
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: WP_LEVEL and WP_LEVEL_2 both FLOAT min 0.0 / default 0.0 / max 1.01, DoubleToInteger(200.0,0.0), 1 byte; LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL OPEN = 255, not 202
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the calendar level max been 1.0, #createLevelParameter's last argument would read 1.0 and our validator would be admitting an out-of-range level; it reads 1.01. Had 1.01 been the OPEN sentinel, #createLockTargetLevelParameter would map OPEN to 202 rather than 255. Had the Level2 bound matched, Blind…#createWeekProfile would have used a different factory for WP_LEVEL_2; it calls the same one. Had durBase 7 not been one hour, LinkTimeBase[7] would be something other than BASE_1_H.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: All four triplets are CONFIRMED character-for-character against the CCU's own editor, which is a stronger result than the previous pass reached — but two of its reasoning steps are broken and one boundary was missed. (1) CONFIRMED: our LockActionTable is the firmware's table. AutoRelockStart(0,0,0)="Lock + Auto Relock start", AutoRelockEnd(0,7,31)="Lock + Auto Relock end", Unlock(1.0,7,31)="Unlock + Auto Relock end", Open(1.01,7,31)="Auto Relock end". Our string values match the labels one-to-one, including "autorelock_end" for the 1.01 slot. (2) CONTRADICTED — the Go identifier LockActionOpen is wrong: 1.01 is "Auto Relock end", not open/latch release. The previous pass reached the same conclusion by the wrong route. (3) CONTRADICTED — its supporting argument, that 0.0→physical 0 and 1.0→physical 200 'are exactly the declared LOCKED and UNLOCKED codes of LOCK_STATE / LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL, so the locked/unlocked mapping is grounded', is a cross-surface inference between a calendar CONFIG parameter and a STATE parameter, and it does not survive: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLockTargetLevelParameter declares TWO variants — non-dlp {LOCKED,UNLOCKED,OPEN}={0,200,255} and dlp {LOCKED,UNLOCKED,OPEN,…}={0,1,2,…}. So 'the firmware's OPEN sentinel is 255' is the DLD reading only; on HmIP-DLP it is 2, and the 0/200 coincidence the argument leans on vanishes. The locked/unlocked mapping is grounded — by setDoorLockActionValues, not by LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL. (4) CONFIRMED: 1.01 is the declared MAX of every calendar WP_LEVEL (Tier 1 factory + 3858 Tier-2 declarations, all MAX 1.01), so simple.go:200's `Level > 1.01` reproduces the firmware maximum. (5) CONFIRMED CONTRADICTION at simple.go:202-204: `*e.Level2 > 1` rejects a value the firmware declares legal — WP_LEVEL_2 max is 1.01 on Tier 1 and on all 513 Tier-2 declarations, and internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:844-845 writes Level2 to `<NN>_WP_LEVEL_2`, so it is the same parameter. A cover slot read at LEVEL_2 = 1.01 fails our own validator on a read→validate→write round-trip. (6) NEW NARROWING the previous pass missed: the four-action table is the HmIP-DLD family ONLY (isDoorLockDrive at :317 = HmIP-DLD/-A/-S). HmIP-DLP uses a different editor — HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1899 `_getDLPModeSelector`, which offers THREE modes (PERMISSION, DOOR_LOCK, AUTO_RELOCK, distinguished by which of PERMISSION_TRANSCEIVER / DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER / AUTO_RELOCK_TRANSCEIVER is the target channel, mode remembered in device metadata `wpMode_<n>`) and writes WP_LEVEL only 0 or 1. Our model has two LockModes and no auto_relock, and internal/model/schedule/lock.go:76-83 DetectLockMode keys solely on a target channel starting "1_" — so on a DLP every AUTO_RELOCK slot is mislabelled, and (0,7,31) is reported as lock_autorelock_end whether it means lock, permission-denied or auto-relock-off. (7) Corrected in passing: #createTimeFactor's default is the caller's argument; 31 is its declared MAX, and the switch factory happens to pass 31. Calling 31 a 'sentinel always' remains our interpretation. (8) Unverified and unchanged: what the lock's own firmware does with physical WP_LEVEL 202 is not in any readable tree.

reachesDevice.title: The whole profile catalogue — base channels and field offsets — carries no per-entry source citation
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/custom/profiles.go:127-163 (elv-sh-*), :1234 (hmip-scth230 IPDimmer ch 12), :1360-1398 (hmip-wgt: IPThermostat ch 8 / IPDimmer ch 2 / IPButtonLock ch 0 / IPSwitch ch 4), :1440-1444 (hmip-wsm IPIrrigationValve ch 4); internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:215-231 (IPIrrigationValve offsets -1/-2), :506-521 (IPThermostat offsets -5/0/7/8); resolution semantics in internal/model/custom/field_resolve.go:33-61 and profile_schema.go:108-157 (ChannelFields keys are relative offsets from the base channel, FixedChannelFields absolute)
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 2, ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json + ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json, read as (channel INDEX, TYPE, declared VALUES/MASTER parameter names): HmIP-WGTC — ch0 MAINTENANCE (MASTER declares GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK), ch2 BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER (VALUES declares LEVEL), ch3 SWITCH_TRANSMITTER (VALUES declares STATE), ch4/5/6 SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (VALUES declares STATE), ch8 HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER (VALUES declares SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE, ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE, HUMIDITY, CONCENTRATION). HmIP-SCTH230 — ch11 DIMMER_TRANSMITTER, ch12/13/14 DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (VALUES declares LEVEL, RAMP_TIME, ON_TIME). ELV-SH-WSM — ch2 FLOW_METER_TRANSMITTER (VALUES declares WATER_FLOW, WATER_VOLUME, WATER_VOLUME_SINCE_OPEN), ch3 WATER_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER (VALUES declares STATE), ch4/5/6 WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (VALUES declares STATE). HmIP-BWTH — ch1 HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER, ch8 CLIMATECONTROL_FLOOR_DIRECT_TRANSMITTER (MASTER declares HEATING_VALVE_TYPE, VALUES declares STATE), ch9 SWITCH_TRANSMITTER (VALUES declares STATE). reachesDevice.firmwareValue: Tier 1 does not carry these. Tier 2 gives, per model: WGTC climate=8, backlight dimmer=8? no — backlight LEVEL=2, first switch receiver=4, maintenance=0; SCTH230 first dimmer receiver=12; WSM water receiver=4, flow meter=2, water transmitter=3; BS2 switch receivers=4 and 8; SW1-BAT switch receiver=3; BWTH climate=1, floor-direct=8, switch transmitter=9; eTRV-2 climate=1.
reachesDevice.ourValue: hmip-wgt: IPThermostat ch 8, IPDimmer ch 2, IPSwitch ch 4, IPButtonLock ch 0. hmip-scth230: IPDimmer ch 12. elv-sh-wsm / hmip-wsm: IPIrrigationValve ch 4, ChannelFields -1 (GroupState←STATE), AdditionalDataPoints -2 (WATER_FLOW, WATER_VOLUME, WATER_VOLUME_SINCE_OPEN). elv-sh-bs2: IPSwitch ch 4 and 8. elv-sh-sw1-bat: IPSwitch ch 3. IPThermostat ChannelFields -5 (State←STATE), 0 (Concentration←CONCENTRATION, Level←LEVEL), 7 (HeatingValveType←HEATING_VALVE_TYPE), 8 (State←STATE).
reachesDevice.finding: Every entry the bundle named as high-exposure lands on a channel that declares the parameter it maps, and the unusual-looking numbers are the descriptor's, not a convention. HmIP-WGTC really is climate-on-8 / dimmer-on-2 / switch-on-4: ch2 is BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER (it declares LEVEL, so the 'dimmer' is the display backlight — it binds, whatever one thinks of the presentation), ch4 is the first SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, ch8 is the HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER. IPButtonLock on ch 0 binds because GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK is a MASTER parameter of the MAINTENANCE channel, not a VALUES one. HmIP-SCTH230 ch12 is the first DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (ch11 is the transmitter). ELV-SH-WSM ch4 is the first WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER; offset -2 lands on ch2 FLOW_METER_TRANSMITTER, which declares exactly the three water parameters the config lists, and offset -1 lands on ch3 WATER_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER, which declares STATE. The IPThermostat offset table resolves per base channel and each offset is correct for the family it was written for: from base 1 (BWTH) offset 7 → ch8 which carries HEATING_VALVE_TYPE in MASTER, offset 8 → ch9 SWITCH_TRANSMITTER which carries STATE; from base 8 (WGTC) offset -5 → ch3 SWITCH_TRANSMITTER which carries STATE, offset 0 → the climate channel which carries CONCENTRATION. The offsets that are dead for the other family (-5 from base 1 is a negative channel; +8 from base 8 is CLIMATECONTROL_HEAT_DEMAND_PUMP_TRANSMITTER with an empty VALUES set) resolve to nothing and cost nothing. Where the boundary runs: (a) elv-sh-psmci ch 3 — no descriptor for ELV-SH-PSMCI exists in ../pydevccu or ../openccu-data, so that single entry is unverified; (b) the audit covered the nine named entries, not the catalogue, so 'the catalogue carries no citation' remains true as a process statement even though every entry I could measure is right; (c) Tier 1 is structurally silent for HmIP channel layouts (see notes), so the source our code should follow for these is the runtime descriptor, which is what it already reads — extending profiles.go with per-entry Tier-1 citations is not possible for the HmIP half of the catalogue.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had a base channel or offset been wrong, the descriptor lookup would have named a channel whose declared parameter set does not contain the mapped parameter — and it did produce exactly that result in the dead-offset cases (offset +8 from base 8 lands on CLIMATECONTROL_HEAT_DEMAND_PUMP_TRANSMITTER with an empty VALUES set; offset -5 from base 1 is a negative index). The check therefore demonstrably distinguishes a binding channel from a non-binding one on this very data, and did not return 'binds' uniformly.
reachesDevice.missingInput: A device description for ELV-SH-PSMCI — absent from ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/ and from ../openccu-data — leaves profiles.go:135-143 (IPSwitch, elv-sh-psmci, channel 3) unmeasurable from any available source.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Every entry I could measure reproduces exactly — WGTC climate-on-8 / backlight-dimmer-on-2 / first switch-on-4 / GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK as a MASTER parameter of ch0, SCTH230 ch12, WSM ch4 with -1→ch3 STATE and -2→ch2 carrying exactly those three water parameters, BS2 4+8, SW1-BAT 3. Two corrections to the bundle.

(1) WRONG SURFACE — a second unverified entry the bundle missed. It grounded `hmip-wsm` on ELV-SH-WSM.json and wrote them as one line ("elv-sh-wsm / hmip-wsm"). They are two independent registrations (profiles.go:1439 and the elv-sh-wsm entry), and registry matching is exact-then-longest-prefix (registry.go:383-385, :416, :426-442), so "hmip-wsm" never matches an ELV-SH-* model. There is NO HmIP-WSM descriptor in ../pydevccu, none in ../openccu-data, and HmIP channel layouts are not in OpenCCU-Base rftypes. So hmip-wsm ch4 and its -1/-2 offsets are unverified on the same footing as elv-sh-psmci, which the bundle did name. The transfer rests on "the ELV and HmIP brand twins carry the same channel layout" — a convention read from nowhere. Two unverified entries, not one.

(2) A DEAD OFFSET THE BUNDLE DID NOT NAME, and it costs a field. IPThermostat ChannelFields offset 7 → HeatingValveType. From base 1 (BWTH) it lands on ch8 FLOOR_DIRECT whose MASTER declares HEATING_VALVE_TYPE — correct. From base 8 (WGTC) it lands on ch15 HEAT_DEMAND_BOILER, whose MASTER declares four parameters and not HEATING_VALVE_TYPE. WGTC carries HEATING_VALVE_TYPE on ch14, i.e. offset 6. So the field is silently unbound on WGTC even though the device declares it. The bundle listed only -5-from-base-1 and +8-from-base-8 as the dead offsets and concluded the table "is correct for the family it was written for"; it is correct for BWTH and one offset short for WGTC.

Worth recording alongside: the shared FieldState entries at -5 and 8 resolve per family only because resolveChannelKeyedField walks ascending and takes the first hit (field_resolve.go:66-70). On WGTC -5→ch3 (STATE) wins before 8→ch16 is consulted; on BWTH -5→ch-4 misses and 8→ch9 (STATE) binds. The two entries carry different visibility (Bare at -5, Visible at 8), so the same field ships hidden on WGTC and visible on BWTH — a consequence of map ordering, not of any device property.

The process statement in the title stands unchanged: the catalogue carries no per-entry citation, and for the HmIP half Tier 1 is structurally silent, so the runtime descriptor is the right source and it is what the code already reads.

reachesDevice.title: HmIP COMBINED_PARAMETER string shape and slot order are pinned only by an in-package test
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/custom/cover/blind.go:299-302 (the comment) and :350-355 (`fmt.Sprintf("L2=%d,L=%d", int(wireT*100+0.5), int(wireL*100+0.5))`), reached from :249, :269 and :412; internal/model/custom/cover/init.go:334-351 (IPHdm is also BlindKindIP)
