reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#setValue (routes a COMBINED_PARAMETER write into #convertCombinedParameter and then #putParameterSet on VALUES), #convertCombinedParameter (the parse), #validateAndConvertValues, #addSpecialCommaSeparatedParameter (declares COMBINED_PARAMETER as a write-only STRING in VALUES), #getParamsetDescription (the channel-type set that gets it). Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-FBL.json — ch4/5/6 BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER VALUES declares COMBINED_PARAMETER (TYPE STRING, OPERATIONS 2 = write-only) alongside LEVEL and LEVEL_2 (TYPE FLOAT, MIN 0.0, MAX 1.01); ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-DRBLI4.json — same on ch10/11/12, ch14-16, ch18-20, ch22-24; ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-HDM1.json — ch1 SHADING_RECEIVER VALUES declares LEVEL and LEVEL_2 but NOT COMBINED_PARAMETER. Secondary, and on a different surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/webui/js/dialog/blindCombinedParamDialog.js:100-112 builds the LINK-paramset value as `result = "L="+valL+",L2="+valL2` and :88-91 parses it back positionally.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: #convertCombinedParameter splits the string on ',' then each token on '='; `"L"` → key LEVEL, value Double.parseDouble(v)/100.0; `"L2"` → key LEVEL_2, value Double.parseDouble(v)/100.0. Each pair is put into an RpcStruct (a map) which is then handed to putParameterSet on VALUES, so token order carries no meaning. An unrecognised token hits the switch default, is logged at debug and skipped — no fault. COMBINED_PARAMETER is added to a channel's VALUES paramset only for the channel types enumerated in #getParamsetDescription: SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (except on BWTH devices), BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, OPTICAL_SIGNAL_RECEIVER, SERVO_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, WINDOW_DRIVE_RECEIVER, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER, BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER, WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, WEATHER_DISPLAY_RECEIVER (plus the week-program and identification-mode cases). SHADING_RECEIVER is absent from that set.
reachesDevice.ourValue: `"L2=<tilt_pct>,L=<level_pct>"`, both integer percents produced by int(v*100+0.5) after clamping v to [0,1]; written on hmenum.ParameterCombinedParameter for every BlindKindIP device including IPHdm.
reachesDevice.finding: The tokens, the scale and the acceptance are right: L is LEVEL, L2 is LEVEL_2, the CCU divides by 100 so integer 0..100 is exactly the percent form it wants, and it parses with Double.parseDouble so our integers are a strict subset of what it accepts. The claim in the comment that 'tilt slot first' matters is not a device property — the parse builds a map, so order is irrelevant, and the CCU's own WebUI emits the opposite order on the LINK surface. That is harmless for us but it means TestBlindIPCombinedFormat pins a choice, not a contract, and a future reordering would be safe. Where the boundary runs, and this one bites: COMBINED_PARAMETER is only ever added to VALUES for a fixed set of channel types, and SHADING_RECEIVER is not in it. HmIP-HDM1's ch1 is SHADING_RECEIVER, the descriptor confirms its VALUES has LEVEL and LEVEL_2 but no COMBINED_PARAMETER, and init.go:348 builds IPHdm as BlindKindIP — so every combined position/tilt write on an HmIP-HDM targets a parameter that channel does not declare. The firmware has a purpose-built path for that channel instead: on SHADING_RECEIVER a plain setValue of LEVEL_2 auto-fills LEVEL with 1.01 (the NO_MODIFICATION special value) and sends both together, i.e. the per-parameter write already does what the combined write does elsewhere. Two smaller notes. The percent ceiling is not 100: LEVEL/LEVEL_2 are declared MAX 1.01, and the WebUI's own dialog offers 100.5 (last value) and 101 (ignore), which after /100.0 are the two special values — we clamp to [0,1] and never reach them, which is correct for a position command but means 'both values are integer 0..100' describes our range, not the parameter's. And the WebUI's LINK-paramset dialog does parse positionally (arElmValues[0] is read as L), so order does matter on that surface — a reason not to reuse this string shape for a LINK write without rechecking.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the token mapping been reversed, #convertCombinedParameter's switch would have shown `case "L": key = "LEVEL_2"` — the mapping is a literal switch on the token string, read directly, not inferred from position. And the check did produce a different answer where the rule does not hold: the same method's channel-type enumeration excludes SHADING_RECEIVER and the HmIP-HDM1 descriptor lacks the parameter, so the procedure returned 'not accepted here' for one of the five models in scope rather than confirming uniformly. Caveat on the channel-type set: in the readable form of #getParamsetDescription the assignments inside that switch are not recoverable (each case body reduces to a dead local), so what I read is the set of channel types the switch considers, not the boolean each sets. SHADING_RECEIVER appears nowhere in that switch, and Tier 2 agrees independently, which is why I state the exclusion; the positive membership of the listed types rests on the enumeration plus the descriptors.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD on the shape: L→LEVEL, L2→LEVEL_2, both divided by 100.0, parsed with Double.parseDouble so our integers are a strict subset, unknown tokens skipped without a fault. UPHELD that order is irrelevant on this surface (the parse builds a map) — so the comment's "tilt slot first" and TestBlindIPCombinedFormat pin a choice, not a contract. UPHELD that the CCU's own WebUI parses positionally on the LINK surface, so this string shape must not be reused there without rechecking.

THE BUNDLE'S HEADLINE BOUNDARY IS CONTRADICTED. It concluded "this one bites" — that every combined write on an HmIP-HDM targets a parameter the channel does not declare. The write reaches the device anyway. #setValue tests `DEVICE_STATE_COMBINED_PARAMETER.equals(valueKey)` and branches into convertCombinedParameter + putParameterSet("VALUES", …) BEFORE any lookup of the channel's parameter set; the only declaration check downstream is #validateAndConvertValues, which sees the decomposed keys LEVEL and LEVEL_2 — both declared on SHADING_RECEIVER per HmIP-HDM1.json — so it passes and the pair is dispatched as a normal DEVICE_VALUE_SET. What HDM misses relative to a BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER is only routing: #checkBlindLevel returns false for any channelType != BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, so the write skips the QUEUE_LEGACY_BLIND_LEVEL_CORRECTION path. And the SHADING auto-fill of LEVEL=1.01 that the bundle cited lives in #checkRequiredValues, which is reached only from the single-parameter setValue branch, never from the combined branch — and our combined write names both axes, so it would be a no-op regardless.

So the real boundary is narrower and different: the gap is in the DESCRIPTOR, not the firmware. getParamsetDescription omits COMBINED_PARAMETER for SHADING_RECEIVER, so any client or proxy that validates a write against the published paramset description will reject it on HDM ch1 — the CCU itself accepts it. The bundle's smaller notes stand: LEVEL/LEVEL_2 are declared MAX 1.01 and the WebUI offers 100.5/101 as the two special values, so "integer 0..100" describes our clamp, not the parameter's range.

One caveat on the channel-type set: the enumeration is readable and matches, but the boolean that drives it did not survive into readable form (the branches assign dead locals), so "SHADING_RECEIVER is absent from the set" is read from the switch's case labels, and the Tier-2 descriptor independently agrees.

reachesDevice.title: IP lock LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL is written as ENUM label strings, and the 'OPEN = 2' index claim is a bare comment
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/custom/lock/lock.go:519-535 (the comment and the three constants) and :537-556 (Lock.sendIP writes the label on hmenum.ParameterLockTargetLevel); internal/model/custom/lock/init.go:18
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLockTargetLevelParameter (the enum strings and their device values, and the WRITE-only IOOperations); de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (publishes VALUE_LIST as the converter's enum strings, so the labels a client sees are these); de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical (matches the label, falls back to byte 0 on no match) and #convertPhysicalToLogical; de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue (the label/ordinal handling, gated on the Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal service property); de.eq3.cbcs.server.local.LocalServer and de.eq3.ccu.server.ip.HMIPServer read that property with default false. Tier 1 on the operator surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/door_opener.fn:202-204 (DOOR_LOCK_STATE_TRANSMITTER: `setDpState(<LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL>, 0)` labelled ${lblLock}, `, 1)` ${lblUnlock}, `, 2)` ${lblOpen}), :386-388 (DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER, identical 0/1/2), :381 (the retired option list, in order: LOCKED,UNLOCKED,OPEN,RESET_TEACH_IN,…).
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL is a WRITE-only ENUM with PhysicalType INTEGER. Non-DLP (HmIP-DLD) variant: enum strings {LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN} with device values {0, 200, 255}. DLP variant: {LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN, TEACH_IN_DRIVE_OPEN_DOOR_NEUTRAL_UNLOCKED, TEACH_IN_DRIVE_OPEN_DOOR_NEUTRAL_VERTICAL, TEACH_IN_DRIVE_OPEN_DOOR_NEUTRAL_HORIZONTAL, LOAD_CALIBRATION_OPEN_DOOR} with device values {0, 1, 2, 20, 21, 22, 33}. In both variants the first three labels are LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN at list positions 0, 1, 2, and the published VALUE_LIST is exactly that string array. The WebUI drives the same parameter with the ReGa ordinals 0/1/2 under the labels Lock/Unlock/Open.
reachesDevice.ourValue: The strings "LOCKED", "UNLOCKED", "OPEN" written on LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL, and the comment 'IP locks support open (LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL=2)'.
reachesDevice.finding: The three labels are exactly the declared VALUE_LIST, and OPEN really is at position 2 in both device variants, so the write and the '=2' note are both right. The comment's justification is the part that does not survive: 'The CCU XML-RPC interface accepts both integer indices and string labels for ENUM parameters' is false for this surface in its default configuration. The label/ordinal translation in #convertParameterValue is gated on the service property Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal, whose default is false in both server entry points; with it false an inbound integer is passed through unconverted to StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical, which compares the value against each enum string, finds no match, and returns byte 0 — the LOCKED device value. So sending the index 2 would not open the latch, it would lock the door, silently and without a fault. String labels work in both configurations (with the flag on, an inbound String falls through every branch untouched; with it off, nothing is applied and the converter matches it). Our choice is the correct and the safe one; the reasoning written next to it inverts which form is robust. Two boundaries worth recording. (a) The same silent-zero fallback means any future typo or a label from the wrong variant degrades to LOCKED rather than to an error — the failure mode of this write is actuation, not rejection. (b) The device values behind the labels differ between the two variants (UNLOCKED is 200 on DLD, 1 on DLP; OPEN is 255 vs 2), which is exactly why the label form is the portable one and why spelling the HA discovery payload as positional indices, as the comment at lock.go:527-534 says it deliberately did not, would have been fragile.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had OPEN sat at a different position, or had the labels been spelled differently, #createLockTargetLevelParameter would have shown a different literal String[] — the array is read directly and its element order is the VALUE_LIST order that #addDesriptionOfParameter publishes, so this is not an ordering inferred from anything. The two variants provide a live control: the procedure did return different device values for the same labels (200/255 vs 1/2), so it distinguishes cases rather than reporting agreement uniformly. And the ReGa control page, an independent Tier-1 surface, drives the same parameter with 0/1/2 under Lock/Unlock/Open, which would have disagreed with the array had the positions been otherwise.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The core rule is UPHELD and re-read verbatim: the three labels are exactly the declared enumStrings, and OPEN sits at list position 2 in both device variants. The write is correct.

BUT THE BUNDLE'S CENTRAL CORRECTION IS ITSELF CONTRADICTED, on Tier 1. It claimed the comment's "accepts both integer indices and string labels" is false, that the flag defaults to false, and — its strongest sentence — that "sending the index 2 would not open the latch, it would lock the door, silently and without a fault." That reads the CODE default and stops there. The distribution overrides it. crRFD.conf:47 sets Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true, and S62HMServer:15-17 launches de.eq3.ccu.server.ip.HMIPServer with /var/etc/crRFD.conf, generated from that template with three sed lines that do not touch the flag. crRFD is the HmIP-RF interface our client writes on (the WebUI's own Interface.*Metadata_crRFD calls pass "interface":"HmIP-RF"). So on a real OpenCCU the flag is TRUE, and with it true #convertParameterValue takes the `!out && value instanceof Number` branch and maps an inbound ordinal to values[n] — the label — before it ever reaches StringEnumToInteger. Both forms work; the comment is right as written.

A second, independent Tier-1 witness on the operator surface says the same thing: door_opener.fn:202-204 and :386-388 drive LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL with the bare integers 0/1/2 via setDpState. The CCU's own lock UI uses the index form. If index writes silently locked the door, the WebUI's Open button would lock it.

What SURVIVES from the bundle, and what I add:
(a) The silent-zero fallback is real and verified verbatim — StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical initialises `byte[] b = new byte[]{0}` and returns it unchanged when nothing matches. So an unmatched value degrades to the LOCKED device value; the failure mode of this write is actuation, not rejection. That is a genuine reason to prefer the label form, and it is the honest version of the bundle's point.
(b) NEW, and the real narrowing: with the flag true, the integer form is the ORDINAL into enumStrings, not the device value. On the non-DLP variant the device values are {0, 200, 255}, so the ordinal 2 means OPEN → device 255. The init.go comment "IP locks support open (LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL=2)" is therefore correct only as a list position, and coincides with the device value only on DLP. Anyone reading it as a wire value would be wrong on every HmIP-DLD.
(c) Which variant a given device gets is selected by a ParameterMapKey qualifier ("dlp"); I could not resolve that per device type from the readable material, so the device-value half of the mapping stays unverified per device — which is exactly why writing labels rather than numbers is the right call.

reachesDevice.title: FixedColorLight.Color() decodes the COLOR descriptor index as a FixedColor ordinal
reachesDevice.ourValue: FixedColor ordinal BLACK=0, RED=1, GREEN=2, YELLOW=3, BLUE=4, PURPLE=5, TURQUOISE=6, WHITE=7 (color.go:451-458), applied to the raw descriptor index by Color() at color.go:581
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: COLOR index order BLACK=0, BLUE=1, GREEN=2, TURQUOISE=3, RED=4, PURPLE=5, YELLOW=6, WHITE=7
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColor (enum constants BLACK(0), BLUE(1), GREEN(2), TURQUOISE(3), RED(4), PURPLE(5), YELLOW(6), WHITE(7)); the COLOR StateParameter is built from it via HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createColorSelectionParameter, whose VALUE_LIST is SimpleRGBColor#getNames(false); the same first-eight order via HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColorOpticalSignal#getNames. Independently, Tier 1 WebUI: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/opticalsignalreceiver.fn:64-65 and :72-78 (`! string listColor = "black\tblue\tgreen\tturquoise\tred\tpurple\tyellow\twhite"`, then `<option value=#loop#>` for loop=0..7 with `setDpState(oColor.ID(), this.value)` and read-back `jQuery(...).val(#oColor.Value()#)`), ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/dimmer.fn:179, and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/getColorElement.tcl:10-17 (options(0)=BLACK … options(7)=WHITE).
reachesDevice.finding:
The firmware's COLOR ordinal is the RGB bit pattern (bit0=blue, bit1=green, bit2=red), not the order FixedColor enumerates. Four of eight slots differ: index 1 is BLUE (we say RED), index 3 is TURQUOISE (we say YELLOW), index 4 is RED (we say BLUE), index 6 is YELLOW (we say TURQUOISE). BLACK/GREEN/PURPLE/WHITE coincide by accident.

The ordinal is what actually arrives on the wire. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue replaces an ENUM's logical label with its index in VALUE_LIST when the flag replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal is set, and the CCU's shipped HmIP config sets it: ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true`. So every COLOR event and getValue on HmIP-BSL / HmIP-MP3P ch2-5 / HmIPW-WGC delivers the RGB-bit index, and generic.Select.Value() hands it to Color() verbatim.

Consequences on our side: ColorName(), the MQTT fixed_color field and ChannelHsColor's index leg all mislabel four of eight colours; ChannelHsColor's sibling read via custom.EnumLabelValue (label-driven) disagrees with Color(); and SoundPlayerLED writes `colorLabel := fixedColorNames[color]` (sound_led.go:337) into the put_paramset, so a mis-decoded slot is written back to the device. SetColor's optimistic `l.color.OnEvent(int32(c))` (color.go:606) also stores our ordinal, which is not the one the CCU will echo.

The write path is correct and its comment (color.go:610-613) is exactly right: a label write is accepted. Only the read path substitutes the convention.

Scope note: the `RfDimmer_Color_Fixed` profile also routes through newFixedColorConstructor for DeviceType `hbw-lc-rgbww-in6-dr` (profiles.go:210-241). That is not a firmware-shipped device — no XML under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/ declares it — so its COLOR ordering is not decidable from these sources. It does not change the verdict: the decode is shared, and it is contradicted on every device the firmware does describe.

Witness (Tier 3, explains provenance, not authority): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:63-75 declares FixedColor as a StrEnum whose members are the labels; the Python reference never carries a numeric ordinal at all, so our integer ordering is a Go-side invention with no upstream source.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had FixedColor matched the CCU, all three independent Tier-1 orderings would have read BLACK, RED, GREEN, YELLOW, BLUE, PURPLE, TURQUOISE, WHITE. Each of them instead reads BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE, so the check does separate the two hypotheses rather than returning the same answer either way.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld, and every quote re-verified against the source. The firmware's COLOR ordinal is the index into a VALUE_LIST ordered BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE. Four of eight slots differ from ours: index 1 is BLUE (we say RED), 3 is TURQUOISE (we say YELLOW), 4 is RED (we say BLUE), 6 is YELLOW (we say TURQUOISE). BLACK/GREEN/PURPLE/WHITE coincide. I additionally confirmed the two links the previous grounding left implicit: (a) COLOR really is a StringEnumToInteger ENUM, which is the precondition for the ordinal substitution in convertParameterValue, and (b) the outbound branch returns the list index rather than SimpleRGBColor's own value field — so the extended VALUE_LIST (RANDOM/OLD_VALUE/DO_NOT_CARE appended) does not shift the first eight either. Our own code already states the correct order in a comment at color.go:610-613 while Color() contradicts it.

One correction to the previous consequence list, which overstates by one item: ChannelHsColor (color.go:676-690) is entirely label-driven — it calls custom.EnumLabelValue(l.channelColor) and matches the returned CCU name against fixedColorNames, never touching an index. It is therefore correct, and it is the sibling that will visibly disagree with Color()/ColorName() on the four wrong slots. The genuinely affected surfaces are Color(), ColorName() (color.go:640-649) and everything downstream of them, plus SetColor's optimistic l.color.OnEvent(int32(c)) (color.go:606), which seeds the store with our ordinal rather than the one the CCU will echo. sound_led.go:337 (`colorLabel := fixedColorNames[color]`) is only a write-back hazard for a caller that round-trips a value it read from Color().

Scope note verified, not changed: RfDimmer_Color_Fixed also routes through newFixedColorConstructor (internal/model/custom/light/init.go:71) for DeviceType hbw-lc-rgbww-in6-dr (internal/model/custom/profiles.go:210-215). No XML under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/ or rftypes/ mentions rgbww, so that device's COLOR ordering is not decidable here — but the decode is shared and is contradicted on every device the firmware does describe.

reachesDevice.title: The combined Timer stores DURATION_VALUE's descriptor default as a seconds count without reading DURATION_UNIT's default
reachesDevice.ourValue: defaultSeconds := DURATION_VALUE's descriptor DEFAULT, interpreted as hmenum.TimerUnitSeconds (timer.go:123-133); DURATION_UNIT's own DEFAULT never read
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: DURATION_UNIT: LogicalType.ENUM, defaultValue "S", minValue "S", maxValue "H" (siren/oldFormat) or "10MS"; DURATION_VALUE: LogicalType.INTEGER, defaultValue 0, min 0, max 16343
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDurationUnitParameter and #createDurationValueParameter; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createDurationUnitParameter and #createDurationValueParameter. Constructor argument positions confirmed against HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.StateParameter (argument 6 = defaultValue, 7 = minValue, 8 = maxValue). Registration of the siren variant: GeneralStateParameterFactory, ParameterMapKey("DURATION_UNIT", "siren") -> createDurationUnitParameter(..., oldFormat=true). Tier 2 negative check: `grep -al 'DURATION_VALUE\|DURATION_UNIT' ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml` returns nothing — the pair is HmIP-only.
reachesDevice.finding:
Our rule holds on the surface our code is on. Every DURATION_UNIT-family state parameter the HmIP server constructs carries the literal defaultValue "S" — the siren variant (oldFormat=true, VALUE_LIST S,M,H), the non-siren variants (S,M,H,10MS, used for the withColor / uniLight / withRoom lights and for RAMP_TIME_UNIT and RAMP_TIME_TO_OFF_UNIT), and the climate set_point variant. There is no HmIP channel where DURATION_VALUE's default is expressed in minutes or hours, so reading the value default as seconds is right.

Two qualifications the reader should carry:

1. It is right by the firmware's construction, not by measurement. The value the code stores is still not derived from the unit parameter that is already resolved two lines above (timer.go:120). Nothing in our code would notice if a future channel type declared DURATION_UNIT DEFAULT "M". Reading unitDP's descriptor default and converting through the existing toTimerUnit path would ground it instead of leaving it resting on this audit.

2. DURATION_VALUE's declared default is 0, not a positive on-time. So DefaultDuration() on a stock HmIP siren returns 0 seconds, and the siren's "send the device default" paths (siren.go:334 and siren.go:415) send DURATION_VALUE=0 / DURATION_UNIT=S rather than a device-declared on-time. That is a separate behavioural question from the unit, and the comment at siren.go:334 ("so the device uses its declared on-time") describes something the firmware does not declare. Worth checking against a live descriptor before relying on it.

The pair does not exist on BidCos at all, so no wider scope contradicts the rule.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had any HmIP DURATION_UNIT declared a non-seconds default, the defaultValue argument in the two factory methods that construct every parameter of this family would carry a different literal ("M" or "H") — the value is a hard-coded constructor argument, so a differing default would be directly visible. All four construction sites carry the literal "S".
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The firmware reads hold and I re-verified every literal. Demoted from confirmed to narrowed because the rule is true only inside a boundary the previous grounding did not draw, and because one firmware fact it omitted changes how the result should be read.

Boundary: combined.NewTimer has exactly one production caller — internal/model/custom/siren/siren.go:142-146, always with (ParameterDurationValue, ParameterDurationUnit) and therefore always with the HmIP `siren` variant of DURATION_UNIT (oldFormat=true, VALUE_LIST S,M,H). The other DURATION_UNIT-family parameters the previous grounding surveyed (withColor, uniLight, withRoom, RAMP_TIME_UNIT, RAMP_TIME_TO_OFF_UNIT, climate set_point) never reach this code, so their agreement is corroboration about the firmware, not about the rule. That matters because the non-siren variant carries a fourth unit, "10MS" at index 3, and toTimerUnit (timer.go:179-191) blind-casts any integer to hmenum.TimerUnit with no bounds check — a future profile that routed a non-siren DURATION_UNIT through this Timer would silently produce hmenum.TimerUnit(3). The rule is therefore safe today by the choice of caller, not by anything the Timer itself checks.

Omitted firmware fact: both DURATION_VALUE and DURATION_UNIT are declared IOOperations.WRITE in all four factory methods — write-only. The Timer's read leg (push(), valueDP.RawValue()/unitDP.RawValue(), timer.go:136-146) can therefore only ever see values our own optimistic path recorded; the device never reports these back. Combined with DURATION_VALUE's declared DEFAULT of 0, DefaultDuration() (timer.go:207-214) returns 0 s on a stock HmIP siren, so siren.go:334 and siren.go:415 send DURATION_VALUE=0 / DURATION_UNIT=S. The comment at siren.go:333-334 ("so the device uses its declared on-time") describes something the firmware does not declare; that stands as the previous agent flagged it, and it is a live behavioural question, not a unit question.

What would ground the rule instead of resting on this audit: read unitDP's descriptor DEFAULT and run it through the existing toTimerUnit path, and give toTimerUnit an explicit VALUE_LIST-bounded mapping rather than a cast.

reachesDevice.title: HM-CC-VG-1 SET_TEMPERATURE bounds 4.5 / 30.5 overwrite the CCU-declared MIN/MAX
reachesDevice.ourValue: MIN rewritten to 4.5, MAX rewritten to 30.5 on HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE (VALUES), unconditionally at paramset ingest; Reason string "CCU returns invalid MIN/MAX bounds for virtual heating groups (0/0 or string)"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: min="5.0" max="30.0" default="20.0" unit="°C" type="FLOAT" operations="7" control="HEATING_CONTROL.SETPOINT" aggregation="LAST"
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml:504-505 — `<status_parameter aggregation="LAST" control="HEATING_CONTROL.SETPOINT" default="20.0" max="30.0" min="5.0" name="SET_TEMPERATURE" operations="7" tab_order="4" type="FLOAT" unit="°C">`, inside `<channel id="1" type="CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER">` (:433) of the file's single `<group>` (:3), whose `<virtual_device_type>` is HM-CC-VG-1 (:8113). The runtime paramset description is built from those attributes verbatim by HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.GroupDeviceHandler#createParamsetDescriptions -> #createHashMapFromParameterValues, which puts parameter.getMax() / parameter.getMin() into the RpcStruct; those accessors are declared String-typed on HMServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.bidcos.BidCosVirtualChannelParameter. Comparison value: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2392-2395 — HM-CC-RT-DN's own SET_TEMPERATURE is `<logical type="float" min="4.5" max="30.5" default="20.0" unit="°C">`.
reachesDevice.finding:
The firmware does declare bounds for this parameter, and they are not the ones we write. HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE is declared min=5.0, max=30.0, default=20.0, unit=°C. Our patch replaces that with 4.5 / 30.5 — which are exactly HM-CC-RT-DN's own logical bounds (rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2395), i.e. the member device's range substituted for the group's. The group is deliberately narrower than its members.

Direction of the error: the patch widens the range on both ends. A setpoint of 4.5 or 30.5 now passes our validation and the SPA slider now offers it, and both are outside the range the CCU declares for the group.

Half of the patch's Reason is corroborated and half is not:
- "or string" is confirmed. GroupDeviceHandler copies parameter.getMin()/getMax() straight into the description, and both accessors are String-typed on BidCosVirtualChannelParameter, so the CCU really does report MIN and MAX for this parameter as XML-RPC strings rather than doubles. A patch that coerces the string form to a number is well founded.
- "0/0" is not. Nothing in the group definition or in the description-building path produces 0/0 for SET_TEMPERATURE; the declared values are "5.0" and "30.0". If a real CCU was observed returning 0/0, that observation is unaccounted for by these sources and should be re-measured before the numbers are changed.

What the patch should carry, on this evidence: keep the string→number coercion, and use 5.0 / 30.0. Note also that DEFAULT (20.0) and UNIT (°C) are declared and currently untouched by the patch.

One scope caveat, stated as unverified: HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.rfd.legacy.VirtualDefinitionFactory#fillChannelParameter can build a channel parameter's min/max from a member device's ParameterDescription instead of from the shipped XML. I did not establish which of the two paths serves a runtime HM-CC-VG-1, so I cannot exclude a configuration in which the group inherits HM-CC-RT-DN's 4.5/30.5. The shipped group definition is unambiguous and is the authority I can cite; if the inheriting path is live, the answer would be 4.5/30.5 and our patch would be right for the wrong stated reason. Settling that needs a getParamsetDescription capture from a real CCU with a heating group.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the firmware genuinely left this parameter's bounds unset or at 0/0, the `<status_parameter>` element would carry no min/max attributes or min="0" max="0", and GroupDeviceHandler would have put null or "0" into the description. It carries min="5.0" max="30.0" — and the neighbouring ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE in the same channel carries min="-10.0" max="50.0", showing the attributes are populated per parameter rather than boilerplate.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld, and the one caveat the previous grounding left open is now closed in its favour. HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE is declared min=5.0, max=30.0, default=20.0, unit=°C. Our patch replaces that with 4.5 / 30.5 — the member device's range substituted for the group's — widening the accepted range by 0.5 K at each end, so a setpoint of 4.5 or 30.5 now passes our validation and the SPA slider offers it.

Resolving the open caveat: VirtualDefinitionFactory#fillChannelParameter, the path that could have made the group inherit a member's ParameterDescription bounds, is called only from HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.rfd.legacy.RFD2VirtualDeviceConverter — which is a developer-side generator, not a runtime path: it carries a `public static void main` and hard-coded source paths of the form D:/SVN/HomeMatic/devicetypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml. The live path is the shipped file, named in Constants and HMServerConfiguration as above. So the inheriting configuration the previous agent could not exclude is not live, and 5.0 / 30.0 is what a real CCU serves.

A second, independent reason the answer cannot be 4.5/30.5: BidCosVirtualChannelParameter's own field initialisers are min "5.0", max "30.0", default "20.0". Whether the group-definition parser fills those attributes or leaves them at the class defaults, SET_TEMPERATURE comes out 5.0 / 30.0 either way.

Provenance, stated as unverified as to intent: the shipped group values do not match what the generator would produce from today's device XML — HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU channel 2 SET_TEMPERATURE is 4.5/30.5, and MANU_MODE (4.5/30.5) and ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE (-10.0/50.0) in the same group channel did carry through from the device, while the four ACTION parameters (AUTO_MODE, BOOST_MODE, COMFORT_MODE, LOWERING_MODE) all carry a nonsensical min 5.0 / max 30.0, i.e. the class defaults. So 5.0/30.0 for SET_TEMPERATURE may be a class-default leftover rather than a deliberate narrowing. That does not change what the CCU serves, and it is what our patch must not contradict.

The Reason string splits as the previous agent found. "or string" is confirmed — getMin/getMax are String-typed and copied verbatim into the description, so MIN and MAX really do arrive as XML-RPC strings; the coercion half of the patch is well founded, and DEFAULT ("20.0") and UNIT ("°C") arrive the same way and are currently untouched. "0/0" is not corroborated anywhere in the group definition or the description-building path and should be re-measured before the numbers are trusted.

reachesDevice.title: Out-of-int32 values are silently clamped and then written to the CCU
reachesDevice.site: internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:14-27 (toXMLRPCInt32), :72 and :76 (int / int64 cases of goToXMLRPCValue); reached from binrpc_caller.go:30-39 as well
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1, the CCU's own XML-RPC codec: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:34-36 `static const char INT_TAG[] = "<int>"; static const char I4_TAG[] = "<i4>";`; :260 `else if (typeTag == I4_TAG || typeTag == INT_TAG)` — both tags accepted on parse; :499-509 `int32_t ivalue = strtol(valueStart, &valueEnd, 10); … _value.asInt = int(ivalue);` — no ERANGE check; :511-521 `intToXml()` emits `<i4>` only; :233 the union member is `int asInt`. BIN-RPC uses the same value class: :533-545 `intFromStream` does `memcpy(&v, data, 4); v=ntohl(v); _value.asInt = int(v);` and :547-556 `intToStream` writes `htonl(_value.asInt)` — a fixed 4-byte integer, no wider form. Tier 2: across ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml (148 files) the largest `<logical type="integer" max=…>` is 65536 (rftypes/rf_es_tx_wm.xml, rf_es_tx_wm_le_v1_0.xml); across the 399-device ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions corpus, zero parameters with TYPE=INTEGER declare a MIN, MAX or DEFAULT outside [-2147483648, 2147483647] — the extremes are RSSI_DEVICE/RSSI_PEER MIN=-2147483648, exactly math.MinInt32. HmIP config parameters are bit-fields: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory builds them with create8bitInteger / create9bitInteger / create14bitInteger / create16bitInteger / create24bitInteger / createSigned8bitInteger / createSigned24bitInteger — 24 bits is the widest.
reachesDevice.finding:
The premise is confirmed and the surface is confirmed: `<i4>` (or the equivalent `<int>`) is the only integer the CCU's XML-RPC codec has, it is stored and emitted as int32_t, and BIN-RPC — the CUxD path that reuses the same helper — is a fixed 4-byte network-order integer with no wider form. No integer parameter anywhere in the shipped device XMLs or the descriptor corpus reaches the int32 boundary from outside; the >int32 magnitudes that do exist are all TYPE=FLOAT (ENERGY_COUNTER MAX 1.099e11 on HmIP-ESI, `max="109951162.7775"` in rftypes/rf_es_tx_wm.xml) and travel as `<double>`, which goToXMLRPCValue routes to DoubleValue without touching the clamp.

Where it narrows: the clamp-versus-fault choice is not something the firmware decides, and the comment's word "defensive" overstates what the firmware would do. rfd's parser has no overflow detection either (strtol result assigned straight into int32_t with no ERANGE test, XmlRpcValue.cpp:501-506), so a substituted 2147483647 would be accepted and acted on exactly like a value the caller asked for — the CCU can neither reject nor report it. The clamp is therefore not a guard the CCU backs up; it is a silent substitution whose only justification is that no descriptor-declared parameter can reach it. That justification holds for every value that came from a parameter descriptor and does not extend to the helper's actual contract: goToXMLRPCValue accepts any Go `int`/`int64` argument from any caller and never consults the descriptor's MIN/MAX, so the safety rests on the callers, not on the type. I did not enumerate every caller, so the boundary is stated, not measured.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the rule been wrong I would have found either an integer wider than 32 bits in the CCU's own codec — a long/int64 branch in XmlRpcValue, or a BIN-RPC integer longer than 4 bytes — or at least one TYPE=INTEGER parameter declaring MIN/MAX outside int32. The same two scans did surface out-of-int32 magnitudes (the FLOAT energy counters) and did surface a second integer tag (`<int>` alongside `<i4>`), so they were capable of returning a different answer; they returned int32 for every integer path.
reachesDevice.ourValue: n > math.MaxInt32 → math.MaxInt32; n < math.MinInt32 → math.MinInt32, then sent
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: int32_t on both wires (`<i4>`/`<int>` parsed into int32_t, `<i4>` emitted; BIN-RPC integer = 4 bytes ntohl/htonl); no ERANGE check on receipt either
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD as narrowed. Every quote verifies verbatim and the XML-RPC half now has the link evidence it was missing. Two narrowings the prior grounding did not name, both of which cut against its reassurance. (1) SURFACE: the BIN-RPC half is grounded on rfd's codec, and our binrpcCaller does not talk to rfd — binrpc_caller.go's own comment says 'CUxD shares the XML-RPC value set', and CUxD is a closed third-party add-on with no source in OpenCCU-Base, OpenCCU or any reference tree here. rfd is the protocol's reference implementation, so the 4-byte claim is well founded for BIN-RPC as specified, but it is not a measurement of the peer this code path reaches. That leg is unverified for CUxD. (2) The descriptor-extreme statement understates the risk. I re-ran the scan and the corpus does reach the ceiling from inside: MAX = 2147483647 is declared on writable MASTER parameters — CYCLIC_INFO_MSG_OVERDUE_THRESHOLD on 124 channels, CENTRAL_ADDRESS on 11, AES_KEY on 1 — alongside the read-only RSSI_DEVICE/RSSI_PEER/NEXT_TRANSMISSION/LED_STATUS pairs the prior report cited. So the value the clamp substitutes is itself a legally declared MAX for a writable parameter: rfd accepts it (strtol straight into int32_t, no ERANGE), acts on it, and neither side can tell it apart from a value the caller intended. That is a stronger statement of the same defect, not a weaker one. The prior report's own residual stands unchanged: goToXMLRPCValue never consults a descriptor MIN/MAX, so the safety rests entirely on callers, and I did not enumerate them either.

reachesDevice.title: 'MAX greater than 1.0 means the device supports last-known-level' is a comment-claim, and the 1.005 sentinel named in the comment is nowhere in the code
reachesDevice.site: internal/central/adapter/uischema_link.go:175-181 (`if meta.DisplayAsPercent && rawFloatGreaterThan(p.Max, 1.0) { p.HasLastValue = true }`); assets/ui/src/lib/components/parameter/ParameterLevelField.svelte:37-40 and :153 (`{#if !readOnly && parameter.has_last_value && max > 1 + 1e-6}`)
reachesDevice.ourValue: MAX > 1.0 (Go: rawFloatGreaterThan(p.Max, 1.0); SPA render gate: max > 1 + 1e-6)
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: max="1.0" — with the sentinel declared separately as <special_value id="OLD_LEVEL" value="1.005"/>, exported in the paramset description's SPECIAL array, never in MAX
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_d.xml:608-615, inside <paramset id="dimmer_linkset"> (:319-1045, referenced by <paramset type="LINK" id="dimmer_ch_link"> at :149): `<parameter id="SHORT_ON_LEVEL"> <docu default="true"></docu> <logical type="float" min="0.0" max="1.0" default="1.0" unit="100%"> <special_value id="OLD_LEVEL" value="1.005"/> </logical> <physical type="integer" interface="config" list="3" index="0x11" size="1"/> <conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/> </parameter>`. Same declaration in rf_d_le_v1_7.xml:552, rf_d_le_v1_9.xml:564/929, rf_d.xml:976, rf_dim_1l_644.xml:697/1180, rf_dim_1l_644_le_v2_4.xml:677/1160, rf_dim_2l_644.xml:689/1172, rf_dim_2l_644_le_v2_4.xml:672/1155. Export path: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeFloat.cpp:105-118 `(*val)["MIN"]=min; (*val)["MAX"]=max; (*val)["DEFAULT"]=default_value; if(special_values.size()){ (*val)["SPECIAL"]=special_values; }` and :60-74 (InitFromXml widens effective_min/effective_max to include each special value while min/max stay as declared), with :85-99 EnforceConstraints clamping to effective_max. Tier 2 corpus: ../pydevccu/paramsets_db.json — zero FLOAT parameters with UNIT "100%" and MAX > 1.0.
reachesDevice.finding:
CONTRADICTED. The firmware declares max="1.0" for these parameters and carries 1.005 as a <special_value>, i.e. a member of the SPECIAL set that lives *outside* the min/max range. The paramset-description exporter keeps the two apart: MAX is the declared max, and the special values go into a separate SPECIAL array. A write of 1.005 is nevertheless accepted because InitFromXml widens `effective_max` to 1.005 while leaving `max` at 1.0 — that is precisely the mechanism our rule mistakes for a raised MAX.

The firmware's own name for the value is **OLD_LEVEL**. Our comment's "1.005 means last known level" is right about the number and about the meaning; it is wrong about where the value lives, and the code tests the wrong field.

Scope of the contradiction, measured rather than assumed: across all 130 rftypes and 18 hs485types device XMLs, every `<logical type="float" ... unit="100%">` declares max="1.0" — 159 occurrences, one bucket, no exceptions. Tier 2 agrees: pydevccu's paramsets_db.json has no FLOAT parameter with UNIT "100%" and MAX above 1.0 anywhere.

Consequence — a live, user-visible defect, not just a wrong comment. In Go the dead branch is masked: the classifier already sets HasLastValue: true for every *LEVEL suffix (link_param_metadata.go:233-241), so `has_last_value` still reaches the SPA. But the SPA applies its own gate, `parameter.has_last_value && max > 1 + 1e-6`, to the firmware MAX of 1.0 — so the "last value" checkbox never renders on any real device, and an operator cannot select OLD_LEVEL through the link editor at all. The write path exists (toggleLastValue sends 1.005) and is unreachable.

Which source to follow: Tier 2 — the per-device MAX/SPECIAL read at runtime, not a firmware constant. The correct discriminator is the presence of a SPECIAL entry with ID == "OLD_LEVEL" in the parameter description. Our stack already carries SPECIAL as a raw descriptor blob elsewhere (internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1368-1381 reads SPECIAL.OPTIONAL), so this is plumbing, not new wire work — but nothing in the current link path reads it, which is why the sentinel exists only in prose on the Go side and only as an untriggerable constant in the SPA.

reachesDevice=true: the flag governs a value written into a device's LINK paramset (list 3, index 0x11 on these dimmers).
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, at least one LINK-paramset percent parameter would declare a max above 1.0. I histogrammed the max attribute of every `<logical type="float" ... unit="100%">` across all shipped RF and wired device XMLs and got a single bucket — max="1.0", 159 times — and then confirmed at the exporter that the 1.005 goes to SPECIAL and never to MAX. Both checks would have returned a different result had a raised MAX been the firmware's encoding; the same measurement against Tier 2 (pydevccu) independently returned zero.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
CONTRADICTION UPHELD — and both the previous pass's Tier-2 citation and its scope statement were wrong, so the boundary needs restating.

The mechanism, re-read verbatim: GetDescription exports the *declared* max (`(*val)["MAX"]=max;`) and puts the special values in a separate SPECIAL array of {ID, VALUE} structs; InitFromXml widens only `effective_max`, which EnforceConstraints uses for clamping. A write of 1.005 is accepted while MAX stays 1.0 — precisely the mechanism our rule mistakes for a raised MAX. The firmware's name for the value is OLD_LEVEL.

CITATION DEFECT in the previous pass. It cited "../pydevccu/paramsets_db.json — zero FLOAT parameters with UNIT '100%' and MAX > 1.0". That file is 2 bytes long and contains `{}` — it is an empty runtime cache, so the citation is vacuously true and grounds nothing. The real Tier-2 corpus is ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json, which I measured instead.

SCOPE CLAIM REFUTED. The previous pass wrote that no FLOAT with UNIT "100%" has MAX above 1.0 "anywhere". Measured on the real corpus, 260 do: 258 in VALUES paramsets and 2 in MASTER, all MAX 1.01, concentrated in HmIP LEVEL / LEVEL_2 / SATURATION (HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-DRBLI4, HmIPW-DRBL4, HmIP-FALMOT-C12, HmIP-RGBW, HmIP-BSL, …). The correct statement is surface-scoped: on the **LINK** surface — the one uischema_link.go serves — all 1645 percent floats have MAX 1.0, and in the firmware XMLs all 542 percent-float declarations are max="1.0" (one outlier at 0.2, none above). The contradiction therefore holds on our surface, but the previous grounding proved it with a false universal.

CONSEQUENCE, re-verified in our code. Go: uischema_link.go:85 fills Max from the descriptor's MAX, and link_param_metadata.go:233-241 already sets HasLastValue: true for every *LEVEL suffix, so the rawFloatGreaterThan branch and its else-branch produce the same value — dead, not harmful. SPA: ParameterLevelField.svelte:153 gates the checkbox on `parameter.has_last_value && max > 1 + 1e-6` against a MAX of 1.0, so the "last value" control never renders on any device in either corpus, and toggleLastValue (which writes 1.005) is unreachable. Live, user-visible.

NEW FINDING the previous pass missed, and it is the same class of error one level down: the SPA hard-codes `const lastValueSentinel = 1.005` as *the* sentinel. The firmware declares four different sentinel IDs on percent floats, and on LINK paramsets alone Tier 2 shows OLD_LEVEL=1.005, NO_MODIFICATION=1.01 (HM-LC-Ja venetian-blind actuators, on the same SHORT/LONG_ON/OFF_LEVEL parameters), ACT_LEVEL=1.275 and LOCKED=-0.005. A fix that only swaps the MAX test for "has a SPECIAL entry" but keeps 1.005 as the written value would send the wrong sentinel to the Ja actuators — a value the device's own effective_max (1.01) would then clamp.

Which source to follow: Tier 2, the per-device SPECIAL array read at runtime — never a firmware constant and never MAX. The discriminator is the presence of a SPECIAL entry, and the value to write is that entry's VALUE, keyed by its ID. One trap for the implementer: the wire shape is the firmware's array of {ID, VALUE} structs (HSSLogicalTypeFloat.cpp:110-112); pydevccu stores most of its corpus as a flattened {ID: VALUE} object (1421 of 1501 SPECIAL fields) and only 80 in the array shape, so the corpus shape must not be taken as the wire shape. Our stack already carries SPECIAL as a raw blob (internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1368-1381, which does a substring search for "OPTIONAL" rather than decoding), so nothing on the link path reads it today.

reachesDevice.title: Three different models of the CCU's float behaviour coexist: 6-decimal rounding on write, 1e-6 relative tolerance on echo, exact equality in profile matching
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:65 — `std::string XmlRpcValue::_doubleFormat("%f");`, consumed by :591-594 `doubleToXml()` and :659-662 `doubleToText()` via `snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf)-1, getDoubleFormat().c_str(), _value.asDouble)`; `setDoubleFormat` (XmlRpcValue.h:151) has no caller anywhere under src/, so the default stands. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:222 — `snprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer)-1, "%f", (double)v);`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:625-637 — `doubleToStream()`: `mantissa=int(frexp(_value.asDouble, &exponent)*double(1<<30));`, decoded at :605-620 as `ldexp(double(mantissa)/double(1<<30), exponent)`. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcSerializer — the <double> element is written with `String.valueOf(o)`, i.e. Java Double.toString, shortest round-trip.
reachesDevice.ourValue: Write: every outgoing float64 rounded to 6 decimals (`math.Round(v*1e6)/1e6`). Echo: match when `|sent-got| / max(1,|sent|,|got|) <= 1e-6`.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: BidCos rfd XML-RPC and ReGa/tclrpc: `%f`, i.e. exactly 6 decimal places, rounded — absolute quantisation of 5e-7. BIN-RPC: `int(frexp(v,&e)*2^30)`, a truncating binary-mantissa form with a constant relative step of 2^-30 ≈ 9.3e-10. HmIP legacy XML-RPC: `String.valueOf(double)` — full binary64 round-trip, no quantisation at all.
reachesDevice.finding: The premise that the three sites cannot all be right does not survive reading them. (a) The write-side 6-decimal round is not an unverified claim — it is an exact match for what rfd and tclrpc emit, `%f` being `%.6f`. (b) The echo tolerance is adequate on every transport, and the `max(1,·)` denominator is why: for |v|<=1 it degrades to an absolute 1e-6, which covers %f's 5e-7; for |v|>1 it is 1e-6 relative, which covers both %f (whose relative error only shrinks as |v| grows) and BIN-RPC's 9.3e-10. The bundle's reasoning — that a mantissa/exponent form makes a large value lose 'far more than 1e-6 relative' — is backwards: a mantissa/exponent form is by construction a constant-relative quantiser. (c) The third site is misreported. internal/store/linkprofile/store.go:483-486 `floatsEqual` is `math.Abs(a-b) <= 1e-6*math.Max(math.Max(math.Abs(a),math.Abs(b)),1.0)` — character-for-character the diff.go shape, not exact equality. Where the claim does need narrowing: our 6-decimal write round is correct for the BidCos and ReGa surfaces and lossy for the HmIP one, whose serialiser preserves full binary64. The boundary runs at the interface, not at the parameter. Practically small (HmIP float parameters declare one or two decimals), but the rule as written asserts more than the firmware does. One genuine internal inconsistency remains and it is inside diff.go itself: the ValueKindList branch (:49-58) compares elements with `!=`, so floats inside a list get bit-exact comparison while scalar floats get the tolerance — the same echo through a list-valued parameter can be reported as a mismatch that a scalar would pass.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the CCU's XML-RPC serialiser not quantised to 6 decimals, `_doubleFormat` would hold `%g`, `%.17g`, or a wider precision, or `setDoubleFormat` would be called somewhere in src/ — I checked for both and found neither. The HmIP side is the control that the check discriminates: the same question asked of HMIPServer's serialiser returned a different answer (`String.valueOf`, no quantisation), which is how the narrowing was found rather than assumed.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: The firmware half is sound; the rule's own premise about our code is not, and it fails on two of three sites. (1) The write leg is measured on dead code. `parameter.ToHomematicValue` and `value.ToHomematicValue` are both referenced exclusively from `_test.go` files. Whatever the CCU's `%f` does, the daemon never rounds an outgoing float to 6 decimals — XML-RPC emits the shortest exact decimal and BIN-RPC emits the frexp pair. So "6-decimal rounding on write" is not one of three coexisting models; it is a property of a helper the write path does not execute, and the previous agent upheld it as "an exact match for what rfd and tclrpc emit" without establishing that the site is on the write path. (2) The previous agent correctly caught that the third site is not exact equality — internal/store/linkprofile/store.go:483-486 `floatsEqual` is `math.Abs(a-b) <= 1e-6*math.Max(math.Max(math.Abs(a),math.Abs(b)),1.0)`, the diff.go shape — but its replacement finding is itself built on a guessed input. It reports that "floats inside a list get bit-exact comparison" at diff.go:49-58. `hmtypes.ParamValue.List` is declared `List []string` (pkg/hmtypes/value.go:25); no float can ever occupy a ValueKindList, so the `!=` there is a string comparison and the claimed internal inconsistency does not exist. (3) What survives is the echo tolerance, and it is adequate: with denominator max(1,|sent|,|got|) the bound degrades to an absolute 1e-6 for |v|<=1, covering %f's 5e-7 quantisation, and stays 1e-6 relative for |v|>1, covering both %f (whose relative error shrinks as |v| grows) and BIN-RPC's mantissa truncation (relative error bounded by 2^-29 ~ 1.9e-9, since frexp normalises the mantissa into [0.5,1)). One model, in two places, with the same expression. The rule's title is false as stated.

reachesDevice.title: The target-channel key ordering (sorted-group position = actor index) is a convention the source does not state
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseHmIPWeeklyProgram.js:517-540 — `getRelevantChannels: function() { ... jQuery.each(this.device.channels, function(index,chn) { if (chn.channelType.indexOf(virtualChID) !== -1) ... result.push(index)` (channel-ascending scan over `_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER`, ACCESS_RECEIVER, ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER, DOOR_LOCK_STATE_TRANSMITTER, OPTICAL_SIGNAL_RECEIVER, PERMISSION_TRANSCEIVER, SWITCH_TRANSCEIVER, AUTO_RELOCK_TRANSCEIVER, DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER); same file :48-107 the explicit per-model overrides `this.relevantChn = (this.expert) ? [4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14] : [4,8,12]` (HmIP-BSL fw>=2), `[1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15]` (HmIP-WKP), `[10,11,12]` (HmIP-SMO230), `(this.expert) ? [7,9,10,11] : [7,9]` (WGS), `[6]` (wired WGS), `(this.expert) ? [2,4,5,6] : [2,4]` (WGT), `[2]` (window drive / wired WGT), `[1]`/`[1,2]`/`[1,2,3,4]` (RGBW by mode); :599-627 `getBinChannelState: function() { ... bVal = this.opts.channelLocks.toString(2); ... bVal = this.reverseString(bVal); if (! this.expert) { for (var x = 0; x < bVal.length; x += 3) { tmp += bVal[x]; } bVal = tmp; }`; :355-372 the bit value itself `if (self.expert) { valCheckBox = Math.pow(2, index); } else { if (index == 0) { valCheckBox = 1; tmpVal = 1; } else { valCheckBox = tmpVal << 3; tmpVal = valCheckBox; } }` with `Math.pow(2,(val-1))` reached only inside `else if (self.deviceIsHmIP_DALI)`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:200-240 `getWPVirtualChannels` and :64-92 `getOnlyExpertChannels` (the 3-per-actor collapse: `virtChnCounterWP = (virtChnCounterWP >= 3) ? 0 : virtChnCounterWP; virtChnCounterWP++; if (virtChnCounterWP == 1) { return channelNr; } else { return null; }`), :394-481 the same per-model overrides, :2896-2935 the same bit computation, plus `valHmIP_FWI = [8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,1,2,4]` at :2892.
reachesDevice.ourValue: actor index = 1-based position in the group-number-sorted set of schedule-relevant custom-DP channel groups; sub index = 1-based position within the group, primary channel first then secondaries; `<actor>_<sub>` maps to CHANNEL_LOCKS bit 3*(actor-1)+(sub-1) over a fixed 8x3 grid; TARGET_CHANNELS bit = ChannelNo - 1 (internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go TargetChannelBitsFrom).
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: There is no actor/sub decomposition in the CCU. The editor builds one flat, channel-ascending list of the device's virtual-receiver / transceiver channels (`relevantChn` / `virtualChannels`), overridden by an explicit hard-coded list for nine named model families, and the bit is the 0-based POSITION in that list: `Math.pow(2, index)` for TARGET_CHANNELS and, for CHANNEL_LOCKS, the reversed binary string indexed by the same position. The 3-wide stride appears only in the non-expert view, as `tmpVal << 3` and `x += 3`, for devices whose receivers genuinely come in triples. `2^(channelNumber-1)` occurs in exactly one branch, `deviceIsHmIP_DALI`.
reachesDevice.finding: Two halves of this join land differently. The CHANNEL_LOCKS table in channel_keys.go is right wherever a device's schedule channels really are triples: for HmIP-BSL fw>=2 the firmware's own list is [4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14], so positions 0..8 are exactly our 1_1..3_3 bits 0..8 — the 24-bit mask, the LSB-first order and the 3-per-actor grouping are all confirmed by getBinChannelState and getOnlyExpertChannels. The boundary runs at devices whose list is not a run of triples, and the firmware names them: HmIP-WKP [1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15] is eight one-channel actors, so the CCU's bits are 0,1,2,...,7 while our keys 1_1,2_1,...,8_1 give 0,3,6,...,21; HmIP-WGS [7,9,10,11], HmIP-WGT [2,4,5,6], the RGBW modes [1,2] and [1,2,3,4], HmIP-DLD/HmIPW-WRC6 and HmIP-FWI (explicit table [8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,1,2,4]) are the same shape. On those the two writes address different physical channels, and both reach real actors. Separately and unambiguously contradicted: TargetChannelBitsFrom's `ChannelNo - 1`. The rawconvert.go comment cites `Math.pow(2,(self.virtualChannels[index]-1))` as the CCU's rule, but that line sits inside the `deviceIsHmIP_DALI` branch — it is the one exception, and the general branch two lines above is `Math.pow(2, index)`. For HmIP-BSL fw>=2 the difference is not subtle: channel 8 is position 3 (bit 3) for the CCU and bit 7 for us; channel 12 is position 6 for the CCU and bit 11 for us. The sound construction for both parameters is the same one the CCU uses: order the device's virtual-receiver/transceiver channels ascending, apply the per-model override where the firmware carries one, and take the 0-based position. Our sub-ordering rule 'primary channel first, then secondaries' is also not the firmware's — the CCU has no primary notion and orders strictly by channel number, so any profile whose primary channel number exceeds one of its secondaries reorders the pair.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had 'sorted-group position = actor index, bit = 3*(actor-1)+(sub-1)' and 'TARGET_CHANNELS bit = channel number - 1' been the CCU's rules, the editor would compute the checkbox value from the channel number uniformly and would not need per-model channel lists at all. Instead the general branch is position-based (`Math.pow(2, index)`), the channel-number form appears in exactly one device-specific branch, and nine model families carry hard-coded lists precisely because position and channel number diverge on them. A device with contiguous 1..3N receivers produces the same answer under both rules, which is why the check had to be run against HmIP-BSL and HmIP-WKP rather than a generic actuator.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: The rule is upheld and the previous agent's narrowing is too generous. Four things. (1) The `ChannelNo-1` contradiction is confirmed at the source: the expression the rawconvert.go comment cites as the CCU's rule sits inside the DALI branch (:2918); the general branch two lines above (:2899) is `Math.pow(2, index)`. For HmIP-BSL fw>=2 the CCU puts channel 8 at bit 3 and channel 12 at bit 6; we put them at bits 7 and 11. (2) The CHANNEL_LOCKS half reaches a real write, not a display. WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS itself is read-only (OPERATIONS 5), and `getBinChannelState` is the display decoder. Our writer emits `WPTCLS=<bit>,WPTCL=<0|2>` on COMBINED_PARAMETER (internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:663 via BuildCombinedParameterValue). The CCU's own producer of that exact string is iseHmIPWeeklyProgram_AccessReceiver.js:392, and its bit is `Math.pow(2, index)` — positional. So the wrong bit locks a channel the operator did not select, on the device. (3) The BSL agreement the previous agent called "confirmed" is a coincidence of two independent derivations, not a grounding. The CCU's [4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14] is a hard-coded per-model override; ours comes from the IPFixedColorLight profile's `PrimaryChannel: 0, SecondaryChannels: []int{1, 2}` rebased per group number (internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:132-138 with schedule_targets.go:97-102). Nothing links the two. The firmware carries overrides for nine families and `deriveTargetChannels` consults none of them, so on HmIP-WKP [1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15] (eight single-channel actors: CCU bits 0..7, our keys 1_1..8_1 give 0,3,6,…,21), HmIP-WGS [7,9,10,11], HmIP-WGT [2,4,5,6], RGBW [1,2] / [1,2,3,4] and HmIP-DLD/HmIPW-WRC6 the two writes address different physical channels. (4) Two boundaries the previous agent did not name. iseHmIPWeeklyProgram_AccessReceiver.js:190,198 hard-codes role bits 1 / 256 / 512 for HmIP-DLD and HmIP-DLP that are neither positional nor channel-derived — no formula of ours reproduces them. And the 8x3/24-bit grid is not universal: HmIP-DRG-DALI declares CHANNEL_LOCKS as a STRING with MAX 281474976710655 (2^48-1), so our uint32 table cannot address it at all — and DALI is precisely the one device family where `Math.pow(2, channelNumber-1)` is the firmware's actual rule. The sound construction on both parameters is the CCU's own: order the device's virtual-receiver/transceiver channels ascending, apply the per-model override where the firmware carries one, take the 0-based position. Our sub-ordering rule (primary first, then secondaries) is also not the firmware's — it orders strictly by channel number and has no primary notion.

reachesDevice.title: Garage ventilation position is hard-coded as level 0.5
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/door_opener.fn:28-76 (CreateDoorReceiver) — the CCU's own operator control for a garage drive. It reads DOOR_STATE as an index into a four-label list (`string arState = "lblPosClosed,lblPosOpen,lblPosVentilation,lblPosUnknown"`, :32) and writes DOOR_COMMAND by ordinal: `setDpState(oCommand.ID(), 3)` Close, `, 4)` Vent, `, 1)` Open, `, 2)` Stop (:60-72). No level, no percentage, anywhere in the control. Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MOD-HO.json and HmIP-MOD-TM.json, channel :1 (DOOR_RECEIVER) VALUES — DOOR_STATE ENUM VALUE_LIST ['CLOSED','OPEN','VENTILATION_POSITION','POSITION_UNKNOWN'] OPERATIONS 5; DOOR_COMMAND ENUM VALUE_LIST ['NOP','OPEN','STOP','CLOSE','PARTIAL_OPEN'] OPERATIONS 2 (write-only), DEFAULT 'NOP'. The channel declares NO LEVEL parameter at all.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: no LEVEL on the garage channel; the ventilation step is the enum label DOOR_STATE=VENTILATION_POSITION, commanded as DOOR_COMMAND=PARTIAL_OPEN (ordinal 4)
reachesDevice.ourValue: level == 0.5, a synthetic mid-point our own code both produces and consumes
reachesDevice.finding: The reader's framing is wrong and our code shows it: 0.5 is not a device value. Garage.Position() (garage.go:209-223) synthesises it from the DOOR_STATE enum — OPEN→1.0, VENTILATION_POSITION→0.5, CLOSED→0.0 — and the only consumer of Position.Vent() in the whole repo is Garage.IsStateChangeArgs (garage.go:338). The write path never carries a level: Garage.Vent() writes DOOR_COMMAND=PARTIAL_OPEN (garage.go:269-274, command() at :293-299). So 0.5 is a closed round trip between two literals in one package, both exactly 0.5 (exactly representable in float64, and custom.NewPosition clamps to [0,1] without touching it), and the failure mode the reader describes — the drive reporting the vent step as some other level — cannot occur, because the firmware puts no level on that channel. Where the rule IS narrow: the doc comment says "the position matches the garage door's intermediate ventilation step", which reads as a device property. It is not one. The boundary runs at the enum: the firmware's ventilation step is a label (VENTILATION_POSITION / PARTIAL_OPEN, ordinal 4 in the DOOR_COMMAND VALUE_LIST and in the CCU's own control at door_opener.fn:68), and 0.5 is purely our normalisation of it. Anyone porting Position.Vent() to a surface that reads a real LEVEL — a Cover with an intermediate stop — must not carry 0.5 across as a device constant. I kept reachesDevice=true because the guard suppresses a real DOOR_COMMAND write if the two literals ever drift apart, not because 0.5 is written.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had 0.5 been the level the drive reports, the MOD-HO / MOD-TM DOOR_RECEIVER VALUES paramset would declare a LEVEL parameter (it declares six parameters and LEVEL is not among them), and the CCU's own door control would render a position percentage rather than three ordinal buttons. Both checks come back negative, and both would have come back positive on a real cover — the same script run against a HmIP-BROLL channel finds LEVEL with MIN/MAX.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: NARROWING UPHELD, BOUNDARY WIDER THAN STATED, and one factual error in the prior finding. Verified verbatim: door_opener.fn:32 and the four setDpState ordinals; the DOOR_COMMAND VALUE_LIST indices line up with them exactly (1 OPEN, 2 STOP, 3 CLOSE, 4 PARTIAL_OPEN), and DOOR_STATE index 2 is VENTILATION_POSITION in both the CCU control's label list and the descriptor. So 'the firmware's ventilation step is a label, not a level' is correct and Tier-1 grounded. WHERE THE PRIOR FINDING IS WRONG: it states '0.5 is a closed round trip between two literals in one package' and 'the only consumer of Position.Vent() in the whole repo is Garage.IsStateChangeArgs'. The second half is true (grep: garage.go:338 is the sole `.Vent()` call site). The first half is not. Garage.Position() has a second consumer, payload.go:320, which multiplies it through Position.OpenFraction() (mixins.go:430) into `current_position: 50` on the garage state payload that MQTT and REST publish. So the synthetic mid-point IS user-visible, as a percentage the drive never reports and the CCU's own operator control never shows. That is exactly the 'reads as a device property but is not one' hazard the prior agent named in the doc comment — it just also happens on the wire. SECOND BOUNDARY, unnamed before: Garage.SetPosition (garage.go:283-291) maps an incoming position onto a DOOR_COMMAND using thresholds 0.50 and 0.10, and its own comment cites the Python reference for them. The firmware has no position-to-command mapping on this channel to compare against — no LEVEL exists — so those two constants are Tier-1 silent, not merely 'our normalisation'. A caller sending position 0.3 gets PARTIAL_OPEN on Tier-3 authority alone. reachesDevice stays true: a drift between Position()'s 0.5 and Vent()'s 0.5 suppresses a real DOOR_COMMAND=PARTIAL_OPEN write through the idempotence guard at garage.go:338.

reachesDevice.title: Timer promotion truncates toward zero on the port's authority, and the comment says so
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/custom/mixins.go:219 (EncodeTimerDuration), threshold at :136, rounding claim at :209-214, disclaimer at :133-135
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#migrateDurations — the seconds→pair promotion, verbatim in structure: `onTime > 0.0 && onTime < 1.0` → DURATION_UNIT "10MS", DURATION_VALUE `(int)(onTime * 100.0)`; `< 16000.0` → "S", `(int)onTime`; `< 960000.0` → "M", `(int)(onTime / 60.0)`; else → "H", `(int)(onTime / 3600.0)`. Same four-way split for RAMP_TIME with the same constants. Reverse direction in the same method: `onTime = durationUnitFaktor * durationValueFaktor; if (onTime >= 111600.0) onTime = 8580000.0;`. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#correctInfiniteDuration — when DURATION_UNIT is "H" (or "2") and DURATION_VALUE >= 31.0, DURATION_VALUE is replaced by 16383, with the firmware's own log line naming it "handle duration of 31h as infinity (0x3FFF)". HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues calls correctInfiniteDuration on the raw parameter set for every paramset write; #migrateDurations is reached only from #convertCombinedParameter. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDurationValueParameter declares DURATION_VALUE / RAMP_TIME_VALUE as INTEGER, WRITE-only, default 0, min 0, max 16343; #createDurationUnitParameter declares the enum as {"S","M","H"} (oldFormat) or {"S","M","H","10MS"}. Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json — DURATION_VALUE INTEGER MIN 0 MAX 16343 DEFAULT 0 in all 95 declarations, RAMP_TIME_VALUE identical in all 72; DURATION_UNIT VALUE_LIST ['S','M','H'] on 23 devices and ['S','M','H','10MS'] on 72.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: truncation via Java (int) narrowing — but at thresholds 1 s / 16000 s / 960000 s, with a 10MS bucket below 1 s, and on the COMBINED_PARAMETER surface only. On our surface the firmware performs no promotion, and instead rewrites any (value>=31, H) pair to (16383, H) = infinite.
reachesDevice.ourValue: truncation via int32 cast, thresholds 16343 in both units, no 10MS bucket, sentinel (111600, H)
reachesDevice.finding: The rounding claim itself holds and can now be grounded: where the CCU does promote a duration into a (value, unit) pair it truncates — `(int)(onTime / 60.0)` and `(int)(onTime / 3600.0)`, Java narrowing, toward zero — so 16373 s → 272 M is what the firmware would produce too. mixins.go:133-135's admission that float_configtime does not govern this is correct; the governing code is DeviceUtil, not HSSTypeConversionFloatConfigtime. Three ways the surrounding claim is false one step wider, and the boundary is the surface. (1) SURFACE: #migrateDurations is called only from #convertCombinedParameter, i.e. it decodes the COMBINED_PARAMETER string the WebUI builds (`L=..,DU=..,DV=..,RTU=..,RTV=..,R=..,SL=..`, www/webui/webui.js:19831). Our Siren and Light write DURATION_VALUE/DURATION_UNIT directly into a VALUES paramset (siren.go:328-336, light.go:873-877), which reaches #validateAndConvertValues, where no promotion happens at all. So on OUR path the firmware supplies no rounding rule — that half is genuinely tier-1-silent and the port is the only authority, as the comment says. (2) THRESHOLDS: the firmware's own promotion switches at 16000 s and 960000 s; ours at 16343 in both units. 16100 s → ours (16100, S), firmware (268, M). Between 960000 s and 980580 s → ours (16000..16343, M), firmware (266..272, H). Both encodings are in range and denote the same duration to within the firmware's own truncation loss, so neither is broken — but our threshold is not the firmware's, and mixins.go:126-129's "Promoting only once the value would exceed the declared maximum is therefore the field's rule" describes the parameter's MAX (16343, confirmed at Tier 1 by #createDurationValueParameter), not the CCU's promotion rule. (3) THE ONE THAT BITES, and it is on our surface: #correctInfiniteDuration runs on every VALUES paramset we send, and turns any DURATION_VALUE >= 31 carrying DURATION_UNIT=H into 16383, which the firmware's own log calls infinity. Our encoder reaches unit H only when the minutes value already exceeds 16343, i.e. for durations above 980580 s — so the smallest hours value it can ever emit is 272, and 272 >= 31. Every single duration our encoder promotes to hours is therefore silently converted by the CCU into "run forever". A requested 20-day siren (1728000 s → our (480, H)) becomes infinite. So does the TimerNotUsed sentinel: our (111600, H) is rewritten to (16383, H), which happens to be the right outcome but not for the reason mixins.go:141-144 gives — the comment says "the value stays unchanged and the unit is forced to hours", and on this path the value does not stay unchanged. 111600 does appear in the firmware, but as the seconds-side infinity threshold in the reverse mapping (`if (onTime >= 111600.0) onTime = 8580000.0`), not as an encodable DURATION_VALUE; 111600 also exceeds the declared MAX of 16343. Fourth, smaller: we have no 10MS bucket, so a sub-second duration truncates to (0, S) and is lost — the firmware would send (50, 10MS) for 0.5 s, and 72 of 95 DURATION_UNIT declarations carry 10MS.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rounding been wrong — had the port rounded to nearest — the firmware's promotion would read `(int)Math.round(onTime / 60.0)` or `(int)(onTime / 60.0 + 0.5)`; it reads `(int)(onTime / 60.0)`, and the same scan does show the firmware using a different form where it means something different (`(int)(onTime * 100.0)` for the 10MS bucket), so the check distinguishes rounding from truncation. For the 31 h finding the control is arithmetic on a firmware constant rather than a second reading: our encoder's minimum hours value is 16344/60 = 272, and correctInfiniteDuration's guard is >= 31 — had our promotion threshold been low enough to emit small hour counts, values below 31 would pass through untouched and the finding would not stand.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: THE HEADLINE SUB-FINDING IS CONTRADICTED. The prior report's item (3), presented as 'THE ONE THAT BITES, and it is on our surface' — every hours-unit duration we send is silently rewritten by the CCU to 16383 = infinite, a 20-day siren running forever — does not follow, and the refutation is one type coercion deep. #correctInfiniteDuration gates on `"2".equals(x) || "H".equals(x)`, i.e. String.equals(Object). It runs on the RAW parameter set, before any enum conversion. We send DURATION_UNIT as an integer ordinal: hmenum.TimerUnitHours = 2 (pkg/hmenum/timer.go:35), staged as int32 by EncodeTimerDuration, converted by goToXMLRPCValue (internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:73) to xmlrpc.IntValue, marshalled as `<int>2</int>` (value.go:104), and decoded by the CCU's own XML-RPC parser via Integer.parseInt into a java.lang.Integer. `"2".equals(Integer.valueOf(2))` is false; so is `"H".equals(Integer.valueOf(2))`. The rewrite cannot fire on any write this daemon makes. The same disproves the prior claim that our (111600, H) sentinel 'is rewritten to (16383, H)' — it is not; 111600 goes through as sent. The disjunction `"0".equals(x) || "S".equals(x)` throughout #migrateDurations shows what the firmware expects when it wants an ordinal: the STRING "2", not the integer 2. This is a latent condition, not a live bug — and worth recording as such, because it inverts: the day anyone changes DURATION_UNIT to be written as the label "H" or the string "2" (which is how we write other enums, e.g. the siren's acoustic selection), every hours-unit duration WOULD become infinite. WHAT I UPHELD. The surface analysis is right and I re-traced the whole call graph rather than taking it: #migrateDurations reaches only COMBINED_PARAMETER, so the firmware supplies no promotion rule on our VALUES-paramset path, and mixins.go:133-135's admission that float_configtime does not govern this is correct — the governing code is DeviceUtil, not HSSTypeConversionFloatConfigtime. The truncation transcription is exact, including `(int)` Java narrowing toward zero, so 16373 s -> 272 M is what the firmware would produce on its own surface. MAX 16343 is Tier-1 confirmed by #createDurationValueParameter, so timeUnitThreshold is not an invented constant — but the prior agent is right that mixins.go:126-129 describes the field's MAX and calls it 'the field's rule', which the firmware's own 16000/960000 promotion contradicts. Both encodings denote the same duration within truncation loss, so neither is broken. ONE CORRECTION to sub-finding (4): the missing 10MS bucket does not apply to the siren. #createDurationUnitParameter is registered for the siren channel with oldFormat = true, whose enum is {"S","M","H"} with no 10MS at all; the 72-of-95 figure is fleet-wide, not siren-wide. A sub-second siren duration truncating to (0, S) is still a real loss, but the firmware would not have sent 10MS there either. Route note: the siren batches DURATION_VALUE and DURATION_UNIT through one PutParamset (siren.go:317-323 collector; internal/model/generic/collector.go:219-221 collapses same-order same-channel writes), so #putParameterSet -> #validateAndConvertValues really is our path — the refutation is the value type, not the surface.

reachesDevice.title: The RF tunable-white COLOR_LEVEL <-> Kelvin mapping is a ported formula with no CCU source
reachesDevice.ourValue: level 0.0 ≡ 500 mireds (2000 K), level 1.0 ≡ 153 mireds (6535 K), linear in mireds; colorLevelFromKelvin writes (500 − 1000000/K)/347 to the white-point LEVEL
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: DUAL_WHITE_COLOR.LEVEL: `<logical type="float" default="0.0" min="0.0" max="1.0" unit="100%"/>` with `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/>`.
