reachesDevice.finding: Our site is the RF tunable-white branch (l.colorLevel), so the surface is HM-LC-DW-WM's DUAL_WHITE_COLOR channel — I checked the firmware is on that same path before citing. The CCU declares that channel's LEVEL as a dimensionless 0..1 "colour value" with unit "100%" and a 0..200 integer wire scale; the WebUI shows it only as a percentage. Deciding what Kelvin 0.0 and 1.0 mean requires the colour temperatures of the two white LED strips wired to the PWM outputs — hardware the CCU never sees. That input exists in no Tier-1 or Tier-2 source, so the measurement is not performable and the endpoint values 2000 K / 6535 K cannot be grounded (they are HA's own default mired range, arriving via light.py). Two further firmware facts bear on the rule and are worth recording even though they do not settle the endpoints: (1) the warm↔cold *direction* is per-device configurable and only agrees with ours at the CHARACTERISTIC_LOW_IS_WARM default — on a CHARACTERISTIC_LOW_IS_COLD device our mapping is inverted for every value; (2) the transfer curve defaults to CHARACTERISTIC_SQUARE, not linear, so no single fixed linear mapping is universally right. Where the CCU *does* model colour temperature — the HmIP UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER channel — it declares COLOR_TEMPERATURE as an INTEGER in Kelvin with min 1000, max 10200, step 20; our l.kelvin branch writes Kelvin directly there and is unaffected.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the CCU carried the mapping, it would have appeared as a unit or logical range on the parameter (the way HmIP's COLOR_TEMPERATURE carries min 1000 / max 10200 / step 20), or as a Kelvin/mired conversion in the WebUI control. Both checks demonstrably react: the same reads found an explicit Kelvin range on the HmIP colour-temperature parameter and an explicit % rendering on the DUAL_WHITE control. For DUAL_WHITE_COLOR they returned "100%" and a percent slider — the CCU carries no colour-temperature semantics for this channel.
reachesDevice.missingInput: the colour temperature of the two white LED strips at LEVEL 0.0 and 1.0 (a property of the installation, not of the CCU), plus the per-device CHARACTERISTIC_COLOURASSIGNMENT and CHARACTERISTIC_LINSQUARETYPE settings that decide direction and curve

reachesDevice.finding: Two halves, and they land differently. The *semantic* half is confirmed: the descriptor really does advertise LEVEL as READ|WRITE|EVENT on the eTRV climate channel — our comment's premise is exact — and the CCU's own operator surface never writes it, rendering it as a bare percentage readout while the page's only writable control is SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE. That is the read/write-direction answer the descriptor alone cannot give, and it backs the demotion. The *scope* half is narrower than the firmware's own family. The CCU keys eTRV-family membership off the device TYPE label, and its list includes "Thermostat AA", an OEM-branded label the CCU maps to the eTRV paramset and which does not begin with "HmIP-eTRV"; our prefix match therefore leaves its LEVEL writable. The channel-type catalogue also carries a `..._transceiver_trv_bosch` variant that declares LEVEL, consistent with an OEM radiator thermostat under a non-HmIP label. The list also shows why case-insensitivity is load-bearing rather than incidental: the CCU itself ships "HMIP-eTRV-2" alongside "HmIP-eTRV-2". Nothing suggests the rule is too *wide*: only radiator-thermostat channel versions declare LEVEL at all, and "HmIP-HEATING" is the exact group type string with no wider HmIP type sharing that prefix. One limit I will not paper over: whether a LEVEL write is *rejected* by the device is not decided by these sources — DeviceUtil#checkRequiredValues only requires SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE companions on that channel type and does not block the key, and an unrecognised or unsupported write is forwarded to the HmIP backend, so the outcome is valve-firmware behaviour I cannot read here. The demotion is justified by the CCU's own UI treatment, not by a proven write rejection.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the descriptor genuinely made LEVEL read-only — the alternative explanation for the demotion — the channel definition would have carried `<parameter subtype="READ_ONLY">LEVEL</parameter>`, binding createReadOnlyLevel (READ|EVENT). That subtype exists and is used elsewhere, so the check reacts; here the attribute is absent, giving subtype "default" and READ|WRITE|EVENT. Conversely, had the family been exactly our two prefixes, the CCU's own membership list would have contained only HmIP-eTRV*/HmIP-HEATING labels; reading it produced "Thermostat AA" and "HMIP-eTRV-2", which is how the boundary was found rather than assumed.
reachesDevice.missingInput: the device-label → channel-type-version binding (which model uses …_trv_bosch), which none of the readable CCU sources carries — so I can name "Thermostat AA" as a family member our prefixes miss, but cannot state from firmware that its channel declares LEVEL
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD on the semantic half, NARROWED FURTHER than the bundle on the scope half, and one of the bundle's scope arguments demoted to inference. Verified end to end: the map-key chain (unsubtyped <parameter> -> subtype "default" -> ParameterMapKey("LEVEL") -> createLevel -> READ|EVENT|WRITE) is complete and verbatim, and Tier 2 independently reports OPERATIONS 7 with MIN 0.0 / MAX 1.01, matching createLevel's constructor arguments exactly. So the comment's premise is exact: the descriptor really does advertise LEVEL as writable, and the CCU's own operator page never writes it. I also confirmed the WebUI answer survives the distribution patch that rewrites that very block — a step the bundle did not report and the one that could most easily have inverted the finding. I found one channel-type version the bundle's list omitted, _wth_cooling_optimized (tv 10); it declares no LEVEL, so the conclusion is unchanged. The group half is now settled on two tiers: HMIP_HEATING_GROUP_TYPE is verbatim "HmIP-HEATING", the thermostat channel state is an unfiltered merge of the WTH and TRV channel-1 state descriptions with no LEVEL aggregation, and the descriptor corpus shows the resulting group device really does expose LEVEL with OPERATIONS 7. DEMOTED — (a) The bundle says 'the only writable control on that page is the SETPOINT slider'. heating_control.fn also writes ACTIVE_PROFILE via setDpState (:460) alongside the setpoint input and slider. Immaterial to LEVEL, but it is an overstatement. (b) The 'Thermostat AA' scope gap is INFERENCE, not measurement, and I decline to promote it. What the source carries is a line in a section headed '# Mapping of the paramset id' mapping the string 'Thermostat AA' to 'hmip-etrv'. That maps a paramset id used for Control/Unit label lookup; it does not say the device declares HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER at a trv typeversion, and therefore does not establish that such a device has a LEVEL to demote. The same section maps 'ALPHA-IP-RBG' to 'hmip-wth-2' — a wall-thermostat paramset whose channel types declare no LEVEL — which shows the mapping does discriminate but also shows it is a paramset-id mapping, not a channel-type mapping. That the key is a runtime device model string is supported only by a Tier-3 witness. Treating the config key as a device TYPE our matcher sees is exactly the kind of convention this audit exists to catch, so the gap is credible but unverified. (c) The bundle's citation 'DeviceUtil#getParamsetId' is a wrong symbol: DeviceUtil declares no such method; getParamsetId lives on the legacy service handler and the virtual-remote-control component. (d) 'trv_bosch consistent with an OEM radiator thermostat under a non-HmIP label' is speculation the source does not support — the channel-type file names a typeversion, not a manufacturer. CONFIRMED SCOPE: case-insensitivity is load-bearing, not incidental — the config ships 'HMIP-eTRV-2' next to 'HmIP-eTRV-2'; and the rule is not too wide, since only radiator-thermostat typeversions declare LEVEL at all and no other HmIP type shares the 'HmIP-HEATING' prefix. The bundle's own limit stands and I add nothing to it: whether a LEVEL write is rejected at the valve is not decided by these sources — DeviceUtil#checkRequiredValues imposes no LEVEL guard on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER, and an unrecognised or unsupported write is forwarded to the HmIP backend. The demotion is justified by the CCU's operator surface, not by a proven write rejection.

reachesDevice.title: ON_TIME is written as raw seconds and ON_TIME=0 is assumed to cancel the timer
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/generic/switch.go:127 (the ON_TIME=0 comment) and :79-86 (SetOnTime writes d.Seconds(), clamped at 0)
reachesDevice.ourValue: ON_TIME written as raw seconds (float, negative clamped to 0); ON_TIME=0 carried through as an explicit "timer-cancel"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: seconds — confirmed on both stacks. But 0 is not an opcode: BidCos omits the field from the radio frame (`omit_if="0"`), HmIP removes the key from the paramset. There is no distinct cancel value.
reachesDevice.citation: BidCos, Tier 2 descriptor + Tier 1 frame layout: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_s_644.xml:276 `<logical type="float" min="0.0" max="85825945.6" default="0.0" unit="s"/>` with `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="10"/>` + `<conversion type="integer_tinyfloat" mantissa_start="5" mantissa_size="11" exponent_start="0" exponent_size="5"/>` at :278-279; the LEVEL_SET frame at :230 `<parameter type="integer" index="14.0" size="2.0" PARAM="ON_TIME" omit_if="0"/>`; STATE at :270 `<reset_after_send param="ON_TIME"/>`. Same shape in rf_dim_1l_644.xml:320-326. HmIP declared unit: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config:691 `SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER.ON_TIME.Unit=s` (also :271 DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, :688 SWITCH_TRANSCEIVER, :772 WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, :806 WINDOW_DRIVE_RECEIVER). HmIP zero-handling and the seconds proof: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#migrateDurations and #correctInfiniteDuration.
reachesDevice.finding:
The unit half is confirmed outright and on both stacks. BidCos declares ON_TIME `unit="s"`, float, 0.0..85825945.6, and the CCU owns the encoding (×10, then an 11+5-bit tinyfloat) — so writing raw seconds is correct and we must not pre-encode. HmIP declares ON_TIME.Unit=s on every switch/dimmer receiver, and migrateDurations proves the unit by construction: it converts between ON_TIME and DURATION_VALUE using factors 1.0 (S), 60.0 (M), 3600.0 (H) and 0.01 (10MS), which only balances if ON_TIME is seconds.

The zero half is where our comment is wrong, though our behaviour is not. Neither stack has a cancel opcode. On BidCos the LEVEL_SET frame carries `omit_if="0"` on the ON_TIME field: an encoded 0 makes the field vanish from the radio frame, so what the device receives is a plain unbounded switch-on. On HmIP, migrateDurations removes the ON_TIME key and — when no RAMP_TIME accompanies it — puts nothing in its place; when a RAMP_TIME is present it substitutes DURATION_UNIT="H", DURATION_VALUE=16383, which correctInfiniteDuration documents as infinity (0x3FFF, applied to any H-duration ≥ 31 h). So ON_TIME=0 means "no time limit", reached by dropping the value, not by signalling a cancel.

Where the boundary runs: the observable result is identical to our alternative path. Sending {STATE:true, ON_TIME:0} and sending {STATE:true} alone produce the same frame on BidCos (the field is omitted either way, and `reset_after_send` clears the stored ON_TIME after every STATE write so a stale timer cannot leak) and the same paramset on HmIP (the key is removed before dispatch). So switch.go:126-131 is safe as written; the justification "the CCU interprets ON_TIME=0 as a timer-cancel, so we must carry it through" is the part that is not what the firmware does — carrying it through is a no-op, not a necessity. Unrelated bound worth noting while the file is open: SetOnTime clamps only the lower end; BidCos declares max 85825945.6 s and the HmIP path saturates anything ≥ 111600 s to 8580000 s inside migrateDurations, so a very large duration is silently reshaped rather than rejected.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Unit: had ON_TIME been in tenths of a second or in minutes, the logical attribute would read something other than unit="s" (the ×10 scale is a separate <conversion>, not the unit), and migrateDurations could not reconcile ON_TIME with DURATION_UNIT S/M/H/10MS using factors 1/60/3600/0.01. Zero: had 0 been a distinct cancel value, the LEVEL_SET frame would encode it rather than carry omit_if="0", and migrateDurations would emit a specific DURATION pair for onTime==0.0 instead of falling through every `onTime > 0.0` branch with the key already removed. Both discriminators are present and both point away from our comment's mechanism.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The unit half is upheld and I strengthened it. The zero half is upheld for BidCos and DEMOTED for HmIP, because the candidate cited the wrong surface.

What I verified on BidCos. The descriptor line, the two conversions and the frame field are all verbatim as cited. I then closed two gaps the candidate left open. (a) The frame field spells the attribute uppercase, `PARAM="ON_TIME"`, while FrameDescription.cpp reads `node.getAttribute("param")`; that only binds because xmlParser compares attribute names case-insensitively (_tcsicmp) — had it been case-sensitive the whole omit argument would have collapsed. (b) omit_if is documented nowhere in device.xsd (the annotation is literally "???"), so the semantics had to come from the C++: FrameDescription.h:60 states them and FrameDescription.cpp:235 implements them. reset_after_send is SetToDefault, and ON_TIME's default is 0.0, so a stale timer genuinely cannot leak. BidCos conclusion stands: {STATE:true, ON_TIME:0} and {STATE:true} produce the same frame, and 0 is not a cancel opcode.

Where the candidate is wrong. Its entire HmIP argument rests on migrateDurations. That method has exactly one caller — convertCombinedParameter — which is reached only when the written value key is COMBINED_PARAMETER. Our code never writes COMBINED_PARAMETER (grep over the repo: zero occurrences); SetOnTime writes hmenum.ParameterOnTime as a plain VALUES key. On that path the legacy layer runs convertParameterValue, which for a FLOAT parameter passes the value straight through — no key removal, no DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE substitution, no infinity sentinel. So "on HmIP the key is removed before dispatch" and the H/16383 substitution describe a surface we are not on. The 111600 -> 8580000 saturation the candidate attributed to our writes is worse: it sits in the OTHER branch of migrateDurations, the DURATION_* -> ON_TIME direction, so it is misattributed twice over.

The right-surface HmIP grounding, which I did find and which the candidate did not: createOnTimeParameter declares ON_TIME as FLOAT with default 0.0, min 0.0, max 8580000.0 and the converter DoubleToDirectExecutionTime. That converter is the same tinyfloat shape BidCos declares (x10, then 11-bit mantissa + 5-bit exponent) with a stated 0.1 granularity, so ON_TIME is seconds on the path we actually use, proven without migrateDurations. It also fixes the bound: HmIP's declared ceiling is 8 580 000 s, not "saturated above 111600 s", and BidCos's is 85 825 945.6 s. Our SetOnTime clamps only the lower end, so an oversized duration is silently reshaped or rejected downstream on both stacks; that part of the candidate's note survives, its mechanism does not.

What is now unverified: ON_TIME=0 on a plain HmIP write encodes to 0x0000 and is transmitted. Whether the device treats a zero direct-execution time as "no timer" is device firmware and is not in any readable source — tier-1 silent. So "there is no cancel opcode on either stack" is established for BidCos only. Our comment at switch.go:126-131 remains wrong as written and the behaviour remains safe, but the HmIP leg of that argument does not stand.

TargetChannels "X_Y" with X=1..8, Y=1..3 (rest_contract.go:402-404, channelPattern `^[1-8]_[123]$`). DURATION forced to "(HOUR_1, 31)". ColorType discriminator 0/1/2, ColorValue packed 20-bit.
reachesDevice.finding:
Five sub-claims, three outcomes.

CONTRADICTED — astro offset. Every one of the 47 models in the descriptor corpus declares 01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET as INTEGER MIN -128 MAX 127. We accept and emit -720..+720. The CCU's own editor does not carry a constant at all: HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1128-1134 reads ASTRO_OFFSET_MIN/MAX out of the paramset description (hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:39-46 fills them from `$psDescr(01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET)` MIN/MAX) and clamps the input field to them. So the firmware answer is "whatever the channel declares", and what every channel declares is ±128, not ±720. rawconvert.go:832-835 lets anything in ±720 through to the wire, so a value between 128 and 720 is written and the device either rejects the putParamset or stores a clipped switching time. The unit is confirmed as minutes (`'ASTRO_OFFSET_UNIT' : 'min'`).

CONTRADICTED — the 24-slot comment at rest_contract.go:361. It contradicts SlotNo 1..75 three lines below and both the firmware and the descriptors: `_getMaxEntries` returns 69 or 75, and every model in the corpus declares NN_WP_* keys up to exactly 69 or 75. The 75/69 constant at simple.go:329 and its existing citation to `_getMaxEntries` are verbatim correct, including the 69-model list (HmIP-MP3P, HmIPW-WRC6(-A), WRC6-230, water switches, HmIP-BSL fw 2.x); the descriptors add HmIP-HDM1/HDM2 to the 69 group. `default: return -1` means the switch does not bound a lock / access-transmitter channel — for those the descriptor is the only bound, which is what the SlotNo comment already says.

NARROWED — target channels. The firmware field is not an "X_Y" grammar at all: it is an integer bitmask, MAX 16777215 = 2^24-1, addressed by the device's own virtual-receiver channel number minus one (the derivation at internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:940-985 already cites HmIPWeeklyProgram.js correctly and takes the bit from the device, so the write path is sound). What is narrowed is the DTO's grammar: HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-LSC and HmIP-RGBW declare TARGET_CHANNELS as STRING with MAX '281474976710655' = 2^48-1, i.e. 48 addressable bit positions. `channelPattern` `^[1-8]_[123]$` can express at most 24 keys and rejects anything past `8_3`, and internal/central/adapter/week_profile_filter.go:237-247 mints keys as `<group index+1>_<member index+1>` with no upper bound, so a device with more than 8 schedule-relevant groups produces a key its own validator rejects. Separately, those three models declare the field STRING while rawconvert.go:840 writes a Go int — I did not establish what the legacy API does with an int for a STRING-typed config parameter, so that part is unverified.

CONFIRMED with a naming correction — the lock DURATION pair. DURATION_BASE index 7 is BASE_1_H and DURATION_FACTOR's max and default are both 31, so (7, 31) is the CCU's own "maximum duration" encoding. That the wire value of an ENUM is the VALUE_LIST index is read from HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:96-110, not assumed. The name "HOUR_1" in the comment is not a CCU name — it appears nowhere in the descriptors or the CCU editor; it is the Python reference's enum (../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:2550 `HOUR_1 = 7`, a witness). The CCU calls it BASE_1_H.

CONFIRMED — the colour field. NN_WP_HUE_SATURATION_COLOR_TEMPERATURE_EFFECT_VALUE declares MAX 1048575 = 2^20-1 on all three universal-light models, so "packed 20-bit" is exact; the TYPE discriminator declares MAX 2, so the acceptance set {0,1,2} is exact for these devices. One caveat: the CCU's own editor offers five options for that select — 0 hue/saturation, 1 colour temperature, 2 effect, 3 Switch, 4 Dimmer (HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1676-1682) — so 3 and 4 exist in the editor but exceed every shipped device's declared MAX. Because we carry the field as an opaque int, the round-trip is lossless either way; the comment's enumeration is simply not the editor's full list.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had ±720 been the real astro bound, at least one of the 47 models in the descriptor corpus would declare MIN/MAX beyond ±128 — none does, all 47 declare exactly -128/127 — and the CCU editor would have carried a literal rather than reading psDescr. Had 24 been the slot bound, no channel would declare an NN_WP_* key above 24 and `_getMaxEntries` would return 24; every model declares up to 69 or 75 and the function returns 69 or 75. Had (7,31) been wrong, DURATION_BASE's VALUE_LIST would put a different symbol at index 7 or DURATION_FACTOR's MAX would not be 31. Had the colour field not been 20 bits, its declared MAX would not be exactly 2^20-1.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
EVERY SUB-CLAIM REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY. I re-derived the descriptor corpus myself rather than trusting the candidate's counts: 01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET is INTEGER -128..127 DEFAULT 0 on all 44 files that carry it (candidate said 47 — an overcount, substance unaffected); max NN_WP_WEEKDAY index is 69 on exactly {HmIP-BSL, HmIP-HDM1, HmIP-HDM2, HmIP-MP3P, HmIPW-WRC6} and 75 on the other 40; 01_WP_TARGET_CHANNELS is INTEGER 0..16777215 on 42 files and STRING '0'..'281474976710655' on exactly {HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-LSC, HmIP-RGBW} (candidate said 43/3); DURATION_BASE VALUE_LIST is the 8-element list ending BASE_1_H on 38 files, DURATION_FACTOR INTEGER 0..31 DEFAULT 31 on 38; colour VALUE 0..1048575 and TYPE 0..2 on 3. The two contradictions therefore stand, and the write path is the right surface (rawconvert.go:801 mints `%02d_WP_`, i.e. the HmIP MASTER keys the editor edits).

ONE CITATION DEMOTED — WRONG SURFACE. The candidate grounded "an ENUM's wire value is the VALUE_LIST index" on ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:96-110. That code is verbatim as quoted, but libhsscomm is the BidCos stack (rfd / hs485d); 01_WP_DURATION_BASE is an HmIP MASTER parameter served by HMIPServer's legacy XML-RPC surface. The two demonstrably differ: HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDescription emits MIN=int(0), MAX=int(size-1), DEFAULT=int, whereas the captured HmIP descriptor for 01_WP_DURATION_BASE emits MIN="BASE_100_MS", MAX="BASE_1_H", DEFAULT="BASE_1_H" — strings. The cited code is not the code that produced this descriptor.

I FOUND THE RIGHT-SURFACE GROUNDING AND IT REACHES THE SAME ANSWER, WITH A NEW CAVEAT. On the HmIP legacy surface the ordinal substitution is a configuration-gated behaviour: DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue converts an ENUM value to its VALUE_LIST ordinal outbound and back to the string inbound ONLY when `replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal` is set; the field defaults to false in code (set from property `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal`, default false, in both LocalServer and HMIPServer startup), and the shipped CCU config turns it ON at crRFD.conf:47. So (7, 31) is correct on a stock CCU — but it is correct BECAUSE of a config line, not because the protocol says so. On a deployment where that property is false the legacy surface passes ENUM values as strings, and rawconvert.go's `toInt(val)` read would yield 0 while its int write would hand an Integer to a String-typed parameter. That conditionality is not stated anywhere in our code or in the candidate's finding; it is a real, previously-unnamed fragility. The "HOUR_1" naming correction is upheld: HOUR_1 appears nowhere in the firmware tree or the descriptors, and is aiohomematic's enum name at const.py:2550 (verified). The CCU calls it BASE_1_H.

TARGET-CHANNELS NARROWING UPHELD AND SHARPENED. `channelPattern` `^[1-8]_[123]$` (simple.go:158) admits at most 24 keys, while internal/central/adapter/week_profile_filter.go:246-248 mints keys as `fmt.Sprintf("%d_%d", actorIdx+1, subIdx+1)` with no upper bound on either index — verified verbatim — so a device with more than 8 schedule-relevant groups, or more than 3 members in one, produces a key its own validator rejects. The three STRING-typed models declare 48 addressable bit positions. Whether the legacy API accepts a Go int for a STRING-typed config parameter remains unverified in those words; the DeviceUtil path I read converts only ENUM and LONG, and leaves other types untouched, which suggests but does not establish that an Integer would reach the parameter unconverted.

reachesDevice.title: RX_MODE bit layout is a bare literal block decoded straight into a REST field
reachesDevice.site: pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:138-145; decoded at internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:161-172; populated for every interface at internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:594
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDeviceDescription.h:42-46 — `RX_ALWAYS=(1<<0)`, `RX_BURST=(1<<1)`, `RX_CONFIG=(1<<2)`, `RX_WAKEUP=(1<<3)`, `RX_LAZY_CONFIG=(1<<4)`; :50 `RX_BURST_AND_WAKEUP=0x0A`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDeviceDescription.cpp:110-121 — the `rx_modes` XML attribute is parsed with `strstr` onto exactly those bits, and `TRIPLE_BURST` also sets `RX_BURST`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:250 — `dev_desc["RX_MODE"]=GetDeviceDescription()->GetRxMode();` (the raw mask is what getDeviceDescription/listDevices returns). Descriptor example: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:3 `rx_modes="CONFIG,WAKEUP,BURST" rx_default="BURST"` → 14. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getDeviceDescriptions sets the legacy RX_MODE from `device.getListenerMode().getValue()`, and de.eq3.cbcs.protocol.hmip.networkmanagement.ListenerMode is a sparse enum.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF (rfd): ALWAYS=1, BURST=2, CONFIG=4, WAKEUP=8, LAZY_CONFIG=16 — a bitmask, reported verbatim. HmIP-RF: RX_MODE is the ListenerMode ordinal — PERMANENT_LISTENER=0, SINGLE_BURST_LISTENER=1, TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER=3, EVENT_LISTENER=4, EVENT_LISTENER_WITH_POWER_SAVE=5, CYCLIC_LISTENER=8, CYCLIC_AND_SINGLE_BURST_LISTENER=9, CYCLIC_AND_TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER=11, PERMANENT_LISTENER_WIRED=12, PERMANENT_LISTENER_BACKBONE=14 — an enum, not a bitmask.
reachesDevice.ourValue: One bitmask applied to every interface: 1/2/4/8/16, decoded at devices.go:166-171 into Always/Burst/Config/Wakeup/LazyConfig, and 0 rendered as "no rx mode" (rxModeInfo returns nil).
reachesDevice.finding:
The five bit values are exactly right for BidCos-RF and are settled at Tier 1: the enum is written as `(1<<0)`…`(1<<4)` and the CCU parses the device XML's `rx_modes` attribute straight onto them, then hands the raw integer to clients unmodified. Two BidCos details our block does not carry: `strstr(temp, "CONFIG")` also fires on the token `LAZY_CONFIG`, so a device declaring only LAZY_CONFIG reports CONFIG|LAZY_CONFIG = 20 — our decode reproduces that, matching the CCU; and `TRIPLE_BURST` is folded into RX_BURST, so triple-burst devices are indistinguishable from single-burst on this field. BidCos-Wired is silent: no RX_MODE, rx_modes or RX_* token appears anywhere under src/hs485d.

The rule is false one step wider. internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:594 assigns `hmenum.RxMode(dd.RXMode)` for every interface, and on HmIP-RF the CCU fills that same field from a different vocabulary entirely: DeviceUtil#getDeviceDescriptions sets it from ListenerMode's ordinal, a sparse enum with values 0,1,3,4,5,8,9,11,12,14 whose `getByValue` masks with 0xF. Consequences, each a real fleet value (pydevccu descriptor corpus, parent entries only): an HmIP mains device reporting PERMANENT_LISTENER=0 makes rxModeInfo return nil, so an always-listening device is rendered as having no receive mode; HmIP-eTRV-2/B/B1/C-2 report 11 = CYCLIC_AND_TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER and we render Always+Burst+Wakeup for a battery TRV; HmIP-ASIR/ELV-SH-WSM report 3 = TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER and we render Always+Burst; HmIP battery sensors reporting 4 = EVENT_LISTENER are rendered as Config. Where the boundary runs: the bitmask is correct for every device delivered by rfd (BidCos-RF, including CUxD-fronted BidCos), and wrong for every device delivered by the HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface.

One adjacent, unrelated observation while reading the write path: rfd's putParamset/setValue accept only "WAKEUP" and "BURST" as the rx_mode argument and throw XmlRpcException(-5) otherwise (RFManager.cpp:105-113 and :181-189). pkg/hmenum/device.go:102 also defines CommandRxModeLazyConfig, which BidCos-RF would reject; I did not check whether anything sends it.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the five bit values been wrong, RFDeviceDescription.cpp:113-117 would OR the ALWAYS/BURST/CONFIG/WAKEUP/LAZY_CONFIG tokens onto different powers of two than 1/2/4/8/16, or RFDevice.cpp:250 would transform the mask before publishing it — neither is the case. Had HmIP used the same bitmask, DeviceUtil would compose RX_MODE from an OR of mode flags; instead it assigns a single ListenerMode ordinal, and that enum's declared values (0,1,3,4,5,8,9,11,12,14) skip 2, 6, 7 and 10 — a pattern no five-bit OR can produce.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
CORE CLAIM UPHELD AT TIER 1 ON BOTH SURFACES. Every C++ and every HmIP citation reproduced verbatim, including the ListenerMode ordinal list and the 0xF mask. The strstr overlap is real (both `strstr(temp,"CONFIG")` and `strstr(temp,"LAZY_CONFIG")` fire on a LAZY_CONFIG token), and the write-path restriction to WAKEUP/BURST is verbatim. pkg/hmenum/device.go:102 does define CommandRxModeLazyConfig; I found no non-test caller for it, so nothing currently sends the value rfd would reject.

MATERIAL DEMOTION OF THE FLEET EVIDENCE. The candidate's consequence paragraph is sourced to "the pydevccu descriptor corpus, parent entries only". That corpus is NOT faithful for RX_MODE on BidCos. I counted 172 parent entries reporting RX_MODE=0, of which 104 are BidCos-RF types (HM-*, and the ELV order-number types '263 130'…'263 147', which rf_s.xml:50 declares as BidCos Schueco switch actuators). rfd cannot report 0 for those: the ctor sets rx_modes=RX_ALWAYS (RFDeviceDescription.cpp:29) and InitFromXml overwrites it only when the `rx_modes` attribute is present — and only 73 of 127 shipped rftypes XMLs carry that attribute; rf_s.xml and rf_es_pmsw.xml do not. A real CCU therefore reports 1, not 0, for HM-LC-Sw1-Pl and HM-ES-PMSw1-Pl. The corpus's 0 is an artefact of not applying the firmware default. So RX_MODE=0 in that corpus cannot be attributed to HmIP PERMANENT_LISTENER without knowing the device's interface.

WHAT SURVIVES ANYWAY. The HmIP examples do not need the corpus: PERMANENT_LISTENER=0 is what ListenerMode gives for an HmIP mains device, read directly from the enum, and rxModeInfo returns nil for 0 — so an always-listening HmIP device is rendered as having no receive mode. Values 3 and 11 occur in the corpus only on HmIP types (HmIP-ASIR/ELV-SH-WSM; HmIP-eTRV-2/B/B1/C-2) and are decoded by us as Always+Burst and Always+Burst+Wakeup respectively.

A COLLISION THE CANDIDATE DID NOT NAME. Value 12 is legal in BOTH vocabularies: on BidCos it is CONFIG|WAKEUP, declared by 28 shipped XMLs as rx_modes="CONFIG,WAKEUP" (I verified '263 135' = HM-PB-2-WM55 and ASH550 are BidCos devices reporting 12); on HmIP it is PERMANENT_LISTENER_WIRED. 14 collides the same way (BidCos CONFIG|WAKEUP|BURST on HM-CC-RT-DN vs HmIP PERMANENT_LISTENER_BACKBONE), and 4 (BidCos CONFIG vs HmIP EVENT_LISTENER). The field is therefore not merely mis-decoded on HmIP — it is undecodable from the value alone. Any fix must key on the delivering interface, which device_pipeline.go:594 has in scope and discards.

BOUNDARY: correct for every device delivered by rfd (BidCos-RF, incl. CUxD-fronted BidCos); wrong for every device delivered by the HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface. hs485d is silent — no RX_MODE, rx_modes or RX_* token anywhere under src/hs485d (re-verified), so the corpus's 0 for HMW-* devices is absence, not a value.

reachesDevice.title: The cached MASTER paramset is never invalidated by anything the CCU says
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:73-89 — `RFChannel::PutParamsetValues` writes the paramset, calls `CommitToDevice`, and on failure sets `config_data_dirty` and calls `GetDevice()->CheckConfigPendingEvent()`; it emits no callback. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:786, :793, :805, :817, :1177 — the complete set of asynchronous callbacks rfd makes: `newDevices`, `replaceDevice`, `deleteDevices`, `readdedDevice`, `updateDevice`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.h:47 — `enum{UPDATE_HINT_ALL=0, UPDATE_HINT_LINKS=1};` is the entire hint vocabulary. The only `ReportUpdate` call sites in rfd are RFChannel.cpp:756 and :868 (both UPDATE_HINT_LINKS, on link removal/creation) and RFDevice.cpp:1618-1620 (UPDATE_HINT_ALL after an OTAU rebuild, and only when the config option "Call UpdateDevice On OTAU Device Rebuild" is set — RFManager.cpp:219-220 defaults it to false, otherwise ReportNewDevice is used). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:480, :535 — the wired daemon's updateDevice calls likewise carry UPDATE_HINT_LINKS. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp CheckConfigPendingEvent — emits CONFIG_PENDING as an internal VALUES event only on a 0↔1 transition. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.IBackendApi declares the client callback surface (event, listDevices, newDevices, deleteDevices, updateDevice, replaceDevice, readdedDevice, system.multicall, firmwareUpdateStatusChanged); de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyNotificationHandler#handleCommonNotification dispatches DEVICE_EXCLUDED / DEVICE_INCLUDED / DEVICE_REINCLUDED / RECEIVED_STATUS_DATA(_TRANSACTION) / RECEIVED_ACCESS_POINT_STATUS_DATA / DEVICE_CONFIGURATION_PENDING_CHANGED / DEVICE_READY_FOR_UPDATE / DUTY_CYCLE_EVENT / CENTRAL_DEVICE_COMMAND / OEM_CONTAINER_EVENT / REPORT_DEVICE_TEST_* / EMC_DATA_EVENT, and #handleConfigurationPendingChanged turns the config-pending notification into a channel-0 CONFIG_PENDING value event.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: No callback carries a MASTER paramset change. updateDevice's only hints are ALL=0 and LINKS=1, and rfd emits LINKS only for link add/remove and ALL only after an over-the-air firmware rebuild behind a config flag that defaults off. There is no generation counter or timestamp on a MASTER paramset: getParamsetId returns the static description id from the device XML (e.g. "switch_dev_master"), which does not change when values change.
reachesDevice.ourValue: The SQLite row is the cache; the only removals are channel/device/interface deletion.
reachesDevice.finding:
The concern is confirmed at Tier 1, and it is stronger than the candidate states. A MASTER write from another source — the WebUI's device-configuration page, hmcli, any second XML-RPC client — goes through RFChannel::PutParamsetValues, which stores the values and pushes them to the device and then returns. It emits nothing. The one client-visible side effect is conditional: `CheckConfigPendingEvent()` is called only when `CommitToDevice` fails, i.e. only when the device could not be reached immediately. For a mains-powered RX_ALWAYS device the commit succeeds inline, config_pending never leaves 0, and a WebUI MASTER write produces literally zero traffic to any registered callback. For a battery device the daemon sees CONFIG_PENDING go 1 then 0 on the maintenance channel — an edge that names neither the channel nor the parameter that changed, and which our store does not act on. The HmIP legacy surface behaves the same way: its notification switch has no "configuration changed" case, and its config-pending path emits CONFIG_PENDING on channel 0 exactly like BidCos. (`LegacyBackendClient#updateDevice` exists on the HmIP side but I found no caller for it in that tree; that tree can hide a reflective or event-bus dispatch, so treat "HmIP never emits updateDevice" as unverified — "HmIP emits no notification that carries changed MASTER values" is what the notification switch does settle.)

So what our rule rests on: nothing the CCU says. The signals that do exist and could bound the staleness are the device-lifecycle callbacks — newDevices, readdedDevice (RFManager.cpp:786, :817, fired on re-pair), replaceDevice, deleteDevices — plus updateDevice(hint=0) after a firmware update if the CCU is configured to send it. Of the four causes the damage note lists, a re-pair and a firmware update are therefore detectable at the callback level; a WebUI configuration write and a direct device write are not detectable at all, by any means short of re-reading getParamset(MASTER). There is also no cheap comparand: getParamsetId is the paramset's static XML id, not a version, so a poll cannot be made cheap by comparing a generation counter.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the CCU notified on MASTER change, RFChannel::PutParamsetValues (or RFParamset::Put beneath it) would reach one of rfd's five XmlRpcCallAsync sites, or ReportUpdate would appear with a third hint constant. rfd has exactly five async callbacks and exactly two hint values, and grep for ReportUpdate across src/rfd returns three call sites, none of them on the paramset-write path — the check would have named the emitting line had one existed, the way it named RFChannel.cpp:756 for links.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
THE FIRMWARE HALF IS FULLY UPHELD AT TIER 1. Every citation reproduced verbatim, including the conditional nature of CheckConfigPendingEvent (called only when CommitToDevice fails), the two-value hint enum, the OTAU config default of false, and the HmIP notification switch. The candidate's caveat that LegacyBackendClient#updateDevice has no caller in that tree is also correct as stated — I re-checked and found the interface declaration and the client method, no invoker.

BUT THE FINDING MAKES A FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT OUR OWN CODE, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. The candidate writes that the daemon sees CONFIG_PENDING go 1 then 0 "and which our store does not act on". It does act on it. internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:77-130 installs `wireConfigPendingHook` on the central's EventCoordinator (wired at internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:472); on the CONFIG_PENDING True→False settle it reloads week profiles, re-applies operation-mode gating, waits `configPendingSettleDelay` = 10 s, then issues a targeted getParamset(MASTER) per channel of the affected device and persists the result into the very MasterValuesStore under audit (`refreshDeviceMasterCache`). That IS invalidation driven by something the CCU says, so the rule as titled is false for the interfaces that reach it.

BOUNDARY, NAMED. The settle path is gated by `hmenum.PushesConfigPendingFor(iface, productGroup) || iface.PushesConfigPending()` (auto_refresh.go:110-113), whose set is HmIP-RF + HmIP-Wired plus HmIP/HmIPW product groups on VirtualDevices. So:
- HmIP devices whose config write raises the CONFIG_PENDING edge: the cache IS refreshed, whoever wrote — including a WebUI write. The rule is FALSE here.
- BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, VirtualDevices, CUxD: `newMasterPollerForInterface` returns nil for pushing interfaces and otherwise builds a MasterPoller whose OnRefresh is scheduled POST-WRITE from our own putParamset (auto_refresh.go:262-300, device/channel_set.go:284-286). A poll of our own write detects nothing a third party did. The rule is TRUE here, and the candidate's central point — a WebUI MASTER write on a BidCos mains device produces literally zero traffic to any registered callback, because CommitToDevice succeeds inline and CheckConfigPendingEvent is never reached — survives intact and is the real defect.
- HmIP mains devices whose write commits without ever raising CONFIG_PENDING are uncovered too, but I did not establish from the HmIP tree when the pending flag is and is not raised; that part is unverified.

The rest of the reasoning is upheld: getParamsetId is the static XML paramset id, not a generation counter, so there is no cheap comparand; and of the four staleness causes, re-pair (newDevices/readdedDevice) and a firmware update (updateDevice hint 0, only if the CCU is configured to send it) are detectable at the callback level while a WebUI write and a direct device write are not.

reachesDevice.title: An unknown TIME_BASE silently decodes as one second, and preset encoding breaks ties by list position
reachesDevice.ourValue: timeBaseSeconds {0:0.1, 1:1, 2:5, 3:10, 4:60, 5:300, 6:600, 7:3600}, with unit=1.0 for any base outside that set
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: every LINK *_TIME_BASE in the descriptor corpus is TYPE ENUM, MIN BASE_100_MS, MAX BASE_1_H, VALUE_LIST ['BASE_100_MS','BASE_1_S','BASE_5_S','BASE_10_S','BASE_1_M','BASE_5_M','BASE_10_M','BASE_1_H'] — 8 entries, indices 0..7, matching our table exactly. One step wider the same *_BASE family is different: HmIP-SPDR MASTER EVENT_BLINDTIME_BASE is ['100MS','S','M','H'], where index 2 means 60 s and index 3 means 3600 s, not our 5 s and 10 s
reachesDevice.missingInput: whether a running CCU sets the service property Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal (code default false) — i.e. whether the legacy XML-RPC surface exchanges the ordinal at all or the label string. I could not read a shipped properties file for it; that half stays unverified.
reachesDevice.citation: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json — LINK *_TIME_BASE: TYPE=ENUM, MIN=BASE_100_MS, MAX=BASE_1_H, VALUE_LIST as above (2940 occurrences across 64 files, e.g. HMIP-PS.json, HmIP-BDT.json, HmIP-ASIR-2.json, ELV-SH-BS2.json); outlier HmIP-SPDR.json VCU1289997:1 MASTER EVENT_BLINDTIME_BASE VALUE_LIST ['100MS','S','M','H']. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.StringEnumToInteger. Absence check: grep TIME_BASE over ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml → 0 hits.
reachesDevice.finding:
Right-surface note first: LINK *_TIME_BASE is an HmIP-only parameter. It appears in 64 descriptor files, none of them HM-* (BidCos), and the string TIME_BASE does not occur in any of the 130 ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml. The bundle's firmwareQuestion pointed at rftypes and src/rfd, where the answer is simply absent; the authority for this surface is the HmIP side.

The base table: confirmed, and the ordinal→unit relation is read from the firmware rather than assumed. addDesriptionOfParameter sets VALUE_LIST = StringEnumToInteger#getEnumStrings() for every ENUM parameter, and convertParameterValue maps an inbound Number n to values[n] over that same array (rejecting n >= values.length as "out of range") and an outbound label to its index in it. So "index into VALUE_LIST" is the firmware's own ordinal, not a convention I supplied. Note StringEnumToInteger separately supports a sparse physical mapping (constructor with int[] enumValues, and an offset variant) — but that sparseness lives strictly below the legacy surface; what our SPA writes is always the VALUE_LIST index.

Consequence for the unknown-base fallback: on the surface ClassifyLinkParameter actually serves (LINK paramset, suffix _TIME_BASE), a base outside 0..7 cannot occur — the domain is closed by the 8-entry VALUE_LIST and the CCU rejects an out-of-range ordinal before it reaches a device. The unit=1.0 branch is unreachable there. Where it stops being true is one step wider: the sibling MASTER parameter EVENT_BLINDTIME_BASE uses a 4-entry list with a different meaning per index. Our classifier misses it on both counts — it requires the literal suffix _TIME_BASE (EVENT_BLINDTIME_BASE ends in D+TIME_BASE, not _TIME_BASE) and only runs on LINK — so the boundary runs exactly at those two conditions. Widen either and the table becomes wrong rather than merely unused.

The tie-break half of the candidate is not a firmware question, and it is not on a device path. The firmware defines the encoding of a (base,factor) pair; it says nothing about how a UI snaps an arbitrary second-count to a preset. And EncodeTimeValue has no production caller in the repo (grep: only its own definition and its internal DecodeTimeValue call). What ships is GetTimePresets → uischema_link.go:167 → hmapi.UISchemaTimePreset → ParameterTimePair.svelte, where onPresetChange writes preset.a / preset.b by list index — never by nearest-seconds. Within each of the three preset lists all 21/10/9 durations are distinct, so no two presets can even collide on an exact value. reachesDevice is true because that integer base is written to the LINK paramset, but the tie-break itself is unreachable.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had a ninth base or a differently-scaled base existed on this surface, at least one LINK *_TIME_BASE VALUE_LIST in the corpus would carry a different length or different labels. The corpus demonstrably produces that other answer: HmIP-SPDR EVENT_BLINDTIME_BASE comes back with 4 entries and a different scale, which is how I know the survey distinguishes the two rather than reporting one shape for everything.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD, TIER RAISED FROM 2 TO 1, AND THE BOUNDARY CORRECTED — THE PRIOR AGENT'S COUNTEREXAMPLE WAS THE WEAK ONE.

Right-surface note confirmed independently: `TIME_BASE` does not occur in any of the 127 rftypes or 15 hs485types XMLs. On BidCos the LINK time parameter is a single FLOAT in seconds (rf_s.xml: `SHORT_ON_TIME`, logical float min 0.0 max 108000.0 with special_value NOT_USED=111600.0) and the base/factor split lives inside the firmware conversion, not on the paramset surface. The base/factor pair is HmIP-only.

TIER 1 UPGRADE. The base→unit table need not rest on the descriptor corpus at all: the CCU's own easymode helper carries it as an ordinal-indexed <select>, hmip_helper.tcl:2847-2854, values 0..7 = optionUnit100MS, 1S, 5S, 10S, 1M, 5M, 10M, H — exactly our timeBaseSeconds. hmipHeatingClimateControlTransceiverEffect.tcl:49-56 emits the same list with class='BASE_100_MS' … class='BASE_1_H' on ordinals 0..7, which ties the descriptor VALUE_LIST labels to the ordinals in one Tier 1 file. And KEY_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:58 pins the domain on the LINK surface itself: `{7 range 0 - 7}`.

I ALSO GROUNDED AN INPUT THE PRIOR AGENT ASSERTED WITHOUT CITING. Its "index into VALUE_LIST is the firmware's own ordinal" rests on DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue, whose entire enum branch is gated on a static flag `replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal` that defaults to FALSE in the Java (set from ServiceProperties "Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal", default false, in LocalServer and HMIPServer). If that flag were off, the legacy surface would carry enum STRINGS and our integer table would never apply. The shipped CCU config sets it to true — crRFD.conf:47. That is the missing input; it now reads from the source instead of from the shape of the answer.

BOUNDARY, CORRECTED. The prior agent named EVENT_BLINDTIME_BASE (HmIP-SPDR) as the counterexample. That one is a MASTER parameter and never reaches ClassifyLinkParameter at all, so it is the weak case. The sharp one, which the prior agent missed, sits on exactly our surface: SHORT_SWITCHING_INTERVAL_BASE is a LINK-paramset parameter on HmIP-FAL230-C10 and HmIPW-FAL230-C6 whose VALUE_LIST is the shifted 8-entry table (ordinal 0 = 1 s, ordinal 7 = 1 day), matching hmip_helper.tcl's getTimeUnitComboBoxB. Our table would be wrong for every ordinal there. It escapes only on the literal suffix test at link_param_metadata.go:191-193 (`_BASE` matches, `_TIME_BASE` does not), i.e. the boundary is one substring wide, on the same paramset. Widening that test to `_BASE` — an obvious-looking cleanup — silently misdecodes it. The SPA repeats the same literal test (assets/ui/src/lib/channel/time-pairs.ts:188), so both sides are consistent, and both sides are one edit away from being wrong.

TIE-BREAK HALF. Confirmed, and stronger than stated: EncodeTimeValue has no production caller (grep over the repo returns its definition, its own DecodeTimeValue call, and three tests), and DecodeTimeValue's only caller is EncodeTimeValue — so timeBaseSeconds is unreached by production code entirely, and the unit=1.0 fallback is doubly unreachable. GetTimePresets (uischema_link.go:167) emits base/factor/label with no seconds arithmetic, and ParameterTimePair.svelte:75-79 writes preset.a / preset.b by list index. reachesDevice is therefore false for the decode table and the tie-break; the integer base that does reach the LINK paramset comes from the hand-written preset lists, not from this table.

reachesDevice.title: The 3-second test-fire duration claims HmIP "Test-Alarm" parity with no cited source
reachesDevice.site: internal/alarm/outputs/testfire.go:15-17 (used at :107 and :117 for the OnConfig.Duration and the stop watchdog)
reachesDevice.ourValue: 3 s, justified as parity with an HmIP "Test-Alarm"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: the CCU has no Test-Alarm. Its HmIP siren dialog is setAlarmDialogTitle = "Alarm auslösen", and its fixed duration list is 3 s / 10 s / 30 s / 2 min / 10 min plus a free entry (unit S or M, value 0–600). 3 s is the first and shortest entry. The device descriptor's own DURATION_VALUE DEFAULT is 0
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/msg/asir_setAlarm.htm (DurationSelect options 3_S, 10_S, 30_S, 2_M, 10_M, setDuration; DurationValue range hint "(0 - 600)"); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js:85-96; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/de/translate.lang.option.js:185 "optionUnit3S" : "3 Sekunden"; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/de/translate.lang.extension.js:685 "setAlarmDialogTitle" : "Alarm auslösen"; Tier 2 ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-ASIR.json VCU9333179:3 DURATION_VALUE {TYPE INTEGER, MIN 0, MAX 16343, DEFAULT 0, OPERATIONS 2} and DURATION_UNIT {TYPE ENUM, VALUE_LIST ['S','M','H'], DEFAULT 'S'}
reachesDevice.finding:
The named authority does not exist. There is no "Test-Alarm" action, button or string anywhere in the CCU's HmIP siren surface: the only alarm-firing control is iseAlarmSirenHMIP.activateAlarm, whose dialog title translates as "Alarm auslösen" and which writes DURATION_UNIT / DURATION_VALUE / ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION / OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION as a single Interface.putParamset to VALUES. Grepping the German language files for Testalarm / Test-Alarm returns nothing alarm-related. So the comment's parity claim is unsupported as written.

The number itself is nevertheless the CCU's own: 3 s is the first and shortest of the five fixed durations that dialog offers (3_S / 10_S / 30_S / 2_M / 10_M), i.e. what an operator gets by opening the dialog and firing without changing the duration. That is a real firmware-offered value and a defensible source for a short bounded activation — it is simply not "the Test-Alarm duration". The descriptor default is not a source either: HmIP-ASIR DURATION_VALUE declares DEFAULT 0 with DURATION_UNIT DEFAULT 'S', so the device default is 0 s, which cannot be an audible test.

Same file, one Tier 1 mapping worth having on the record because our own EncodeTimerDuration depends on it: the CCU writes DURATION_UNIT as an int with oUnit.S = 0, M = 1, H = 2, D = 3 (iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js:85), while the ASIR descriptor's VALUE_LIST is only ['S','M','H'] — the WebUI carries a fourth code the ASIR channel does not declare.

Recommendation for the comment, if it is rewritten: cite the dialog's duration list, not a Test-Alarm.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the CCU shipped a fixed test duration, iseAlarmSirenHMIP would write a constant instead of the dialog's selection, or a separate test action would exist — and the check does distinguish the two cases: the same file shows the CCU writing constants elsewhere (oUnit's fixed 0/1/2/3 codes) and reading the dialog for the duration. Had 3 s been absent from the CCU's own options, the DurationSelect list would have started at 10_S.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:

I re-ran the absence check with a negative control (below): zero hits for testalarm / test-alarm / test_alarm anywhere under www/ or src/webui/. The only HmIP siren firing control is iseAlarmSirenHMIP.activateAlarm, whose dialog title resolves to setAlarmDialogTitle. Verbatim from the language file, escaping and all: "setAlarmDialogTitle" : "Alarm ausl%F6sen" — note the prior agent quoted the decoded form, which is a paraphrase of the file.

The number is nevertheless the CCU's own, and slightly better grounded than the prior agent argued: 3_S is not merely the first option in the list, it is what the dialog actually loads. asir_setalarmdialog.js calls setTimeShortCut() from bindElements() at construction, and setTimeShortCut splits the selected option on "_" and writes value=3, unit=S into the duration fields. An operator who opens the dialog and confirms without touching anything fires a 3-second alarm. That is a real firmware-offered value; it is simply not "the Test-Alarm duration", because there is none.

The descriptor default is confirmed as no source: DURATION_VALUE DEFAULT 0 with DURATION_UNIT DEFAULT 'S' on all three ASIR variants — 0 s, which cannot be an audible test.

The collateral Tier 1 mapping is confirmed verbatim (iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js:86: `oUnit.S = 0; oUnit.M = 1; oUnit.H = 2; oUnit.D = 3;`) and it does ground our own encoder: pkg/hmenum/timer.go:29-35 declares TimerUnitSeconds=0, Minutes=1, Hours=2, which internal/model/custom/mixins.go:219-249 writes as DURATION_UNIT. reachesDevice.title: The MP3 chirp volume default 0.5 is a bare literal on a device write
reachesDevice.ourValue: 0.5, on a scale the site does not document, written as ParameterLevel
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: HmIP-MP3P channel 2 (our IPSoundPlayer primary channel) LEVEL: TYPE FLOAT, MIN 0.0, MAX 1.01, DEFAULT 0.0, UNIT "100%", OPERATIONS 7, CONTROL ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER.LEVEL
reachesDevice.citation: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MP3P.json VCU1543608:2 VALUES LEVEL {MIN 0.0, MAX 1.01, DEFAULT 0.0, UNIT "100%", TYPE FLOAT, OPERATIONS 7, FLAGS 1, CONTROL ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER.LEVEL}; contrast ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-OU-CFM-Pl.json, whose channels 1 and 2 declare only STATE/ON_TIME/INHIBIT/WORKING/INSTALL_TEST/SUBMIT and no LEVEL at all
reachesDevice.finding:
The scale question is settled and our value is safe on it: the parameter the chirp writes is LEVEL on the sound-player channel, declared FLOAT 0.0 … 1.01 with UNIT "100%" — a 0..1 fraction, so 0.5 is 50 % and neither inaudible nor full volume. The risk the reader named (a 0..100 or 0..255 scale) is ruled out.

What is not settled is the default. The descriptor's own DEFAULT for LEVEL is 0.0 — silence — so no firmware value backs 0.5. It is a product choice, and it is duplicated: chirp.go:73 has `vol := 0.5` and sound.go:348 has `const defaultVolume = 0.5` applied at :386-390 whenever `volume <= 0`. The second one also means our layer cannot express "write LEVEL 0" through PlaySound at all — a caller passing 0 silently gets 50 %. StopSound is the only path that writes LEVEL 0.

Right-surface note: the bundle's firmwareQuestion named the HM-OU-CFM-Pl family alongside HmIP-MP3P. That device is not on this path and could not answer the question anyway — it exposes no LEVEL parameter, only SWITCH.STATE and ON_TIME, and our SoundPlayer profiles (IPSoundPlayer, IPSoundPlayerLed) are registered for DeviceType "hmip-mp3p" only (internal/model/custom/profiles.go:1150-1167).
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had LEVEL been a percent or byte scale, MAX would read 100 or 255 rather than 1.01, and the corpus does report large maxima where they exist — DURATION_VALUE on the same device family comes back MAX 16343 and CURRENT_ILLUMINATION MAX 163830 — so the survey is not flattening every maximum to a small number. Had 0.5 been the device's own default, the descriptor's DEFAULT field would read 0.5 instead of 0.0.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD, TIER RAISED FROM 2 TO 1 FOR THE HALF THAT MATTERS.

The scale question no longer rests on the descriptor alone. The CCU's own easymode profile for the ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER channel — the exact channel role our IPSoundPlayer binds — writes LEVEL bounds as `range 0.0 - 1.0` for the DIM_MIN/DIM_MAX pair and `range 0.0 - 1.005` for ON_LEVEL, which is Tier 1 and settles both that the parameter is a 0..1 fraction and that MAX 1.01 in the descriptor exists to carry the 1.005 old-level sentinel rather than to extend the volume range. 0.5 is 50 %, and the 0..100 / 0..255 risk the reader named is ruled out.

The default half is confirmed unchanged and stays a product choice: DEFAULT is 0.0 on the descriptor and there is no CCU-side volume default of 0.5 anywhere. It is duplicated at chirp.go:73 (`vol := 0.5`) and sound.go:348/386-390 (`const defaultVolume = 0.5`, applied when `volume <= 0`). I verified the consequence the prior agent drew: PlaySound cannot express LEVEL 0 — a caller passing 0 gets 50 % — and StopSound is the only path that writes LEVEL 0.

Right-surface note confirmed by reading both files: HM-OU-CFM-Pl exposes no LEVEL on any channel (only SWITCH-style STATE/ON_TIME/INHIBIT/WORKING/INSTALL_TEST/SUBMIT), so it could not have answered the question. Profile registration confirmed at internal/model/custom/profiles.go:1159-1167: IPSoundPlayer is DeviceType "hmip-mp3p" only, primary channel 2. Worth adding as a nearby hazard the prior agent did not flag: the sibling IPSoundPlayerLed profile (profiles.go:1149-1157) takes channel 6, whose LEVEL is CONTROL DIMMER.LEVEL — same parameter name, same 0..1 scale, entirely different meaning (LED brightness, not volume). Nothing on the chirp path resolves there today, but the two are one profile lookup apart.

One more path detail: resolver.go:141-145 also pins Duration: 2 s on every chirp, so PlaySound writes DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE alongside LEVEL — the chirp is a three-parameter write, not a single LEVEL write.

reachesDevice.title: "CUxD closes after one request" and "nil is an empty string" are CUxD protocol claims with no reachable source
reachesDevice.missingInput: CUxD's own implementation — its connection lifetime after a request/response pair, and how it encodes a void return over BIN-RPC. CUxD is closed third-party software and the string appears in no file in ../OpenCCU-Base or ../OpenCCU. Nothing in either tree, and nothing in the descriptor corpus, carries it. Settling it needs either CUxD's source or a wire capture against a CUxD instance.
reachesDevice.citation: Adjacent surface only (the CCU's own BIN-RPC endpoints, not CUxD): ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/config_templates/InterfacesList.xml:5 `<url>xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001</url>`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:35 `const char XmlRpcServerConnection::BINARY_SIGNATURE[] = "Bin";`, :98-101 (binary framing: signature + 1 type byte + big-endian u32 length), :157 `_keepAlive = true;` in the binary branch, :222 `return _keepAlive;`, :354-364 (generateResponse writes signature + 0x01 + length + body), :408-414 (fault writes 0xFF); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:389-404 `toStream()` … :403 `return std::string();   // Invalid value`
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: (CCU's own BIN-RPC server) connection kept alive unconditionally for binary requests; a void/invalid return is framed as Bin + 0x01 + length 0 + NO body
reachesDevice.ourValue: client dials per call and server reads exactly one request per connection; WriteResponse(nil) emits Bin + 0x01 + length 8 + [type 3 (string)][length 0]
reachesDevice.finding: Both claims are about CUxD, and CUxD is in neither tree, so as written they are not performable — I am naming that rather than promoting a substitute. What the trees DO settle is the adjacent surface, and it is worth recording because it is the reference implementation of the same protocol: the CCU serves BIN-RPC itself (BidCos-RF is registered as xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001 and hs485dLoader writes the same scheme for BidCos-Wired), implemented in libXmlRpc. That implementation does the opposite of both of our claims. (1) Connection lifetime: the binary branch of readHeader sets _keepAlive = true unconditionally — BIN-RPC carries no Connection header, so the server keeps monitoring the socket and loops back to READ_HEADER after writing each response (XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:157, :215-222). It expects multiple request/response cycles per connection. (2) Void return: generateResponse frames result.toStream(), and XmlRpcValue::toStream returns an empty std::string for an invalid (void) value (XmlRpcValue.cpp:403), so the CCU emits a zero-length body — eight header bytes and nothing else. Our WriteResponse(nil) instead emits an 8-byte payload holding a zero-length string value. Those are different byte sequences for the same meaning. Note the reverse asymmetry this exposes in our decoder: ReadResponse calls readValue on the payload unconditionally, so a zero-length response body fails with a read error rather than decoding as void. That is not reachable today (our BIN-RPC client only ever dials CUxD; BidCos-RF goes over XML-RPC in our stack), but it is the shape a wire capture should be aimed at. Our per-call dial in client.go is safe either way — it works whether or not the peer keeps the connection alive; the exposed half is server.go:134-141, which reads exactly one request and closes, and would silently drop a second pipelined request from a peer that behaves like libXmlRpc.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had CUxD been present in either tree the search would have found it: the same grep pattern over both trees returned nothing for cuxd/CUxD/CUXD while returning concrete hits for xmlrpc_bin, BINARY_SIGNATURE and the BIN-RPC framing. So the negative result is a real absence, not a failed search — and it is why the verdict is not-performable rather than confirmed or contradicted.

reachesDevice.title: The COLOR-integer hue round-trip is asymmetric: read divides by 200, write multiplies by 199
reachesDevice.citation: Read (CCU's own control page): ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/rgbw.fn:30-31 — verbatim: `WriteLine( "if (colorVal > 199) {colorVal = 200; saturation = '0%'}");` / `WriteLine( "var convertedValue = parseInt(colorVal / 199 * 360); " );`. Same arithmetic in two further independent CCU paths: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/RGBW_Controller.js:52,55 (`var hsvVal = parseInt(this.curValue / 199 * 360);` … `if (this.showWhite && this.curValue == 200) { saturation = "0%"; hsvVal = 0; }`) and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/webui.js:18210-18215,18254. Write: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/extern/spectrum.js:1383-1386 — `toHMString: function() { var hsv = rgbToHsv(this._r, this._g, this._b); var h = mathRound(hsv.h * 360) … return parseInt(h / 360 * 199); }`, selected by `preferredFormat: "convert360To200"` (spectrum.js:1490-1493; set at rgbw.fn:37, RGBW_Controller.js:65, webui.js:18219). White sentinel on write: spectrum.js:959-964 `convertWhiteValue` returns 200 only when `(preferredFormat == "convert360To200") && (currentHue == 0) && (currentSaturation == 0) && (currentValue == 1)`. Descriptor (Tier 2, firmware-shipped): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_rgbw.xml:279-292 — `<parameter id="COLOR" operations="read,write,event" control="RGBW_COLOR.COLOR">` with `<logical type="integer" min="0" max="255" default="0"/>`, physical integer value_id="LEVEL", no SPECIAL entries and no `<conversion>`. Witness (Tier 3): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:456 `return color / 200 * 360, _MAX_SATURATION` and :472 `color = 200 if saturation < 0.1 else int(round(max(min(hue, 1), 0) * 199))` — the Python family carries the identical asymmetry, which is where ours came from.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: read hue = parseInt(COLOR / 199 * 360); write COLOR = parseInt(hue / 360 * 199); white ⟺ COLOR > 199 (read) / hue==0 && sat==0 && value==1 → 200 (write); descriptor COLOR is integer 0..255 with no SPECIAL
reachesDevice.ourValue: read hue = trunc(COLOR / 200 * 360); write COLOR = round(hue / 360 * 199); white ⟺ COLOR >= 200 (read) / saturation < 10 → 200 (write)
reachesDevice.finding: The comment's model is right and the arithmetic is not. Firmware confirms the hue circle is 0..199 with 200 as the white point: the write factor is 199 (spectrum.js toHMString), the read divisor is also 199, and the white test is `colorVal > 199` — matching our `c >= 200` exactly. But our read divides by 200 where all three CCU paths divide by 199, so the pair is asymmetric on our side and symmetric on the CCU's. Concretely: 135 of the 200 in-circle COLOR values decode to a different hue than the CCU's own UI reports — first divergence at COLOR=26 (ours 46°, firmware 47°), maximum 2°, and at the top COLOR=199 ours reads 358° where the firmware reads 360°. A second, smaller difference on the write half: the firmware truncates (`parseInt`) where we round (`math.Round`), so for 180 of the 360 hues we send one COLOR step more than the CCU's picker would (hue=1° → ours 1, firmware 0). Fixing the read divisor to 199 makes our round-trip converge and matches the CCU; matching the write to truncation would additionally make our writes byte-identical to the WebUI's. Note also that the descriptor declares COLOR up to 255 with no SPECIAL — 200..255 are simply undefined, and both we and the firmware fold the whole tail to white, so that half is already right. One caveat on scope: rfd applies no conversion to COLOR (physical is a plain integer), so the integer's meaning is defined only by the operator layer — the WebUI paths above are the authority here, and they are unanimous.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our read been right, rgbw.fn:31 and RGBW_Controller.js:52 and webui.js:18215 would read `/ 200 * 360`; all three read `/ 199 * 360`. Had the circle been 0..200 with 201 as white, toHMString would multiply by 200 and the white tests would compare against 200 rather than 199. Had the descriptor reserved 200 as a documented sentinel I would have found a SPECIAL block in rf_rgbw.xml; there is none, which is why the sentinel is a WebUI convention and had to be read there.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld as contradicted. I opened every cited file and every quote is exact, including the two truncation-vs-rounding details that carry the finding.

Surface check (the attack this project keeps catching, and it fails here): this is the same parameter, not a look-alike. rgbw.fn resolves its datapoint by `cObj.DPByControl("RGBW_COLOR.COLOR")`, and rf_rgbw.xml:279 declares COLOR with exactly `control="RGBW_COLOR.COLOR"` on the channel our profile maps. The device XML applies no conversion and declares only an opaque integer 0..255, so the CCU's operator layer is the only place the hue span is stated at all — and it is unanimous across three files written at different times, in both directions.

Patch check (which the prior finding did not do): rgbw.fn is patched twice by the distribution. I read both patched copies; neither touches lines 30-31. The /199 read is what ships.

Arithmetic reproduced independently: read divergences 135 of the 200 in-circle values, first at COLOR=26 (ours 46°, firmware 47°), maximum delta 2° (105 values off by 1, 30 by 2), and COLOR=199 → ours 358° vs firmware 360°. Write divergences 180 of 360 hues, ours one step higher (hue=1° → ours 1, firmware 0), because math.Round is half-away-from-zero where parseInt truncates. The prior finding's numbers are exactly right.

The defect is also internal, independent of which authority one picks: our write uses span 199 and our read uses divisor 200, so our own round-trip is unstable — write(270°)=149, read(149)=268°; write(359°)=198, read(198)=356°. Fixing the read divisor to 199 makes it converge AND matches all three CCU paths; matching the write to truncation would make our writes byte-identical to the WebUI's.

Scope, per notes/parity/by_design.md:3400 and :3449: RfDimmer_Color is registered for exactly one model, HM-LC-RGBW-WM (COLOR on VCU3747418:2), so the divergence reaches one device family. That narrows the blast radius but not the verdict.

One caveat I will state rather than paper over: what a given COLOR integer physically renders is decided inside the device, and the CCU applies no conversion. The WebUI is therefore the authority on the CCU's stated interpretation, not on the LED's response curve. There is no descriptor-level statement of the hue span anywhere; the operator layer is the strongest source available, and it is consistent in both directions.

reachesDevice.title: Two different CPV-to-level scales, both cited only to the Python reference
reachesDevice.citation: BidCos: ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/rf_ja_conf_644.xml — `<parameter id="LEVEL" …><logical type="float" default="0.0" min="0.0" max="1.0" unit="100%">…<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/></parameter>` and `<parameter id="LEVEL_COMBINED" operations="write" control="JALOUSIE.LEVEL_COMBINED"><logical type="string"/>…<conversion type="hexstring_bytearray" has0XPrefix="true" delimiter=","/></parameter>`. The scale itself: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger.cpp:56-66 `double dval=((double&)in+offset)*factor; if(dval>=0)dval+=0.5; else dval-=0.5; ((int&)*out)=(int)dval;` and :69-77 `((double&)*out)=(((double)((int&)in))/factor)-offset;`. LEVEL_COMBINED carries the physical bytes unscaled: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionHexStringToByteArray.cpp:63-95 (LogicalToPhysical) and :153-172 (`fromHexValue`). The CCU's own client applies the ×2: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseBlindShutter.js:294-305 `var level = parseInt(this.state) * 2, levelHex = level.toString(16) … dpValue = "0X" + levelHex; dpValue += ","; …`. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertCombinedParameter — case "L" → key "LEVEL", value = Double.parseDouble(pair[1]) / 100.0; case "L2" → key "LEVEL_2", same; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLevel — LogicalType.FLOAT, PhysicalType.INTEGER, DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0), range 0.0..1.01; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.DoubleToInteger#getStepGranularity returns 1.0/factor.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: BidCos LEVEL_COMBINED: comma-separated `0xNN` bytes carrying the PHYSICAL value; physical = round_half_away(level*200); decode = raw/200. HmIP COMBINED_PARAMETER: `L=<percent>`; LEVEL = percent/100.0 (logical 0..1), which the HmIP stack then encodes with its OWN factor 200. Both families' LEVEL therefore sit on the same 0.005 physical grid.
reachesDevice.ourValue: ConvertCPVToHMLevel = raw/100/2 (= raw/200); ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel = raw/100; ConvertHMLevelToCPV = fmt.Sprintf("0x%02x", int(math.Round(value*100*2)))
reachesDevice.finding: Both divisors are right, and the encoder matches the firmware exactly — but the reason given in the code is wrong, and that is where the rule will drift. (1) Divisors: confirmed. BidCos /200 is the device XML's own `factor="200"` on LEVEL, and LEVEL_COMBINED is a raw byte-array conversion that adds no scale of its own, so its bytes ARE the physical LEVEL. HmIP /100 is literally `Double.parseDouble(pair[1]) / 100.0` in the CCU's HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface. (2) Rounding: our encoder's `math.Round` (half away from zero) is the firmware's own rule verbatim — HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger.cpp:59-61 adds ±0.5 before truncating. The reference's `int(value*100*2)` truncates and is wrong; our documented divergence from it is the correct call. (3) The NARROWING: the candidate's premise — 'the two radio families really use different level grids' — is false. HmIP LEVEL is DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0), the same factor 200, the same 0.005 step. The boundary runs at the STRING GRAMMAR of the two combined-parameter parameters, not at the radio family: LEVEL_COMBINED transports the already-scaled physical byte, COMBINED_PARAMETER transports a percent number that the CCU divides by 100 into the logical value first. Our doc comment at converter.go:119 calls the HmIP one 'a BidCos CPV integer string', which is the same conflation. (4) Two live acceptance-set facts about the encode path (blind.go:346 / :351, which IS wired): `fromHexValue` requires each token to be EXACTLY 4 characters when has0XPrefix is set (HexStringToByteArray.cpp:155-158) — our `0x%02x` always produces 4 for a clamped 0..200, so we are inside the set, but a 3-character token would be rejected outright with nothing written; and the firmware parses HmIP `L=` with Double.parseDouble, so `L=50.5` is legal, while our `fmt.Sprintf("L2=%d,L=%d", int(w*100+0.5))` restricts us to whole percent — half the resolution the device offers, and coarser than the CCU's own HmIP UI, which quantises to 0.5 % (iseHmIPServo.js:99 `roundValue05`).
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the BidCos divisor been wrong, rf_ja_conf_644.xml's LEVEL conversion would have carried a factor other than 200 (the corpus does contain factor=1, 2, 10, 100 parameters, so 200 is not a constant of the format) and iseBlindShutter.js would multiply by something other than 2. Had the HmIP divisor been wrong, DeviceUtil#convertCombinedParameter's "L" case would divide by something other than 100.0 — the same method's "OT", "DV", "TC" and "H" cases divide by nothing at all, and "IMTL"/"SAT" divide by 100.0, so the method demonstrably distinguishes scaled from unscaled keys. Had the two families used different grids as the candidate assumed, createLevel would have used a factor other than 200 — it uses 200.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Verdict UPHELD, boundary widened in two places the candidate missed and one supporting citation withdrawn. Re-verified and confirmed: the /200 and /100 divisors, both quoted formulas character-exact (including that the firmware rounds half-away-from-zero, matching our math.Round and diverging from the reference's truncation), the 4-character token rule our `0x%02x` satisfies, and the candidate's central narrowing — HmIP LEVEL is also DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0), so the boundary is the string grammar of the two write parameters, not the radio family. WIDENING 1: the decode half of this rule is unreachable. ConvertCPVToHMLevel and ConvertCPVToHMIPLevel have no production caller anywhere in internal/ or pkg/ (tests only), and the firmware declares BOTH combined parameters write-only — rf_ja_conf_644.xml `operations="write"` and HMIPServer #addSpecialCommaSeparatedParameter setting IOOperations.WRITE — so no CPV is ever read back to decode. Only ConvertHMLevelToCPV is wired, via internal/model/custom/cover/blind.go:346. WIDENING 2, a fact worth keeping: the CCU's own client emits level first, slats second (iseBlindShutter.js:294-305), which is the order blind.go:346 uses; that ordering was read from the source, not assumed. WITHDRAWN: the candidate's claim that whole-percent HmIP writes are 'coarser than the CCU's own HmIP UI, which quantises to 0.5%' cites iseHmIPServo.js:99, which is a servo control, not a blind. The CCU's HmIP blind control never writes COMBINED_PARAMETER at all — iseBlindShutter.js `iseHmIPJalousieShutter.saveValue` and `saveSliderValue` issue `Interface.putParamset` with LEVEL / LEVEL_2 as doubles (state/100), and the slats slider is declared `step: 5`. The resolution point still stands on Tier 1 without that citation: #convertCombinedParameter parses `L=` with Double.parseDouble and #createLevel gives LEVEL a 0.005 physical grid, so our `int(wireL*100+0.5)` at blind.go:351 discards half the resolution the device can represent.

reachesDevice.title: The sender channel-type alias table is invented by this repo — the comment says the reference has none
reachesDevice.citation: OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/linkHmIP_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER.tcl:12-51 — the CCU's own sender-type resolution: `if {[catch {set x $dev_descr_sender(TYPE)}] == 0} { … if {[catch {source [file join $env(DOCUMENT_ROOT) config/easymodes/$ACTOR/$x.tcl]}] != 0} { catch {source [file join $env(DOCUMENT_ROOT) config/easymodes/NO_PROFILE.tcl]} } }`. The only rewrites the firmware performs are explicit and named: :14-29 KEY_TRANSCEIVER on HmIP-MOD-RC8 → SWITCH_TRANSCEIVER (CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE 2) or SHUTTER_CONTACT (mode 3), read from the device's MASTER paramset; :32-45 LEVEL_COMMAND_TRANSMITTER_{CO2,HUMIDITY,TEMPERATURE} → COND_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER_{CO2,HUMIDITY,TEMPERATURE}. Profile sets are files under OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/<RECEIVER_TYPE>/<SENDER_TYPE>.tcl; MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl, MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER.tcl and PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl exist as three separate files under 12 receiver directories. Concrete divergence: ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:44-45 `set PROFILE_1(SHORT_OFFDELAY_TIME_BASE) 0` / `set PROFILE_1(SHORT_OFFDELAY_TIME_FACTOR) 0` vs PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:44-45 `{0 range 0 - 7}` / `{0 range 0 - 7}`; SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:31 `set PROFILE_1(SHORT_JT_OFFDELAY) 6` vs PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:30 `set PROFILE_1(SHORT_JT_OFFDELAY) {6 5}`, and :26-27 `SHORT_CT_OFFDELAY/SHORT_CT_ON {3 0}` vs `{3 0 2}`.
reachesDevice.ourValue: MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER ≡ MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER ≡ PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER for profile selection; SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER ≡ SHUTTER_CONTACT.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: Three distinct sender classes with three distinct profile files per receiver, differing in the jump-table and constraint values they write. SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER is not a channel type the firmware knows at all.
reachesDevice.finding: The CCU keys link profiles by the verbatim sender TYPE and normalises only where it says so explicitly, per receiver, in a linkHmIP_<RECEIVER>.tcl file. It has no MOTIONDETECTOR↔PRESENCEDETECTOR alias. It ships all three names as separate profile files, and they are not interchangeable: comparing the three files across the 15 receiver directories that carry any of them, MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER and PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER differ in 10 of the 12 receivers where both exist (identical only under ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and STATE_RESET_RECEIVER). The differences are in the values ApplyLinkProfile writes: the presence detector's profile 1 leaves SHORT_OFFDELAY_TIME_BASE/FACTOR operator-editable over 0-7 where the motion detector's pins them to a fixed 0, and under SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the presence variant widens SHORT_JT_OFFDELAY from a fixed 6 to the acceptance set {6,5} and SHORT_CT_OFFDELAY/SHORT_CT_ON from {3,0} to {3,0,2}. Substituting one for the other therefore hands the operator a different jump table and writes it into the receiver's LINK paramset. The third alias, SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER → SHUTTER_CONTACT, is unfounded but inert: the literal SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER appears nowhere in OpenCCU-Base and no device in the descriptor corpus declares it, so that entry can never fire. Separately, the archive our code searches (go-openccu-data v0.1.3 data/profiles) carries PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER under 14 receivers but carries neither MOTIONDETECTOR key at all — the extraction dropped profile files the firmware ships. The alias is papering over that gap with the wrong file rather than extending the extraction.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the firmware treated these as one sender class I would have found either a single shared file (or a symlink/`source` indirection) for all three names, or an entry rewriting one to the other in the linkHmIP_* normalisation step. That step demonstrably can express such a rewrite — it does so for KEY_TRANSCEIVER and for the three LEVEL_COMMAND_TRANSMITTER_* types — and it names neither MOTIONDETECTOR nor PRESENCEDETECTOR.
