The file comparison likewise can return 'identical': it does, for the MOTIONDETECTOR/MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL pair under 7 receivers and for MD/PD under 2. It returned 'different' for MD vs PD under 10.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Firmware grounding upheld; impact narrowed on two counts. WRONG SURFACE (inside our own repo): the finding names `link_profiles_adapter.go:133-165 -> PutLinkParamset` as the alias table's write path. It is not. grep shows resolveSenderType/filterProfileDocBySender have exactly one non-test caller, uischema_link.go:126. LinkProfilesAdapter.ApplyLinkProfile passes the RAW sender type to linkprofile.Store.GetProfileByID, and store.go's sender lookup is a plain map index (`profs, ok := bucket[senderChannelType]`) with no sender aliasing — only a RECEIVER alias file (_receiver_type_aliases.json). So ApplyLinkProfile never sees an aliased sender; for a MOTIONDETECTOR_* sender it returns `profile id=%d not found` and writes nothing. The alias does still reach a device write, by a different route the finding did not identify: uischema_link.go:120-146 -> hmapi.UISchemaProfile -> ProfileSelector.svelte apply() (builds a patch of fixed values + range defaults) -> ChannelPanel.svelte:778-795 applyProfilePatch (stages into the LINK working values) -> the operator's channel Save, which is a LINK putParamset. That is the path to cite. COUNT CORRECTION: MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER and PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER both exist under 11 receiver directories plus hmip/ (12 comparisons, not 12 receivers + more); byte-comparing them, 9 differ and 2 are identical (ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, STATE_RESET_RECEIVER) — not '10 of 12'. THIRD ENTRY CONFIRMED INERT: the literal SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER appears nowhere in OpenCCU-Base and in no pydevccu device description; its only occurrence anywhere is our own extractor's sender list, so that alias can never fire. Archive state re-measured: PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER is a key under 14 of the 35 receiver archives; neither MOTIONDETECTOR key appears in any. The honest fix is to extend the extraction (fix the misspelled probe name, add the VIRTUAL form), not to substitute a different sender's file.

reachesDevice.title: The generic '_VIRTUAL_ → _' sender-type normalisation is a convention, not a value read from the archive or the firmware
reachesDevice.citation: OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/linkHmIP_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER.tcl:12-51 (and the same shape in all 28 linkHmIP_*.tcl files) — the sender key is `$dev_descr_sender(TYPE)` verbatim, sourced as `config/easymodes/$ACTOR/$x.tcl`, with only the explicit KEY_TRANSCEIVER and LEVEL_COMMAND_TRANSMITTER_* rewrites; no `_VIRTUAL_` handling anywhere. The firmware ships MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER.tcl as a file of its own under 12 receiver directories. Divergence from the non-virtual file: OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:25 `set PROFILE_1(SHORT_CT_OFF) {2 0}` and :27 `set PROFILE_1(SHORT_CT_ON) {3 0}` vs MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:25 `{2 0 1}` and :27 `{3 0 2}`.
reachesDevice.ourValue: Any *_VIRTUAL_* sender type is profile-equivalent to the same name with the _VIRTUAL_ token collapsed to _ (KEY_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER → KEY_TRANSCEIVER).
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: No such normalisation exists. The virtual and non-virtual forms are separate profile files with different parameter constraints; MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER vs MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER differ under 5 of the 12 receivers that carry both.
reachesDevice.finding: The firmware's sender-type resolution is a single verbatim filename lookup plus a short, explicitly enumerated rewrite list; there is no token-stripping step in any of the 28 linkHmIP_*.tcl files. The generic strip is contradicted at exactly the one sender type where it can fire. Enumerating the descriptor corpus, only two channel types containing _VIRTUAL_ are senders — MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER and STATE_RESET_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER; the other seven (SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, SHUTTER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER) are receivers and never reach this lookup as a sender key. For MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER the firmware carries a dedicated file under 12 receivers, and it differs from the non-virtual file under DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, STATE_RESET_RECEIVER, SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and hmip/ — in SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER by widening the SHORT_CT_OFF and SHORT_CT_ON acceptance sets, which is a difference in what gets written to the receiver's LINK paramset. Worse, the strip is third in resolveSenderType's candidate order, behind the c004 alias: for MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER the chain yields [raw, PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER, MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER, PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER], so if an archive ever carried both the presence set wins over the motion set the firmware would have picked. The comment's own example, KEY_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER, names a channel type that appears in neither OpenCCU-Base nor the descriptor corpus.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the firmware performed this normalisation, either no MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER.tcl would exist (the lookup would fall through to the non-virtual file), or a linkHmIP_*.tcl would carry a string-rewrite step collapsing the token. The rewrite step exists and demonstrably can express such a mapping — it does, three times over, for other names — and never mentions _VIRTUAL_. The file comparison can also return 'equivalent', and does for 7 of the 12 receivers; it returned 'different' for 5, including the constraint values that get written.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Firmware grounding upheld and independently re-measured: the sender key really is a single verbatim filename lookup plus an explicitly enumerated rewrite list, with no token-stripping step anywhere; MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER and MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER differ in exactly the 5 places the finding names (DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, STATE_RESET_RECEIVER, SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, hmip/) out of 12 receivers carrying both — that count is exact. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) The sender enumeration is wrong by one: the finding names MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER and STATE_RESET_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER as the two _VIRTUAL_ senders. Grounding DIRECTION at Tier 1 (SENDER=1, RECEIVER=2) and measuring the descriptor corpus, STATE_RESET_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER declares DIRECTION 2 — it is a receiver. Exactly ONE _VIRTUAL_ channel type in the corpus is a sender. (2) That makes the strip DEAD, not a live hazard, and the finding overstates it. For the one sender type it can see, resolveSenderType's candidate chain is [MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER, PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (c004 alias), MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (the strip), PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER]. The archive carries only PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER, so candidate 2 always wins and the stripped form is never the resolved key — the strip cannot change any outcome against today's archive and corpus. It is unfounded code that currently decides nothing; the wrong answer it would otherwise reach is already produced by c004's alias. The comment's own example, KEY_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER, I confirm appears in neither OpenCCU-Base nor the descriptor corpus.

reachesDevice.title: The optical alarm pattern defaults to the LAST entry of the device's light value list — a position, not a declared property
reachesDevice.site: internal/alarm/outputs/manager.go:475 (`p = lights[len(lights)-1]`) and internal/alarm/outputs/testfire.go:80 (same expression). `AvailableLights()` (internal/model/custom/siren/siren.go:213) returns the OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION VALUE_LIST verbatim, in declaration order.
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1, ordering: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SignalOptical — the enum is declared, in order: DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL, BLINKING_ALTERNATELY_REPEATING, BLINKING_BOTH_REPEATING, DOUBLE_FLASHING_REPEATING, FLASHING_BOTH_REPEATING, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_0, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_1, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2. Tier 1, the same order on the operator surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/msg/asir_setAlarm.htm:33-40 maps ordinal 0→DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL … ordinal 7→${stringTableAlarmConfirmingSignal2}, and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js:95 writes that ordinal as `{name:'OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION', type:'int', value: opticalSignal}`. Tier 1, semantics of the last entry: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:30 "stringTableAlarmConfirmingSignal2" : "Confirmation signal 2 - long short short" (:25 "Alternating slow flashing", :26 "Simultaneous slow flashing", :36 "Simultaneous fast flashing", :41 "Simultaneous short flashing"). Tier 2, per-device declaration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/{HmIP-ASIR,HmIP-ASIR-2,HmIP-ASIR-O}.json, channel :3 VALUES OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION — TYPE=ENUM, OPERATIONS=2, DEFAULT='DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL', MIN='DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL', MAX='CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2', VALUE_LIST identical to the enum above on all three. The same file's LINK paramset shows the firmware's own choice of an alarm pattern: LONG_SIGNAL_SELECTION_OPTICAL DEFAULT='BLINKING_ALTERNATELY_REPEATING' (index 1), SHORT_SIGNAL_SELECTION_OPTICAL DEFAULT='FLASHING_BOTH_REPEATING' (index 4) — never the last entry.
reachesDevice.finding: The firmware fixes the order and it is stable across HmIP-ASIR, HmIP-ASIR-2 and HmIP-ASIR-O (identical 8-entry VALUE_LIST, identical MIN/MAX). Our rule therefore resolves deterministically to the last entry, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2 — the third of three one-shot confirmation signals ("long short short"), not an alarm pattern. Every repeating optical alarm pattern the device offers is one of the four *_REPEATING entries at indices 1-4; the three CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_* entries at indices 5-7 are the only members whose names do not carry REPEATING, and the firmware's own LINK-paramset defaults for a signalling optical link pick index 1 and index 4. So the positional convention picks the entry furthest from what an optical alarm needs: an optical-only activation or optical test fire writes a confirmation blink pattern, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE goes true, the watchdog is satisfied, and the sustained alarm flash never happens. Scope note: the rule cannot misfire on HM-Sec-Sir-WM — that device declares no OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION at all (../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-Sec-Sir-WM.json: channels :1..:3 VALUES carry only ERROR_SABOTAGE, INHIBIT, INSTALL_TEST, LOWBAT, ON_TIME, STATE, WORKING; :4 carries ARMSTATE), so AvailableLights() is empty and `len(lights) > 1` is false. HmIP-ASIR-B1 is not present in the descriptor corpus; the HmIP-side enum is device-independent, so its VALUE_LIST can only be a prefix/subset of the same order. The sound fix is the one the acoustic half already uses: answer it in the model from the descriptor, choosing a declared *_REPEATING member (or refusing when none exists), not from a position in the flattened projection.
reachesDevice.ourValue: lights[len(lights)-1] = "CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2" (ordinal 7)
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: the alarm patterns are ordinals 1-4: BLINKING_ALTERNATELY_REPEATING, BLINKING_BOTH_REPEATING, DOUBLE_FLASHING_REPEATING, FLASHING_BOTH_REPEATING; ordinal 7 is "Confirmation signal 2 - long short short"
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, the last member of SignalOptical / of the declared VALUE_LIST would have been a *_REPEATING flash pattern, and the firmware's own optical LINK defaults would have pointed at the tail of the list. Both checks return the opposite: the tail is the third confirmation signal, and the firmware defaults sit at indices 1 and 4. The check can distinguish the two cases — it did.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD, with two attached claims demoted. I re-read every cited file: SignalOptical, asir_setAlarm.htm, iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js, the English string table and all three ASIR descriptors are verbatim as reported, and I confirmed AvailableLights() is the OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION VALUE_LIST copied without reordering. The positional rule therefore resolves deterministically to CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2 — a one-shot confirmation blink, not one of the four *_REPEATING alarm patterns the firmware's own LINK defaults pick (indices 1 and 4). Wrong-surface check passed: the WebUI writes OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION into the VALUES paramset, which is the same parameter and paramset our alarm write targets, not a LINK-paramset twin. I also grepped the two other readable Tier-1 HmIP surfaces named in the firmwareQuestion — ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/ — both are silent on OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, so no substitute source was available and none was invented. Two demotions. (a) The consequence narrative "OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE goes true, the watchdog is satisfied" is device behaviour: no CCU source says a confirmation signal raises OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE. The grounded damage is narrower and sufficient — the daemon writes a confirmation blink where an alarm pattern was intended. (b) The HmIP-ASIR-B1 scope note ("its VALUE_LIST can only be a prefix/subset of the same order") is an inference, not a reading; and it is the weaker form of a true statement — SignalOptical#getNames takes no size argument, so any list generated from this enum is the full eight in this order, and a device declaring a different list would not be using this enum. I checked the whole descriptor corpus: exactly three files declare OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION (the three ASIRs), all identical. HM-Sec-Sir-WM re-verified: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-Sec-Sir-WM.json channels :1..:3 VALUES = ERROR_SABOTAGE, INHIBIT, INSTALL_TEST, LOWBAT, ON_TIME, STATE, WORKING and :4 adds ARMSTATE — no OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, so AvailableLights() is empty there and the rule cannot fire.

reachesDevice.title: The WKP channel-to-user-slot layout (channels 1..16, odd=lock, slot=(ch+1)/2) is asserted in a comment, not read from the device
reachesDevice.site: internal/alarm/intents.go:467 (`wkpPairIndex`: `if err != nil || ch < 1 || ch > 16 { return 0, false }` / `return (ch + 1) / 2, true`) and intents.go:242 (`correlated := c != nil && known && codeID >= 1 && codeID <= 8 && codeID == pairIdx && now.Sub(at) <= wkpCorrelationWindow`). Routing is by parameter, not by model: intents.go:145-148 dispatches on hmenum.ParameterPressLock / ParameterPressUnlock.
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1, the pairing formula verbatim: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/control/function.fn:159-169 — `if (chn.HssType() == "ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER") { if (chn.Label() == "HmIP-FWI") { … ${chType_ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER} "#chNumber#" … } if (chn.Label() == "HmIP-WKP") { integer tmpChn = (chNumber + 1) / 2; … ${chType_ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER} "#tmpChn#" … } }`, with chType_ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER = "Access Control" / "Benutzer" (../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/{en,de}/translate.lang.channelDescription.js:7). Tier 1, the pairing on the config surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:7026-7028 — for HmIP-WKP, a channel that does NOT carry NUMERIC_PIN_CODE renders `${lblPinOfChannelLockA} [expr $chn / 2] ${lblPinOfChannelLockB}` = "The PIN code of the channel 'User <chn/2> Lock' is used." (labels at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.label.js:225-226). Tier 2, the channel list and the alternation: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-WKP.json declares VCU4273771:1 … :16 all TYPE=ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER, DIRECTION=1, with :0 MAINTENANCE, :17 ALARM_COND_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER, :18 SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE. ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-WKP.json: every odd channel 1,3,…,15 declares VALUES ['ACCESS_AUTHORIZATION','PRESS_LOCK'], every even channel 2,4,…,16 declares VALUES ['ACCESS_AUTHORIZATION','PRESS_UNLOCK']; MASTER NUMERIC_PIN_CODE exists only on the odd channels. Tier 2, the slot count: VCU4273771:0 VALUES CODE_ID — TYPE=INTEGER, OPERATIONS=5, DEFAULT=1, MIN=1, MAX=8, alongside USER_AUTHORIZATION_01 … USER_AUTHORIZATION_08.
reachesDevice.finding: All four assertions in the comment are grounded, and the pairing formula is character-for-character the one ReGa uses: `(chNumber + 1) / 2` with integer division, on the same 1-based channel index, for exactly HmIP-WKP. The 1..16 bound is the declared ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER channel span; the odd=lock / even=unlock alternation is declared per channel (PRESS_LOCK vs PRESS_UNLOCK) rather than assumed, and the PIN lives on the odd channel of each pair, which is why the config dialog tells the even channel it borrows `chn/2`'s PIN. The 1..8 CODE_ID bound is the WKP's declared MIN/MAX and matches USER_AUTHORIZATION_01..08. Two scope notes. (1) The router keys on the parameter, not the model, so wkpPairIndex would be applied to any device firing PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK; in the descriptor corpus only HmIP-WKP declares them, and HmIP-FWI — the other ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER device, which does have CODE_ID with MAX=21 and a 1:1 channel-to-user mapping (function.fn:161 uses chNumber, not (chNumber+1)/2) — declares STATE on its access channels, never PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK, so it cannot reach this path. Deriving the bounds from the device rather than the constants 16/8 would make that safety structural instead of incidental. (2) One predicate our code applies is NOT settled by any CCU source: the equality `codeID == pairIdx`, i.e. that the keypad fires the press on the channel pair whose index equals the CODE_ID of the PIN just entered. The CCU only relays the two events; which channel the WKP raises is device firmware. What the CCU does show is that both numbers live in one "User N" namespace with N in 1..8 — ReGa names channel pair (chNumber+1)/2 "Access Control N" and renders CODE_STATE=1 as "user: <CODE_ID>" (../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/maintenanceWKP.fn:91) — which is consistent with the predicate but does not prove it.
reachesDevice.ourValue: channels 1..16, pair = (ch+1)/2, codeID accepted in 1..8
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: ReGa for HmIP-WKP: tmpChn = (chNumber + 1) / 2; descriptor: 16 ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER channels, PRESS_LOCK on odd / PRESS_UNLOCK on even, NUMERIC_PIN_CODE on odd only, CODE_ID MIN=1 MAX=8
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the layout been wrong, ReGa's WKP branch would have carried a different formula (it carries a distinct one for HmIP-FWI — plain chNumber — so the file demonstrably distinguishes layouts), the config dialog would have named a different pair for an even channel, or the descriptor would have shown PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK in a different arrangement or a channel span other than 1..16. Each of those was checked against the source and none holds. For the `codeID == pairIdx` predicate the check cannot produce a different answer either way — no CCU source decides it — which is why that half is reported as unsettled rather than confirmed.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: NARROWED. Every one of the layout citations checks out verbatim — I read function.fn:159-170 (the formula is `(chNumber + 1) / 2` with ReGa integer division, guarded on exactly `chn.Label() == "HmIP-WKP"`), hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:7028 (`[expr $chn / 2]`, Tcl integer division, on the branch where NUMERIC_PIN_CODE is absent, i.e. the even/unlock channel), both label catalogues, the device description's 16 ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER channels, and the per-channel PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK alternation with NUMERIC_PIN_CODE on odd channels only. The two firmware formulas are mutually consistent: (2n-1+1)/2 = n and (2n)/2 = n. The FWI containment argument also holds — HmIP-FWI declares STATE on its access channels, never PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK, so it cannot reach wkpPairIndex even though the router keys on the parameter rather than the model (intents.go:145-148). So the title's rule — the layout — is grounded on Tier 1. I demote the id from confirmed because the predicate the production path actually turns on is not the layout. intents.go:242 requires `codeID == pairIdx`, and no CCU source states that the keypad fires the press on the channel pair whose index equals the CODE_ID of the PIN just entered. I searched the CCU tree for every use of CODE_ID and USER_AUTHORIZATION outside the string tables: only maintenanceWKP.fn:13/16-24 (which reads them for display) and maintenanceFWI.fn:14. Nothing binds a CODE_ID to a channel. The structural correspondence is suggestive — CODE_ID MIN=1 MAX=8, USER_AUTHORIZATION_01..08 and eight channel pairs all live in one "User N" namespace, and ReGa names pair n "Access Control n" while rendering CODE_STATE=1 as "<user>: <CODE_ID>" — but suggestive is not read from the source. Treat `codeID == pairIdx` as not-performable from CCU material and name it in the comment as an untested device-behaviour assumption; if it is wrong, no keypad press ever correlates and every arm/disarm silently lands in journalKeypadUnmatched. Secondary observation, not a defect claim: the 16 and 8 bounds are hard-coded constants rather than read from the declared channel span and CODE_ID MIN/MAX, so the FWI safety above is incidental rather than structural.

reachesDevice.title: reportValueUsage is classified as a read although the daemon uses it to mutate the CCU
reachesDevice.site: internal/client/reliability/classifier.go:63 (`"reportvalueusage": {}` inside readMethods, whose header at :49-51 reads "readMethods enumerates every method that returns CCU state without / Mutating it…") and internal/central/adapter/central_links.go:224 (`if err := caller.ReportValueUsage(ctx, ch.Address, valueID, refCounter); err != nil && chErr == nil {`, called per channel with refCounter 1 to create and 0 to tear down, the teardown also zeroing PRESS_LONG).
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1, BidCos: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:700-723 — the method's own documentation block states verbatim: "Diese Methode teilt dem Interfaceprozeß mit, wie oft ein Wert innerhalb der Logikschicht verwendet wird. Dadurch kann der Interfaceprozeß die Verbindung mit der entsprechenden Komponente herstellen bzw. löschen. Diese Funktion sollte bei jeder Änderung aufgerufen werden. Der Rückgabewert ist true, wenn die Aktion sofort durchgeführt wurde. Er ist false, wenn die entsprechende Komponente nicht erreicht werden konnte und vom Benutzer zunächst in den Config-Mode gebracht werden muß. Der Interfaceprozeß hat dann aber die neue Einstellung übernommen und wird sie bei nächster Gelegenheit automatisch an die Komponente übertragen. In diesem Fall ist dann auch der Wert \"CONFIG_PENDING\" im Kanal \"MAINTENANCE\" der Komponente gesetzt." The implementation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1425-1449 — `value_usage_map[value]=count;` then, on a non-zero total, `AddLinkPeer(central_device->GetListenerChannel()->GetSerial(), false); central_device->GetListenerChannel()->LowLevelAddLinkPeer(GetDevice()->GetAddress(), GetIndex());` and, on a zero total, `LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(central_address, central_channel); central_device->GetListenerChannel()->LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(...)`, returning `!(config_data_dirty || link_peers_dirty)`. Wired: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:680 and src/hs485d/HS485Channel.cpp:409 carry the same method. Tier 1, HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage — it reads the per-address metadata record whose id is the constant META_DATA_ID_REPORT_VALUE = "reportValueUsageData", writes the (valueId → refCounter) entry back via MetadataUtil#setMetaData, sums the entries, and then calls DeviceUtil#createCentralLink when the sum is > 0 or DeviceUtil#deleteCentralLink when it is 0, waiting on the device's response and raising a transmission-pending fault when the device cannot be reached.
reachesDevice.finding: reportValueUsage is a write on both south-bound stacks, and it is a write in two senses at once: it persists per-channel state (the BidCos `value_usage_map` / the HmIP `reportValueUsageData` metadata record, which is the very record we read back through getMetadata to compute the links' active state) and it performs radio configuration on the device — adding or removing the direct link peer between the channel and the central. The BidCos return value is explicitly a transmission verdict, not a query result: false means the device could not be reached, the setting is queued, and CONFIG_PENDING is now set on the device's MAINTENANCE channel. The classifier's own header says readMethods holds methods that return state "without mutating it", so the entry contradicts its own contract, and TestClassifyMethod pins the table rather than the semantics. Consequence as the reader described: link create/teardown bursts are paced on the read pool. Note this is not a hypothetical burst — central_links.go issues one call per press-capable channel and two per channel on teardown, each one a device configuration frame. The neighbouring entries in the firmwareQuestion could not be settled here: getSearchResults, getServiceInformation and clientServerInitialized appear nowhere in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd or src/hs485d, and only reportValueUsage among them appears on the HmIP legacy surface; classifying those three is a separate measurement I did not perform.
reachesDevice.ourValue: RPCClassRead (readMethods entry "reportvalueusage")
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: a mutation: persists the per-channel usage/refCounter record and creates or removes the device's central link; on BidCos returns false with CONFIG_PENDING set when the device is unreachable
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our classification been right, the rfd implementation would have read `value_usage_map` without assigning to it and would never have reached AddLinkPeer/LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer, the method's doc block would not describe establishing and deleting the connection with the component, and the HmIP handler would not call MetadataUtil#setMetaData or createCentralLink/deleteCentralLink. Contrast with a genuine read on the same surface, getParamsetId (XmlRpcMethods.cpp:690-697), which only fills a result string — so the check does distinguish the two classes.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD. Every citation is verbatim; I read the XmlRpcMethods.cpp block, RFChannel::ReportValueUsage in full, both hs485d entry points and the HmIP handler. reportValueUsage is a write on both south-bound stacks and in two distinct senses: it persists state (the BidCos value_usage_map, the HmIP "reportValueUsageData" metadata record — the same record we later read back through getMetadata for the links' active state) and it performs radio configuration, adding or removing the direct link peer between the channel and the central. The BidCos return value is a transmission verdict, not a query result: false means the device was unreachable, the setting is queued, and CONFIG_PENDING is now set on its MAINTENANCE channel. So the entry contradicts its own table's stated contract (classifier.go:49-51). I also verified the consequence rather than taking it on trust: internal/client/interface_client.go:665-668 routes RPCClassRead to cfg.ReadThrottle while writes go to cfg.WriteThrottle (:120-130), so link create/teardown bursts — one call per press-capable channel, two per channel on teardown, each a device configuration frame — are paced on the read pool. Wrong-surface check passed on both stacks: the BidCos doc block and RFChannel implementation are the rfd XML-RPC method our XML-RPC backend calls, and the HmIP handler is the legacy XML-RPC surface, i.e. the same method name on the same transport, not a REST or internal twin. One correction to the previous report's scope note, which was already honest and which I confirm: getSearchResults, getServiceInformation and clientServerInitialized appear nowhere in src/rfd or src/hs485d and only reportValueUsage of the four is on the HmIP legacy surface — those three remain unmeasured, not classified. Unrelated but worth flagging while in the file: the readMethods header comment at classifier.go:50 is textually corrupted ("without / Mutating it.py +") and no longer names a coherent source.

reachesDevice.title: RF CONTROL_MODE index→label table is hard-coded while every neighbouring ENUM is resolved through the descriptor
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:1645-1659 (rfControlModeLabel), called only from OnControlMode (:1594-1610) via the KindRF Subscribe branch (:1921)
reachesDevice.ourValue: 0=AUTO-MODE, 1=MANU-MODE, 2=PARTY-MODE, 3=BOOST-MODE, applied to every device our registry maps to profile RfThermostat / RfThermostatGroup
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: AUTO-MODE(0), MANU-MODE(1), PARTY-MODE(2), BOOST-MODE(3) on the CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER channel — but AUTO-MODE(0), MANU-MODE(1), HOLIDAY-MODE(2), INACTIVE-MODE(3) on the ST6-SH SWITCH channel that carries the same parameter name
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1 ordinal rule: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:37-65 (InitFromXml appends each <option> in document order unless it carries an explicit index= attribute), :95-110 (GetDescription exports TYPE="ENUM", MIN=0, MAX=options.size()-1, VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i]), :72-93 (EnforceConstraints accepts the int index directly and resolves a label string to its position). Tier 1 for the group device: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml:433-457 — channel id="1" type="CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER", status_parameter name="CONTROL_MODE" type="ENUM" min="0" max="3", valueList <value>AUTO-MODE</value><value>MANU-MODE</value><value>PARTY-MODE</value><value>BOOST-MODE</value>, virtual_device_type HM-CC-VG-1 (:8113). Tier 2 device XMLs: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2315-2323 (VALUES paramset cc_rt_ch_rt_values, parameter CONTROL_MODE operations="read,event" control="HEATING_CONTROL.CONTROL_MODE", <logical type="option"> AUTO-MODE default=true / MANU-MODE / PARTY-MODE / BOOST-MODE), rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml:2268-2276, rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:5166-5174 — identical block, no index= attribute in any of the three. Wire width agrees: rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2718 and :2735 carry CONTROL_MODE as index="14.6" size="0.2" in INFO_LEVEL / ACK_STATUS, i.e. exactly two bits. Counter-case: rf_st_6_sh.xml, switch_valueset, parameter CONTROL_MODE — <option id="AUTO-MODE" default="true"/><option id="MANU-MODE"/><option id="HOLIDAY-MODE"/><option id="INACTIVE-MODE"/>.
reachesDevice.finding: Confirmed for every family the CCU ships a definition for, and the table is exactly right there: HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM, HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU (Tier 2 device XMLs) and the HM-CC-VG-1 virtual heating group (Tier 1 groupdefinitions.xml) all declare AUTO-MODE, MANU-MODE, PARTY-MODE, BOOST-MODE at 0..3, and libhsscomm settles that the exported VALUE_LIST is the XML option order and that the wire value is the index into it. Narrowed on two edges. (1) Our table is keyed on the parameter name, not on the channel type; one step wider the same name carries a different list — rf_st_6_sh.xml's SWITCH-channel CONTROL_MODE has HOLIDAY-MODE at 2 and INACTIVE-MODE at 3, so index 2 does not universally mean PARTY-MODE. It does not bite today only because internal/model/custom/profiles.go routes rfControlModeLabel exclusively through the climate profiles; ST6-SH is not registered there. (2) internal/model/custom/profiles.go:96-124 also registers RfThermostat for device types bc-rt-trx-cyg, bc-rt-trx-cyn and bc-tc-c-wm; no device XML for those exists anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base (grep for BC-RT-TRX over the whole tree hits nothing outside the compiled jars), so their CONTROL_MODE list is unverified and the hard-coded table is an unchecked assumption for those three. Resolving through custom.EnumWireLabel, as HEATING_COOLING and TEMPERATURE_OFFSET already do on the same subscription path, would close both edges without changing behaviour on the four verified families.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the option order differed, the same extraction would have shown it: the option blocks are read verbatim from the XML, and the `index=` override that HSSLogicalTypeOption::InitFromXml honours is genuinely in use in this same corpus — e.g. the ERROR parameters declare <option id="NO_ERROR" index="0"/> and <option id="LOAD_FAILURE" index="3"/>, producing a deliberately sparse list with empty slots 1 and 2. So the check distinguishes dense-document-order lists from sparse ones, and it returned dense with no index= for all four CONTROL_MODE blocks. Had our rule been wrong, either an index= attribute or a different label sequence would have appeared.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed; I re-derived rather than re-read. Extracting every CONTROL_MODE parameter block in src/devicetypes by regex (not by spot check) yields exactly six declarations in six files, and they partition cleanly into the four PARTY/BOOST climate families and the one HOLIDAY/INACTIVE switch family — no third variant hides in the tree. The table is exactly right for all four climate families. Both narrowing edges survive, and I tightened each.

Edge (1) — keying on the parameter name rather than the channel type — does not bite today, and I checked this properly rather than trusting the original claim, because profile lookup is prefix-based, not exact (registry.go:434-447: exact match first, then longest-prefix-wins). Prefix matching is what makes HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM pick up hm-cc-rt-dn's RfThermostat, which is benign since rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml:2268 carries the identical list. It is also what could have let an unrelated device type slip into a climate profile. I enumerated all 19 Climate-category registrations and confirmed none is a prefix of "st6-sh" (ST6-SH's own type id, from its supported_types block at rf_st_6_sh.xml:8), so the HOLIDAY/INACTIVE list is unreachable from rfControlModeLabel. SimpleRfThermostat devices (hm-cc-tc, zel stg rm fwt) are KindSimpleRF and the Subscribe switch wires CONTROL_MODE only under KindRF, so they never reach it either.

Edge (2) is the stronger one and it holds under a harder search than the original: bc-rt-trx-cyg, bc-rt-trx-cyn and bc-tc-c-wm have no CONTROL_MODE definition anywhere the firmware can be read. Case-insensitive grep for BC-RT-TRX and BC-TC-C-WM over the whole of ../OpenCCU-Base returns nothing; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/replaceMap/rfReplaceMap.xml — the mechanism that would alias an OEM clone onto an existing type XML, and the obvious way this edge could have collapsed — contains no BC-RT entry; and no pydevccu descriptor or paramset carries the type. For those three registrations the hard-coded table is an assumption with no firmware behind it. This is a Tier-1-and-Tier-2-silent input, not a contradiction: the honest statement is that the rule is confirmed for four families and not performable for three.

The remedy named in the original stands, and I confirmed the precedent is real and on the same subscription path: climate.go:1857 and :1873 already resolve TEMPERATURE_OFFSET and HEATING_COOLING through custom.EnumWireLabel (internal/model/custom/replay.go:65). Routing CONTROL_MODE the same way would close both edges without changing behaviour on the four verified families, because for those four the descriptor VALUE_LIST is byte-for-byte the hard-coded table.

reachesDevice.title: Garage DOOR_STATE / DOOR_COMMAND labels are compared and written verbatim with no descriptor or firmware source
reachesDevice.ourValue: DoorStateUnknown = "UNKNOWN"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: "POSITION_UNKNOWN" — there is no DOOR_STATE label spelled "UNKNOWN"
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDoorState — with ventilation, enumStrings = {"CLOSED", "OPEN", "VENTILATION_POSITION", "POSITION_UNKNOWN"} paired with enumValues = {0, 1, 2, 7}; without ventilation, {"CLOSED", "OPEN", "POSITION_UNKNOWN"} / {0, 1, 7}; built as LogicalType.ENUM with a read+event IOOperations. #createDoorCommand — with ventilation, enumStrings = {LinkJumpTarget.NOP.name(), "OPEN", "STOP", "CLOSE", "PARTIAL_OPEN"} / enumValues = {0, 2, 3, 5, 8}; without, {NOP, "OPEN", "STOP", "CLOSE"} / {0, 2, 3, 5}; IOOperations.WRITE only. Registered in #initialise under ParameterMapKey("DOOR_STATE", "ventilation") / ("DOOR_STATE") and the same pair for DOOR_COMMAND. Export path: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#createParameterDescription sets VALUE_LIST from the converter's enum strings, and #convertParameterValue replaces the label with its position in that list (and an inbound Number with values[intValue]) because ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 sets Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true. Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MOD-HO.json — VCU3574044:1 VALUES DOOR_STATE {TYPE ENUM, MIN 'CLOSED', MAX 'POSITION_UNKNOWN', DEFAULT 'CLOSED', VALUE_LIST ['CLOSED','OPEN','VENTILATION_POSITION','POSITION_UNKNOWN'], OPERATIONS 5}; DOOR_COMMAND {TYPE ENUM, MIN 'NOP', MAX 'PARTIAL_OPEN', DEFAULT 'NOP', VALUE_LIST ['NOP','OPEN','STOP','CLOSE','PARTIAL_OPEN'], OPERATIONS 2}; identical on HmIP-MOD-TM.json (VCU6166407:1). Tier 3 witness on provenance: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:456-463 also spells it POSITION_UNKNOWN, so the divergence was introduced in our port rather than inherited.
reachesDevice.finding: Eight of the nine labels are verbatim correct — CLOSED, OPEN, VENTILATION_POSITION on DOOR_STATE, and NOP, OPEN, STOP, CLOSE, PARTIAL_OPEN on DOOR_COMMAND, all matching the firmware's enumStrings exactly. The ninth is wrong: our DoorStateUnknown is "UNKNOWN" and the firmware label is "POSITION_UNKNOWN". The consequence is smaller than the bundle's damage note assumes, and I checked rather than assumed: DoorStateUnknown is never matched against a wire value on any live path. Position() (garage.go:214-223) has no case for it and falls through to the same (zero, false) it would return anyway; closureStateFor (matter_closure.go:60-63) has `case DoorStateUnknown: return nil` immediately followed by `default: return nil`. The doorMode EnumSelect (garage.go:184-188) lists only CLOSED / VENTILATION_POSITION / OPEN, all correct. So today the wrong spelling is a dead constant plus one test (internal/model/custom/cover/matter_test.go:268) that drives a label no device ever sends — a bracketing test that will keep passing whatever the constant says. It should still read POSITION_UNKNOWN before something starts comparing it. Two further facts worth recording while the source is open. (a) The physical byte for POSITION_UNKNOWN is 7 and for PARTIAL_OPEN is 8, but the value the daemon sees is the ordinal into VALUE_LIST (3 and 4 respectively), not the physical value — DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue with the crRFD.conf flag does the translation, so custom.EnumLabelValue's positional resolution is on the right surface. (b) On a drive without the ventilation option the list is only three long and PARTIAL_OPEN does not exist at all, so Vent() must stay gated on Capabilities.SupportsVent as it is.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: The extraction prints each parameter's VALUE_LIST verbatim from two independent surfaces, and it does return different spellings for different parameters in the same run — ACTIVITY_STATE comes back with a bare 'UNKNOWN' as its first entry while DOOR_STATE comes back with 'POSITION_UNKNOWN' as its last. Had our spelling been right, 'UNKNOWN' would have appeared in the DOOR_STATE list from both the firmware factory and the descriptor corpus; it appeared in neither. The ventilation/non-ventilation split is likewise a value the check produced rather than assumed.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld as contradicted, and the original's damage assessment survives a harder look — which is the part I most expected to break, since "the wrong constant is harmless" is exactly the claim that usually turns out to be optimistic.

Eight of nine labels are verbatim correct: CLOSED, OPEN, VENTILATION_POSITION on DOOR_STATE, and NOP, OPEN, STOP, CLOSE, PARTIAL_OPEN on DOOR_COMMAND. The ninth is wrong — ours is "UNKNOWN", the firmware's is "POSITION_UNKNOWN".

It is genuinely dead, and I established that from the read path rather than by grepping for the constant. DOOR_STATE arrives as an ordinal and is resolved to a label through custom.EnumLabelValue before OnState sees it (garage.go:365-366: `if label, ok := custom.EnumLabelValue(g.doorStateDp); ok { g.OnState(DoorState(label)) }`). So a real drive in that state produces DoorState("POSITION_UNKNOWN"), which is unequal to DoorStateUnknown and falls to the default arm everywhere. The two arms it could have reached both already return the same thing: closureStateFor's `case DoorStateUnknown: return nil` sits immediately above `default: return nil`, and Position() has no case for it and returns (zero, false) either way. The whole-repo usage set is three sites — the declaration, that one Matter case, a nolint comment — plus internal/model/custom/cover/matter_test.go:268, which drives a label no device can send and will therefore stay green whatever the constant says. A textbook bracketing test.

The write path cannot carry the wrong spelling either: command() writes string(c) where c is a DoorCommand, and the doorMode EnumSelect (garage.go:184-188) lists only CLOSED / VENTILATION_POSITION / OPEN, all correct.

It should still be corrected before something starts comparing it, and the fix is a one-token rename with no behavioural surface.

Two facts worth recording while the source is open, both of which I confirmed independently. (a) The physical byte for POSITION_UNKNOWN is 7 and for PARTIAL_OPEN is 8, but what the daemon sees is the ordinal into the value list (3 and 4), because the two-array StringEnumToInteger maps physical→label and DeviceUtil then maps label→position; so custom.EnumLabelValue's positional resolution is on the correct surface, and a client decoding the physical value directly would be wrong. (b) On a drive without the ventilation option the list is three long and PARTIAL_OPEN does not exist at all, so Vent() must stay gated on Capabilities.SupportsVent as it is. I also checked for an RF-side counterpart that would narrow the rule: there is none — DOOR_STATE and DOOR_COMMAND appear nowhere in src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}, so this is HmIP-only, and the descriptor corpus confirms the parameter pair exists on exactly two device types.

reachesDevice.title: The WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE value list is a comment, not a source
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/safety/classify.go:42-44 (waterStateActiveValues), consumed at :77-81 and narrowed by internal/model/safety/activation.go ActiveFromRaw
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 2 (device XML the firmware ships): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_wds_v1_1.xml, channel index=1 type="WATERDETECTIONSENSOR", paramset VALUES id="wds_ch_values": `<parameter id="STATE" operations="read,event"><logical type="option"><option id="DRY" /><option id="WET"/><option id="WATER"/></logical>` with `<conversion type="option_integer"><value_map device_value="0" parameter_value="0"/><value_map device_value="100" parameter_value="1" mask="0x00"/><value_map device_value="200" parameter_value="2"/></conversion>`; identical in rf_wds_v1_0.xml (there DRY carries default="true"). Both files declare supported_types HM-Sec-WDS and HM-Sec-WDS-2. Tier 1 (operator-facing semantics): ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/stringtable_de.txt:2143 `WATERDETECTIONSENSOR|STATE=DRY`, :2144 `…=WATER`, :2165 `…=WET` — exactly three keys, no others; resolved at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:914-916 `"stringTableWDSStateDry":"Dry"`, `"stringTableWDSStateWater":"Water level detected"`, `"stringTableWDSStateWet":"Humidity detected"`.
reachesDevice.ourValue: VALUE_LIST [DRY, WET, WATER]; active = {WET, WATER}
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: VALUE_LIST [DRY, WET, WATER] in that order; DRY="Dry", WET="Humidity detected", WATER="Water level detected"
reachesDevice.finding: Both the declared list and its order match our comment exactly, on both firmware revisions of the device (v1_0 and v1_1), and the CCU's own operator strings confirm the semantics: WET is moisture detected and WATER is a detected water level — both mean water present — while DRY (index 0) is the idle state. The active set {WET, WATER} is therefore right and complete. The wire values are 0/100/200 but the CCU's option_integer conversion maps them to parameter values 0/1/2 before XML-RPC, so ActiveFromRaw's index narrowing against the device's declared VALUE_LIST reads index 1 -> WET and index 2 -> WATER correctly. Worth noting for the comment: order is a per-parameter property, not a global one — the same device's MASTER parameters spell the same tokens in three different orders (MSG_FOR_POS_A [NO_MSG, DRY], MSG_FOR_POS_B [NO_MSG, DRY, WATER, WET], MSG_FOR_POS_C [NO_MSG, WATER, WET]), so the rule is safe only because ActiveFromRaw resolves the index against the device's own list rather than against this constant.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the list been e.g. [DRY, WET] or used different spellings, the `<logical type="option">` block in rf_wds_v1_0/v1_1.xml would have carried different or fewer `<option id=…>` tokens, and the stringtable would have carried a different set of `WATERDETECTIONSENSOR|STATE=` keys. I enumerated every such key in the tree: exactly DRY, WATER, WET and nothing else. Had WET meant something other than water present, translate.lang.stringtable.js would have given it a non-water label; it says "Humidity detected".
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Upheld on the half the title names, and demoted on the half that actually fires an alarm. What I checked and confirms: the declared list and its order are identical on both shipped revisions of the device (v1_0 and v1_1) and in the runtime descriptor, and the CCU's own three operator strings carry the semantics the comment assumes. I also closed the gap the previous pass left open by assumption: it asserted "the CCU's option_integer conversion maps them to parameter values 0/1/2 before XML-RPC, so index narrowing reads index 1 -> WET" without citing where position-equals-value is written down. It is written down — HSSLogicalTypeOption::InitFromXml/GetDescription build VALUE_LIST positionally and pad sparse option indices with empty strings — so ActiveFromRaw's index narrowing against the device's own list is grounded, not conventional. Two corrections to the previous citation: (a) v1_0 declares only supported_type HM-Sec-WDS; only v1_1 declares HM-Sec-WDS and HM-Sec-WDS-2 (rf_wds_v1_0.xml:8-13 vs rf_wds_v1_1.xml:8-17), so "both files declare" is wrong; (b) nothing in the firmware classifies WET or WATER as an ALARM state. The CCU's alarm handling for this channel is per-installation link/program configuration; the only firmware statement about these values is what the labels mean. So {WET, WATER} = active is our product reading of two operator strings, correct and defensible but not a firmware fact, and the comment should not read as though the CCU declared an active set. Boundary: WATERDETECTIONSENSOR is declared in exactly two shipped device XMLs (rf_wds_v1_0.xml, rf_wds_v1_1.xml) and in one descriptor model; the rule is verified for HM-Sec-WDS / HM-Sec-WDS-2 only. The HmIP water sensor takes the separate WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER boolean path in the same table and is untouched by this.

reachesDevice.title: The CCU backup-restore CGI contract (endpoint, `@sid@` wrapping, `action` in two places) rests on no cited source
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_security.cgi:1026-1028 — `form "$env(SCRIPT_NAME)?sid=$sid" name=backup_form {target=config_upload_iframe} enctype=multipart/form-data method=post { export action=backup_upload  file_button backup_file size=20 maxlength=1000000 }`. Receiver: :1510-1516 `proc action_backup_upload {} { … import_file -client backup_file; file rename -force -- [lindex $backup_file 0] "/tmp/new_config.tar" }`, which then chains (:1523) `dlgPopup.LoadFromFile(url, "action=backup_restore_check")`; the actual restore is :511 `proc action_backup_restore_go {}` and needs the system security key (:505 `"action=backup_restore_go&key="+…`). Dispatch: :1589-1601 `cgi_input; set action "put_page"; catch { import action }; if {[session_requestisvalid 8] > 0} then action_$action`. Session id form: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/tcl/eq3_old/session.tcl:464 `set sid "@$sid@"` and :312 `if { ![regexp "$sidname=(@\[A-Za-z0-9\]*@)" $queryparams dummy querysid] }`. Newer OCCU stand that ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0163-WebUI-ImprovedFileUploadButton.patch:133 carries as unchanged context: `form "/config/fileupload.ccc?sid=$sid&action=backup_upload&url=$env(SCRIPT_NAME)" name=backup_form … { file_button backup_file … }`.
reachesDevice.ourValue: POST /config/cp_security.cgi?sid=@<sid>@&action=restore_backup, multipart field "file", plus a second `action=restore_backup` in the body
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: POST to cp_security.cgi?sid=@<sid>@ with `action=backup_upload` as a POST field and the payload in field `backup_file` (older stand), or POST /config/fileupload.ccc?sid=@<sid>@&action=backup_upload&url=/config/cp_security.cgi with field `backup_file` (newer stand). `restore_backup` occurs nowhere in either tree.
reachesDevice.finding: Four points, three of them wrong. (1) Endpoint /config/cp_security.cgi — correct on the older stand; on the OCCU stand the OpenCCU distribution patches, the upload form already posts to /config/fileupload.ccc and passes the CGI back as `url=`, so the endpoint is version-dependent. (2) `@`-wrapping of the sid — CORRECT and required: the canonical session id literally contains the delimiters (session.tcl:464 `set sid "@$sid@"`), and the query parser only accepts an @-wrapped value (:312), so a bare sid is rejected. (3) The action value is wrong: the firmware verb is `backup_upload`; `restore_backup` does not appear anywhere in OpenCCU-Base or in the ~200 OpenCCU patches. Because the CGI dispatches by string concatenation (`action_$action`, :1601) an unknown action raises a Tcl "invalid command name action_restore_backup" rather than a clean error. (4) The file field is wrong: the firmware reads `import_file -client backup_file`, i.e. the field must be named `backup_file`, not `file`. Two further contract facts our code does not model: the CGI requires user level 8 (`session_requestisvalid 8`), and upload is only step one of three — `backup_upload` merely stores /tmp/new_config.tar; `backup_restore_check` validates the archive signature and `backup_restore_go` performs the restore and needs the system security key. So even with the field and action fixed, a single POST would upload and never restore, which is exactly the silent-acceptance failure the candidate feared. Sending `action` in both the query and the body is not itself fatal (cgi_input merges both), but it is redundant — the firmware sends it once, as a POST field on the older stand and as a query parameter on the newer one.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had `restore_backup` and `file` been the firmware's names, a tree-wide grep for those literals would have hit in cp_security.cgi or in the patch set. It returns nothing for `restore_backup` anywhere, while `backup_upload` hits at cp_security.cgi:1027 and :1510 and in 0007/0163 of the patch set, and `backup_file` hits at :1027 and :1515. Had the sid needed to be bare, session.tcl:312's regexp would not require the @ delimiters and :464 would not add them.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Upheld as contradicted; every cited line verifies verbatim, and I re-ran the decisive negative search myself. `restore_backup` appears exactly once anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base plus ../OpenCCU, in an unrelated file — the recovery-system's own upload form (../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/package/recovery-system/external/package/hm-platform/rootfs-overlay/www/index.cgi:74, `action="cgi-bin/restore_backup.cgi"`), which is the separate recovery boot mode, not the CCU's config CGI our restorer posts to. So: the action verb is wrong (firmware: `backup_upload`), the multipart field name is wrong (firmware: `backup_file`, read by `import_file -client backup_file`), and the endpoint is stand-dependent (cp_security.cgi on the OpenCCU-Base stand, /config/fileupload.ccc on the newer OCCU stand the distribution patches — fileupload.ccc does not exist in OpenCCU-Base, so the newer stand's receiver cannot be read here). The one point our code has right is the `@`-wrapping: the canonical sid literally contains the delimiters and the query parser only accepts an @-wrapped value. Two claims in the previous pass I could NOT confirm and am demoting to inference: (a) "the CGI requires user level 8" — `session_requestisvalid` has no definition anywhere in either tree, only call sites, whose arguments are 0 and 8; the literal is there, the meaning of 8 is not read from any source; (b) "an unknown action raises a Tcl 'invalid command name' rather than a clean error", and by extension that the CCU answers HTTP 200 — `cgi_eval` is likewise not defined in this tree, so the status code an undefined `action_*` produces cannot be established here. What IS readable and sufficient: no `action_restore_backup` proc exists, so the upload is never processed. Additional defect on the same surface that the previous pass did not name: the doc comment at backup_restorer.go:36-39 ("The CCU runs the restore asynchronously and reboots when done; the HTTP response only confirms that the upload was accepted") is false in a second way — even a correctly-formed backup_upload only writes /tmp/new_config.tar; the restore requires backup_restore_check and then backup_restore_go with the system security key, neither of which our code sends.

reachesDevice.title: The climate channel-type candidate set and the schedule-domain classification tables are unanchored
reachesDevice.citation: Complete WEEK_PROFILE set + families: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:265-271 and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/hmip/{BLIND,DIMMER,DIMMER_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR,SERVO,SWITCH,UNIVERSAL_LIGHT,WATER_SWITCH}_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl (line 18/20/21/22/24 each, the `getHmIPWeeklyProgram … '<family>'` argument); ramp/level rendering ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:687-690,695,708-709 and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:26-38; lock branch :285,:317,:1899-2014; climate profile params ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/{rf_cc_rt_dn.xml,rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml,rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml,rf_cc_tc.xml,rf_cc_tc_le_v1_9.xml}; HmIP names HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createWeekProgramParameterNames; Tier 2 ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-HDM1.json, HmIP-HDM2.json
reachesDevice.ourValue: SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE -> "valve" (strips level_2 and ramp_time); WATER_SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE -> "valve"; climateScheduleChannelTypes = {CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER, CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR, HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER} described as "carry the climate week-profile paramset"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE -> family 'dimmer', WITH a ramp-time field (lblWPServoRamptime, "Geschwindigkeit/Fahrzeit") and a level field (lblWPServoPos, "Servoposition"); WATER_SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE -> family 'switch'; CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER carries no ENDTIME_/TEMPERATURE_ parameters in any shipped device XML; CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR carries its profile as TIMEOUT_<DAY>_<N> / TEMPERATUR_<DAY>_<N> (no trailing E)
reachesDevice.finding: The firmware's own set of `*_WEEK_PROFILE` channel types is exactly seven — DIMMER, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT, DIMMER_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR, SWITCH, WATER_SWITCH, BLIND, SERVO (JS constants :265-271, one easymode .tcl each) — and each easymode declares its actor family as the fifth argument to getHmIPWeeklyProgram. Confirmed: BLIND->'blind' (our cover), DIMMER->'dimmer' (light; firmware switches to 'window' for HmIP-MOD-WD-VK, a boundary we fold into light), DIMMER_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR->'dimmer' (light), UNIVERSAL_LIGHT->'dimmer' (light), SWITCH->'switch' (switch). Contradicted with a consequence: SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:18 passes 'dimmer', and the editor renders a ramp-time input for chnType SERVO (JS:687-690, label lblWPServoRamptime) plus a level input (:708-709); hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:33-38 exposes 01_WP_RAMP_TIME_FACTOR MIN/MAX for the 'dimmer' family. Our "valve" bucket strips ramp_time (schedules.go:719), so a SERVO schedule round-trips without its travel time. WATER_SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:20 passes 'switch' where we say "valve" — no consequence, both buckets strip the same fields. SHADING_WEEK_PROFILE does not exist in this firmware at all (HmIP-HDM1/HDM2 absent); it is a Tier-2-only type, so its "cover" bucket is not firmware-grounded. Lock precedence is confirmed on a different discriminator: the firmware also refuses to decide from the channel type — SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:21,47 passes 'switch' for an HmIP-DLD, and the JS then branches on DEVICE TYPE (`isDoorLockDrive` :317 for HmIP-DLD/-A/-S, `isDLP` :285 for HmIP-DLP) to render the lock pickers (:1899-2014). Our "any DOOR_LOCK*/KEYMATIC channel wins" is a different but same-axis rule; note the firmware treats DLD and DLP as two distinct encodings, where we have one "lock" bucket. On climateScheduleChannelTypes: a sweep of src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types} finds only five XMLs with a weekly climate profile. rf_cc_rt_dn(.bom) put bare ENDTIME_/TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_<N> (182 params) in the DEVICE master `cc_rt_dev_master`, rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu puts P1_..P3_ prefixed ones (546) in `tc_it_dev_master` — never on the CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER channel, so that entry's stated justification is wrong (harmless: Path 2 probes the paramset and Path 3 catches the device root). rf_cc_tc(.le_v1_9) DO put a profile on the CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR channel's MASTER `cc_tc_ch_master`, but named TIMEOUT_/TEMPERATUR_ — neither matches slotPattern's (ENDTIME|TEMPERATURE), so that candidate can never resolve. HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER is confirmed on both tiers (HmIP names P<n>_{TEMPERATURE,ENDTIME}_<DAY>_<1..13>, weekProgramNumber 1-based; 20 devices in the descriptor corpus). No climate-profile-carrying channel type is missing from the set.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had SERVO belonged to the firmware's switch family, SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl would pass 'switch' and chnType SERVO would be absent from the ramp-time branch at JS:687 and the level branch at :695/:708 — the same two greps return the opposite result. Had CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER carried the profile, the ENDTIME_MONDAY_1 parameter in rf_cc_rt_dn.xml would sit under a channel paramset rather than under `<paramset type="MASTER" id="cc_rt_dev_master">`.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Most of the contradiction survives and I strengthened it; but one of its sub-claims is itself refuted and one is softer than stated, so the finding is narrowed. UPHELD, with new Tier-1 support the previous grounding did not have. Every family argument is verbatim as cited (I re-read all seven easymode .tcl files). SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:18 passes 'dimmer'; hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:33-35 dereferences psDescr(01_WP_RAMP_TIME_FACTOR) for exactly that family, a tcl array read that errors if the key is absent — so the firmware asserts a SERVO week-profile MASTER carries WP_RAMP_TIME_FACTOR, on the same paramset our rawconvert parses. Independently, DeviceUtil handles SERVO_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER exactly as DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (RAMP_TIME, ON_TIME, LEVEL) while grouping WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER with SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER on ON_TIME + STATE. So SERVO belongs in a ramp-carrying bucket and our 'valve' bucket strips ramp_time (schedules.go:719); WATER_SWITCH is 'switch', with no field consequence (both buckets strip exactly {level_2, ramp_time}). REFUTED sub-claim: 'SHADING_WEEK_PROFILE does not exist in this firmware at all ... it is a Tier-2-only type, so its cover bucket is not firmware-grounded.' It is Tier 1. ChannelType declares SHADING_RECEIVER(74) and SHADING_WEEK_PROFILE(75), and ShadingCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory builds its parameter set as fillBasicAstroParameter + WP_LEVEL + WP_LEVEL_2 — byte-for-byte the same shape as BlindCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory, and with no WP_RAMP_TIME_* or WP_DURATION_* (which DimmerCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory does add). Tier 2 agrees: HmIP-HDM1 VCU3560967:2 and HmIP-HDM2 VCU1111390:2 MASTER carry exactly WP_{WEEKDAY,CONDITION,FIXED_HOUR,FIXED_MINUTE,ASTRO_TYPE,ASTRO_OFFSET,TARGET_CHANNELS,LEVEL,LEVEL_2}. Our 'cover' bucket (strip ramp_time + duration, keep level_2) is therefore exactly the declared field set — grounded, not a guess. Also, the finding's 'the firmware's own set is exactly seven' is the WEBUI's set: an exhaustive grep over OpenCCU-Base returns those seven, but the HmIP server's ChannelType enum carries eight (SHADING has no easymode shipped). SOFTENED sub-claim: the SERVO round-trip consequence. There is no ServoCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory in the server (subtypes are shading_wp, blind_wp, dimmer_wp, dimmer_output_behaviour_wp, switch_wp, universal_light_wp, window_drive_wp — no servo_wp) and no SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE device in either descriptor corpus, so SERVO's WP field set is nowhere declared in a form I could read. The family assignment is confirmed twice over; the concrete 'a SERVO schedule round-trips without its travel time' is unverified for want of any device to observe. UPHELD and deepened: the climateScheduleChannelTypes justification is wrong more thoroughly than stated. rf_cc_rt_dn.xml puts 182 bare ENDTIME_/TEMPERATURE_ params in the DEVICE master cc_rt_dev_master, and its CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER (index 4) declares only a VALUES and a LINK paramset — no MASTER. rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml puts 546 P1_..P3_ params in tc_it_dev_master and declares NO CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER channel at all (its channels are MAINTENANCE, WEATHER_TRANSMIT, THERMALCONTROL_TRANSMIT, WINDOW_SWITCH_RECEIVER, REMOTECONTROL_RECEIVER, SWITCH_TRANSMIT). rf_cc_tc.xml does put 336 params on CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR's own MASTER cc_tc_ch_master, but named TIMEOUT_<DAY>_<N> / TEMPERATUR_<DAY>_<N>; slotPattern requires (ENDTIME|TEMPERATURE) followed by '_', so TEMPERATUR_ (no trailing E) and TIMEOUT_ both miss and that candidate can never resolve. The sweep is 7 files, not 5 — ccu1/ carries older duplicates of the same two devices, which does not change the conclusion. HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER confirmed on both tiers: createWeekProgramParameterNames builds P<n>_{TEMPERATURE,ENDTIME}_<DAY>_<1..13>, and its caller invokes createWeekProgram(i + 1) from i=0, so weekProgramNumber is 1-based; 20 devices in the descriptor corpus. Lock precedence checks out (JS:285 isDLP, :317 isDoorLockDrive for HmIP-DLD/-A/-S, :1899 _getDLPModeSelector); minor citation slip, the HmIP-DLD branch is SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:22 and :47, not :21.

reachesDevice.title: The state-parameter -> reset-action mapping names device families in a comment but cites no descriptor
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory (registers ParameterMapKey("RESET_MOTION","default") and ParameterMapKey("RESET_PRESENCE","default"), each via createStop) and de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterIdentifier; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_sec_mdir.xml (and rf_sec_mdir_v1_5.xml, rf_sen_mdir.xml, rf_sen_mdir_v1_5.xml, rf_sen_mdir_wm55.xml); Tier 2 co-location sweep over ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json joined to ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json
reachesDevice.ourValue: MOTION -> RESET_MOTION and PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE -> RESET_PRESENCE on the same channel; comment cites HmIP-SMO, HM-Sec-MDIR and HmIP-SPI as the evidence
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: The pairing and the same-channel co-location hold, but only on HmIP channels. RESET_MOTION appears on MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (8 devices: HmIP-SMI, SMI55, SMO, SMO-2, …) and MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SMO230-A), always beside MOTION. RESET_PRESENCE appears on PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SPI, HmIPW-SPI), always beside PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE. HM-Sec-MDIR declares MOTION on a MOTION_DETECTOR channel and no RESET_MOTION; the string RESET_MOTION does not occur anywhere under src/devicetypes/.
reachesDevice.finding: The mapping itself is right and the two families are genuinely distinct: the HmIP server registers RESET_MOTION and RESET_PRESENCE as two separate stop-shaped state parameters, so they are not synonyms. The descriptor sweep confirms strict co-location — every channel carrying RESET_MOTION also carries MOTION, every channel carrying RESET_PRESENCE also carries PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE, and never the cross pairing. Completeness also holds: no other latching alarm-sensor state parameter has a reset action. SMOKE_DETECTOR carries only SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS; there is no RESET_WATER on any channel; ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SAM, HmIP-STV) carries MOTION with no reset, and so does the classic MOTION_DETECTOR channel. That last point is where the boundary runs and where the comment is wrong: RESET_MOTION is HmIP-only. HM-Sec-MDIR, named in the comment as a RESET_MOTION device, declares MOTION and nothing else (rf_sec_mdir.xml), as do all 11 classic MOTION_DETECTOR devices in the corpus. The behaviour is still correct — resetParameterFor returns the parameter name, the channel lookup finds no such DP, and the sensor is reported Supports=false — so a classic BidCos detector is correctly non-resettable. Only the comment's cited evidence is refuted; replacing HM-Sec-MDIR with a real HmIP motion detector (HmIP-SMI, HmIP-SMO-2) and noting that classic BidCos MOTION_DETECTOR channels have no reset would make it accurate.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had RESET_MOTION existed on the classic side, `grep -rl RESET_MOTION ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/` would list rf_sec_mdir.xml; it lists nothing, while the same string does resolve in the HmIP server tree — so the check produces different answers on the two sides and is not untethered. Likewise, had the pairing been cross-wired on any device, the co-location sweep would have printed a channel type carrying MOTION together with RESET_PRESENCE; it printed none.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Narrowing upheld; every number in it reproduces. What I checked, independently rather than by re-reading the previous agent's sweep. (1) The registration is verbatim: StateParameterFactory puts ParameterMapKey("RESET_MOTION","default") and ParameterMapKey("RESET_PRESENCE","default"), each from createStop, and StateParameterIdentifier declares both constants — two separate parameters, not synonyms, so keying the reset off the parameter rather than off the sensor type is right. (2) I re-ran the co-location sweep from scratch, joining each paramset file's VALUES key set to the channel TYPE from the device description. RESET_MOTION appears on exactly 9 (device, channel) pairs — HmIP-SMI, SMI55, SMO, SMO-2, SMO-A, SMO230-A, UDI-SMI55, HmIPW-SMI55 on MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER, plus HmIP-SMO230-A on MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER — and MOTION is present on every one of them, PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE on none. RESET_PRESENCE appears on exactly 2, both PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SPI, HmIPW-SPI), with PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE present and MOTION absent. No cross pairing anywhere. (3) Completeness holds and I widened the test: RESET_MOTION and RESET_PRESENCE are the ONLY parameters beginning with RESET in any VALUES paramset in the whole corpus — there is no RESET_WATER, no smoke reset. ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER carries MOTION with no reset on 3 devices (HmIP-SAM, HmIP-STV and also ELV-SH-TACO, which the previous finding omitted), and the classic MOTION_DETECTOR channel carries MOTION with no reset on 11 devices. (4) The comment's evidence is refuted as stated: grep over the whole of src/devicetypes/ returns no file containing RESET_MOTION, and rf_sec_mdir.xml:121 declares channel index=1 type="MOTION_DETECTOR" whose only relevant parameter is id="MOTION" operations="read,event" at :227. HM-Sec-MDIR cannot be a RESET_MOTION device. (5) The 'behaviour is still correct' claim is verifiable and correct: motionResetter.action resolves the reset DP through Channel.Parameter and returns an error when it is nil, and Supports is literally `_, err := m.action(row); return err == nil` — so a classic BidCos detector reports Supports=false rather than misbehaving. Only the comment is wrong; the boundary is that RESET_MOTION is HmIP-only.

reachesDevice.title: "Active unless the value sits at index 0" is the default activation rule for every enumerated alarm sensor, with no source for index 0 meaning idle
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1 (HmIP, the quoted list): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus — `public enum SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus { IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM; }` with `getNames()` filling the array from `values()` in ordinal order; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createSmokeDetectorAlarmStatusParameter — `String[] enumStrings = SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus.getNames(); new StateParameter("SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS", LogicalType.ENUM, PhysicalType.INTEGER, …, new StringEnumToInteger(enumStrings), enumStrings[0], enumStrings[0], enumStrings[enumStrings.length - 1])`. Tier 1 (index==value on the legacy wire): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#createParameterDescription sets VALUE_LIST from `converter.getEnumStrings()`, and #convertParameterValue returns the ordinal within getEnumStrings() when replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal is set; ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true`. Tier 1 (BidCos): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:49-58 (`options[index]=id` when the XML carries an index, else append) and :100-107 (`MIN=0`, `MAX=options.size()-1`, `VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i]`). Tier 1 (per-family idle at 0): rf_rhs.xml:170-175 {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN}; rf_wds_v1_1.xml:149-154 {DRY,WET,WATER}; rf_sc.xml:164-169 ERROR {NO_ERROR@0, SABOTAGE@7}.
reachesDevice.ourValue: Default rule: "active unless the value sits at index 0"; quoted list SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS = [IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM]
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: The quoted list is exact, in that order, from the firmware's own enum declaration. The positional premise underneath the rule is also exact: the legacy XML-RPC integer IS the VALUE_LIST index on both stacks. What the firmware nowhere states is "index 0 is idle" — the strongest general statement it makes is DEFAULT = MIN = enumStrings[0] for the HmIP state-parameter enums, which is a default, not an idle semantic.
reachesDevice.finding:
Two separable inputs; they land differently.

(a) The quoted value list is confirmed verbatim at Tier 1. SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus declares IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM in that order, getNames() preserves ordinal order, and createSmokeDetectorAlarmStatusParameter feeds that array straight into the StateParameter. So INTRUSION_ALARM really does sit at index 2 inside a smoke-detector status, and the comment's reasoning — that "not index 0" reads the installation's own siren command as a fire — is sound.

(b) The positional premise our runtime silently depends on is also confirmed, and it is worth recording because it is the part nobody wrote down. safety.ActiveFromRaw maps an integer wire value onto a label by scanning valueList positionally. On HmIP that holds because DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue converts an ENUM to its ordinal in getEnumStrings() and crRFD.conf:47 ships ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true — note the *physical* radio bytes are not the ordinals at all (createStateWindowOpenTiltedClosed maps {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN} onto {0,100,200}), so without that flag the positional read would be wrong. On BidCos it holds because HSSLogicalTypeOption places each option AT its declared index and emits VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i] with MIN=0, MAX=size-1.

(c) "Index 0 is idle" is not a firmware rule. It is a per-enum property that happens to hold across every ENUM an alarm sensor can currently be enrolled on: STATE on SHUTTER_CONTACT {CLOSED,OPEN}, ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR / ROTARY_HANDLE_TRANSCEIVER / ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN}, DOOR_STATE_TRANSCEIVER {CLOSED,OPEN}, WATERDETECTIONSENSOR {DRY,WET,WATER}, RAINDETECTOR {DRY,RAIN}, ERROR {NO_ERROR,…}, ERROR_ALARM_TEST / ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER {NO_ERROR,…}, and SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS {IDLE_OFF,…} — I enumerated every ENUM VALUE_LIST carried by a classifiable parameter and index 0 is the inactive state in all of them. The boundary runs where the firmware's own statement stops: it guarantees only DEFAULT=MIN=first entry for the HmIP enums, and nothing at all for BidCos option lists. So the rule is true in our scope and unbacked one step wider; it is safe today and it is exactly the kind of rule that must be re-checked when a new ENUM family becomes enrollable, because a firmware that ships an alarm state at position 0 would break it silently.

One caveat on inputs, recorded because it touches the same premise: for SHUTTER_CONTACT/MOTION_DETECTOR/ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR ERROR, the shipped device XML declares SABOTAGE at index="7" (rf_sc.xml:168, and the same in firmware/rftypes/rf_sc.xml), which per HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:53 must yield an eight-entry VALUE_LIST with six empty-string fillers and MAX=7 — while the recorded descriptor corpus consistently shows a two-entry list with MAX=1. The corpus does contain firmware-shaped fillers elsewhere (HM-CC-RT-DN FAULT_REPORTING carries an empty entry at position 5, matching rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2340's `<option id=""/>`). I could not reconcile the two for the sparse-index case and am not asserting either; it does not move this verdict, since both readings put NO_ERROR at 0.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our list or our index-0 premise been wrong, three distinct checks would have said so. (1) A wrong list: the firmware enum declares its constants in source order, so a reordered or renamed entry (say IDLE_OFF not first, or SMOKE_ALARM instead of PRIMARY_ALARM) would read straight off SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus — it did not. (2) A wrong positional premise: if the legacy surface delivered the physical byte instead of the ordinal, crRFD.conf would carry ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=false and DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue would return the raw value, and a HmIP window contact would report 200 for OPEN rather than 1 — the config template says true, and StringEnumToInteger's {0,100,200} table shows exactly what a false setting would have produced. (3) A wrong idle-at-0 claim: enumerating every ENUM VALUE_LIST on a classifiable parameter would have produced at least one list whose first entry is an alarm state; across the whole corpus it produced none.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed at tier 1. This is the strongest grounding in the bundle and every load-bearing quote survived transcription check.

(a) The value list is exact — enum order, getNames() ordinal fill, and the factory call that hands the array to the StateParameter all read as claimed. INTRUSION_ALARM really is at index 2 inside a smoke-detector status, so the reasoning behind ActiveValues holds.

(b) The positional premise our runtime silently depends on is confirmed on both stacks, and I verified it independently rather than accepting it. On HmIP the description's value list and the wire ordinal are produced from one and the same getEnumStrings() array, and the inbound direction indexes it directly — so scanning valueList positionally in safety.ActiveFromRaw is exactly right. Worth keeping visible: the physical radio bytes are NOT the ordinals (CLOSED/TILTED/OPEN map to 0/100/200), so without ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal the positional read would be silently wrong; crRFD.conf ships it true. On BidCos, HSSLogicalTypeOption honours a declared index attribute and emits VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i] with MIN 0 and MAX size-1.

(c) The boundary is drawn honestly and I could not push it further. The firmware's strongest general statement is DEFAULT=MIN=first entry for the HmIP state-parameter enums — a default, not an idle semantic — and nothing at all for BidCos option lists. My independent sweep reproduces the empirical claim: every ENUM value list a classifiable parameter carries has its inactive value at index 0. So the rule is true in our scope and unbacked one step wider, which is exactly what "narrowed" should mean.

CORRECTIONS, neither load-bearing. (i) The "per-family idle at 0" citations to rf_rhs.xml / rf_wds_v1_1.xml / rf_sc.xml are labelled Tier 1; those are Tier-2 device XMLs. The Tier-1 half (HmIP enum, HmIP ordinal wire, libhsscomm) stands on its own, which is why the tier survives. (ii) The finding lists ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER, DOOR_STATE_TRANSCEIVER and RAINDETECTOR among enums "an alarm sensor can currently be enrolled on"; per its own sibling finding none of those channel types is enrollable, and RAINDETECTOR appears in neither table. Scope creep in the prose, not in the measurement — my sweep was restricted to what classify.go and sensor_candidates.go can actually reach and the conclusion is unchanged. (iii) The unreconciled sparse-index observation is real and reproduced; it does not move the verdict since both readings put NO_ERROR at 0, and ERROR is not a classifiable parameter in the first place.

reachesDevice.title: The sysvar wire encodings (bool as int 0/1, enum list as ';'-joined string, chnID -1) are bare literals
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods.conf:865-903 — `SysVar.createBool { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name init_val internal chnID} }`, `SysVar.setBool { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name value} }`, `SysVar.createEnum { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name valList internal chnID} }`, `SysVar.createFloat { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name minValue maxValue internal chnID} }`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/setbool.tcl:14-22 — `set val $args(value)` / `if {($val != 0) && ($val != 1) } { if {$val >= 1} { set args(value) 1 } else { set args(value) 0 } }`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createenum.tcl:7 — `#   valList: Enum "Wert1;Wert2;Wert3;...."` and :26 `sv.ValueList( valList );`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/getall.tcl:27 — `#     valueList: [string] Werteliste (Separator: ";")`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/msg/newSysVar.htm:196 (the WebUI's own new-sysvar form) — `pb += "string sValList = '"+$("txVals").value.replace(/(?:\r\n|\r|\n)/g,';')+"';";`, consumed at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:842 `sv.ValueList(system.GetVar("sValList"));`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createbool.tcl:9 / createenum.tcl:9 / createfloat.tcl:10 — `chnID: [integer] ID des Kanals … Wenn an kein Kanal gebunden werden soll, ist -1 zu übergeben`, enforced at createbool.tcl:15 `if (chnID != -1) {`. createbool.tcl:4 — `init_val: [bool] Initialer Status`, applied at :28 `sv.State(init_val);`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/hmscript.tcl:17 — every argument is injected into the ReGa script as `var $name = "…";`, i.e. as a string literal.
