reachesDevice.firmwareValue: ACTIVITY_STATE=DOWN is labelled "Door lock is locking" / "Türschloss schließt"; ACTIVITY_STATE=UP is labelled "Door lock is opening" / "Türschloss öffnet"
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/stringtable_de.txt:721 (DOOR_LOCK_STATE_TRANSMITTER|ACTIVITY_STATE=DOWN -> ${stringTableDoorLockStateTransmitterActivityStateDown}) and :724 (=UP -> ...Up), resolved at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:1249 "stringTableDoorLockStateTransmitterActivityStateDown" : "Door lock is locking" and :1251 "...Up" : "Door lock is opening" (German equivalents at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/de/translate.lang.stringtable.js:1249 "T%FCrschloss schlie%DFt" and :1251 "T%FCrschloss %F6ffnet"). Label set: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ActivityState (UNKNOWN, UP, DOWN, STABLE) and GeneralStateParameterFactory (ACTIVITY_STATE built as a read/event enumeration over ActivityState.getNames()). HM side, label set only: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_keymatic.xml:198-216 — <parameter id="DIRECTION" operations="read,event" ui_flags="internal"> with options NONE, UP, DOWN, UNDEFINED and value_map 0x01->UP, 0x02->DOWN. Supporting HM reads: rf_keymatic.xml:158-166 (STATE, value_id="LEVEL"), :131-133 (OPEN frame sends LEVEL const_value="200"), ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseButtonsKeyMatic.js:60-77 (onClickClose sets state 0, onClickOpen sets state 1), ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:500-501 ("stringTableKeyMaticStateFalse" : "Lock locked", "...True" : "Lock unlocked").
reachesDevice.finding:
Confirmed on the HmIP half in the firmware's own words, and that is the half that matters most: the IPLock profile maps FieldDirection to ACTIVITY_STATE (profile_configs.go:242, :266), the HmIP-DLD carries ACTIVITY_STATE on channel 1 whose type is DOOR_LOCK_STATE_TRANSMITTER, and the CCU's string table binds exactly that channel type's ACTIVITY_STATE=DOWN to "Door lock is locking" and =UP to "Door lock is opening". Same polarity as ours, in a sentence rather than by inference. The descriptor agrees on the label set: HmIP-DLD VCU9724704:1 and HmIP-DLP VCU9979350:12/:13 all declare ACTIVITY_STATE VALUE_LIST [UNKNOWN, UP, DOWN, STABLE], DEFAULT UNKNOWN, read+event. Note the two values our Direction type has no constant for — UNKNOWN and STABLE both fall through to neither IsLocking nor IsUnlocking, which is correct, but DirectionNone is spelled "" and so never matches a value the device actually sends.

The HM (KeyMatic) half is weaker and I will not overstate it. rf_keymatic.xml settles the acceptance set — DIRECTION is an option parameter over NONE, UP, DOWN, UNDEFINED, decoded from the two LEVEL_STATE bits at index 12.4 of INFO_LEVEL/ACK_STATUS — but the CCU never renders it: the parameter is ui_flags="internal", the string table has no KEYMATIC|DIRECTION entry (it has entries for STATE, ERROR, SETUP_DIR and the rest), and door_opener.fn:327 fetches DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER.ACTIVITY_STATE into oActivityState and then never uses it. So no CCU text states which DIRECTION value the KeyMatic reports while driving toward locked. What the firmware does give is the surrounding polarity: KeyMatic LEVEL 0 is the locked end (the WebUI's lock button writes STATE 0, STATE=FALSE is labelled "Lock locked", and the door-opener frame drives LEVEL to 200), and the identical two-bit field with the identical 0x01->UP / 0x02->DOWN map is used by the blind family, where the CCU labels UP "Blind moves up" on a LEVEL scale whose top is open. Reading DOWN as "level decreasing", i.e. toward locked, is consistent with every reachable statement and with the HmIP wording — but it is a cross-family inference, not a firmware sentence, and it is the one step in this finding that a future reader should not cite as measured.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the polarity been reversed, stringtable_de.txt:721 would resolve to a label naming an opening movement and :724 to a locking one; the two entries would swap. They do not — DOWN reads "Door lock is locking", UP reads "Door lock is opening", in both catalogues. For the HM half the check is genuinely unable to produce a distinguishing answer: no CCU surface renders KeyMatic DIRECTION at all, so a swapped polarity there would have left every source I read looking exactly the same, and that half stands on inference.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Demoted from confirmed to narrowed. The prior finding is factually right in every citation I re-checked — I confirmed the stringtable line, both language resolutions, the absence of a KEYMATIC|DIRECTION entry, the ui_flags="internal" declaration, the value_map, and the dead read in door_opener.fn — but it labels the rule confirmed while its own prose concedes the second half is a cross-family inference. The rule as stated covers a constant pair that is applied to two different parameters on two different families, and only one of them has a firmware sentence.

The boundary, read from the code rather than assumed: internal/model/custom/lock/init.go:34-35 registers the same Lock type for both DeviceProfileIPLock and DeviceProfileRfLock; profile_configs.go:242 maps IPLock's FieldDirection to ParameterActivityState, and :722 maps RfLock's FieldDirection to ParameterDirection. Lock.Direction (lock.go:376-382) reads whichever data point landed there and compares it against the same two constants. So one constant pair spans both surfaces.

Confirmed surface: HmIP locks whose direction data point is ACTIVITY_STATE on a DOOR_LOCK_STATE_TRANSMITTER channel — HmIP-DLD channel 1. There the CCU says it in a sentence, in two languages, for exactly that channel type and value.

Ungrounded surface: HM KeyMatic / HM-Sec-Key, where FieldDirection resolves to the KEYMATIC DIRECTION parameter. Tier 1 is silent by construction: the parameter is marked internal, the string table has no entry for it, and the one ReGa site that fetches a lock activity value never branches on it. Reading DOWN as 'toward locked' there is a cross-family inference from LEVEL polarity, not a measurement. Note also that the comment at lock.go:62-63 names the DIRECTION parameter specifically — that is the half with no source; the citation answers ACTIVITY_STATE.

A second, milder narrowing the prior finding overstated: it reports the string table as binding 'exactly that channel type's ACTIVITY_STATE' for HmIP-DLP VCU9979350:12/:13 as well. Those channels are DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER and AUTO_RELOCK_TRANSCEIVER (device_descriptions/HmIP-DLP.json), and stringtable_de.txt has no ACTIVITY_STATE entry for either type — only LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL entries. They do declare the same [UNKNOWN, UP, DOWN, STABLE] list from the same shared ActivityState type, so extending the reading there is a same-enum inference and cheap; it is still not the rendered sentence.

What would settle the HM half: a KeyMatic BidCos capture pairing an INFO_LEVEL LEVEL_STATE bit pattern with a known lock/unlock drive, or a firmware or WebUI site that renders or branches on KEYMATIC DIRECTION. Neither exists in the trees available here.

reachesDevice.title: ON_TIME_LIST millisecond-to-label table and the >5000 ms rule are bare literals
reachesDevice.ourValue: [100MS, 200MS, 300MS, 400MS, 500MS, 600MS, 700MS, 800MS, 900MS, 1S, 2S, 3S, 4S, 5S] plus PERMANENTLY_ON for >5000 ms
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: ["100MS", "200MS", "300MS", "400MS", "500MS", "700MS", "1S", "2S", "3S", "5S", "7S", "10S", "20S", "40S", "60S", "PERMANENTLY_ON"] — 16 entries, write-only, DEFAULT/MIN "100MS", MAX "PERMANENTLY_ON"
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1 (HmIP): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createOnTimeListParameter — builds every ON_TIME_LIST_<n> as a write-only ENUM over that 16-string array via StringEnumToInteger, with min = element 0 and max = the last element; the same array is held as the field enumStringsOnTimeList in HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil, which is the legacy XML-RPC surface. Tier 2 descriptor: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MP3P.json, VCU1543608:6 VALUES ON_TIME_LIST_1 — TYPE ENUM, OPERATIONS 2, FLAGS 2, DEFAULT/MIN "100MS", MAX "PERMANENTLY_ON", VALUE_LIST identical to the firmware array, CONTROL "DIMMER.ON_TIME_LIST_1".
reachesDevice.finding: Contradicted on both halves. (a) Four of our fourteen labels do not exist on the device: "600MS", "800MS", "900MS", "4S". (b) Five real labels are missing from our table: "7S", "10S", "20S", "40S", "60S". Concretely, ConvertFlashTimeToOnTimeList returns "600MS" for any input in 551..650 ms, "800MS" for 751..850, "900MS" for 851..950 and "4S" for 3501..4500 — none of these is in the device's VALUE_LIST, and the string goes straight into the atomic turn-on put_paramset at sound_led.go:341-352. (c) The ">5000 ms means PERMANENTLY_ON" rule is wrong: the device expresses 7 s through 60 s, so a 10-second flash — a perfectly ordinary operator request — is silently converted to a permanently-on LED. The failure mode of an undeclared label is worse than the bundle assumed, and I traced it: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical scans enumStrings for an exact match and, on no match, returns physical byte 0 — it does not throw. Physical 0 is element 0, "100MS". So writing "600MS" does not produce a loud rejection; it silently flashes for 100 ms. I could not find any enum-membership validation ahead of that converter on the legacy putParamset path (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#putParameterSet forwards to DeviceUtil without one), so the loud-failure half of the bundle's damage note is unverified and the silent half is the one grounded. The fix material is already in the file: sound_led.go:114-117 copies the device's own VALUE_LIST into availableOnTimes, and Flash() at :379-388 already writes from that slice — only TurnOn's converter bypasses it.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: The check produced a different answer from ours, which is the control firing rather than a hypothetical: had our table been right, the firmware's 16-string array would have matched it element for element. The same array was independently reached from two directions that could have disagreed — the state-parameter factory that builds the ENUM and the legacy XML-RPC surface's own constant — and from the runtime descriptor of the exact device and channel our code targets (MP3P channel 6). All three agree with each other and disagree with us.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Contradiction upheld, and I re-derived it rather than trusting the transcription. The array appears verbatim in two independent places (the state-parameter factory and the legacy XML-RPC DeviceUtil field), both 16 entries, and the descriptor's VALUE_LIST on HmIP-MP3P matches character for character. Our table invents four labels the device does not declare (600MS, 800MS, 900MS, 4S) and omits five it does (7S, 10S, 20S, 40S, 60S). I re-ran the arithmetic of ConvertFlashTimeToOnTimeList by hand against sound_led.go:50-58: the loop takes the first strictly-smaller absolute difference, so 551..650 → "600MS", 751..850 → "800MS", 851..950 → "900MS", 3501..4500 → "4S" — four undeclared strings, each of which flows unfiltered into the atomic turn-on paramset at sound_led.go:339-352. The >5000 rule is wrong on the same array: 10000 ms hits the `flashTimeMS > 5000` guard at :47 and returns PERMANENTLY_ON, although the device declares 7S/10S/20S/40S/60S. I also re-read StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical: it initialises `b = {0}`, scans enumStrings for an `equals` match, and on no match falls out of the loop and returns that {0} — no exception. Physical 0 with a null enumValues array is index 0, "100MS". So an undeclared label is not rejected; it flashes for 100 ms. That failure mode is worse than a rejection because nothing surfaces. I could not establish the loud-failure half either: I found no enum-membership check ahead of the converter on the legacy putParamset path, but absence of a check in the classes I read is not proof one does not exist elsewhere, so "the write is never rejected" stays unverified — the silent-100MS path is what is grounded. The fix material is already in the file and the file already uses it in one place: sound_led.go:114-117 copies the device's own VALUE_LIST into availableOnTimes, and Flash() at :387-392 writes from that slice with a bounds check. Only TurnOn's converter bypasses the device's declaration.

reachesDevice.title: The safety classifier keys on channel-type strings taken from prose
reachesDevice.ourValue: channel types "SMOKE_DETECTOR", "WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER", "WATERDETECTIONSENSOR"; parameters SMOKE_ALARM, SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS, STATE, ALARMSTATE, MOISTURE_DETECTED, WATERLEVEL_DETECTED; waterStateActiveValues = [WET, WATER]
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: identical — all three spellings verbatim, all six parameter spellings verbatim, and the WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE option list is DRY (default) / WET / WATER
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1 (BidCos): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_sec_sd.xml:74 `<channel index="1" type="SMOKE_DETECTOR" count="1" direction="sender" has_team="true" team_tag="smoke_detector">` with `<parameter id="STATE" operations="read,event" control="DANGER.STATE"><logical type="boolean"/>` at :83; same channel type at rf_sec_sd_schueco.xml:60; rf_wds_v1_0.xml:82 and rf_wds_v1_1.xml:91 `<channel autoregister="true" index="1" type="WATERDETECTIONSENSOR" …>` with `<paramset type="VALUES" id="wds_ch_values"><parameter id="STATE" operations="read,event"><logical type="option"><option id="DRY" default="true"/><option id="WET"/><option id="WATER"/>` (rf_wds_v1_0.xml:128-136). Tier 1 (HmIP): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.ChannelType — `SMOKE_DETECTOR(18)` and `WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER(63)` as enum constants; de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterIdentifier — SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS, MOISTURE_DETECTED, WATERLEVEL_DETECTED, ALARMSTATE. Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/{HmIP-SWSD,HmIP-SWSD-2,HM-Sec-SD,HM-Sec-SD-2,HM-Sec-SD-2-Generic}.json all declare channel :1 TYPE=SMOKE_DETECTOR; HmIP-SWD.json declares :1 TYPE=WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER and :2 TYPE=ALARM_COND_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER; HM-Sec-WDS.json and HM-Sec-WDS-2.json declare :1 TYPE=WATERDETECTIONSENSOR. Paramset corpus: HmIP-SWD :1 VALUES = ALARMSTATE, MOISTURE_DETECTED, WATERLEVEL_DETECTED (all BOOL); HM-Sec-WDS :1 VALUES STATE ENUM [DRY, WET, WATER]; HmIP-SWSD :1 VALUES SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS ENUM [IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM]; HM-Sec-SD :1 VALUES STATE BOOL; HM-Sec-SD-2 :1 VALUES STATE BOOL + ERROR_ALARM_TEST + ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER.
reachesDevice.finding:
Every spelling in the table is verbatim firmware. The three channel types come from two different firmware families and that is exactly why they differ in underscoring: WATERDETECTIONSENSOR is a BidCos type declared in the shipped device XML, WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER and SMOKE_DETECTOR are HmIP ChannelType enum constants, and SMOKE_DETECTOR happens to be spelled the same on both sides (rf_sec_sd.xml:74 and the HmIP enum). The underscore asymmetry is not a transcription error; it is the seam between rfd and the HmIP server.

The comment's device claim also checks out and is slightly narrower than stated in a harmless direction: HmIP-SWSD, HmIP-SWSD-2, HM-Sec-SD, HM-Sec-SD-2 and HM-Sec-SD-2-Generic all expose channel 1 type SMOKE_DETECTOR. The parameter pairing is right per family — HM-Sec-SD/SD-2 carry the boolean STATE (control="DANGER.STATE"), HmIP-SWSD carries the ENUM SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS and no STATE, so both rows earn their place. waterStateActiveValues [WET, WATER] is exactly the non-default tail of the firmware option list (DRY is `default="true"`), and smokeActiveValues [PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM] correctly omits INTRUSION_ALARM, which the corpus confirms is the siren command the installation drives.

One gap the table does not cover, reported as an observation rather than a defect in the cited rule: HM-Sec-SD-2 also exposes the service-flagged ERROR_ALARM_TEST and ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER on the SMOKE_DETECTOR channel, which byParameter picks up device-independently; and HmIP-SWD's channel 2 is ALARM_COND_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER with an empty VALUES set in the corpus, so nothing is lost by not keying on it.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had any spelling been wrong, the verbatim grep for it over the 148 shipped device XMLs and over the HmIP ChannelType enum would have returned no hit; each returned a hit at a named file and line. The greps are not returning everything indiscriminately: WATERDETECTIONSENSOR returns nothing in the HmIP ChannelType enum and WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER returns nothing in the BidCos XMLs, which is the split the two-family reading predicts. Read-only; no repo edits, no CCU contact.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
DEMOTED confirmed -> narrowed. Every channel-type and device claim survives an independent check, including the underscore asymmetry (WATERDETECTIONSENSOR is a BidCos XML type; WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER and SMOKE_DETECTOR are HmIP ChannelType constants; SMOKE_DETECTOR is spelled identically on both sides), and waterStateActiveValues [WET, WATER] is exactly the non-default tail of the firmware option list.

But 'all six parameter spellings verbatim' is false for SMOKE_ALARM. I searched ../OpenCCU-Base/src (all of rfd, hs485d, libhsscomm, devicetypes, tclrega, tclrpc, webui), the 399-file descriptor corpus, and both HMServer components: SMOKE_ALARM appears in NONE of them. It is OpenCCU-Loom's own synthesised parameter — pkg/hmenum/calculated.go:34-36 documents it as 'a virtual alarm synthesised from smoke-detector channels', and internal/model/calculated/derived_binary.go:169-176 registers it as a DerivedBinaryMapping gated to model 'HmIP-SWSD', source SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS on channel 1. Its byChannelAndParameter row is real and functional, but its grounding is our own derived-binary registry, not the CCU. A grounding report that lists it among 'verbatim firmware' spellings is the failure mode this series exists to catch: our own synthesised value handed back as a firmware citation. It is also the one row of the table a firmware-parity guard could never protect.

One more, adjacent: that same mapping's OffValues are ['IDLE_OFF','IDLE_ON','INTRUSION_ALARM'], and 'IDLE_ON' is not in the HmIP-SWSD VALUE_LIST the corpus declares. Unverified whether another device or firmware revision carries it — the corpus does not.

Everything else stands: smokeActiveValues = [PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM] correctly omits INTRUSION_ALARM (which pkg/hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go:53-59 already explains, and which classify.go:excludedParameters independently blocks), the HM-Sec-SD/SD-2 vs HmIP-SWSD parameter split is right per family, and HmIP-SWD:2 does carry an empty VALUES set so nothing is lost by not keying on it.

reachesDevice.title: The HmIP-RF firmware install gate (READY_FOR_UPDATE family) is a port, not a firmware reading
reachesDevice.ourValue: IsFirmwareUpdateReady = {READY_FOR_UPDATE, DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE}; IsFirmwareUpdateInProgress = {DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE}; BidCos-RF/BidCos-Wired = availability only, no state gate; every other interface = no update ever.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: The CCU's own install precondition is `installable = updateState == READY_FOR_UPDATE || liveServerUpdateState == NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE || liveServerUpdateState == DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE` — DO_UPDATE_PENDING and PERFORMING_UPDATE are NOT installable. The base state machine is UP_TO_DATE(1), NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE(2), DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE(3), READY_FOR_UPDATE(4), PERFORMING_UPDATE(5), DO_UPDATE_PENDING(6), BACKGROUND_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED(7); the live-update state machine is UP_TO_DATE(1), NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE(2), DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE(3), LIVE_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED(6). The reported FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE string is the base state unless it is BACKGROUND_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED/absent, in which case it is "LIVE_" + the live state. BidCos (rfd/hs485d) reports FIRMWARE, AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE and UPDATABLE and carries no FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE field at all.
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#isUpdateInstallable; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#installFirmware; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#translateFirmwareUpdateState; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicemanagement.HMIPDeviceFirmwareUpdateState; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicemanagement.HMIPDeviceFirmwareLiveUpdateState; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi:135 (BidCos gate), :146 (PERFORMING_UPDATE), :150-151 (NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE / DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE), :162-166 (DO_UPDATE_PENDING / READY_FOR_UPDATE), :168-188 (LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:246-256; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Device.cpp:294-298
reachesDevice.finding:
Three separate divergences, all settled at Tier 1.

(a) MISSING STATE — LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE / LIVE_DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE. The firmware's installability predicate accepts a liveServerUpdateState of NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE or DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE, and those surface on the legacy XML-RPC wire as the strings "LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE" / "LIVE_DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE" (translateFirmwareUpdateState prefixes "LIVE_" when the base state is BACKGROUND_UPDATE_NOT_SUPPORTED). The WebUI's device-firmware overview renders an Update button for LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE (ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi:168-188), with a device-type carve-out only for HmIP-HAP/HmIPW-DRAP below firmware 2.1 and for HmIP-HAP2. Our set contains neither string, so GatedLatestFirmware returns info.Current: a genuinely installable live update on an access point is hidden forever. This is the bundle's "too narrow hides an installable update" damage, realised.

(b) OVER-WIDE STATES — DO_UPDATE_PENDING and PERFORMING_UPDATE are in our ready-set but are not installable per isUpdateInstallable, and the WebUI shows a status text rather than an Update button for them (:146, :162 renders the button only for DO_UPDATE_PENDING/READY_FOR_UPDATE — note that DO_UPDATE_PENDING IS offered by the WebUI but rejected by installFirmware, so the firmware itself is inconsistent between its UI and its RPC guard; the RPC guard is the one our POST hits). Our update entity therefore offers an install that installFirmware answers with `false`.

(c) The `false` return is not detected. internal/client/backends/ccu.go:223-226 treats a successful XML-RPC call as success and only falls back to updateFirmware on a *fault*; installFirmware returns a plain boolean false when not installable, so a rejected install is reported to the operator as a started install.

BidCos branch: CONFIRMED. RFDevice.cpp:246-256 and HS485Device.cpp:294-298 populate FIRMWARE / AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE / UPDATABLE and never FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE, and the WebUI's non-HmIP branch gates purely on `AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE != "0.0.0" && AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE != FIRMWARE`. So "BidCos reports installability directly with no state gate" is exactly what the firmware does. InProgress()'s hard gate to HmIP-RF is also correct — there is no BidCos in-progress phase to miss.

One unit-in-the-last-place divergence on the zero-version rule: our isZeroVersion also rejects "0.0" and "0"; the WebUI's BidCos action panel compares only against "0.0.0" (:135), while its display helper suppresses both "0.0" and "0.0.0" (:107). Ours is the safer superset, not a defect, but it is not what the install gate does.

Also worth recording: the WebUI picks the RPC by interface, not by device — updateFirmware for everything except HmIP-RF and HmIP-Wired, installFirmware for those two (ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368). Our try-installFirmware-then-fall-back-on-fault ordering reaches the same place for the interfaces we model (there is no InterfaceHmIPWired in pkg/hmenum/interface.go).
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our ready-set been right, isUpdateInstallable would have read `updateState == READY_FOR_UPDATE || DO_UPDATE_PENDING || PERFORMING_UPDATE` with no live-state clause, and the WebUI switch would have had no LIVE_* case that renders an Update button. It reads the opposite in both places: DO_UPDATE_PENDING/PERFORMING_UPDATE absent from the predicate, two LIVE_ states present. For the BidCos half, had a state gate existed I would have found FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE written into dev_desc in RFDevice.cpp / HS485Device.cpp next to AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE; the key is absent from both.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted at Tier 1. Every citation checked and every quote present verbatim: both firmware enums, isUpdateInstallable's three-term disjunction, translateFirmwareUpdateState's "LIVE_" prefix rule, installFirmware's plain `return false` on a non-installable device, and all six WebUI switch arms at the exact cited lines. The BidCos half is confirmed the hard way — FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE occurs nowhere in src/rfd, src/hs485d or src/devicetypes (zero grep hits), so "BidCos reports installability directly with no state gate" is what the firmware does, and InProgress()'s hard gate to HmIP-RF is right because BidCos has no in-progress phase.

Finding (a) MISSING STATE stands and is the one that matters. LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE is installable per the RPC guard AND gets a real Update button in the WebUI (:168-188; the only carve-outs are HmIP-HAP/HmIPW-DRAP below fw 2.1 and HmIP-HAP2, which show an info message instead). Our enum already carries the constant; IsFirmwareUpdateReady simply omits it, so GatedLatestFirmware returns info.Current and an installable access-point update is hidden. Confirmed.

Finding (b) OVER-WIDE STATES: the set-width divergence is real against both firmware surfaces, but the stated damage is NOT reachable and I demote it. DeriveDeviceUpdateStatus (pkg/hmenum/device.go:68-70) tests IsFirmwareUpdateInProgress FIRST, and both over-wide members (DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE) are in that set — so the update entity reports "installing", never "update_available", and never presents itself as an offer that installFirmware would answer false. The only observable effect is that LatestFirmware()/UpdateAvailable() report the target version while an install runs, which is what the WebUI's PERFORMING_UPDATE row conveys too. Downgrade (b) from "offers an install the CCU rejects" to a latent set-width divergence.

Finding (c) stands and is strengthened: ccu.go:223-231 treats a successful call as success and only retries updateFirmware on an XMLRPCFault, while installFirmware returns a plain boolean. The CCU's OWN client checks it — ic_ifacecmd.cgi:371 reads `if { $result == 1 }` before reporting success. We do not.

Two refinements to the bundle's own text: LIVE_DELIVER_FIRMWARE_IMAGE is accepted by isUpdateInstallable but the WebUI renders a status row for it (:189-191), so the two firmware surfaces disagree there — only LIVE_NEW_FIRMWARE_AVAILABLE is unambiguously "offer it" on both. And the firmware carries a third grouping our sets match neither of: UPDATE_PENDING is true for {DO_UPDATE_PENDING, PERFORMING_UPDATE, READY_FOR_UPDATE}. The isZeroVersion note is right: :135 compares only "0.0.0", the display helper at :107 suppresses "0.0" and "0.0.0"; ours is a safe superset.

reachesDevice.title: An empty string coerces a boolean data point to false
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/generic/coerce.go:53-75 (toBool), reached via coerceWire → DataPoint.OnWireValue / RestoreCachedValue / paramDefault
reachesDevice.ourValue: toBool accepts "true","1","on","yes" → (true,true) and "false","0","off","no","" → (false,true). An empty string is a *confirmed* false.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: The CCU's own string→boolean conversion is Tcl_GetBoolean, whose accepted set is {0,1,true,false,yes,no,on,off} (case-insensitive, unambiguous abbreviations allowed) and which returns TCL_ERROR — not false — for the empty string. In the other direction a boolean is marshalled to the string "1" or "0", never "". An unknown value is a fault, not an empty string: rfd's getValue throws XmlRpcException("Failure") and the HmIP side throws an unknown-parameter-value RPC exception when the channel holds no value.
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:119-123 (`}else if(strstr(type, "bool")==type){//bool` … `retval=Tcl_GetBoolean(interp, value, &b);`); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:204-209 (`case XmlRpcValue::TypeBoolean: sval=(bool)v?"1":"0";`); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/getvalue.tcl (Interface.getValue returns that string; Interface.setValue passes `[list $type $value]` straight into the same converter); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:286-300; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getValue
reachesDevice.finding:
The literal set our code accepts is exactly the firmware's — {true,1,on,yes} / {false,0,off,no} is Tcl_GetBoolean's acceptance set, which is a real and useful grounding for the eight named literals. The empty string is the one member that is not: the firmware's converter returns TCL_ERROR for it, i.e. "this is not a boolean", which is our (false,false), not our (false,true).

And the premise behind including it does not hold on either ingest path. (i) The ReGa seed: our fetch_all_device_data script only emits a data point that has a valid Timestamp(), and for ValueType()==2 it writes the unquoted JSON literals true/false — so a bool arrives as a Go bool, never as a string, and an unknown bool is omitted from the document entirely rather than sent as "". (ii) Direct reads: Interface.getValue hands back the marshalled "1"/"0"; a value the CCU does not have produces an XML-RPC fault, which checkXmlRpcStatus turns into a JSON-RPC error. There is no CCU surface I could find that encodes "unknown boolean" as an empty string.

So the "" case is dead on the seeding path and live only on the REST generic SetValue path, where it is the wrong answer in the damaging direction: a client posting "" gets a confirmed false written toward the device, whereas the CCU would have rejected the same string. Dropping "" from the falsey list makes toBool agree with the firmware exactly and leaves the DP unobserved instead of confidently off.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been right I would have found either "" inside the firmware's boolean acceptance path (Tcl_GetBoolean accepting it, or a guard mapping empty→false before it) or a CCU response shape that emits "" for a BOOL whose value is unknown. Instead the converter errors on "", the marshaller emits only "1"/"0", and both the BidCos and HmIP getValue implementations raise a fault for an absent value — three independent places that would have looked different.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The VERDICT survives but the GROUNDING does not, and I have re-sourced it.

What I broke. (1) The load-bearing input is unreadable. The bundle's central claim — "Tcl_GetBoolean's accepted set is {0,1,true,false,yes,no,on,off} and it returns TCL_ERROR for the empty string" — is not in any Tier-1/2/3 tree. Tcl core is not bundled (find for tclGet*, tclUtil.c, tclInt.h over ../OpenCCU-Base and ../OpenCCU returns nothing). That is external Tcl API documentation presented as a firmware reading. What tclrpc.cpp itself shows is only that a bool-typed value is handed to Tcl_GetBoolean and that a non-OK return propagates as TCL_ERROR rather than as false — the acceptance set is invisible there.
(2) Wrong surface. tclrpc's XmlRpcValueFromString is the CCU acting as an XML-RPC *client*: a ReGa/WebUI script passing `[list bool <string>]` into Interface.setValue. Our toBool decodes values arriving FROM the CCU and values arriving from our own REST clients. Different direction, different consumer.
(3) The supporting claim is refuted outright. "The literal set our code accepts is exactly the firmware's — a real and useful grounding for the eight named literals" is false. On the surface our code is actually on — the CCU's own XmlRpcValue parser — "on", "yes", "off" and "no" appear nowhere. Our set is WIDER than the firmware's, not equal to it. Strike that half of the grounding.

What replaces it, and why the verdict still stands. libXmlRpc is the value library rfd and hs485d link, so boolFromXml/boolFromStream/boolFromText are the CCU's own decoders for exactly the values we decode. All three reject an empty input as a parse failure, and both emitters produce non-empty tokens, so no CCU surface encodes an unknown boolean as "". Independently, the seeding premise holds in our own repo: fetch_all_device_data.fn emits bare JSON true/false for ValueType()==2 and omits any DP without a valid Timestamp(), so a bool never reaches coerceWire as a string on that path. The "" branch is therefore dead on ingest and live only on the REST generic SetValue path, where a client posting "" gets a confirmed false written toward the device that the CCU itself would have rejected. Dropping "" leaves the DP unobserved instead of confidently off.

reachesDevice.title: The WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS key-to-bit assignment is explicitly unestablished
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseHmIPWeeklyProgram.js:357 `valCheckBox = Math.pow(2, index);` (expert) and :363 `valCheckBox = tmpVal << 3;` (non-expert, seeded `tmpVal = 1` at :361); :614 `for (var x = 0; x < bVal.length; x += 3) { tmp += bVal[x]; }`; :239-241 `_bit"+index+"0").attr("checked",true); // Auto` else `_bit"+index+"1") // Manu`; :517-555 getRelevantChannels (pushes the device's channel-list index of every `*_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER` / access-control channel); per-family overrides at :52 (HmIP-BSL `[4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14]`), :57 (HmIP-WKP `[1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15]`), :336-345+:470-476 (HmIP-FWI Wiegand: list index 0-7 -> bits 3-10, index 8-10 -> bits 0-2), :351 (HmIP-DRG-DALI `Math.pow(2,(val-1))`, channels 1-48 -> bits 0-47). Door-lock surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseHmIPWeeklyProgram_AccessReceiver.js:302 `Math.pow(2, index)`, :308 `value='256'` (DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER :12), :311 `value='512'` (AUTO_RELOCK_TRANSCEIVER :13). The value read is our parameter: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/hmip_weekly_program.fn:17 `object objChannelLocks = cObj.DPByControl("WEEK_PROFILE.CHANNEL_LOCKS");` and :64 `opts.channelLocks`.
reachesDevice.finding: The firmware DOES define an explicit mapping, and it is not the uniform 8x3 grid our table hard-codes. The CCU's own weekly-program editor derives the bit positionally from the channel's index in `relevantChn` — the device's channel list filtered to `*_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER` plus the access-control channel types — and that list is overridden per device family. Two firmware facts do back our table: the inverted semantics (set bit = Manu = schedule off; :239-241) and the stride of 3 (the easy-mode view takes every third bit, :614, and writes 1, 1<<3, 1<<6, ..., :361-364), so 'actor N primary = bit 3(N-1)' is the firmware's own scheme for ordinary multi-actor virtual-receiver actors (HmIP-BSM/PS/FSM, and HmIP-BSL where the firmware's own override [4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14] lands on bits 0-8 exactly as our keys 1_1..3_3 do). It breaks where the firmware overrides the list, and our deriveTargetChannels (custom-DP groups sorted by group number, primary-then-secondaries) has no equivalent: (a) HmIP-DLP — our registry gives IPLock a single scheduled group at channel 12 (profiles.go:887-891), so key 1_1 -> bit 0, while the firmware puts DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER :12 at bit 8 (256) and bit 0 is PERMISSION_TRANSCEIVER :4 (user 1); (b) HmIP-FWI — our IPAccessPermission gives 8 single-member groups at channels 1..8 (profiles.go:1081-1085), keys 1_1..8_1 -> bits 0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21, while the firmware puts those same 8 ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER channels at bits 3..10 and reserves bits 0-2 for the virtual switch receivers; (c) HmIP-DRG-DALI — our 48 single-member groups (profiles.go:961-965) yield keys 9_1..48_1 that ChannelKeyToBitmask rejects outright, and keys 2_1..8_1 -> bits 3..21 while the firmware uses bit = channelNo-1 (bits 1..7), needing 48 bits, not 24. The '24-bit mask measured on live hardware' in the comment is therefore a per-device property, not a scheme-wide one. HmIP-RGBW is a partial case: our keys 1_1..1_3 land on the firmware's bits 0-2 correctly, but the group's 4th member (channel 4, firmware bit 3) has no key `1_4` in the table and is silently dropped.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our positional grid been the firmware's universal scheme, iseHmIPWeeklyProgram.js would contain one bit formula and no per-family `relevantChn` overrides; instead it carries eight device-specific overrides and two alternative bit formulas (`index+3`/`index-8` for Wiegand, `val-1` for DALI). Had the firmware carried no mapping at all, the dialog would submit a channel list rather than a summed `Math.pow(2, ...)` bitmask into WEEK_PROGRAM_TARGET_CHANNEL_LOCKS. Both alternatives are visibly absent.
reachesDevice.ourValue: key `<actor>_<sub>` -> bit 3*(actor-1)+(sub-1), uniformly, 24 bits; actor = rank of the custom-DP channel group by group number, sub = primary then secondaries
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: bit = index of the channel in the device's schedule-relevant channel list (`*_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER` + access-control types, channel order), with explicit per-family overrides; e.g. HmIP-DLP :12 -> 256, :13 -> 512, :4..:11 -> 1..128; HmIP-FWI ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER :1..:8 -> bits 3..10; HmIP-DRG-DALI bit = channelNo-1 over 48 bits
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD and strengthened. I re-read every cited line and closed the one gap the prior agent left open: that the WebUI editor is on our surface. It is — legacy-parameter-definition.config maps the ReGa control `WEEK_PROFILE.CHANNEL_LOCKS` the editor reads onto the legacy parameter `WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS` our code parses, and the editor's write (`WPTCLS=<bit>,WPTCL=<mode>`, iseHmIPWeeklyProgram.js:635) is byte-for-byte the string our datapoint.go:663 BuildCombinedParameterValue emits. Same read parameter, same write parameter, same bit space. The `relevantChn` entries are channel NUMBERS, not array positions guessed from order: three independent places in the source say so — the DALI branch computes the bit as `val-1`, the AccessReceiver renders `relevantChn[8]`/`[9]` as the operator-visible channel label, and the non-expert Wiegand list is hard-coded `[1..8,10,11,12]`, exactly HmIP-FWI's ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER and SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER channels. So the bit position was read from the source, not conventionalised. Our path confirmed device by device: HmIP-DLP — IPLock declares ScheduleChannelNo=14 (profiles.go:892), so ScheduleRelevantChannelGroups keeps only that group; primary channel 12 becomes key 1_1 -> bit 0, while the firmware puts :12 at bit 8 and bit 0 at PERMISSION_TRANSCEIVER :4. HmIP-FWI — IPAccessPermission's 8 single-member groups (profiles.go:1085) yield 1_1..8_1 -> bits 0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21 against the firmware's 3..10. HmIP-DRG-DALI — 48 single-member groups (profiles.go:965) yield 9_1..48_1, which ChannelKeyToBitmask rejects outright, and the parameter is a 48-bit STRING our uint32 path cannot hold at all. Agreement where the prior agent said so, verified: BSM :4,:5,:6 -> bits 0,1,2; BSL's own firmware override [4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14] lands on bits 0..8 exactly as keys 1_1..3_3. HmIP-RGBW is worse than 'partial': its ProfileConfig (profile_configs.go:256-262) declares PrimaryChannel + SecondaryChannels {1,2,3}, so deriveTargetChannels MINTS key `1_4` for channel 4 — a key absent from channelKeyBitmask, so ChannelKeyToBitmask returns false and SetScheduleEnabled fails with 'unknown channel key "1_4"' for a channel the firmware addresses at bit 3. The table comment's '24-bit mask measured on live hardware' is a per-device fact (Tier 2: 43 devices at MAX 16777215, DALI at 2^48-1), not a scheme-wide one.

reachesDevice.title: The RSSI normalisation bands and their rejected sentinels rest on the Python sibling alone
reachesDevice.citation: BidCoS: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:503 `int rssi=-1*frame.GetByteData(13);` and :505 `if(receiver && rssi){`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFCommMessage.cpp:174 `payload.SetRSSI(-1*GetRSSI());`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/multimacd/SerialFrame/HmLegacyFrameBidcos/HmLegacyFrameBidcosRxTelegram.cpp:38-40 `return -Data().GetUInt8Value( 2 );`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/multimacd/SerialFrame/LowLevelMacFrame/LowLevelMacFrameRxTelegram.cpp:52-54 `return -Data().GetUInt8Value( 3 );`; the 'unknown' marker ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosFrame.h:214 `INVALID_RSSI_VALUE=-0xffff`, seeded in RFDevice.cpp:63-64 and returned verbatim by the getValue path RFDevice.cpp:707-710. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory#createReadEvent8bitSignedIntegerParameter (RSSI_DEVICE and RSSI_PEER are read+event 8-bit SIGNED integers, min -128, max 127); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.IncomingHMIPFrameHandler#handleIncomingFrame (`rssiDevice = incomingFrame.getRssi() * -1`, the source being a Java `byte` from de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.internal.HMIPTRXListener); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler#handleStatusFrame — RSSI_PEER is published only when `(statusFrame.getRssiValue() & 0xFF) != 128`, then as `getRssiValue() * -1`; the same method publishes RSSI_DEVICE with no such guard. Tier 2 is silent: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_wds_v1_1.xml:79-88 declares both as `<logical type="integer"/>` with no min, max or special_value.
reachesDevice.finding: Our two claims that matter are confirmed, and one boundary is one unit too tight. Confirmed: 128 (0x80) is the CCU's own no-signal marker — HMIPApplicationHandler tests `(getRssiValue() & 0xFF) != 128` before publishing RSSI_PEER — and it must be dropped client-side because the same method publishes RSSI_DEVICE with no such test, so a raw 128 (from the signed byte -128 negated) does reach us. Confirmed: the two encodings our bands straddle are real. BidCoS negates an UNSIGNED byte (`-1*GetByteData(13)`, `-Data().GetUInt8Value(2)`), giving [-255,-1] where the magnitude is the dBm figure; HmIP negates a SIGNED byte, giving mostly positive values (+70 meaning -70 dBm). Our band 3 (`-256 < v < -129 -> -v-256`) is exactly the two's-complement reinterpretation of a BidCoS byte >= 130, and band 2 (`1 < v < 127 -> -v`) is exactly the HmIP case. Narrowed: the firmware's rejected set is {128} plus BidCoS's INVALID_RSSI_VALUE = -65535 and the `if(receiver && rssi)` suppression of 0; our strict inequalities additionally discard -129, -127, 1 and 127, which the firmware publishes as ordinary readings — HmIP byte -127 negated is exactly 127 and passes every firmware guard; BidCoS bytes 127 and 129 yield -127 and -129. The boundary runs at |128| exactly, not at the exclusive |127|/|129| our bands use. -65535 is correctly dropped by our fall-through, but by no named rule. Which source to follow: Tier 1, not the descriptor — the shipped device XMLs declare RSSI as a bare integer with no bounds and no special values, so a per-device MIN/MAX read at runtime carries nothing here.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had 128 not been a sentinel, HMIPApplicationHandler would publish RSSI_PEER unconditionally like it does RSSI_DEVICE; the `& 0xFF != 128` test is present and is the only value-dependent guard in that method. Had the wire value been plain dBm rather than a negated byte, there would be no `* -1` in IncomingHMIPFrameHandler and no `-1*GetByteData(13)` in RFDevice.cpp — both are present, on both stacks.
reachesDevice.ourValue: reject -127, 0, 1, 127, 128, 129 and |v| >= 256; accept everything else via the four bands
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: reject 128 only (HmIP, and only enforced by the CCU for RSSI_PEER); BidCoS emits [-255,-1] with 0 suppressed at source and -65535 (INVALID_RSSI_VALUE) for 'never measured'; declared HmIP logical range is min -128 / max 127
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD as narrowed, with two corrections to the prior narrowing itself. (1) OVERSTATED: 'BidCoS emits [-255,-1] with 0 suppressed at source' holds only for RSSI_DEVICE on the ACK/INFO_STATUS path (RFDevice.cpp:505). The two paths that set RSSI_PEER — BidcosInterfaceConcentrator.cpp:382 (response frames) and :854 (received frames) — guard only against INVALID_RSSI_VALUE, so a frame byte of 0 becomes RSSI_PEER = 0 and reaches our client. Our rejection of 0 is therefore load-bearing, not redundant, and the prior agent's account would have let it be removed as dead. (2) NOT PERFORMABLE, and it is one of our four bands: band 4 (`129 < v < 256 -> v-256`) is unreachable from either firmware stack. BidCoS negates an unsigned byte and so publishes only [-255, 0]; HmIP negates a signed byte and so publishes at most 128. Nothing in Tier 1 produces 130..255 on RSSI_DEVICE or RSSI_PEER, so no firmware evidence can confirm or refute that band's transformation — it can only be grounded on a source neither tree carries (CUxD or Homegear descriptors). (3) A limit the prior agent stated as fact but did not ground: band 3's transformation `-v-256` reinterprets the CCU's own `-1 * unsigned char` result as a signed char. The firmware never does that reinterpretation anywhere; what Tier 1 establishes is only that values in [-255,-130] arrive, not what they mean. Call the arrival measured and the meaning unverified. Confirmed unchanged: 128 is the CCU's no-signal marker and does reach us on RSSI_DEVICE (the &0xFF test guards RSSI_PEER alone), so dropping it client-side is required; -65535 is correctly dropped, though by fall-through rather than a named rule; our extra exclusions of -129, -127, 1 and 127 discard values both stacks can publish, the firmware's own boundary sitting at |128| exactly. Which source to follow: Tier 1. The HmIP descriptor declares min -128/max 127 yet the same server publishes 128 on RSSI_DEVICE, and the BidCoS XMLs declare no bounds at all, so a per-device MIN/MAX read at runtime carries nothing here.

reachesDevice.title: FixedColorLight `slot` is cast straight to a FixedColor ordinal on the strength of an uncited claim about the descriptor's COLOR value order
reachesDevice.site: internal/central/adapter/custom_dp_dispatcher.go:373-388 (`light.FixedColor(slot)`), with internal/model/custom/light/color.go:451-458 (the ordinals) and :576-581 (`Color()` casting the CCU's raw enum index)
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/getColorElement.tcl:10-17 `set options(0) "${BLACK}" / options(1) "${BLUE}" / options(2) "${GREEN}" / options(3) "${TURQUOISE}" / options(4) "${RED}" / options(5) "${PURPLE}" / options(6) "${YELLOW}" / options(7) "${WHITE}"` (identical files under easymodes/UNIVERSAL_ACTOR/ and easymodes/UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER_PWM/); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/msg/setDimmerVirtualReceiverCombinedParam.htm:11,13 (`<option value="3">TURQUOISE`, `<option value="5">PURPLE`); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/dimmer.fn:89 and opticalsignalreceiver.fn:65 (`"${lblOff}\t${optionColorBLUE}\t${optionColorGREEN}\t${optionColorTURQUOISE}\t${optionColorRED}\t${optionColorPURPLE}\t${optionColorYELLOW}\t${optionColorWHITE}"`). HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColor — BLACK(0), BLUE(1), GREEN(2), TURQUOISE(3), RED(4), PURPLE(5), YELLOW(6), WHITE(7), RANDOM(253), OLD_VALUE(254), DO_NOT_CARE(255) — whose #getNames(false) supplies the first eight names, in that order, as the legacy VALUE_LIST.
reachesDevice.finding: The comment's claim is confirmed verbatim by Tier 1 on both stacks: the CCU's COLOR value list is the RGB bit pattern (bit0 blue, bit1 green, bit2 red) — 0 BLACK, 1 BLUE, 2 GREEN, 3 TURQUOISE, 4 RED, 5 PURPLE, 6 YELLOW, 7 WHITE. The cast it justifies is nevertheless wrong in both directions. Our light.FixedColor ordinals are 0 BLACK, 1 RED, 2 GREEN, 3 YELLOW, 4 BLUE, 5 MAGENTA("PURPLE"), 6 CYAN("TURQUOISE"), 7 WHITE: only 0, 2, 5 and 7 coincide; 1<->4 (RED/BLUE) and 3<->6 (YELLOW/TURQUOISE) are transposed. So `set_color {"slot": 4}` from any caller holding the CCU's own index writes "BLUE" where the firmware means RED. The read path has the same defect and no documentation: FixedColorLight.color is a generic.Select whose Value() is the raw VALUE_LIST index the CCU pushed, and color.go:576-581 casts it straight to FixedColor, so a device reporting the firmware's BLUE(1) surfaces as RED through Color()/ColorName() — while ChannelHsColor() (color.go:672-688) resolves CHANNEL_COLOR by NAME via custom.EnumLabelValue and gets it right, so the two accessors disagree about the same colour. SetColor's optimistic `l.color.OnEvent(int32(c))` (color.go:606) writes our ordinal into that same index-valued DP, so the disagreement persists until the CCU echo arrives. One further hazard the source carries and our enum does not: SimpleRGBColor's extended set is sparse (RANDOM 253, OLD_VALUE 254, DO_NOT_CARE 255), so on any device declaring the extended list the VALUE_LIST index and the wire value diverge above 7 as well.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the descriptor list matched our enum, the CCU's own colour selectors would read BLACK, RED, GREEN, YELLOW, BLUE, ... — four independent firmware sites (three easymode getColorElement.tcl files, dimmer.fn, opticalsignalreceiver.fn, setDimmerVirtualReceiverCombinedParam.htm) instead all read BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE, and SimpleRGBColor assigns those same ordinals explicitly rather than by declaration order.
reachesDevice.ourValue: FixedColor: 0 BLACK, 1 RED, 2 GREEN, 3 YELLOW, 4 BLUE, 5 PURPLE, 6 TURQUOISE, 7 WHITE
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: COLOR: 0 BLACK, 1 BLUE, 2 GREEN, 3 TURQUOISE, 4 RED, 5 PURPLE, 6 YELLOW, 7 WHITE (+ RANDOM 253, OLD_VALUE 254, DO_NOT_CARE 255)
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD for the read path, which is the half that is a live defect; the other two halves of the prior finding need correcting. CONFIRMED: FixedColorLight.color is a generic.Select bound to the raw COLOR wire parameter (color.go:481, custom.SelectField), its Value() is the VALUE_LIST index, and crRFD.conf:47 plus DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue prove the CCU sends exactly that index. Color() at color.go:576-581 casts it straight to FixedColor, so a device reporting BLUE(1) surfaces as RED and TURQUOISE(3) as YELLOW; only 0, 2, 5 and 7 coincide. ColorName() inherits it, while ChannelHsColor() (color.go:676-688) resolves CHANNEL_COLOR by NAME through custom.EnumLabelValue and gets it right — the two accessors disagree about the same colour, and the fix is one line (l.color.Label(), which generic.Select already provides). CONFIRMED: SetColor's optimistic `l.color.OnEvent(int32(c))` at color.go:604 writes our ordinal into an index-valued DP, so the disagreement persists until the CCU echo lands. OVERSTATED — the write path: the prior agent presents `set_color {"slot": 4}` writing BLUE-for-RED as a defect. It is a documented contract. custom_dp_dispatcher.go:373-376 says in as many words that the descriptor's value list is ordered by the RGB bit pattern and that a caller holding only the descriptor must use "label"; SetColorByName (color.go:610-621) is that path, and it resolves through fixedColorNames to the string the CCU parses. The write path is correct for a caller that reads its own API. REFUTED — the 'one further hazard': the prior agent claims that on a device declaring the extended list, VALUE_LIST index and wire value diverge above 7 because SimpleRGBColor is sparse at 253/254/255. Wrong surface. Those are the HmIP-internal physical bytes; StringEnumToInteger converts them to the enum NAME, and DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue then converts the name to a dense ordinal into getEnumStrings() before it reaches legacy XML-RPC. The observed Tier-2 VALUE_LIST is 10 dense entries with no gap. Nothing sparse crosses our wire.

reachesDevice.title: Two CCU-behaviour claims on the device-admin port have no source: the deleteDevice bitmask and the channel-rename cascade
reachesDevice.site: pkg/interfaces/rest_ports.go:109-116; constants at internal/client/backends/backend.go:61-69; rename at internal/central/central.go:1062-1089
reachesDevice.citation: (a) Bitmask, verbatim from ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:51-56: `//! Flags für DeleteDevice()` / `DELETE_FLAG_RESET=(1<<0), //!< Gerät in Werkszustand zurücksetzen` / `DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=(1<<1), //!< Löschen erzwingen, auch wenn Gerät nicht erreichbar` / `DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=(1<<2) //!< Wenn Gerät nicht erreichbar, bei nächster Gelegenheit löschen`. Same three in the XML-RPC doc comment ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:115-117 as 0x01 / 0x02 / 0x04. Semantics, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:913-931: `if (flags & DELETE_FLAG_RESET) { success = dev->FactoryReset(); } else { success = dev->UnpeerCentral(); }` then `if (!success) { if (flags & DELETE_FLAG_DEFER) { dev->ScheduleDelete(flags & ~DELETE_FLAG_DEFER); return true; } if (!(flags & DELETE_FLAG_FORCE)) return false; }`. Wire acceptance, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:126-130: booleans in params[1]/params[2] map to RESET/FORCE, and `if(params[1].getType()==XmlRpcValue::TypeInt)flags=params[1];` — the integer form overwrites, so our two-argument integer call is the documented path. (b) Rename: the OpenCCU distribution patch ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0099-WebUI-Add-DeviceRenameAllChannels.patch adds `DeviceConfigDialog.renameChannels`, which builds `var chNumber = channel.address.split(':')[1];` and `var chName = $(this.NAME_ID).value + $(this.SEPARATOR_ID).value + chNumber;` where the separator is a text input declared in the same patch as `<input id="DeviceConfigDialog_DeviceChannelsRenameSeparator" size="2" type="text" value=":"/>`; it also treats `this.device.name+":"+chNumber` as the un-renamed default name and skips channels that differ from it unless "including own names" is ticked. Corroborating the same convention inside the shipped firmware: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/pages/GroupEditPage.ftl:449 `homematic("Channel.setName", {id: channel.id, name: groupName+":"+parseInt(index + channelOffset)}, ...)`. Neither ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/webui/js/webui.js nor ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/webui.js contains renameChannels or the separator field.
reachesDevice.finding: (a) is confirmed exactly and needs no change: DeleteFlagReset=1 and DeleteFlagForce=2 in internal/client/backends/backend.go:64,68 match DELETE_FLAG_RESET=(1<<0) and DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=(1<<1), with the right meanings — RESET selects FactoryReset() over UnpeerCentral(), FORCE decides only whether a failed unpair still removes the device. One narrowing worth writing down, because it changes what FORCE does: a third bit, DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=4, is checked before FORCE, and when set it swallows the failure, schedules the delete for the device's next contact and returns success. We never set it, so our FORCE semantics hold; but "the reset and force booleans map onto the bitmask" understates a surface that has three bits, and abortDeleteDevice (XmlRpcMethods.cpp:145-155) exists solely to cancel a deferred delete we cannot currently create. (b) is where the claim narrows. The pattern is right and the channel number is right — we compose `name + ":" + ch.Number` from the real channel number, matching the patch's `channel.address.split(':')[1]` rather than a list index — and the firmware's own HmIP group editor writes channel names the same way. But "matching the CCU WebUI behaviour" is true only one step in: the rename-all-channels dialog is an OpenCCU distribution patch, absent from the OCCU WebUI sources entirely, so on stock eQ-3 firmware there is no WebUI behaviour to match. Even on OpenCCU the separator is an operator-editable field whose default — not whose fixed value — is ":", and the dialog by default leaves manually renamed channels alone, which we do not: our loop renames every channel unconditionally. The boundary: our string is what the CCU produces with default settings, and it is what the CCU itself treats as a channel's default name, so a name catalogue we write stays consistent with one the CCU wrote. It is not what an operator who changed the separator, or who kept custom channel names, will see.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: (a) Had the bits been swapped, RFManager.h:53-54 would read FORCE=(1<<0)/RESET=(1<<1) and RFManager::DeleteDevice would branch FactoryReset() on `flags & (1<<1)`; it branches on DELETE_FLAG_RESET, the (1<<0) constant. Had the integer form not been accepted, XmlRpcMethods.cpp:128 would have no `TypeInt` branch and our two-argument call would land on the boolean path with params[1] unmatched, sending flags=0. (b) Had the WebUI used a different pattern, the patch would build the name from something other than device name + separator + `address.split(':')[1]`, and GroupEditPage.ftl would not concatenate with a literal colon. Had the feature been stock, renameChannels would appear in the OCCU webui.js — searching both copies returns nothing, which is the different result the check was able to produce.
reachesDevice.ourValue: DeleteFlagReset=1, DeleteFlagForce=2; channel name = name + ":" + ch.Number, applied to every channel
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: DELETE_FLAG_RESET=1, DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=2, DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=4 (checked before FORCE); WebUI channel name = deviceName + <operator separator, default ":"> + channelNo, custom-named channels skipped by default, and only on OpenCCU-patched firmware
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld with the reader's own narrowing intact, plus three corrections.

(a) confirmed exactly. Our two constants and their meanings match, RESET selects FactoryReset() over UnpeerCentral(), FORCE decides only whether a failed unpair still removes the device, and the third bit DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=4 is genuinely tested before FORCE and swallows the failure. We never set it, so our FORCE semantics hold; abortDeleteDevice exists solely to cancel a deferred delete we cannot currently create. I additionally checked the wire shape the reader asserted was "the documented path": XmlRpcMethodDeleteDevice::execute touches params[1] and params[2] unconditionally before the type tests, so a two-argument integer call is accepted and the integer form overwrites any boolean mapping. Confirmed.

(b) narrowed, as claimed, and our composition is sound: internal/central/central.go:1080 builds `name + ":" + strconv.Itoa(ch.Number)` where ch.Number comes from internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:2296 `channelNumber(addr)`, which parses the address suffix — the same derivation as the patch's `channel.address.split(':')[1]`, NOT an array index. We do not commit the ordinal-convention error here.

Three corrections to the reader. (i) The citation is wrong in form: the `.patch` file does not contain the JS quoted against it; the expanded directory does. A reader chasing the given path finds only translation strings and a CSS height change. (ii) GroupEditPage.ftl:449 is weaker corroboration than presented — it composes `groupName+":"+parseInt(index + channelOffset)`, an ARRAY-INDEX-derived number with a per-type offset (0 for HmIP-HEATING, else 1), not a parsed channel number. It corroborates the `<name>:<n>` shape only; on the number derivation it is an instance of exactly the convention this project bans, and must not be cited as authority for ch.Number. (iii) The reader called this a WebUI-behaviour claim and stopped at the patch. I looked for a stock Tier-1 source establishing `<devicename>:<channelno>` as the CCU's own default channel name at pairing and found none — no ReGa/tclrega naming site, and the only stock witness is the patch's own `origChName` treating that string as the un-renamed default. So the boundary is: our string is what an OpenCCU CCU produces at default settings and what the patched WebUI itself treats as a channel's default name; that it is the STOCK eQ-3 default is tier1-silent in this corpus. The divergence the reader named stands and is real — the dialog skips manually renamed channels by default, our loop at central.go:1080-1087 renames every channel unconditionally with no equivalent opt-in.

reachesDevice.title: PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT field layout and the -11 h/-10 h/12 °C cancellation code are ported values that reach the device verbatim
reachesDevice.ourValue: "%.1f,%d,%s,%d,%s" with start.Format("02,01,06") / end.Format("02,01,06") → temp, start_minutes_of_day, dd, mm, yy, end_minutes_of_day, dd, mm, yy; cancellation = partyModeCode(now-11h, now-10h, 12.0)
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: Nine comma-separated tokens in exactly that order: PARTY_TEMPERATURE, PARTY_START_TIME, PARTY_START_DAY, PARTY_START_MONTH, PARTY_START_YEAR, PARTY_STOP_TIME, PARTY_STOP_DAY, PARTY_STOP_MONTH, PARTY_STOP_YEAR. Temperature ×2 with +0.5 rounding into 6 bits (≤31.5 °C); both time fields integer-divided by 30 (truncating) into 6 bits; days 5 bits, months 4 bits, years 7 bits.
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1 — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionCCRTDNParty.cpp, `HSSTypeConversionCCRTDNParty::LogicalToPhysical`, which tokenises the string on ',' via the local `getNextToken` and packs 9 bytes. Each token is preceded by the firmware's own copy of the device-XML parameter line it feeds, in this order: `//<parameter type="integer" index="11.0" size="0.6" param="PARTY_TEMPERATURE"/>` with `//float integer scale factor 2` then `d = (d * (double)2); ... unsigned int uintValue = (int)(d + (double)0.5); byte = (unsigned char)(uintValue & BITMASK_LS_6_BIT);`; `//<parameter ... size="0.6" param="PARTY_START_TIME"/>` with `//<conversion type="integer_integer_scale" div="30"/>` then `uintValue = uintValue / 30; byte = (unsigned char)(uintValue & BITMASK_LS_6_BIT);`; `param="PARTY_START_DAY"` (`& BITMASK_LS_5_BIT`); `param="PARTY_START_MONTH"` (`(uintValue << 4) & BITMASK_MS_4_BIT`); `param="PARTY_START_YEAR"` (`& BITMASK_LS_7_BIT`); then PARTY_STOP_TIME (/30, 6 bits), PARTY_STOP_DAY (5 bits), PARTY_STOP_MONTH (4 bits), PARTY_STOP_YEAR (7 bits). A missing token aborts with `"Too few arguments (N)."` and returns false; `in.size()==0` returns false before any parsing. Tokens are parsed with `strtol(..., 10)` and `strtod`, so zero-padded "08"/"09" are decimal, not octal. Tier 1 for ranges and direction — ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml:590-744, the HEATING_CONTROL virtual-device channel that maps 1:1 onto HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU channel 2 and HM-CC-RT-DN channel 4: PARTY_TEMPERATURE `type="FLOAT" min="5.0" max="30.0" default="20.0" unit="°C" operations="3"`; PARTY_START_TIME and PARTY_STOP_TIME `type="INTEGER" min="0" max="1410" unit="minutes" operations="3"`; *_DAY `min="1" max="31"`; *_MONTH `min="1" max="12"`; *_YEAR `min="0" max="99" unit="year"`; and PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT `control="NONE" default="" operations="2" type="STRING"`.
reachesDevice.finding: Field order, count, units and widths are all confirmed against the CCU's own converter — our nine tokens sit in exactly the nine slots it reads, minutes-of-day is the right unit for the two time fields, and two-digit year is right (declared 0..99, packed into 7 bits). The write-only claim is confirmed too: operations="2" and the DP's DEFAULT is the empty string, which the converter rejects outright (`in.size()==0` → return false), so our comment that the empty string cannot cancel a running party is exactly right for the reason stated. Three things the comment does not carry. (1) The CCU truncates both time fields to a 30-minute grid — `uintValue / 30` on an unsigned integer, no rounding — and the descriptor's max of 1410 (= 23:30) states the same grid. Our `startMOD`/`endMOD` are the exact minute, so any window not landing on :00 or :30 is silently snapped BACKWARD by up to 29 minutes at both ends. For SetAway that means a party that ends earlier than the operator asked; for the cancel path it is harmless. (2) A real range hazard on the SetAway path, not the cancel path: `SetAway` documents "pass 0 for the device default", and the KindIP branch honours that with `if away > 0`, but the KindRF branch passes `away` straight into `partyModeCode` unguarded (climate.go:1337). With away == 0 the first token is "0.0", the converter computes 0×2 = 0 and packs a 0 — a 0 °C setpoint, below the firmware's own declared minimum of 5.0 °C. There is no clamp anywhere on this path, and because PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT is a STRING the CCU applies no per-field range check either; the converter's masks only wrap (30.0 °C → 60 fits 6 bits, but 32.0 °C → 64 → wraps to 0). (3) The cancellation convention itself is NOT settled by any source available here, and this is the honest limit of the exercise. The CCU converter is a pure packer: it validates nothing about the window and takes `abs()` of a negative temperature. Whether a window already in the past cancels a running party, and what 12.0 °C means, are decided by the HM-CC-RT-DN's own radio firmware, which is in neither ../OpenCCU-Base nor ../OpenCCU nor the descriptor corpora. Tier 1 is silent on that half; our rule there rests on the Python reference's disable_away_mode RF override alone (Tier 3), and 12.0 in particular has no firmware meaning — it is simply an in-range value the converter accepts. A separate surface caveat worth recording: the shipped ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml carries no PARTY_* parameters at all and no device XML in the tree references `type_conversion_ccrtdn_party`, so this converter is reached through the HmIP heating-group virtual device rather than through a shipped RF device description. The channel mapping in groupdefinitions.xml (HM-CC-RT-DN ch4 / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU ch2) is the firmware's statement of where this parameter lives.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the field order been anything else — say temp last, or mm before dd, or seconds instead of minutes-of-day — the converter's nine inline `param="PARTY_*"` comments would have appeared in that other order, or the START_TIME token would not have been divided by 30, or the descriptor would not have declared max=1410 minutes. Had the year been full four-digit, PARTY_*_YEAR would not be `min="0" max="99"` masked to 7 bits. Each of those would have produced a visibly different reading; they did not. For the 12.0 °C half the control fails by construction: no source in the trees produces a different answer depending on whether 12.0 is meaningful, which is precisely why that half is reported as not settled rather than as verified.
reachesDevice.missingInput: The HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU on-device radio firmware, which is what decides whether a window lying in the past terminates a running party and whether PARTY_TEMPERATURE carries any sentinel. No tree available here contains it; the CCU-side converter only packs the nine fields.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The nine-token layout, both units, the two-digit year and the write-only shape are CONFIRMED on the right surface — and more strongly than claimed, because the CCU's own WebUI emits the identical token order for the same parameter on the same devices. Our `partyModeCode` output maps token-for-token onto the converter's nine `getNextToken` reads.

The prior agent's headline caveat is a measurement error, and it inverted the surface question. It reported that rf_cc_rt_dn.xml "carries no PARTY_* parameters at all" and that "no device XML in the tree references type_conversion_ccrtdn_party", concluding the converter is reached only through the HmIP heating-group virtual device. Both files declare it; the XMLs are ISO-8859-1 and a plain `grep -n` silently suppresses matches in them. The consequence matters: the converter is squarely on the KindRF path our code takes, and the grounding is on-surface rather than adjacent. Related: the ranges were cited from opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml — the HmIP group virtual device, which is a *different* surface that happens to carry the same numbers by mapping. The authority for an RF setValue is the RF device XML, and it agrees.

Three things I confirm and carry forward. (i) The 30-minute truncation is real (`uintValue / 30`, no rounding, and max=1410 = 23:30 declares the same grid), so a SetAway window not on :00/:30 is snapped backward by up to 29 minutes at both ends. (ii) The away==0 hazard is real and unguarded: SetAway's doc says "pass 0 for the device default", the KindIP branch honours it with `if away > 0` (climate.go:1328), and the KindRF branch at climate.go:1337 passes `away` straight into `partyModeCode`; "0.0" packs to 0, i.e. a 0 °C setpoint against a declared min of 5.0. Because PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT is a STRING, no per-field range check runs anywhere; the masks only wrap. (iii) The empty-string claim in DisableAway's comment is right for the reason given — `if(in.size() == 0) return false` at :81, and DEFAULT is the empty string.

What stays open is the half the id names second. Both trees are silent on whether a window already in the past cancels a running party, and 12.0 has no firmware meaning — the converter validates nothing, takes `abs()` of a negative temperature, and packs whatever it is given. The WebUI writes only forward windows. That half rests on ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/climate.py:567-577 alone, which is a Tier-3 witness.

reachesDevice.title: 'Some CCU firmware variants reject a raw setValue' is an uncited comment steering a write path
reachesDevice.ourValue: "Some CCU firmware variants reject a raw setValue for parameters they accept inside put_paramset — HmIP CONTROL_MODE=0 (AUTO) is the canonical case."
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: The asymmetry is real, unconditional and channel-type-driven (not variant-driven): setValue gates on checkRequiredValues, putParameterSet does not. But on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER the gated key is SET_POINT_MODE, not CONTROL_MODE — a bare setValue of CONTROL_MODE passes the gate and is dispatched.
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1 — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#setValue builds a DeviceChannelValuesCommandDTO for the single key and then guards the dispatch with `if (!DeviceUtil.checkRequiredValues(device, channelIndex, valueKey, commandDTO)) { return false; }` — no event-bus send, no fault, and the incomplete DTO is parked in the class's `storedDeviceChannelValuesCommandDTO` static to be merged into the next setValue on the same device+channel. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#putParameterSet has no such call: for parameterSetType "VALUES" it goes straight from #validateAndConvertValues to the event-bus send. #checkRequiredValues builds a per-channel-type required set and decides with `if (paramSet.size() > 0 && (!paramSet.contains(valueKey) || paramSet.contains(valueKey) && paramSet.size() == commandDTO.getValues().size())) { ret = true; }`. Its HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER branch adds SET_POINT_MODE only when the write already carries it, then unconditionally adds SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE. Parameter shape: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createControlModeParameter — `byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE;` and a StateParameter("CONTROL_MODE", LogicalType.INTEGER, PhysicalType.INTEGER, IOOperations(ops), null, 0, 0, 3, ...), i.e. write-only, default 0, range 0..3; IOOperations values are READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4 (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations). Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M.json, channel :1 VALUES — CONTROL_MODE `"OPERATIONS": 2, "MIN": 0, "MAX": 3, "DEFAULT": 0, "TYPE": "INTEGER"`; SET_POINT_MODE `"OPERATIONS": 7`; ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M.json gives channel :1 TYPE = HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER. BidCos side for contrast: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:318-330 forwards setValue straight to RFManager::SetValue with no companion-parameter gate at the RPC layer.
reachesDevice.finding: The mechanism the comment gestures at exists and is exactly the shape claimed — the CCU's HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface really does accept inside put_paramset writes it refuses as a bare setValue, and the refusal is the worst kind: setValue returns false with no XML-RPC fault and no frame sent, so the caller sees success-shaped silence. PutParamsetForce is therefore defensible. But three parts of the sentence are wrong or wider than the firmware. (1) "Some CCU firmware variants" — it is not a variant question. checkRequiredValues is an unconditional branch on the channel's ChannelType, present on every build of this surface; the outcome is deterministic per (channel type, key set). (2) CONTROL_MODE is the wrong canonical case. On HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER the required set is {SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE} (plus SET_POINT_MODE when the write already carries it), and the final predicate short-circuits to ret=true for any valueKey NOT in that set — CONTROL_MODE is not in it, so a bare setValue(CONTROL_MODE, 0) is dispatched normally. The key on that channel that setValue actually refuses alone is SET_POINT_MODE: it lands in the required set, the set has 2 entries against a 1-entry write, the predicate fails, and nothing is sent. That is a striking result because the neighbouring comment in setIPMode (climate.go:1493-1499) already claims writing SET_POINT_MODE "has no effect on most CCU firmwares" — that claim is the one the firmware backs, and it backs it through this gate rather than through read-only-ness (SET_POINT_MODE is declared OPERATIONS 7, fully writable). The two comments have the right facts attached to the wrong parameters. (3) The genuinely gated cases on other channel types are worth naming instead of a vague "some parameters": DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE and RAMP_TIME_UNIT/RAMP_TIME_VALUE (each pair required whole, on any channel type); IDENTIFY_TARGET_LEVEL with IDENTIFY_DURATION and the IDENTIFICATION_MODE_* pair; WEEK_PROGRAM_TARGET_CHANNEL_LOCK(S); STATE on SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER/WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER; LEVEL on SERVO_/DIMMER_/BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and SHADING_RECEIVER (which also injects LEVEL=1.01 when only LEVEL_2 is given); the COLOR/COLOR_BEHAVIOUR pair; the DISPLAY_DATA_* set on ACOUSTIC_DISPLAY_RECEIVER; and on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the four-way {DURATION_UNIT, DURATION_VALUE, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION} — which is directly relevant to the siren path and means a bare setValue of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION alone is silently dropped. Net effect on our code: PutParamsetForce is not needed for the CONTROL_MODE-only ModeAuto write it was justified by, and is needed for cases the comment does not mention. Nothing is broken today — PutParamsetForce is strictly safe, and the two multi-key ModeHeat/ModeOff writes would take put_paramset regardless — but the justification should be rewritten around checkRequiredValues and the ALARM_SWITCH/siren cases, not around CONTROL_MODE and "firmware variants".
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had CONTROL_MODE genuinely been gated, it would have had to appear inside the HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER branch of checkRequiredValues (the way SET_POINT_MODE and SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE do) or in isLegacyParameterDisabled; it appears in neither, and the final predicate's `!paramSet.contains(valueKey)` clause explicitly lets an unlisted key through. Conversely, had there been no asymmetry at all, putParameterSet would have called the same guard — it does not, which is what makes the general claim survive while the example fails.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Demoted from `narrowed` to `contradicted`, because both load-bearing assertions in the comment are false against Tier 1 and I verified each by opening the method.

"Some CCU firmware variants" — #checkRequiredValues is an unconditional branch on the channel's ChannelType. The outcome is a pure function of (channel type, key set); there is no build flag, no version gate. A reader who believes "variants" will conclude the risk is probabilistic and untestable, which is the opposite of true.

"CONTROL_MODE=0 (AUTO) is the canonical case" — I traced the predicate by hand for the exact write our code makes. For a bare {CONTROL_MODE} on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER, paramSet = {SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE}: size > 0 and `!paramSet.contains("CONTROL_MODE")` is true, so ret = true and the DTO is sent. For a bare {SET_POINT_MODE}: paramSet = {SET_POINT_MODE, SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE}, valueKey IS contained and 2 != 1, so the condition fails, ret stays false, the DTO is parked and setValue returns false. So `PutParamsetForce` at internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:1530 is not needed for the ModeAuto write it is justified by, and the ModeHeat/ModeOff writes carry two keys and would take put_paramset regardless. Nothing is broken — PutParamsetForce is strictly safe — but the comment's example is the one case that does not need it.

One narrowing of the prior report, which I checked because it read as too clean. It says SET_POINT_MODE is "declared OPERATIONS 7, fully writable", making the gate the whole story for the neighbouring comment at climate.go:1493 ("writing SET_POINT_MODE has no effect on most CCU firmwares — the value is read-only on the wire"). ClimateStateParameterFactory registers two SET_POINT_MODE variants; the "READ_ONLY" one really is READ|EVENT. So the old comment's read-only claim is correct for channels bound to that variant and wrong for those bound to "default" (the eTRV-B-2 R4M shows 7), where the gate is the operative mechanism. Which variant a given channel gets is a per-channel-type binding I did not enumerate, so "the gate, not read-only-ness" is right for the devices in the corpus and not proven in general.

The siren consequence the prior report surfaced is real and I confirm it verbatim: on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the branch adds all four of DURATION_UNIT, DURATION_VALUE, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION as soon as any one is present, so a bare setValue of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION is dropped silently. That, not CONTROL_MODE, is what the comment should point at.
