ERROR_JAMMED is not an ENUM at all: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory registers it via createReadEventBooleanBit0Parameter.
reachesDevice.finding: Confirmed on both transports. The integer a classified ENUM carries on the XML-RPC surface IS a 0-based position in that parameter's VALUE_LIST, and the two firmware paths build VALUE_LIST from exactly the array they index. BidCos: HSSLogicalTypeOption stores each option AT its declared index (resizing the vector), and GetDescription emits the vector positionally — so a sparse enum (rf_rhs.xml ERROR: NO_ERROR index=0, SABOTAGE index=7; rf_d.xml LOAD_FAILURE index=3) produces a VALUE_LIST with EMPTY-STRING placeholders at the gaps, not a compacted list. Position i therefore still equals wire integer i. HmIP: the legacy surface converts the enum string to its ordinal in getEnumStrings() and publishes the same array as VALUE_LIST; this holds even for converters constructed with explicit enumValues/offset (e.g. SMOKE_DETECTOR_EVENT), because the legacy conversion is purely positional. None of the classified parameters is a bit mask, a count or a 1-based index. Specifics: SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS ordinals are IDLE_OFF=0, PRIMARY_ALARM=1, INTRUSION_ALARM=2, SECONDARY_ALARM=3 — exactly the order pkg/hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go declares, so excluding INTRUSION_ALARM at index 2 is grounded. WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE is [DRY,WET,WATER] = 0,1,2, matching waterStateActiveValues. ERROR_ALARM_TEST and ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER are two-entry options with NO_ERROR at index 0, so classify.go:104-108's claim is exact. ERROR_JAMMED is BOOLEAN on HmIP, not an ENUM — it never enters the index path, and our bool arm handles it. Two narrowings worth recording, neither breaking the rule: (a) 'exhaustive by construction' is true positionally but the list can contain empty strings at gap indices, so any consumer that filters empty VALUE_LIST entries before handing the slice to ActiveFromRaw would silently shift every label past the gap — the exhaustiveness lives in the SLICE INDEX, not in the entry count; (b) out-of-range handling differs: we return inactive, the firmware coerces to default_option (HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:76-77) or passes the number through with a debug log (HmIP). For every parameter this domain classifies default_option is index 0 (NO_ERROR/IDLE_OFF), which is inactive too, so the verdicts agree.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong I would have found one of: a compacting VALUE_LIST builder (options pushed back only when non-empty, so declared index ≠ emitted position); a legacy conversion keyed on StringEnumToInteger#getEnumValues() or #getOffset() rather than the loop index; `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal` absent or false in crRFD.conf, which would make HmIP emit the enum STRING and our int path unreachable; or a classified parameter declared with a bitmask conversion (`option_integer` value_map with mask semantics binding several bits). I found the opposite in each case, and rf_rhs.xml/rf_d.xml prove the sparse case is real and handled by index, not by position-in-file.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld for every parameter this domain actually classifies; demoted because the sparse case, which the prior pass asserted as settled, is not.

What I checked and confirmed. The surface is right: `VALUE_LIST` is written in exactly one place in the entire firmware C++ tree (grep over --include=*.cpp --include=*.h returns only HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:104), and HSSParameter.cpp:118 builds the factory tag as "logical_type_" + the XML `type` attribute, so `<logical type="option">` really does reach this class. The formula is transcribed exactly, including that resize()-then-assign stores each option AT its declared index. On the HmIP side I read DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue and confirmed the outbound conversion is a plain 0-based scan with no offset applied — this matters, because StringEnumToInteger has a (enumStrings, offset) constructor that would have broken the rule had the legacy path used it, and it does not. SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus's ordinals are not a convention I supplied: Java values()/ordinal() is declaration order by definition, and the declaration order is IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM, matching pkg/hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go, so excluding INTRUSION_ALARM at index 2 is grounded. I also confirmed our side does not disturb the list: internal/security/index.go:267 and internal/alarm/resolver.go:187 hand ParameterData().ValueList straight to ActiveFromRaw with no filtering of empty entries.

What breaks the prior verdict. The prior finding states as fact that a sparse enum yields a placeholder-padded VALUE_LIST so 'position i still equals wire integer i', and cites rf_rhs ERROR (SABOTAGE index=7) and rf_d LOAD_FAILURE (index=3) as the examples. That is what Tier 1 computes. It is not what the descriptor corpus reports: those same parameters come back compacted, two entries, MAX=1, in 6 RHS descriptors and 20 dimmer descriptors. I checked the obvious escape — that the distribution patches the XMLs or the option class — and neither rf_rhs nor HSSLogicalTypeOption is touched by any patch under ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu. So which shape a real CCU puts on the wire for a sparse option list is not settled by the material available to me, and I will not pick one by convention.

Why the demotion is narrow rather than fatal. All four parameters this domain classifies are dense and carry their idle label at index 0 (SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS, WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE, ERROR_ALARM_TEST, ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER), and Tier 1 and Tier 2 agree on all four; classify.go:104-108's claim about NO_ERROR at index 0 is exact. ERROR_JAMMED never enters the index path — HMIPServer GeneralStateParameterFactory registers it via createReadEventBooleanBit0Parameter, so it is BOOLEAN and our bool arm handles it. The unresolved case is the operator-enrolment path at internal/alarm/resolver.go:187, which hands ActiveFromRaw an arbitrary enrolled parameter's ValueList: enrol HM-Sec-RHS ERROR with ActiveValues [SABOTAGE] and the wire value 7 resolves correctly under the Tier-1 shape and returns ActivationIndexOutOfRange -> inactive under the Tier-2 shape. That is the direction that loses a sabotage alarm rather than raising a false one, which is the safer failure, but it is a failure. The prior finding's narrowing (b) about out-of-range handling I confirmed and it stands: HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:76-77 coerces to default_option, HmIP logs and passes through, and for every parameter this domain classifies default_option is index 0, so the verdicts agree.

reachesDevice.title: The low-battery flag is searched on exactly channels 0, 1 and 2 — a channel set nothing in the source states
reachesDevice.citation: BidCos-RF/Wired descriptors: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml and ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml — 176 device XMLs declare LOWBAT; parsing every `<channel index=… count=…>` and expanding `count`, the minimum channel carrying LOWBAT is 0 in ALL 176. Channel 0 declarations are `<channel index="0" type="MAINTENANCE" ui_flags="internal" class="maintenance" count="1">` with `<parameter id="LOWBAT" operations="read,event" ui_flags="service"><logical type="boolean"/><physical … interface="internal" value_id="LOWBAT"/>`. Duplicates on functional channels exist but never alone: rf_sec_sd_2.xml (ch0 + ch1 SMOKE_DETECTOR), rf_sc.xml / rf_sc_e_v1_7.xml / rf_sc_le_v1_6.xml / rf_sci_3.xml / rf_sec_sco.xml (ch0 + ch1 SHUTTER_CONTACT), rf_rhs.xml / rf_rhs_e_v1_7.xml / rf_rhs_le_v1_6.xml (ch0 + ch1 ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR), rf_tis.xml / rf_tis_le_v1_0.xml (ch0 + ch1 TILT_SENSOR), rf_wds_v1_0.xml / rf_wds_v1_1.xml (ch0 + ch1 WATERDETECTIONSENSOR), rf_em_8.xml (ch0 + ch1 KEY), and the one device that goes above 2: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_wds30_ot2.xml — ch0 MAINTENANCE, ch1 WEATHER count=4 (channels 1-4), and ch5 WEATHER. No device XML declares LOWBAT/LOW_BAT/LOWBAT_SENSOR only above channel 2. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler — the status-frame handler binds `byte channelIndex = 0; IChannel channel0 = device.getChannel(channelIndex);` and writes `channel0.setParameterValue("LOW_BAT", timestamp, statusFrame.isLowBat())`, notifying under that same channelIndex 0; the parameter itself is registered as BOOLEAN by de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory (createReadEventBooleanIntegerParameter("LOW_BAT")).
reachesDevice.finding: Our three-channel scan is a strict superset of what the firmware requires, so it produces no wrong answer — but the damage the reader posited does not exist, and the widening is not what makes the code correct. Channel 0 alone is sufficient on every shipped device: BidCos always declares LOWBAT on the MAINTENANCE channel (ui_flags="service", interface="internal" — rfd derives it itself), and duplicates it on the functional channel only as an additional copy fed from the same frame bit (`param="LOWBAT"` in the EVENT/INFO_LEVEL frames, e.g. rf_sec_sd_2.xml). HmIP writes LOW_BAT to channel 0 exclusively. The boundary the reader was reaching for is real but one step further out: HM-WDS30-OT2-SM (rf_wds30_ot2.xml) does declare LOWBAT on channel 5, above the {:0,:1,:2} window — and the scan would still be right there, because the same device declares it on 0 and 1-4 as well. So: our rule is true in our scope, and the reason it is true is the channel-0 MAINTENANCE invariant, not the 0/1/2 widening. The ordering worry is also moot — the extra copies are the same device bit, so 'first hit in ascending channel order' cannot pick a contradicting value. Our type guard matches too: both firmware sides declare the parameter BOOLEAN, and we only accept raw.(bool). What our code SHOULD follow is the channel-0 rule that internal/central/adapter/relevant_init.go:34-36 already states for the other device-meta parameters; the :1/:2 arms are dead weight rather than a defect, and no device in the shipped set makes them load-bearing.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong I would have found at least one device XML whose only LOWBAT declaration sits at channel index ≥ 3 after expanding `count`, or an HmIP path writing LOW_BAT to a non-zero channel. The scan was built to surface exactly that (it prints every file whose minimum LOWBAT channel exceeds 2, and it did print the ch5 declaration on rf_wds30_ot2.xml when not filtered by minimum) — it produced no such file, and the HmIP handler binds the literal 0.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Verdict upheld, boundary confirmed by re-running the census rather than accepting it, and one defect added that the prior grounding missed.

What I checked. I re-derived the census independently with an XML parser over all four directories, expanding `count` attributes, and reproduced the prior pass's numbers exactly: 176 files, minimum channel 0 in every one, one device (rf_wds30_ot2.xml, HM-WDS30-OT2-SM) reaching channel 5 and also declaring channel 0. So the {:0,:1,:2} window is a strict superset of what the firmware requires, no shipped device makes the :1/:2 arms load-bearing, and the rule is true in our scope for the reason the prior pass named — the channel-0 MAINTENANCE invariant, not the widening.

What I upgraded from inference to grounding. The prior finding asserted that the duplicate copies on functional channels are 'fed from the same frame bit' and therefore cannot contradict channel 0. That was an inference; it is now read from the source. RFDevice::UpdateDeviceFlags extracts the LOWBAT bit from the frame and routes it through SetInternalValue, which sets the device-level maintenance_flags FLAG_LOWBAT; the channel-0 read returns that same flag; and the functional-channel parameter is populated from the frame field the decoder names "LOWBAT", which BidcosFrame.h places at exactly the bit positions UpdateDeviceFlags reads. First-hit-in-ascending-order therefore cannot pick a contradicting value, and our fall-through when a channel has no value yet is safe.

What the prior grounding missed. The comment being grounded is itself wrong. availability.go:249-250 reads 'LOW_BAT (HM/BidCos) and LOWBAT (HmIP)'. The two are inverted. Every BidCos device XML spells it LOWBAT — all 176 in the census, on the MAINTENANCE channel with interface="internal" — and HmIP spells it LOW_BAT, in the frame handler, the state-parameter factory and the group definitions alike. Tier 2 agrees at 224-to-65. The code is unharmed because it tries both names, but this is precisely the class of comment the project's own rule targets: a property of a data source asserted without having been read from it. The fix is one line, and the code should follow the channel-0 rule that internal/central/adapter/relevant_init.go:34-36 already states for the other device-meta parameters.

One boundary the prior pass named loosely. LOWBAT_SENSOR does appear outside the window — ST6-SH channels 3 and 4 — but that device carries LOWBAT on channel 0 too, and lowBattery() does not look for that alias at all (only hmenum.ParameterLowBat and ParameterLowbat), so it is not a gap on this surface. It is a gap on internal/model/safety/classify.go's lowBatAliases, which does list LOWBAT_SENSOR; that is a different site and outside this rule.

reachesDevice.title: The allow-list of INTERNAL-flagged parameters that may still surface
reachesDevice.citation: HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter — the FLAGS assignment is a single if/else chain: UNREACH → 25; ERROR_CODE and service-message parameters → 1 or 9; `parameter.getName().equals("REPETITIONS") || parameter.getName().equals("OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE") || parameter.getName().startsWith("COLOR_LIST_") || parameter.getName().startsWith("ON_TIME_LIST_") || parameter.getName().startsWith("SOUNDFILE_LIST_")` → setFlags(2); everything else → setFlags(1). DeviceUtil#fillLegacyParameter, the only later mutator, sets TAB_ORDER, UNIT and CONTROL only — never FLAGS. CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is a configuration parameter (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.ConfigurationParameterIdentifier#CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE, built by GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory#createEnumeration) and matches no branch above, so it takes the else → FLAGS=1. BidCos: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/ declares DIRECTION 12 times, every one of them `<parameter id="DIRECTION" operations="read,event" ui_flags="internal">` (e.g. rf_d.xml:274, rf_winmatic.xml:198, rf_dim_1l_644.xml:360); rfd emits FLAGS from HSSParameter.cpp:210 `(*val)["FLAGS"]=flags;`. ON_TIME_LIST_*, REPETITIONS and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE do not appear in rftypes/ or hs485types/ at all — they are HmIP-only. Tier 2 corroboration, ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json (FLAGS as actually declared at runtime): CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE FLAGS=1 TYPE=ENUM in 105 descriptors (e.g. HmIP-STV.json, VCU3432945:1 MASTER); DIRECTION FLAGS=3 TYPE=ENUM in 124 (e.g. HMW-LC-Bl1-DR.json, VCU0000011:3 VALUES); REPETITIONS FLAGS=2 in 5 (HmIP-WRCD.json, VCU4243444:3 VALUES); ON_TIME_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 in 3 (HmIP-MP3P.json, VCU1543608:6 VALUES); plus COLOR_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 (3), SOUNDFILE_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 (1), OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE FLAGS=2 (4).
reachesDevice.ourValue: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE listed as an INTERNAL-flagged parameter needing an exemption to surface
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE carries FLAGS=1 (VISIBLE, no INTERNAL bit) — the firmware never flags it internal, on either transport
reachesDevice.finding: Three of the four entries are grounded; the fourth is not, and it is precisely the one the comment presents as the Go-side addition. DIRECTION, REPETITIONS and ON_TIME_LIST_1 do carry the INTERNAL bit (DIRECTION: ui_flags="internal" in all 12 BidCos declarations, FLAGS=3 = VISIBLE|INTERNAL at runtime; REPETITIONS and ON_TIME_LIST_* : the HmIP legacy surface sets FLAGS=2 by name-match), so exempting them is doing real work. CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE does not: the HmIP FLAGS chain has no branch for it and the else yields FLAGS=1, and 105 real descriptors agree. The entry is therefore inert — the exemption at internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:401 and reason.go:206 can never fire for it, because the guard those sites sit behind only asks about INTERNAL-flagged parameters. That is harmless in behaviour but wrong as documentation: the comment asserts a property of the descriptor ('their Flags field includes FLAG.INTERNAL') that the firmware contradicts for that name, and the stated reason for the entry ('the operation-mode gating pipeline reads it directly') is a claim about our pipeline, not about the CCU. Second, smaller result: the firmware's INTERNAL-by-name set is wider than our allow-list — OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE, COLOR_LIST_* and SOUNDFILE_LIST_* are also FLAGS=2. That is a deliberate difference in the safe direction (an allow-list is what we want visible), not a gap, but it means 'ported verbatim from the Python sibling's field map' is not the same set the firmware flags, and the two should not be conflated.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE claim been true I would have found either a name-match for it in the DeviceUtil FLAGS chain (the chain is exhaustive — every parameter takes exactly one branch, so an INTERNAL classification could not come from anywhere else in that method), a later FLAGS mutation in fillLegacyParameter, or descriptors carrying FLAGS 2/3/6 for it. The same scan that returned FLAGS=1 for CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE returned FLAGS=2 for REPETITIONS/ON_TIME_LIST_1 and FLAGS=3 for DIRECTION in the same pass, so the check demonstrably distinguishes the two outcomes.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Contradiction upheld, verified independently on both tiers rather than accepted.

What I checked. I opened the FLAGS chain and transcribed it rather than trusting the summary — it is a single if/else with four arms, and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE matches none of them, so it lands on the else and takes FLAGS=1. I then closed the escape the prior pass asserted without showing: fillLegacyParameter really does touch only TabOrder, Unit and Control, and the properties file it reads from carries no FLAGS key anywhere in its 1092 lines and no entry for this parameter at all, so nothing downstream can set the bit. I confirmed the parameter is absent from every BidCos device XML in both trees, and I re-ran the descriptor census myself: 105 real descriptors report FLAGS=1 for it. The three genuine entries hold up: DIRECTION carries ui_flags="internal" in all 31 BidCos declarations and comes back FLAGS=3 at runtime, and REPETITIONS / ON_TIME_LIST_1 are set to 2 by the name-match arm, so exempting those three is doing real work.

One count corrected. The prior finding said DIRECTION appears 12 times in rftypes; it appears 31 times across src/devicetypes/rftypes and firmware/rftypes together. All 31 carry ui_flags="internal", so the conclusion is unchanged, but the number should not be repeated as given.

Why this is documentation and not behaviour. I read both consumers. Each tests Flags.IsInternal() before consulting the map — reason.go:205-209 and operation_mode.go:397-401 — so a FLAGS=1 parameter never reaches the allow-list and the entry can never fire. The cost is entirely in what the comment claims: it asserts a property of the descriptor ('their Flags field includes FLAG.INTERNAL') that the firmware contradicts for that one name, and it justifies the entry with a claim about our own pipeline ('the operation-mode gating pipeline reads it directly') rather than about the CCU. The prior finding's second result also stands and is worth keeping: the firmware's INTERNAL-by-name set is wider than our allow-list — OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE, COLOR_LIST_* and SOUNDFILE_LIST_* are FLAGS=2 as well — so the comment's provenance line, that this set was ported verbatim from the Python sibling's field map, describes a different set from the one the firmware flags. Leaving them out is the safe direction for an allow-list; conflating the two sets is not.

reachesDevice.title: The default pairing window and the CCU's clamp are stated as facts with no source
reachesDevice.site: internal/model/hub/install_mode.go:214 (DefaultInstallModeDuration = 60s), :199-208 (Press); internal/model/hub/writers.go:42-44 (InstallModeWriter contract); default applied at internal/north/rest/handlers/system_hub.go:325
reachesDevice.citation: Default, BidCos-RF: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:598-634 (XmlRpcMethodSetInstallMode) — `if(params.size()>=2)time=params[1]; else time=60;` at :608-609, with the method's own doc comment at :594-595 verbatim: "Der Parameter \"seconds\" ist optional und gibt die Zeit in Sekunden an, die der Install-Mode aktiv bleiben soll. \"seconds\" darf maximal 600 sein. Defaultwert ist 60." Default, HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#setInstallMode and #setInstallModeWithWhitelist — both open `int internalTime = 60; if (time != null) { internalTime = time; }` before calling AccessPointUtil#setInclusionMode. Operator surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_add_device.cgi:903 `xmlrpc $RFD_URL setInstallMode [list bool $activate]` — the WebUI's BidCos teach-in passes NO seconds argument and so runs on the firmware default; the HmIP teach-in dialog in the same file (:918-940, hmip_install_mode_start) hard-codes `installTime = 60` and posts it as `'time' : installTime`. Clamp, BidCos-RF: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:580-597 and :599-616 (both SetInstallMode overloads) `if (seconds > INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME) seconds = INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME;` with ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:562 `enum{INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME=600};`; there is no lower bound — `if (seconds)` then arms the timer, and the else branch (`seconds == 0`) sets install_mode = INSTALL_OFF. Clamp, HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.AccessPointUtil#setInclusionMode passes the value straight through — `long timeoutTimestamp = System.currentTimeMillis() + (long)time.intValue() * 1000L; long timerID = vertx.setTimer((long)time.intValue() * 1000L, new InclusionTimeoutHandler(accessPoint, vertx));` — with no bound check anywhere on the path.
reachesDevice.ourValue: "duration is clamped by the CCU (typically 60 s min, 3600 s max); the writer does not clamp itself" (writers.go:43)
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF: no minimum at all (0 means OFF), maximum 600 s (RFManager.h:562 INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME=600). HmIP: no minimum and no maximum — the value is used verbatim as the inclusion timer.
reachesDevice.finding: Split verdict, and the two halves point in opposite directions. The 60-second default is confirmed three times over and is genuinely a property of the pairing behaviour rather than of any one surface: the BidCos daemon substitutes 60 when the caller omits `seconds`, the HmIP legacy handler substitutes 60 in both its setInstallMode entry points, and the CCU's own teach-in dialog relies on the first and hard-codes the second. DefaultInstallModeDuration = 60s at install_mode.go:214 is right, and so is the comment's framing of it. The clamp claim at writers.go:43 is wrong on both bounds and on both transports, and it is the load-bearing half — it is the stated reason the writer does not validate. There is no 60 s minimum anywhere; on BidCos-RF a `seconds` of 0 does not become 60, it turns install mode OFF, and the maximum is 600 s, a factor of six below the 3600 s the comment asserts. On HmIP nothing clamps at all: a caller-supplied 3600 really does open a one-hour pairing window, while the same request against BidCos-RF silently becomes ten minutes. So the operator-visible behaviour our comment describes as uniform is in fact transport-dependent and unbounded on one of the two. What our code should follow is the firmware's own ceiling per transport, not a single invented pair of bounds: if the daemon wants to keep not clamping, the contract should say the CCU truncates to 600 s on BidCos-RF and does not bound HmIP at all — and a duration above 600 s should not be reported back to the operator as if it had been honoured. Our lower guard (duration <= 0 → ErrInstallModeInvalidDuration, install_mode.go:225) is a divergence from the firmware's 0-means-off, but a safe one.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the comment been right I would have found a lower-bound raise (a `if (seconds < 60) seconds = 60`-shaped line, or a 60 substituted for a non-null small value) and a 3600 ceiling constant on at least one of the two paths. I read both SetInstallMode overloads in RFManager.cpp end to end and the whole AccessPointUtil inclusion path, and grepped INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME across ../OpenCCU-Base/src — it resolves to exactly one enum, 600, referenced only by the two clamp sites. The check plainly distinguishes: the same reading produced a confirmed 60 for the default in the very same functions where it produced a refuted 3600/60-min for the clamp.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Contradiction upheld on the clamp, and extended: the half the prior pass reported as confirmed is also wrong at our surface. The severity is higher than recorded.

The clamp half — upheld, verified verbatim. I read all four sites. There is no 60 s minimum anywhere: on BidCos-RF a `seconds` of 0 does not become 60, it takes the else branch and turns install mode OFF; the only bound is the 600 s ceiling in both RFManager::SetInstallMode overloads, a factor of six below the 3600 s our contract asserts. On HmIP nothing clamps at all — AccessPointUtil multiplies the value by 1000 and hands it to the timer. So the same requested 3600 opens a one-hour window on HmIP and is silently truncated to ten minutes on BidCos-RF, while writers.go:43 describes one uniform pair of bounds. That comment is the stated reason the writer does not validate, which is what makes it load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

The default half — the prior pass called this 'confirmed three times over' and 'genuinely a property of the pairing behaviour rather than of any one surface'. That framing is the wrong-surface failure this audit exists to catch, and I found the surface it missed. Our HmIP-RF path does not call the legacy XML-RPC setInstallMode the prior grounding cites. It calls JSON-RPC Interface.setInstallModeHMIP, and that method's Tcl implementation defaults `time` to 30, not 60, then forwards an explicit time onward so HMIPServer's 60 is unreachable from here. Three surfaces, two defaults. The default is a property of the surface, exactly as the comment denies.

What is still safe, and what is not. The constant's value survives, because no firmware default is ever exercised from this daemon: Press() at install_mode.go:202 passes 60 explicitly, the REST handler substitutes hub.DefaultInstallModeDuration for a zero at system_hub.go:323-326, and ccu_extended.go always puts a `time` on the wire. So DefaultInstallModeDuration = 60s is a defensible choice of our own; its justification is not. What is not safe is the missing ceiling: validateInstallModeRequest (system_hub.go:362-376) rejects only Seconds < 0, so an operator asking for 3600 on BidCos-RF is told the request succeeded and gets 600. If the daemon keeps not clamping, the contract should say the CCU truncates to 600 s on BidCos-RF and does not bound HmIP at all, and a duration above 600 s should not be reported back as honoured. Our own lower guard — duration <= 0 -> ErrInstallModeInvalidDuration at install_mode.go:225 — diverges from the firmware's 0-means-off, but in the safe direction; I would keep it.

reachesDevice.title: The 70-name IGNORED_PARAMETERS deny list and its 13 wildcard patterns rest on the Python port alone
reachesDevice.ourValue: INHIBIT, SPEED, BOOST_TIME, BOOST_STATE, ADAPTION_DRIVE, RELOCK_DELAY, SELF_CALIBRATION, USER_PROGRAM, WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER, INSTALL_TEST all suppressed unconditionally; plus every VALUES parameter ending in _STATUS/_RESULT/_REPORTING/_SUBMIT/_OVERFLOW/_OVERRUN or starting with HANDLE_/IDENTIFY_/ADJUSTING_/ERR_TTM_/PARTY_START_/PARTY_STOP_/STATUS_FLAG_
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: INSTALL_TEST is the only one the firmware declares internal (ui_flags="internal"; FLAGS 2 or 3 on all 829 descriptor occurrences). The other nine are declared FLAGS=1 (VISIBLE set, INTERNAL clear, SERVICE clear); INHIBIT is operations="read,write,event" on 268 channels; LED_STATUS, caught by the _STATUS$ suffix rule, is operations="read,write,event" on 16 channels of HM-OU-LED16 with VALUE_LIST [OFF,RED,GREEN,ORANGE]
