WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER appears only in MASTER, never in VALUES: (3,1,ENUM)x2.
reachesDevice.finding: Contradicted for nine of the ten names the reader asked about, and for two of the thirteen wildcard prefixes/suffixes. Only INSTALL_TEST matches the justification written next to it — it is the sole entry the firmware declares ui_flags="internal", and its descriptor FLAGS carry the INTERNAL bit on all 829 occurrences. The other nine carry FLAGS=1: VISIBLE set, INTERNAL and SERVICE clear, i.e. exactly the shape the CCU's own visible-parameter test (../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParamset.cpp:70, `(param->GetFlags() & (FLG_INTERNAL|FLG_VISIBLE))==FLG_VISIBLE`) accepts. They would NOT have been filtered anyway. Five of them (INHIBIT, BOOST_STATE, BOOST_TIME, RELOCK_DELAY, SELF_CALIBRATION) plus USER_PROGRAM carry operator labels in the CCU's own parameter string table. INHIBIT is read+write+event on 268 channels — a live device write path our list removes fleet-wide. The widest damage is in the wildcards, as the bundle predicted: the `_STATUS$` suffix suppresses LED_STATUS, a read/write/event ENUM on all 16 channels of HM-OU-LED16 with a four-value list and its own string-table entries, for which the OpenCCU distribution ships a dedicated WebUI control; the `HANDLE_` prefix suppresses HANDLE_LOCK and HANDLE_LED_MODE (both OPERATIONS=7, FLAGS=1, both labelled under ACTOR_WINDOW in the string table). Of the 82 distinct wildcard-matched VALUES parameters in the descriptor corpus, 23 are writable (OPERATIONS bit 2 set): LED_STATUS, HANDLE_LOCK, HANDLE_LED_MODE, IDENTIFY_DURATION, IDENTIFY_TARGET_LEVEL, PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT and the eight PARTY_START_*/PARTY_STOP_* pairs. Separately: WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER never occurs in a VALUES paramset in the corpus (MASTER only), so that entry appears inert on the surface the list documents itself as governing. Not audited here: the remaining ~60 names on the list.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the list's stated basis been right, each name would carry ui_flags="internal" or "service" in src/devicetypes and its descriptor FLAGS would set bit 2 (INTERNAL) or bit 3 (SERVICE), and none would appear in the CCU's operator string table. The check demonstrably produces that other answer: INSTALL_TEST came out with ui_flags="internal", FLAGS 2/3, and no string-table label, on the same measurement that put the other nine at FLAGS=1 with labels.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Narrowed hard. Five bites. (1) The headline damage claim is false against our own code: LED_STATUS on HM-OU-LED16 is explicitly carved out at internal/store/visibility/rules.go:341, inside `unIgnoreParametersByDevice` (declared :316), consumed by `deviceUnIgnoresByPrefix` (decider.go:309-320) in the step-0 early exit at decider.go:237 — one line above the :243 the finding cites — so it returns not-ignored before the `_STATUS$` wildcard is ever evaluated. Pinned by internal/store/visibility/rules_test.go:184 `{"HM-OU-LED16", hmenum.ParameterLEDStatus, true}`. The surviving remnant is HM-OU-X VCU0000159:1, one channel, not sixteen. (2) 'Suppressed unconditionally' is false for all ten names: step 0 and the required-parameter whitelist (`custom.DefaultRegistry().RequiredParameters()`, wired at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:105) both bypass the list, and the effect is a forced DataPointUsageIgnored mark, not DP removal — internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline_visibility_test.go:82-88 asserts the INHIBIT DP IS created ('every wire parameter becomes a DP under the new architecture'). So 'a live device write path our list removes fleet-wide' is not established. (3) Wrong surface on the load-bearing inference: HSSParamset.cpp:70 is not a visible-parameter test, it is a TAB_ORDER assignment (`param->SetTabOrder(tab_order++)`) — every parameter is inserted into `params` regardless, and GetDescription emits every one with no FLAGS gate, so 'they would NOT have been filtered anyway' rests on a line that filters nothing. FLAGS answers what the descriptor declares; our list governs a northbound entity surface, whose CCU counterpart is template-driven per channel type (www/rega/esp/controls/*.fn), and INHIBIT appears nowhere in the whole WebUI/ReGa tree except stringtable_de.txt. (4) Each verbatim quote carries contrary evidence the finding did not address: control="NONE" on INHIBIT, SPEED, RELOCK_DELAY and LED_STATUS, where the operator-facing siblings in the same paramsets carry a real control (rf_s.xml:219 STATE control="SWITCH.STATE"; rf_ou_led16_le_v1_0.xml:163 PRESS_SHORT control="BTN_SHORT_ONLY.SHORT"). CONTROL is emitted on the wire at HSSParameter.cpp:212. (5) Tier inflation: six of the ten names — BOOST_TIME, BOOST_STATE, ADAPTION_DRIVE, SELF_CALIBRATION, USER_PROGRAM, WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER — have ZERO declarations in any of the 142 shipped device XMLs; their FLAGS=1 is Tier 2 only, plus Tier 1 on the HmIP side by construction (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter assigns 1 to everything outside its UNREACH / ERROR_CODE / service-message / REPETITIONS+OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE+COLOR_LIST_*/ON_TIME_LIST_*/SOUNDFILE_LIST_* branches), which the finding did not cite. It reads as if all nine were BidCos Tier 1. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is real: INSTALL_TEST is the one entry whose written justification is Tier-1 grounded (46/46 ui_flags="internal"), and the `HANDLE_` prefix does over-reach — HANDLE_LOCK and HANDLE_LED_MODE, OPERATIONS=7 FLAGS=1, one channel each on HM-ReSC-Win-PCB-xx, labelled at stringtable_de.txt:95-99, with no un-ignore entry. That is the boundary: a one-device over-reach, not a fleet-wide one. Counts corrected: 67 names not 70, 14 writable wildcard-matched parameters not 23 (the finding's own list enumerates exactly 14). Separately true and worth keeping: the doc comment at rules.go:198-200 ('parameter names for which no data points are created') is refuted by our own test at device_pipeline_visibility_test.go:86.

reachesDevice.title: HmIP-FWI CODE_ID MAX widened from 21 to 31 on the claim that CODE_ID is a 5-bit field with 31 = idle
reachesDevice.ourValue: MAX=31, justified as "5-bit field, 31 = no active code"; the CCU's MAX=21 asserted to be wrong
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: HmIP-FWI CODE_ID: MIN=1, MAX=21, DEFAULT=1 (deliberate, channel-type-specific); CODE_ID is decoded as valueData[0] & 0x1F; idle is CODE_STATE=0 (CodeState.IDLE), not CODE_ID=31; CODE_ID=21 = bell button
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createCodeId — registered three times: default key CODE_ID → createCodeId(0, 30); key (CODE_ID, "fwi") → createCodeId(1, 21); key (CODE_ID, "wkp") → createReadOnlyCodeId(1, 8, -1.0). createCodeId builds StateParameter("CODE_ID", LogicalType.INTEGER, PhysicalType.INTEGER, read|write|event, null, default=minvalue, min=minvalue, max=maxvalue, …) — no bit-width field. · HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler, CODE_STATUS case: CODE_STATE is decoded as (valueData[0] & 0xFF) >> 5 and CODE_ID as valueData[0] & 0x1F. · HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.CodeState — IDLE is the first constant (ordinal 0), followed by KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED. · ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/maintenanceFWI.fn:80-91 — `if (codeState == 0) {curState = "${codeIdle}";}` and, only under `codeState == 1`, `if ((objCodeID.Value() == 21) || (objCodeID.Value() == "21")) { curState = "${lblBellButton}"; }`. Tier 2 is silent: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-FWI.json carries the device/channel descriptions only, and ../pydevccu/paramsets_db.json contains no CODE_ID entry at all.
reachesDevice.finding:
Both premises of the patch comment fail, in opposite ways.

(1) "the CCU declares MAX=21 … [wrongly]" is contradicted. 21 is not a stale or generic bound the CCU got wrong: the firmware registers CODE_ID three times under distinct channel-type keys, and the HmIP-FWI variant is deliberately (1, 21) — narrower than the generic (0, 30) and wider than the keypad (1, 8). The WebUI then gives 21 a name: on the FWI maintenance control, CODE_ID == 21 renders as the bell button, i.e. 1..20 are the twenty finger codes and 21 is the doorbell. So MAX=21 is the firmware's considered answer for exactly this device.

(2) "5-bit field" is confirmed — CODE_ID is the low five bits of the CODE_STATUS byte (`valueData[0] & 0x1F`), CODE_STATE the top three (`>> 5`) — so the wire can indeed carry 0..31 and a 31 observation is physically possible. But nothing in the firmware names 31 as an idle/no-active-code sentinel; that half of the comment is Tier-1 silent. The firmware's idle indicator is a different parameter: CODE_STATE = 0 = CodeState.IDLE, and the WebUI reads CODE_ID *only* when CODE_STATE == 1 (KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED), ignoring it in every other state.

Consequence for our code: the patch widens a bound the firmware set on purpose, and does so with a sentinel meaning the firmware does not assign. CODE_ID carries read|write|event on the fwi variant, so the widened MAX also admits writes of 22..31 that the declared range rejects. The reported symptom ("the entity never returned to 31 after a recognized code") is better served by following CODE_STATE — which is what the CCU's own operator surface does — than by re-interpreting an out-of-range CODE_ID. If the raw 31 must be kept, the honest framing is "the wire field is 5 bits wide, so values above the declared MAX are observable", not "31 means idle".
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, createCodeId for the "fwi" key would have carried max=31 (or the generic 0..30 registration would have applied to FWI with no fwi-specific override), and either the CODE_STATUS decode or the WebUI control would special-case 31 the way it special-cases 21. Instead the fwi override exists and pins 21, and the only value the WebUI singles out is 21. The check discriminates: the same file proves the mechanism can express per-device bounds (fwi 1..21 vs wkp 1..8 vs generic 0..30), so an idle sentinel or a wider FWI bound would have been visible in the same place I looked.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld, and the case is stronger than the first pass made it, but one link in its stated chain was unread and I close it differently.

Premise 1 — "the CCU declares MAX=21 [wrongly]" — is contradicted. 21 is the firmware's considered answer: the generic registration is (0,30), the keypad one is (1,8), and only the fwi-keyed one is (1,21). The WebUI then gives 21 a meaning on exactly our surface: the FWI maintenance control reads MAINTENANCE.CODE_ID, lists twenty CODE_USED_01..20 slots, and renders CODE_ID == 21 as the bell button. Twenty finger codes plus the doorbell is 21.

Premise 2 — "5-bit field, 31 = no active code" — splits. The bit layout is confirmed verbatim, and I added the leg that makes the observation credible: the event path applies no range check, so a raw 31 is deliverable and the reported symptom is physically consistent. But nothing in the firmware assigns 31 any meaning. The firmware's idle indicator is a different parameter — CODE_STATE = 0 = CodeState.IDLE — and the CCU's own operator surface reads CODE_ID only while CODE_STATE == 1, ignoring it in all seven other states. "31 = no active code" is a convention supplied by us, sitting behind a firmware citation. Under the project's own rule that half of the comment is not confirmable — it is Tier-1 silent, and the honest framing is "the wire field is 5 bits wide, so values above the declared MAX are observable".

Correction to the first pass's reasoning (not its verdict): it asserted that the (CODE_ID, "fwi") registration is the one HmIP-FWI receives. The second element of ParameterMapKey is a parameterSubtypeID, not a channel or device type, and it is assigned from a `subtype` attribute in a channel-type XML that is not readable here. That mapping was presented as read; it was not. It survives by elimination — (1,21) is the only registration in the whole firmware that can produce MAX=21, and our own patch records observing MAX=21 — plus the FWI-specific WebUI evidence above. Conclusion unchanged, chain repaired.

Consequence for our code: the patch widens a deliberate bound on a parameter that carries WRITE on this variant (ops = 7), so it also admits writes of 22..31 that the CCU's declared range rejects — that half is an inference about our validation path, not a firmware measurement. Following CODE_STATE, which is what the CCU's own surface does, addresses the reported symptom without re-interpreting an out-of-range CODE_ID.

reachesDevice.title: The BIN-RPC type tags and message types carry no source at all
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:55-62 (STREAM_TAG_INTEGER=0x001, BOOLEAN=0x002, STRING=0x003, DOUBLE=0x004, DATETIME=0x005, BINARY=0x006, ARRAY=0x100, STRUCT=0x101); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:35 (BINARY_SIGNATURE[]="Bin"), :96-100 (header = sig + 1 type byte + ntohl u32 length, body at sig+5), :356-362 (response appends type byte 1), :405-411 (fault appends type byte 0xff); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:334-361 (request appends type byte 0), :475-479 (client reads the type byte, 0xff = fault)
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: marker 'Bin'; msgType request=0, response=1, fault=0xff; tags 0x001 int / 0x002 bool / 0x003 string / 0x004 double / 0x005 datetime / 0x006 binary / 0x100 array / 0x101 struct; big-endian throughout
reachesDevice.ourValue: marker {'B','i','n'}; msgTypeRequest=0x00, msgTypeResponse=0x01, msgTypeFault=0xFF; typeInt=0x01, typeBool=0x02, typeString=0x03, typeDouble=0x04, typeArray=0x100, typeStruct=0x101
reachesDevice.finding: Every constant in wire.go matches the CCU's own BIN-RPC codec exactly, and so do the payload shapes our encoder writes: int is a 4-byte big-endian word (XmlRpcValue.cpp:539-547), bool is a single 0/1 byte (:461-468), string is a u32 length followed by the raw bytes with no terminator (:709-719), double is mantissa then exponent as two big-endian int32 (:605-616, matching our value = mantissa * 2^exp / 2^30). The request framing our WriteRequest builds is the firmware's, verbatim: 8-byte header, then a length-only method name with no type tag, then a u32 parameter count, then each parameter as a self-tagged value — note the top-level parameter list carries no 0x100 array tag, which is what our writeParamArray also does (XmlRpcClient.cpp:335-352, and the server's matching parseRequest at XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:259-266 reads stringFromStream then arrayFromStream). Two narrowings worth recording rather than fixing blind: the firmware codec also accepts DATETIME (0x005) and BINARY (0x006), which our readValue rejects with "unknown value type tag", and the firmware's client treats any header byte other than 0xff as a non-fault rather than requiring exactly 0x01. Neither is wrong for the CUxD path we drive, but wire.go states the tag set as if it were complete, and it is a strict subset. CUxD itself is a closed add-on present in neither reference tree, so this grounds the framing our client speaks, not CUxD-specific behaviour.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had a tag been wrong, the firmware's constant block would have shown a different number against the same name — the check reads eight named constants and compares each to ours, so a single mismatched value (e.g. bool at 0x03) would have surfaced as a named disagreement rather than the eight-for-eight agreement observed. The bundle correctly notes the existing round-trip test cannot produce that result, since it encodes and decodes with the same constants; reading the firmware's own definitions is the only check that can.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: I re-read every cited line. All eight constants, the 8-byte header, the request framing (tagless method name, u32 parameter count, no top-level 0x100 array tag) and all four payload shapes are exactly as claimed; the double formula matches in both directions (firmware frexp + int() truncation vs our math.Trunc; firmware ldexp(mant/2^30, exp) vs our 2^exp*mant/2^30). I demote from confirmed to narrowed for three reasons the grounding either understated or missed. (1) The tag set in wire.go is a strict subset — DATETIME 0x005 and BINARY 0x006 are refused by readValue with "unknown value type tag"; the grounding names this but still reports the rule confirmed. (2) Missed: our ReadRequest rejects any header type byte other than 0x00, while XmlRpcServerConnection never inspects that byte on the read path at all — it branches on the "Bin" signature alone (:96-101) — so our server is strictly stricter than the CCU's, in the same way our client is stricter than XmlRpcClient's 0xff-or-not fault test. (3) Scope: our BIN-RPC peer is CUxD, a closed add-on present in neither reference tree. What is grounded is that our codec matches the CCU's own BIN-RPC codec, which is strong evidence for the protocol family and no evidence at all about CUxD-specific behaviour. Separately verified as a scope note: rfd and hs485d never construct a TypeDateTime or TypeBase64 value (0 hits), so the two unsupported tags are a codec capability, not something the CCU emits.

reachesDevice.title: HSColor's 0..1 wire range and x100 exposure are asserted in a comment, not read from the SATURATION descriptor
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLevel and #createHue (SATURATION registered via createLevel, HUE via createHue in #initializeStateParameterList); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.StateParameter (constructor argument order: name, logicalType, physicalType, ioOperations, typeConverter, defaultValue, minValue, maxValue, ...); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.AbstractParameterFactory#PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_MIN / #PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_MAX / #PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_OLD_VALUE / #PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_DON_T_CARE; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (publishes MIN/MAX verbatim from the parameter). Tier 2 corroboration of scope: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml and hs485types/*.xml declare neither HUE nor SATURATION on any device (0 files each), so both parameters are HmIP-only.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: SATURATION: LogicalType.FLOAT, DEFAULT 0.0, MIN 0.0, MAX 1.01 (physical conversion DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0)). HUE: LogicalType.INTEGER, DEFAULT 0, MIN 0, MAX 361, with 0..359 the real hue range, 360 = OLD_VALUE and 361 = DON'T_CARE.
reachesDevice.ourValue: SATURATION clamped to [0.0, 1.0] on read (hscolor.go:205-211) and written as sat/100.0 from a [0,100] input (hscolor.go:241). HUE folded ((v%360)+360)%360 on both read (hscolor.go:255) and write (hscolor.go:234).
reachesDevice.finding: Both halves of the comment are off, and the HUE half mis-decodes real device values. SATURATION's declared MAX is 1.01, not 1.0 — a one-ulp-class difference in exactly the sense the brief asks about, so our read clamp truncates the top of the declared range. HUE's declared MAX is 361, and the two values above 359 are named constants, not slack: 360 is OLD_VALUE and 361 is DON'T_CARE. Our modulo maps them to hue 0 and hue 1, so a light reporting "don't care" (the value the config-side POWERUP_ON_HUE and SHORT_ON_HUE parameters use to mean "leave hue alone") is published as a real red hue with nothing anywhere indicating a sentinel was swallowed. The write path is unaffected in practice: we send hue in [0,359] and saturation in [0,1], both inside the declared bounds, so no out-of-range value reaches a device. The bundle's worry about a device declaring SATURATION as 0..100 or 0..255 does not arise — the corpus is uniform because these parameters exist only on the HmIP side and are built from one factory method. The structural criticism stands regardless: Subscribe already holds the DP at hscolor.go:127 and never reads Descriptor.Min/Max, so the code cannot notice any of this. The right fix is to consult the descriptor and treat HUE values above the declared real maximum as sentinels rather than folding them.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, createHue would have carried maxValue 359 and createLevel maxValue 1.0, and AbstractParameterFactory would not have named 360 and 361 at all. The check reads the declared MIN/MAX triple straight out of the factory call and compares it to our clamp bounds, so agreement and disagreement produce visibly different results; here it produced 1.01 vs 1.0 and 361 vs 359, plus two named sentinel constants our code has no branch for.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: Half of this grounding holds and half is a wrong-surface transfer. Upheld: the declared ranges contradict our comment. createLevel gives SATURATION maxValue 1.01, not 1.0, and createHue gives HUE maxValue 361, not 359; both are published verbatim over the legacy XML-RPC surface (addDesriptionOfParameter copies min/max off the parameter, and fillLegacyParameter can only set TabOrder/Unit/Control, so nothing downstream rewrites them). The structural criticism is also upheld: hscolor.go contains no reference to Descriptor at all. Demoted: the claim that 360/361 are live sentinels on the state HUE, so that our modulo publishes a "don't care" as a red hue, is not grounded. PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_OLD_VALUE and _DON_T_CARE are declared and then used nowhere in HMIPServer or HMServer; the 361 default appears only on POWERUP_ON_HUE (MASTER) and SHORT_ON_HUE / LONG_ON_HUE (LINK), built by a different factory method, while the state HUE's declared default is 0. Reading the config-paramset sentinel meaning onto the VALUES parameter because both stop at 361 is exactly the convention this audit exists to catch, and it is the half a reader would later cite as a device fact. Two smaller corrections: the grounding's line numbers are wrong (read fold is :189 not :255, write fold :230 not :234, Subscribe :124 not :127), and Tier 2 is silent in both directions — no HUE or SATURATION appears in the shipped device XMLs or in the pydevccu descriptor corpus, so nothing outside the HmIP server says what a real device declares.

reachesDevice.title: MASTER OPERATIONS=0 is rewritten to READ|WRITE on a ported claim about CCU firmware behaviour
reachesDevice.ourValue: OPERATIONS=0 on MASTER -> 3 (READ|WRITE)
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: 3 (OP_READ|OP_WRITE) is the firmware's own default for a parameter that declares no operations attribute; the firmware never emits 0 in a paramset description
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:31 `operations=(OP_READ|OP_WRITE);` (constructor default) and :55-61 `temp=node.getAttribute("operations"); if(temp){ operations=OP_NONE; if(strstr(temp,"read"))operations|=OP_READ; ... }` — the attribute is the ONLY thing that can clear it. Bit values: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:53-59 `OP_NONE=0, OP_READ=1, OP_WRITE=2, OP_EVENT=4, OP_DETERMINE=8`. Sole emitter of the field: HSSParameter.cpp:209 `(*val)["OPERATIONS"]=operations;`. Visibility gate on the description: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParamset.cpp:207 `if(!param->IsVisible())continue;` with HSSParameter.h:93 `inline bool IsVisible(){return !hidden;}`. HmIP side: OPERATIONS is written verbatim from the parameter's IOOperations — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (`setOperations(parameter.getIoOperations().getValue())`); the class default is READ=1 and IOOperations#toString maps 0 to "undefined" — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations. Tier 3 witness for where our rule came from: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/__init__.py:144-146 (comment "required to fix hm master paramset operation values", no source).
reachesDevice.finding: The SUBSTITUTE VALUE IS EXACTLY RIGHT: 3 is the firmware's own default, not a guess — HSSParameter's constructor initialises operations to OP_READ|OP_WRITE, and only an explicit `operations=` attribute can lower it. But the PREMISE ("some CCU firmwares return OPERATIONS=0 for MASTER parameters") is not reproduced anywhere in Tier 1. Where the boundary runs: (a) in the shipped device XMLs, `operations="none"` (the only spelling that yields 0) occurs 28 times, ALL in LINK paramsets on wired devices (hmw_lc_dim1l_dr, hmw_lc_bl1_dr[_V3_02], hmw_lc_sw2_dr[_V3_02], hmw_io_4_fm[_V3_02]), ZERO in MASTER; (b) every one of those 28 also carries `hidden="true"`, and GetDefinition skips non-visible parameters — so getParamsetDescription cannot emit OPERATIONS=0 at all on BidCos-RF/Wired; (c) on HmIP no IOOperations is ever constructed with 0. What our rule actually fires on is a DESCRIPTOR that dropped the default: pydevccu records OPERATIONS=0 for e.g. HMW-LC-Bl1-DR MASTER INPUT_TYPE/INPUT_LOCKED/LONG_PRESS_TIME and HM-LC-Bl1-FM MASTER AES_ACTIVE — and each of those parameters carries NO operations attribute in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes (hs485types/hmw_lc_bl1_dr.xml:144,154; rftypes AES_ACTIVE declarations), i.e. a real CCU reports 3 for them (210 of 376 pydevccu device files carry MASTER OPERATIONS=0; MASTER histogram over that corpus: 0x2942, 1x495, 3x69214). So our code should follow Tier 1 (3), which it does; the rewrite is correct but is a corpus repair, not a firmware workaround, and it would be WRONG if a MASTER parameter ever genuinely declared `operations="none"`. Consequence side: rfd/hs485d does not fault a write to a non-writable parameter — HSSParamset::Put silently `continue`s (HSSParamset.cpp:190), and the HmIP legacy surface enforces nothing at all, so a wrongly-offered MASTER write is dropped, not rejected. Sibling claim at :1995 ("no MASTER parameter carries EVENT") is CONFIRMED at Tier 1: zero MASTER parameters in any of the 148 rftypes/hs485types XMLs declare an operations string containing `event`, and neither firmware default grants EVENT.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our value been wrong I would have found the constructor initialising `operations` to OP_READ (1) or OP_NONE, or a getParamsetDescription path that emits 0 for a visible MASTER parameter. The constructor reads OP_READ|OP_WRITE, and the 28 zero-valued parameters are all LINK and all filtered out by IsVisible() before the description is built — a different result in both directions.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD as narrowed, with two corrections and one scope gap the prior pass missed.

What I re-checked and confirm verbatim: the constructor default (HSSParameter.cpp:30), the attribute branch as the only path to a lower value (:55-61), the single emitter (:209), the bit values (HSSParameter.h:53-59), and the visibility gate in GetDefinition (HSSParamset.cpp:210). I additionally grepped all of src/rfd, src/hs485d and src/libhsscomm for any other assignment to `operations` and found exactly two — lines 30 and 57 of HSSParameter.cpp — so no rfd/hs485d code path can inject 0 outside the XML attribute. Same for HmIP: every `new IOOperations(...)` call site in the HMIPServer channelspecification factories passes RW, READ, or a local `ops` byte initialised from READ/WRITE/EVENT; none passes 0. The substitute value 3 is therefore the firmware's own default, not a convention.

CORRECTION 1 — the corpus scan was undercounted. The prior pass reported 28 occurrences of `operations="none"` in 4 device families. That number comes from a grep that silently skipped four latin-1-encoded XMLs as binary. Re-scanned in Python with explicit latin-1 decoding: 44 occurrences across 11 files (hmw_io_sr_fm, hmw_io_12_fm, hmw_io12_sw7_dr, hmw_io12_sw7_dr_V3_02 are the four that were dropped). The conclusion survives the correction and is strengthened: all 44 sit in a paramset with type="LINK" and all 44 carry hidden="true", so GetDefinition skips every one. Zero in MASTER, zero in rftypes. Had one of the four skipped files carried a non-hidden or MASTER instance the conclusion would have flipped, so this was a real hole, not a rounding error.

CORRECTION 2 — the file count. 142 device XMLs (124 rftypes + 18 hs485types), not 148.

SCOPE GAP the prior pass did not name. The rewrite lives in `hydrateParamset`, which is called for every channel of every interface through the generic `backends.Operations` — I read the call site: `hydrateChannel` invokes it once for VALUES and once for MASTER with no interface discrimination. Tier 1 covers rfd, hs485d and the HmIP legacy surface; it says nothing about CUxD (BIN-RPC, a third-party addon) or Homegear, both of which our pipeline runs this rewrite against. A CUxD MASTER descriptor that genuinely means "neither readable nor writable" would be rewritten to read+write and the parameter offered as writable in the UI and over MQTT. That half of the rule is not performable against Tier 1 and should be recorded as such rather than left implied.

TIER 2 vs TIER 1, restated sharply. I reproduced the pydevccu histogram exactly: over 399 paramset-description files, MASTER OPERATIONS is 3 in 69214 cases, 0 in 2942, 1 in 495, with 210 of 399 files carrying at least one 0. I then chased one of the recurring names: AES_ACTIVE is declared in the rftypes XMLs as `<parameter id="AES_ACTIVE" ui_flags="internal">` with no operations attribute, so a live rfd must emit 3 for it. The descriptor corpus and the firmware disagree, and Tier 1 wins: our code should keep writing 3. The rewrite is a repair of a lossy descriptor corpus, not a firmware workaround, and the comment should say so.

SIBLING CLAIM at :1995 ("No MASTER parameter carries EVENT in practice") — CONFIRMED at Tier 1 by a binary-safe scan: 2645 MASTER parameters across all 142 XMLs, zero declaring an operations string containing `event`; and neither firmware default grants EVENT (BidCos default 3, HmIP default 1).

reachesDevice.title: The two XML-RPC write-formatting rules that reach every device write rest only on a comment claiming fault -5
reachesDevice.ourValue: "<i4> is silently rejected with xml-rpc fault -5"; "<double>1</double> is rejected with fault -5, <double>1.0</double> is accepted"; both attributed to "the CCU firmware (eQ-3 ReGaHss)"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: <i4> and <int> are synonyms in all three CCU-side XML-RPC parsers; <double>1</double> parses fine (strtod / Double.parseDouble); fault -5 in rfd is "Unknown parameter", and the string "Invalid parameter or value" belongs to the HmIP legacy surface and is raised for an unknown parameter or an out-of-domain value, never for a tag or literal form
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:260-261 `else if (typeTag == I4_TAG || typeTag == INT_TAG)\n      result = intFromXml(valueXml, offset);` — and libXmlRpc itself EMITS <i4>: :515-519 `xml += I4_TAG;` in `XmlRpcValue::intToXml`. Double: :577-584 `bool XmlRpcValue::doubleFromXml(...) { ... double dvalue = strtod(valueStart, &valueEnd); if (valueEnd == valueStart) return false; ...}`. Tcl surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:111 `}else if(strstr(type, "int")==type || strstr(type, "i4")==type){//int`. HmIP legacy XML-RPC: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcParser#parseValue — `case 3307: case 104431:` (the hashCodes of "i4" and "int", declared as TYPE_INTEGER_4_BYTE and TYPE_INTEGER) fall through to the same `Integer.parseInt` branch, and the double branch is `Double.parseDouble(this.reader.getText())`. Fault -5 in rfd: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:128,140,163 and :1738 `throw XmlRpcException("Unknown parameter", -5);`. The exact string "Invalid parameter or value" with faultCode -5: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException (cases UNKNOWN_PARAMETER / INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE).
reachesDevice.finding: Both stated reasons are false on both CCU-side XML-RPC surfaces our transport actually reaches. (1) <i4>: libXmlRpc (rfd, hs485d) dispatches I4_TAG and INT_TAG to the identical intFromXml, and it serialises its OWN integers as <i4> — a client that rejected <i4> could not talk to the CCU at all. tclrpc accepts both. The HmIP legacy parser (HmIP-RF, HmIP-Wired, VirtualDevices) puts "i4" and "int" in the same switch case. (2) <double>1</double>: libXmlRpc converts with strtod and the HmIP parser with Double.parseDouble; both accept "1", and both discard the literal text at that point — the value is a C++ TypeDouble / Java Double before any putParamset type check runs, so NO downstream validator can distinguish "1" from "1.0". (3) The fault attribution is doubly wrong: -5 in rfd reads "Unknown parameter", and the message our comment quotes comes from the HmIP legacy surface (raised when the backend reports UNKNOWN_PARAMETER or INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE — a parameter-identity or value-domain failure), not from ReGaHss and not from value formatting. What our code DOES is harmless: emitting <int> and forcing at least one fractional digit are both accepted everywhere. The defect is the recorded reason — it names a constraint that does not exist, and an operator who "simplifies" the formatter on that basis will change nothing, while one who trusts it will look for -5 in the wrong place. Scope caveat: I checked the three CCU-side parsers only; CUxD is BIN-RPC (no value tags) and Homegear is third-party, so an observation behind the original comment may have come from a non-CCU peer — that possibility is unverified.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the claims been right I would have found a tag whitelist that maps only INT_TAG to the integer branch (each of the three parsers could trivially have done so — they all enumerate tag names explicitly), and a double path that kept the literal string for a later validator. All three parsers accept both integer tags in one branch, and both double paths call strtod/parseDouble immediately — the opposite result in each case.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted. I opened every cited line and each contains what was claimed, transcribed exactly.

The decisive point is one I re-verified independently: libXmlRpc does not merely tolerate <i4>, it EMITS it. `XmlRpcValue::intToXml` at :517 appends I4_TAG. rfd and hs485d serialise every integer they send us as <i4>. A CCU that rejected <i4> on input would be rejecting its own wire form, and our transport — which parses incoming <i4> — could not have worked at all. That single fact settles rule (1) without needing the parser dispatch, and the parser dispatch (:260-261) settles it a second time.

Rule (2) is equally dead. Both surfaces convert the literal before any validator sees it: strtod in C++ (:580-584), Double.parseDouble in the HmIP parser. Neither preserves the text "1" vs "1.0", so no downstream putParamset check can distinguish them — the distinction our comment asserts is not merely unenforced, it is unrepresentable at the point where enforcement would happen.

I add a THIRD independent wrongness the prior pass gestured at but did not state as a finding: the attribution names a peer this transport never addresses. `internal/client/transport/xmlrpc` speaks to the interface processes — rfd, hs485d (both libXmlRpc) and HMIPServer's legacy surface. ReGaHss is reached over JSON-RPC (`internal/client/transport/jsonrpc`), never over this codec. So the comment attributes a constraint to a component that is not on the path, in addition to describing a constraint that does not exist on the components that are.

What our code does is harmless — <int> and a forced fractional digit are accepted everywhere — so this is a documentation defect, not a delivery bug. The cost is directional: an operator debugging a -5 will look in ReGaHss and at value formatting, when -5 from rfd means the parameter name is unknown and -5 from the HmIP legacy surface means unknown parameter or out-of-domain value.

I keep the prior pass's scope caveat and endorse it: only the three CCU-side parsers were read. CUxD is BIN-RPC and carries no value tags at all; Homegear is third-party. Whatever observation originally produced this comment may have come from a non-CCU peer, and that remains unverified — it is not a reason to keep the comment as written, but it is a reason not to assert the comment was invented.

reachesDevice.title: setInstallMode is always sent with mode=1 on the strength of a comment alone
reachesDevice.ourValue: mode=1 = "normal"; "mode=2 means ready for re-pairing"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: INSTALL_OFF=0, INSTALL_NORMAL=1, INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG=2, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST=3
reachesDevice.finding: The value we send is CORRECT: mode=1 is INSTALL_NORMAL, the ordinary teach-in that registers the CCU as central. The GLOSS of mode=2 is wrong and dangerous: 2 is INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG, which resets the device to the default configuration from its device/channel description AND deletes all existing links — not "ready for re-pairing". "Ready for re-pairing / known device only" is mode 3, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST, and rfd's int range check is `0 <= mode <= INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG(2)`, so passing 3 as an int is rejected with fault -1; the whitelist mode is reachable ONLY by putting the serial as a STRING in params[2]. Our device-scoped path already does exactly that (ccu_extended.go:104 `b.xml.Call(ctx, "setInstallMode", on, duration, deviceAddress)`), so it matches the firmware — and installModeNormal is simply unused on that branch and on the HmIP branch. Second, unrelated-site defect found while grounding this: internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods.go:163-165 documents the same argument as "mode selects the learning mode (0 = normal, 1 = set, 2 = unset)", which matches neither the enum nor the adapter's comment; and the CCU's JSON-RPC wrapper discards both extra arguments — ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/setinstallmode.tcl reads only `interface` and `on` and calls `xmlrpc $interface(URL) setInstallMode [list bool $on]`, so duration and mode sent through Interface.setInstallMode never reach rfd (the window silently becomes the 60 s default).
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had mode=1 not been "normal" the enum would have ordered the constants differently (e.g. INSTALL_NORMAL=0), or RFDevice's switch would have taken a non-teach-in branch for it; instead INSTALL_NORMAL is the first non-zero ordinal and its case performs the central-address write. Had mode=2 meant re-pairing, RFDevice.cpp's INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG case would not call InitDefault()/SetDefaultConfig() — it does, so the check produced a different answer for the half of the claim that is false.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD as narrowed. Every citation opened and matched, including the enum's implicit ordinals and the exact fault string. One transcription note: the prior pass rendered the rfd source comment as "bestehenden"; the file reads "besehenden" (a typo in eQ-3's source). Immaterial to the finding, but a quote is a quote.

The value we send is CORRECT and the gloss is WRONG and dangerous, exactly as reported. Mode 2 is INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG: it calls InitDefault on config list 0 and SetDefaultConfig on the device description, which the source itself says deletes all existing links. It is not "ready for re-pairing". The re-pairing/known-device flavour is mode 3, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST, and rfd's int range check tops out at 2, so an integer 3 is refused with fault -1 — the whitelist mode is reachable only by passing the serial as a STRING in params[2].

I CORRECT one statement in the prior finding. It says installModeNormal "is simply unused on that branch and on the HmIP branch". That reads as though the constant never reaches the wire. It does: install_mode.go:59 passes installModeNormal on the broadcast path (empty deviceAddress), and ccu_extended.go:107 sends it as the third argument to the XML-RPC setInstallMode. So mode=1 IS live on the broadcast pairing path — which is fine, since 1 is INSTALL_NORMAL. It is unused only on the device-scoped path (install_mode.go:69 also passes it, but ccu_extended.go:104 takes the deviceAddress branch and drops it). The correct statement is: the constant is sent, its value is right, and its comment is wrong.

Second-site defect, re-verified: internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods.go:163-165 documents the mode argument as "0 = normal, 1 = set, 2 = unset", which matches neither the enum nor the adapter comment nor each other. I add the severity qualifier the prior pass omitted: `SetInstallModeBidCos` has NO production caller — grep across internal/ and cmd/ finds only its own declaration and one test. It is a dead method carrying a wrong comment, which lowers urgency but not the case for fixing it, since a future caller would inherit the error. And the wrapper it names would discard the argument anyway: setinstallmode.tcl reads only `interface` and `on` and forwards a single bool, so duration and mode sent through Interface.setInstallMode never reach rfd and the window silently falls back to the 60 s default.

BOUNDARY (why narrowed rather than confirmed): the enum, the range check and the mode-2 semantics are rfd-only. Our SetInstallMode also serves HmIP-RF, where ccu_extended.go:92-99 takes an entirely different route (`Interface.setInstallModeHMIP` with an installMode/address/key/keymode struct) that carries no numeric mode at all, and CUxD/Homegear, for which Tier 1 says nothing. The grounded rule is "mode=1 is INSTALL_NORMAL on the rfd XML-RPC surface", not "on every interface".

reachesDevice.title: The central-link create/remove asymmetry rests on a claim about the CCU WebUI with no path citation
reachesDevice.ourValue: create raises PRESS_SHORT only; remove zeroes PRESS_SHORT and PRESS_LONG
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: create: reportValueUsage(addr, PRESS_SHORT, 1). remove: reportValueUsage(addr, PRESS_SHORT, 0) AND reportValueUsage(addr, PRESS_LONG, 0)
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0171-WebUI-Add-HmIPKeyTransceiverCentralLinkConfiguration.patch:81-107 (post-patch text at ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0183-WebUI-ImprovedFirmwareupdateDialog/occu/WebUI/www/webui/webui.js:15619-15647): `createCentralLink: function(channeltype) { ... homematic("Interface.reportValueUsage", {"interface": "HmIP-RF", "address": addr, "valueId": "PRESS_SHORT", "refCounter":"1"}); ... }` and `removeCentralLink: function(channeltype) { ... {"valueId": "PRESS_SHORT", "refCounter":"0"}); ... {"valueId": "PRESS_LONG", "refCounter":"0"}); ... }` — interface chosen by channelType: KEY_TRANSCEIVER / MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER -> HmIP-RF, KEY -> BidCos-RF. Why the asymmetry is required: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1425-1449 `bool RFChannel::ReportValueUsage(const std::string& value, int count) { if(!GetDescription()->GetAutoregisterCentral())return true; value_usage_map[value]=count; int total_count=0; for(...){ if(it->second > 0)total_count+=it->second; } ... if(total_count && !IsLinkedTo(central_address, central_channel)){ AddLinkPeer(...); }else if(!total_count && IsLinkedTo(...)){ LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(...); ... } }`. HmIP equivalent: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage — reads channel metadata "reportValueUsageData" as a Map, `dataMap.put(valueId, refCounter)`, writes it back, `newRefCounter = dataMap.values().stream().mapToInt(Integer::valueOf).sum()`, then createCentralLink when `Math.max(0, newRefCounter) > 0` else deleteCentralLink. RPC entry point and semantics: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:700-724 (returns false when the device must first be put into config mode; CONFIG_PENDING is then set on MAINTENANCE) and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/reportvalueusage.tcl:19.
reachesDevice.finding: Confirmed verbatim, on both the operator surface and the mechanism beneath it. The WebUI's create path issues one reportValueUsage with PRESS_SHORT/1; the remove path issues two, PRESS_SHORT/0 and PRESS_LONG/0. More than a UI convention: the interface process keys the counters per value-id and gates the device-internal peering on the SUM, so zeroing PRESS_SHORT alone leaves the link standing whenever PRESS_LONG was ever raised, while raising PRESS_SHORT alone is sufficient to establish it. Our implementation matches on both paths. On the metadata question in the brief: reportValueUsageData is a map valueId -> integer refCounter stored per channel address; a value-id absent from the map simply contributes nothing to the sum, so "absent means zero" is correct — but note it means "absent from the sum", and reading the map back is the right way to determine the active state. Two details worth carrying: rfd sums only POSITIVE counters (`if(it->second > 0)`) whereas the HmIP side sums all values and then clamps with max(0, sum) — irrelevant for the 0/1 values we send, but a negative counter would behave differently on the two interfaces; and reportValueUsage returns false (not an error) when the device could not be reached, meaning the setting is queued and CONFIG_PENDING is raised on MAINTENANCE — our adapter treats only a transport error as failure, which matches. Scope note: the WebUI applies this only to channelTypes KEY (BidCos-RF) and KEY_TRANSCEIVER / MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER (HmIP-RF); our eligibility rule lives in device.CentralLinkEligibility and was not compared against that set here.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the asymmetry been the other way round, webui.js would show a PRESS_LONG call inside createCentralLink or a single call inside removeCentralLink; and had the counters not been summed across value-ids, RFChannel::ReportValueUsage would test only the just-written entry rather than accumulating total_count over the whole map, in which case zeroing PRESS_SHORT alone would suffice and the second call would be pointless. Both checks read the opposite of the alternative.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
DEMOTED from confirmed to narrowed. The quote itself is exact — I opened patch 0171 and both functions read verbatim as cited, create with one call and remove with two, on both interface branches. The rfd mechanism is exact too, including the positive-only sum. So the rule under grading is grounded. What I am demoting is its reach, by settling the question the prior pass explicitly left open ("our eligibility rule lives in device.CentralLinkEligibility and was not compared against that set here").

I compared it, and the gap is real and measurable. The firmware gates the ENTIRE mechanism on one flag: `if(!GetDescription()->GetAutoregisterCentral())return true;` — identically in rfd (RFChannel.cpp:1425) and hs485d (HS485Channel.cpp:411). When the flag is unset the call is a no-op that returns TRUE, indistinguishable at our transport from a successful link. Our eligibility (aggregate.go:551-561) admits any non-virtual-remote device on BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired or HmIP-RF, filtered per channel only by channelHasPressEvents (central_links.go:277-287, PRESS_SHORT or PRESS_LONG present in VALUES). Measured against the shipped device XMLs:

- BidCos-Wired: ZERO channels in any of the 18 hs485types XMLs carry an `autoregister` attribute, and HS485ChannelDescription defaults it false. Yet 12 hs485types files declare PRESS_SHORT/PRESS_LONG. So every central-link create or remove we issue on BidCos-Wired passes channelHasPressEvents, reaches hs485d, does nothing, and returns true — which our adapter counts as a channel touched and reports to the operator as a created link.
- BidCos-RF: 32 of 34 KEY channels carry `autoregister`; the two that do not are rf_ou_led16_ge_v1_1.xml and rf_ou_led16_le_v1_0.xml (HM-OU-LED16), whose KEY channels do declare PRESS_SHORT. Same silent-success shape on a real, shipping device.

The WebUI's own scope is narrower still: it offers the control only for channelType KEY on BidCos-RF and KEY_TRANSCEIVER / MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER on HmIP-RF. It never offers it on BidCos-Wired at all.

Two further details from the prior pass that I re-checked and confirm: reportValueUsageData on the HmIP side is a map valueId -> refCounter, so "absent contributes nothing to the sum" is right and reading the map back is the correct way to determine active state; and reportValueUsage returning false is not an error but "queued, device must enter config mode, CONFIG_PENDING raised on MAINTENANCE" — our adapter treating only a transport error as failure matches. I also confirm the divergence in summation the prior pass noted: rfd and hs485d both sum only counters `> 0`, while the HmIP handler sums all values then clamps with max(0, sum) — immaterial for the 0/1 values we send.

reachesDevice.title: installFirmware-then-updateFirmware fallback: the doc claims a device-family split and 'any error', the code branches only on an XML-RPC fault
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1092 `XmlRpcMethodUpdateFirmware(XmlRpcServer* s):XmlRpcServerMethod("updateFirmware", s){};` — rfd registers `updateFirmware` and no `installFirmware` (grep -ra over src/rfd) · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:486 the same for hs485d · unknown-method behaviour: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:240-242 `if ( ! executeMethod(…) && ! executeMulticall(…)) generateFaultResponse(methodName + ": unknown method name");` with the default code from XmlRpcServerConnection.h:78 `void generateFaultResponse(std::string const& msg, int errorCode = -1);` — an XML-RPC fault, faultCode -1, never a transport error · HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.IServiceApi declares both `@RpcMethod("updateFirmware")` and `@RpcMethod("installFirmware")`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#updateFirmware throws a NotImplementedException RPC remote exception, while #installFirmware is the real implementation and returns boolean `false` when `DeviceUtil.isUpdateInstallable` is false or the transaction result is unsuccessful, faulting only for DeviceNotFound / AccessPointNotFound / transmission-pending · the CCU's own caller: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368 branches on the interface (`if {($iface != $HmIPIdentifier) && ($iface != $HmIPWiredIdentifier)} { … updateFirmware … } else { … installFirmware … }`) and :371 checks `if { $result == 1 }`.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: rfd/hs485d: `updateFirmware` only, unknown method → XML-RPC fault, faultCode -1, faultString "installFirmware: unknown method name". HMIPServer: `installFirmware` is real and returns boolean false on a legitimate refusal; `updateFirmware` exists but throws NotImplemented. The CCU's own WebUI never probes — it selects by interface and then checks the boolean.
reachesDevice.ourValue: try installFirmware; fall back to updateFirmware only when errors.As(err, *hmerr.XMLRPCFault); return value discarded
reachesDevice.finding: The probe mechanism is sound where the doc says it matters, and false one step wider. The described danger — 'a transport-level failure (not a fault) is what an old rfd returns for an unknown method' — does not occur: libXmlRpc answers an unregistered method with a real XML-RPC fault (faultCode -1), so `errors.As(callErr, &fault)` fires and the BidCos fallback runs. The comment's 'fall back on any error' is the half that is wrong, and the code is the half that is right. Two boundaries the rule does not cover. (1) The CCU's own caller does not probe at all: ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368 picks the method from the interface — HmIP-RF/HmIP-Wired → installFirmware, everything else → updateFirmware. Our probe costs every BidCos update one guaranteed round trip that ends in a logged fault. (2) The boolean is load-bearing and we drop it. HMIPServer's installFirmware returns `false` — not a fault — when the update is not installable or the transaction fails; `_, callErr := b.xml.Call(...)` sees callErr == nil and we return success for an update that never started. The WebUI checks `$result == 1` at :371 precisely for this. The bundle's other worry (a fault on HmIP fires a second update at the same device) is real but harmless in effect: HMIPServer's updateFirmware immediately throws NotImplemented, so no second update starts — it only converts a specific fault into a misleading one.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had rfd answered an unknown method with a transport error rather than a fault, the shared server would have had no `generateFaultResponse(methodName + ": unknown method name")` path — it would have closed the connection or returned nothing. XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:240-242 shows the fault path and XmlRpcServerConnection.h:78 shows the code it carries, which is a different observation from the one the damage note predicts. Had 'installFirmware fails only by faulting' been right, LegacyServiceHandler#installFirmware would have had no `return false` branches; it has two before any throw.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: The previous agent's core result stands and I re-measured every leg of it: libXmlRpc answers an unregistered method with a real XML-RPC fault (code -1), not a transport error, so errors.As fires and the BidCos fallback runs; the comment's 'fall back on any error' is the wrong half and the code is the right half; and the CCU itself never probes, it branches on the interface at ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368. I BREAK one framing and add one boundary. (1) The finding presents the dropped return value as an HmIP problem ('HMIPServer's installFirmware returns false ... we return success for an update that never started'). It is both families. rfd's updateFirmware also returns a boolean: XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1096 assigns the result of RFManager::UpdateFirmware into the reply, and the WebUI's `$result == 1` at :371 sits AFTER the if/else, so eQ-3 checks the boolean on the BidCos branch too. Our `_, err := b.xml.Call(ctx, "updateFirmware", address)` discards it identically. Reported as an HmIP-only defect it would get an HmIP-only fix. (2) NEW narrowing the previous agent missed, and it matters for any fix: the two BidCos daemons do not return the same SHAPE. rfd writes a scalar `(bool&)result` from params[0] only; hs485d loops over all params and writes `(bool&)result[i]` - a one-element array for our single-address call. Code that starts reading the return has to handle bool and []bool, or it will silently mis-read BidCos-Wired. (3) Quote precision, not a defect: the grounding gives faultString as the literal `"installFirmware: unknown method name"`. The firmware constructs it as `methodName + ": unknown method name"` - the rendered string is right, but it is a concatenation, and presenting a constructed string as a verbatim constant is the kind of transcription that later gets matched against literally. (4) I confirm the finding's own narrowing about the second update: a fault on HmIP's installFirmware makes us call updateFirmware, which throws NotImplemented immediately, so no second update starts - the damage is a misleading error, not a duplicate write.

reachesDevice.firmwareValue: HM-CC-TC channel 2 CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR, VALUES paramset: `<parameter id="SETPOINT" operations="read,event,write" control="TEMP.SETPOINT">` with `<logical type="float" min="6.0" max="30.0" default="21.0" unit="°C">`, two special values `VENT_CLOSED` = 0.0 and `VENT_OPEN` = 100.0, and `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="2"/>`. MASTER TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE: `<logical type="float" min="6.0" max="30.0" default="21.0" unit="°C"/>`.
reachesDevice.ourValue: MinTemperature 6.0, MaxTemperature 30.0, TemperatureStep 0.5 — frozen in simpleRfCapabilities; setSimpleRFMode writes MaxTemperature for HEAT and MinTemperature for OFF, bypassing MinTemp()/MaxTemp().
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_tc.xml:185 (channel index 2, type CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR), :269 (paramset type="VALUES"), :271 (the SETPOINT parameter), :286 (the logical min/max/default), :287-288 (special_value VENT_CLOSED 0.0 / VENT_OPEN 100.0), :293 (float_integer_scale factor 2 → the 0.5 step), :424+:434 (MASTER TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE), :449 (TEMPERATUR_LOWERING_VALUE), :533 (TEMPERATUR_PARTY_VALUE), :606 (a weekly TEMPERATUR_SATURDAY_1) — all 6.0/30.0; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_tc_le_v1_9.xml:267-268 (same SETPOINT block on the LE variant). Our side: internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:831-852 (SimpleRfThermostat primary channel 1, ChannelFields[1] → FieldSetpoint: Bare(ParameterSetpoint)), internal/model/custom/profiles.go:287-296 and :1629-1638 (hm-cc-tc and "zel stg rm fwt"), internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:638-663 and :672-693 (MinTemp/MaxTemp read c.setpoint.DescriptorMin/Max BEFORE the capability fallback), :1022-1033 (SetTemperature's range validation), :1073-1086 (SetMode dispatches on Kind and never consults SupportsOff).
reachesDevice.finding: The numbers are right, and right for a better reason than the comment gives. The comment's premise is false: the SimpleRF family DOES ship a writable setpoint descriptor — it is named SETPOINT, not SET_TEMPERATURE, it lives in the VALUES paramset of the very channel we write to (device channel 2, CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR), and it declares min=6.0 max=30.0 default=21.0 with a factor-2 integer scale that is also where our 0.5 step comes from. Our own profile writes exactly that DP. The named source, MASTER TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE, happens to carry the same bounds, as do TEMPERATUR_LOWERING_VALUE, TEMPERATUR_PARTY_VALUE and every weekly TEMPERATUR_<day>_<n>; but calling it a "weekly-schedule descriptor" is wrong — it is the comfort-temperature config parameter, and the weekly entries are a separate family. Where the rule is false one step wider: the device's acceptance set for SETPOINT is NOT [6.0, 30.0]. Two special values sit outside it — VENT_CLOSED (0.0), which fully closes the linked valves, and VENT_OPEN (100.0), which fully opens them. SetTemperature rejects anything outside [MinTemp, MaxTemp], so neither is reachable through our climate DP, and setSimpleRFMode(ModeOff) writes 6.0 — the lowest regulating setpoint, not the device's actual off. SetMode reaches that path even though simpleRfCapabilities.SupportsOff is false, because SetMode dispatches on Kind alone. Second boundary: the verification covers HM-CC-TC only. The firmware device-type set carries no ZEL_STG_RM_FWT XML (grep over src/devicetypes returns nothing), and it is absent from ../pydevccu and ../openccu-data as well; our profile registers "zel stg rm fwt" as an alias of hm-cc-tc at profiles.go:1629-1638. Its descriptor is not in any tree I can read, so the bounds are unverified for that model. Which source to follow: Tier 2, the per-device descriptor read at runtime. MinTemp()/MaxTemp() already do that and fall back to the capability struct only when the setpoint carries no MIN/MAX; setSimpleRFMode is the one path that skips them. Today the two agree exactly, so nothing is mis-written — the defect is that the code takes the frozen copy where the live descriptor is one call away.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had 6.0/30.0 been wrong, the `logical` element on SETPOINT at rf_cc_tc.xml:286 would have carried different min/max attributes. The same read does return different bounds for neighbouring parameters in the same file — TEMPERATURE at :158 is min=-40.0 max=80.0, HUMIDITY at :171 is min=0 max=99, ADJUSTING_COMMAND at :304 is min=0 max=4 — so the read discriminates rather than echoing whatever it is asked for.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: The numbers are right and the comment's premise is false, as reported — but the prior grounding inflated its tier and named a boundary that does not exist, so I am redrawing both. TIER: rf_cc_tc.xml is a device-type XML, which this audit's own map places at Tier 2, not Tier 1. The bounds are a descriptor fact. The only Tier-1 leg is the step, which I added below. BOUNDARY REMOVED: the prior grounding reported ZEL STG RM FWT as unverified because "the firmware device-type set carries no ZEL_STG_RM_FWT XML; grep over src/devicetypes returns nothing". The firmware id is space-separated — `ZEL STG RM FWT` — and it is declared in rf_cc_tc.xml's own `<supported_types>` at :13, beside HM-CC-TC at :9. One XML, one channel-2 SETPOINT descriptor, serving both models; our alias registration at profiles.go:1629-1638 reproduces the firmware's own grouping exactly. A grep for the underscore form finds nothing, which is presumably how the boundary was invented — a boundary asserted from a grep miss reads exactly like one read from the source. SURFACE, traced end to end rather than assumed: the profile registers primary channel 1, ChannelFields keys are relative offsets rebased by groupNo (`rebased[ch+groupNo]`), so ChannelFields[1] resolves to absolute channel 2 — the CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR channel that carries SETPOINT — and ParameterSetpoint is literally "SETPOINT". So we do bind to that descriptor, and the comment's "no SET_TEMPERATURE DP whose descriptor would otherwise drive these" is false; the DP is simply named SETPOINT. The "weekly-schedule descriptor" label is also wrong: TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE is `docu brief="Konforttemperatur"`, a config parameter on list 5, and the weekly TEMPERATUR_<day>_<n> entries are a separate family that merely shares the range. CORRECTION to the prior reading of our own code: setSimpleRFMode does NOT bypass MinTemp()/MaxTemp(). It calls SetTemperature, which validates against both at :1023-1033. What it bypasses is the descriptor as the SOURCE of the value — it writes the frozen capability constant. A descriptor/capability disagreement would therefore surface as ErrTemperatureOutOfRange, not as a silently wrong write; the defect shape reported was more severe than the code supports. STEP, now grounded on Tier 1 and worth recording because nothing else names it: `float_integer_scale` is handled by HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger, which rfd links, and LogicalToPhysical is a C cast — it TRUNCATES. At factor 2 the logical grid is 0.5 and an off-grid setpoint goes toward zero, not to nearest. SURVIVING BOUNDARY: the device's acceptance set for SETPOINT is [6.0,30.0] plus {0.0, 100.0}; VENT_CLOSED and VENT_OPEN are unreachable through Climate.SetTemperature, and setSimpleRFMode(ModeOff) writes 6.0 — the lowest regulating setpoint, not the device's valve-closed value — over a path SetMode reaches although simpleRfCapabilities.SupportsOff is false, because SetMode dispatches on Kind alone. Which source to follow: Tier 2, the per-device descriptor read at runtime; MinTemp()/MaxTemp() already do, and setSimpleRFMode is the one place that takes the frozen copy where the live descriptor is one call away.

reachesDevice.ourValue: value_cache.go:314-332: BidCos-RF and VirtualDevices are skipped interface-wide because a per-parameter fallback "cannot return a device-fresh reading — only a CCU-internal placeholder (reported with *_STATUS = NORMAL so the status cannot be used to reject it)" and because "the fallback then returns the paramset default instead of a real reading".
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: For BidCos-RF: (a) a read that cannot be satisfied does NOT return the paramset default — `HSSParamset::Get` aborts on the first failing readable parameter and the whole getParamset answers fault -1 "Failure". The DEFAULT fallback exists only for parameters whose device XML declares `use_default_on_failure="true"`, which in the shipped rftypes is 21 parameters, all `logical type="string" default=""`. (b) There is no `*_STATUS = NORMAL` sibling convention on BidCos-RF; the only `*_STATUS` ids in the 130 shipped rftypes are ACK_STATUS and LED_STATUS. (c) The suppression is not interface-shaped: the no-active-query branch is gated on `RxNeedsWakeup()`, i.e. on the device's RX_MODE, so a mains BidCos-RF device (RX_ALWAYS) DOES get the get-request frame sent and answered from the device. (d) The CCU already computes the exact flag we want — `undefined`, true from construction and cleared only when a device frame delivered the value — and exposes it through the 3-argument getValue/getParamset (mode==1).
reachesDevice.finding: The rule's stated firmware basis does not hold for BidCos-RF on any of its three legs. The failure mode is not a plausible-looking default value quietly marked valid; it is a hard fault -1 on the whole paramset, because HSSParamset::Get is all-or-nothing. The `*_STATUS = NORMAL` reasoning is imported from the HmIP surface and has no counterpart in the BidCos-RF descriptors. And the skip keys on the interface while the firmware keys on RX_MODE, which is exactly the over-broad scope the reader flagged: mains-powered BidCos-RF devices are actively queried by rfd and are paying for the battery subset. Most usefully, the input our code is trying to guess at is carried by the source after all — rfd tracks `undefined` per parameter and hands it over on the 3-argument form, so the honest fix is to read that flag rather than to widen or narrow a heuristic. I could not settle the VirtualDevices half: that interface is served by the HMServer group/virtual-device stack, not by rfd, and I did not verify its read path — treat the VirtualDevices leg of this rule as still ungrounded.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our claim been right, `HSSParamset::Get` would have inserted the logical DEFAULT for an unreadable parameter and continued to the next one, and `use_default_on_failure` would appear on ordinary numeric value parameters across the rftypes corpus rather than on 21 empty-string parameters. It does neither: Get `return false`s on the first failure, and the attribute defaults to false (HSSLogicalType.cpp:25). Had the battery/mains distinction been irrelevant, `RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand::GetData` would have had no RX_MODE branch; it has one, and the branch is the only place the get-request frame is skipped.

Confirmed by my reading: (a) the failure mode is a hard fault, not a plausible default. HSSParamset::Get (:162-176) aborts on the first readable parameter whose GetValue fails and XmlRpcMethodGetParamset turns that into -1 "Failure" — there is no partial struct and no silently-substituted default. The DEFAULT fallback exists only behind `use_default_on_failure`, which in the shipped descriptors is 21 empty-string parameters. Our code's fallback path is `loader.GetParamset(..., ParamsetKeyValues)`, so this is the right surface. (b) There is no *_STATUS = NORMAL convention in the RF descriptors; the only ids are ACK_STATUS and LED_STATUS. (d) The firmware does carry the flag we are guessing at — `undefined`, true from construction (:28), cleared only in ProcessIncomingFrame (:355), exposed on the 3-argument getValue/getParamset (mode==1, :252-280). Reading it is the honest fix.

Overstated by the audited report: leg (c), "the suppression is not interface-shaped, it is RxNeedsWakeup-shaped, so mains BidCos-RF devices DO get queried". The RxNeedsWakeup gate at :166 is reached only after the guard at :152 — `if(get_request_frame.id.empty()) return GetStoredValue(...)`. Only 76 parameters across 21 of the 127 shipped RF device XMLs declare a `<get request="..."/>` frame at all. For every other BidCos-RF VALUES parameter no active query is issued regardless of RX_MODE; the read returns the stored value or fails. So the firmware's key is (declares a get frame) AND (RX_ALWAYS or already stored) — not RX_MODE alone. Our interface-wide skip is still wrong, but it is less wrong than the audited report implies, and a fix keyed purely on RX_MODE would be a second guess.

The VirtualDevices half stays ungrounded; the audited report says so and I did not close it either.

reachesDevice.title: "A MASTER setValue is answered with fault -5" is the stated basis for routing single MASTER writes through putParamset
reachesDevice.citation: OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:155-170 `RFChannel::SetValue`: `RFParamset* ps=GetDescription()->GetParamset("VALUES"); if(!ps){ throw XmlRpcException("Unknown paramset", -3); } HSSParameter* param=ps->GetParameter(name); if(!param){ throw XmlRpcException("Unknown parameter", -5); }`. OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:305 (verbatim doc) "Mit dieser Methode wird ein einzelner Wert aus dem Parameter-Set \"VALUES\" geschrieben."; :303-330 the method takes only (address, value_key, value[, rxmode]) — no paramset argument. OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Channel.cpp:90-97 `HS485Channel::SetValue`: same VALUES-only lookup but `if(!param)return false;`, and OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:244-246 turns that into `throw XmlRpcException("Failure")` — default code -1 per OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcException.h:29 `XmlRpcException(const std::string& message, int code=-1)`. CONFIG_PENDING on BidCos: OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1036-1040 `if((config_pending == last_config_pending) && !force)return; last_config_pending=config_pending; ... SendInternalValueEvent("CONFIG_PENDING", val);`, :701 (GetInternalValue), RFDevice.h:188-192; wired equivalent OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Device.cpp:64,650. HmIP equivalent: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil serves the legacy `CONFIG_PENDING` value key from `device.isAnyConfigurationTransmissionPending()`.
reachesDevice.ourValue: channel_set.go:568-573 "xml-rpc setValue, which always targets VALUES" / "Sending it through SetValue instead makes the CCU answer fault -5, or silently apply a same-named VALUES parameter"; channel_set.go:610-616 "Classic HM devices wire this to MasterPoller.SchedulePoll; HmIP devices leave it nil because they use the CONFIG_PENDING True→False signal instead."
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: setValue targets VALUES and only VALUES on every stack — confirmed, and the method signature carries no paramset argument at all. The fault code is interface-dependent: rfd answers -5 with the message "Unknown parameter" (not "Invalid parameter or value"); hs485d answers -1 with the message "Failure". CONFIG_PENDING is NOT an HmIP-only signal: rfd raises it on every True↔False transition for BidCos-RF devices and hs485d does the same for BidCos-Wired.
reachesDevice.finding: The load-bearing half is confirmed outright: `RFChannel::SetValue` hard-codes `GetParamset("VALUES")` before looking the name up, so a MASTER parameter can never be reached through setValue, and the dangerous branch our comment worries about is real by construction — the lookup is by name inside VALUES, so a MASTER parameter that shares a name with a VALUES parameter gets the VALUES one written silently. Two details are narrower than stated. First, the fault code is not universal: BidCos-Wired returns -1 "Failure", not -5, because hs485d returns a bool where rfd throws; anything that keys recovery on -5 will miss the wired case. Second, the stated reason for the nil master-refresh hook on HmIP is contradicted — CONFIG_PENDING is emitted by rfd and hs485d as well, so it is not what distinguishes the two stacks. The wiring may still be correct, but its written justification is not a firmware distinction and should not be cited as one.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had setValue been paramset-aware, `RFChannel::SetValue` would have taken a paramset key from the call rather than hard-coding "VALUES", and `XmlRpcMethodSetValue::execute` would have accepted a fourth non-rxmode argument; it accepts only an optional rxmode string constrained to "WAKEUP"/"BURST" (RFManager.cpp:181-189). Had CONFIG_PENDING been HmIP-only, `grep -rn CONFIG_PENDING ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/` would have been empty; it returns the emitter, the getter and the header documentation.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed, and there is a third fault path the audited report missed — the one that matters for the very parameter class c009 is about.

Confirmed line-exact: `RFChannel::SetValue` hard-codes `GetParamset("VALUES")` before the name lookup, so a MASTER parameter can never be reached through setValue, and the dangerous branch our comment worries about is real by construction — the lookup is by name inside VALUES, so a MASTER parameter sharing a name with a VALUES parameter gets the VALUES one written silently. I also checked the layer above: `RFManager::SetValue` does not catch, so the -5 genuinely reaches the client.

Added: our comment's "-5" holds only for rfd at a CHANNEL address. `RFDevice::SetValue` (RFDevice.cpp:225-228) returns false unconditionally, so a setValue at a bare device address on rfd is turned into -1 "Failure" by XmlRpcMethodSetValue (:322/:327). That is exactly the address a device-level MASTER parameter lives at on HM-TC-IT and HM-CC-RT-DN (see c009), so the three outcomes are: channel/rfd -5 "Unknown parameter", device/rfd -1 "Failure", hs485d -1 "Failure". Anything keying recovery on -5 misses two of the three. The message in our comment is wrong too — rfd says "Unknown parameter", not "Invalid parameter or value".

Confirmed contradiction of the second claim: CONFIG_PENDING is emitted by rfd on every True↔False transition (RFDevice.cpp:1036-1040) and by hs485d identically (HS485Device.cpp:64), so it is not what distinguishes HmIP from classic HM. The wiring may still be correct for other reasons, but its written justification is not a firmware distinction. Note this sentence lives at channel_set.go:284-286, repeated at :531 and channel.go:211-213 — three sites, not the one the audited report named.

reachesDevice.title: Per-interface capability sets (replaceDevice, searchDevices, setTeam, restoreConfigToDevice) rest on prose about which CCU daemon implements what
reachesDevice.citation: OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1222-1276 `InitXmlRpcMethods` — the complete rfd method table; it contains `static XmlRpcMethodRestoreConfigToDevice ...(&s);` (:1250), `static XmlRpcMethodSetTeam ...(&s);` (:1253), `static XmlRpcMethodListTeams ...(&s);` (:1230), `static XmlRpcMethodReplaceDevice ...(&s);` (:1268), `static XmlRpcMethodListReplaceableDevices ...(&s);` (:1270) and NO searchDevices entry. OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:618-645 — the complete hs485d method table; it contains `static XmlRpcMethodSearchDevices ...(&s);` (:626), `static XmlRpcMethodReplaceDevice ...(&s);` (:642), `static XmlRpcMethodListReplaceableDevices ...(&s);` (:643) and NO restoreConfigToDevice / setTeam / listTeams. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler — the @RpcMethod-annotated legacy XML-RPC surface (init, listDevices, getParamsetDescription, getParamset(String,String,Integer), putParamset, getValue, setValue, addLink, removeLink, setInstallMode, deleteDevice, ...) — implements #replaceDevice, #listReplaceableDevices (both overloads), #countNewDevices (@RpcMethod("searchDevices")), #listTeams, #setTeam and #restoreConfigToDevice each as a single `throw NotificationUtil.getRpcRemoteException(new NotImplementedException("<method>"))`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.ExtendedLegacyServiceHandler, its only subclass, overrides none of them. Corroboration on the operator surface: OpenCCU-Base/www/tools/devconfig.cgi:1145-1161 gates the Team selector on `[info exist dev_descr(TEAM)]` and only then calls `listTeams`.
reachesDevice.ourValue: InterfacesSupportingConfigRestore = {BidCos-RF, HmIP-RF}; InterfacesSupportingTeams = {BidCos-RF, HmIP-RF}; InterfacesSupportingReplace = {BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired}; InterfacesSupportingDeviceSearch = {BidCos-Wired}.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: restoreConfigToDevice: rfd yes, hs485d no, HmIP NotImplementedException → {BidCos-RF} only. setTeam/listTeams: rfd yes, hs485d no, HmIP NotImplementedException → {BidCos-RF} only. replaceDevice/listReplaceableDevices: rfd yes, hs485d yes, HmIP NotImplementedException → {BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired} — matches. searchDevices: hs485d yes, rfd does not register it at all, HmIP NotImplementedException → {BidCos-Wired} — matches.
reachesDevice.finding: Two of the four sets are wrong, and both are false positives in the direction the reader called silent — we will send a call the HmIP daemon refuses. `InterfacesSupportingConfigRestore` includes HmIP-RF, but the HmIP legacy handler answers restoreConfigToDevice with NotImplementedException. `InterfacesSupportingTeams` includes HmIP-RF, but both setTeam and listTeams answer the same way; the comment's smoke-detector rationale does not survive, since HmIP smoke-detector grouping goes through the HmIP group/virtual-device path, not through the legacy team methods. The two sets that were only asserted in prose — Replace and DeviceSearch — are confirmed exactly, including the negative half of each: rfd genuinely registers no searchDevices, and hs485d genuinely registers no team or config-restore methods. The comment's specific sentence "HMIPServer (HmIP-*) throws NotImplementedException" for replaceDevice is verbatim correct; the same sentence simply needed to be applied to three more methods.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had HmIP implemented these, LegacyServiceHandler would carry a body for them the way it does for setValue, getParamset, addLink and deleteDevice in the same class — each of which dispatches onto the vertx event bus and waits on a response queue. Instead each of the six is a one-line throw. Had rfd implemented searchDevices, the string would appear in OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp; `grep -n '"searchDevices"' ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp` returns nothing while the same grep against hs485d returns line 66.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Upheld, and I checked the one thing that could have overturned it. Two of the four sets are wrong, both in the direction that sends a call the HmIP daemon refuses: InterfacesSupportingConfigRestore includes HmIP-RF and InterfacesSupportingTeams includes HmIP-RF, and all three of those methods answer with NotImplementedException. The comment's smoke-detector rationale for Teams does not survive — HmIP smoke-detector grouping goes through the HmIP group/virtual-device path, not the legacy team methods.

I verified both method tables line by line rather than trusting the summary; every cited line number was exact, and I confirmed the negative halves directly: rfd contains no searchDevices symbol at all (not just an unregistered class), and hs485d contains no team or config-restore symbol. I also checked ExtendedLegacyServiceHandler's full override list to make sure none of the six is rescued by the subclass, and found the same six throwing in HMServer as well as HMIPServer, so the result does not depend on which server serves a given legacy interface.

The one counter-signal I found, and why it does not overturn: OpenCCU patch 0151-WebUI-Add-DeviceRestoreConfigButton gates the new Restore Config button on `$EASYLINKMODE == "false"` only — it is NOT interface-gated. (The `if {($iface != $HmIPIdentifier) && ($iface != $HmIPWIdentifier)}` line in the same hunk is pre-existing context belonging to the firmware-update block, not the restore gate.) So the OpenCCU WebUI does offer restore-config on HmIP devices. That is a WebUI bug, not evidence of support: the call lands on HMIPServer's throwing method, and devconfig.cgi's own `cmd_restore_config` is written to `catch` the failure and render a "failed" page. The daemon is authority over the button.

reachesDevice.title: The per-interface endpoint path rule (and the 'bare / crashes putParamset' claim) has no source
