reachesDevice.citation: HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT (= "/groups") and #DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT (= 9292); HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer (routes "/bidcos" and "/groups"; a routeWithRegex(".*") catch-all answers 404 "404 - page no exist" and closes the connection); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyApiServerUtil#startHttpServer (ServiceProperties.getInt("Legacy.Port", 2010), requestHandler = BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler, no Router); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle (reads only the body, never request.uri()); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:84-160 (readHeader parses only the BIN-RPC signature, Content-length and the HTTP version — the request URI is never extracted or compared); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:67,74,96,117 (_uri = "/RPC2" as the client-side default); witness ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/central/config.py:284 remote_path="/groups"
reachesDevice.finding:
The path VALUES are right; the stated REASON is false, and the two halves live on different servers.

(a) /groups for VirtualDevices — CONFIRMED at Tier 1. The 9292 service (HMServer) is the only CCU XML-RPC server that routes by path at all: BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer registers exactly "/bidcos" and "/groups", and Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT is the literal "/groups" with DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT 9292. So our /groups + 9292 pair matches the firmware.

(b) /RPC2 for the rest — CONFIRMED as harmless, not as required. rfd (2001) and hs485d (2000) run libXmlRpc's XmlRpcServerConnection, whose header parser never extracts a request URI (XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:84-160); it looks only for the BIN-RPC signature, "Content-length: " and "HTTP/1.0". The HmIP legacy surface on 2010 installs a bare requestHandler with no Router (LegacyApiServerUtil#startHttpServer) and BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle consumes the body without touching request.uri(). On 2000/2001/2010 the path is ignored entirely. /RPC2 is nonetheless the correct value to send: it is libXmlRpc's own client default (XmlRpcClient.cpp:67,74,96,117).

(c) 'POSTing to the bare "/" causes the CCU's putParamset handler to crash internally (Vert.x NPE or fault -5) while reads still succeed' — CONTRADICTED. On the one server where the path matters (9292), the catch-all route answers HTTP 404 with the body "404 - page no exist" and closes the connection, for every method — putParamset and getParamset alike. Reads do not 'still succeed'. On 2000/2001/2010 nothing dispatches on the path, so a bare "/" cannot select a different handler at all. The comment attributes a crash to a routing mechanism that either 404s uniformly or does not exist.

Boundary: keep the paths explicit — but because the 9422/9292 groups service 404s an unrouted path, not because any handler crashes. The Vert.x/fault -5 sentence is unsourced and should not be repeated as observed CCU behaviour.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong, BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer would have registered a different literal (or none) for the virtual-device surface, and Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT would have held something other than "/groups" — the check reads two independent firmware sites that could each have disagreed. For the crash claim the control is sharper: had the CCU really mishandled writes on "/", the 9292 router would have needed a route that accepts "/" and forwards to a dispatcher; instead the only non-/bidcos, non-/groups route is a 404-and-close terminal handler, which cannot produce 'reads still succeed'.
reachesDevice.ourValue: /RPC2 for all interfaces, /groups for VirtualDevices; comment: bare "/" crashes putParamset (Vert.x NPE or fault -5) while reads succeed
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: /groups + port 9292 confirmed (Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT, BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer). Bare "/" on 9292 = HTTP 404 "404 - page no exist" + connection close for every method. On 2000/2001/2010 the request URI is never read, so no path selects any handler.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD on substance, with two corrections; verdict stays narrowed.

I re-read every cited symbol rather than trusting the transcription. All eight check out verbatim: GROUP_CONTEXT is "/groups", DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT is 9292, initializeHttpServer registers exactly two exact-match routes plus a `.*` catch-all that 404s and closes, LegacyApiServerUtil installs a bare requestHandler with no Router, BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle touches only the body, XmlRpcClient defaults _uri to "/RPC2" at all four constructors, and readHeader contains no URI parse.

Correction 1 — the prose carries a port that exists in no source. The boundary sentence says "the 9422/9292 groups service". "9422" appears nowhere in the firmware, nowhere in our DetectionPorts (which pairs 9292 with TLS 49292), and nowhere in the aiohomematic witness. It must not be carried forward; a stray number inside an otherwise-verified grounding is exactly what gets quoted later as fact.

Correction 2 — (b) is stronger than "harmless" and should be stated as such. I verified that rfd's putParamset and getParamset are registered on the same libXmlRpc XmlRpcServer instance whose connection reads headers via XmlRpcServerConnection::readHeader. That parser walks the header buffer looking only for the BIN-RPC signature, "Content-length: ", "Connection: " and the header/body separator. The request line is never tokenised, so "POST / HTTP/1.1" and "POST /RPC2 HTTP/1.1" differ only in bytes that no comparison in the daemon ever touches. On 2000/2001/2010 the path cannot select a different handler, therefore it cannot select a *crashing* one. That is a proof, not an absence of evidence.

(c) stays contradicted, and I add the reason the comment is self-defeating: it claims reads succeed where writes crash. On 9292 the catch-all fires before any method name is decoded — the RPC body is never parsed — so getParamset and putParamset receive the identical 404 and a closed connection. There is no server among the four on which a path can make reads and writes diverge.

Keep the explicit paths. The justification in the comment should be: 9292 routes by path and 404s anything but /bidcos and /groups; 2000/2001/2010 ignore the path entirely and /RPC2 is libXmlRpc's own client default. Drop the Vert.x/NPE/fault -5 sentence — it is unsourced and, on the only path-routing server we talk to, refuted.

reachesDevice.title: The mixed-case-address rule rests on a comment claiming HmIP-RCV-1 is the only mixed-case address in a CCU's inventory
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFCentral.cpp:37 `serial="BidCoS-RF";` (type="HM-RCV-50" at :36); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Central.cpp:37 `serial="BidCoS-Wir";`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.VirtualRemoteControl (DEVICE_ID_BASE = "HmIP-RCV-", id = DEVICE_ID_BASE + vrcNr with vrcNr starting at 1 and incremented per instance; #isIdMatching uses this.id.equals(serial), a case-sensitive String.equals); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler (new VirtualRemoteControl(ap.getID(), ap.getAddress(), vertx) — one per access point); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException (DeviceNotFoundException -> faultCode -2, faultMessage "Invalid device"); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:591,593 `typedef std::map<std::string, RFDevice*> t_dev_instances; t_dev_instances dev_instances;`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:347-365 (GetInstance does dev_instances.find(dev_address) on that map); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:160,169 `throw XmlRpcException("Unknown instance", -2);`; HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.GroupVirtualDevice (GroupDeviceIdentifier = "INT") and de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.ip.IpVirtualDevice (DEVICE_DESCRIPTION_SERIAL_ADDRESS = "VIP", serial String.format("%s%07d", "VIP", n)) — both upper-case
reachesDevice.finding:
Two claims in the comment; the mechanism claim holds, the inventory claim does not.

Case sensitivity — CONFIRMED, on both south-bound daemons. rfd looks a device up by serial in a std::map<std::string, RFDevice*> (RFManager.h:591) via dev_instances.find (RFManager.cpp:356), i.e. byte-wise std::less<std::string>; a miss throws XmlRpcException("Unknown instance", -2) from RFManager.cpp:160 (getValue) / :169 (setValue). The HmIP legacy surface matches the virtual remote with this.id.equals(serial) (VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching) and maps the resulting DeviceNotFoundException to faultCode -2 / "Invalid device" (NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException). Note the fault TEXT our comment quotes is the HmIP one; rfd says "Unknown instance" for the same -2.

'HmIP-RCV-1 is the one mixed-case address in a CCU's inventory' — CONTRADICTED. There are at least three mixed-case address roots, one per south-bound daemon:
  • BidCoS-RF   — rfd's own central device (RFCentral.cpp:37)
  • BidCoS-Wir  — hs485d's central device (HS485Central.cpp:37)
  • HmIP-RCV-<n> — the HmIP virtual remote (VirtualRemoteControl.DEVICE_ID_BASE)
And the ordinal is not fixed: vrcNr starts at 1 and is incremented for each VirtualRemoteControl, one of which is constructed per access point in LegacyServiceHandler — a CCU with a second HmIP access point yields HmIP-RCV-2.

The rest of this repository already knows this: internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:41-43 lists all three roots, and internal/central/adapter/devices.go:56 names them too (with a typo, "BidCos-Wir" for the firmware's "BidCoS-Wir"). Only the mqtt_sink comment claims a set of one. The mechanism (case-insensitive registry scan) is unaffected and covers all three when the model knows them; what is wrong is the comment's justification, and by extension any future code that hard-codes {HmIP-RCV-1} as the exhaustive set — pkg-level lists that pin "HmIP-RCV-1" literally will miss HmIP-RCV-2 on a two-AP CCU.

The group/virtual pseudo-devices are not a further exposure: INT<id> (GroupVirtualDevice.GroupDeviceIdentifier) and VIP%07d (IpVirtualDevice) are both all-upper-case.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the case-sensitivity claim been wrong, rfd's lookup would have used a case-insensitive comparator (a strcasecmp-based map comparator or an upper-casing normaliser before find) and VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching would have used equalsIgnoreCase — the tree does use equalsIgnoreCase elsewhere (DeviceUtil, for "ALL_SMOKE_DETECTORS"), so the check could have come back the other way and did not. Had the 'only mixed-case address' claim been right, RFCentral.cpp and HS485Central.cpp would have assigned all-upper-case serials; both assign mixed-case literals.
reachesDevice.ourValue: comment: the virtual remote "HmIP-RCV-1" is the one mixed-case address in a CCU's inventory; wrong case faults with "Invalid device"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: three mixed-case roots — BidCoS-RF (rfd), BidCoS-Wir (hs485d), HmIP-RCV-<n> (HmIP, n from an incrementing counter, one VRC per access point). Fault on a case mismatch: rfd "Unknown instance" / -2; HmIP "Invalid device" / -2.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The two headline claims hold and I verified them independently. The ORDINAL MECHANISM the previous grounding offered is CONTRADICTED by the source, and its stated consequence does not follow.

What I confirmed. Case sensitivity, on both south-bound daemons: rfd resolves a serial through std::map<std::string,RFDevice*>::find (RFManager.cpp:356 on the map declared at RFManager.h:591-593), i.e. byte-wise std::less<std::string>, and a miss throws XmlRpcException("Unknown instance", -2) from GetValue (:160) and SetValue (:169). On the HmIP legacy surface I traced the actual write path rather than assuming it: LegacyServiceHandler#setValue takes the VRC branch only when isIdMatching passes, so a case-mismatched address falls through to DeviceUtil#setValue -> #getDeviceID, whose lookup is a case-sensitive map get followed by a case-sensitive endsWith scan, and which throws DeviceNotFoundException -> NotificationUtil -> -2 / "Invalid device". So the fault text our comment quotes is reachable, though by the generic device path, not by VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching as the previous grounding implied. Three mixed-case roots confirmed at the two C++ sites and the DEVICE_ID_BASE constant. INT/VIP are upper-case, so the pseudo-devices add no exposure.

What breaks. The previous grounding wrote: "one VRC per access point ... a CCU with a second HmIP access point yields HmIP-RCV-2", citing LegacyServiceHandler. The source says otherwise. There is exactly one `new VirtualRemoteControl(...)` in the entire HmIPServer tree, and its argument is AccessPointUtil.getFirstMasterAccessPoint(vertx) — a method that iterates the access-point map, breaks on the FIRST entry whose hasMaster() is false, and returns that one. No loop over access points exists. Adding a second HmIP access point therefore does not create a second virtual remote through this path.

What actually drives the ordinal — and why it is not answerable here. vrcNr is a private static Integer initialised to 1 and incremented once per VirtualRemoteControl construction, i.e. once per LegacyServiceHandler construction. Two workers construct one: LegacyAPIWorker#initializeService (new LegacyServiceHandler) and ExtendedLegacyAPIWorker#initializeService (new ExtendedLegacyServiceHandler, which extends LegacyServiceHandler). So within one process the second handler's virtual remote is named HmIP-RCV-2. Which of those two is reachable on the 2010 legacy port, and whether both workers are deployed on a stock CCU, is verticle-deployment configuration I cannot read out of the readable material. So the question our code actually cares about — "can an address other than HmIP-RCV-1 appear in a CCU inventory?" — is not settled by anything I found. It is not-performable from these sources, and the answer is certainly not "yes, via a second access point".

Tier 2 is silent here and cannot be promoted: I scanned all 2924 entries of ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json for an ADDRESS whose device part is neither all-upper nor all-lower and found zero — the corpus uses synthetic VCU* addresses and carries no real central or virtual-remote address at all.

Standing exposure, unchanged and real: internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:39-44 hard-codes the literal "HmIP-RCV-1" as an exhaustive member of virtualRemoteRoots. If any CCU ever presents HmIP-RCV-2, that entry silently fails to namespace it per central. The mechanism in mqtt_sink.go is not affected — it scans the registry case-insensitively and covers whatever roots the model knows. Also note internal/central/adapter/devices.go:56 spells the wired root "BidCos-Wir"; the firmware writes "BidCoS-Wir" (HS485Central.cpp:37). That is a comment, not a lookup key, so it is cosmetic — but it is the same class of error the rule is about.

reachesDevice.title: The auto-generated link name and description are written to the CCU with no length or charset check
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:413-430 (XmlRpcMethodAddLink: AddLink(params[0],params[1]) then, only if params.size()>=3, SetLinkInfo(params[0..3]); no validation of params[2]/params[3]); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:715-726 (RFChannel::SetLinkInfo — `it->second.name=name; it->second.description=description; RequestSave();`, no length or charset check, no truncation); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1154,1156 (SaveToXml: name -> the `link_name` XML attribute, description -> the `description` child node text); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LinkUtil#setLinkInfo (stores a LinkData verbatim into a HashMap keyed "%s:%02d-%s:%02d" and Jackson-serialises it to linkData.conf; no validation); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LinkData (name/description are plain Strings defaulting to ""); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LinkUtil#getLinkInfo and #getDefaultName (on a miss returns new LinkData(getDefaultName(...), "NO_DESCRIPTION") where getDefaultName = String.format("%s:%02d %s:%02d", ...)); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:126 (WebUI cmd_addLink calls addLink with two arguments only) and :150-152 (it calls setLinkInfo only `if { $description != "" || $name != "" }`); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/tools/devconfig.cgi:1040 (addLink with two arguments)
reachesDevice.finding:
The feared damage does not exist; a different, real divergence does.

Constraints — none, on either surface. rfd's addLink hands name and description straight to RFChannel::SetLinkInfo, which assigns them into the link_peers entry as std::string and requests a save (RFChannel.cpp:719-724). Nothing measures a length, filters a character set, truncates, or rejects. Persistence is XML (link_name attribute + description text node, RFChannel.cpp:1154-1156). The HmIP legacy surface is the same shape: LinkUtil#setLinkInfo puts a LinkData holding the two raw Strings into a map and Jackson-writes linkData.conf. So the hypothesis 'the firmware silently truncates or rejects' is contradicted — there is no code path that could.

What the firmware does differently is that it never writes a default at all. Both firmware-side callers pass addLink two arguments (ic_ifacecmd.cgi:126, devconfig.cgi:1040) and the WebUI reaches setLinkInfo only when the operator actually typed something (ic_ifacecmd.cgi:150-152). With nothing stored, the HmIP side synthesises on READ: LinkUtil#getLinkInfo returns getDefaultName = "%s:%02d %s:%02d" (a space, zero-padded two-digit channel indices, no arrow) and the literal description "NO_DESCRIPTION".

Our AddLink always writes, and writes a different shape: name = `<sender> -> <receiver>` (unpadded channel numbers, an arrow separator), description = `created by openccu-loom`. The consequence is on the same operator-visible surface — what getLinkInfo returns after an unnamed link creation — so a link we create is distinguishable from one the WebUI created, and an operator-blank name is stored as a value rather than left absent. Note the two defaults also differ in kind: ours is persisted (surviving into linkData.conf / the rfd XML), the firmware's is computed per read and disappears the moment a real name is set.

Surface caveat: getDefaultName/"NO_DESCRIPTION" is the HmIP legacy API's read-side synthesis. On rfd there is no equivalent synthesis — an unnamed link's entry simply carries empty strings — so the firmware's two south-bound surfaces are not even consistent with each other. Matching either is a product decision, not a firmware constraint; what is settled is that no constraint exists to violate.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had a length or charset limit existed, RFChannel::SetLinkInfo would have had to compare a size or copy into a fixed buffer before assigning (the same file does exactly that for numeric fields — `char buffer[16]` + snprintf in SaveToXml at RFChannel.cpp:1123), and LinkUtil#setLinkInfo would have had to validate before constructing LinkData. Both assign the caller's string unconditionally, so a limit would have been visible at the one place it could live. Had our concern about the empty-name path been unfounded, ic_ifacecmd.cgi would have computed and sent a name; instead it explicitly skips setLinkInfo when both fields are blank.
reachesDevice.ourValue: name = "<sender> -> <receiver>" (unpadded channels), description = "created by openccu-loom", always written
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: no length or charset constraint anywhere; nothing is written when the caller supplies no name. HmIP read-side default: name = String.format("%s:%02d %s:%02d", ...) (space-separated, zero-padded channel indices), description = "NO_DESCRIPTION".
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The half that matters for the audited concern is CONFIRMED and I re-verified it end to end. The supporting narrative is CONTRADICTED on the HmIP surface.

Confirmed — no constraint exists to violate. I followed rfd's write path from the RPC method to persistence: XmlRpcMethodAddLink -> RFManager::SetLinkInfo -> RFChannel::SetLinkInfo, which assigns two std::strings into the link_peers entry and requests a save; then SaveToXml writes name as an XML attribute and description as a child text node. There is no length measurement, no character filter, no truncation, no rejection at any of the four hops. The HmIP side is the same shape: LinkUtil#setLinkInfo puts a LinkData holding the raw Strings into a map and Jackson-serialises it. The hypothesis that the firmware silently truncates or rejects a long or non-ASCII link name is refuted — no code path could.

Contradicted — "the firmware never writes a default at all". The previous grounding built its whole divergence story on the premise that both firmware callers pass addLink two arguments, therefore nothing is stored, therefore the HmIP side synthesises getDefaultName/"NO_DESCRIPTION" on read. I checked what a 2-argument call actually becomes on the HmIP legacy surface and the premise fails.

XmlRpcParser#parseParams sizes its argument array from the TARGET METHOD's parameter count, not from the number of <param> elements on the wire, and fills only as many as the document supplies. Omitted trailing parameters arrive as Java null; the reflective invoke in AnnotationAwareRpcHandler#execute therefore succeeds rather than throwing on arity. So the WebUI's two-argument addLink reaches LegacyServiceHandler#addLink as addLink(sender, receiver, null, null) — and that method, on success, calls DeviceUtil.setLinkInfo(..., null, null) with no guard. LinkUtil#setLinkInfo then stores `new LinkData(null, null)` under both directional keys and saves linkData.conf.

Consequence: on HmIP the firmware DOES write on every addLink, and getLinkInfo subsequently finds that entry and returns nulls. getDefaultName and "NO_DESCRIPTION" are reached only for links with NO stored entry — links predating linkData.conf, or ones whose entry removeLinkInfo/removeAllLinkInfo deleted. They are not what an operator sees after creating a link through the WebUI. The "firmware value" column of the original finding is wrong on both halves.

What survives as the real divergence, restated per surface:
  - rfd (2000/2001): the `params.size()>=3` guard means a 2-argument addLink never calls SetLinkInfo, so the link_peers entry keeps its default-constructed empty strings, and GetLinkInfo returns them verbatim — I confirmed rfd has no read-side synthesis at all. Our AddLink always sends four arguments, so we store "A:1 -> B:2" / "created by openccu-loom" where the WebUI would have left ""/"".
  - HmIP (2010): both write. The firmware writes nulls, we write our synthesized strings.
Either way the operator-visible read-back differs, so the boundary conclusion (a link we create is distinguishable from a WebUI one; an operator-blank name becomes a stored value) stands — but not for the reason given, and the getDefaultName shape must not be cited as "what the firmware leaves for an unnamed link".

One further caveat the original left out: RFChannel::SaveToXml passes the name straight into addAttributeConst and the description into addTextConst. Whether that path escapes XML metacharacters is not something I established, so a link name containing a quote or an angle bracket is an open question — irrelevant for our generated name, which is ASCII address text, but relevant for an operator-supplied one that we forward unchanged.

reachesDevice.title: DefaultBaseTemperature 18.0 is written into the device's unused slots
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:1017-1023 `<parameter id="TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1">` … `<logical type="float" min="5.0" max="30.0" default="17.0" unit="°C"/>`; same file :1077-1092 `<parameter id="ENDTIME_MONDAY_5">` `<logical type="integer" min="5" max="1440" default="1440" unit="minutes"/>` and `<parameter id="TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_5">` `<logical type="float" min="5.0" max="30.0" default="17.0" unit="°C"/>` (slots 5..13 all default 1440 / 17.0; only the comfort points 2 and 4 default to 21.0); same pattern in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml and rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml (TEMPERATURE_*_13 default="17.0"); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues — `int endTime = 1440; double temperature = 17.0;` with overrides only for _1 (endTime 360), _2 (21.0 / 540 or 1320), _3 (endTime 1020), _4 (21.0 / 1320); #createWeekProgram builds each ConfigurationParameter with that default and bounds 5.0 / 30.0; witness ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:2579 `DEFAULT_CLIMATE_FILL_TEMPERATURE: Final = 18.0`
reachesDevice.finding:
CONTRADICTED, on both climate surfaces, by 1.0 K.

Our constant is 18.0 and it does not stay read-side: RawToClimate stores it as the weekday's BaseTemperature, climateWeekdayToSlotsExpand fills every gap with it (rawconvert.go:396, :407) and fillUpWeekdaySlots pads the remaining slots to 13 with EndTime "24:00" and that same temperature (slot.go:121-133). Those padding slots are exactly the case the firmware declares a default for.

Classic BidCos (HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU): the padding slots — ENDTIME_<DAY>_5..13, whose own default is 1440 minutes, i.e. 24:00 — declare `default="17.0"` on TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_5..13, bounds min 5.0 / max 30.0 (rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:1077-1092 and the parallel blocks through slot 13). The factory profile is 17.0 at points 1 and 3, 21.0 at points 2 and 4, then 17.0 for every unused slot.

HmIP: ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues opens with `int endTime = 1440; double temperature = 17.0;` and overrides only points 1..4; every other slot of every weekday of every profile gets 17.0 / 1440, with the same 5.0/30.0 bounds. Byte-for-byte the same rule as the BidCos XML.

So the firmware's fill setpoint for an unconfigured climate slot is 17.0 °C; ours is 18.0 °C. A load-then-save on a weekday the reader could not decode writes 18.0 into slots the device would otherwise hold at 17.0 — a 1 K error written into the thermostat's MASTER paramset, on both transports.

The comment's own justification is accurate about provenance and wrong about authority: 18.0 is the Python reference's DEFAULT_CLIMATE_FILL_TEMPERATURE (aiohomematic/const.py:2579 — Tier 3, a witness), not a CCU value. Tier 1 and Tier 2 agree with each other and disagree with it. Our code should follow 17.0.

One boundary worth stating: the firmware value is a parameter DEFAULT (what the device declares and reverts to), while ours is a runtime fallback for an undecodable weekday. Those are the same role — 'what an unconfigured slot holds' — which is why the comparison is on the right surface; but the honest fix is to prefer the per-device declared DEFAULT read from the paramset description at runtime, and to use 17.0 only as the constant when no descriptor is at hand. Every shipped descriptor I checked declares 17.0, so the constant and the descriptor agree today.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had 18.0 been the firmware's value, TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_5..13 in rf_cc_rt_dn.xml would have read default="18.0" and ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues would have initialised `temperature = 18.0`. The check is capable of returning 18.0 — the same files do carry a second, different default (21.0) for the comfort points, so the extraction distinguishes values rather than reporting one constant everywhere. Both independent sources returned 17.0.
reachesDevice.ourValue: 18.0 °C (schedule.DefaultBaseTemperature), written into every gap and every padding slot 1..13
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: 17.0 °C — TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_5..13 default="17.0" (ENDTIME default 1440), bounds 5.0/30.0, in rf_cc_rt_dn.xml / rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml; and `double temperature = 17.0; int endTime = 1440;` in ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues on the HmIP side
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The firmware number is CONFIRMED — I re-derived it by machine scan rather than trusting the quoted line range, and it is 17.0 at every padding ordinal on both surfaces. But three qualifications shrink the finding, and the middle one matters most.

(1) 18.0 is a failure fallback, not the normal fill. The original states our value as "18.0, written into every gap and every padding slot 1..13". That overstates. DefaultBaseTemperature has exactly two production readers (climate.go:304 and :333), both inside IdentifyBaseTemperature / IdentifyBaseTemperatureFromSegments, and both fire only when the weekday yields no usable stretch. On every normal round-trip the fill is cwd.BaseTemperature = the temperature that actually dominates the day as read off the device, and 18.0 never appears. So the exposure is the degenerate case — an empty or undecodable weekday map — not the ordinary load-then-save the original implies.

(2) The comparand is a DECLARED DEFAULT, not device state. The original's boundary paragraph names this and its own damage sentence then crosses it: "writes 18.0 into slots the device would otherwise hold at 17.0". A `default=` attribute in the type XML, and ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory's `temperature`, are what getParamsetDescription advertises as DEFAULT and what a factory reset restores. Neither tells us what a given thermostat currently holds in slot 9 — that is whatever was last written to it. The honest statement is: our fallback disagrees with the value the descriptor declares for those slots by 1.0 K. Whether that constitutes a 1 K error written into a device depends on what the device held, which no descriptor can answer.

(3) 17.0 is ordinal-dependent. The original generalises to "the firmware's fill setpoint for an unconfigured climate slot is 17.0". Ordinals 5..13 do declare 17.0 uniformly — 63 parameters on HM-CC-RT-DN, 189 on HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU, all with min 5.0 / max 30.0 — but ordinal 2 declares 21.0 on all seven days and ordinal 4 declares 21.0 on the five weekdays. Our fill is applied to gaps as well as to padding, and a gap fill can land at ordinal 2 or 4. So the comparison is exact for the padding slots and not for a gap that lands early.

One citation hygiene note. "TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_5..13 ... in rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml" is right in substance and wrong as written: the identifiers in that file are P1_/P2_/P3_-prefixed. A reader following the citation with a literal grep finds nothing (I did, first pass). The HmIP factory names them the same way. Also, the original's paraphrase of getDefaultValues ("overrides only for _1, _2, _3, _4") flattens a real branch — SATURDAY/SUNDAY and week programs 2 and 3 override only _1 and _2, which is exactly why the XML shows 17.0 at ordinal 4 on two of seven days.

Provenance is correct and worth keeping: 18.0 is the Python reference's DEFAULT_CLIMATE_FILL_TEMPERATURE (Tier 3, a witness), and Tier 1 and Tier 2 both say 17.0. The recommendation to prefer the per-parameter DEFAULT read from the paramset description at runtime, with a constant only as last resort, is the right shape — and the descriptor does carry DEFAULT, so it is performable.

reachesDevice.title: XML-RPC bodies are transcoded to ISO-8859-1 unconditionally, so a non-Latin-1 device name fails the whole call
reachesDevice.ourValue: charmap.ISO8859_1 encoder on every outbound body, prolog encoding="ISO-8859-1", Content-Type charset=ISO-8859-1; a rune above U+00FF fails at encode time
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: ISO-8859-1 on all three south-bound XML-RPC surfaces, and the declared encoding is never read: BidCos parses the body as raw bytes; HmIP and VirtualDevices force a configured encoding into the StAX reader, overriding the prolog
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1, BidCos (rfd :2001→:32001, hs485d :2000→:32000, both libXmlRpc): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:24 and :414 (emits <?xml version="1.0" encoding="iso-8859-1"?> and Content-Type: text/xml; charset=iso-8859-1); XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:366, :388, :414 (same on the server side); XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:105-112 (readHeader scans only for "Content-length: ", "Connection: " and the header terminator — the charset parameter and the request URI are never read); XmlRpcUtil.cpp:135-144 and :217 (nextTagIs / xmlDecode operate on std::string bytes; the prolog is skipped as an ordinary tag, its encoding attribute never inspected). Tree-wide grep for "encoding|charset" in libXmlRpc yields three hits, all emission sites, none in a parse path. VirtualDevices (:9292→:39292): HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer constructs both RpcMessageHandlers with the literal "ISO-8859-1". HmIP-RF (:2010→:32010): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.AbstractLegacyAPIWorker reads the encoding from ServiceProperties key "Legacy.Encoding" (code default "UTF-8") and passes it to HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRequestResponseProcessor#parseRequest → XmlRpcParser, whose constructor calls XMLInputFactory#createXMLStreamReader(InputStream, String) — the two-argument form, which takes the encoding from the caller and does not consult the XML declaration. The shipped value is pinned by ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:15 "Legacy.Encoding=ISO-8859-1" (same file, :25, pins Legacy.Port=32010, which is exactly the proxy target in ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/lighttpd/conf.d/webui_remoteapi.conf:74).
reachesDevice.finding: Confirmed, and the firmware is stronger than the comment claims: not one of the three surfaces reads the encoding we declare. On BidCos the parser is a hand-written byte scanner — a UTF-8 body would not be *rejected*, it would be accepted and stored byte-for-byte, then rendered as Latin-1 downstream. That is silent corruption, which is worse than the encode-time error we produce. On HmIP and VirtualDevices the declared encoding is overridden by a configured constant before the first byte is decoded. So sending a UTF-8-declared body buys nothing anywhere and corrupts on one surface; our unconditional transcode is the right behaviour, and the failure on a rune above U+00FF is the CCU's own representational ceiling, not a self-inflicted restriction. Which source to follow: Tier 1, the firmware constant — not any per-request declaration, because none is read. One boundary worth recording: on the HmIP surface alone the encoding is a *configuration* value, not a compiled-in one. Its code default is UTF-8; only the shipped crRFD.conf overrides it to ISO-8859-1. An operator who edits Legacy.Encoding=UTF-8 in /etc/config/crRFD.conf would make our bodies mis-decode for every byte ≥ 0x80 on HmIP-RF while BidCos and VirtualDevices stayed correct. OpenCCU does not ship that, and nothing in our config surface exposes it — but it is the one configuration under which this rule is false, and it belongs in the comment.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had any surface honoured the declared encoding, it would show as an inspection of the prolog or the Content-Type charset in a parse path — libXmlRpc has three encoding/charset occurrences and all three are writes, none a read — and HMIPServer would call the one-argument XMLInputFactory#createXMLStreamReader(InputStream), which lets StAX auto-detect from the declaration; it calls the two-argument form instead. The check distinguishes the cases: the two-argument form is exactly the API shape that ignores the prolog, and the one-argument form is exactly the shape that honours it.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
The rule itself is confirmed and every citation reproduces verbatim; I am demoting to narrowed because the finding's stated boundary is half wrong and its load-bearing step is not a firmware reading.

Upheld: the outbound leg. Not one of the three surfaces reads the encoding we declare on a request — BidCos by byte-scanning (readHeader never touches the charset parameter; findTag/nextTagIs skip the prolog as an ordinary tag), HmIP and VirtualDevices by forcing a configured constant into the reader. Our unconditional transcode is right, and the failure above U+00FF is the CCU's representational ceiling.

Narrowing 1 — the leg the finding omits. The response/notification direction is NOT symmetric. HMIPServer's XmlRpcSerializer opens every request and response with `writeStartDocument(encoding, "1.0")`, so the CCU declares its configured encoding on the wire, and our decoder honours declarations (message.go:188-192, `d.CharsetReader = charset.NewReaderLabel`). Inbound is therefore correct under any Legacy.Encoding. The prior finding's operator scenario ("our bodies mis-decode for every byte ≥ 0x80 on HmIP-RF") is true only outbound, and the comment should say which direction it governs.

Narrowing 2 — a convention smuggled into the boundary. "The two-argument form takes the encoding from the caller and does not consult the XML declaration" was not read from any eQ-3 source; it is a property of the StAX implementation. If it were false, an operator setting Legacy.Encoding=UTF-8 would still decode our ISO-8859-1 bodies correctly, because our prolog says ISO-8859-1 — and the boundary would evaporate. That sub-claim is unverified in those words, and only Tier-1 evidence about the shipped JRE's XMLInputFactory, or a wire test against a CCU with Legacy.Encoding=UTF-8, would settle it. The rule's main body does not depend on it.

Two transcription corrections. (i) "Tree-wide grep for encoding|charset in libXmlRpc yields three hits" is wrong: there are five emission sites (client 24, 414; serverconnection 366, 388, 414) plus three unrelated comment hits in XmlRpcValue.cpp:907,1318 and XmlRpcUtil.cpp:207. The conclusion — none in a parse path — is correct. (ii) "a UTF-8 body would be accepted byte-for-byte and rendered as Latin-1 downstream" is an inference from the byte-scanner's shape, not a measurement; it should be labelled as such.

One genuine addition for the comment: the shipped HmIP config also pins the *outbound* encoding — LegacyNotificationHandler reads the same Legacy.Encoding for what it sends us — so a single operator edit moves both legs at once.

reachesDevice.title: The per-interface XML-RPC default paths (/RPC2, /groups) are documented in config but sourced nowhere
reachesDevice.site: internal/config/config.go:67-70 (RemotePath doc); the real table is internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:1567-1580
reachesDevice.ourValue: "/RPC2" for HmIP-RF / BidCos-RF / BidCos-Wired, "/groups" for VirtualDevices, described as the path each interface serves XML-RPC on
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: /RPC2 is the CCU's XML-RPC *client-side* default URI, not a server route. Three of the four interfaces ignore the request path entirely; only VirtualDevices routes by path, where /groups (and /bidcos) are real routes and anything else gets HTTP 404 with the connection closed. All four external ports are lighttpd reverse proxies selected by $SERVER["socket"] — by port, never by path.
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:67, :74, :96, :117 (_uri = "/RPC2" whenever the target URL carries no path — this is the client default; a tree-wide grep for "RPC2" over ../OpenCCU-Base matches this one file and nothing else); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:105-112 (readHeader parses only Content-length, Connection and the header terminator; the request URI is never stored or compared — this is the server for both rfd/BidCos-RF and hs485d/BidCos-Wired); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyApiServerUtil#startHttpServer (installs a bare requestHandler on Legacy.Port, default 2010, with no Router) feeding HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle (forwards the body on the event bus; the path is not read); HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer (route("/bidcos") and route("/groups") on the HM server port, plus a routeWithRegex(".*") catch-all returning 404 and closing the connection) with HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT = "/groups", #BIDCOS_CONTEXT = "/bidcos", #DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT = 9292; ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/lighttpd/conf.d/webui_remoteapi.conf:70 (:2010→:32010), :94 (:9292→:39292), :118 (:2001→:32001), :142 (:2000→:32000) — every rule keyed on $SERVER["socket"] with proxy.server = ( "" => … ), i.e. all paths forwarded unchanged.
reachesDevice.finding: Our table works, and it agrees with the client code it documents (config.go:67-70 matches ccu_wiring.go:1572-1575 exactly — the doc comment is not drifting from the implementation). But the framing — "which URL path each CCU interface serves XML-RPC on" — is only a real constraint for one of the four. /RPC2 is not a route anywhere in the CCU: it is the default URI libXmlRpc fills in when an outbound URL has no path, which is why every Homematic client has used it for twenty years. On BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired the server never looks at the request line's URI at all; on HmIP-RF the legacy XML-RPC server is a bare Vert.x requestHandler with no Router, so any path reaches the handler. VirtualDevices is the exception and the boundary: HMServer registers /groups and /bidcos and terminates everything else with a 404 and a connection close, so a wrong remote_path there takes the interface down hard — which is why reachesDevice is true: nothing written to a group or virtual device reaches the CCU. Two things an operator reading this comment should be told and currently is not: (a) an override on the three /RPC2 interfaces cannot break routing, because there is no routing — the failure mode the comment warns about does not exist there; (b) on VirtualDevices there is a second XML-RPC surface, /bidcos, on the same port, which our table does not mention. Also worth recording for the operator-facing rationale: the CCU already *is* the reverse-proxied case the comment imagines — every port we connect to (2000/2001/2010/9292 and their 4xxxx TLS twins) is lighttpd forwarding to a 3xxxx internal port, and lighttpd selects on the socket, not the path.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the three /RPC2 interfaces routed by path, a comparison of the request URI against "/RPC2" would exist on a server path; the tree-wide grep over ../OpenCCU-Base finds "RPC2" in XmlRpcClient.cpp only, and LegacyApiServerUtil passes no Router. The control fires the other way for VirtualDevices, which is what makes it a control rather than an absence argument: there the route literal, the Constants entry and the 404 catch-all are all present and all found by the same searches.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
Narrowed, upheld — every citation reproduces exactly, including the four lighttpd line numbers and the fact that "RPC2" appears in precisely one file in the whole tree. The framing correction stands: /RPC2 is a client default, not a route; the failure mode the comment warns about exists only on VirtualDevices, where a wrong path yields 404 + connection close and takes the interface down; and /bidcos is a second XML-RPC surface on that same port that our table omits.

What the prior agent missed, and it is the more consequential half of the same comment block: config.go:72-73 also asserts that "the bare '/' is rejected because POSTing to it crashes the CCU's putParamset handler", ccu_wiring.go:1569-1571 elaborates it as "Vert.x NPE or fault -5 while reads still succeed", and config.go:154 ships it to operators as a validation error string ("the CCU's putParamset handler crashes on it; name the real endpoint path"). No Tier-1 surface supports that mechanism. On BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired the request URI is never read (XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:103-114), so no path can select a different handler and "/" is indistinguishable from "/RPC2". On HmIP-RF the legacy server has no Router at all, so "/" reaches BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle unchanged. On VirtualDevices — the only Vert.x surface that routes, and therefore the only place the named mechanism could live — "/" falls to `routeWithRegex(".*")`, which returns 404 and closes the connection: not a crash, not a fault -5, and reads do not survive it either. So the stated mechanism is contradicted on all four surfaces; whether some empirical crash was once observed I cannot rule out, and that residue is unverified. As written the comment names a cause that cannot occur and a symptom asymmetry (writes break, reads succeed) that the routing surface does not produce. The validator's behaviour may well be worth keeping; its stated reason is not.

Also worth recording for the operator-facing rationale, and correct as the prior agent had it: the CCU already is the reverse-proxied case the comment imagines — 2000/2001/2010/9292 and their 4xxxx TLS twins are all lighttpd forwarding to 3xxxx internal ports, selected on the socket, never the path.

reachesDevice.title: The central-link eligible-interface set is a comment-justified literal
reachesDevice.citation: BidCos-RF: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:714-724 registers `reportValueUsage` → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:1132-1139 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1425-1450, which on total_count>0 does `AddLinkPeer(central_device->GetListenerChannel()->GetSerial(), false)` and on 0 `LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(central_address, central_channel)`. BidCos-Wired: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:511-520 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:680-686 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Channel.cpp:409-430, same AddLinkPeer/RemoveLinkPeer against the central listener channel. Both gate first on `if(!GetDescription()->GetAutoregisterCentral())return true;` (RFChannel.cpp:1427, HS485Channel.cpp:411). HmIP-RF: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage (persists the per-address metadata key "reportValueUsageData" and forwards to the backend; throws on a null refCounter). VirtualDevices: HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.rega.IRegaServer#reportValueUsage, annotated @RpcMethod("reportValueUsage"), implemented by HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.rega.VirtualDeviceHandlerRega#reportValueUsage as an unconditional `return true;`. Virtual remote: LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage short-circuits with `return true` when the VirtualRemoteControl is enabled and the address matches it. Operator surface: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0171-WebUI-Add-HmIPKeyTransceiverCentralLinkConfiguration/occu/WebUI/www/webui/webui.js:198 (buttons rendered only for channelType KEY_TRANSCEIVER, KEY, MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER) and :15625,15627,15639-15643 (KEY_TRANSCEIVER|MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER → interface "HmIP-RF"; KEY → interface "BidCos-RF"; create raises PRESS_SHORT only, remove zeroes PRESS_SHORT and PRESS_LONG). RPC plumbing: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/reportvalueusage.tcl:19.
reachesDevice.finding: The three interfaces we accept all implement reportValueUsage with real device-side effect — rfd and hs485d both add/remove the central listener channel as a link peer, the HmIP legacy API persists reportValueUsageData and forwards — so the positive half of the set is confirmed on Tier 1. Two corrections to the reason and the justification. (1) VirtualDevices does NOT reject the call: its XML-RPC surface declares reportValueUsage (@RpcMethod on IRegaServer) and the implementation returns true unconditionally. Excluding it yields the right user-visible outcome (nothing would happen), but our token "interface_unsupported" and the comment "VirtualDevices and CUxD do not participate in CCU link management / use a different event dispatch path" state something the firmware contradicts in the letter — the CCU accepts and silently no-ops. (2) CUxD is a third-party add-on and appears nowhere in the CCU source trees; its half of the set is tier1-silent and rests on nothing I could read. Two boundaries the reader should know: the CCU's own central-link UI is one interface narrower than us — it never offers the buttons for BidCos-Wired, hard-coding "BidCos-RF" for channelType KEY and "HmIP-RF" for KEY_TRANSCEIVER/MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER — although hs485d does implement the call, so our wider set is defensible rather than wrong. And both BidCos daemons short-circuit on the channel description's AUTOREGISTER flag (`GetAutoregisterCentral()`), returning true with no effect; our eligibility filter uses press-event presence only, so CentralLinksStatus can report a channel eligible whose reportValueUsage is a firmware no-op. The virtual-remote conjunct is confirmed for HmIP-RF by the LegacyServiceHandler short-circuit; I found no equivalent guard for HM-RCV-50 / HMW-RCV-50 in rfd or hs485d, so that part of the model filter stays ungrounded.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had BidCos-Wired lacked the concept, src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp would not register a `reportValueUsage` method at all (it registers it at :639) or HS485Channel::ReportValueUsage would be the base-class `return true` stub from HS485LogicalInstance.h:40 — instead it is overridden with a real AddLinkPeer/RemoveLinkPeer body. Had VirtualDevices genuinely lacked it, IRegaServer would carry no @RpcMethod("reportValueUsage") entry — I read the full interface and it does, next to addLink/removeLink/getLinks. For CUxD the check cannot produce a different answer either way: nothing about CUxD exists in these trees.
reachesDevice.ourValue: eligible = {BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, HmIP-RF}; VirtualDevices and CUxD → reason "interface_unsupported" ("no concept of CCU press-event link management")
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF / BidCos-Wired / HmIP-RF: real link-peer effect (AUTOREGISTER-gated). VirtualDevices: method declared and accepted, `return true;` no-op. CUxD: not present in the CCU sources. CCU's own UI: only BidCos-RF and HmIP-RF, dispatched by channel type.
reachesDevice.missingInput: CUxD's XML-RPC surface — the add-on is not part of OpenCCU-Base/OpenCCU, so whether it implements reportValueUsage cannot be settled from Tier 1 or Tier 2 here.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: The prior verdict (narrowed) is right but its boundary is in the wrong place, and its positive half does not survive. Where it holds: BidCos-RF and HmIP-RF do carry real device-side effect, and I re-read every line to confirm the chain — rfd adds/removes the central listener channel as a link peer, and the HmIP legacy handler is stronger than cited, calling DeviceUtil.createCentralLink / deleteCentralLink on the summed ref counter rather than merely persisting metadata. Where it breaks: the prior finding wrote "the three interfaces we accept all implement reportValueUsage with real device-side effect", which takes "implements the method" for "has effect". Both BidCos daemons return true before touching anything when the channel description's `autoregister` attribute is false, and that attribute is not a runtime property — it is a literal in the shipped device-type XML, defaulting to false in the schema and in both daemons' constructors, with no other writer. Counting it: 0 of 40 channel declarations across all 15 shipped hs485types XMLs carry `autoregister="true"`. So on BidCos-Wired, HS485Channel::ReportValueUsage is a no-op for every wired device type this firmware ships. Our set includes an interface on which the operation cannot do anything, and central_links.go will report success. That is exactly why the CCU's own UI never offers the button for BidCos-Wired — the 0171 dispatch hard-codes HmIP-RF and BidCos-RF only — so the WebUI's narrowness is not an oversight to be shrugged off, it matches the descriptors. On BidCos-RF the gate bites too, though far less: 29 of 34 KEY channel declarations are armed, so 5 declarations in 2 files (rf_em_8.xml, rf_em_8_bit.xml, rf_st_6_sh.xml among the armed) sit the other way; our eligibility filter uses press-event presence only and cannot see the attribute at all, because the XML-RPC device description does not export it. Two prior corrections upheld unchanged: VirtualDevices does NOT reject the call (IRegaServer declares it, VirtualDeviceHandlerRega returns true unconditionally), so the token "interface_unsupported" and the comment "do not participate in CCU link management / use a different event dispatch path" are contradicted in the letter even though the user-visible outcome is right; and CUxD is a third-party add-on with no trace in either tree, so its half of the set is tier1-silent and rests on nothing readable. One prior gap I can close in our favour: the virtual-remote conjunct is groundable after all. The virtual remotes ARE the central device — RFCentral.cpp:36 names HM-RCV-50 — and rf_central.xml / hmw_central.xml carry no `autoregister` on any channel, so reportValueUsage on a virtual-remote VIRTUAL_KEY channel returns true with no effect, the same outcome our filter produces; HmIP-RCV-50 is settled independently by the LegacyServiceHandler VirtualRemoteControl short-circuit. The exact three-model set in pkg/hmenum/device_model.go:21-25 is therefore grounded on Tier 1 across all three bus families (hm_autoconf:112-122 and ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi:281-283 enumerate the same three), not just for HmIP.

reachesDevice.title: setInstallMode's third positional argument is overloaded between device address and mode on a comment alone
reachesDevice.ourValue: `setInstallMode(on, time, deviceAddress)` when an address is given, else `setInstallMode(on, time, mode)`; comment claims this holds for "BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired".
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: rfd: `setInstallMode(bool on [, int seconds [, {int mode | string serial}]])` — exactly as we do it, third slot type-dispatched. hs485d: the method does not exist. HMIPServer legacy: `setInstallMode(Boolean, Integer, String)` — third slot String-only, no int-mode form.
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:589 (doc: "void setInstallMode(Boolean on, Integer seconds)"), :602 (registration), :606-609 (`InstallModes mode = INSTALL_NORMAL;`, `if(params.size()>=2)time=params[1]; else time=60;`), :610 `if(params.size()>=3)`, :612-613 (`params[2].getType() == XmlRpcValue::TypeInt` and the range check `>= INSTALL_OFF && <= INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG`), :621-623 (`else if(params[2].getType() == XmlRpcValue::TypeString) { … SetInstallMode(INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST, time, params[2]); return; }`), :634. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:562 `enum{INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME=600};`; RFManager.cpp:565-570 (whitelist branch throws "Device serial number must not be empty." on empty serial), :582-583 (clamp to 600). hs485d method registrations: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:48-601 (26 methods; setInstallMode absent, pairing is :66 `searchDevices`). Working CCU callers: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/setinstallmode.tcl (`xmlrpc $interface(URL) setInstallMode [list bool $on]` — one arg), ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_add_device.cgi:903. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.IServiceApi#setInstallMode and de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#setInstallMode (signature `(Boolean on, Integer time, String address)`, defaults time to 60 when null), plus #setInstallModeWithWhitelist(Boolean, Integer, RpcStruct[]).
reachesDevice.finding: The signature the bundle feared — `(on, time, mode, address)` — does not exist anywhere. rfd reads at most params[2] and dispatches on its XML-RPC type: TypeInt selects a mode (range-checked 0..2, anything else faults -1), TypeString is taken as the device serial and forces INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST. Our two branches are therefore exactly right for BidCos-RF, and the security scenario in the bundle (address landing in the mode slot, unrestricted window) is refuted. Two boundaries the comment crosses, though. (1) BidCos-Wired: hs485d registers no setInstallMode at all — the CCU's own wired pairing is `searchDevices` — yet `hmenum.InterfacesSupportingInstallMode` (pkg/hmenum/interface.go:190-194) includes InterfaceBidCosWired, so `WireInstallModeDPs` (internal/central/adapter/install_mode.go:104-106) creates an install-mode DP for it and every enable/disable is an XML-RPC call to a method hs485d does not implement. (2) On the HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface the third slot is declared `String` only; our int-mode branch would not type-map there. Our code never reaches it (HmIP-RF is routed to Interface.setInstallModeHMIP via JSON-RPC, which matches the WebUI's own caller in www/api/methods/interface/setinstallmodehmip.tcl), but the comment's blanket wording does. Two side facts worth carrying: seconds defaults to 60 when omitted and is silently clamped to 600 (INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME); with `on == false` rfd ignores params[1]/params[2] entirely and sets INSTALL_OFF.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong I would have found either a read of `params[3]` in XmlRpcMethodSetInstallMode::execute, or a params[2] handled only as TypeInt with the address carried elsewhere. Neither appears; the whole method body is 30 lines and reads params[0..2] only. For the wired half, had hs485d implemented the method it would appear among the 26 `XmlRpcServerMethod("…", s)` registrations in src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp — it does not, and a case-insensitive grep for install_mode/installmode over src/hs485d returns nothing.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD on the BidCos-RF surface, with the bundle's own HmIP parenthetical REFUTED. What I re-read line by line and confirm verbatim: rfd reads at most params[2]; TypeInt selects a mode range-checked to 0..2 (anything else faults -1); TypeString is taken as the serial and forces INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST; with on==false params[1]/[2] are never read and time stays 0, which drives SetInstallMode into the INSTALL_OFF branch that also clears the whitelist serial; seconds defaults to 60 and is clamped to 600. The feared `(on, time, mode, address)` form exists nowhere. Boundary (1) UPHELD and strengthened: hs485d registers no setInstallMode (26 methods; the sibling grep in src/rfd finds 51 registrations including it), and the CCU's own Add-Device page pairs BidCos-Wired with `wir_search()` — a search, not an install mode — while `hmenum.InterfacesSupportingInstallMode` (pkg/hmenum/interface.go:190-194) includes InterfaceBidCosWired, so WireInstallModeDPs (internal/central/adapter/install_mode.go:104-106) still mints an install-mode DP whose every enable/disable is an XML-RPC call to a method hs485d does not implement. Boundary (2) is where the bundle's grounding BREAKS. It wrote that our HmIP route "matches the WebUI's own caller in setinstallmodehmip.tcl". It does not. methods.conf requires `address` as an argument, but the wrapper only uses it in the LOCAL branch; our CcuBackend hard-codes `installMode: "ALL"` (ccu_extended.go:92) and in the ALL branch the Tcl calls `setInstallMode [list bool $on] [list int $time]` — two arguments, `address` silently discarded. Consequence: on HmIP-RF, installModeWriter.SetInstallModeForDevice and DeviceAdminDomain.SetInstallMode open an UNSCOPED broadcast pairing window while the operator surface says the window is scoped to one device. The bundle's third boundary is therefore an unqualified "the address never reaches the HmIP daemon", not just "the comment's wording overreaches". Separately, the bundle's "working CCU caller" setinstallmode.tcl is not registered in methods.conf and is unreachable over the JSON-RPC API — the live callers are the CGIs, all one-argument.

reachesDevice.title: setInstallMode mode=1 / mode=2 semantics rest on a comment with no cited source
reachesDevice.ourValue: "`mode=1` is the CCU's \"normal\" install mode (mode=2 means \"ready for re-pairing\")", called as `setInstallMode(true, durationSecs, mode=1, address)`.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: `enum InstallModes { INSTALL_OFF = 0, INSTALL_NORMAL, INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST }` — 2 is INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG (write the description's default configuration and delete every existing link), 3 is INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST. There is no 4-argument form, and the per-device call selects mode 3, not 1.
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:28-34 (the enum, with the inline note on the last member "Only the device with matching serial … only one device with given serial can be installed."). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:353-354 (`case INSTALL_NORMAL: case INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST:` share one branch — central address into list 0 index 10, manual peering disabled, then ScheduleConfig) versus :388-390 (German note "setzt die default Configuration die in der Devicedescription bzw. der Channeldescription hinterlegt sind / auserdem werden alle besehenden Verknüpfungen gelöscht" immediately above `case INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG:`, whose body calls `config_data[0].InitDefault()` and `description->SetDefaultConfig(this)`). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:613 (int modes accepted only in 0..INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG, i.e. 0..2 — mode 3 is not reachable as an integer), :622 (a String third argument is what selects INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:447-450 (the whitelist filter compares the sysinfo serial and returns early on a mismatch).
reachesDevice.finding: Both halves of the comment are wrong, while the code is right. (a) mode=2 is not "ready for re-pairing": INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG re-provisions the device from its device/channel description and, per the firmware's own note at RFDevice.cpp:388-389, deletes all existing links — a destructive re-configuration, not a pairing flavour. (b) The signature in the comment, `setInstallMode(true, durationSecs, mode=1, address)`, does not exist; `DeviceAdminDomain.SetInstallMode` passes address non-empty, so `CcuBackend.SetInstallMode` takes the string branch and rfd runs INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST (3). mode=1 is never transmitted on this path — and could not be, since the int branch rejects 3. The behaviour is nonetheless correct: RFDevice.cpp:353-354 gives INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST exactly the INSTALL_NORMAL treatment, and RFManager.cpp:447-450 adds the serial restriction the operator asked for. The only genuinely correct use of `installModeNormal = 1` is the broadcast path in install_mode.go:60 (empty address), where mode 1 does mean INSTALL_NORMAL. What is at risk is future work: a reader following this comment would try to add a 4th argument, or would reach for mode=2 wanting a re-pair and get a link-wiping default-config push instead.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had "mode=2 = ready for re-pairing" been right, the third enum member would carry a re-pairing name and its RFDevice case would re-run the pairing handshake. Instead the member is named INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG and its case calls InitDefault()/SetDefaultConfig(). Had mode=1 actually been sent on the per-device path, RFManager::SetInstallMode(InstallModes, int, const std::string&) would have to accept a mode argument from the wire — it is reached only from the TypeString branch, which hard-codes INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: CONFIRMED contradicted on both halves, with one addition that makes the bundle's exoneration of the behaviour too generous. Verified verbatim: the enum ordinals; that INSTALL_NORMAL and INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST share a single case body at RFDevice.cpp:353-354, so mode 3 gets exactly the normal treatment plus the serial filter; that INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG's body re-initialises config_data[0] and pushes the description's default config, under a firmware comment that says all existing links are deleted — a destructive re-provisioning, not a pairing flavour; and that the integer branch's upper bound is 2, so mode 3 cannot be sent as an int. The comment's 4-argument signature does not exist on any surface. ADDITION the bundle missed: its closing "The behaviour is nonetheless correct" holds only when the resolved device sits on BidCos-RF. `DeviceAdminDomain.SetInstallMode` (device_admin.go:381-387) resolves the backend by address; for a device on HmIP-RF the call takes the JSON-RPC branch (ccu_extended.go:79-98) where the `mode` argument is unused AND the CCU's own wrapper discards `address` in installMode=ALL (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:66-68). So on HmIP-RF a "pair this one device" request opens a broadcast window with no serial restriction at all. `installModeNormal = 1` at install_mode.go:20 is genuinely correct only for the BidCos-RF broadcast path at install_mode.go:60.

reachesDevice.title: Duty-cycle and transmission-pending recovery windows are ported constants, not measured against the CCU
reachesDevice.missingInput: The transceiver's duty-cycle accounting-window semantics (how the reported percentage decays over time). rfd reads the percentage from the coprocessor's HELLO message and never models its recovery; no readable source carries the decay law, so no honest wait can be derived from it.
reachesDevice.ourValue: RetryDutyCycleDelay = 40 s on XML-RPC fault -8; RetryTransmissionPendingDelay = 5 s on fault -10; both fixed, jitter-free, and both freezing the exponential schedule, with MaxAttempts = 3.
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: Fault -8 ("not enough DutyCycle free") is raised at exactly one place in the whole CCU source tree — inside `RFDevice::UpdateFirmware()` — and never by setValue/putParamset; the HmIP legacy surface has no -8 at all. Fault -10 ("Transmission is pending.") exists only on the HmIP side and is emitted when `device.isReachable()` is false; it is cleared by the device becoming reachable, not by elapsed time. Neither daemon defines any recovery interval.
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1490-1492 (`if(!… ->DutyCycleForUpdate(this->address,updateFile)) { throw XmlRpcException("not enough DutyCycle free",-8); }`) — the sole `-8` in ../OpenCCU-Base/src. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosInterfaceConcentrator.cpp:1045-1076, whose whole test is instantaneous: verbatim `//450000 Byte entsprechen bei 100k Datenrate 100%` then `if((uint32_t)(450000 - (4500 * dutycycle)) > (bytesToSend + 90000)) // nach dem Update sollen noch mehr als 20% DutyCycle übrigsein`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosInterface.cpp:38-51 (`DUTYCYCLE_THRESHOLDMAP[] = {0,40,65,80,90,95,98,99,100}`) and :234-247 (`SetDutyCycle` fires a DUTY_CYCLE update only when a threshold band is crossed) — hysteresis for notification, not a budget. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosRemoteInterface.cpp:505-506 (`int dutyCycle = msg.GetUIntParam(BidcosInterfaceMessage::PARAM_INDEX_HELLO_DUTYCYCLE); SetDutyCycle(dutyCycle);`) — the percentage arrives from the transceiver. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#createTransmissionPendingRpcRemoteException (message "Transmission is pending.", code -10), #getRpcRemoteException (only -1/-2/-5/-10 are produced; no -8), #createDeleteDeviceRpcRemoteException (AP_BUSY, RESPONSE_NAK, TIMEOUT, TRANSMISSION_PENDING, STACK_BUSY and UNREACH all collapse to -10); de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleSetConfigCommand (persists the config as pending, then `if (device.isReachable()) { … } else { sendBackendResponseObject(… BackendNotificationType.TRANSMISSION_PENDING) }`) and #handleExcludeCommand (same reachability test).
reachesDevice.finding: The trigger mapping is contradicted on both codes, and the durations themselves are not derivable. -8: a CCU never rejects a value write with a duty-cycle fault. The only producer is the firmware-update path, gated by an instantaneous airtime-budget test (does the image fit in the remaining 450000-byte allowance with 20 % to spare). So RetryDutyCycleDelay = 40 s cannot fire on the write path its own doc comment describes ("when a CCU rejects a command with a duty-cycle / RF-throttle error"); against a real CCU it is reachable only from `updateFirmware`. -10: real, but HmIP-only (rfd and hs485d never emit it), and it does not mean "the CCU is busy for a moment" — it means the target device is not currently reachable and the command has been persisted as pending configuration for delivery when the device next talks to the access point. It is cleared by that event, so a fixed 5 s wait re-asks a question whose answer cannot have changed; with MaxAttempts = 3 the chain then gives up 10 s later while the CCU still intends to deliver the write. The duration questions themselves are not performable from any source I can read: rfd holds no duty-cycle recovery model at all (it reads a percentage out of the transceiver's HELLO frame and only re-notifies on band crossings), and the HmIP pending window is bounded by the device's own wake-up cycle, which no CCU source carries. Do not substitute a plausible number: the honest outputs here are (i) re-key the -8 handling to the firmware-update path or drop it, and (ii) treat -10 as "queued at the CCU, stop retrying" rather than as a timed backoff.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the firmware defined a recovery interval, `DutyCycleForUpdate` or `BidcosInterface::SetDutyCycle` would compute or wait on one; both only compare the instantaneous percentage, and the threshold map is consumed exclusively by `GetDutyCycleLowerBound`/`GetDutyCycleUpperBound` for change notification. Had -8 been produced on the value path, a grep for `-8)` across ../OpenCCU-Base/src would return more than one hit — it returns exactly RFDevice.cpp:1492 — and NotificationUtil's fault mapping would carry an -8 arm; it carries -1, -2, -5 and -10 only. Had -10 been a timed condition, DeviceSubcommandHandler would emit it behind a timer or retry count; it emits it behind `device.isReachable()`.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: CONFIRMED contradicted on the -8 mapping, and NARROWED FURTHER than the bundle on -10 — the bundle was itself too generous. -8: I re-grepped the whole src tree; RFDevice.cpp:1492 is the only producer, inside UpdateFirmware, and DutyCycleForUpdate is a pure airtime-budget predicate with no time dimension whatsoever, so RetryDutyCycleDelay's own doc comment describes a path on which the fault cannot occur. -10: the bundle wrote that it is real on the write path and means "the device is not reachable". Half right. handleSetConfigCommand (reached by putParamset MASTER) does emit it on !isReachable(), verbatim as cited. But handleSetValueCommand — the setValue path, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleSetValueCommand — never emits TRANSMISSION_PENDING: with zero tasks it answers RESPONSE_ACK, otherwise it queues the transaction (or, for a non-permanent listener, defers it into ShareableAccessPointDevicePendingCommands with no notification at all). I grepped every TRANSMISSION_PENDING producer in HMIPServer; they are handleExcludeCommand, handleSetConfigCommand, handleDoUpdateDeviceCommand, handleUpdateListenerModeDeviceCommand, LinkSubcommandHandler, the two RestoreConfiguration response handlers and DeviceBackgroundUpdateSubsystem — none on the value-write result path — and TransmissionPendingException is imported by NotificationUtil but never constructed anywhere, so it is a dead branch. Net: BOTH of our special delays are keyed to faults our value-write path cannot receive. -10 remains reachable on putParamset MASTER, deleteDevice, link operations, restoreConfig and firmware update — and on deleteDevice specifically it does cover genuinely transient AP_BUSY / STACK_BUSY, for which a short timed retry IS defensible, so "treat -10 as queued, stop retrying" is right for setConfig and wrong for deleteDevice. The two durations themselves stay NOT PERFORMABLE from any readable source: rfd carries no duty-cycle recovery model (it reads a percentage out of the HELLO frame and only re-notifies on band crossings), and the HmIP pending window is bounded by the device's own wake-up cycle, which no CCU source states. The 40 s is traceable to aiohomematic/const.py:166 — a Tier 3 witness, which is where the number came from, not evidence about the CCU.

reachesDevice.title: Every XML-RPC fault -5 on a schedule putParamset is reported to the operator as a successful save
reachesDevice.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/dispatch.tcl:144 `-5 { jsonrpc_error 505 "XML-RPC: unknown argument or value" }` | ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:112 (in RFManager::PutParamsetValues, :89-121) `throw XmlRpcException("Value not supported at parameter 4. Supported values are WAKEUP and BURST", -5);` | ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:203,208 `throw XmlRpcException("Failure");` with ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcException.h:29 `XmlRpcException(const std::string& message, int code=-1)` | HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException and #getRpcRemoteException, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#putParameterSet
reachesDevice.ourValue: fault -5 on a schedule MASTER putParamset is always the documented CCU false positive; log a warning and return success
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: -5 is the CCU's own "unknown argument or value" error (jsonrpc_error 505). On rfd it is thrown BEFORE the paramset is touched and is the only -5 that surface can produce; on the HmIP legacy surface one of its two producers is thrown before the write command reaches the event bus.
reachesDevice.finding: Wrong surface first: HmIP-PSM SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE — the device the read-back observation came from — is served by HMIPServer's legacy XML-RPC surface, not by rfd, yet the filter is applied to every backend. On rfd (the surface our bare-schema climate writes to HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU use) putParamset can emit exactly one -5: RFManager::PutParamsetValues rejects any rx_mode string other than WAKEUP/BURST at RFManager.cpp:112, before `inst->PutParamsetValues(key, set)` is ever reached. Every other rfd putParamset failure is XmlRpcException("Failure") whose default code is -1. So a -5 from a BidCos schedule write provably means nothing was written — and our code reports it as saved. On the HmIP side there are two -5 producers: NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException, thrown from DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues before `vertx.eventBus().send("backend.command.hmip", ...)` (nothing written at all), and NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException(JsonObject), which maps backend notification types UNKNOWN_PARAMETER and INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE to faultCode -5 / "Invalid parameter or value". LegacyServiceHandler#putParameterSet has no branch that returns success after either. Whether the second kind can leave the recognised subset applied on the device is access-point behaviour that HMIPServer does not model — that half is unverified — but it cannot rescue the blanket rule, because the first kind and the whole BidCos surface write nothing. The rule as written cancels exactly the protection that FilterRawScheduleByFields, filterClimateScheduleByDescKeys and the deactivateUpTo bound exist to provide. Side note on the same surface: internal/client/write_options.go:42 documents `LEVEL` as an rx-mode value; rfd accepts only WAKEUP and BURST and answers anything else with -5 before writing. The schedule path passes CommandRxModeUnset so no 4th argument is appended today, but any caller that sets RxMode to LEVEL or LAZY_CONFIG on a BidCos putParamset would produce a -5 that this filter then reports as success.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, the firmware's -5 producers would sit after the commit — in rfd after `inst->PutParamsetValues` returned, and in HMIPServer after the DEVICE_CONFIG_SET command was placed on the event bus. Both sit on the pre-dispatch side, and the CCU's own fault catalogue would not have classified -5 as an error at all. It classifies it as jsonrpc_error 505.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: I re-ran the prior agent's attack and it holds only on a narrower base than claimed. Three corrections. (1) "the only -5 that surface can produce" is true of the putParamset path, not of rfd: a whole-tree grep finds seven -5 throws in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/, five of them on getValue/readValue/setValue/setValueAsUndefined/determineParameter. I traced the actual write path end to end and it is cleaner than the prior agent showed — RFManager::PutParamsetValues -> RFChannel/RFDevice::PutParamsetValues -> RFParamset::Put -> HSSParamset::Put, and HSSParamset::Put skips a key it does not know (`if(it2!=params.end())`, no else) and `continue`s past a non-writable one, then unconditionally returns true. So an undeclared schedule key on BidCos cannot fault at all; nothing below the rx_mode check can produce -5. (2) Reachability kills the operator-harm half of the contradiction. putParamsetViaCaller appends the 4th argument only `if appendRxMode && rxMode != hmenum.CommandRxModeUnset` (internal/client/backends/wire_shared.go:155-160), PutClimateSchedule passes CommandRxModeUnset, and no production caller anywhere in internal/, cmd/ or pkg/ sets a non-unset RxMode. Today's daemon therefore cannot elicit a -5 from rfd on any putParamset. The prior agent's side note named `LEVEL`; LEVEL is only a doc comment at internal/client/write_options.go:26,42 and is not an hmenum constant — the live hazard is hmenum.CommandRxModeLazyConfig = "LAZY_CONFIG" (pkg/hmenum/device.go:102), which rfd also answers with -5 before writing. (3) The HmIP pre-send leg does not cover our payload. DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue returns the value unchanged when the channel declares no such parameter (`if (parameter == null) return value;`), so an undeclared MASTER slot key is NOT rejected before the event-bus send; the only pre-send -5 on the MASTER branch is DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues throwing NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException for a legacy-disabled parameter. Our schedule payload's characteristic failure (13x7 slot keys, some undeclared) therefore lands on the post-send backend notification, whose UNKNOWN_PARAMETER / INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE -> -5 mapping in NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException(JsonObject) says nothing about whether the access point applied the recognised subset. The empirically observed HmIP-PSM false positive sits on exactly that unmodelled branch and is not contradicted by Tier 1. Also: NotificationUtil has a third -5 producer the prior agent missed, #getDeviceExpectedException ("A device address was expected but a chanel address was given"), used by DeviceUtil — not on our channel-address MASTER path, but "two producers" was wrong. Finally, the dispatch.tcl citation is www/api's JSON-RPC error mapping (-5 -> jsonrpc_error 505), a gloss on what -5 means, not a statement about the XML-RPC surface our code calls. Net: the blanket rule is unsound in principle — a -5 from a BidCos putParamset provably means nothing was written — but the demonstrated harm is confined to two legs neither of which the schedule call site reaches today: a future caller that sets RxMode on a BidCos putParamset, and an HmIP write that hits a legacy-disabled parameter.

reachesDevice.title: The motion-latch model (MOTION held until blocking time expires or RESET_MOTION is written) rests on a comment with no cited source
