reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory#createStop (`byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE; new StateParameter(name, LogicalType.ACTION, PhysicalType.INTEGER, new IOOperations(ops), ...)`) registered for "RESET_MOTION" and "RESET_PRESENCE" in #getStateParameterList | ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config:561-562 and :602-603 | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/motiondetector.fn:6, :112-118, :126 | ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_sec_mdir.xml:227-235 `<parameter id="MOTION" operations="read,event">` with `<domino_event value="0" delay_id="NEXT_TRANSMISSION"/>` | ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.cpp:310-327 `inst->CancelAutotimerEvent(param_id); inst->ScheduleAutotimerEvent(param_id, logical_value, ((int&)temp)*1000);` | witness (Tier 2): ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-SMO.json VCU5628817:1 VALUES RESET_MOTION OPERATIONS 2 TYPE ACTION, MOTION OPERATIONS 5; HmIP-SPI.json VCU9344471:1 RESET_PRESENCE OPERATIONS 2 TYPE ACTION; HM-Sec-MDIR.json VCU0000251:1 VALUES has MOTION only
reachesDevice.ourValue: a motion detector holds MOTION until its own blocking time expires or RESET_MOTION is written; resettable = the channel exposes a writable RESET_MOTION data point
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: true only for HmIP MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER / MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER (and PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER via RESET_PRESENCE) on a permanent listener; on BidCos-RF no RESET_MOTION exists and the CCU itself un-latches MOTION on a server-side timer
reachesDevice.finding: The narrow parts are confirmed exactly. RESET_MOTION and RESET_PRESENCE are declared write-only, LogicalType.ACTION; the pairing our resetParameterFor uses (MOTION -> RESET_MOTION, PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE -> RESET_PRESENCE) is the firmware's own pairing; the WebUI writes the parameter as a plain `setDpState(<id>, true)`. Two boundaries run tighter than the comment. (1) BidCos-RF has no RESET_MOTION anywhere: no file under src/devicetypes/rftypes mentions it, and HM-Sec-MDIR's descriptor carries MOTION alone. On those devices the un-latching is done by the CCU, not the device: rf_sec_mdir.xml declares MOTION read+event with a domino_event of value 0 and delay_id NEXT_TRANSMISSION, and rfd turns that into an autotimer that writes MOTION back to 0 after NEXT_TRANSMISSION seconds. So for the whole BidCos family the comment is wrong in both halves — there is no writable parameter, and the expiry is a CCU timer, not "the device's own blocking time". Supports() correctly returns false for them, so the code is right and the doc comment is not. (2) On HmIP the firmware gates the reset on a MASTER value our port never reads: motiondetector.fn:112 fetches PERMANENT_FULL_RX via Interface.getMasterValue and :117 shows the reset button only when it is != 0, with the reason at :116 verbatim — "If the device is a non-permanent listener then hide the button. Otherwise the state of the control doesn't change after using the button which will cause enquiries at the customer service." Our Supports() qualifies on the presence of a writable RESET_MOTION alone, so on an HmIP-SMI55 configured as a non-permanent listener the daemon writes on every arm and reports the sensor as resettable, while the firmware's own UI declares that write ineffective. That is where the operator-facing "resettable latched detectors" count over-counts. Not settled, and not settleable from these trees: whether a successful write clears MOTION immediately or only ends the blocking interval, and what the latch duration is. MOTION_ACTIVE_TIME is created by HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory as a 3-bit integer config parameter with no type converter (min 0, max 7, default 4) — the source carries an ordinal, not a duration, and no mapping to seconds. Deriving a blocking time from it would be substituting a convention; that sub-question is not performable here.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had the rule been right at full width, RESET_MOTION would appear in the BidCos device-type XMLs and the WebUI would render the reset button unconditionally. Grep over all 130 rftypes XMLs returns no hit, and the button is wrapped in an explicit PERMANENT_FULL_RX != 0 guard.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: The narrowing verdict stands, but one of its sub-conclusions is wrong and I am overturning it. UPHELD, each re-checked: createStop is verbatim write-only ACTION and RESET_MOTION / RESET_PRESENCE are the only two parameters besides STOP that go through it; the MOTION -> RESET_MOTION and PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE -> RESET_PRESENCE pairing our resetParameterFor uses is the firmware's own; the WebUI writes it as `setDpState(<id>, true)`; BidCos-RF genuinely has no RESET_MOTION — a find-exec grep over all 127 rftypes and 18 hs485types XMLs returns zero files, and rf_sec_mdir.xml declares MOTION read+event with `<domino_event value="0" delay_id="NEXT_TRANSMISSION"/>`, which rfd converts into a CancelAutotimerEvent/ScheduleAutotimerEvent pair, so on that whole family the doc comment is wrong in both halves while Supports() is right; the pydevccu descriptors read exactly as quoted. The PERMANENT_FULL_RX boundary is real and in fact tighter than described: the reset button's own `<td>` ships `class='hidden'` at motiondetector.fn:99 and is revealed only by :118 inside `if (permanentFullRX != 0)`. Two things to correct. FIRST, and this is the substantive one: the prior agent reported the MOTION_ACTIVE_TIME ordinal-to-duration mapping as "not performable here" because the HmIP source carries an ordinal with no seconds mapping. Tier 1 carries it, in the tree the map itself designates as the authority the descriptor cannot be — the WebUI. www/config/easymodes/hmip/MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl builds an index-keyed options array, options(0)="15$s" through options(7)="32$m", with $s and $m bound by `upvar #0 unit_sec s` / `upvar #0 unit_min m` and defined as "s" and "min" in EnterFreeValue.tcl:6-7. The same table appears verbatim in PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl and MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER.tcl. This is not array order standing in for a mapping — each index is written down next to its value. So: 0=15 s, 1=30 s, 2=1 min, 3=2 min, 4=4 min, 5=8 min, 6=16 min, 7=32 min, and the HmIP factory's default of 4 means the shipped latch is 4 minutes. I verified the factory constants against the createInteger signature rather than by argument position: createInteger(name, listNumber, bitIndex, defaultValue, bitLength) with min defaulting to 0 and max to 2^bitLength - 1, so ("MOTION_ACTIVE_TIME", 31, 2, 4, 3) is bitIndex 2, default 4, 3 bits, min 0, max 7, converter null. SECOND, an over-read: "the firmware's own UI declares that write ineffective" is stronger than the source says. The verbatim reason at motiondetector.fn:116 is "Otherwise the state of the control doesn't change after using the button which will cause enquiries at the customer service" — a statement about the observable control state, not about the write being discarded. The honest form of the boundary: our Supports() qualifies on the presence of a writable RESET_MOTION alone, while the CCU's own UI additionally requires PERMANENT_FULL_RX != 0 before offering the button, so on a non-permanent-listener HmIP-SMI55 the daemon writes on every arm and counts the sensor as resettable where the firmware would not offer the action; whether that write eventually lands is not settled by these trees. Still open and still not settleable here: whether a successful RESET_MOTION write clears MOTION immediately or only ends the blocking interval.

reachesDevice.title: The retryable XML-RPC fault set and the message-substring override decide how often the daemon re-hits a device
reachesDevice.ourValue: retryable = {-1, -8, -9, -10}; permanent = everything else; five substrings override a retryable code to permanent: "not found", "does not exist", "unknown method", "unknown parameter", "invalid address"
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: Emitted by the firmware: -1 (default code, XmlRpcException.h:29 — carries BOTH transient and permanent conditions), -2, -3, -4, -5, -6, -7, -8, -9 in rfd/hs485d; -1, -2, -3, -5, -10, -321 on the HmIP legacy surface. -8 and -9 are thrown from exactly one function each, both inside RFDevice::UpdateFirmware(). -10 does not exist anywhere in the C++ sources.
reachesDevice.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcException.h:29 (`XmlRpcException(const std::string& message, int code=-1)`); src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:323,328 (setValue → `throw XmlRpcException("Failure")`); src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1483 (-7), :1492 ("not enough DutyCycle free",-8), :1547 ("Device is out of range",-9); src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:74 et al. ("Unknown instance",-2); src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:61 ("Unknown paramset",-3), :202 ("Missing parameter "+name, default -1), :208 ("Dependency parameter not found.", default -1), :218,:222 ("Command parameter not found[.]", default -1); src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:120,196 ("Cannot find device instance for given address parameter", default -1); src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:242 and :337 (`methodName + ": unknown method name"`, faultCode -1); src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:52 et al. ("Failure", default -1), :592 ("Device expected",-4). HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException, #createTransmissionPendingRpcRemoteException, #getUnknownParamsetRpcRemoteException, #getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException, #getDeviceExpectedException, #createDeleteDeviceRpcRemoteException; de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.rpc.AnnotationAwareRpcHandler#execute; de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcSerializer#serializeResponse.
reachesDevice.finding:
The retryable SET is right where the firmware speaks; the OVERRIDE list is half-grounded and misses the cases that matter most.

What the firmware confirms.
-1 must be retryable. Two independent Tier-1 reasons. (a) rfd's setValue throws a bare `XmlRpcException("Failure")` (XmlRpcMethods.cpp:323,328) which takes the default code -1 (XmlRpcException.h:29) — this is the ONLY signal the classic RF path emits for a device that did not answer, and 43 rfd throws plus 22 hs485d throws share it. (b) On the HmIP side, NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException maps AP_BUSY, RESPONSE_NAK, TIMEOUT and UNKNOWN to faultCode -1 with faultString "Generic error (<TYPE>)" — AP_BUSY and TIMEOUT are transient by construction. Our comment's reasoning is correct and is now grounded.
-10 exists and is transient. NotificationUtil#createTransmissionPendingRpcRemoteException returns faultCode -10, faultString "Transmission is pending." It appears nowhere in rfd/hs485d — it is an HmIP-RF-only code. Retryable is right.
The permanent codes are all real: -2 ("Unknown instance" rfd, "Invalid device"/"Invalid access point, device or channel" HmIP), -3 ("Unknown paramset" / "Unknown Paramset: <name>"), -4 ("Device expected", rfd/hs485d only), -5, -6 ("Operation not supported"), -7 ("the interface is not able to carry an update"). Defaulting unknown codes to permanent is also right: the HmIP handler emits **-321** for any internal exception that is not an RpcRemoteException (AnnotationAwareRpcHandler#execute), a genuinely permanent condition our catalogue does not name.

Where our rule is narrower than the firmware.
1. -8 and -9 are reachable only through firmware update. "not enough DutyCycle free" (-8) is thrown once, at RFDevice.cpp:1492, and "Device is out of range" (-9) once, at :1547 — both inside RFDevice::UpdateFirmware(), the latter only when the FIRST update frame goes unacked after three tries. Neither is reachable from setValue or putParamset on any interface, and neither exists on the HmIP side at all. Classifying them retryable is harmless but dead outside installFirmware; the fixed 40 s duty-cycle backoff the comment describes will not fire on a normal write, because a duty-cycle rejection during setValue arrives as -1 "Failure" like everything else.
2. Three of the five markers match no firmware fault string on a retryable code. "does not exist" and "invalid address" appear in no fault string in rfd, hs485d, libXmlRpc or the HmIP legacy surface (both appear only in log lines — src/rfd/RFParamset.cpp:84 is a LOG_WARNING). "unknown parameter" matches only code -5 strings ("Unknown parameter"/"Unknown Parameter" in rfd, "Unknown Parameter for value key: <k>" on the HmIP side), which IsRetryable already rejects — so the marker never changes an outcome.
3. Two markers ARE grounded, and precisely: "unknown method" catches libXmlRpc's `methodName + ": unknown method name"`, emitted with faultCode -1 (XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:242, and :337 inside system.multicall). "not found" catches rfd's `"Dependency parameter not found."` (RFChannel.cpp:208) and `"Command parameter not found[.]"` (:218, :222), all three thrown with the default code -1 and all three permanent (a parameter-definition mismatch on a combined write). These two markers do real work.
4. The list misses permanent -1 messages the firmware does emit. On the same code path: `"Missing parameter " + <name>` (RFChannel.cpp:202), `"Cannot find device instance for given address parameter"` (RFManager.cpp:120,196), plus "Parameter is not readable", "UndefinedValues invalid for this Paramset", "wrong mode", "Insufficient parameters.", "Peering failed. Possibly AES key mismatch." — each -1, each permanent, each currently retried for the ~7 s the comment budgets. Adding "missing parameter" and "cannot find device instance" would be exact-source additions rather than guesses.

The localization worry in the bundle is unfounded. Every fault string on both surfaces is a compiled-in English literal — C++ string literals in rfd/hs485d/libXmlRpc, Java literals in the HmIP legacy surface (NotificationUtil). There is no resource-bundle or catalogue lookup anywhere on the fault path, and none of these strings appear in www/webui/js/lang/*. An English-only marker list is not defeated by the operator's language.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Two directions, both produce a different answer if our rule is wrong. (a) On the retryable set: had -1 been permanent-only in the firmware, NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException would have mapped AP_BUSY/TIMEOUT to a distinct transient code — it maps them to -1, so the check discriminates. Symmetrically, had -8/-9 been live on the write path, I would have found them thrown from RFManager::SetValue or PutParamsetValues; the exhaustive throw inventory over src/rfd finds exactly one site each, both in UpdateFirmware. (b) On the marker list: the way to see the list is wrong is a firmware fault string that is transient AND matches a marker, or permanent-on--1 and misses. The first search returned nothing (the transient -1 strings are "Failure" and "Generic error (…)", matching no marker — had the list contained "failure", "timeout" or "generic error", every real duty-cycle and unreach retry would be suppressed). The second returned seven hits, listed above. Both halves of the control fired.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
UPHELD IN SUBSTANCE — I re-read every quote and they transcribe correctly — but the boundary is drawn in the wrong place and three citations are misattributed.

WHAT I CHECKED AND CONFIRMED MYSELF.
- XmlRpcException.h:29 default code is -1, verbatim as quoted. rfd setValue throws a bare `XmlRpcException("Failure")` at exactly 323 and 328.
- -8 and -9: grep across src/rfd and src/hs485d returns one site each (RFDevice.cpp:1492, :1547), both after `bool RFDevice::UpdateFirmware()` at :1470 and before the next function. "not enough DutyCycle free" is the ONLY duty-cycle throw in rfd. -10 and -321 appear in no C++ file.
- I enumerated every default-code (implicit -1) XmlRpcException message in rfd + hs485d + libXmlRpc. The complete set is: Failure / Failure. Wrong parameter. / Failure: link successfully added, but SetLinkInfo failed / Cannot find device instance for given address parameter / Command parameter not found[.] / Dependency parameter not found. / Missing parameter <n> / Bootloader in device <s> didn't start / Unable to load updatefile / Unable to set datarate to 100k / Firmware update aborted / Peering failed. Possibly AES key mismatch. / Parameter callerId must be of type string / type error[: expected a struct|an array] / range error: array index too large. Cross-checked against our five markers: the only hits are the three "...not found" parameter-definition throws and libXmlRpc's "unknown method name" — all permanent. NO TRANSIENT -1 MESSAGE MATCHES A MARKER on these surfaces. "does not exist" and "invalid address" match nothing anywhere I searched.

CORRECTION 1 — the -8 gap has a mechanism the previous agent missed. Saying "neither exists on the HmIP side at all" understates it. BackendNotificationType declares DUTY_CYCLE(14), UNREACH(12), STACK_BUSY(13) and ROUTING_BUSY(31) as first-class notification types, and NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException(JsonObject) maps NONE of them: they fall through its `default:` arm, keeping faultCode -1 with faultString "Generic error (DUTY_CYCLE)" / "(UNREACH)". So an HmIP duty-cycle rejection is a -1 by construction, not merely by omission — and retry.go:450's DutyCycleDelay branch is unreachable on BOTH surfaces, not just outside installFirmware. Same for DeviceOutOfRange/-9.

CORRECTION 2 — the permanent-message gap list is incomplete in the same direction. That `default:` arm also flattens MISSING_NON_OPTIONAL_PARAMETER(25), INVALID_DEVICE_TYPE(18) and SUBSYSTEM_GET_CONFIG_NOT_SUPPORTED(16) to -1. All three are permanent and NONE is reachable by any string marker, because the message is "Generic error (<ENUM_NAME>)" — SCREAMING_SNAKE, so "not found" (with a space) can never match. A marker list cannot close this gap at all; only a code-plus-notification-type distinction could, and the legacy surface does not expose the type.

CORRECTION 3 — misattributed citations. (a) "Device expected",-4 is at src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:908 and :959 and src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:593 — NOT src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:592, which is a doc comment for the ping/pong method. (b) NotificationUtil#getDeviceExpectedException was listed as evidence for -4; it emits **-5** ("A device address was expected but a chanel address was given"). Both are permanent so behaviour is unaffected, but our XMLRPCFaultAddressExpected(-4) comment describes the rfd condition only. (c) -6 "Operation not supported" is at RFParamset.cpp:262, which the previous agent asserted without a line.

CORRECTION 4 — the localization claim is overstated. XmlRpcSerializer#serializeResponse writes faultString = `response.getErrorCause().getMessage()`, i.e. Throwable.getMessage(), which for RpcRemoteException is its FIRST constructor argument — an English literal for every NotificationUtil construction (the `internalException.toString()` second argument never reaches the wire). But on the -321 path AnnotationAwareRpcHandler#execute passes `e.getTargetException()` straight through, so an arbitrary internal Throwable's message becomes the wire faultString and can be JVM- or library-localized. -321 is already permanent under our default, so there is no behavioural risk — but "every fault string on both surfaces is a compiled-in English literal" is not true as stated.

CORRECTION 5 — a scope boundary that was not named. pkg/hmerr.IsRetryable is shared by all backends, including CuxdBackend (BIN-RPC) and HomegearBackend. Neither emits faults from this firmware tree. Nothing here grounds the classification, or the marker list, for CUxD or Homegear; that is unverified.

UNSOURCED IN OUR OWN COMMENTS (flagged, not part of the rule): errors.go:283 attributes "Unbekannter Parameter oder Wert" to "the catalogue" for -5; that string appears nowhere in ../OpenCCU-Base. Likewise the symbolic names "INSUFFICIENT_DUTYCYCLE" and "DEVICE_OUT_OF_RANGE" in the -8/-9 comments are not firmware identifiers — the firmware strings are "not enough DutyCycle free" and "Device is out of range", and the HmIP enum name is DUTY_CYCLE.

What our code should follow: the firmware (Tier 1) on both surfaces. The retryable set {-1,-8,-9,-10} and default-permanent are correct as written and should stay. The marker list should keep "not found" and "unknown method" (each grounded on an exact -1 fault string), may drop "does not exist", "invalid address" and "unknown parameter" as dead, and cannot be extended to cover the HmIP "Generic error (X)" family at all.

reachesDevice.title: Display geometry (5 rows, 24 characters) is asserted without a source and is published to Home Assistant as a hard limit
reachesDevice.ourValue: maxDisplayID = 5 (rows 1..5, enforced at textdisplay.go:527); MaxRowLength = 24 bytes, enforced as `len(r.Text) > MaxRowLength` (textdisplay.go:153) and republished as HA's `"max": 24` (payload.go:122)
reachesDevice.firmwareValue: row count: DISPLAY_DATA_ID MIN=1 MAX=5 on HmIP-WRCD — matches. Row length: DISPLAY_DATA_STRING's declared MAX is the constraint regex `[0x20-0x7E]{16}` — 16 characters, restricted to printable ASCII 0x20..0x7E, not 24 bytes of anything
reachesDevice.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory — the DISPLAY_DATA_ID entries register three variants via #createDisplayDataIDParameter, keyed "two" (1,2), "five" (1,5) and "eight" (0,7); DISPLAY_DATA_STRING is registered via #createDisplayDataStringParameter with the max-value regex `[0x20-0x7E]{16}` (default, ASCII converter), `[U+00-U+FF]{16}` ("utf8") and `[U+00-U+FF]{14}[0-9A-F]{0,4}` ("wgd"). Tier 2, the device's own declaration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-WRCD.json, channel VCU4243444:3 VALUES — DISPLAY_DATA_ID {TYPE INTEGER, MIN 1, MAX 5, DEFAULT 1, OPERATIONS 2}; DISPLAY_DATA_STRING {TYPE STRING, MIN "", MAX "[0x20-0x7E]{16}", DEFAULT "", OPERATIONS 2}
reachesDevice.finding: Our profile is scoped to exactly one device: internal/model/custom/profiles.go:1429-1438 registers IPTextDisplay for DeviceType "hmip-wrcd", channel 3. Within that scope maxDisplayID = 5 is right, and both tiers agree (the WRCD descriptor declares MIN 1 / MAX 5; the firmware's "five" variant is createDisplayDataIDParameter(1, 5)). Note it is right only in that scope — the same parameter is registered with (1,2) and (0,7) for other display channels, so the constant must not be lifted to a fleet-wide rule, and the honest source is the runtime descriptor's MIN/MAX rather than a literal. MaxRowLength = 24 is wrong by 8: firmware and descriptor both cap the row at 16 characters, and additionally restrict the alphabet to 0x20..0x7E (the default variant's converter is the ASCII one). Two consequences, both reaching the device: a 17..24-character row passes our validator and goes out in the put_paramset for the CCU to truncate or reject, and HA is told `max: 24` so operators are invited to type 8 characters that cannot arrive. Our comment cites "the HmIP-SDV* firmware limit" — no HmIP-SDV device appears in the pydevccu descriptor corpus, in ../openccu-data, or in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/, so that attribution is unsourced as well as numerically wrong. Also worth recording: the descriptor's MAX for a STRING parameter is a constraint regex, not a length, so any code that reads MAX numerically will read nothing usable — the 16 has to be parsed out of the regex or kept as a WRCD-scoped constant with this citation. Separately, the doc comment at textdisplay.go:519 ("Validation: ID must be >= 1") understates the code, which enforces an upper bound too.
reachesDevice.negativeControl: Had maxDisplayID been wrong, the WRCD descriptor would have declared a different pair — 1/2 or 0/7, the two other variants the firmware registers — and rows 3..5 (or row 0) would have been mis-gated; it declares 1/5. Had MaxRowLength = 24 been right, the declared MAX would read `{24}` or a numeric 24 in at least one of the four DISPLAY_DATA_STRING variants the firmware registers; none contains a 24, and the WRCD's own declaration reads `[0x20-0x7E]{16}`.
reachesDevice.challengeNote: UPHELD on the contradiction, with the consequence narrowed. Right surface established: internal/model/custom/profiles.go:1429-1438 registers IPTextDisplay for DeviceType "hmip-wrcd" channel 3 only, and the WRCD descriptor's channel :3 is exactly where both DISPLAY_DATA_ID and DISPLAY_DATA_STRING live — so the factory's default (non-utf8, non-bwth, non-wgd) variant is the one this profile writes. maxDisplayID = 5 is right and doubly sourced (firmware "five" variant = (1,5); descriptor MIN 1 / MAX 5); it must stay WRCD-scoped, since the same parameter is also registered (1,2) and (0,7). MaxRowLength = 24 is wrong by 8 in both tiers: 16, not 24. The "HmIP-SDV*" attribution in the comment is unsourced — no HmIP-SDV appears in ../pydevccu, ../openccu-data or ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/. THREE CORRECTIONS to the reader. (1) The reader's downstream claim "for the CCU to truncate or reject" is not sourced and I could not source it: the converter bound to this parameter is the no-arg AsciiStringToInteger, whose length field is 0, so #convertLogicalToPhysical allocates `temp.length + 1` bytes and truncates nothing, and I found no length or regex validation of STRING values on the legacy put_paramset path (DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue special-cases only the Unicode/WGD converters and METER_OBIS_SEARCH_STRING). What a 17..24-character row actually does at the device is therefore UNVERIFIED — say that rather than "truncate or reject". (2) The converter's charset is ISO_8859_1, so the 0x20..0x7E alphabet is a DECLARED constraint, not one the conversion enforces. (3) Our validator counts BYTES (`len(r.Text)`) while the declared limit counts characters; inside the declared alphabet these coincide, but a UTF-8 non-ASCII row would be measured wrongly by our check as well. What our code should follow here is the runtime descriptor (MIN/MAX read from the device), not a literal — the firmware's per-variant registration is precisely why a fleet-wide constant is unsafe.

../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json: of 2924 distinct "ADDRESS" values, 0 contain a dot. || Tier 3 witness (provenance only) — ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/rega_scripts/get_service_messages.fn:53: `!# Extract address from alarm name (format: "AL-ADDRESS:X.PARAM")`, which is verbatim where our comment and our own internal/client/rega/scripts/get_service_messages.fn came from.
reachesDevice.finding:
Both claims survive, but each is true for a different reason than the comment gives, and one surface the comment implies does not exist.

(A) The last-dot split. The firmware does compose the name as "AL-" + X + "." + Y with exactly one literal dot, so "the segment after the last dot" recovers Y. But our justification — "device / channel addresses never contain a dot" (hub_wiring.go:1579-1580) — is the wrong invariant and is not asserted anywhere in the firmware. The split is safe iff the PARAMETER contains no dot (X may contain any number). That property is real and measurable: 0 of all id="…" values in the shipped device-type XMLs contain a dot, and the HmIP acceptance set (ServiceMessage#isServiceMessageParameter) is a closed list of [A-Z0-9_] names — LOW_BAT, UNREACH, SABOTAGE, CONFIG_PENDING, VALVE_STATE, plus extended forms built as "%s_%s" (e.g. VALVE_STATE_ERROR_POSITION). Note our comment's example "LOWBAT" is the BidCos spelling; the HmIP name is LOW_BAT, and only the HmIP spelling is in the accepted set.

Three consequences the comment does not carry:
1. Interface.suppressServiceMessages exists only on the HmIP side. rfd (BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired via hs485d) registers getServiceMessages but no suppressServiceMessages and no getSuppressedServiceMessages; the CCU's tcl (suppressservicemessages.tcl:20) forwards blindly to $interface(URL), so a Disable() on a BidCos channel is an unknown-method XML-RPC fault, not a suppression. Our Disable() at messages.go:571 passes msg.InterfaceID through unconditionally.
2. A wrong non-empty parameter is a SILENT no-op: DeviceUtil#setSuppressedServiceParam only writes the channel's service-message-filter metadata when isServiceMessageParameter or isExtendedServiceParameterName matches; otherwise it falls off the end and returns normally. No fault reaches us, so our suppressed[] map records a suppression that never happened.
3. An empty parameter is not merely "all parameters" — with enable=true it replaces the channel's filter with the single entry "*"; with enable=false it removes the filter metadata entirely, i.e. our Unsuppress with an empty parameter clears every suppression on that channel, including ones we never set. serviceMessageParameter() returns "" for any name without a dot and Disable() does not check, so a name outside the "AL-…" shape silently escalates to channel-wide.

The firmware's own route to the parameter does not go through the name at all: serviceMessages.htm and the distribution's Device.setEnabledServiceMsg both resolve AlTriggerDP() -> the trigger DP object and read HSSID(). Our own get_service_messages.fn already resolves that exact object (for Operations() and Channel()); emitting oTrigger.HSSID() would replace the inherited string convention with the value the CCU itself uses, and would leave Parameter empty only when the trigger DP is genuinely absent.

(B) The 65535 sentinel. Confirmed as a value, narrowed as a name: 65535 is ID_ERROR, ReGaHss's script constant for "no such object", not an alarm-specific "unknown" marker — ReGa writes it itself to clear a reference (system.fn:864). What the firmware does show for our case is that the operator's alarm variable is created without ever setting a trigger DP, and that the CCU's own pages guard the trigger by resolving the object and comparing to ID_ERROR, never by `> 0` — which is exactly the failure our script comment records. What no readable source states is the AlarmDP field's default in so many words; that AlTriggerDP() specifically returns ID_ERROR rather than 0 for such a variable rests on ID_ERROR being ReGa's unset-reference value plus our own live observation, and stays unverified at that last step. Suggested wording: "…so the CCU leaves its trigger data point at ID_ERROR (65535), ReGa's invalid-object-reference constant" — and drop "unknown".
reachesDevice.negativeControl: For (A): had the firmware composed the name with a different separator, with no separator, or with the parameter first, the two "AL-" code sites would have loaded a different literal than 0x18e5bc (".") between the two appends, or would have ordered the appends differently — the disassembly at 0x10272f-0x102798 and 0x114de3-0x114e3c would have read differently, and I would have reported the split contradicted. Had a parameter id contained a dot, the sweep of every id="…" in the shipped device-type XMLs would have returned a non-zero count instead of 0; had an address contained a dot, the sweep of the 2924 descriptor ADDRESS values would have. Had rfd implemented suppressServiceMessages, it would have appeared among the 51 XmlRpcServerMethod("…") registrations in src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp alongside getServiceMessages — it does not, while getServiceMessages does, which is the control that the grep was looking in the right file. For (B): had ID_ERROR been any other value, the 8 bytes following the name pointer at 0x1f2360 would not have read 0x000000000000ffff; the control that the table is the constant table (and not a coincidence) is that the adjacent entries decode to ID_PRESENT=950, ID_SERVER_DP=945, pppNone=0, pppServer=1, pppClient=2 — values that would be nonsense if the stride or field order were wrong. What this check cannot produce is a different answer about AlTriggerDP()'s default for an alarm system variable, because no readable source carries that field's initialiser; that sub-claim is therefore reported as unverified above rather than confirmed.
reachesDevice.challengeNote:
I could not break the claim's citations. Every one of them — the binary offsets, the two constant values, the exact xref count, the tcl line numbers, the 51/26 registration counts, the 2924 ADDRESS values — reproduces exactly when executed independently. No invented source, no tier inflation, no simulator. I am upholding it on that basis, and narrowing it on three points the claim did not reach.

NARROWING 1 — the invariant is about the parameter, and the claim's restatement still smuggles the operand identity. The claim says the firmware composes "AL-" + address + "." + parameter, "one dot after the address part". What the binary actually carries is "AL-" + X + "." + Y with nothing appended after Y. ReGaHss is stripped: X and Y have no names. Calling X "the address" is inference. But Y is better grounded than the claim managed: the AL- name is built inside CreateDPs (../Platform/DOM/iseXmlRpc.cpp) in the loop over a getParamsetDescription response, and Y is assigned from the loop entry's own string field, sibling to the per-entry "FLAGS" and "TYPE" lookups. So Y is a paramset parameter name, read from the firmware rather than assumed. That is exactly and only what the last-dot split needs, and it makes the invariant measurable on the right corpus: 220 distinct <parameter id> values in the shipped device-type XMLs, 0 with a dot; and on the HmIP side a closed acceptance set of [A-Z0-9_] names with "%s_%s" extensions. Our comment's justification — "device / channel addresses never contain a dot" (hub_wiring.go:1579-1580) — is the wrong condition and is asserted by no firmware source; X may contain any number of dots without harming the split. The claim's 2924-ADDRESS measurement is real but measures the operand that does not matter.

NARROWING 2 — (B) splits into a confirmed half and a Tier-1-silent half, and the claim's suggested rewrite still asserts the silent one. Confirmed: 65535 IS ID_ERROR, ReGa's invalid-object-reference constant — I read it out of the .data table myself, and ReGa writes it to clear a reference (system.fn:864) and tests for it on the sibling accessor (Interface(), LastTriggerID()). Not confirmed, and not confirmable from any source I can reach: that AlTriggerDP() specifically returns 65535 rather than 0 for an operator-created alarm variable. I searched the whole www/ tree and the patch set. Nothing anywhere compares AlTriggerDP() to ID_ERROR or to 0 — every consumer resolves the object and guards on the object. The claim's proposed wording ("the CCU leaves its trigger data point at ID_ERROR (65535)") is a firmware-flavoured restatement of an unverified value; adopting it would convert an honest live observation into a false firmware citation, which is the exact failure this series exists to catch. The observation is real (get_alarm_messages.fn records the ScriptRuntimeError that an `if (trigger > 0)` guard let through) and should stay attributed to the live CCU. Note this half touches no live code path at all: get_alarm_messages.fn walks ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES and never calls AlTriggerDP(); the comment is documentation of why it does not.

NARROWING 3 — one correction against the claim, and one piece of evidence it missed. The claim says our example "LOWBAT" is the wrong spelling and "only the HmIP spelling is in the accepted set". Half right, and the wrong half matters: LOWBAT is the correct BidCos spelling — 29 shipped rftypes XMLs declare id="LOWBAT", none declare id="LOW_BAT". The sharper statement is that a BidCos LOWBAT cannot be suppressed at all, because rfd and hs485d register no suppressServiceMessages. That reinforces the claim's consequence 1 rather than weakening it, and I found independent corroboration the claim did not: the firmware's ONE caller of Interface.suppressServiceMessages, at src/webui/www/config/easymodes/hmip/CLIMATECONTROL_FLOOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:40, hardcodes 'interface':'HmIP-RF' and 'parameterId':''. eQ-3 uses this method only on HmIP, and only channel-wide.

All three of the claim's consequences hold on our path. Disable() at messages.go:571 forwards msg.InterfaceID unconditionally into the JSON-RPC Interface.suppressServiceMessages (adapter/hub_wiring.go:2795 -> jsonrpc/methods.go:152), so a BidCos channel yields an unknown-method fault; a wrong non-empty parameter is a silent no-op that our suppressed[] map records as a success; and an empty parameter with enable=false removes the channel's filter metadata outright, clearing suppressions we never set. serviceMessageParameter() has no "AL-" prefix check — unlike our own ReGa script, which does guard with Find("AL-") == 0 — so any non-AL-shaped name silently escalates to channel-wide.

What our code should follow: Tier 1 for the mechanism (the CCU's own route to the parameter never touches the name — serviceMessages.htm and patch 0044 both resolve AlTriggerDP() -> HSSID()), Tier 2 for the dot-freeness of the parameter. Our get_service_messages.fn already resolves that exact trigger object for Operations() and Channel(); emitting oTrigger.HSSID() would replace an inherited string convention with the value the CCU itself uses. I endorse the claim's suggestion there — it is the one change that removes the guessed input rather than re-justifying it.

all.title: ALARM sysvar state is accepted only as the literal "1"/"0" from a ReGa boolean ToString()
all.citation: AlState() is NOT a boolean: every firmware call site compares it against an enum constant — ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:328,329,356,1463; www/rega/pages/tabs/statusviews/alarmMessages.htm:23; www/pda/eq3/sysvar.tcl:22 (`oSV.AlState() == asOncoming`). The alarm-state constant table is carried by ReGaHss itself as name→value pairs (../OpenCCU-Base/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu/ReGaHss, .data at file offset 0x1f1c60..0x1f1c80): asNone=0, asOncoming=1, asReceipted=2. The value column is a real value column, not an array index — the same table shows iulNone=0/iulGuest=1/iulUser=2/iulMainuser=4/iulAdmin=8 and ctSMTPvisaSOAP=16/ctSMSviaSOAP=32/ctMMSviaSOAP=64/ctMSGviaSOAP=128. Integer .ToString() renders decimal digits: www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/views/newdevicechannelsloader.htm:97 and www/rega/pages/tabs/startpage.htm:126 compare `oEntry.ID().ToString()` against members of an EnumIDs() id list. BOOLEAN .ToString()/string-concat renders "true"/"false", not "1"/"0": ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/channel/setlogging.tcl:18 does `Write(channel.ChnArchive())` on a boolean and line 24 accepts only `("true" == $result) || ("false" == $result)`, everything else being a "homematic script error". Operator semantics: www/rega/esp/system.fn:1461-1470 renders an ALARM sysvar as ValueName1 iff AlState()==asOncoming, ValueName0 otherwise.
all.finding: Our two accepted renderings are the right ones, but the acceptance set is incomplete and the comment's premise is wrong. AlState() is a three-valued integer enum, not a boolean; ToString() therefore yields "0", "1" or "2". "1"=asOncoming→true and "0"=asNone→false are correct. "2"=asReceipted (alarm raised, then acknowledged via ReceiptAlarm / AlAutoReceipt) falls through our switch to parseSysvarValue on the structurally EMPTY getAll payload, returns ok=false, and records no value at all — exactly the failure mode the comment says it prevents, just one state further along. The WebUI's own rule for the same variable is binary and total: ValueName1 iff asOncoming, else ValueName0, i.e. asReceipted reads as NOT triggered. Correcting our switch to map "2"→false would match the CCU. Separately, the code comment and the script header both call this "a ReGa boolean": if the script were ever rewritten to `(oVar.AlState()==asOncoming).ToString()` the Go switch would silently stop matching, because ReGa renders booleans as "true"/"false" (setlogging.tcl). Residual, stated as unverified: ReGaHss is stripped, so I did not read the AlState accessor's own return type; the integer reading rests on the enum constants being integers and on integer ToString() rendering decimals, both read from source above.
all.ourValue: accepted set {"1"→true, "0"→false}; anything else → no value recorded
all.firmwareValue: AlState() ∈ {asNone=0, asOncoming=1, asReceipted=2}; WebUI treats asOncoming as raised and both asNone and asReceipted as not raised
all.negativeControl: Had the rendering been "true"/"false", setlogging.tcl would have accepted "1"/"0" from `Write(channel.ChnArchive())` — it accepts only "true"/"false" — and the ReGaHss constant table would not carry integer values for asNone/asOncoming/asReceipted. Had our two values been wrong, the table would have shown asOncoming ≠ 1 or asNone ≠ 0. Had the enum been two-valued, there would be no asReceipted entry. The check separated all three cases.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD in substance, with one premise demoted and one new firmware fact added. (a) The enum reading is now grounded with a real negative control inside the data itself (iulOtherThanAdmin=7 in the same contiguous table proves the value column is not an index), so asReceipted=2 stands and the acceptance-set gap is real: "2" falls through to parseSysvarValue and records no value. (b) NEW — the operator rule is not single-valued across the WebUI. system.fn:1461-1470 renders the sysvar's VALUE as binary on asOncoming (so asReceipted reads as not-triggered, which is what the previous agent reported), but ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:329 counts a sysvar into the ALARM MESSAGE LIST only when `(oSV.AlState()==asOncoming) && (oSV.State()==true)` — a second, stricter rule on a different surface, with the AlState-only form sitting commented out on line 328. Mapping "2"→false matches the value-rendering surface; it does not follow from the message-list surface. (c) DEMOTED — the premise both our code comment and the script header assert, that SysVar.getAll's value is 'structurally EMPTY' for every alarm variable, is UNVERIFIED and the firmware evidence leans against 'structural': getall.tcl emits `WriteLine("VALUE {" # sv.Value() # "}")` for every subtype identically, with no alarm special case, and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/functions.fn:14-27 shows an ALARM sysvar's ValueType is ivtBinary and treats btoLogic and btoAlarm with the SAME value string. ReGa also handles `Value()==""` for LOGIC, LIST and NUMBER alike (system.fn:1447,1473,1489), so emptiness is a general uninitialised-sysvar condition, not an alarm-specific structural guarantee. Whether an alarm DP's Value() is in fact always empty is a runtime observation no readable source settles. (d) STILL INDIRECT — no firmware call site ever renders AlState() into a string; all six uses in the tree are `== asOncoming` comparisons (system.fn:328,329,356,1463; alarmMessages.htm:23; pda/eq3/sysvar.tcl:22). That AlState().ToString() yields decimal "0"/"1"/"2" rests on integer ToString() rendering decimals (startpage.htm:126 and newdevicechannelsloader.htm:97 compare `oEntry.ID().ToString()` against decimal EnumIDs members) plus the constants being integers. Sound, but inferred, and I could not read ReGaHss's AlState accessor (stripped). (e) The code comment's word 'boolean' is wrong and is a live trap exactly as reported: if the script were rewritten to `(oVar.AlState()==asOncoming).ToString()` the Go switch would silently stop matching, because ReGa renders booleans "true"/"false".

all.title: The door-lock action LEVEL values, including the out-of-range 1.01 'open', rest on nothing
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.CalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createLevelParameter — ConfigurationParameter(LogicalType.FLOAT, PhysicalType.INTEGER, RW, DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0), list, listIndex, 0, 1 /*byte*/, 0, default 0.0, min 0.0, max 1.01). Same factory's #create16BitLevelParameter is identical but 2 bytes with DoubleToInteger(50000.0,0.0) and the same max 1.01. Callers: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.SwitchCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createWeekProfile builds NN_WP_LEVEL / NN_WP_DURATION_BASE / NN_WP_DURATION_FACTOR over lists 12..14 × 25 entries (#getMaxPeriods = 75); BlindCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createWeekProfile builds NN_WP_LEVEL_2 from the same #createLevelParameter. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.DoubleToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical: `d *= factor; d += offset; d = d>=0 ? d+0.5 : d-0.5; (int)d`. Duration encoding: #createTimeFactor declares min 0 / max 31 / default 31; #createTimeBase is a StringEnumToInteger over de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.LinkTimeBase = {BASE_100_MS, BASE_1_S, BASE_5_S, BASE_10_S, BASE_1_M, BASE_5_M, BASE_10_M, BASE_1_H} — index 7 = BASE_1_H. Lock physical scale: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLockTargetLevelParameter declares LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL {LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN} = {0, 200, 255}, and LOCK_STATE {UNKNOWN, LOCKED, UNLOCKED} = {255, 0, 200}. Channel type: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.ChannelType declares SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE(48) and no door-lock week-profile type, matching internal/central/adapter/schedules.go:570-577. Witness (Tier 3): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/schedule_models.py:293-298 carries the same four triplets and names the 1.01 case AUTORELOCK_END, not "open".
all.finding: The numbers are right; the label attached to 1.01 is not, and the neighbouring Level2 bound is one ulp too tight. (1) 1.01 IS a legal LEVEL — it is exactly the declared MAX of every calendar WP_LEVEL parameter, so simple.go:200's `e.Level > 1.01` bound reproduces the firmware maximum verbatim rather than admitting an out-of-range value. (2) 0.0 → physical 0 and 1.0 → physical 200 under DoubleToInteger(200,0); on a door lock those are exactly the declared LOCKED and UNLOCKED codes of LOCK_STATE / LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL, so the locked/unlocked mapping is grounded. (3) The 'open / latch release' reading of 1.01 is NOT supported: 1.01×200+0.5 → physical 202, whereas the firmware's OPEN sentinel is 255 (logical 1.275, above the WP_LEVEL max and unreachable through this parameter). Our code does not in fact claim 'open' on the wire — LockActionOpen's string value is "autorelock_end" (simple.go:98), matching the Python witness; only the Go identifier and the reader's summary say 'open'. What the device does with WP_LEVEL=202 is decided by the lock's own firmware, which is not in any tree here — that part stays unverified. (4) CONTRADICTION on the same site: simple.go:202 rejects Level2 > 1.0, but WP_LEVEL_2 is created by the identical #createLevelParameter with max 1.01. A CCU-reported cover slot at LEVEL_2=1.01 fails our validator on a read→validate→write round-trip. (5) Corroborated in passing: durBase 7 = BASE_1_H and durFactor 31 = the declared factor max/default; our comment calling 31 a "sentinel 'always'" is our interpretation, the firmware declares it only as the maximum.
all.ourValue: Level bound 0..1.01; Level2 bound 0..1.0; 1.01 identified as 'open'/latch release

all.title: deleteDevice flag bits 1 = RESET and 2 = FORCE rest on a comment, and a wrong bit factory-resets a paired device
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:53-55 — `DELETE_FLAG_RESET=(1<<0)`, `DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=(1<<1)`, `DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=(1<<2)`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.h:34-36 — identical. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:108-131 — doc block: "flags ist ein bitweises oder folgender Werte: 0x01 (DELETE_FLAG_RESET) … 0x02 (DELETE_FLAG_FORCE) … 0x04 (DELETE_FLAG_DEFER)"; the handler body takes `if(params[1].getType()==XmlRpcValue::TypeInt)flags=params[1];`. Same doc at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:182-200. Behaviour: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:919-930 — `if (flags & DELETE_FLAG_RESET) success = dev->FactoryReset(); else success = dev->UnpeerCentral();` then `if (flags & DELETE_FLAG_DEFER) ScheduleDelete(...)` and `if (!(flags & DELETE_FLAG_FORCE)) return false;`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:597-603 mirrors it. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#deleteDevice(String,Integer) → #doDeleteDevice → de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#excludeDevice, which tests `!device.isReachable() && (flags & 2) != 0` to suppress the exclude request — bit 2 = force-on-unreachable, same as BidCos.
all.finding: Both bit values are exactly as our constants say, on rfd and on hs485d, and the second argument really is an OR-able integer bitmask that our `Call(ctx, "deleteDevice", address, flags)` matches (rfd reads params[1] as TypeInt). Two narrowings worth recording. (a) A third flag exists that we do not model: DELETE_FLAG_DEFER = 4 — "if the device is unreachable, delete it at the next opportunity" — with its own abortDeleteDevice XML-RPC method (XmlRpcMethods.cpp:136-149) to cancel it. Our UnpairDevice can never set it, so a deferred unpair is unreachable from the daemon; harmless, but the comment's "the CCU's deleteDevice flag constants" reads as a complete set and is not one. (b) On the HmIP interface only bit 2 is honoured — DeviceUtil#excludeDevice consults `(flags & 2)` and nothing else, so DeleteFlagReset is silently inert against an HmIP device while it really does trigger dev->FactoryReset() on BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired.
all.ourValue: DeleteFlagReset = 1, DeleteFlagForce = 2, sent as an int bitmask
all.firmwareValue: DELETE_FLAG_RESET=(1<<0)=1, DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=(1<<1)=2, DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=(1<<2)=4; HmIP honours only bit 2
all.negativeControl: Had the pair been swapped, RFManager.h:53 would read `DELETE_FLAG_RESET=(1<<1)` and XmlRpcMethods.cpp:115 would document 0x02 as RESET; both read the other way. Had the second argument not been a bitmask, RFManager.cpp:919-929 would not test it with `&` and the doc would not say "bitweises oder".
all.challengeNote: UPHELD. Both constants are exactly right on rfd and on hs485d, and our `Call(ctx, "deleteDevice", address, flags)` hits the integer branch the handler provides (`params[1].getType()==TypeInt`). Three refinements. (a) The previous pass's paraphrase of the DEFER control flow flattens the nesting: DEFER and FORCE are BOTH inside `if (!success)` — DEFER is only consulted when the FactoryReset/UnpeerCentral attempt failed, and it returns true immediately, so it is not an independent post-step. (b) NEW: hs485d DECLARES DELETE_FLAG_DEFER in its header but HS485Manager.cpp:596-603 never tests it — there is no ScheduleDelete branch on the wired path. So the flag is inert on BidCos-Wired as well as on HmIP, and is honoured only by rfd. (c) NEW: the rfd handler also accepts a legacy three-argument boolean form (params[1] boolean = RESET, params[2] boolean = FORCE); a caller sending booleans instead of a bitmask still works, and a caller sending an int overrides whatever the boolean branch computed. Our int form is the correct and unambiguous one. (d) UPHELD unchanged: DeleteFlagReset really does reach dev->FactoryReset() on BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired and is silently inert on HmIP, and our constants' doc comment reads as a complete set while omitting bit 2 (DEFER) and its abortDeleteDevice companion.

all.title: Device/paramset change-detection hash cannot see unmodelled CCU wire fields, though the comments say it does
all.citation: Device description, BidCos-RF: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:242-260 emits ADDRESS, RF_ADDRESS, TYPE, PARENT, FIRMWARE, VERSION, INTERFACE, ROAMING, RX_MODE, FLAGS, AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE, UPDATABLE, PARAMSETS, CHILDREN, then `description->GetAdditionalDescription()->Describe(&dev_desc)`. Channel: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:969-996 emits ADDRESS, TYPE, PARENT_TYPE, PARENT, INDEX, PARAMSETS, LINK_SOURCE_ROLES, LINK_TARGET_ROLES, DIRECTION, **AES_ACTIVE** (line 981: `(*descr)["AES_ACTIVE"]=aes;`), VERSION, FLAGS, GROUP, TEAM, TEAM_TAG. The additional-description hook is data-driven: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSDescription.cpp:21-28 copies every `<field id=… value=…>` from the device-type XML straight into the struct; the shipped XMLs define exactly one such field, `AutoconfRoles` (6 occurrences under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/). HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.objects.DeviceDescription declares 26 @RpcMember names — TYPE, SUBTYPE, ADDRESS, RF_ADDRESS, CHILDREN, PARENT, PARENT_TYPE, INDEX, **AES_ACTIVE**, PARAMSETS, FIRMWARE, AVAILABLE_FIRMWARE, UPDATABLE, FIRMWARE_UPDATE_STATE, VERSION, FLAGS, LINK_SOURCE_ROLES, LINK_TARGET_ROLES, DIRECTION, GROUP, TEAM, TEAM_TAG, TEAM_CHANNELS, INTERFACE, ROAMING, RX_MODE — and no AES_KEY, SERIAL, DIRECT_LINK_DEACTIVATED, FIRMWARE_STATE or UPDATE_STATE. Parameter description: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:205-218 emits ID, OPERATIONS, FLAGS, TAB_ORDER, CONTROL (optional) then the logical type's keys — UNIT (HSSLogicalType.cpp:53-60), TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL (HSSLogicalTypeFloat.cpp:105-119, HSSLogicalTypeInteger.cpp:112), VALUE_LIST (HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:104) — then the same additional_description hook. Tier 2 census over ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json: AES_ACTIVE appears on 2654 channel descriptions, AES_KEY on zero; over ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json the only key outside ParameterData is AutoconfRoles (17).
all.finding: The blind spot is real and the firmware supplies a concrete, mutable instance of it. Verified in our tree: DeviceDescription.Extra and ParameterData.Extra both carry `json:"-"`, marshalCanonical (normalize.go:151) is a plain json.Marshal, and there is no custom UnmarshalJSON on either type and no production write to `.Extra` — so an unmodelled key is not merely excluded from the digest, it is discarded at decode. The comment at normalize.go:22-23 claiming Extra "preserves wire fidelity … in the hash" is false in both halves, and sortedRawMap (normalize.go:187) returns an unordered map, so its stated mechanism does not exist either (determinism comes from encoding/json's key sorting). The firmware key that falls into this hole is AES_ACTIVE, emitted on every channel by BOTH rfd and HMIPServer. It is runtime-mutable, not device-type static: RFChannel.cpp:1377 assigns `this->aes` from a MASTER write, RFChannel.cpp:1136-1198 persists and reloads it, RFChannel.cpp:1285-1307 pushes it to the device. So toggling a channel's AES per-device security produces an identical descriptor hash and the configuration coordinator never reloads. Compounding it, we model a field the CCU never emits: DeviceDescription.AESKey `json:"AES_KEY"` (device.go:75) — AES_KEY exists only as a per-device MASTER *parameter* in the device-type XMLs, never as a description key, and is absent from the HmIP @RpcMember list and from all 2924 corpus descriptions. The second unmodelled key, AutoconfRoles, is static per device type and therefore harmless. Everything else the CCU emits is modelled.
all.ourValue: DeviceDescription models AES_KEY; no AES_ACTIVE field; Extra is `json:"-"` and never populated
all.firmwareValue: rfd and HMIPServer both emit AES_ACTIVE on every channel description (runtime-mutable); neither emits AES_KEY
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU emitted only keys we model, RFDevice::Describe / RFChannel::Describe and the HmIP DeviceDescription @RpcMember list would contain no name outside our struct, and the Tier-2 census would show zero unmodelled keys. Instead AES_ACTIVE appears in all three and AES_KEY in none of them. Had AES_ACTIVE been device-type static, RFChannel.cpp would set `aes` only in the constructor; it also assigns it from a MASTER write at :1377.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD, and I could not weaken it. The Tier-2 census I ran independently returns exactly the 26 keys the HmIP @RpcMember list declares — so AES_ACTIVE is the ONLY key the CCU emits on a device/channel description that our DeviceDescription does not model, and it is the one key on that list that changes at runtime rather than per device type. The blind spot is real in both halves the comment claims otherwise: `json:"-"` excludes Extra from the hash AND there is no custom decoder that would ever populate it, so an unmodelled key is discarded at decode, not merely omitted from the digest; and normalize.go:187's stated mechanism (a 'sorted-by-key view') does not exist — it returns a map, and whatever determinism the hash has comes from encoding/json's key sorting, which Extra never reaches anyway. Consequence stands: toggling a channel's per-device AES via the internal MASTER value "AES" yields a byte-identical descriptor hash and the configuration coordinator never reloads. The inverse defect stands too — pkg/hmproto/device.go:75 models `AESKey *int `json:"AES_KEY"``, a key no CCU description carries on either transport (0 of 2924 corpus entries, absent from the HmIP member list, absent from rfd/hs485d/libhsscomm). One refinement to the previous pass: it wrote 'RFChannel.cpp:1377 assigns this->aes from a MASTER write'; the parameter's name on the wire is "AES", not "AES_ACTIVE" — the description key and the writable parameter are differently named, which is precisely why a grep for the description key does not find the mutation site.

all.title: The virtual-remote address roots are a bare literal set — including a truncated "BidCoS-Wir" — with no cited source
all.site: internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:40-44 (virtualRemoteRoots), consumed by needsCentralPrefix at :111-123 via exact match on addressRoot
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFCentral.cpp:36-37 — `type="HM-RCV-50"; serial="BidCoS-RF";`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Central.cpp:36-37 — `type="HMW-RCV-50"; serial="BidCoS-Wir";`. These are the only two hard-coded serials in src/rfd, src/hs485d and src/libhsscomm (`grep -rn 'serial="'`). The description address is built from that serial: RFDevice.cpp:243 `dev_desc["ADDRESS"]=RFManager::GetSingleton()->BuildStringAddress(serial)` and RFDevice.cpp:268 `(*val)[dev_index]["CHILDREN"][i]=ch_address` from `BuildStringAddress(serial, ch->GetIndex())`; the WebUI addresses it verbatim at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/tabs/startpage.htm:303 — `Interface.getDeviceDescription {"interface":"BidCos-RF","address":"BidCoS-RF"}`. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.VirtualRemoteControl declares DEVICE_ID_BASE = "HmIP-RCV-", DEVICE_TYPE = "HmIP-RCV-50", a static `vrcNr` initialised to 1, and in its constructor `this.id = DEVICE_ID_BASE + vrcNr; vrcNr = vrcNr + 1;` — one instance per access point — then #createDeviceDescription sets the description ADDRESS to that id and the CHILDREN to `id + ":" + channelIndex` for channelIndex 0..Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.ChannelIndex.Last (default 50). de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyNotificationHandler tests `deviceId.startsWith("HmIP-RCV-")`, i.e. the firmware itself treats the family as a prefix, never as the single literal.
all.finding: Two of the three literals are confirmed character-for-character and the truncation worry is unfounded: "BidCoS-Wir" is not a truncation we inferred, it is the string the wired daemon assigns to its own central (HS485Central.cpp:37), and it is the complete BidCos-Wired virtual-remote serial. "BidCoS-RF" likewise. Both are the only fixed serials in the C++ daemons, so the BidCos half of the set is complete. The HmIP entry is where the rule narrows: "HmIP-RCV-1" is only the FIRST member of a counter-generated family. VirtualRemoteControl builds its id as "HmIP-RCV-" + a static counter that starts at 1 and increments once per constructed instance (one per HmIP access point), and the firmware's own membership test is a startsWith on "HmIP-RCV-". Our exact map lookup on addressRoot therefore matches "HmIP-RCV-1" and misses "HmIP-RCV-2" and up. The boundary: a CCU with a single HmIP access point — the ordinary case, and the only case the corpus and the contract test cover — is handled correctly; a CCU with a second access point emits a virtual remote whose channels get an UNSCOPED unique_id, which is exactly the collision the map exists to prevent, and with a retained MQTT payload the loss outlives the daemon. A prefix test on "HmIP-RCV-" would match the firmware's own rule. Note also that the HmIP virtual remote is off by default (ServiceProperties "Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.Enabled", default false), which is why the second instance is rare rather than impossible.
all.ourValue: exact-match set {"BidCoS-RF", "BidCoS-Wir", "HmIP-RCV-1"}
all.firmwareValue: "BidCoS-RF" (rfd), "BidCoS-Wir" (hs485d), and "HmIP-RCV-" + n for n = 1, 2, … (one per HmIP access point)
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU spelled the wired central "BidCoS-Wired", HS485Central.cpp:37 would carry that string — it carries the 10-character form. Had a fourth BidCos-side virtual-remote root existed, `grep -rn 'serial="'` over src/rfd, src/hs485d and src/libhsscomm would have returned more than two hits; it returns exactly these two. Had "HmIP-RCV-1" been a fixed constant, VirtualRemoteControl would declare the full id as a constant instead of concatenating a static counter, and LegacyNotificationHandler would compare with equals rather than startsWith.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD as a boundary, but the previous pass's MECHANISM is wrong and its remediation carries a cost it did not name. (1) CONFIRMED: "BidCoS-RF" and "BidCoS-Wir" are exact, complete, and not truncations. (2) CONTRADICTED — 'a static vrcNr … one instance per access point' is not what the code does. The access point is ALWAYS `AccessPointUtil.getFirstMasterAccessPoint`, so adding a second HmIP access point does not create a second VirtualRemoteControl. vrcNr increments once per LegacyServiceHandler CONSTRUCTION, and there are at least two such constructions per HMIPServer process — LegacyAPIWorker builds a LegacyServiceHandler and ExtendedLegacyAPIWorker builds an ExtendedLegacyServiceHandler whose super-constructor runs the same code. So "HmIP-RCV-2" is produced routinely inside the process, not 'rare' and not tied to a second access point. (3) NARROWED and left honest: which of the two instances a given legacy XML-RPC port publishes is not determinable from what I read — each handler serves only its OWN id (isIdMatching is an exact comparison against this.id), the shared-map instance key is overwritten by whichever handler constructs last, and verticle deployment counts are not in the readable material. Whether our daemon's interface ever sees "HmIP-RCV-2" is therefore UNVERIFIED; what IS settled is that our exact-match entry pins the first-constructed instance only, while the firmware's own family test (LegacyNotificationHandler) is a prefix on "HmIP-RCV-". (4) NEW CAVEAT the previous pass missed: 'a prefix test would match the firmware's own rule' is true of the firmware but not free here. internal/routingkey is declared at uniqueid.go:5-18 to be a cross-backend algorithm-of-record that MUST produce bit-identical output with the other backends, pinned by a golden fixture set; the Python reference carries the same three literals at ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:2096-2098 (Tier 3 witness — this is where our set came from, not an authority for what the CCU does). Widening one side alone splits the contract and re-scopes keys asymmetrically, which is the failure mode the package exists to prevent. The fix is a coordinated change plus a fixture, not a one-line prefix. (5) Unchanged: with the feature off by default, and one access point, our set is correct for the ordinary case.

all.title: The CCU UserLevel → Loom role mapping and the "UPL_NONE = 0" claim rest on a comment, and they gate authentication
all.site: internal/config/config.go:1607-1613; internal/auth/ccuauth/store.go:72-74 and :140-158 (the code that actually applies it); internal/client/rega/scripts/get_user_level.fn:13-15 (the value's source)
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/index.htm:94 `ul = <% Write( oUser.UserLevel()); %>;` and :100-103 `UPL_NONE  = 0;` / `UPL_GUEST = 1;` / `UPL_USER  = 2;` / `UPL_ADMIN = 8;`. Corroborating gates on the same accessor: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:176, :761, :874, :891, :908, :1165 (`oUser.UserLevel() == iulAdmin` guards the admin-only actions), :116, :236, :279, :1067, :1091 (`!= iulGuest && != iulNone` denies guest and none), :298 (`!= iulNone`); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/ise/htm/header.htm:86 (`getUPL() != UPL_GUEST` strips the alarm/service-message surface for guests); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/logout.htm:94 (`oUser.UserLevel() <= 1` gets the lighter session teardown).
all.firmwareValue: UPL_NONE=0, UPL_GUEST=1, UPL_USER=2, UPL_ADMIN=8 — exactly four constants; no other UPL_* constant is defined anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base (grep over www/ and src/ returns only index.htm, ise/htm/header.htm, www_source/webui/js/dialog/installWizard.js, all using this set).
all.ourValue: MinUserLevel default 1 ("guest"), 0 always denied; role mapping keys "8"/"2"/"1" → admin/operator/viewer, applied by ccuauth/store.go:143-157 as thresholds ≥8 admin, ≥2 operator, ≥1 viewer, else deny.
all.finding: The ordinals are right, and they are read off the same accessor our ReGa script calls. `get_user_level.fn` returns `oUser.UserLevel()`; index.htm writes that same expression into `ul` and immediately defines UPL_NONE=0 / UPL_GUEST=1 / UPL_USER=2 / UPL_ADMIN=8 against it, so the four values our config documents are the firmware's own, on our path. The semantics match too: the WebUI treats iulAdmin as the sole administrator level, and guest/none as the two levels denied every user- and object-management action — which is what admin / operator / viewer / deny encode. Two honest qualifications. (a) Our threshold form (≥8, ≥2, ≥1) is our construction, not the firmware's; the firmware compares for equality against exact constants. It maps the four defined levels correctly and it is a deliberate tolerance for an unforeseen level, but the firmware defines no fifth level for it to tolerate — nothing in the readable tree defines a value between 2 and 8 or above 8. (b) I could not locate the WebUI's level-assignment control (`system.fn:1125 user.UserLevel(system.GetVar("level"))` is the sink; the caller that supplies `level` is not in the readable www/ or www_source/ tree), so whether UPL_NONE=0 is *assignable* to a stored user is unsettled. It is certainly a state a session can be in — system.fn:298 gates UpdateUI on `!= iulNone` — and we deny it either way, so the open question does not touch behaviour. Note the operator-facing consequence of the default: min_user_level=1 admits UPL_GUEST, and the CCU itself treats a guest as a real but heavily restricted account (header.htm:86 removes alarm and service messages from a guest's page), so mapping it to viewer is consistent with the firmware's own treatment.
all.negativeControl: Had our reading been wrong — say admin were 4, or an intermediate level 3 existed — index.htm:100-103 would have carried that different constant set, since it is a literal table of assignments read straight from the source rather than inferred from ordering or position. The check reads named constants, so a different firmware value produces a visibly different table; it cannot return our expected answer by construction.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD by re-measurement: index.htm:100-103 reads exactly UPL_NONE=0/UPL_GUEST=1/UPL_USER=2/UPL_ADMIN=8, and a grep for `UPL_` over the whole tree returns those four definitions plus three consumer sites (header.htm:86 and installWizard.js) — the "exactly four constants" claim holds.

TWO ATTACKS LAND.

(a) WRONG SURFACE in the corroborations. Every UPL_ADMIN / UPL_USER / UPL_GUEST comparison in the tree runs against getUPL(), which is NOT oUser.UserLevel(). index.htm:147-159 defines it as `system.GetSessionVarStr(sessionId).StrValueByIndex(";",1).ToInteger()` — the second field of the semicolon-separated session string (session.fn::GetUPL is identical; field 0 is the user id). Who writes that field is inside the ReGa interpreter, not in the tree. Meanwhile `ul = oUser.UserLevel()` at index.htm:94 is assigned and, by grep for `\bul\b`, never compared to any UPL_ constant in that file. And all 22 gates on the accessor use the symbolic iulAdmin/iulGuest/iulNone, whose numeric values are interpreter built-ins — a grep for any `iul… =` definition over the whole tree returns nothing. The ONLY numeric comparison against oUser.UserLevel() anywhere is logout.htm:94, `<= 1`. So "UserLevel() == 8 means admin" — the exact binding our authentication rests on — is inference from name plus adjacency, not read from the source. The 0/1 boundary IS read (logout.htm:94); 2 and 8 are not.

(b) THE THRESHOLD FORM FAILS IN THE WRONG DIRECTION. The bundle called ≥8 "a deliberate tolerance for an unforeseen level" and dismissed it because "the firmware defines no fifth level". That reads the absence of a *constant* as the absence of a *value*. system.fn:1125 stores `user.UserLevel(system.GetVar("level"))` with no validation on the readable path, so an out-of-set level is at least storable; and the firmware's own admin gates are equality (`== iulAdmin`, 22 sites), i.e. an unforeseen level ≥8 is denied admin by the CCU and granted admin by us. Our ≥1 viewer line, by contrast, is firmware-shaped: logout.htm:94 uses a low-boundary threshold itself.

I could not locate the WebUI control that supplies `level` either (saveUser is only reachable from system.htm:25; no JS caller in www/ or www_source/), so the bundle's qualification (b) stands as written.

all.finding: Every entry the bundle named as high-exposure lands on a channel that declares the parameter it maps, and the unusual-looking numbers are the descriptor's, not a convention. HmIP-WGTC really is climate-on-8 / dimmer-on-2 / switch-on-4: ch2 is BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER (it declares LEVEL, so the 'dimmer' is the display backlight — it binds, whatever one thinks of the presentation), ch4 is the first SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, ch8 is the HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER. IPButtonLock on ch 0 binds because GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK is a MASTER parameter of the MAINTENANCE channel, not a VALUES one. HmIP-SCTH230 ch12 is the first DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (ch11 is the transmitter). ELV-SH-WSM ch4 is the first WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER; offset -2 lands on ch2 FLOW_METER_TRANSMITTER, which declares exactly the three water parameters the config lists, and offset -1 lands on ch3 WATER_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER, which declares STATE. The IPThermostat offset table resolves per base channel and each offset is correct for the family it was written for: from base 1 (BWTH) offset 7 → ch8 which carries HEATING_VALVE_TYPE in MASTER, offset 8 → ch9 SWITCH_TRANSMITTER which carries STATE; from base 8 (WGTC) offset -5 → ch3 SWITCH_TRANSMITTER which carries STATE, offset 0 → the climate channel which carries CONCENTRATION. The offsets that are dead for the other family (-5 from base 1 is a negative channel; +8 from base 8 is CLIMATECONTROL_HEAT_DEMAND_PUMP_TRANSMITTER with an empty VALUES set) resolve to nothing and cost nothing. Where the boundary runs: (a) elv-sh-psmci ch 3 — no descriptor for ELV-SH-PSMCI exists in ../pydevccu or ../openccu-data, so that single entry is unverified; (b) the audit covered the nine named entries, not the catalogue, so 'the catalogue carries no citation' remains true as a process statement even though every entry I could measure is right; (c) Tier 1 is structurally silent for HmIP channel layouts (see notes), so the source our code should follow for these is the runtime descriptor, which is what it already reads — extending profiles.go with per-entry Tier-1 citations is not possible for the HmIP half of the catalogue.
all.negativeControl: Had a base channel or offset been wrong, the descriptor lookup would have named a channel whose declared parameter set does not contain the mapped parameter — and it did produce exactly that result in the dead-offset cases (offset +8 from base 8 lands on CLIMATECONTROL_HEAT_DEMAND_PUMP_TRANSMITTER with an empty VALUES set; offset -5 from base 1 is a negative index). The check therefore demonstrably distinguishes a binding channel from a non-binding one on this very data, and did not return 'binds' uniformly.
all.missingInput: A device description for ELV-SH-PSMCI — absent from ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/ and from ../openccu-data — leaves profiles.go:135-143 (IPSwitch, elv-sh-psmci, channel 3) unmeasurable from any available source.
all.challengeNote:
Every entry I could measure reproduces exactly — WGTC climate-on-8 / backlight-dimmer-on-2 / first switch-on-4 / GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK as a MASTER parameter of ch0, SCTH230 ch12, WSM ch4 with -1→ch3 STATE and -2→ch2 carrying exactly those three water parameters, BS2 4+8, SW1-BAT 3. Two corrections to the bundle.

(1) WRONG SURFACE — a second unverified entry the bundle missed. It grounded `hmip-wsm` on ELV-SH-WSM.json and wrote them as one line ("elv-sh-wsm / hmip-wsm"). They are two independent registrations (profiles.go:1439 and the elv-sh-wsm entry), and registry matching is exact-then-longest-prefix (registry.go:383-385, :416, :426-442), so "hmip-wsm" never matches an ELV-SH-* model. There is NO HmIP-WSM descriptor in ../pydevccu, none in ../openccu-data, and HmIP channel layouts are not in OpenCCU-Base rftypes. So hmip-wsm ch4 and its -1/-2 offsets are unverified on the same footing as elv-sh-psmci, which the bundle did name. The transfer rests on "the ELV and HmIP brand twins carry the same channel layout" — a convention read from nowhere. Two unverified entries, not one.

(2) A DEAD OFFSET THE BUNDLE DID NOT NAME, and it costs a field. IPThermostat ChannelFields offset 7 → HeatingValveType. From base 1 (BWTH) it lands on ch8 FLOOR_DIRECT whose MASTER declares HEATING_VALVE_TYPE — correct. From base 8 (WGTC) it lands on ch15 HEAT_DEMAND_BOILER, whose MASTER declares four parameters and not HEATING_VALVE_TYPE. WGTC carries HEATING_VALVE_TYPE on ch14, i.e. offset 6. So the field is silently unbound on WGTC even though the device declares it. The bundle listed only -5-from-base-1 and +8-from-base-8 as the dead offsets and concluded the table "is correct for the family it was written for"; it is correct for BWTH and one offset short for WGTC.

Worth recording alongside: the shared FieldState entries at -5 and 8 resolve per family only because resolveChannelKeyedField walks ascending and takes the first hit (field_resolve.go:66-70). On WGTC -5→ch3 (STATE) wins before 8→ch16 is consulted; on BWTH -5→ch-4 misses and 8→ch9 (STATE) binds. The two entries carry different visibility (Bare at -5, Visible at 8), so the same field ships hidden on WGTC and visible on BWTH — a consequence of map ordering, not of any device property.

The process statement in the title stands unchanged: the catalogue carries no per-entry citation, and for the HmIP half Tier 1 is structurally silent, so the runtime descriptor is the right source and it is what the code already reads.

all.title: HmIP COMBINED_PARAMETER string shape and slot order are pinned only by an in-package test
all.site: internal/model/custom/cover/blind.go:299-302 (the comment) and :350-355 (`fmt.Sprintf("L2=%d,L=%d", int(wireT*100+0.5), int(wireL*100+0.5))`), reached from :249, :269 and :412; internal/model/custom/cover/init.go:334-351 (IPHdm is also BlindKindIP)
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#setValue (routes a COMBINED_PARAMETER write into #convertCombinedParameter and then #putParameterSet on VALUES), #convertCombinedParameter (the parse), #validateAndConvertValues, #addSpecialCommaSeparatedParameter (declares COMBINED_PARAMETER as a write-only STRING in VALUES), #getParamsetDescription (the channel-type set that gets it). Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-FBL.json — ch4/5/6 BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER VALUES declares COMBINED_PARAMETER (TYPE STRING, OPERATIONS 2 = write-only) alongside LEVEL and LEVEL_2 (TYPE FLOAT, MIN 0.0, MAX 1.01); ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-DRBLI4.json — same on ch10/11/12, ch14-16, ch18-20, ch22-24; ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-HDM1.json — ch1 SHADING_RECEIVER VALUES declares LEVEL and LEVEL_2 but NOT COMBINED_PARAMETER. Secondary, and on a different surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/webui/js/dialog/blindCombinedParamDialog.js:100-112 builds the LINK-paramset value as `result = "L="+valL+",L2="+valL2` and :88-91 parses it back positionally.
all.firmwareValue: #convertCombinedParameter splits the string on ',' then each token on '='; `"L"` → key LEVEL, value Double.parseDouble(v)/100.0; `"L2"` → key LEVEL_2, value Double.parseDouble(v)/100.0. Each pair is put into an RpcStruct (a map) which is then handed to putParameterSet on VALUES, so token order carries no meaning. An unrecognised token hits the switch default, is logged at debug and skipped — no fault. COMBINED_PARAMETER is added to a channel's VALUES paramset only for the channel types enumerated in #getParamsetDescription: SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (except on BWTH devices), BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, OPTICAL_SIGNAL_RECEIVER, SERVO_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, WINDOW_DRIVE_RECEIVER, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER, BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER, WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, WEATHER_DISPLAY_RECEIVER (plus the week-program and identification-mode cases). SHADING_RECEIVER is absent from that set.
all.ourValue: `"L2=<tilt_pct>,L=<level_pct>"`, both integer percents produced by int(v*100+0.5) after clamping v to [0,1]; written on hmenum.ParameterCombinedParameter for every BlindKindIP device including IPHdm.
all.finding: The tokens, the scale and the acceptance are right: L is LEVEL, L2 is LEVEL_2, the CCU divides by 100 so integer 0..100 is exactly the percent form it wants, and it parses with Double.parseDouble so our integers are a strict subset of what it accepts. The claim in the comment that 'tilt slot first' matters is not a device property — the parse builds a map, so order is irrelevant, and the CCU's own WebUI emits the opposite order on the LINK surface. That is harmless for us but it means TestBlindIPCombinedFormat pins a choice, not a contract, and a future reordering would be safe. Where the boundary runs, and this one bites: COMBINED_PARAMETER is only ever added to VALUES for a fixed set of channel types, and SHADING_RECEIVER is not in it. HmIP-HDM1's ch1 is SHADING_RECEIVER, the descriptor confirms its VALUES has LEVEL and LEVEL_2 but no COMBINED_PARAMETER, and init.go:348 builds IPHdm as BlindKindIP — so every combined position/tilt write on an HmIP-HDM targets a parameter that channel does not declare. The firmware has a purpose-built path for that channel instead: on SHADING_RECEIVER a plain setValue of LEVEL_2 auto-fills LEVEL with 1.01 (the NO_MODIFICATION special value) and sends both together, i.e. the per-parameter write already does what the combined write does elsewhere. Two smaller notes. The percent ceiling is not 100: LEVEL/LEVEL_2 are declared MAX 1.01, and the WebUI's own dialog offers 100.5 (last value) and 101 (ignore), which after /100.0 are the two special values — we clamp to [0,1] and never reach them, which is correct for a position command but means 'both values are integer 0..100' describes our range, not the parameter's. And the WebUI's LINK-paramset dialog does parse positionally (arElmValues[0] is read as L), so order does matter on that surface — a reason not to reuse this string shape for a LINK write without rechecking.
all.negativeControl: Had the token mapping been reversed, #convertCombinedParameter's switch would have shown `case "L": key = "LEVEL_2"` — the mapping is a literal switch on the token string, read directly, not inferred from position.
