And the check did produce a different answer where the rule does not hold: the same method's channel-type enumeration excludes SHADING_RECEIVER and the HmIP-HDM1 descriptor lacks the parameter, so the procedure returned 'not accepted here' for one of the five models in scope rather than confirming uniformly. Caveat on the channel-type set: in the readable form of #getParamsetDescription the assignments inside that switch are not recoverable (each case body reduces to a dead local), so what I read is the set of channel types the switch considers, not the boolean each sets. SHADING_RECEIVER appears nowhere in that switch, and Tier 2 agrees independently, which is why I state the exclusion; the positive membership of the listed types rests on the enumeration plus the descriptors.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD on the shape: L→LEVEL, L2→LEVEL_2, both divided by 100.0, parsed with Double.parseDouble so our integers are a strict subset, unknown tokens skipped without a fault. UPHELD that order is irrelevant on this surface (the parse builds a map) — so the comment's "tilt slot first" and TestBlindIPCombinedFormat pin a choice, not a contract. UPHELD that the CCU's own WebUI parses positionally on the LINK surface, so this string shape must not be reused there without rechecking.

THE BUNDLE'S HEADLINE BOUNDARY IS CONTRADICTED. It concluded "this one bites" — that every combined write on an HmIP-HDM targets a parameter the channel does not declare. The write reaches the device anyway. #setValue tests `DEVICE_STATE_COMBINED_PARAMETER.equals(valueKey)` and branches into convertCombinedParameter + putParameterSet("VALUES", …) BEFORE any lookup of the channel's parameter set; the only declaration check downstream is #validateAndConvertValues, which sees the decomposed keys LEVEL and LEVEL_2 — both declared on SHADING_RECEIVER per HmIP-HDM1.json — so it passes and the pair is dispatched as a normal DEVICE_VALUE_SET. What HDM misses relative to a BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER is only routing: #checkBlindLevel returns false for any channelType != BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, so the write skips the QUEUE_LEGACY_BLIND_LEVEL_CORRECTION path. And the SHADING auto-fill of LEVEL=1.01 that the bundle cited lives in #checkRequiredValues, which is reached only from the single-parameter setValue branch, never from the combined branch — and our combined write names both axes, so it would be a no-op regardless.

So the real boundary is narrower and different: the gap is in the DESCRIPTOR, not the firmware. getParamsetDescription omits COMBINED_PARAMETER for SHADING_RECEIVER, so any client or proxy that validates a write against the published paramset description will reject it on HDM ch1 — the CCU itself accepts it. The bundle's smaller notes stand: LEVEL/LEVEL_2 are declared MAX 1.01 and the WebUI offers 100.5/101 as the two special values, so "integer 0..100" describes our clamp, not the parameter's range.

One caveat on the channel-type set: the enumeration is readable and matches, but the boolean that drives it did not survive into readable form (the branches assign dead locals), so "SHADING_RECEIVER is absent from the set" is read from the switch's case labels, and the Tier-2 descriptor independently agrees.

all.title: HM LEVEL_COMBINED byte order (position byte first, slat byte second) rests on a bare comment
all.site: internal/model/custom/cover/blind.go:303-307 (the comment) and :345-349 (`parameter.ConvertHMLevelToCPV(wireL) + "," + parameter.ConvertHMLevelToCPV(wireT)`); internal/parameter/converter.go:269-277 (`fmt.Sprintf("0x%02x", int(math.Round(value*100*2)))` after clamping to [0,1]); gate in internal/model/custom/cover/init.go:262-277
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_ja_conf_644.xml:110-112 `<frame id="LEVEL_SET" …><parameter type="integer" index="11.0" size="1.0" param="LEVEL"/><parameter type="integer" index="12.0" size="1.0" const_value="202"/></frame>`; :115-117 `<frame id="LEVEL_SLATS_SET" …><parameter type="integer" index="11.0" size="1.0" const_value="202"/><parameter type="integer" index="12.0" size="1.0" param="LEVEL_SLATS"/></frame>`; :120-121 `<frame id="LEVEL_COMBINED_SET" …><parameter type="string" index="11.0" size="2.0" param="LEVEL_COMBINED"/></frame>`; :162-177 LEVEL `<logical type="float" default="0.0" min="0.0" max="1.0" unit="100%">` … `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/>`; :249-266 LEVEL_SLATS, identical logical range and `factor="200"`; :311-316 `<parameter id="LEVEL_COMBINED" operations="write" control="JALOUSIE.LEVEL_COMBINED"><logical type="string"/>…<conversion type="hexstring_bytearray" has0XPrefix="true" delimiter=","/></parameter>`. Conversion mechanics: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionHexStringToByteArray.cpp:63-93 (LogicalToPhysical: tokenise on the delimiter, trim, fromHexValue each token, append one byte per token, in order), :128-151 (getNextToken), :152-171 (fromHexValue requires exactly 4 characters when has0xPrefix). Supporting: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/blind.fn:88-93 (the WebUI's own jalousie control binds JALOUSIE.LEVEL, JALOUSIE.LEVEL_SLATS and JALOUSIE.LEVEL_COMBINED on one channel).
all.firmwareValue: LEVEL_COMBINED is a 2-byte payload occupying frame indices 11.0 and 12.0. LEVEL_SET writes LEVEL at index 11 and a constant 202 at 12; LEVEL_SLATS_SET writes constant 202 at 11 and LEVEL_SLATS at 12. Index 11 is therefore the position byte and index 12 the slat byte, and the hexstring_bytearray conversion emits one byte per comma-separated token in token order, so token 1 = position, token 2 = slats. Scale on both axes: float_integer_scale factor 200 over a logical range 0.0..1.0 (special values 1.005 OLD_LEVEL, 1.010 NO_MODIFICATION — note 1.010*200 = 202, which is exactly the 'leave this axis alone' constant the two single-axis frames use). Token syntax with has0XPrefix="true": exactly four characters, '0x' plus two hex digits; anything else fails the whole conversion.
all.ourValue: `ConvertHMLevelToCPV(level) + "," + ConvertHMLevelToCPV(tilt)` — position token first, slats second; each token `fmt.Sprintf("0x%02x", int(math.Round(v*200)))` with v clamped to [0,1], i.e. 0x00..0xc8, always four characters.
all.finding: Confirmed on every axis of the claim, and the firmware supplies its own cross-check for the order: the two single-axis frames put the live parameter at opposite indices (LEVEL at 11, LEVEL_SLATS at 12) and fill the other slot with the constant 202, which is the NO_MODIFICATION special value (1.010 x factor 200) — so 'index 11 is position, index 12 is slats' is stated twice, independently, in the same file. LEVEL_COMBINED_SET then covers both indices with one 2-byte string parameter, and the hexstring_bytearray converter appends one byte per token in the order the tokens appear, so our position-first ordering is the firmware's. The scale matches to the unit: factor 200 against a 0.0..1.0 logical range is exactly int(round(v*200)); our clamp to [0,1] keeps us inside the logical range and away from the two special values. The token shape matches: fromHexValue with has0xPrefix demands a string of exactly length 4, and "0x%02x" over 0..200 is always exactly 4 — one digit fewer and the conversion returns false for the whole write, which is a loud failure rather than a wrong position. Case is not an issue (the firmware emits uppercase but parses with std::hex, which is case-insensitive). Two scope notes, neither a defect: LEVEL_COMBINED is declared only on the jalousie type file (HM-LC-Ja1PBU-FM and the generic HM-LC-JaX), not on the rf_bl* shutter families, which matches our gate — newRfCoverConstructor only builds a BlindKindHM when the profile's tilt parameter actually resolves on the device, and the shutter families have none. And the doc comment's '#04x' is Python's format spec for the same four-character output the Go code produces; it is a stale idiom, not a wrong value.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware read slats first, LEVEL_SET would have carried `param="LEVEL"` at index 12.0 with the 202 constant at 11.0, and LEVEL_SLATS_SET the mirror image — the indices are literal attributes on the frame parameters, read from the file, not derived from the order the elements appear in. The procedure demonstrably separates the two cases: it read two frames that disagree about which index is live and used that disagreement to pin the assignment.
all.challengeNote:
CONFIRMED; every cited line reproduced verbatim, and two of the bundle's scope notes verified independently rather than taken on trust.

Scope check I ran myself: `grep -rl --binary-files=text` over src/devicetypes/rftypes/ returns EXACTLY ONE file containing LEVEL_COMBINED and exactly one containing LEVEL_SLATS — rf_ja_conf_644.xml, whose supported_types block covers HM-LC-Ja1PBU-FM and the generic HM-LC-JaX. That matches our gate tightly: newRfCoverConstructor is registered for the RfCover profile only (cover/init.go:38), RfCover maps FieldLevel2 → ParameterLevelSlats (profile_configs.go:592), and init.go:262-277 promotes to BlindKindHM only when that parameter resolves on the concrete device. So the set of devices that ever take the LEVEL_COMBINED path is a subset of the two device types that declare the parameter. The shutter families carry neither and stay plain covers.

One step in the chain is entailed rather than quoted, and I name it because the whole ordering hangs on it: that the first byte of the 2-byte string field lands at frame index 11 and the second at 12. The XML gives the field's start index and size, not an explicit intra-field byte order, and I looked for the frame serializer in src/rfd (BidcosFrame*.cpp) without locating the string-field placement. What closes it: device.xsd documents `index` as the parameter's START ADDRESS, the converter appends one byte per token in token order, and the two single-axis frames fix index 11 = position and index 12 = slats using 202 = NO_MODIFICATION as the filler on the other axis. The bundle wrote that the order is "stated twice, independently" — that overstates it slightly (the two frames fix index-to-axis, not token-to-index), but with the xsd's start-address semantics the reading is entailed, not conventional.

Also upheld: `"0x%02x"` over 0..200 is always exactly four characters, which is precisely what fromHexValue demands; case is irrelevant (std::hex); the clamp to [0,1] keeps us inside the logical range and clear of 1.005/1.010; and the comment's `#04x` is a stale Python idiom for the same four-character output, not a wrong value.

all.title: IP lock LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL is written as ENUM label strings, and the 'OPEN = 2' index claim is a bare comment
all.site: internal/model/custom/lock/lock.go:519-535 (the comment and the three constants) and :537-556 (Lock.sendIP writes the label on hmenum.ParameterLockTargetLevel); internal/model/custom/lock/init.go:18
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLockTargetLevelParameter (the enum strings and their device values, and the WRITE-only IOOperations); de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (publishes VALUE_LIST as the converter's enum strings, so the labels a client sees are these); de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical (matches the label, falls back to byte 0 on no match) and #convertPhysicalToLogical; de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue (the label/ordinal handling, gated on the Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal service property); de.eq3.cbcs.server.local.LocalServer and de.eq3.ccu.server.ip.HMIPServer read that property with default false. Tier 1 on the operator surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/door_opener.fn:202-204 (DOOR_LOCK_STATE_TRANSMITTER: `setDpState(<LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL>, 0)` labelled ${lblLock}, `, 1)` ${lblUnlock}, `, 2)` ${lblOpen}), :386-388 (DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER, identical 0/1/2), :381 (the retired option list, in order: LOCKED,UNLOCKED,OPEN,RESET_TEACH_IN,…).
all.firmwareValue: LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL is a WRITE-only ENUM with PhysicalType INTEGER. Non-DLP (HmIP-DLD) variant: enum strings {LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN} with device values {0, 200, 255}. DLP variant: {LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN, TEACH_IN_DRIVE_OPEN_DOOR_NEUTRAL_UNLOCKED, TEACH_IN_DRIVE_OPEN_DOOR_NEUTRAL_VERTICAL, TEACH_IN_DRIVE_OPEN_DOOR_NEUTRAL_HORIZONTAL, LOAD_CALIBRATION_OPEN_DOOR} with device values {0, 1, 2, 20, 21, 22, 33}. In both variants the first three labels are LOCKED, UNLOCKED, OPEN at list positions 0, 1, 2, and the published VALUE_LIST is exactly that string array. The WebUI drives the same parameter with the ReGa ordinals 0/1/2 under the labels Lock/Unlock/Open.
all.ourValue: The strings "LOCKED", "UNLOCKED", "OPEN" written on LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL, and the comment 'IP locks support open (LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL=2)'.
all.finding: The three labels are exactly the declared VALUE_LIST, and OPEN really is at position 2 in both device variants, so the write and the '=2' note are both right. The comment's justification is the part that does not survive: 'The CCU XML-RPC interface accepts both integer indices and string labels for ENUM parameters' is false for this surface in its default configuration. The label/ordinal translation in #convertParameterValue is gated on the service property Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal, whose default is false in both server entry points; with it false an inbound integer is passed through unconverted to StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical, which compares the value against each enum string, finds no match, and returns byte 0 — the LOCKED device value. So sending the index 2 would not open the latch, it would lock the door, silently and without a fault. String labels work in both configurations (with the flag on, an inbound String falls through every branch untouched; with it off, nothing is applied and the converter matches it). Our choice is the correct and the safe one; the reasoning written next to it inverts which form is robust. Two boundaries worth recording. (a) The same silent-zero fallback means any future typo or a label from the wrong variant degrades to LOCKED rather than to an error — the failure mode of this write is actuation, not rejection. (b) The device values behind the labels differ between the two variants (UNLOCKED is 200 on DLD, 1 on DLP; OPEN is 255 vs 2), which is exactly why the label form is the portable one and why spelling the HA discovery payload as positional indices, as the comment at lock.go:527-534 says it deliberately did not, would have been fragile.
all.negativeControl: Had OPEN sat at a different position, or had the labels been spelled differently, #createLockTargetLevelParameter would have shown a different literal String[] — the array is read directly and its element order is the VALUE_LIST order that #addDesriptionOfParameter publishes, so this is not an ordering inferred from anything. The two variants provide a live control: the procedure did return different device values for the same labels (200/255 vs 1/2), so it distinguishes cases rather than reporting agreement uniformly. And the ReGa control page, an independent Tier-1 surface, drives the same parameter with 0/1/2 under Lock/Unlock/Open, which would have disagreed with the array had the positions been otherwise.
all.challengeNote:
The core rule is UPHELD and re-read verbatim: the three labels are exactly the declared enumStrings, and OPEN sits at list position 2 in both device variants. The write is correct.

BUT THE BUNDLE'S CENTRAL CORRECTION IS ITSELF CONTRADICTED, on Tier 1. It claimed the comment's "accepts both integer indices and string labels" is false, that the flag defaults to false, and — its strongest sentence — that "sending the index 2 would not open the latch, it would lock the door, silently and without a fault." That reads the CODE default and stops there. The distribution overrides it. crRFD.conf:47 sets Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true, and S62HMServer:15-17 launches de.eq3.ccu.server.ip.HMIPServer with /var/etc/crRFD.conf, generated from that template with three sed lines that do not touch the flag. crRFD is the HmIP-RF interface our client writes on (the WebUI's own Interface.*Metadata_crRFD calls pass "interface":"HmIP-RF"). So on a real OpenCCU the flag is TRUE, and with it true #convertParameterValue takes the `!out && value instanceof Number` branch and maps an inbound ordinal to values[n] — the label — before it ever reaches StringEnumToInteger. Both forms work; the comment is right as written.

A second, independent Tier-1 witness on the operator surface says the same thing: door_opener.fn:202-204 and :386-388 drive LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL with the bare integers 0/1/2 via setDpState. The CCU's own lock UI uses the index form. If index writes silently locked the door, the WebUI's Open button would lock it.

What SURVIVES from the bundle, and what I add:
(a) The silent-zero fallback is real and verified verbatim — StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical initialises `byte[] b = new byte[]{0}` and returns it unchanged when nothing matches. So an unmatched value degrades to the LOCKED device value; the failure mode of this write is actuation, not rejection. That is a genuine reason to prefer the label form, and it is the honest version of the bundle's point.
(b) NEW, and the real narrowing: with the flag true, the integer form is the ORDINAL into enumStrings, not the device value. On the non-DLP variant the device values are {0, 200, 255}, so the ordinal 2 means OPEN → device 255. The init.go comment "IP locks support open (LOCK_TARGET_LEVEL=2)" is therefore correct only as a list position, and coincides with the device value only on DLP. Anyone reading it as a wire value would be wrong on every HmIP-DLD.
(c) Which variant a given device gets is selected by a ParameterMapKey qualifier ("dlp"); I could not resolve that per device type from the readable material, so the device-value half of the mapping stays unverified per device — which is exactly why writing labels rather than numbers is the right call.

all.title: FixedColorLight.Color() decodes the COLOR descriptor index as a FixedColor ordinal
all.ourValue: FixedColor ordinal BLACK=0, RED=1, GREEN=2, YELLOW=3, BLUE=4, PURPLE=5, TURQUOISE=6, WHITE=7 (color.go:451-458), applied to the raw descriptor index by Color() at color.go:581
all.firmwareValue: COLOR index order BLACK=0, BLUE=1, GREEN=2, TURQUOISE=3, RED=4, PURPLE=5, YELLOW=6, WHITE=7
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColor (enum constants BLACK(0), BLUE(1), GREEN(2), TURQUOISE(3), RED(4), PURPLE(5), YELLOW(6), WHITE(7)); the COLOR StateParameter is built from it via HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createColorSelectionParameter, whose VALUE_LIST is SimpleRGBColor#getNames(false); the same first-eight order via HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColorOpticalSignal#getNames. Independently, Tier 1 WebUI: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/opticalsignalreceiver.fn:64-65 and :72-78 (`! string listColor = "black\tblue\tgreen\tturquoise\tred\tpurple\tyellow\twhite"`, then `<option value=#loop#>` for loop=0..7 with `setDpState(oColor.ID(), this.value)` and read-back `jQuery(...).val(#oColor.Value()#)`), ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/dimmer.fn:179, and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/getColorElement.tcl:10-17 (options(0)=BLACK … options(7)=WHITE).
all.finding:
The firmware's COLOR ordinal is the RGB bit pattern (bit0=blue, bit1=green, bit2=red), not the order FixedColor enumerates. Four of eight slots differ: index 1 is BLUE (we say RED), index 3 is TURQUOISE (we say YELLOW), index 4 is RED (we say BLUE), index 6 is YELLOW (we say TURQUOISE). BLACK/GREEN/PURPLE/WHITE coincide by accident.

The ordinal is what actually arrives on the wire. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue replaces an ENUM's logical label with its index in VALUE_LIST when the flag replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal is set, and the CCU's shipped HmIP config sets it: ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true`. So every COLOR event and getValue on HmIP-BSL / HmIP-MP3P ch2-5 / HmIPW-WGC delivers the RGB-bit index, and generic.Select.Value() hands it to Color() verbatim.

Consequences on our side: ColorName(), the MQTT fixed_color field and ChannelHsColor's index leg all mislabel four of eight colours; ChannelHsColor's sibling read via custom.EnumLabelValue (label-driven) disagrees with Color(); and SoundPlayerLED writes `colorLabel := fixedColorNames[color]` (sound_led.go:337) into the put_paramset, so a mis-decoded slot is written back to the device. SetColor's optimistic `l.color.OnEvent(int32(c))` (color.go:606) also stores our ordinal, which is not the one the CCU will echo.

The write path is correct and its comment (color.go:610-613) is exactly right: a label write is accepted. Only the read path substitutes the convention.

Scope note: the `RfDimmer_Color_Fixed` profile also routes through newFixedColorConstructor for DeviceType `hbw-lc-rgbww-in6-dr` (profiles.go:210-241). That is not a firmware-shipped device — no XML under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/ declares it — so its COLOR ordering is not decidable from these sources. It does not change the verdict: the decode is shared, and it is contradicted on every device the firmware does describe.

Witness (Tier 3, explains provenance, not authority): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:63-75 declares FixedColor as a StrEnum whose members are the labels; the Python reference never carries a numeric ordinal at all, so our integer ordering is a Go-side invention with no upstream source.
all.negativeControl: Had FixedColor matched the CCU, all three independent Tier-1 orderings would have read BLACK, RED, GREEN, YELLOW, BLUE, PURPLE, TURQUOISE, WHITE. Each of them instead reads BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE, so the check does separate the two hypotheses rather than returning the same answer either way.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, and every quote re-verified against the source. The firmware's COLOR ordinal is the index into a VALUE_LIST ordered BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE. Four of eight slots differ from ours: index 1 is BLUE (we say RED), 3 is TURQUOISE (we say YELLOW), 4 is RED (we say BLUE), 6 is YELLOW (we say TURQUOISE). BLACK/GREEN/PURPLE/WHITE coincide. I additionally confirmed the two links the previous grounding left implicit: (a) COLOR really is a StringEnumToInteger ENUM, which is the precondition for the ordinal substitution in convertParameterValue, and (b) the outbound branch returns the list index rather than SimpleRGBColor's own value field — so the extended VALUE_LIST (RANDOM/OLD_VALUE/DO_NOT_CARE appended) does not shift the first eight either. Our own code already states the correct order in a comment at color.go:610-613 while Color() contradicts it.

One correction to the previous consequence list, which overstates by one item: ChannelHsColor (color.go:676-690) is entirely label-driven — it calls custom.EnumLabelValue(l.channelColor) and matches the returned CCU name against fixedColorNames, never touching an index. It is therefore correct, and it is the sibling that will visibly disagree with Color()/ColorName() on the four wrong slots. The genuinely affected surfaces are Color(), ColorName() (color.go:640-649) and everything downstream of them, plus SetColor's optimistic l.color.OnEvent(int32(c)) (color.go:606), which seeds the store with our ordinal rather than the one the CCU will echo. sound_led.go:337 (`colorLabel := fixedColorNames[color]`) is only a write-back hazard for a caller that round-trips a value it read from Color().

Scope note verified, not changed: RfDimmer_Color_Fixed also routes through newFixedColorConstructor (internal/model/custom/light/init.go:71) for DeviceType hbw-lc-rgbww-in6-dr (internal/model/custom/profiles.go:210-215). No XML under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/ or rftypes/ mentions rgbww, so that device's COLOR ordering is not decidable here — but the decode is shared and is contradicted on every device the firmware does describe.

all.title: The combined Timer stores DURATION_VALUE's descriptor default as a seconds count without reading DURATION_UNIT's default
all.ourValue: defaultSeconds := DURATION_VALUE's descriptor DEFAULT, interpreted as hmenum.TimerUnitSeconds (timer.go:123-133); DURATION_UNIT's own DEFAULT never read
all.firmwareValue: DURATION_UNIT: LogicalType.ENUM, defaultValue "S", minValue "S", maxValue "H" (siren/oldFormat) or "10MS"; DURATION_VALUE: LogicalType.INTEGER, defaultValue 0, min 0, max 16343
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDurationUnitParameter and #createDurationValueParameter; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createDurationUnitParameter and #createDurationValueParameter. Constructor argument positions confirmed against HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.StateParameter (argument 6 = defaultValue, 7 = minValue, 8 = maxValue). Registration of the siren variant: GeneralStateParameterFactory, ParameterMapKey("DURATION_UNIT", "siren") -> createDurationUnitParameter(..., oldFormat=true). Tier 2 negative check: `grep -al 'DURATION_VALUE\|DURATION_UNIT' ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml` returns nothing — the pair is HmIP-only.
all.finding:
Our rule holds on the surface our code is on. Every DURATION_UNIT-family state parameter the HmIP server constructs carries the literal defaultValue "S" — the siren variant (oldFormat=true, VALUE_LIST S,M,H), the non-siren variants (S,M,H,10MS, used for the withColor / uniLight / withRoom lights and for RAMP_TIME_UNIT and RAMP_TIME_TO_OFF_UNIT), and the climate set_point variant. There is no HmIP channel where DURATION_VALUE's default is expressed in minutes or hours, so reading the value default as seconds is right.

Two qualifications the reader should carry:

1. It is right by the firmware's construction, not by measurement. The value the code stores is still not derived from the unit parameter that is already resolved two lines above (timer.go:120). Nothing in our code would notice if a future channel type declared DURATION_UNIT DEFAULT "M". Reading unitDP's descriptor default and converting through the existing toTimerUnit path would ground it instead of leaving it resting on this audit.

2. DURATION_VALUE's declared default is 0, not a positive on-time. So DefaultDuration() on a stock HmIP siren returns 0 seconds, and the siren's "send the device default" paths (siren.go:334 and siren.go:415) send DURATION_VALUE=0 / DURATION_UNIT=S rather than a device-declared on-time. That is a separate behavioural question from the unit, and the comment at siren.go:334 ("so the device uses its declared on-time") describes something the firmware does not declare. Worth checking against a live descriptor before relying on it.

The pair does not exist on BidCos at all, so no wider scope contradicts the rule.
all.negativeControl: Had any HmIP DURATION_UNIT declared a non-seconds default, the defaultValue argument in the two factory methods that construct every parameter of this family would carry a different literal ("M" or "H") — the value is a hard-coded constructor argument, so a differing default would be directly visible. All four construction sites carry the literal "S".
all.challengeNote:
The firmware reads hold and I re-verified every literal. Demoted from confirmed to narrowed because the rule is true only inside a boundary the previous grounding did not draw, and because one firmware fact it omitted changes how the result should be read.

Boundary: combined.NewTimer has exactly one production caller — internal/model/custom/siren/siren.go:142-146, always with (ParameterDurationValue, ParameterDurationUnit) and therefore always with the HmIP `siren` variant of DURATION_UNIT (oldFormat=true, VALUE_LIST S,M,H). The other DURATION_UNIT-family parameters the previous grounding surveyed (withColor, uniLight, withRoom, RAMP_TIME_UNIT, RAMP_TIME_TO_OFF_UNIT, climate set_point) never reach this code, so their agreement is corroboration about the firmware, not about the rule. That matters because the non-siren variant carries a fourth unit, "10MS" at index 3, and toTimerUnit (timer.go:179-191) blind-casts any integer to hmenum.TimerUnit with no bounds check — a future profile that routed a non-siren DURATION_UNIT through this Timer would silently produce hmenum.TimerUnit(3). The rule is therefore safe today by the choice of caller, not by anything the Timer itself checks.

Omitted firmware fact: both DURATION_VALUE and DURATION_UNIT are declared IOOperations.WRITE in all four factory methods — write-only. The Timer's read leg (push(), valueDP.RawValue()/unitDP.RawValue(), timer.go:136-146) can therefore only ever see values our own optimistic path recorded; the device never reports these back. Combined with DURATION_VALUE's declared DEFAULT of 0, DefaultDuration() (timer.go:207-214) returns 0 s on a stock HmIP siren, so siren.go:334 and siren.go:415 send DURATION_VALUE=0 / DURATION_UNIT=S. The comment at siren.go:333-334 ("so the device uses its declared on-time") describes something the firmware does not declare; that stands as the previous agent flagged it, and it is a live behavioural question, not a unit question.

What would ground the rule instead of resting on this audit: read unitDP's descriptor DEFAULT and run it through the existing toTimerUnit path, and give toTimerUnit an explicit VALUE_LIST-bounded mapping rather than a cast.

all.title: BATTERY_STATE > 10 is used as the test for "this reading is a percentage, not a voltage"
all.ourValue: BATTERY_STATE is surfaced as a 0-100 battery percentage when its value is > 10 (availability.go:234, rationale comment at :28-31)
all.firmwareValue: BATTERY_STATE is `<logical type="float" min="1.5" max="4.6" unit="V"/>` — a cell voltage in volts, docu brief "Batteriespannung" ("battery voltage"); physical integer, `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="10.0" offset="-1.5"/>`
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2350-2359 (parameter id="BATTERY_STATE", operations="read,event", logical float min=1.5 max=4.6 unit="V"; declared inside `<channel index="4" type="CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER">` at :2309); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml:2313-2319; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:5211-5220. Those three files are the complete set: `grep -aln BATTERY_STATE ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/hs485types/*.xml` returns exactly them. The HmIP side never declares it — no occurrence of BATTERY_STATE anywhere in HMIPServer or HMServer.
all.finding:
The descriptor answers this without a threshold and answers it the other way. BATTERY_STATE is a cell voltage in volts on every device that declares it — HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM and HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU, all three with the identical logical block min=1.5 max=4.6 unit="V". No device XML in the firmware declares BATTERY_STATE as a percentage, in millivolts, or with any unit but V. HmIP has no BATTERY_STATE at all (it carries OPERATING_VOLTAGE plus OPERATING_VOLTAGE_STATUS instead — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory, ParameterMapKey("OPERATING_VOLTAGE","highRes") and ("OPERATING_VOLTAGE_STATUS")).

So `f > 10` cannot be satisfied by any firmware-declared BATTERY_STATE: the declared maximum is 4.6. The branch at availability.go:234 is dead code, not a mis-scaling risk — the bundle's "3000 %" / "12 %" damage scenario has no device behind it. What it does cost is the opposite of what the comment claims: for the three thermostats that do report BATTERY_STATE, no battery level is surfaced at all.

A second, independent reason the branch never fires: BATTERY_STATE is declared on channel 4 (CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER) on HM-CC-RT-DN, while channel0Float (availability.go:179-180) looks only at `<address>:0`. So even a hypothetical percentage-valued BATTERY_STATE would not be found where the code looks.

The honest replacement is the declared UNIT: the descriptor carries unit="V" together with MIN/MAX, and Channel.ParameterFloatRange already exposes it. Note this is a Tier-2 grounding — the rfd firmware itself carries no BATTERY_STATE semantics; the device XMLs are what the daemon reads at runtime, so they are the right authority for this question, and they and the runtime descriptor cannot disagree here (they are the same document).
all.negativeControl: Had BATTERY_STATE been a percentage on any family, at least one `<parameter id="BATTERY_STATE">` block would carry unit="%" with a 0..100 logical range — the pattern the same files use for VALVE_STATE (`<logical type="integer" min="0" max="99" default="0" unit="%"/>`, rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2365). All three BATTERY_STATE declarations instead carry unit="V" min="1.5" max="4.6", so the check distinguishes the two cases.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld and strengthened. Every one of the three device XMLs declares BATTERY_STATE identically as a cell voltage, min 1.5, max 4.6, unit V — no device XML in the firmware declares it as a percentage, in millivolts, or with any other unit. `f > 10` cannot be satisfied by any firmware-declared BATTERY_STATE, so the branch at availability.go:234 is dead code, not a mis-scaling risk; the bundle's "3000 %" damage scenario has no device behind it. The cost runs the other way: on the three thermostats that do report BATTERY_STATE, no battery level is surfaced at all.

Two additions to the previous grounding. First, the channel argument generalises: the previous agent named channel 4 for HM-CC-RT-DN only, and I confirmed the other two — HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM is also channel 4, and HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU is channel 2 (THERMALCONTROL_TRANSMIT). None of the three is on `:0`, and channel0Float looks only at `<address>:0`, so the branch is unreachable for a second, independent reason on every declaring device. Second, an independent Tier-2 corpus (pydevccu) is silent on BATTERY_STATE, which removes the possibility that some non-shipped descriptor carries a percentage form.

Tier is 2 and correctly labelled: the rfd firmware source carries no BATTERY_STATE semantics of its own; the device type XMLs are what the daemon reads at runtime, and here the shipped XML and the runtime descriptor are the same document, so they cannot disagree. The honest replacement remains the declared UNIT, which the descriptor carries together with MIN/MAX and which Channel.ParameterFloatRange already exposes.

all.title: Whose authority says an ENUM write travels as a label string rather than an index?
all.ourValue: A non-empty VALUE_LIST means the wire value is the label string; an empty VALUE_LIST means send the integer index (action_select.go:110-140). Authority cited today: the Python sibling's _enum_value_is_index only.
all.firmwareValue: Both families accept the label string AND the integer index on write. BidCos/Wired: an Int is taken as the VALUE_LIST index; anything else is matched against the option ids and replaced by that index. HmIP: a String logical value passes through the legacy conversion untouched and is mapped to the physical byte by the enum converter; an Integer is mapped to the label first.
all.citation: BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired (shared libhsscomm): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:72-92 — `if(val->getType() == XmlRpcValue::TypeInt){ int& v=(int&)*val; if(v<0)v=default_option; if(v>=(int)options.size())v=default_option; } else { std::string s_val=*val; ... for(unsigned int i=0;i<options.size();i++)if(options[i]==s_val){ *val=(int)i; return true; } *val=atoi(s_val.c_str()); return true; }`. Reached on every write via ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:296-300 (`HSSParameter::SetValue` -> `EnforceConstraints(inst, &log_temp, HSSLogicalType::OP_WRITE)`), and on read/event via the same file at :241 (OP_READ) and :352/:370 (OP_EVENT). Descriptor shape: HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:94-112 — `(*val)["TYPE"]="ENUM"; (*val)["MIN"]=int(0); (*val)["MAX"]=int(options.size()-1); (*val)["DEFAULT"]=int(default_option); VALUE_LIST = options`. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue (inbound branch converts a Number to the label; a String on the inbound path matches no branch and is returned unchanged) together with HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.StringEnumToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical (matches the logical String against enumStrings and emits the mapped byte). Flag state on a shipped CCU: ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true`.
all.finding:
Our encoding is accepted by the firmware on both interface families, and the acceptance set is wider than the code assumes: label and index are both accepted on write everywhere, so TriggerLabel and TriggerIndex are both valid on either family. The VALUE_LIST-emptiness test is therefore a safe-by-construction choice rather than a protocol requirement.

Two real differences worth recording, neither of which our current code gets wrong but both of which it is one edit away from getting wrong:

1. BidCos fails a bad label silently, not loudly. In HSSLogicalTypeOption::EnforceConstraints, a string that matches no option id falls through to `*val=atoi(s_val.c_str())` and returns true — a misspelt label writes option 0, with no fault. Our TriggerLabel validates against Descriptor.ValueList before dispatching (action_select.go:128-131), which is exactly what keeps this from biting; that guard is load-bearing and should stay.

2. The two families spell the descriptor's DEFAULT differently, and the read direction differs in kind. BidCos reports DEFAULT as an integer index (`(*val)["DEFAULT"]=int(default_option)`), while the HmIP server stores an ENUM parameter's defaultValue as the label string. That is precisely the both-forms case DefaultLabel already handles at action_select.go:46-70, so that comment is confirmed against firmware rather than inherited. On the read side, BidCos values are integers by construction (EnforceConstraints converts a string to an index before the value is stored), and HmIP values are integers too on a stock CCU because crRFD.conf enables ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal — the index into VALUE_LIST, not the enum's own numeric value where those differ (e.g. SimpleRGBColor RANDOM=253 is index 8 when the extended list is used).

The file's stated authority can now be the firmware rather than the Python sibling.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU rejected a label string, HSSLogicalTypeOption::EnforceConstraints would have had no string branch at all — it would return false for anything but TypeInt, the way HS485LogicalTypeAddress and the boolean/float types constrain their own inputs — and HMIPServer DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue would have taken its `else if (out || !(value instanceof String))` diagnostic branch on an inbound String write. Neither happens: the BidCos path explicitly resolves the label to an index and returns true, and the HmIP path leaves the label for the enum converter.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld. I re-read every cited quote and the constructor/dispatch chain around it, and I added the one check the previous grounding did not perform: whether the BidCos half answers a surface our ActionSelect actually reaches. It does. Five BidCos device XMLs declare write-only parameters with `<logical type="option">`, which our resolver builds as an ActionSelect — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_rc_19.xml (UNIT, BEEP, BACKLIGHT), rf_ou_led16_ge_v1_1.xml (LED_SLEEP_MODE) and rf_resc_win_pcb_sc.xml (SHEV_POS). So TriggerLabel can genuinely reach HSSLogicalTypeOption::EnforceConstraints on OP_WRITE, and the grounding is not answering a hypothetical.

Our encoding is accepted on both families, and the acceptance set is wider than the code assumes: label and index are both accepted on write everywhere, so TriggerLabel and TriggerIndex are both valid on either family. The VALUE_LIST-emptiness test is a safe-by-construction choice, not a protocol requirement.

The two differences the previous agent recorded both hold, and both matter:
1. BidCos fails a bad label silently. In EnforceConstraints, a string matching no option id falls through to `*val=atoi(s_val.c_str()); return true;` — a misspelt label writes option 0 with no fault. TriggerLabel validates against Descriptor.ValueList before dispatching (action_select.go:126-129), which is what prevents this; that guard is load-bearing.
2. The families spell DEFAULT differently. BidCos reports it as an integer index (`(*val)["DEFAULT"]=int(default_option)`), while HmIP stores an ENUM parameter's defaultValue as the label string (visible in every GeneralStateParameterFactory ENUM constructor, e.g. createDurationUnitParameter passing "S" and createAcousticAlarmSelectionParameter passing enumStrings[0]). DefaultLabel already accepts both forms at action_select.go:59-70, so that comment is now grounded on firmware rather than inherited.

On the read side, BidCos values are integers by construction and HmIP values are integers too on a stock CCU because crRFD.conf enables ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal — and the ordinal is the index into VALUE_LIST, not the enum's own numeric value where those differ (SimpleRGBColor RANDOM=253 is index 8 when the extended list is used; I confirmed convertParameterValue returns the loop index, not the value field). The file's stated authority can now be the firmware rather than the Python sibling.

all.title: HM-CC-VG-1 SET_TEMPERATURE bounds 4.5 / 30.5 overwrite the CCU-declared MIN/MAX
all.ourValue: MIN rewritten to 4.5, MAX rewritten to 30.5 on HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE (VALUES), unconditionally at paramset ingest; Reason string "CCU returns invalid MIN/MAX bounds for virtual heating groups (0/0 or string)"
all.firmwareValue: min="5.0" max="30.0" default="20.0" unit="°C" type="FLOAT" operations="7" control="HEATING_CONTROL.SETPOINT" aggregation="LAST"
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml:504-505 — `<status_parameter aggregation="LAST" control="HEATING_CONTROL.SETPOINT" default="20.0" max="30.0" min="5.0" name="SET_TEMPERATURE" operations="7" tab_order="4" type="FLOAT" unit="°C">`, inside `<channel id="1" type="CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER">` (:433) of the file's single `<group>` (:3), whose `<virtual_device_type>` is HM-CC-VG-1 (:8113). The runtime paramset description is built from those attributes verbatim by HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.GroupDeviceHandler#createParamsetDescriptions -> #createHashMapFromParameterValues, which puts parameter.getMax() / parameter.getMin() into the RpcStruct; those accessors are declared String-typed on HMServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.bidcos.BidCosVirtualChannelParameter. Comparison value: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2392-2395 — HM-CC-RT-DN's own SET_TEMPERATURE is `<logical type="float" min="4.5" max="30.5" default="20.0" unit="°C">`.
all.finding:
The firmware does declare bounds for this parameter, and they are not the ones we write. HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE is declared min=5.0, max=30.0, default=20.0, unit=°C. Our patch replaces that with 4.5 / 30.5 — which are exactly HM-CC-RT-DN's own logical bounds (rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2395), i.e. the member device's range substituted for the group's. The group is deliberately narrower than its members.

Direction of the error: the patch widens the range on both ends. A setpoint of 4.5 or 30.5 now passes our validation and the SPA slider now offers it, and both are outside the range the CCU declares for the group.

Half of the patch's Reason is corroborated and half is not:
- "or string" is confirmed. GroupDeviceHandler copies parameter.getMin()/getMax() straight into the description, and both accessors are String-typed on BidCosVirtualChannelParameter, so the CCU really does report MIN and MAX for this parameter as XML-RPC strings rather than doubles. A patch that coerces the string form to a number is well founded.
- "0/0" is not. Nothing in the group definition or in the description-building path produces 0/0 for SET_TEMPERATURE; the declared values are "5.0" and "30.0". If a real CCU was observed returning 0/0, that observation is unaccounted for by these sources and should be re-measured before the numbers are changed.

What the patch should carry, on this evidence: keep the string→number coercion, and use 5.0 / 30.0. Note also that DEFAULT (20.0) and UNIT (°C) are declared and currently untouched by the patch.

One scope caveat, stated as unverified: HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.rfd.legacy.VirtualDefinitionFactory#fillChannelParameter can build a channel parameter's min/max from a member device's ParameterDescription instead of from the shipped XML. I did not establish which of the two paths serves a runtime HM-CC-VG-1, so I cannot exclude a configuration in which the group inherits HM-CC-RT-DN's 4.5/30.5. The shipped group definition is unambiguous and is the authority I can cite; if the inheriting path is live, the answer would be 4.5/30.5 and our patch would be right for the wrong stated reason. Settling that needs a getParamsetDescription capture from a real CCU with a heating group.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware genuinely left this parameter's bounds unset or at 0/0, the `<status_parameter>` element would carry no min/max attributes or min="0" max="0", and GroupDeviceHandler would have put null or "0" into the description. It carries min="5.0" max="30.0" — and the neighbouring ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE in the same channel carries min="-10.0" max="50.0", showing the attributes are populated per parameter rather than boilerplate.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, and the one caveat the previous grounding left open is now closed in its favour. HM-CC-VG-1 channel 1 SET_TEMPERATURE is declared min=5.0, max=30.0, default=20.0, unit=°C. Our patch replaces that with 4.5 / 30.5 — the member device's range substituted for the group's — widening the accepted range by 0.5 K at each end, so a setpoint of 4.5 or 30.5 now passes our validation and the SPA slider offers it.

Resolving the open caveat: VirtualDefinitionFactory#fillChannelParameter, the path that could have made the group inherit a member's ParameterDescription bounds, is called only from HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.rfd.legacy.RFD2VirtualDeviceConverter — which is a developer-side generator, not a runtime path: it carries a `public static void main` and hard-coded source paths of the form D:/SVN/HomeMatic/devicetypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml. The live path is the shipped file, named in Constants and HMServerConfiguration as above. So the inheriting configuration the previous agent could not exclude is not live, and 5.0 / 30.0 is what a real CCU serves.

A second, independent reason the answer cannot be 4.5/30.5: BidCosVirtualChannelParameter's own field initialisers are min "5.0", max "30.0", default "20.0". Whether the group-definition parser fills those attributes or leaves them at the class defaults, SET_TEMPERATURE comes out 5.0 / 30.0 either way.

Provenance, stated as unverified as to intent: the shipped group values do not match what the generator would produce from today's device XML — HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU channel 2 SET_TEMPERATURE is 4.5/30.5, and MANU_MODE (4.5/30.5) and ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE (-10.0/50.0) in the same group channel did carry through from the device, while the four ACTION parameters (AUTO_MODE, BOOST_MODE, COMFORT_MODE, LOWERING_MODE) all carry a nonsensical min 5.0 / max 30.0, i.e. the class defaults. So 5.0/30.0 for SET_TEMPERATURE may be a class-default leftover rather than a deliberate narrowing. That does not change what the CCU serves, and it is what our patch must not contradict.

The Reason string splits as the previous agent found. "or string" is confirmed — getMin/getMax are String-typed and copied verbatim into the description, so MIN and MAX really do arrive as XML-RPC strings; the coercion half of the patch is well founded, and DEFAULT ("20.0") and UNIT ("°C") arrive the same way and are currently untouched. "0/0" is not corroborated anywhere in the group definition or the description-building path and should be re-measured before the numbers are trusted.

all.title: The per-model MASTER channel whitelist encodes 30 devices' channel layouts with no firmware citation
all.citation: Tier 2 (deciding): ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-DRDI3.json — MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is declared on VCU6948166:1,:2,:3,:4,:8,:12. At :4/:8/:12 the declared fields are TYPE=ENUM, VALUE_LIST=['OFF','ON'], DEFAULT='ON', MIN='OFF', MAX='ON', OPERATIONS=3, FLAGS=1; at :1/:2/:3 they are VALUE_LIST=['INACTIVE','KEY_BEHAVIOR','SWITCH_BEHAVIOR','BINARY_BEHAVIOR'], DEFAULT='KEY_BEHAVIOR'. ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-DRDI3.json gives channel TYPE=MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER for 1/2/3 and DIMMER_TRANSMITTER for 4/8/12. Tier 1 (shape, not the numbers): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory registers CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE once per channel-specification subtype key (distinct value lists per key: an {OFF,ON} variant, an {OFF,ON,ON_LED} variant, {INACTIVE,KEY_BEHAVIOR,SWITCH_BEHAVIOR,BINARY_BEHAVIOR}, {SHUTTER,BLIND}, {NORMAL_MODE,SILENT_MODE}, the HEAT_DEMAND_* set, the SENSOR_ES_* set, …) — never per model plus channel number. Tier 1 for the descriptor's own reach: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config carries no CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE entry at all (it maps only Control/Unit/TabOrder metadata), so that file cannot settle this question.
all.finding:
Contradicted at HmIP-DRDI3. Our value: Channels {1,2,3} (rules.go:79-82). Firmware/descriptor value: {1,2,3,4,8,12}. Channels 4, 8 and 12 are the DIMMER_TRANSMITTER channels and their CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is the {OFF,ON} channel-enable flavour, a different knob from the {INACTIVE,KEY_BEHAVIOR,…} input mode on 1/2/3 — but it is declared, writable (OPERATIONS=3) and today never becomes a data point, because decider.go step 3 default-skips every MASTER parameter without a whitelist hit.

Everything else in the table that the corpus can reach is confirmed exactly: HmIP-DRBLI4 {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,13,17,21}; HmIP-MIO16-PCB {13,14,15,16}; HmIP-DRSI1 {1}; HmIP-DRSI4 {1,2,3,4}; HmIP-DSD-PCB {1}; HmIP-FCI1 {1}; HmIP-FSI16 {1}; HmIP-MOD-RC8 channelRange(1,9)={1..8}; HmIPW-DRBL4 {1,5,9,13}; HmIPW-DRI32 channelRange(1,33)={1..32}; HmIPW-FIO6 channelRange(1,7)={1..6}; ELV-SH-TACO {2}; HmIP-RGBW ch0 DEVICE_OPERATION_MODE. Climate side confirmed too: HmIP-BWTH {1,8} (ch1 = MIN_MAX_VALUE_NOT_RELEVANT_FOR_MANU_MODE/OPTIMUM_START_STOP/TEMPERATURE_{MAXIMUM,MINIMUM,OFFSET}, ch8 = HEATING_VALVE_TYPE); key "HmIP-WGT" prefix-matches the real model HmIP-WGTC, whose climate MASTER sits at 8 and 14 — {8,14} correct; HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU / HM-CC-VG-1 carry theirs on the device-level MASTER, which the empty-Channels wildcard covers.

The structural half: because the firmware attaches CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE to a channel specification, not to a (model, channel) pair, a per-model channel table cannot be complete by construction. Thirteen further models in the 399-device descriptor corpus declare MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE and get no entry and no prefix hit — HmIP-DLP {2,3,12}, HmIP-ESI {1}, HmIP-SAM {1}, HmIP-SMO230-A {4}, HmIP-SPDR {2,3,4}, HmIP-STV {1}, HmIP-SWO-B/-PL/-PR {2}, HmIP-UDI-SMI55 {3,6}, HmIPW-DRD3 {1,5,9} — plus HmIP-eTRV-2/-C-2/-F, which do match the "HmIP-eTRV" key but whose Parameters set is climateMasterParameters, so their CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE ({NORMAL_MODE,SILENT_MODE} per the factory) is withheld; same for HmIP-HEATING:1, which declares both the climate set and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE. Not verifiable from these sources: HmIP-FCI6 channelRange(1,7), HmIP-FSI6 {1} and HmIPW-DRI16 channelRange(1,17) — those three models are absent from the descriptor corpus and from the shipped BidCos XMLs.
all.negativeControl: Had the table been right, the per-model channel sets extracted from paramset_descriptions/*.json would have matched every entry the corpus can reach, and no model outside the table would have declared MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE. The extraction did produce a different answer in both directions — one exact mismatch (DRDI3, three extra channels) and thirteen uncovered models — while returning byte-for-byte agreement on the other twelve entries, so the check discriminates rather than agreeing by construction.
all.ourValue: HmIP-DRDI3 → Channels {1, 2, 3}
all.firmwareValue: HmIP-DRDI3 → MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE on channels {1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12}
all.challengeNote: UPHELD as contradicted, and strengthened from Tier 2 to Tier 1 on the operator surface — but the prior agent's completeness claim is wrong and I widened the boundary. Corpus re-measured over all 399 paramset_descriptions: 29 models declare MASTER CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE (the prior report listed 28 — it omitted 'HmIP-eTRV-2 I9F'). Every channel-operation-mode entry it called confirmed does check out exactly: DRBLI4 {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,13,17,21}, MIO16-PCB {13,14,15,16}, DRSI1 {1}, DRSI4 {1,2,3,4}, DSD-PCB {1}, FCI1 {1}, FSI16 {1}, MOD-RC8 {1..8}, HmIPW-DRBL4 {1,5,9,13}, HmIPW-DRI32 {1..32}, HmIPW-FIO6 {1..6}, ELV-SH-TACO {2}. The claim 'Climate side confirmed too' is NOT sound: I re-ran the same measurement over the climate MASTER set and found six further models that declare a whitelisted climate parameter and get no entry and no prefix hit — HmIP-FAL230-C10 ch0 and HmIPW-FAL230-C6 ch0 (HEATING_VALVE_TYPE), HmIPW-SCTHD ch1 and HmIPW-WTH ch1 (the key 'HmIP-WTH' does not prefix 'HmIPW-WTH' — the 'W' falls where the '-' is), HmIP-SCTH230 ch4 and ELV-SH-CTH ch1 (TEMPERATURE_OFFSET) — plus ELV-SH-TACO ch1 TEMPERATURE_OFFSET, which the model's own entry (ch2, CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE only) actively withholds. HmIP-STE2-PCB ch1/ch2 is also uncovered but is named as deliberate in decider.go's own comment. Where I demote the framing rather than the verdict: the descriptor settles which channels DECLARE the parameter and the WebUI settles which the CCU EXPOSES, but neither carries our data-point policy, so 'contradicted' is exact as a channel-layout claim and is not a firmware statement about what should be whitelisted. Damage is also smaller than the bundle's damage clause says: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is in hiddenParameters, so even a whitelisted hit is marked NoCreate for UI/MQTT — the missing entries deny applyChannelOperationModeGating an input, they do not withhold a rendered knob.

all.title: Out-of-int32 values are silently clamped and then written to the CCU
all.site: internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:14-27 (toXMLRPCInt32), :72 and :76 (int / int64 cases of goToXMLRPCValue); reached from binrpc_caller.go:30-39 as well
all.citation: Tier 1, the CCU's own XML-RPC codec: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:34-36 `static const char INT_TAG[] = "<int>"; static const char I4_TAG[] = "<i4>";`; :260 `else if (typeTag == I4_TAG || typeTag == INT_TAG)` — both tags accepted on parse; :499-509 `int32_t ivalue = strtol(valueStart, &valueEnd, 10); … _value.asInt = int(ivalue);` — no ERANGE check; :511-521 `intToXml()` emits `<i4>` only; :233 the union member is `int asInt`. BIN-RPC uses the same value class: :533-545 `intFromStream` does `memcpy(&v, data, 4); v=ntohl(v); _value.asInt = int(v);` and :547-556 `intToStream` writes `htonl(_value.asInt)` — a fixed 4-byte integer, no wider form. Tier 2: across ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml (148 files) the largest `<logical type="integer" max=…>` is 65536 (rftypes/rf_es_tx_wm.xml, rf_es_tx_wm_le_v1_0.xml); across the 399-device ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions corpus, zero parameters with TYPE=INTEGER declare a MIN, MAX or DEFAULT outside [-2147483648, 2147483647] — the extremes are RSSI_DEVICE/RSSI_PEER MIN=-2147483648, exactly math.MinInt32. HmIP config parameters are bit-fields: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory builds them with create8bitInteger / create9bitInteger / create14bitInteger / create16bitInteger / create24bitInteger / createSigned8bitInteger / createSigned24bitInteger — 24 bits is the widest.
all.finding:
The premise is confirmed and the surface is confirmed: `<i4>` (or the equivalent `<int>`) is the only integer the CCU's XML-RPC codec has, it is stored and emitted as int32_t, and BIN-RPC — the CUxD path that reuses the same helper — is a fixed 4-byte network-order integer with no wider form. No integer parameter anywhere in the shipped device XMLs or the descriptor corpus reaches the int32 boundary from outside; the >int32 magnitudes that do exist are all TYPE=FLOAT (ENERGY_COUNTER MAX 1.099e11 on HmIP-ESI, `max="109951162.7775"` in rftypes/rf_es_tx_wm.xml) and travel as `<double>`, which goToXMLRPCValue routes to DoubleValue without touching the clamp.

Where it narrows: the clamp-versus-fault choice is not something the firmware decides, and the comment's word "defensive" overstates what the firmware would do. rfd's parser has no overflow detection either (strtol result assigned straight into int32_t with no ERANGE test, XmlRpcValue.cpp:501-506), so a substituted 2147483647 would be accepted and acted on exactly like a value the caller asked for — the CCU can neither reject nor report it. The clamp is therefore not a guard the CCU backs up; it is a silent substitution whose only justification is that no descriptor-declared parameter can reach it. That justification holds for every value that came from a parameter descriptor and does not extend to the helper's actual contract: goToXMLRPCValue accepts any Go `int`/`int64` argument from any caller and never consults the descriptor's MIN/MAX, so the safety rests on the callers, not on the type. I did not enumerate every caller, so the boundary is stated, not measured.
all.negativeControl: Had the rule been wrong I would have found either an integer wider than 32 bits in the CCU's own codec — a long/int64 branch in XmlRpcValue, or a BIN-RPC integer longer than 4 bytes — or at least one TYPE=INTEGER parameter declaring MIN/MAX outside int32. The same two scans did surface out-of-int32 magnitudes (the FLOAT energy counters) and did surface a second integer tag (`<int>` alongside `<i4>`), so they were capable of returning a different answer; they returned int32 for every integer path.
all.ourValue: n > math.MaxInt32 → math.MaxInt32; n < math.MinInt32 → math.MinInt32, then sent
all.firmwareValue: int32_t on both wires (`<i4>`/`<int>` parsed into int32_t, `<i4>` emitted; BIN-RPC integer = 4 bytes ntohl/htonl); no ERANGE check on receipt either
all.challengeNote: UPHELD as narrowed. Every quote verifies verbatim and the XML-RPC half now has the link evidence it was missing. Two narrowings the prior grounding did not name, both of which cut against its reassurance. (1) SURFACE: the BIN-RPC half is grounded on rfd's codec, and our binrpcCaller does not talk to rfd — binrpc_caller.go's own comment says 'CUxD shares the XML-RPC value set', and CUxD is a closed third-party add-on with no source in OpenCCU-Base, OpenCCU or any reference tree here. rfd is the protocol's reference implementation, so the 4-byte claim is well founded for BIN-RPC as specified, but it is not a measurement of the peer this code path reaches. That leg is unverified for CUxD. (2) The descriptor-extreme statement understates the risk. I re-ran the scan and the corpus does reach the ceiling from inside: MAX = 2147483647 is declared on writable MASTER parameters — CYCLIC_INFO_MSG_OVERDUE_THRESHOLD on 124 channels, CENTRAL_ADDRESS on 11, AES_KEY on 1 — alongside the read-only RSSI_DEVICE/RSSI_PEER/NEXT_TRANSMISSION/LED_STATUS pairs the prior report cited. So the value the clamp substitutes is itself a legally declared MAX for a writable parameter: rfd accepts it (strtol straight into int32_t, no ERANGE), acts on it, and neither side can tell it apart from a value the caller intended. That is a stronger statement of the same defect, not a weaker one. The prior report's own residual stands unchanged: goToXMLRPCValue never consults a descriptor MIN/MAX, so the safety rests entirely on callers, and I did not enumerate them either.

all.title: The 10 s CONFIG_PENDING settle delay is a comment-claim about CCU internals with a duty-cycle consequence
all.site: internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:20-28 (configPendingSettleDelay) and the doc block at :45-63 that repeats the rationale
all.citation: Tier 1, the HmIP path our hook is actually gated to: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getParameterSet maps getParamset(address, "MASTER") to BackendCommandType.DEVICE_CONFIG_GET; de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.BackendCommandHandler routes that to de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleGetConfigCommand, whose whole body issues PersistenceCommandType.PERSISTENCE_COMMAND_LOAD_DEVICE_CONFIGURATION on the persistence bus; de.eq3.cbcs.persistence.kryo.KryoPersistenceWorker#loadSpecificDevice answers it by deserialising the device's persisted config file (with the .new/.old rename dance). The over-the-air read is a different command entirely — DEVICE_CONFIG_ASK → DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleAskConfigCommand → TransactionSubsystemCommandType.DYNAMIC_TRANSACTION_COMMAND_START_CONFIG — and getParamset never reaches it. Ordering: de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.task.TransactionTaskFactory#createDeviceConfigurationTransaction appends the tasks in the order SendFrame(setParameterByIndex…) → SendFrame(commitParameterSetting) → PersistenceTask(PERSISTENCE_COMMAND_SAVE_DEVICE_CONFIGURATION) → CyclicTimeoutUpdateTask → NotifyDeviceConfigurationPendingChangedTask; de.eq3.cbcs.persistence.kryo.KryoPersistenceWorker#saveDevice is a synchronous write-then-rename. Tier 1, the BidCos path: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFLogicalInstance.cpp:35-45 — `RFConfigData& cd=config_data[…]; if(!cd.MustBeRead(list))return &cd; … if(cd.ReadFromDevice(this, list))`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFConfigData.h:99-106 documents the gate as `must_be_read` — "Flag für 'Es wurden noch keine Daten vom Gerät übernommen'", cleared by `SetRead()`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1384-1389 `RequestSave(){ //Next time we are idle, Save() will be called\n KillTimer(TIMER_SAVE); RequestTimer(0, TIMER_SAVE); }` and :765-767 calls `RequestSave()` immediately before `CheckConfigPendingEvent()`.
all.finding:
Both halves of the stated mechanism are contradicted, on both interface daemons.

On HmIP — the only surface the hook runs on, since it is gated by hmenum.PushesConfigPendingFor — getParamset(MASTER) is answered from the server's persisted device file and never initiates a radio transaction, at any delay. So "reading earlier would … force a fresh radio validation" and "the carenz is what makes the read duty-cycle-neutral" are wrong: the read is duty-cycle-neutral at 0 s just as much as at 10 s. Worse for the rationale, the file save is task #3 and the CONFIG_PENDING notification is task #5 of the same transaction task list, so on the normal write path the configuration is already on disk before we are told CONFIG_PENDING went False. There is one narrower path where a window exists at all — AbstractPersistency#savePendingDeviceConfiguration sends createAndSendConfigPending before its own saveDevice call when cleanupPendingDeviceConfiguration turns the flag off — and there the consequence of reading early is a stale value, not radio traffic, on a window bounded by one synchronous file write plus rename.

On BidCos, rfd holds MASTER values in memory (config_data) and consults the disk file only at load; a getParamset(MASTER) issues a radio read exactly when `must_be_read` is still set for that list, i.e. when the chunk has never been read from the device — not on any freshness or file-cache condition. And rfd requests its save before it emits the CONFIG_PENDING event, with a 0-ms idle timer.

The 10 s value itself: not-performable to ground. No firmware source carries a settle interval for this transition; the only durations in either daemon's path are a 0-ms idle timer and one synchronous file write. The number is a client-side choice, and the code should say that rather than attribute it to a CCU mechanism.
all.negativeControl: Had the comment been right, handleGetConfigCommand would have queued a transaction on the transaction subsystem (as handleAskConfigCommand does) rather than a persistence load, and the transaction task list would have put NotifyDeviceConfigurationPendingChangedTask before the PersistenceTask; on the rfd side, MustBeRead would have tested a timestamp or a save-in-flight flag rather than a never-read flag. The same reads did find a genuinely radio-bound sibling command (DEVICE_CONFIG_ASK) and a genuinely notify-before-save ordering (savePendingDeviceConfiguration), so the check produced both answers and is not agreeing with itself.
all.ourValue: 10 s carenz, justified as: reading earlier races the CCU's on-disk file-cache update and forces a fresh radio validation
all.firmwareValue: HmIP: getParamset(MASTER) = PERSISTENCE_COMMAND_LOAD_DEVICE_CONFIGURATION, a file read that never reaches the radio; the config file is saved as an earlier task than the CONFIG_PENDING notification. BidCos: MASTER served from in-memory config_data, radio read gated solely on the per-chunk must_be_read ("never yet read from the device") flag; RequestSave() = 0-ms idle timer, issued before the event.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD as contradicted, and I could not find a surface on which the comment's mechanism is true. The path check holds: the hook is gated by hmenum.PushesConfigPendingFor (pkg/hmenum/interface.go:136-144), which returns true for ProductGroupHmIP/HmIPW, false for HM/HmW, and otherwise defers to the interface — so HmIP (RF, Wired, and HmIP-flavoured VirtualDevices groups) is the only surface it runs on, and that surface is HMIPServer. Three additions that make the contradiction sharper, not softer. (1) The mode escape is closed: LegacyServiceHandler computes internalMode and discards it, so no getParamset argument selects the radio path. (2) The ordering is stronger than 'earlier in a list': PersistenceTask awaits the persistence reply through TransactionManagement, so the config file is on disk before the CONFIG_PENDING notification is emitted on the normal write path. (3) The residual risk the prior agent granted — 'the consequence of reading early is a stale value' on the savePendingDeviceConfiguration path — is itself smaller than stated, because processDeviceConfigurationCommand merges the pending configuration over the committed one in the reply, so a read inside that window still returns the new values. The BidCos citations verify verbatim but describe a daemon this hook never runs on; they are corroborating, not load-bearing. On the number itself I agree the verdict is not-performable: no firmware source in any tree carries a settle interval for this transition, and the only durations on either daemon's path are rfd's 0 ms idle save timer and HMIPServer's 5 s persistence-task timeout. The 10 s is a client-side choice and the comment should say so instead of attributing it to a CCU file-cache race.

all.title: The Homematic address grammar used to anonymise shared RPC traces is a bare regex with no source
all.site: internal/central/adapter/rpc_recorder.go:311-314 (hmAddressPattern), :316-360 (anonymiseExport / anonymiseString, which also rewrites map keys)
all.citation: Tier 1, BidCos: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosFrame.h:57 `FIELD_SYSINFO_SERIAL = STRUCTURED_FRAME_FIELD_STR(12, 10)` and :79 `FIELD_CONFIG_SERIAL = STRUCTURED_FRAME_FIELD_STR(11, 10)` — the serial is a 10-byte string field, with no alphabet constraint anywhere. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:298-309 `ParseAddress` splits on the first ':' and takes the channel with `atoi` (unbounded); :311-335 the second overload accepts an alternate form `@<hex>`: `if (address.size() && address[0]=='@') … *dev_address = strtoul(address.substr(1).c_str(), NULL, 16);` — otherwise the device part is looked up verbatim in dev_instances/team_instances, with no format check at all. Tier 1, HmIP: ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:20 `Legacy.AddressPrefix=3014F711A0`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getDeviceLegacyAddress returns `id.substring(addressPrefix.length())`, i.e. the device SGTIN with those 10 leading characters removed, and #getDeviceID / #getChannelIndex treat `CENTRAL_DEVICE` and `ALL_SMOKE_DETECTORS` as named pseudo-addresses and parse the channel with an unbounded Integer.parseInt. HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.GroupDeviceAddressHelper#getVirtualDeviceAddressFromGroup builds group virtual-device addresses as "INT" + the group id left-padded or right-truncated to exactly 7 digits. Tier 2 for the channel ceiling: highest channel index in the shipped device XMLs is 63 (../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_central.xml and hs485types/hmw_central.xml, `index="63"`); highest in the 399-device ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions corpus is 50 (HmIP-RCV-50, VCU4264293:50).
all.finding:
True for the addresses a CCU actually hands out today, false one step wider, and the boundary is specific.

In scope: HmIP legacy addresses are the 24-character SGTIN minus the configured 10-character Legacy.AddressPrefix, i.e. 14 hex — the exact top of the regex's 12-14 hex branch. Group virtual devices are "INT" + 7 digits, which the [A-Z]{2,4}\\d{6,8} branch matches. BidCos serials in practice are 3 letters + 7 digits inside a 10-byte field, also matched. Channel indices top out at 63 across the shipped device XMLs and 50 across the descriptor corpus, so `:\\d{1,2}` covers every channel the fleet has.

Outside it, three things the firmware does carry and the regex does not. (1) rfd accepts an `@`-prefixed hex radio address (`@1A2B3C`) as a first-class address form; 6 hex digits fall below the 12-hex floor, so such a token would pass through a trace unhashed. (2) The BidCos serial is only length-constrained — 10 bytes, no alphabet — and rfd validates nothing; a serial that is all digits, or contains lowercase, matches neither branch. Conversely a 12-14 character hex-looking token that is not an address (a session id, an AES_KEY, a hex-encoded paramset value) is hashed, and because anonymiseString also rewrites map keys, that silently corrupts a golden replay. (3) The 2-digit channel cap and the 12-14 / 6-8 length windows are bounds the firmware does not carry: both rfd (atoi) and HMIPServer (Integer.parseInt) accept any channel integer, and neither SGTIN length nor serial alphabet is asserted anywhere I could read. The named pseudo-addresses BidCoS-RF, CENTRAL_DEVICE and ALL_SMOKE_DETECTORS correctly fall outside the pattern and stay legible.

One residual I could not settle: the SGTIN's own length is not stated in any source I read; the 14-character legacy address follows from the 10-character prefix plus the 24-character SGTIN observed in practice, and the prefix half is the only part I cite from firmware.
all.negativeControl: Had the grammar matched what the CCU emits, the address-construction sites would each have produced a form inside the pattern. Reading them produced two that are not (`@<hex>` in RFManager.cpp, and the unconstrained 10-byte serial field) and one bound the firmware declines to impose (unbounded channel parse), while confirming the 14-hex HmIP form and the INT+7-digit group form — so the check separated the halves rather than confirming the whole.
all.firmwareValue: BidCos: 10-byte serial field, no alphabet, plus an `@`+hex alternate form, channel via unbounded atoi. HmIP: SGTIN minus the configured 10-char Legacy.AddressPrefix (3014F711A0) → 14 hex; groups "INT"+7 digits; channel via unbounded Integer.parseInt; named pseudo-addresses CENTRAL_DEVICE / ALL_SMOKE_DETECTORS. Highest channel index shipped: 63.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD as narrowed. Every quote verifies and the in-scope claim holds: 14-hex HmIP legacy addresses, 'INT'+7-digit group addresses, 3-letter+7-digit BidCos serials and channels up to 63 are all covered, and BidCoS-RF / CENTRAL_DEVICE / ALL_SMOKE_DETECTORS correctly fall outside and stay legible. Three things the prior grounding missed or got wrong. (1) NEW leak class, firmware-carried: addressPrefix is a configuration value defaulting to "", set only by crRFD.conf. With the property absent, getDeviceLegacyAddress returns the full SGTIN — 24 characters in practice — which is outside the 12-14 window and would pass through a shared trace UNHASHED. The prior grounding treated the 10-character prefix as fixed; it is not. (2) I ran the pattern as a measured negative control rather than reasoning about it. Leaks: '@1A2B3C' and '@1A2B3C:1' (rfd's first-class alternate form, 6 hex, below the floor), a 10-digit all-numeric serial, and a lowercase serial — the 10-byte BidCos serial field constrains length only, never alphabet, and rfd validates nothing. False positives: '123456789012' and '1756900000000' both match the hex branch, and because internal/store/session/recorder.go:65-67 renders every parameter with fmt.Sprintf("%#v", params) into the Params string AND into the slot key, a numeric parameter in that width becomes such a token and is replaced with 'anon:<12 hex>' in both key and value. 'OEQ1234567:255' matches only the serial, leaving ':255' in clear — harmless, but it shows the 2-digit cap is a convention: rfd uses atoi and HMIPServer Integer.parseInt, both unbounded. (3) NEW latent defect: pkg/hmlog/capture.go:341 returns "anon:" + 12 hex digits, and after a ':' the \b holds, so the anonymiser's own output matches its 12-hex branch. Single-pass ReplaceAllStringFunc means it does not bite today; a second anonymise pass over an exported trace would re-hash. Why this stays narrowed rather than confirmed: the 12-14 window's upper bound follows from a 24-character SGTIN, and I could not read that length from any Tier-1 source either — I searched the HmIP address helpers, the WebUI's SGTIN handling and src/multimacd's CoproState_GetSgtin path and found no length assertion. That input is missing, so the ceiling half is not-performable and the prior agent was right to flag it.

all.title: Week-profile capability is inferred from the P*_* MASTER parameter name pattern, a convention the descriptor does not state
all.site: internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:2013-2023 (the P*_* branch calling attachWeekProfileToChannel), internal/central/adapter/week_profile_filter.go:69-91 (attach, ProfileCount: 6) and :606-613 (isWeekProfileSlotParameter, Schema A + Schema B)
all.citation: Tier 1, how the CCU picks the channel: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/hmip/ dispatches a config dialog by channel TYPE — the file is named after the channel type (HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:18 calls getHeatingClimateControlTransceiver; BLIND_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl, DIMMER_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl, DIMMER_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl, SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl, SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl, WATER_SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl) — or by paramset id (hmip-wth_1_master.tcl, named after getParamsetId). Tier 1, how many profiles: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:2925 `set weeklyPrograms 3`, :2929-2932 `set param P6_TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1 / if { [info exists ps($param)] == 1 } { set weeklyPrograms 6 }`, :2934-2936 forced back to 3 by the 'only3WeeklyProgramms' argument, which hmip-wth_1_master.tcl:24-27 passes when the device firmware is <= 1.5. Tier 1, slots per day: hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:3003-3012 `for {set i 1} {$i <= 13} {incr i} { set timeout $ps($pNr\_ENDTIME_${day}_$i) … if {$timeout == 1440} then {break} }`, over the day list SATURDAY SUNDAY MONDAY TUESDAY WEDNESDAY THURSDAY FRIDAY. Tier 1, the other schedule schema: hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:26-46 reads 01_WP_DURATION_FACTOR / 01_WP_RAMP_TIME_FACTOR / 01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET — the *_WEEK_PROFILE channels use NN_WP_* names, no P prefix. Tier 2: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml declares exactly 546 P-prefixed ids = P1/P2/P3 x 182, slots 1..13 per day, alongside WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER; rf_cc_rt_dn.xml (and rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml) declare the bare form ENDTIME_<DAY>_1..13 / TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_1..13, 182 ids, on the device-level paramset cc_rt_dev_master. ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HMIP-PS.json: VCU1366171:6 (channel TYPE SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE) carries 750 MASTER parameters, all NN_WP_*, and no P*_* at all.
all.finding:
The heuristic picks the right channels in scope but is not the CCU's mechanism, and two of the numbers around it are off.

In scope it is clean. Across all 148 shipped device XMLs, P<n>_ ids occur in exactly one file (rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml) and are always TEMPERATURE/ENDTIME; across the 399-device descriptor corpus, every P<n>_ parameter without exception has body TEMPERATURE or ENDTIME (9555 each) and appears only on climate channels. No false positive, and no climate channel is missed — HM-CC-RT-DN's device-level MASTER uses the bare form, which Schema B catches.

The mechanism is different, though. The CCU never scans parameter names to decide that a channel carries a week program: it selects the editor by channel TYPE, or by the paramset id from getParamsetId. It uses a name test only for the profile count, and even there the test is the presence of P6_TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1 (default 3, 6 if present), further gated on the device firmware version for hmip-wth. Our refinement pass reads ACTIVE_PROFILE / WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER MAX instead — a different input that happens to agree everywhere in the corpus (ACTIVE_PROFILE MAX 3 on every eTRV that stops at P3, MAX 6 on every device that has P6; WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER MAX 2 with a 3-entry VALUE_LIST on the two BidCos models), but agreement is not the same rule and nothing pins it.

Where the boundary runs: the *_WEEK_PROFILE channel-type family (BLIND, DIMMER, DIMMER_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR, SERVO, SHADING, SWITCH, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT, WATER_SWITCH — 45 models in the corpus) carries a week program in the CCU's own view with NN_WP_* names and zero P*_*, so this branch attaches nothing there. That is not the "no schedule surface at all" the bundle describes: week_profile_filter.go:93-97 reaches those through a separate signal (WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS), so the damage claim is narrower than stated — but the consequence that does survive is that a SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE channel's ~750 NN_WP_* MASTER parameters are not filtered by this branch the way the ~182 climate slot parameters are.

One factual correction to the comment at device_pipeline.go:2004-2008: it says "~14 slots" and "6 profiles x 7 days x ~14 slots = 84+". The firmware says 13 — the WebUI loop is `i <= 13`, and rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml / rf_cc_rt_dn.xml / every climate channel in the descriptor corpus declare slots 1..13 exactly. 6 x 7 x 13 x 2 (TEMPERATURE + ENDTIME) = 1092 parameters on a 6-profile channel, not 84.
