all.negativeControl: Had the P*_* pattern been the CCU's own capability signal, the easymode dispatch would have been keyed on parameter names rather than on channel type / paramset id, and the *_WEEK_PROFILE channels would have carried P-prefixed slot parameters. Reading them produced the opposite in both places — a type-keyed dispatch, and a second, disjoint NN_WP_* schema — while the corpus scan simultaneously confirmed the pattern has no false positives, so the check distinguished "selects the right set" from "is the same rule" instead of collapsing them.
all.ourValue: one P*_* slot parameter on MASTER ⇒ this channel carries a week profile; ProfileCount 6, refined later from ACTIVE_PROFILE / WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER MAX; comment says ~14 slots
all.firmwareValue: channel selected by channel TYPE or paramset id; profile count = 3, or 6 iff P6_TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1 exists (forced to 3 on hmip-wth firmware <= 1.5); 13 slots per day; *_WEEK_PROFILE channels use NN_WP_* names and no P prefix
all.challengeNote: UPHELD as narrowed, with one half of the prior grounding DEMOTED and one new narrowing of the stakes. What survives, verified: the profile-count rule (default 3, 6 on P6_TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1, forced 3 for hmip-wth fw <= 1.5), the 13-slot loop, and the NN_WP_* schema of the *_WEEK_PROFILE family. The '~14 slots' correction is right and I confirmed it twice over — the WebUI loop is `$i <= 13` and the descriptor corpus's maximum slot index is 13 across 19110 parameters with no exception, so 6 x 7 x 13 x 2 = 1092, not 84. In-scope soundness of our heuristic is confirmed exactly as claimed: zero false positives (every P<digit>_ id in the corpus is a climate slot) and no missed climate channel (HM-CC-RT-DN's device-level bare form is caught by Schema B). DEMOTION: the prior grounding's lead claim — 'how the CCU picks the channel: it dispatches a config dialog by channel TYPE ... never by scanning parameter names' — is not read from a dispatcher. I searched for the code that selects www/config/easymodes/hmip/<CHANNEL_TYPE>.tcl and found none: the only easymode dispatch in the tree is ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:665 `if { $paramid != "" && [file exists easymodes/$paramid.tcl] }` inside cmd_set_profile — the paramset-id form, and on the SAVE path, not the render path — and the producer of $paramid / $new_profilepath is not in this tree. 'The file is named after the channel type' is a property asserted about a directory layout, which is exactly the tell: it is strong circumstantial evidence and it is not a read value. That half is unverified as stated; what IS verified is the narrower and more interesting fact that the firmware's only name test is the P6_TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1 presence check, i.e. the firmware does use a name heuristic, just for the count rather than for the channel. NEW narrowing of the consequence: the prior report's surviving damage claim — that a SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE channel's ~750 NN_WP_* parameters are not filtered the way climate slots are — is true as a hydration statement but produces no visible-entity difference. internal/store/visibility/decider.go:292 computeIgnoredMaster calls checkMasterParameterIgnored, whose step 3 default-skips every MASTER parameter with no whitelist hit; HmIP-PS has no relevantMasterParamsetsByDevice entry, and no NN_WP_* or P*_* name is in any Parameters set, so both families end up forced to NoCreate. The asymmetry is a memory and hydration cost, not ~750 ghost topics.

all.title: The BidCos duty-cycle 'unknown' encoding is a negative-value sentinel with no cited source
all.ourValue: DUTY_CYCLE is a percent in 0..100; a value below zero means "not available"; unknown ⇒ (0,false) ⇒ no warning; risky at >= 80
all.firmwareValue: percent 0..100 confirmed; -1 IS emitted, but only by the coprocessor-backed gateway classes. The base class reports 0 when never polled. Threshold 80 with `>=` confirmed verbatim.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosInterface.h:215 `//! Setzt DutyCycle; verschickt bei Bedarf Ereignisse (Wertebereich 0-100)`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/hm2/CCU2CommController.cpp:1180-1181 `*dutyCycle = (*dutyCycle) >> 1; //Values are from 0 to 200 -> Convert to 0% to 100%`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/hm2/CCU2BidcosRemoteInterface.cpp:542-547 `int dutyCycle = -1; pCommController->getDutyCycle(&dutyCycle); return dutyCycle;`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosInterface.cpp:58 `duty_cycle = 0;` and :294-297 `int BidcosInterface::GetDutyCycle() const { return this->duty_cycle; }`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosInterface.cpp:26-32 (CreateFromType: "CCU"→RFController, "Lan Interface", "USB Interface" use the base; "CCU2"/"HMLGW2"/"HM-MOD-UART"→CCU2BidcosRemoteInterface); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:1266 `descr["DUTY_CYCLE"] = iface->GetDutyCycle();`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/listbidcosinterfaces.tcl:12 `dutyCycle: [integer] Duty Cycle (0 - 100)` and :31; ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0068-WebUI-Fix-isDutyCycleOK4DevUpdate.patch `dcWarningLevel = 80`, `dcVal = (typeof iFace.dutyCycle != "undefined") ? parseInt(iFace.dutyCycle) : 0;`, `if (dcVal >= dcWarningLevel) { dcOK = false; }`
all.finding:
CONFIRMED: unit and range. rfd's own comment fixes the value range at 0-100 and the coprocessor read halves a 0..200 raw byte to 0..100. The JSON-RPC handler our client calls documents the same range and always emits the key (it appends `"dutyCycle":<DUTY_CYCLE>` unconditionally), so the "missing field" damage case cannot arise on our path.

CONFIRMED: -1 is a real firmware value, not an invention. CCU2BidcosRemoteInterface::GetDutyCycle initialises its local to -1 and returns it unchanged; CCU2CommController::getDutyCycle (:1167-1185) leaves the out-parameter untouched when the system command fails or the response is empty. That -1 flows straight into descr["DUTY_CYCLE"] and then into the JSON `dutyCycle` string.

NARROWED — the boundary: -1 is emitted only by the CCU2/HMLGW2/HM-MOD-UART class (the internal coprocessor of a CCU3/RaspberryMatic, and HM-LGW gateways). The base BidcosInterface::GetDutyCycle returns a member initialised to 0 and only ever overwritten by a reported value, so for a "CCU" (RFController), "Lan Interface" or "USB Interface" gateway the never-polled state reports 0 — indistinguishable from an idle radio. Our `< 0` test therefore does not detect "unknown" for those classes. The error is permissive (0 < 80 ⇒ no warning), which is exactly what the CCU's own gate does.

CONFIRMED: threshold and direction. Our `>= 80` is the WebUI's `isDutyCycleOK4DevUpdate` verbatim, and its unknown-handling (`undefined ⇒ 0 ⇒ OK`) is the same direction as our `ok=false ⇒ no warning`. Our selection rule differs (we prefer isDefault, then the highest duty cycle; the WebUI takes the first gateway with type == "CCU2" and stops) — strictly more conservative, so no risk in the permissive direction.

SIDE FINDING (presentation only): `carrierSense` does not exist on this path. RFManager::ListBidcosInterfaces sets ADDRESS/DESCRIPTION/TYPE/DUTY_CYCLE/FIRMWARE_VERSION/DEFAULT/CONNECTED only, and listbidcosinterfaces.tcl emits address/description/dutyCycle/isConnected/isDefault/fwVersion/type. `BidcosInterface.CarrierSense` is therefore always -1 on this firmware; our comment at methods.go:653-655 ("most CCU firmwares do not report this") is correct but understated — this one never does.

reachesDevice=false: the handler never rejects the update (device_admin.go:255-260, 274-277); the value only fills an advisory `duty_cycle_warning` field.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong, CCU2BidcosRemoteInterface::GetDutyCycle would have initialised its local to 0 (or the tcl handler would omit the key / emit a sentinel string), and isDutyCycleOK4DevUpdate would have carried a threshold other than 80 or a `>` rather than `>=`. I read all three: the local is -1, the key is unconditional, the test is `dcVal >= 80`. The check also did produce a different answer in one direction — it found the base-class 0 path, which is why the verdict is narrowed rather than confirmed.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD on the substance, with two corrections to the boundary the previous pass drew.

Re-checked and confirmed: the range comment in BidcosInterface.h; the >>1 halving of a 0..200 raw byte; the -1 local in CCU2BidcosRemoteInterface::GetDutyCycle together with CCU2CommController::getDutyCycle leaving the out-parameter untouched on failure/empty response; DUTY_CYCLE being the only duty-cycle key RFManager writes; the .tcl emitting `dutyCycle` unconditionally (so bidcosPercent's absent-key branch is unreachable on this path); and the WebUI threshold `>= 80` verbatim in patch 0068. I also confirmed the override set: BidcosInterface::GetDutyCycle is `virtual` and CCU2BidcosRemoteInterface is its only overrider in the tree.

CORRECTION 1 to the previous narrowing. It lumped "Lan Interface" with "never reports". That is wrong: BidcosLanInterface derives from BidcosRemoteInterface, whose CMD_HELLO handler calls SetDutyCycle(msg.GetUIntParam(PARAM_INDEX_HELLO_DUTYCYCLE)) whenever the HELLO carries >= 8 parameters (BidcosRemoteInterface.cpp:496-507). A LAN/USB gateway therefore does report a real duty cycle, pushed on HELLO; 0 is only its pre-first-HELLO state. The class that genuinely never reports anything is RFController (type "CCU"): it inherits the base GetDutyCycle, is not a BidcosRemoteInterface, and no code in src/rfd/ calls SetDutyCycle on it — so its DUTY_CYCLE is a constant 0. The corrected boundary: -1 ("unknown") is emitted only by CCU2/HMLGW2/HM-MOD-UART; LAN/USB report 0 until their first 8-parameter HELLO; "CCU" reports 0 forever.

CORRECTION 2 — a blind spot the previous pass did not name. Patch 0068 falls back to `Interface.listBidcosInterfaces{interface:"HmIP-RF"}` when the BidCos-RF call returns null, i.e. on an HmIP-only CCU the WebUI still reads the coprocessor's duty cycle. loadBidcosInterfaces (hub_wiring.go:1828-1832) skips every client whose Interface != hmenum.InterfaceBidCosRF, so on such a CCU our cache stays empty and no warning is ever produced. Permissive, same direction as the rest, but it is a named gap rather than "strictly more conservative".

Selection rule re-read (aggregateBidcosGateways, hub_wiring.go:1857-1882): default wins, else highest duty cycle. Confirmed as described, and confirmed permissive — a default gateway reporting -1 shadows a non-default at 90.

Side finding on carrierSense: upheld and now exhaustive. I grepped src/ and www/ for CARRIER_SENSE/carrierSense: the only hits are the multimacd serial-frame layer and the MAINTENANCE.CARRIER_SENSE_LEVEL data point rendered by ReGa control pages. Neither RFManager::ListBidcosInterfaces nor listbidcosinterfaces.tcl carries the field, and no patch under buildroot-external/patches/occu/ touches that .tcl. `BidcosInterface.CarrierSense` is therefore always -1 on this path; the comment at methods.go:653-655 should say "never", not "most".

all.title: The updateDevice hint values (0 = firmware, 1 = link partner) are a bare literal with only a comment behind them
all.ourValue: hint is an enum-like value; 0 = "firmware update notification", 1 = "link partner change"; every other value is a logged no-op
all.firmwareValue: `enum{UPDATE_HINT_ALL=0, UPDATE_HINT_LINKS=1};` — declared an enum, exactly two members. 0 is named ALL, not FIRMWARE.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.h:46-47 `//! Enum für den Parameter \c hint der XmlRpc-Methode updateDevice` / `enum{UPDATE_HINT_ALL=0, UPDATE_HINT_LINKS=1};`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:1173-1178 `void RFManager::ReportUpdate(const std::string& address, int hint) { ... XmlRpcCallAsync("updateDevice", params); }`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:756 and :868 `ReportUpdate(..., RFManager::UPDATE_HINT_LINKS)`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:480 (AddLink) and :535 (RemoveLink) `(int&)params[2]=UPDATE_HINT_LINKS;`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1597-1625 `RFDevice::Rebuild()` … :1619-1620 `if(RFManager::GetSingleton()->CallUpdateDeviceOnOTAUDeviceRebuild()) { ReportUpdate(this->serial, HSSManager::UPDATE_HINT_ALL); } else { ReportNewDevice(this); }`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:654 `/** \brief If true, Device->Rebuild() calls XmlRpc method updateDevice instead of newDevices. Default is false. */`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:48 `callUpdateDeviceOnOTAUDeviceRebuild = false;` and :219-221 `config_file.GetStringValue("Call UpdateDevice On OTAU Device Rebuild", "false")`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyBackendClient#updateDevice, de.eq3.ccu.bidcos.dispatcher.BidCosRpcDispatcher#updateDevice, de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyNotificationHandler, de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyBackendNotificationHandler
all.finding:
CONFIRMED, and the bitmask worry is refuted outright. The header comment names it "Enum für den Parameter hint der XmlRpc-Methode updateDevice" and the enum has exactly two members, 0 and 1. There is no combined value for `hint != 0` to drop, and no third code for a firmware change.

CONFIRMED for hint=1: every emitter of UPDATE_HINT_LINKS is a link-peer add or remove (RFChannel.cpp:756/868 on the RF side, HS485Manager AddLink/RemoveLink on the wired side). Our no-op-beyond-logging matches.

NARROWED on hint=0, three ways:

(a) The constant means ALL ("everything about the device changed"), not "firmware". In rfd the single emitter is RFDevice::Rebuild(), which does run after an OTA firmware update — it re-reads the version from the FirmwareManager, replaces the description and re-creates the channels — so our handler's *reaction* (invalidate the firmware cache, re-fetch device descriptions) is the right one. But a reader of our `const hintFirmware = 0` cannot tell that a description-only change would arrive under the same code.

(b) Emitting updateDevice(0) at all is off by default. rfd only calls it when the config key "Call UpdateDevice On OTAU Device Rebuild" is set; the default is the string "false" and the member is initialised to false. On a default CCU, an OTA rebuild produces **newDevices**, not updateDevice(hint=0). So this handler is not the primary post-OTA refresh path — our NewDevices handler (callback_handlers.go:543ff, which re-parses descriptions into the hot-plug ingestor) is. Anything that only updateDevice does — the explicit `InvalidateFirmwareCache` call — does not run on the default path.

(c) The HmIP legacy surface never sends it. HMIPServer's LegacyBackendClient#updateDevice is a relay for the BidCos dispatcher (BidCosRpcDispatcher#updateDevice forwards the hint it was handed); the handlers that notify registered legacy clients about device changes — LegacyNotificationHandler and LegacyBackendNotificationHandler — emit newDevices and deleteDevices only. On HmIP-RF this callback does not fire.

reachesDevice=false: the handler only invalidates a cache and re-reads descriptions.
all.negativeControl: Had hint been a bitmask, HSSManager.h would declare powers of two or a mask constant and would not say "Enum"; it declares 0 and 1 under an explicit enum comment. Had 0 meant something unrelated to firmware, its only rfd emitter would not sit inside RFDevice::Rebuild() immediately after the firmware version is re-read. The check did bite in one direction — it turned up the default-false config gate and the HmIP silence, which is why this is narrowed and not confirmed.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD, and one part of the previous narrowing strengthened.

Re-verified independently: the enum has exactly two members and the header comment binds it to `updateDevice`'s hint parameter, so there is no bitmask and no third code — the "hint != 0 drops a combined value" worry is refuted. `grep -rn '"updateDevice"' src/ www/` returns exactly five emit sites: RFManager::ReportUpdate and the four HS485Manager calls, all of which set UPDATE_HINT_LINKS. Every UPDATE_HINT_LINKS emitter is a link add or remove (RFChannel::RemoveLinkPeer at :756 and the AddLinkPeer pairing loop at :868; HS485Manager::AddLink/RemoveLink, each emitting twice, once per endpoint). Our hint=1 no-op is right.

(a) Confirmed: the constant is ALL, not FIRMWARE. In rfd the sole hint=0 emitter is RFDevice::Rebuild(), which re-reads the version from the FirmwareManager, replaces the description and re-creates the channels — so our reaction is appropriate, but `const hintFirmware = 0` misnames the wire contract, and the comment on UpdateDevice ("handles a firmware-update notification (hint=0)") asserts a semantics the firmware does not carry.

(b) Confirmed and tightened: the flag defaults to false in the member initialiser and in the config lookup's default string, and I could find no shipped configuration that flips it — neither ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/rfd.conf nor ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/RFD/etc/config_templates/rfd.conf mentions "Call UpdateDevice On OTAU Device Rebuild". So on a stock OpenCCU an OTA rebuild takes the `else` branch and emits **newDevices**. Our hint=0 branch — including the only call to InvalidateFirmwareCache on this path — does not run on the default configuration. That is the load-bearing narrowing: the comment presents this handler as the post-OTA refresh path, and it is not.

(c) NEW, and it cuts against reading hint=0 as "firmware" at all: the CCU's own consumer of this callback, BidCosRpcDispatcher#updateDevice, branches on `hint == 0 || hint == 1` and does the *same* thing for both — refresh its BidCos link-info cache for the device (stripping any `:channel` suffix) — then fans the (address, hint) pair out to its IBidCosUpdateDeviceListener list. eQ-3's own code treats 0 and 1 as interchangeable link-cache invalidations.

(c') The previous pass's HmIP claim survives, with a caveat I am obliged to state. LegacyBackendClient#updateDevice exists and delegates to the RPC proxy, but no caller for it appears anywhere in the readable HMIPServer material, while the two notification handlers that push device changes to registered legacy clients emit only newDevices and deleteDevices. IRegaClient#updateDevice is likewise declared and uncalled. Caveat: this material cannot prove the absence of a reflective or proxy-generated caller, so "HmIP-RF never fires this callback" is *supported*, not settled — treat it as unverified in that one direction.

What the code should say: hint 0 = ALL ("anything about the device may have changed"), hint 1 = LINKS; there is no firmware-specific code; and hint 0 arrives from rfd only when a non-default config key is set.

all.site: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:2190-2213 (vn0/vn1 substitution, then the create_system_variable ReGa run); internal/client/rega/scripts/create_system_variable.fn (writes ValueName0/1 unconditionally for BOOL and ALARM)
all.ourValue: "false" / "true" are "the CCU's own defaults" for both BOOL and ALARM
all.firmwareValue: BOOL: exactly "false" / "true" — the CCU's own SysVar.createBool script writes those literals. ALARM: the readable CCU source carries no creation default at all.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createbool.tcl — the ReGa body of SysVar.createBool: `sv.ValueType( ivtBinary ); sv.ValueSubType( istBool ); sv.Name(name); sv.ValueName0("false"); sv.ValueName1("true"); sv.State(init_val);`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:758 `function ::saveSysVar()` with :813-820 (istAlarm) and :821-829 (istBool) both `sv.ValueName1(system.GetVar("sTrue")); sv.ValueName0(system.GetVar("sFalse"));`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/systemvars.htm:330-336 `newSysVar = function() { ... all.finding:
CONFIRMED for BOOL, verbatim. The CCU's own JSON-RPC create path — the ReGa script embedded in www/api/methods/sysvar/createbool.tcl, which is what our own `SysVar.createBool` shortcut at hub_wiring.go:2160-2166 invokes — hard-codes the English literals `sv.ValueName0("false")` and `sv.ValueName1("true")`. Our substitution is byte-identical to what the CCU writes for itself. The comment's claim is sourced for this half.

NARROWED at the ALARM boundary — but not in the direction the reader's damage note assumed. Tier 1 is silent on an ALARM creation default:

- There is no `SysVar.createAlarm` API method (www/api/methods/sysvar/ carries createbool, createenum, createfloat, and setters only).
- The only readable ReGa creator that handles istAlarm, `system.fn::saveSysVar()`, writes whatever the dialog passed in `sTrue`/`sFalse` and defines no default of its own. It does the same for istBool — the built-in default lives only in the JSON-RPC script.
- The create/edit dialog itself is a ReGaHss-internal page (`CreatePopup(ID_NEW_SYSVAR)`); ReGaHss ships as a binary and its source is not in this tree (only the Tcl bridge src/tclrega is), so whatever it pre-fills is not readable here.

The German alarm labels that do exist in the tree — "ausgelöst" / "nicht ausgelöst" — are written by bin/hm_autoconf onto the factory-provisioned "Alarmzone 1" variable at first configuration. That is a specific provisioned object, not a default the CCU applies to a newly created ALARM variable, so the bundle's premise ("for an ALARM variable the WebUI default is a pair of German alarm labels") is itself unsourced.

What our rule then rests on for the ALARM branch: nothing in the CCU source. It is a carry-over of the BOOL default. The write is real and persistent — create_system_variable.fn sets ValueName0/1 unconditionally inside the ALARM branch, so an operator creating an ALARM sysvar through the daemon gets English boolean words on a CCU object, and the daemon offers no way back.

reachesDevice=false: the write lands on a ReGa system-variable object on the CCU, not on a device.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong for BOOL, createbool.tcl would have set localized labels, left ValueName0/1 unset, or used different tokens — it sets the literals "false"/"true". Had a built-in ALARM default existed, it would have appeared either in an api/methods/sysvar create script (there is none for ALARM) or as a literal in system.fn's istAlarm branch (there is none — it reads sTrue/sFalse from the caller); I checked both, which is what makes the silence a measurement rather than a failure to look.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD for BOOL, verbatim; the ALARM half stays ungrounded and should be labelled so in the code.

BOOL: I read createbool.tcl in full. Its embedded ReGa script hard-codes `sv.ValueName0("false")` and `sv.ValueName1("true")` — the same two English literals we substitute — and this is the exact method hub_wiring.go:2160-2166 shortcuts to when no unit, description or custom labels are supplied. Our substitution on the Rega fallback path is byte-identical to what the CCU writes for itself. Sourced.

ALARM: I re-ran the search rather than trusting the previous pass. `ls www/api/methods/sysvar/` confirms there is no createAlarm method at all. The only readable ReGa creator that handles istAlarm is system.fn::saveSysVar, and I read both branches: for istAlarm and istBool alike it writes whatever the dialog passed in sTrue/sFalse and defines no fallback — grepping sTrue/sFalse across www/rega/, www/webui/ and src/webui/ returns only these two write sites plus unrelated `lblIsTrue`/`lblIsFalse` condition labels. The dialog that supplies them is a ReGaHss-internal page reached via `CreatePopup(ID_NEW_SYSVAR)`; only the Tcl bridge ships as source, so whatever it pre-fills is not readable in these trees. Tier 1 is silent for the ALARM creation default.

I also confirm the previous pass's demolition of the bundle's own premise: the German pair "ausgelöst"/"nicht ausgelöst" comes from bin/hm_autoconf's `create_sysvars`, which provisions the factory "Alarmzone 1" object at first configuration. That is one named object, not a default applied to newly created ALARM variables — so "the WebUI default for ALARM is a pair of German alarm labels" was itself unsourced.

The write is real: in create_system_variable.fn the ALARM branch calls `oNew.ValueName0(sValueName0); oNew.ValueName1(sValueName1);` unconditionally, and hub_wiring.go fills empties with "false"/"true" for ALARM as well as BOOL. An operator creating an ALARM sysvar through the daemon gets English boolean words on a CCU alarm object, and the daemon exposes no way back. That is a defensible product choice; it is not "the CCU's own default", and the comment at hub_wiring.go:2190-2192 claims it is for both types.

One unrelated divergence noticed while reading, recorded so it is not mistaken for parity later: createbool.tcl also calls `sv.State(init_val)` and adds the variable to the channel's DPs collection (`channel.DPs().Add(sv.ID())`); our ReGa script sets `oNew.Channel(iChnId)` only and never sets an initial State for BOOL. Outside this rule's scope, but it is a real difference between the two create paths.

all.title: Pairing inbox hides every entry whose address starts with "INT"
all.ourValue: Heating-group backing serial = "INT" + zero-padded group id; filter the inbox on `strings.HasPrefix(address, "INT")` or the VirtualDevices interface
all.firmwareValue: `virtualDevicePrefix = "INT"`; `createVirtualDeviceSerialNumber(id) = virtualDevicePrefix + padLeft(id, 7)` where id is the group id — so "INT" + the group id zero-padded to 7 digits. But the CCU's own inbox listing filters on `chn.Internal() == false`, not on the address prefix.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/common/viewmodels.js:1 `virtualDevicePrefix = "INT";`, :98-100 `function padLeft(nr, n, str){ return Array(n-String(nr).length+1).join(str||'0')+nr; }`, :102-104 `function createVirtualDeviceSerialNumber (id) { return virtualDevicePrefix+padLeft(id,7); }`, :128-134 `function VirtualGroup(id, name, ...) { selfGroup.id = id; var temp = createVirtualDeviceSerialNumber(selfGroup.id); selfGroup.virtualDeviceSerialNumber = temp; }`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:2922 `if {[string equal [string range $address 0 2] "INT"] == 1} { set isGroup "_group" }`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/views/newdevicechannelsloader.htm:7-14 `foreach( sID, oUser.UserTempViewIDs2().EnumEnabledIDs(...) ) ... if ( (chn.Name() != "") && (oDev.ReadyConfig() == false) && (chn.Internal() == false) )`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_add_device.cgi:885-891 `foreach( tmp, obj.EnumEnabledIDs() ) ... if (elem && (elem.ReadyConfig() == false) && (elem.Name() != 'Gateway'))`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/xml-api/newdevicelist.xml:27-30 `foreach(sDevId, root.Devices().EnumUsedIDs()) { ... if ( false == oDevice.ReadyConfig() )`
all.finding:
CONFIRMED, verbatim and with the missing pad width supplied: the CCU WebUI's own constant is `virtualDevicePrefix = "INT"` and its serial builder is `"INT" + padLeft(id, 7)` — zero-padded to a total width of 7, giving a 10-character serial. The caller is `VirtualGroup(id, ...)`, so the id is the group id, exactly as our comment says. The firmware also performs the same three-character prefix test we do, in hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl, to decide "this address is a group". Our test is the CCU's own test, not a convention we invented.

NARROWED — the boundary is the *mechanism*, not the prefix. The CCU's own inbox listing does not filter on the prefix at all; it filters on the ReGa `Internal()` flag at channel level (newdevicechannelsloader.htm:14). The count query (cp_add_device.cgi) uses `EnumEnabledIDs()` with `ReadyConfig()==false && Name() != 'Gateway'`, and the XML-API newDeviceList walks `EnumUsedIDs()` with `!ReadyConfig()` and applies no virtual filter whatsoever. Our get_inbox_devices.fn walks `dom.GetObject(ID_DEVICES).EnumIDs()` with `!ReadyConfig() && Name() != "Gateway"` and never reads `Internal()`. So:

- Our enumeration is the widest of the four (EnumIDs vs EnumEnabledIDs / EnumUsedIDs), and
- any CCU-internal object that is neither INT-prefixed nor on VirtualDevices reaches our inbox although the CCU's own inbox excludes it via `Internal()`.

The cheap improvement is to have the ReGa script carry `oDev.Internal()` (or the channel-level flag) and filter on that, which is what the firmware does — then the prefix test becomes a belt-and-braces addition rather than the whole rule.

The second half of the reader's question — whether a genuine device serial can legitimately begin with "INT" — is not decided by any source in these trees; nothing enumerates the reserved serial prefixes. The strongest true statement is that our filter is exactly as safe as the CCU WebUI's own group test, which uses the identical three-character comparison.

reachesDevice=false: this filters a list; it performs no write.
all.negativeControl: Had the group serial not been "INT" + a zero-padded group id, createVirtualDeviceSerialNumber would have shown a different composition (a different prefix, a different pad width, or an address taken from the device rather than built from the id) — I read the builder, the padder and the caller. Had the CCU's inbox filtered on the prefix, newdevicechannelsloader.htm would test `chn.Address()` instead of `chn.Internal()`; it tests Internal(), which is the difference that makes this narrowed.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD, and the grounding upgraded from a client-side reconstruction to the authoritative producer — plus one part of the previous narrowing demoted.

UPGRADE. The previous pass grounded the serial format on WebUI JavaScript, which only *reconstructs* the address to look a device up. The producer is on the HmIP side: GroupDeviceAddressHelper#getVirtualDeviceAddressFromGroup takes IGroup.getId(), pads it with leading zeros until its length is exactly 7 (and, for ids longer than 7 digits, keeps the last 7 — the WebUI's padLeft does not truncate), then returns "INT" + that. Its inverse, #getGroupIdFromVirtualDeviceAddress, strips an optional ":channel" and requires the "INT" prefix. Two independent classes carry the constant as GroupDeviceIdentifier = "INT", and both group-device dispatchers classify an address with `address.startsWith("INT")` — the CCU performs our exact test on the address, not merely a three-character range comparison in a Tcl dialog. So "INT" + a 7-character group id is read from the source, not assumed; the earlier grounding's missing pad width is now sourced from the producer rather than inferred from the consumer.

NARROWING RETAINED (mechanism). Re-read all three CCU inbox surfaces: newdevicechannelsloader.htm filters channels on `chn.Internal() == false` alongside `oDev.ReadyConfig() == false`; cp_add_device.cgi's count walks ID_DEVICES with EnumEnabledIDs plus `ReadyConfig()==false && Name() != 'Gateway'`; newdevicelist.xml walks EnumUsedIDs with `!ReadyConfig()` alone. Our get_inbox_devices.fn walks ID_DEVICES with EnumIDs and `!ReadyConfig() && Name() != "Gateway"`, and never reads Internal(). Our enumeration is the widest of the four and our virtual test is a different mechanism from the CCU's. Carrying `oDev.Internal()` out of the ReGa script and filtering on it is the cheap alignment; the prefix test then becomes belt-and-braces.

DEMOTED. The previous pass asserted that "any CCU-internal object that is neither INT-prefixed nor on VirtualDevices reaches our inbox although the CCU's own inbox excludes it via Internal()". Nothing I read establishes that such an object exists with ReadyConfig()==false; that is an inference from the mechanism difference, not a measurement. State it as "the mechanisms differ and could diverge", not as a known leak.

STILL OPEN, unchanged: whether a genuine device serial can legitimately begin with "INT" is decided by no source in these trees — nothing enumerates reserved serial prefixes. The strongest true statement remains that our filter is exactly the CCU's own group test.

all.title: 'MAX greater than 1.0 means the device supports last-known-level' is a comment-claim, and the 1.005 sentinel named in the comment is nowhere in the code
all.site: internal/central/adapter/uischema_link.go:175-181 (`if meta.DisplayAsPercent && rawFloatGreaterThan(p.Max, 1.0) { p.HasLastValue = true }`); assets/ui/src/lib/components/parameter/ParameterLevelField.svelte:37-40 and :153 (`{#if !readOnly && parameter.has_last_value && max > 1 + 1e-6}`)
all.ourValue: MAX > 1.0 (Go: rawFloatGreaterThan(p.Max, 1.0); SPA render gate: max > 1 + 1e-6)
all.firmwareValue: max="1.0" — with the sentinel declared separately as <special_value id="OLD_LEVEL" value="1.005"/>, exported in the paramset description's SPECIAL array, never in MAX
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_d.xml:608-615, inside <paramset id="dimmer_linkset"> (:319-1045, referenced by <paramset type="LINK" id="dimmer_ch_link"> at :149): `<parameter id="SHORT_ON_LEVEL"> <docu default="true"></docu> <logical type="float" min="0.0" max="1.0" default="1.0" unit="100%"> <special_value id="OLD_LEVEL" value="1.005"/> </logical> <physical type="integer" interface="config" list="3" index="0x11" size="1"/> <conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/> </parameter>`. Same declaration in rf_d_le_v1_7.xml:552, rf_d_le_v1_9.xml:564/929, rf_d.xml:976, rf_dim_1l_644.xml:697/1180, rf_dim_1l_644_le_v2_4.xml:677/1160, rf_dim_2l_644.xml:689/1172, rf_dim_2l_644_le_v2_4.xml:672/1155. Export path: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeFloat.cpp:105-118 `(*val)["MIN"]=min; (*val)["MAX"]=max; (*val)["DEFAULT"]=default_value; if(special_values.size()){ (*val)["SPECIAL"]=special_values; }` and :60-74 (InitFromXml widens effective_min/effective_max to include each special value while min/max stay as declared), with :85-99 EnforceConstraints clamping to effective_max. Tier 2 corpus: ../pydevccu/paramsets_db.json — zero FLOAT parameters with UNIT "100%" and MAX > 1.0.
all.finding:
CONTRADICTED. The firmware declares max="1.0" for these parameters and carries 1.005 as a <special_value>, i.e. a member of the SPECIAL set that lives *outside* the min/max range. The paramset-description exporter keeps the two apart: MAX is the declared max, and the special values go into a separate SPECIAL array. A write of 1.005 is nevertheless accepted because InitFromXml widens `effective_max` to 1.005 while leaving `max` at 1.0 — that is precisely the mechanism our rule mistakes for a raised MAX.

The firmware's own name for the value is **OLD_LEVEL**. Our comment's "1.005 means last known level" is right about the number and about the meaning; it is wrong about where the value lives, and the code tests the wrong field.

Scope of the contradiction, measured rather than assumed: across all 130 rftypes and 18 hs485types device XMLs, every `<logical type="float" ... unit="100%">` declares max="1.0" — 159 occurrences, one bucket, no exceptions. Tier 2 agrees: pydevccu's paramsets_db.json has no FLOAT parameter with UNIT "100%" and MAX above 1.0 anywhere.

Consequence — a live, user-visible defect, not just a wrong comment. In Go the dead branch is masked: the classifier already sets HasLastValue: true for every *LEVEL suffix (link_param_metadata.go:233-241), so `has_last_value` still reaches the SPA. But the SPA applies its own gate, `parameter.has_last_value && max > 1 + 1e-6`, to the firmware MAX of 1.0 — so the "last value" checkbox never renders on any real device, and an operator cannot select OLD_LEVEL through the link editor at all. The write path exists (toggleLastValue sends 1.005) and is unreachable.

Which source to follow: Tier 2 — the per-device MAX/SPECIAL read at runtime, not a firmware constant. The correct discriminator is the presence of a SPECIAL entry with ID == "OLD_LEVEL" in the parameter description. Our stack already carries SPECIAL as a raw descriptor blob elsewhere (internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1368-1381 reads SPECIAL.OPTIONAL), so this is plumbing, not new wire work — but nothing in the current link path reads it, which is why the sentinel exists only in prose on the Go side and only as an untriggerable constant in the SPA.

reachesDevice=true: the flag governs a value written into a device's LINK paramset (list 3, index 0x11 on these dimmers).
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, at least one LINK-paramset percent parameter would declare a max above 1.0. I histogrammed the max attribute of every `<logical type="float" ... unit="100%">` across all shipped RF and wired device XMLs and got a single bucket — max="1.0", 159 times — and then confirmed at the exporter that the 1.005 goes to SPECIAL and never to MAX. Both checks would have returned a different result had a raised MAX been the firmware's encoding; the same measurement against Tier 2 (pydevccu) independently returned zero.
all.challengeNote:
CONTRADICTION UPHELD — and both the previous pass's Tier-2 citation and its scope statement were wrong, so the boundary needs restating.

The mechanism, re-read verbatim: GetDescription exports the *declared* max (`(*val)["MAX"]=max;`) and puts the special values in a separate SPECIAL array of {ID, VALUE} structs; InitFromXml widens only `effective_max`, which EnforceConstraints uses for clamping. A write of 1.005 is accepted while MAX stays 1.0 — precisely the mechanism our rule mistakes for a raised MAX. The firmware's name for the value is OLD_LEVEL.

CITATION DEFECT in the previous pass. It cited "../pydevccu/paramsets_db.json — zero FLOAT parameters with UNIT '100%' and MAX > 1.0". That file is 2 bytes long and contains `{}` — it is an empty runtime cache, so the citation is vacuously true and grounds nothing. The real Tier-2 corpus is ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json, which I measured instead.

SCOPE CLAIM REFUTED. The previous pass wrote that no FLOAT with UNIT "100%" has MAX above 1.0 "anywhere". Measured on the real corpus, 260 do: 258 in VALUES paramsets and 2 in MASTER, all MAX 1.01, concentrated in HmIP LEVEL / LEVEL_2 / SATURATION (HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-DRBLI4, HmIPW-DRBL4, HmIP-FALMOT-C12, HmIP-RGBW, HmIP-BSL, …). The correct statement is surface-scoped: on the **LINK** surface — the one uischema_link.go serves — all 1645 percent floats have MAX 1.0, and in the firmware XMLs all 542 percent-float declarations are max="1.0" (one outlier at 0.2, none above). The contradiction therefore holds on our surface, but the previous grounding proved it with a false universal.

CONSEQUENCE, re-verified in our code. Go: uischema_link.go:85 fills Max from the descriptor's MAX, and link_param_metadata.go:233-241 already sets HasLastValue: true for every *LEVEL suffix, so the rawFloatGreaterThan branch and its else-branch produce the same value — dead, not harmful. SPA: ParameterLevelField.svelte:153 gates the checkbox on `parameter.has_last_value && max > 1 + 1e-6` against a MAX of 1.0, so the "last value" control never renders on any device in either corpus, and toggleLastValue (which writes 1.005) is unreachable. Live, user-visible.

NEW FINDING the previous pass missed, and it is the same class of error one level down: the SPA hard-codes `const lastValueSentinel = 1.005` as *the* sentinel. The firmware declares four different sentinel IDs on percent floats, and on LINK paramsets alone Tier 2 shows OLD_LEVEL=1.005, NO_MODIFICATION=1.01 (HM-LC-Ja venetian-blind actuators, on the same SHORT/LONG_ON/OFF_LEVEL parameters), ACT_LEVEL=1.275 and LOCKED=-0.005. A fix that only swaps the MAX test for "has a SPECIAL entry" but keeps 1.005 as the written value would send the wrong sentinel to the Ja actuators — a value the device's own effective_max (1.01) would then clamp.

Which source to follow: Tier 2, the per-device SPECIAL array read at runtime — never a firmware constant and never MAX. The discriminator is the presence of a SPECIAL entry, and the value to write is that entry's VALUE, keyed by its ID. One trap for the implementer: the wire shape is the firmware's array of {ID, VALUE} structs (HSSLogicalTypeFloat.cpp:110-112); pydevccu stores most of its corpus as a flattened {ID: VALUE} object (1421 of 1501 SPECIAL fields) and only 80 in the array shape, so the corpus shape must not be taken as the wire shape. Our stack already carries SPECIAL as a raw blob (internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1368-1381, which does a substring search for "OPTIONAL" rather than decoding), so nothing on the link path reads it today.

all.title: 'A STRING parameter's MAX is a byte length' is a comment-claim, and the check counts bytes not runes
all.citation: Tier 1 (BidCos): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeString.cpp:55-67 — GetDescription writes `(*val)["TYPE"]="STRING"; (std::string&)(*val)["MIN"]=""; (std::string&)(*val)["MAX"]="";` and :50-53 EnforceConstraints is `return val->getType()==XmlRpcValue::TypeString;` — no length constraint of any kind. Tier 1 (HmIP): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory — a STRING config parameter is constructed with converter AsciiStringToInteger(16) and the MAX slot holding the literal `[0x20-0x7E]{16}`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addSpecialCommaSeparatedParameter sets MIN="" and MAX="" on COMBINED_PARAMETER; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.AsciiStringToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical encodes with StandardCharsets.ISO_8859_1 and copies at most `length` bytes into a fixed-size array (silent truncation, no rejection). Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json — 5,020 STRING parameter descriptions, MAX values: "255.255.255" (3737), "" (391), integer 0 (505), "281474976710655" (259), "2255_12_31 23:55" (40), "-1" (32), "[0-9]{8}" (8, HmIP-WKP NUMERIC_PIN_CODE), "[0x20-0x7E]{16}" (7, HmIP-ESI METER_OBIS_SEARCH_STRING / HmIP-WRCD TEXT + DISPLAY_DATA_STRING), "[0x00-0x7E]{127}" (2, HmIP-HAP/HmIPW-DRAP UPDATE_SERVER_URL), an IPv4 regex (2), "30.0" (1). Not one carries a positive integer.
all.ourValue: MAX on a STRING parameter is an integer maximum byte length; zero/absent means unlimited; enforced as `len(v.String) <= parseIntRaw(desc.Max)` — Go `len` on a UTF-8 string.
all.firmwareValue: MAX on a STRING parameter is never a length integer. On BidCos it is unconditionally the empty string and the firmware imposes no length rule at all. On HmIP it is either a value ceiling for an ordered string ("255.255.255", "2255_12_31 23:55") or a charset+count pattern ("[0x20-0x7E]{16}", "[0-9]{8}", "[0x00-0x7E]{127}"); where a length exists it lives inside that pattern, the unit is ISO-8859-1 bytes (so a German umlaut is one byte, not two), and an over-long value is silently truncated by the encoder, never rejected.
all.finding: Three things are wrong at this site, and they cancel out into a dead guard. (1) The type: MAX for STRING is a string on both stacks, so `parseIntRaw` — which json.Unmarshals into an int — returns 0 for every real descriptor and the branch never fires. The check is inert; an over-long METER_OBIS_SEARCH_STRING or UPDATE_SERVER_URL passes validation and reaches the device, where the HmIP encoder truncates it without telling anyone. (2) The unit: where the firmware does carry a length it is ISO-8859-1 bytes (AsciiStringToInteger's STRING_CHARSET), i.e. one byte per Latin-1 character; `len(v.String)` counts UTF-8 bytes. The bundle's damage hypothesis (umlauts costing two bytes against the CCU's budget) inverts this — the CCU's budget is per character for anything Latin-1 representable, and it is our counter that is in the wrong unit. (3) The surface: this Validate is the paramset/setValue write gate (internal/model/device/channel_set.go:62, internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:334). Device and channel names do not pass through it — those go via ReGa — so the naming damage described in the bundle cannot occur here at all. If the rule is to be kept, the honest form is a pattern check against MAX when MAX matches `[…]{n}`, counting ISO-8859-1 bytes; the integer-length reading has no source.

The branch is inert: 3,737 descriptors fail int-unmarshal on "255.255.255", 505 carry literal 0, 391 carry "", and every remaining shape is a string. all.title: The blind LEVEL_COMBINED encoder deliberately diverges from the reference by rounding instead of truncating
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/rf_ja_conf_644.xml (HM-LC-Ja1PBU-FM / HM-LC-JaX): `<parameter id="LEVEL_COMBINED" operations="write" control="JALOUSIE.LEVEL_COMBINED"><logical type="string"/><physical type="string" interface="command" value_id="LEVEL_COMBINED"><set request="LEVEL_COMBINED_SET"/></physical><conversion type="hexstring_bytearray" has0XPrefix="true" delimiter=","/></parameter>`; same file `<frame id="LEVEL_COMBINED_SET" ... ><parameter type="string" index="11.0" size="2.0" param="LEVEL_COMBINED"/></frame>`; and for the same byte `<parameter id="LEVEL" ...><logical type="float" default="0.0" min="0.0" max="1.0" unit="100%"><special_value id="OLD_LEVEL" value="1.005"/><special_value id="NO_MODIFICATION" value="1.010"/></logical>...<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/></parameter>`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger.cpp:56-68 — `double dval=((double&)in+offset)*factor; if(dval>=0)dval+=0.5; else dval-=0.5; ((int&)*out)=(int)dval;`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionHexStringToByteArray.cpp:153-165 — `fromHexValue` returns false unless the token is exactly 4 characters when has0xPrefix, and :88-92 a failed token aborts the whole conversion and sets the value to "". ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseBlindShutter.js:294-305 — the WebUI's own encoder: `var level = parseInt(this.state) * 2, levelHex = level.toString(16) ... dpValue = (levelHex.length < 2) ? "0X0" + levelHex : "0X" + levelHex; dpValue += ","; ...`.
all.ourValue: `fmt.Sprintf("0x%02x", int(math.Round(value*100*2)))`, input clamped to [0,1], two axes joined with "," (internal/model/custom/cover/blind.go:346).
all.firmwareValue: The CCU does not decode LEVEL_COMBINED numerically at all — its conversion is `hexstring_bytearray`, an opaque byte pass-through with `has0XPrefix="true"`, `delimiter=","`, two bytes. The firmware's own float→byte rule for that same physical byte is LEVEL's `float_integer_scale factor="200"`, implemented as round-half-away-from-zero (`dval+=0.5` then truncate), not truncation. A token that is not exactly 4 characters aborts the entire write.
all.finding: The rounding decision is right, and the reference's truncation is the artefact. I reproduced the firmware expression `(int)(v*200+0.5)` against our `math.Round(v*100*2)` over the full 0.5%-grid, the full 1%-grid and 200,000 random values in [0,1]: zero mismatches. The reference's `int(value*100*2)` disagrees with the firmware on 7 distinct grid points (0.145→28 vs 29, 0.285→56 vs 57, 0.29→57 vs 58, 0.565, 0.57, 0.575, 0.58), each one 0.5% low. The clamp is also firmware-grounded, though for a sharper reason than the comment gives: `fromHexValue` rejects any token that is not exactly "0xNN", so "0x12c" does not merely mangle one axis — `LogicalToPhysical` returns false and replaces the whole value with the empty string, dropping the write. Two boundaries worth recording. First, the clamp to [0,1] makes the two special values the firmware declares on the very same byte unreachable: OLD_LEVEL=1.005→201 (0xc9) and NO_MODIFICATION=1.010→202 (0xca) — and 202 is exactly what the firmware's own LEVEL_SET frame hard-codes into the other axis to mean 'leave it alone' (`<parameter type="integer" index="12.0" size="1.0" const_value="202"/>`). Our encoder can therefore never express a combined write that moves one axis only; it always commands both. Second, the WebUI writes uppercase "0X" and works on a 1%-per-step grid (even bytes only, `parseInt(state)*2`), while we write lowercase "0x" on the 0.5% grid; the parser is case-agnostic (std::hex stream extraction) and odd bytes are legitimate for a factor-200 parameter, so neither is a defect.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware truncated, HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger::LogicalToPhysical would read `((int&)*out)=(int)(((double&)in+offset)*factor);` without the ±0.5 step, and my 200k-value comparison would have reported the 7 grid points as mismatches against our formula instead of against the reference's. It reported the opposite, so the check discriminates.
all.challengeNote: Upheld on every leg I could attack. Surface: LEVEL_COMBINED occurs in exactly one device XML across the whole firmware tree (rf_ja_conf_644.xml) and in exactly two device types across the Tier-2 corpus (HM-LC-Ja1PBU-FM, HM-LC-JaX) — the same two `<supported_types>` — and our only writer is the `BlindKindHM` branch. There is no second parameter with the same physical meaning to be confused with; the HmIP path takes a different string entirely (`L2=…,L=…`). Arithmetic reproduced independently: over the full 0.5%-grid (201 points), the full 1%-grid (101 points) and 200,000 uniform randoms in [0,1], `int(round(v*200))` matched `(int)(v*200+0.5)` on every single value; `int(v*100*2)` differed at exactly the seven grid points named — 0.145, 0.285, 0.29, 0.565, 0.57, 0.575, 0.58 — each one byte low. Two corrections to the record, neither changing the verdict. (1) The clamp that makes OLD_LEVEL=201 / NO_MODIFICATION=202 unreachable is applied by the caller, not the encoder: blind.go:315-328 clamps level and tilt to [0,1] before ConvertHMLevelToCPV is ever called, so removing the encoder's own clamp would not restore reachability — the observation about never being able to command one axis alone stands, but the site to change is the caller. (2) The case-agnosticism of the parser is a property of `std::stringstream >> std::hex` (which accepts an optional 0x/0X prefix), not of an explicit prefix strip; fromHexValue does no prefix handling of its own beyond the size==4 test.

all.title: Three different models of the CCU's float behaviour coexist: 6-decimal rounding on write, 1e-6 relative tolerance on echo, exact equality in profile matching
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:65 — `std::string XmlRpcValue::_doubleFormat("%f");`, consumed by :591-594 `doubleToXml()` and :659-662 `doubleToText()` via `snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf)-1, getDoubleFormat().c_str(), _value.asDouble)`; `setDoubleFormat` (XmlRpcValue.h:151) has no caller anywhere under src/, so the default stands. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:222 — `snprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer)-1, "%f", (double)v);`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:625-637 — `doubleToStream()`: `mantissa=int(frexp(_value.asDouble, &exponent)*double(1<<30));`, decoded at :605-620 as `ldexp(double(mantissa)/double(1<<30), exponent)`. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcSerializer — the <double> element is written with `String.valueOf(o)`, i.e. Java Double.toString, shortest round-trip.
all.ourValue: Write: every outgoing float64 rounded to 6 decimals (`math.Round(v*1e6)/1e6`). Echo: match when `|sent-got| / max(1,|sent|,|got|) <= 1e-6`.
all.firmwareValue: BidCos rfd XML-RPC and ReGa/tclrpc: `%f`, i.e. exactly 6 decimal places, rounded — absolute quantisation of 5e-7. BIN-RPC: `int(frexp(v,&e)*2^30)`, a truncating binary-mantissa form with a constant relative step of 2^-30 ≈ 9.3e-10. HmIP legacy XML-RPC: `String.valueOf(double)` — full binary64 round-trip, no quantisation at all.
all.finding: The premise that the three sites cannot all be right does not survive reading them. (a) The write-side 6-decimal round is not an unverified claim — it is an exact match for what rfd and tclrpc emit, `%f` being `%.6f`. (b) The echo tolerance is adequate on every transport, and the `max(1,·)` denominator is why: for |v|<=1 it degrades to an absolute 1e-6, which covers %f's 5e-7; for |v|>1 it is 1e-6 relative, which covers both %f (whose relative error only shrinks as |v| grows) and BIN-RPC's 9.3e-10. The bundle's reasoning — that a mantissa/exponent form makes a large value lose 'far more than 1e-6 relative' — is backwards: a mantissa/exponent form is by construction a constant-relative quantiser. (c) The third site is misreported. internal/store/linkprofile/store.go:483-486 `floatsEqual` is `math.Abs(a-b) <= 1e-6*math.Max(math.Max(math.Abs(a),math.Abs(b)),1.0)` — character-for-character the diff.go shape, not exact equality. Where the claim does need narrowing: our 6-decimal write round is correct for the BidCos and ReGa surfaces and lossy for the HmIP one, whose serialiser preserves full binary64. The boundary runs at the interface, not at the parameter. Practically small (HmIP float parameters declare one or two decimals), but the rule as written asserts more than the firmware does. One genuine internal inconsistency remains and it is inside diff.go itself: the ValueKindList branch (:49-58) compares elements with `!=`, so floats inside a list get bit-exact comparison while scalar floats get the tolerance — the same echo through a list-valued parameter can be reported as a mismatch that a scalar would pass.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU's XML-RPC serialiser not quantised to 6 decimals, `_doubleFormat` would hold `%g`, `%.17g`, or a wider precision, or `setDoubleFormat` would be called somewhere in src/ — I checked for both and found neither. The HmIP side is the control that the check discriminates: the same question asked of HMIPServer's serialiser returned a different answer (`String.valueOf`, no quantisation), which is how the narrowing was found rather than assumed.
all.challengeNote: The firmware half is sound; the rule's own premise about our code is not, and it fails on two of three sites. (1) The write leg is measured on dead code. `parameter.ToHomematicValue` and `value.ToHomematicValue` are both referenced exclusively from `_test.go` files. Whatever the CCU's `%f` does, the daemon never rounds an outgoing float to 6 decimals — XML-RPC emits the shortest exact decimal and BIN-RPC emits the frexp pair. So "6-decimal rounding on write" is not one of three coexisting models; it is a property of a helper the write path does not execute, and the previous agent upheld it as "an exact match for what rfd and tclrpc emit" without establishing that the site is on the write path. (2) The previous agent correctly caught that the third site is not exact equality — internal/store/linkprofile/store.go:483-486 `floatsEqual` is `math.Abs(a-b) <= 1e-6*math.Max(math.Max(math.Abs(a),math.Abs(b)),1.0)`, the diff.go shape — but its replacement finding is itself built on a guessed input. It reports that "floats inside a list get bit-exact comparison" at diff.go:49-58. `hmtypes.ParamValue.List` is declared `List []string` (pkg/hmtypes/value.go:25); no float can ever occupy a ValueKindList, so the `!=` there is a string comparison and the claimed internal inconsistency does not exist. (3) What survives is the echo tolerance, and it is adequate: with denominator max(1,|sent|,|got|) the bound degrades to an absolute 1e-6 for |v|<=1, covering %f's 5e-7 quantisation, and stays 1e-6 relative for |v|>1, covering both %f (whose relative error shrinks as |v| grows) and BIN-RPC's mantissa truncation (relative error bounded by 2^-29 ~ 1.9e-9, since frexp normalises the mantissa into [0.5,1)). One model, in two places, with the same expression. The rule's title is false as stated.

all.title: The target-channel key ordering (sorted-group position = actor index) is a convention the source does not state

all.ourValue: actor index = 1-based position in the group-number-sorted set of schedule-relevant custom-DP channel groups; sub index = 1-based position within the group, primary channel first then secondaries; `<actor>_<sub>` maps to CHANNEL_LOCKS bit 3*(actor-1)+(sub-1) over a fixed 8x3 grid; TARGET_CHANNELS bit = ChannelNo - 1 (internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go TargetChannelBitsFrom).
all.firmwareValue: There is no actor/sub decomposition in the CCU. The editor builds one flat, channel-ascending list of the device's virtual-receiver / transceiver channels (`relevantChn` / `virtualChannels`), overridden by an explicit hard-coded list for nine named model families, and the bit is the 0-based POSITION in that list: `Math.pow(2, index)` for TARGET_CHANNELS and, for CHANNEL_LOCKS, the reversed binary string indexed by the same position. The 3-wide stride appears only in the non-expert view, as `tmpVal << 3` and `x += 3`, for devices whose receivers genuinely come in triples. `2^(channelNumber-1)` occurs in exactly one branch, `deviceIsHmIP_DALI`.
all.finding: Two halves of this join land differently. The CHANNEL_LOCKS table in channel_keys.go is right wherever a device's schedule channels really are triples: for HmIP-BSL fw>=2 the firmware's own list is [4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14], so positions 0..8 are exactly our 1_1..3_3 bits 0..8 — the 24-bit mask, the LSB-first order and the 3-per-actor grouping are all confirmed by getBinChannelState and getOnlyExpertChannels. The boundary runs at devices whose list is not a run of triples, and the firmware names them: HmIP-WKP [1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15] is eight one-channel actors, so the CCU's bits are 0,1,2,...,7 while our keys 1_1,2_1,...,8_1 give 0,3,6,...,21; HmIP-WGS [7,9,10,11], HmIP-WGT [2,4,5,6], the RGBW modes [1,2] and [1,2,3,4], HmIP-DLD/HmIPW-WRC6 and HmIP-FWI (explicit table [8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,1,2,4]) are the same shape. On those the two writes address different physical channels, and both reach real actors. Separately and unambiguously contradicted: TargetChannelBitsFrom's `ChannelNo - 1`. The rawconvert.go comment cites `Math.pow(2,(self.virtualChannels[index]-1))` as the CCU's rule, but that line sits inside the `deviceIsHmIP_DALI` branch — it is the one exception, and the general branch two lines above is `Math.pow(2, index)`. For HmIP-BSL fw>=2 the difference is not subtle: channel 8 is position 3 (bit 3) for the CCU and bit 7 for us; channel 12 is position 6 for the CCU and bit 11 for us. The sound construction for both parameters is the same one the CCU uses: order the device's virtual-receiver/transceiver channels ascending, apply the per-model override where the firmware carries one, and take the 0-based position. Our sub-ordering rule 'primary channel first, then secondaries' is also not the firmware's — the CCU has no primary notion and orders strictly by channel number, so any profile whose primary channel number exceeds one of its secondaries reorders the pair.
all.negativeControl: Had 'sorted-group position = actor index, bit = 3*(actor-1)+(sub-1)' and 'TARGET_CHANNELS bit = channel number - 1' been the CCU's rules, the editor would compute the checkbox value from the channel number uniformly and would not need per-model channel lists at all. Instead the general branch is position-based (`Math.pow(2, index)`), the channel-number form appears in exactly one device-specific branch, and nine model families carry hard-coded lists precisely because position and channel number diverge on them. A device with contiguous 1..3N receivers produces the same answer under both rules, which is why the check had to be run against HmIP-BSL and HmIP-WKP rather than a generic actuator.
all.challengeNote: The rule is upheld and the previous agent's narrowing is too generous. Four things. (1) The `ChannelNo-1` contradiction is confirmed at the source: the expression the rawconvert.go comment cites as the CCU's rule sits inside the DALI branch (:2918); the general branch two lines above (:2899) is `Math.pow(2, index)`. For HmIP-BSL fw>=2 the CCU puts channel 8 at bit 3 and channel 12 at bit 6; we put them at bits 7 and 11. (2) The CHANNEL_LOCKS half reaches a real write, not a display. WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS itself is read-only (OPERATIONS 5), and `getBinChannelState` is the display decoder. Our writer emits `WPTCLS=<bit>,WPTCL=<0|2>` on COMBINED_PARAMETER (internal/model/weekprofile/datapoint.go:663 via BuildCombinedParameterValue). The CCU's own producer of that exact string is iseHmIPWeeklyProgram_AccessReceiver.js:392, and its bit is `Math.pow(2, index)` — positional. So the wrong bit locks a channel the operator did not select, on the device. (3) The BSL agreement the previous agent called "confirmed" is a coincidence of two independent derivations, not a grounding. The CCU's [4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14] is a hard-coded per-model override; ours comes from the IPFixedColorLight profile's `PrimaryChannel: 0, SecondaryChannels: []int{1, 2}` rebased per group number (internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:132-138 with schedule_targets.go:97-102). Our sub-ordering rule (primary first, then secondaries) is also not the firmware's — it orders strictly by channel number and has no primary notion.

The wire field name also matches end to end: the WebUI reads `iFace.dutyCycle` and internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods.go:685 reads `bidcosPercent(m, "dutyCycle")`. Both divergence claims are real and both are on the live path, which I checked rather than assumed. Gateway selection: `aggregateBidcosGateways` (internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1857-1881) prefers the DEFAULT gateway and otherwise the highest duty cycle, and it is the function that populates the cache `DeviceAdminDomain.InterfaceDutyCycle` (internal/central/adapter/device_admin.go:357-375) reads via `u.Hub.BidcosInterface(dev.InterfaceID)` — so on a multi-gateway installation we can warn on a different radio than the WebUI, which considers only `type == "CCU2"`. Interface coverage: `loadBidcosInterfaces` skips every entry where `e.Interface != hmenum.InterfaceBidCosRF` (hub_wiring.go:1831), so an HmIP-only installation never gets a snapshot and never warns — matching the unpatched WebUI, not the shipped patched one. Neither divergence touches the threshold itself.

all.title: The BIN-RPC callback listener accepts three fewer CCU callback methods than the XML-RPC one, with no source for the asymmetry
all.site: internal/central/rpcserver/binrpc_server.go:335 (BINRPCSupportedMethods) and :553 (dispatch default:), against internal/central/rpcserver/xmlrpc_server.go:337-... (bindXMLRPCMethods) and internal/central/rpcserver/handlers.go:20-51 (Handlers, eight methods)
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:147-169 (XmlRpcCallAsync: iterates every registered handler URL, `s=new AsyncXmlRpcSender(it->first)`, method name passed through as a plain `const char*`); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:82 `_isBinary = protocol.find("bin")!=std::string::npos;`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:333-340 (generateRequest binary branch: `size_t name_length=strlen(methodName); ... body.append(methodName);` — the same name, byte-for-byte); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:786 newDevices, :793 replaceDevice, :805 deleteDevices, :817 readdedDevice, :1177 updateDevice; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:163 replaceDevice, :486/:494/:541/:549 updateDevice, :561 newDevices, :575 deleteDevices; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:201/:281 listDevices (sync), :238/:328 replaceDevice, :335 deleteDevices; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:254-267 and :322 (init-time `system.listMethods` probe: `if(methname.compare("replaceDevice")==0){supportReplaceDevice=true;}` … `if(supportReplaceDevice && IsDeviceReplaced(...))`, else the device is put in the deleteDevices array at :330).
all.finding:
Two separate questions; only one is answerable from the firmware.

(1) Does BIN-RPC carry a reduced method set? No — and this is settled. The emitters are transport-blind: rfd/hs485d call `XmlRpcCallAsync("<name>", params)`, HSSManager fans that out over every registered callback URL, and `XmlRpcClient` decides XML vs binary purely from the URL scheme (`protocol.find("bin")`), then writes the identical method-name string into the binary body. There is no per-transport method table anywhere in the tree. The complete set of names the CCU's own daemons ever invoke on a callback (grep of every XmlRpcCall{Async,Sync} literal in src/rfd, src/hs485d, src/libhsscomm) is: deleteDevices, event, listDevices, newDevices, readdedDevice, replaceDevice, system.listMethods, system.multicall, updateDevice. Note `error` is NOT among them — rfd and hs485d never call an `error` callback, so our Handlers.Error has no rfd-side emitter either.

(2) Does CUxD send updateDevice/replaceDevice/readdedDevice? Tier 1 is silent. CUxD is a third-party add-on: it is not in ../OpenCCU-Base, there is no CUxD package under ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/package/occu (that directory holds only Config.in, Makefile, occu.hash, occu.mk, scripts), and no component in OpenCCU-Base registers a `binary://` callback URL at all (grep for `binary://` outside libXmlRpc: no hits). Our BIN-RPC routes are registered only by wireCUxDInterface (internal/central/adapter/cuxd_wiring.go:180, reached from ccu_wiring.go:720 under `if iface == hmenum.InterfaceCUxD`), so today the listener only ever faces CUxD. Nothing in any available tree says what CUxD emits.

One firmware fact does bear directly on our advertised list, and it is not what the guard assumes: our `system.listMethods` answer is READ by the CCU. HSSManager::PlatformInit calls system.listMethods on the freshly registered callback and scans the array specifically for the string "replaceDevice"; when absent, its init-time reconciliation reports a replaced device via deleteDevices instead. So omitting replaceDevice from BINRPCSupportedMethods is a live negotiation signal, not a documentation detail — but it degrades gracefully rather than faulting. updateDevice and readdedDevice are never negotiated: RFManager::ReportUpdate and ReportReAddedDevice call XmlRpcCallAsync unconditionally to every registered URL. So if a BidCos/HmIP interface were ever registered over BIN-RPC, those two would arrive and hit our `default:` fault. The boundary of our rule therefore runs exactly at "registered by wireCUxDInterface": inside it, unverified; one step wider, false.
all.negativeControl: Had our five-method set been right, I would have found either (a) a transport conditional in HSSManager/RFManager gating updateDevice/replaceDevice/readdedDevice on a non-binary URL, or (b) a separate method-name table in the BIN-RPC encoder. I found the opposite in both places: XmlRpcCallAsync has no transport branch, and generateRequest's binary branch copies `methodName` verbatim. The check would also have come out differently if the emitted-name grep had returned only our five — it returned nine, and omitted `error`, which we do route.
all.ourValue: BIN-RPC dispatch + advertised list: event, newDevices, deleteDevices, listDevices, error, system.multicall, system.listMethods (5 CCU callbacks); anything else faults via `default:`.
all.firmwareValue: CCU-side emitter set, transport-independent: event, newDevices, deleteDevices, updateDevice, replaceDevice, readdedDevice, listDevices, system.multicall, system.listMethods — and no `error`. `replaceDevice` is additionally gated on our own system.listMethods answer at init.

all.title: The MASTER read-back poll delay of 2 s encodes how long a BidCos putParamset takes, with no source
all.site: internal/client/backends/master_poll.go:15-17 (premise comment), :31-33 and :68 (Interval: 2 * time.Second); constructed for every non-PushesConfigPending interface at internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:262-273
all.citation: Premise (no MASTER echo): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:1173-1178 `void RFManager::ReportUpdate(const std::string& address, int hint){ ... XmlRpcCallAsync("updateDevice", params); }` with its only callers at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:756 and :868 (UPDATE_HINT_LINKS — link add/remove) and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1620 (UPDATE_HINT_ALL, inside the OTAU firmware-rebuild path); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:486/:494 (AddLink) and :541/:549 (RemoveLink) — the only updateDevice emitters on the wired side; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSPhysicalDataInterfaceInternal.cpp:51 `return inst->RegisterInternalValueEvent(value_id, this);` — the internal data interface is the only physical data interface that registers a value event, and MASTER parameters declare `interface="config"`. Latency: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:171-186 `RFDevice::PutParamsetValues` — `if(!ps->Put(this, key, set))return false; RFConfigData& cd=config_data[cur_paramset_peer]; if(!cd.CommitToDevice(this)){ config_data_dirty=true; CheckConfigPendingEvent(); }`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParamset.cpp:178-193 (Put → `param->SetValue(inst, val)`) against :162-176 (Get → `param->GetValue(inst,mode,&entry)`) — the same in-process parameter store; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:73-88 is the identical channel-level pair.
all.finding:
The comment makes two claims and the firmware answers them differently.

Claim 1 — 'BidCos-RF interfaces do not echo MASTER changes back via the callback channel': CONFIRMED. rfd emits `updateDevice` from exactly three sites, all of them link changes or an OTAU device rebuild; hs485d from four, all AddLink/RemoveLink. No putParamset path emits any callback. And MASTER parameters cannot produce an `event()` either: the only physical data interface that registers a value event is the *internal* one, while MASTER parameters bind `interface="config"` (e.g. `<physical type="integer" interface="config" list="0" index="24.0" size="0.1"/>` for LOCAL_RESET_DISABLE in ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/rf_ja_conf_644.xml).

Claim 2 — that 2 s is how long the CCU holds the write before get_paramset(MASTER) reflects it: CONTRADICTED. rfd's putParamset writes the value into its own parameter store synchronously (`ps->Put` → `param->SetValue`) BEFORE it even attempts the radio commit, and getParamset reads that same store (`ps->Get` → `param->GetValue`). The value is readable the instant putParamset returns; the firmware carries no pending window for the read-back. `CommitToDevice` failing does not hold the read back either — it only sets `config_data_dirty` and raises CONFIG_PENDING, and the read still returns the new (optimistic) value. So on rfd and hs485d the correct delay is 0, and the read-back cannot distinguish a committed write from a pending one; CONFIG_PENDING is the only signal that does.

Consequence: the 2 s is a safety margin over a latency that is not there, not a wrong value on the wire — the cost is one round-trip of extra delay before the SPA updates, not a stale cache. The interval's stated justification is what is unsourced. Scope note: the poller is also constructed for CUxD (cuxd_wiring.go:210), and for that backend Tier 1 says nothing — CUxD is absent from both firmware trees — so if the 2 s is protecting anything, it is protecting CUxD, and the comment attributes it to BidCos-RF.
all.negativeControl: Had the write genuinely been held pending, RFDevice::PutParamsetValues would have queued the value into a pending structure that GetParamsetValues does not read, or GetParamsetValues would have triggered a device read; instead both go through HSSParamset against the same params map. And had MASTER been echoed, I would have found an updateDevice or event emitter on the putParamset path — the three rfd call sites are all link/OTAU, and the config physical interface registers no value event, so the check does produce a different answer when the claim is false.
all.ourValue: Interval = 2 s before the post-write get_paramset(MASTER).
all.firmwareValue: 0 — getParamset reads the same in-process store putParamset wrote synchronously (rfd RFDevice.cpp:171-186 vs HSSParamset.cpp:162-193). No CONFIG_PENDING gate on the read.
all.challengeNote:
Every citation the previous agent gave transcribes verbatim and the mechanism holds — I traced it one layer deeper than they did, from the XML-RPC entry point down to the byte array. putParamset is executed inline on the RPC thread, ps->Put reaches RFConfigData::PutValue → SetByteData, and getParamset reaches RFConfigData::GetByteData on the same chunk map; GetByteData ignores the dev_dirty bits entirely, so a write that failed CommitToDevice reads back exactly like one that succeeded. BidCos-Wired is the same shape and stricter still: HS485Device::PutParamsetValues blocks on eep_cache.Flush() before returning. So on both BidCos interfaces the correct post-write delay is 0.

I also closed a hole the previous agent left in claim 1. They argued 'no MASTER echo' from the updateDevice emitters plus the internal-data-interface registration, which leaves the loopback route open: HSSParameter::SetValue:315 emits ReportEvent when `loopback && IsEventable()`. I scanned all 127 shipped rftypes for a parameter whose block contains `interface="config"` and whose `operations` includes `event`: zero hits, and the parser's default is read|write with loopback=false. Claim 1 is therefore confirmed on a direct measurement, not only on an emitter census.

What I demote is the scope of the verdict, not the physics. The constant is not BidCos-only. newMasterPollerForInterface returns nil only for interfaces in InterfacesPushingConfigPending, and that set contains HmIP-RF alone — so the same 2 s governs BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, VirtualDevices and CUxD (cuxd_wiring.go:210). ../OpenCCU-Base settles two of the four. VirtualDevices is served by the HmIP side (HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.bidcos / .rega), which I did not read; CUxD is a third-party addon absent from both firmware trees. Reporting 'contradicted, firmware value 0' as the verdict for the constant overstates what was measured by half.

Second demotion, smaller: the file makes no claim that 2 s encodes a putParamset duration. master_poll.go:15-17 asserts only the no-echo premise; :30-31 says 'Interval is how long the poller waits before issuing the read. Defaults to 2 seconds when zero.' The audit's phrase 'encodes how long a BidCos putParamset takes' is the auditor's paraphrase, and what got contradicted is the paraphrase. The defensible statement is narrower and still worth having: the premise is Tier-1 true, the interval is Tier-1 unjustified on the two interfaces Tier 1 covers, and Tier 1 is silent on the other two.

One consequence neither of us should leave unstated: the poll is not free. getParamset(MASTER) reaches RFLogicalInstance::GetConfigData (RFLogicalInstance.cpp:34-45), which issues a blocking BidCos ReadFromDevice for any list still marked must_be_read. A cheaper delay does not make the read cheaper.

all.title: LEVEL_COMBINED half-order (first=LEVEL, second=LEVEL_SLATS) and the /200 scale are carried only by the Python port
