Independent Tier-1 corroboration — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseBlindShutter.js:295-304 `var level = parseInt(this.state) * 2, levelHex = level.toString(16), levelSlat = parseInt(this.levelSlats) * 2, levelSlatHex = levelSlat.toString(16); dpValue = (levelHex.length < 2) ? "0X0" + levelHex : "0X" + levelHex; dpValue += ","; dpValue += (levelSlatHex.length < 2) ? "0X0" + levelSlatHex : "0X" + levelSlatHex; setDpState(this.dpLevelCombined, dpValue);`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:459 `"stringTableJalousieLevelCombined" : "Common value: Blind level, slats position"`.
all.finding:
Both halves of the rule are confirmed, and the ordering is read from the source rather than inferred from array position.

Ordering: LEVEL_COMBINED_SET places a 2-byte string at byte index 11.0. The two single-axis frames that occupy the same two bytes name them explicitly — LEVEL_SET puts LEVEL at 11.0 and the const 202 (the NO_MODIFICATION sentinel) at 12.0; LEVEL_SLATS_SET is the exact mirror, const 202 at 11.0 and LEVEL_SLATS at 12.0. So byte 0 = LEVEL, byte 1 = LEVEL_SLATS. Our first=LEVEL, second=LEVEL_SLATS is right, in both the decode (combined.go:118-124) and the encode (blind.go:346, wireL then wireT). The WebUI's own writer and the English string table say the same thing independently.

Scale: both LEVEL and LEVEL_SLATS declare `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/>` over logical float 0.0..1.0, and HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger implements exactly n/factor. So /200 is the firmware's number. Our decode `float64(n)/100/2` is bit-identical to n/200 (halving is exact in binary64), so there is no ULP difference between the two spellings. Our encode `int(math.Round(value*100*2))` with `%02x` produces exactly the 4-character token the firmware requires — HSSTypeConversionHexStringToByteArray::fromHexValue rejects any token whose length is not 4 when has0XPrefix is set, so the zero-padding is load-bearing and we have it. Case is irrelevant: the firmware parses via `stringstream >> std::hex`, and the WebUI itself emits uppercase `0X`.

Two facts worth recording that the rule does not cover:
(a) LEVEL_COMBINED is declared `operations="write"` with no `<event>` element and its only frame is `direction="to_device"`. The CCU therefore cannot deliver a LEVEL_COMBINED event for this device family, so parseLevelCombined on the inbound callback path (internal/central/adapter/callback_handlers.go:293/:434) is decoding a parameter the firmware never pushes. The same helper's use in internal/client/reliability/command_tracker.go:127 — decomposing the value WE wrote — is on the right surface.
(b) The firmware reserves 201 (0xC9, OLD_LEVEL = 1.005) and 202 (0xCA, NO_MODIFICATION = 1.010) as per-axis sentinels above the 0..200 range. ConvertHMLevelToCPV clamps to 1.0 → 200, so neither sentinel is expressible through our encoder; a combined write always commands both axes and can never say 'leave this one alone'.
all.negativeControl: Had the halves been reversed, LEVEL_SLATS_SET would have carried LEVEL_SLATS at index 11.0 and the const at 12.0 — it carries them the other way round, and LEVEL_SET is its mirror; that pair is what pins byte 0 to LEVEL without appealing to any array-order convention. Had the scale been 100 or 255, the `factor` attribute on the two `float_integer_scale` conversions would have carried that number, and the WebUI would multiply the percent by 1 or 2.55 rather than by 2.
all.ourValue: first half = LEVEL, second half = LEVEL_SLATS; each byte / 200 for 0..1.
all.firmwareValue: Same. LEVEL_COMBINED_SET byte index 11.0 = LEVEL (per LEVEL_SET), index 12.0 = LEVEL_SLATS (per LEVEL_SLATS_SET); `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/>` on both axes.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, and I closed the one place where the previous grounding was still an inference. They read the ordering off the two single-axis frames (LEVEL at 11.0, LEVEL_SLATS at 12.0) — correct, and I reproduced both frame declarations mechanically. But that only fixes which frame byte carries which axis; it does not say which CSV token lands in which frame byte, and 'first token = lowest byte' is exactly the kind of convention this audit exists to catch. The firmware states it: HSSTypeConversionHexStringToByteArray::LogicalToPhysical appends tokens to the physical string in encounter order, and StructuredFrame::SetStringValue writes value[i] to byte index+i. Token 0 → byte 11 → LEVEL; token 1 → byte 12 → LEVEL_SLATS. Read from the source at every hop.

Scale checked independently: factor="200" on both axes, HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger implements n/factor on read and round-half-away-from-zero on write. Our decode spells it float64(n)/100/2; I tested n=0..255 and (n/100)/2 == n/200 for every value, so there is no ULP gap between the two spellings. Our encode `fmt.Sprintf("0x%02x", int(math.Round(v*200)))` yields a 4-character token for the whole clamped range 0..200, which is what fromHexValue demands when has0xPrefix is set — the zero-padding is load-bearing and present.

Boundary worth naming, because it looks like narrowness and is not: exactly one of the 127 shipped rftypes declares LEVEL_COMBINED — rf_ja_conf_644.xml, `id="HM-LC-Ja1PBU-FM"` and `id="HM-LC-JaX"` (the generic jalousie actuator) — and zero device descriptions in ../pydevccu carry it. Our dispatcher keys purely on the parameter name (combined.go:57-65), so the rule can only ever fire on that family. A single-file evidence base here is the entire population, not a sample.

I also uphold the previous agent's two side notes. LEVEL_COMBINED is `operations="write"` with no `<event>` element and only a to_device frame, so the inbound decode at internal/central/adapter/callback_handlers.go:293/:434 cannot fire for this family on BidCos-RF (the COMBINED_PARAMETER branch of the same dispatcher is a different, HmIP-side question that ../OpenCCU-Base does not answer). And 201/202 (OLD_LEVEL 1.005, NO_MODIFICATION 1.010) are per-axis sentinels above the 0..200 range that ConvertHMLevelToCPV's clamp to 1.0 makes inexpressible, so a combined write always commands both axes.

all.title: Two-decimal rounding as the float write-confirmation rule is cited to the Python sibling, not to the wire
all.site: internal/client/state_change.go:115-135 (valuesMatch) and :155-157 (roundTo2), reached from internal/client/write_options.go:189 (SetValueWithOptions) and :304 (PutParamsetWithOptions)
all.citation: Echo quantisation — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger.cpp:56-67 `double dval=((double&)in+offset)*factor; if(dval>=0)dval+=0.5; else dval-=0.5; ((int&)*out)=(int)dval;` and :70-77 `((double&)*out)=(((double)((int&)in))/factor)-offset;`. Wire precision — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:65 `std::string XmlRpcValue::_doubleFormat("%f");` used by doubleToXml at :591-603 (`snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf)-1, getDoubleFormat().c_str(), _value.asDouble)`), i.e. six decimals; the BIN-RPC path is a separate mantissa/exponent encoding at :625ff (`ldexp(double(mantissa)/double(1<<30), exponent)`). Descriptor silence — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeFloat.cpp:105-119: GetDescription emits only TYPE, MIN, MAX, DEFAULT and (when present) SPECIAL. Real parameters — ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml `<parameter id="SET_TEMPERATURE" operations="read,write,event" control="HEATING_CONTROL.SETPOINT"><logical type="float" min="4.5" max="30.5" default="20.0" unit="°C"/>…<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="2"/></parameter>`; ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/rf_ja_conf_644.xml `<parameter id="LEVEL" operations="read,write,event" …><conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="200"/></parameter>`.
all.finding:
The firmware does not round float echoes to two decimals, and it does not use a fixed precision at all.

What it does: on a write, the logical float is quantised to `round((v + offset) * factor)` — half away from zero, the `dval += 0.5` branch — and on every read or event the echo is exactly `physical_int / factor - offset`. The quantum is therefore 1/factor, a per-parameter constant declared in the device-type XML. Over XML-RPC the double is serialised with `%f`, six decimals; over BIN-RPC as mantissa/2^30 with an exponent. Neither is two decimals.

A survey of every FLOAT parameter carrying a float_integer_scale across ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/*.xml gives these factors and counts: 2 (873), 200 (533), 10 (281), 1 (40), 100 (38), 10.0 (19), 1000 (6), 62.5 (6), 3.38983050847 (2), 1.0 (1), 31.25 (1), 50 (1). 625 further FLOAT parameters carry no float_integer_scale at all. So the quantum ranges from 1.0 down to 0.001, straddling roundTo2's 0.01 bucket in both directions, and both failure modes are reachable on real read/write/event parameters:

- False reject, factor=2 (SET_TEMPERATURE, the single most common factor). Write 20.3 → physical round(40.6)=41 → echo 20.5. roundTo2 gives 20.3 vs 20.5, no match, WaitForStateChangeOrTimeout blocks the full 60 s and write_options.go:189 turns that into an error from SetValueWithOptions even though the wire write succeeded and the device is at the nearest representable setpoint. Any FLOAT write not already on the device's grid behaves this way whenever factor <= 100.
- False confirm, factor=200 (LEVEL/LEVEL_SLATS, blinds). Physical 23 → 0.115 and physical 24 → 0.12 are two distinct blind positions half a percent apart; roundTo2 maps both to 0.12 (0.115*100 is exactly 11.5 in binary64, and Go's math.Round is half-away-from-zero). An echo of 0.115 confirms an expected write of 0.12.

The cross-check the reader asked for comes out negative: the paramset description cannot supply the right tolerance. HSSLogicalTypeFloat::GetDescription returns TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL only — no step, no precision, no factor. The factor lives solely in the device-type XML that rfd loads at startup and never exposes over XML-RPC. So replacing 2 decimals with a descriptor-derived quantum is not performable from the runtime descriptor; the honest options are to compare the echo against the value the CCU would quantise to (requires the factor, which we do not have), or to accept any echo for the key and stop calling it a value match.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU echoed the written value verbatim, PhysicalToLogical would not exist on this path and getParamset/event would return the stored double unchanged; instead the value makes a documented round trip through an int. Had two decimals been the CCU's own precision, `_doubleFormat` would be "%.2f" rather than "%f", and the float logical type's GetDescription would carry a step or precision field to justify it — it carries neither. And had the collision cases been artefacts of my arithmetic rather than of the rule, roundTo2(0.12) and roundTo2(0.115) would have differed; computed on the same binary64 grid Go uses, they are equal (0.12), while roundTo2(20.3) and roundTo2(20.5) differ — the check discriminates in both directions.
all.missingInput: The per-parameter conversion factor (`<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="…"/>`). It is not carried by getParamsetDescription — HSSLogicalTypeFloat::GetDescription emits TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL only — so a correct per-parameter tolerance cannot be computed from anything the daemon reads at runtime.
all.ourValue: Confirmed iff math.Round(expected*100)/100 == math.Round(actual*100)/100 — a fixed 2-decimal bucket for every FLOAT.
all.firmwareValue: echo = round((written + offset) * factor) / factor - offset, quantum 1/factor per parameter (observed factors 1, 1.0, 2, 3.38983050847, 10, 10.0, 31.25, 50, 62.5, 100, 200, 1000); serialised over XML-RPC with `%f` = 6 decimals.
all.challengeNote:
The contradiction stands, and I rebuilt it rather than accepting it. I re-ran the factor survey over ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/*.xml independently and reproduced the previous agent's histogram exactly, count for count: 2426 float parameters, 1801 with a float_integer_scale spread over 12 distinct factors, 625 with none. The quantum therefore ranges from 1.0 down to 0.001 and straddles roundTo2's 0.01 bucket in both directions. Every cited line transcribes verbatim, including the truncating `(int)dval` after the half-away-from-zero bias.

I checked the one route that would have rescued the rule and the previous agent did not. HSSParameter::SetValue can echo a write back through `inst->ReportEvent(id, log_temp, …)` — and `log_temp` is the logical value *before* LogicalToPhysical, i.e. the un-quantised 20.3, not 20.5. Had SET_TEMPERATURE carried loopback="true", their false-reject example would have collapsed. It does not: the attribute is absent, the parser default is false, no float parameter in any of the 127 rftypes declares loopback="true", and SET_TEMPERATURE's echo is declared to come from `<event frame="INFO_LEVEL"/>` and `<event frame="ACK_STATUS"/>` — both from_device frames carrying the 6-bit physical integer. So the compared value really is the quantised one: write 20.3 → physical round(40.6)=41 → echo 20.5 → roundTo2 mismatch.

I also checked their false-confirm arithmetic, which rests on an exactness claim: 23/200 = 0.115 and 0.115*100 == 11.5 exactly in binary64, so Go's half-away-from-zero math.Round lifts it to 12 and roundTo2(0.115) == roundTo2(0.12) == 0.12. Verified numerically; two blind positions half a percent apart collapse into one bucket. Their 'not performable from the runtime descriptor' conclusion is also right — GetDescription for FLOAT emits TYPE/MIN/MAX/DEFAULT/SPECIAL over a base that adds only UNIT; the factor never leaves the device-type XML that rfd loads at startup.

One correction to the stated consequence, which the previous agent asserted as if it were live. valuesMatch is reachable only through WaitForStateChangeOrTimeout, and both call sites are gated on `opts.WaitForCallback`. Grepping the tree, `WaitForCallback: true` appears in internal/client/write_options_test.go and write_options_waitforcallback_doc_test.go and nowhere else — no production caller enables it (internal/config/timeouts.go carries only the timeout, not the flag). So the false reject and the false confirm are latent in an opt-in path, not defects a running daemon is hitting today. The rule is still contradicted; the severity is 'wrong tolerance waiting to be switched on', not 'writes are failing now'.

all.title: The 'marked system variable' filter is a substring match while its own doc comment says prefix
all.site: internal/client/interface_client_orchestration.go:1009-1033 (GetAllSystemVariablesFiltered, filters `name`) and :952-978 (GetAllProgramsFiltered, filters `description`), both through containsAnyMarker at :981-1002
all.citation: Tier 1, what the CCU actually exposes — ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/getall.tcl: the documented and emitted field set of SysVar.getAll is id, name, type, value, unit, channelId, isVisible, isLogged, isInternal (plus valueName0/valueName1 for LOGIC and ALARM, valueList for LIST, minValue/maxValue for NUMBER); header comment lines 18 and 20 `isVisible : [bool] Gibt an, ob die Systemvariablen sichtbar ist` / `isInternal: [bool] Gibt an, ob die Systemvariable intern verwendet wird`, emitted at :103-104 from `sv.Visible()` and `sv.Internal()`. There is no description field in the response and no `DPInfo` anywhere under ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/. Tier 3 witness (labelled as such) — ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/client/json_rpc.py:975-982 (programs) and :2458-2465 (system variables), both `element_matches_key(search_elements=markers, compare_with=description, ignore_case=False, do_left_wildcard_search=True)`; the semantics are at ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/support/__init__.py:318-326 (signature: `do_right_wildcard_search: bool = True` by default) and :369-393 `if do_left_wildcard_search is True and do_right_wildcard_search is True: if element in compare_with_processed: return True`. Description source in the reference — ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/client/json_rpc.py:2077-2096, a separate ReGa script, not SysVar.getAll.
all.finding:
The CCU defines no marker convention. SysVar.getAll carries no description field at all, and the only 'is this for a logic layer' notions the firmware has are `sv.Visible()` and `sv.Internal()`, both booleans on the ReGa object. Nothing in ReGa or the WebUI reserves a name prefix; a system-variable name is free text. So the marker idea is entirely the Python family's convention and our rule rests on that alone — Tier 1 cannot confirm or contradict it.

What the witness does settle, and it settles both halves of the contradiction:

1. Substring, not prefix. Both call sites pass `do_left_wildcard_search=True` and leave `do_right_wildcard_search` at its default `True`, which lands in the `element in compare_with_processed` branch — a case-sensitive substring test (`ignore_case=False`). So containsAnyMarker's substring behaviour matches the reference and the doc comment at :1009-1010 ('whose name starts with a marker prefix') is simply wrong. The fix is the comment, not the code.

2. The field is wrong for system variables. The reference matches markers against the *description* for programs AND for system variables; our GetAllSystemVariablesFiltered matches against `name` (:1027-1029). Since the CCU's SysVar.getAll has no description, the reference fetches it separately via a ReGa script reading DPInfo(). We have that script too — internal/client/rega/scripts/get_system_variable_descriptions.fn, `sDescription = oVar.DPInfo().UriEncode();` — and the live hub scan uses it at internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1157-1160. So the daemon has the right field available and this API reads the wrong one.

Damage is bounded by something the reader's summary did not have: GetAllSystemVariablesFiltered and GetAllProgramsFiltered have no production caller. A repo-wide grep finds only their definitions and internal/client/interface_client_orchestration_test.go. The live path is loadSysvars/loadPrograms in internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go, which filters on the DPInfo description and treats markers as an enabled-by-default signal rather than an import gate, with INTERNAL as the only marker that actually gates inclusion. So the operator's 'what leaves the house' boundary is not currently drawn by this function — but its doc comment describes a prefix rule that neither it nor the live path implements, and any future caller would inherit the wrong field.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU defined a marker convention, SysVar.getAll would carry a description, a category, or a reserved-prefix check — its field list is fully enumerated in the file's header comment and in the JSON assembly at :95-105, and it carries none. Had the reference been a prefix rule, element_matches_key's `do_right_wildcard_search` default would have been False so the call landed in the `compare_with_processed.startswith(element)` branch; it defaults to True, so both wildcards are on and the branch taken is `element in compare_with_processed`. Both checks would have produced a visibly different answer had our rule been right.
all.ourValue: System variables: case-sensitive substring of any marker in the variable's `name`; doc comment claims prefix. Programs: substring in `description`.
all.firmwareValue: The CCU defines no marker at all — SysVar.getAll exposes id/name/type/value/unit/channelId/isVisible/isLogged/isInternal and no description. Reference convention (witness): case-sensitive substring in the ReGa DPInfo() description, for both programs and system variables.

all.title: The enum sysvar value-list separator ';' is asserted as "CCU wire format" with no cite
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/getall.tcl:27 — verbatim: `#     valueList: [string] Werteliste (Separator: ";")`. And ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createenum.tcl:7 — verbatim: `#   valList: Enum "Wert1;Wert2;Wert3;...."`, whose body at :26 is `sv.ValueList( valList );`. Patch check: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0157-WebUI-Fix-WrongJSONQuotes.patch is the only distribution patch touching createenum.tcl and it changes only the JSON quoting of the response, not the separator.
all.firmwareValue: ';' — semicolon, no spaces in either format example
all.ourValue: ';' — strings.Builder writes ";" between elements, no padding (methods.go:984-993)
all.finding: Confirmed on our exact surface. The CCU's own method-definition file for SysVar.createEnum declares the parameter format as `"Wert1;Wert2;Wert3;...."`, and the sibling SysVar.getAll — the read side of the same round trip — states the separator in words: `Werteliste (Separator: ";")`. Both are Tier-1 files (the CCU's JSON-RPC method surface). So the semicolon is firmware-declared for BOTH halves of the createEnum comment, not just for the `valList` key name; the comment can carry the cite for the separator too. One thing this does NOT settle: whether surrounding whitespace is significant. ReGa's ValueList parser and the `web.webGetValueFromList` / `web.webGetValueListCount` builtins live in ReGaHss (bin/<arch>/ReGaHss, a stripped ELF, no source in the tree), and the WebUI's own enum editor is a compiled ESP page (CreatePopup(ID_NEW_SYSVAR), www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/systemvars.htm:335) — neither is readable. Our joiner emits no spaces, so the question does not arise for us today; a future caller that trims or pads entries has no source to check against.
all.negativeControl: Had our separator been wrong — a comma, a pipe, a newline — createenum.tcl:7's format example would have shown that character in place of ';', and getall.tcl:27 would have named it. Both name ';', and the two files are independent (create vs read-back), so this check can and does distinguish.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD. What I checked, beyond re-reading the two quotes character by character: (1) Wrong-surface attack — failed. createenum.tcl IS the implementation of SysVar.createEnum, the method methods.go:445 calls by name; getall.tcl is the read side of the same ReGa property. I looked for a second, different surface that could carry a different separator and found none: every other ValueList site in the tree (www/rega/esp/system.fn:842, :1376, www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/systemvars.htm:192, www/pda/eq3/sysvar.tcl:31) reads or writes the same single opaque ReGa property. The WebUI's own enum editor converges on it rather than diverging. (2) Patch attack — failed; 0157 is confirmed to touch only Internal() and the response quoting. (3) Tier-inflation attack — nothing Tier-3 is load-bearing here. What DOES limit the grounding, and the prior agent stated it correctly: the citation is a firmware DECLARATION, not executed firmware code. Nothing in the readable tree splits or joins the string — the splitters are the ReGaHss builtins web.webGetValueFromList / web.webGetValueListCount (used at www/rega/esp/controls/rc19_display.fn:133,138 and system.fn:1477), which live in the stripped ELF, and the popup that builds sValList is a compiled ESP page (CreatePopup(ID_NEW_SYSVAR), systemvars.htm:335). So the whitespace question stays open exactly as the prior agent said; our joiner emits none, so it does not arise. One correction of emphasis: the two cites are comments, so the strength here is 'the firmware documents the format of the parameter our code fills', not 'the firmware is observed splitting on ;'. That is still Tier 1 and still our surface — I would not demote it, but a comment citing it should say 'declared' rather than 'implemented'.

all.title: The 3-second hub-scan floor rests on "the ReGa interpreter is single-threaded" and on an unnamed comparable gateway
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrega/tclrega.cpp:208-232 (SendRequest) — the entire ReGa access path in source is a per-call `socket()` + `connect()` + one HTTP/1.0 POST to `/tclrega.exe`; no mutex, no queue, no serialisation of any kind on the client side. The URL is built at :164-165 from `http://127.0.0.1:` + the port read from `/etc/rega_http.port` (default 8183). The server on the other end is ../OpenCCU-Base/bin/{arm-linux-gnueabihf,aarch64-linux-gnu,i686-linux-gnu,x86_64-linux-gnu}/ReGaHss — `file` reports "ELF 32-bit LSB pie executable, ARM, ... stripped"; there is no ReGaHss source anywhere under src/.
all.firmwareValue: not carried by any source in the tree
all.ourValue: 3 * time.Second, justified by two unsourced claims
all.finding: Neither claim behind the number is decidable from the CCU sources. (1) "The ReGa interpreter is single-threaded": the interpreter is ReGaHss, shipped as a stripped prebuilt binary; the only ReGa-related source is tclrega.cpp, a thin HTTP client that says nothing about how the server schedules script runs against its own rule execution. Disassembling the binary for pthread usage would at best show that threads exist — it would not settle whether an incoming script serialises with rule evaluation, which is the load-bearing half of the claim. (2) "Three seconds matches the tightest interval a comparable gateway polls at": this is not a claim about the CCU at all, so no firmware source can speak to it. I also looked for the CCU's own polling cadence against ReGa endpoints as a firmware-grounded comparable and did not find one — the WebUI is user-driven; the only periodic timer in www/webui/webui.js is `setInterval(getOperationMode, 1000)` at :52359, a one-second poll of `Interface.getParamset` during ESI sensor detection, which is an rfd call, not ReGa, and is a transient dialog rather than a steady-state cadence. What our rule rests on today: engineering judgement, not the firmware. That is a legitimate basis for a configuration floor — but the comment states both claims as fact, and neither can be cited.
all.negativeControl: Had ReGa's concurrency model been in-source, tclrega.cpp or a daemon source beside it would show either a serialising lock around script dispatch or a worker pool; the file shows a bare per-call connect with no concurrency control, so the check returns the same "nothing here" whichever way the claim falls. That is exactly why the verdict is tier1-silent rather than confirmed or contradicted: the check cannot produce a different answer.

all.title: Garage ventilation position is hard-coded as level 0.5
all.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/door_opener.fn:28-76 (CreateDoorReceiver) — the CCU's own operator control for a garage drive. It reads DOOR_STATE as an index into a four-label list (`string arState = "lblPosClosed,lblPosOpen,lblPosVentilation,lblPosUnknown"`, :32) and writes DOOR_COMMAND by ordinal: `setDpState(oCommand.ID(), 3)` Close, `, 4)` Vent, `, 1)` Open, `, 2)` Stop (:60-72). No level, no percentage, anywhere in the control. Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MOD-HO.json and HmIP-MOD-TM.json, channel :1 (DOOR_RECEIVER) VALUES — DOOR_STATE ENUM VALUE_LIST ['CLOSED','OPEN','VENTILATION_POSITION','POSITION_UNKNOWN'] OPERATIONS 5; DOOR_COMMAND ENUM VALUE_LIST ['NOP','OPEN','STOP','CLOSE','PARTIAL_OPEN'] OPERATIONS 2 (write-only), DEFAULT 'NOP'. The channel declares NO LEVEL parameter at all.
all.firmwareValue: no LEVEL on the garage channel; the ventilation step is the enum label DOOR_STATE=VENTILATION_POSITION, commanded as DOOR_COMMAND=PARTIAL_OPEN (ordinal 4)
all.ourValue: level == 0.5, a synthetic mid-point our own code both produces and consumes
all.finding: The reader's framing is wrong and our code shows it: 0.5 is not a device value. Garage.Position() (garage.go:209-223) synthesises it from the DOOR_STATE enum — OPEN→1.0, VENTILATION_POSITION→0.5, CLOSED→0.0 — and the only consumer of Position.Vent() in the whole repo is Garage.IsStateChangeArgs (garage.go:338). The write path never carries a level: Garage.Vent() writes DOOR_COMMAND=PARTIAL_OPEN (garage.go:269-274, command() at :293-299). So 0.5 is a closed round trip between two literals in one package, both exactly 0.5 (exactly representable in float64, and custom.NewPosition clamps to [0,1] without touching it), and the failure mode the reader describes — the drive reporting the vent step as some other level — cannot occur, because the firmware puts no level on that channel. Where the rule IS narrow: the doc comment says "the position matches the garage door's intermediate ventilation step", which reads as a device property. It is not one. The boundary runs at the enum: the firmware's ventilation step is a label (VENTILATION_POSITION / PARTIAL_OPEN, ordinal 4 in the DOOR_COMMAND VALUE_LIST and in the CCU's own control at door_opener.fn:68), and 0.5 is purely our normalisation of it. Anyone porting Position.Vent() to a surface that reads a real LEVEL — a Cover with an intermediate stop — must not carry 0.5 across as a device constant. I kept reachesDevice=true because the guard suppresses a real DOOR_COMMAND write if the two literals ever drift apart, not because 0.5 is written.
all.negativeControl: Had 0.5 been the level the drive reports, the MOD-HO / MOD-TM DOOR_RECEIVER VALUES paramset would declare a LEVEL parameter (it declares six parameters and LEVEL is not among them), and the CCU's own door control would render a position percentage rather than three ordinal buttons. Both checks come back negative, and both would have come back positive on a real cover — the same script run against a HmIP-BROLL channel finds LEVEL with MIN/MAX.
all.challengeNote: NARROWING UPHELD, BOUNDARY WIDER THAN STATED, and one factual error in the prior finding. Verified verbatim: door_opener.fn:32 and the four setDpState ordinals; the DOOR_COMMAND VALUE_LIST indices line up with them exactly (1 OPEN, 2 STOP, 3 CLOSE, 4 PARTIAL_OPEN), and DOOR_STATE index 2 is VENTILATION_POSITION in both the CCU control's label list and the descriptor. So 'the firmware's ventilation step is a label, not a level' is correct and Tier-1 grounded. WHERE THE PRIOR FINDING IS WRONG: it states '0.5 is a closed round trip between two literals in one package' and 'the only consumer of Position.Vent() in the whole repo is Garage.IsStateChangeArgs'. The second half is true (grep: garage.go:338 is the sole `.Vent()` call site). The first half is not. Garage.Position() has a second consumer, payload.go:320, which multiplies it through Position.OpenFraction() (mixins.go:430) into `current_position: 50` on the garage state payload that MQTT and REST publish. So the synthetic mid-point IS user-visible, as a percentage the drive never reports and the CCU's own operator control never shows. That is exactly the 'reads as a device property but is not one' hazard the prior agent named in the doc comment — it just also happens on the wire. SECOND BOUNDARY, unnamed before: Garage.SetPosition (garage.go:283-291) maps an incoming position onto a DOOR_COMMAND using thresholds 0.50 and 0.10, and its own comment cites the Python reference for them. The firmware has no position-to-command mapping on this channel to compare against — no LEVEL exists — so those two constants are Tier-1 silent, not merely 'our normalisation'. A caller sending position 0.3 gets PARTIAL_OPEN on Tier-3 authority alone. reachesDevice stays true: a drift between Position()'s 0.5 and Vent()'s 0.5 suppresses a real DOOR_COMMAND=PARTIAL_OPEN write through the idempotence guard at garage.go:338.

all.title: Default diagnostic data points are pinned to channel offsets 0, 2 and 4
all.site: internal/model/custom/default_data_points.go:15, consumed at internal/model/custom/materialize.go:433 (loop variable absCh) via markParametersOnChannel/lookupChannelByNumber (:657-690)
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml, 127 device XMLs, parsed per <channel index=...> block. BATTERY_STATE: exactly three declarations fleet-wide — rf_cc_rt_dn.xml channel 4 (CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER), rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml channel 4, rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml channel 2 (THERMALCONTROL_TRANSMIT); no other file and no other channel. RSSI_DEVICE 125/125 on channel 0, RSSI_PEER 125/125 on channel 0, DUTYCYCLE 59/59 on channel 0. LOWBAT: channel 0 in 89 files AND channel 1 in rf_cc_vd.xml / rf_sec_sd_2.xml / rf_sec_sfa.xml / rf_wds30_ot2.xml, channel 4 in rf_cc_rt_dn.xml / rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml / rf_sec_sir_wm.xml, channel 5 in rf_wds30_ot2.xml. SABOTAGE: channel 0 in 13 files AND channel 1 in rf_sec_sfa.xml, channel 4 in rf_sec_sir_wm.xml. HmIP side, ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json (399 files, VALUES paramsets): LOW_BAT 68/68 channel 0, RSSI_DEVICE 362/362 channel 0, DUTY_CYCLE 108/108 channel 0, TIME_OF_OPERATION 2/2 channel 0, SABOTAGE 16/16 channel 0, OPERATING_VOLTAGE 115 on channel 0 plus 3 on channel 1 (HB-UNI-Sensor1, HB-UNI-Sensor-TH-SHT75, HB-UNI-Sensor-THPD-BME280 — community devices, absent from the CCU's shipped XMLs). BATTERY_STATE is not an HmIP parameter at all: it does not appear in HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterIdentifier, which does declare LOW_BAT, RSSI_DEVICE, DUTY_CYCLE, OPERATING_VOLTAGE, SABOTAGE and TIME_OF_OPERATION.
all.firmwareValue: BATTERY_STATE: channels {2, 4} exactly. The other seven: channel 0 always, but for LOWBAT and SABOTAGE not only channel 0.
all.ourValue: map[int][]Parameter{0: {ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE, DUTY_CYCLE, DUTYCYCLE, LOW_BAT, LOWBAT, OPERATING_VOLTAGE, RSSI_DEVICE, RSSI_PEER, SABOTAGE, TIME_OF_OPERATION}, 2: {BATTERY_STATE}, 4: {BATTERY_STATE}}
all.finding: The BATTERY_STATE half is exactly right and is now firmware-grounded rather than inherited: the CCU's own device XMLs declare it on channel 4 for the two HM-CC-RT-DN variants and on channel 2 for HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU, and nowhere else in 127 files — {2, 4} is the complete fleet, not a sample. Where the map is narrower than its header comment implies: "these are MAINTENANCE (channel 0) parameters everywhere" does not hold. LOWBAT is additionally declared on the functional channel in five families (HM-CC-VD ch1, HM-Sec-SD-2 ch1, HM-Sec-SFA-SM ch1, HM-WDS30-OT2-SM ch1+ch5, HM-Sec-Sir-WM ch4, HM-CC-RT-DN ch4) and SABOTAGE in two (HM-Sec-SFA-SM ch1, HM-Sec-Sir-WM ch4). Those copies are not force-marked and are suppressed on any device carrying a custom profile. The reader's failure mode nevertheless does not fire, and this is the part worth recording: in every one of those files the same parameter is ALSO declared on channel 0 MAINTENANCE, so the diagnostic never disappears from the north-bound surface — it is the duplicate on the functional channel that is dropped, which is what you want. Two smaller boundary notes. (a) The keys are absolute channel numbers, not offsets: materialize.go:433 names the loop variable absCh and passes it straight to lookupChannelByNumber, which compares against Channel.Number; only the profile's own AdditionalDataPoints are rebased by groupNo (:437-439). The file header calling them "channel offsets" is wrong in a way that will mislead the next editor. (b) ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE is in the channel-0 list for devices that report ambient temperature on MAINTENANCE (29 HmIP devices do), but it is far more often a functional-channel parameter (ch1 on 30 devices, and ch2/3/4/8 elsewhere) where the profile owns it — that is by design, not a gap, but the map entry reads like a diagnostic and is not one.
all.negativeControl: Had BATTERY_STATE been declared on a third channel anywhere, the per-<channel index=> scan over all 127 rftypes XMLs would have printed that index — the same scan does print index 1, 4 and 5 for LOWBAT and index 1 and 4 for SABOTAGE, so it demonstrably reports off-map channels when they exist. The check discriminates.
all.challengeNote: THE RULE SURVIVES; A NAMED PART OF THE PRIOR CITATION DOES NOT — do not copy it forward. Reproduced exactly: the BATTERY_STATE half. Three declarations in 127 CCU device XMLs, channels {2, 4}, files as named. That is complete-fleet Tier-1, and it is the half the map's unusual keys rest on. Also reproduced exactly: every Tier-2 figure in the prior citation. CONTRADICTED: (a) 'SABOTAGE: channel 0 in 13 files AND channel 1 in rf_sec_sfa.xml, channel 4 in rf_sec_sir_wm.xml' — the rftypes XMLs declare no parameter named SABOTAGE anywhere. All 13 files carry it only as an enum OPTION of ERROR, and the 'channel 1' / 'channel 4' figures are the option's own `index=` attribute, not a channel index. This is a category error, and it is the exact shape this audit exists to catch: an attribute reused as if it were a different axis. On BidCos, sabotage is an ERROR enum value; our ParameterSabotage entry is grounded on the HmIP descriptor (16 devices, all channel 0) and on nothing else. (b) 'LOWBAT … channel 4 in rf_cc_rt_dn.xml / rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml / rf_sec_sir_wm.xml' — neither rt_dn file declares LOWBAT outside channel 0; only rf_sec_sir_wm.xml has it on channel 4. (c) The channel-1 set is 16 files, not the 4 named, and rf_cc_vd.xml is not one of them (LOWBAT there is channel 0 only). (d) Channel 3 (rf_em_8_bit.xml; 8 devices in the descriptor corpus) was missed entirely. THE LOAD-BEARING CONSEQUENCE, tested independently: I checked all 399 descriptor files for a parameter declared on a non-zero channel with NO channel-0 copy. For LOWBAT / LOW_BAT / SABOTAGE the prior claim holds — there is always a channel-0 copy, so the suppression pass only ever drops the duplicate. It does NOT hold for OPERATING_VOLTAGE: the three HB-UNI community devices declare it on channel 1 and nowhere else. The prior finding mentions those three but asserts the failure mode 'does not fire' on a blanket 'in every one of those files' that is false. It happens not to fire today for a different reason: no HB-UNI device carries a custom profile in this repo (the only occurrences are fixtures in internal/model/custom/registry_hardening_test.go), so the custom-DP suppression pass never runs on them. That is a repo fact, not a firmware one, and it changes the day someone registers such a profile. BOUNDARY NOTE UPHELD: the keys are absolute channel numbers. materialize.go:433 names the loop variable absCh and hands it to lookupChannelByNumber, which compares against Channel.Number — the address-suffix channel number (internal/model/device/channel.go:94). Only profile AdditionalDataPoints are rebased by groupNo (:437-439). The file header at default_data_points.go:11 calling them 'channel offsets', and the comment at materialize.go:432 calling 0/2/4 'the maintenance channels', are both wrong in ways that will mislead the next editor: channel 2 of HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU and channel 4 of HM-CC-RT-DN are functional climate channels, not maintenance channels.

all.title: Timer promotion truncates toward zero on the port's authority, and the comment says so
all.site: internal/model/custom/mixins.go:219 (EncodeTimerDuration), threshold at :136, rounding claim at :209-214, disclaimer at :133-135
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#migrateDurations — the seconds→pair promotion, verbatim in structure: `onTime > 0.0 && onTime < 1.0` → DURATION_UNIT "10MS", DURATION_VALUE `(int)(onTime * 100.0)`; `< 16000.0` → "S", `(int)onTime`; `< 960000.0` → "M", `(int)(onTime / 60.0)`; else → "H", `(int)(onTime / 3600.0)`. Same four-way split for RAMP_TIME with the same constants. Reverse direction in the same method: `onTime = durationUnitFaktor * durationValueFaktor; if (onTime >= 111600.0) onTime = 8580000.0;`. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#correctInfiniteDuration — when DURATION_UNIT is "H" (or "2") and DURATION_VALUE >= 31.0, DURATION_VALUE is replaced by 16383, with the firmware's own log line naming it "handle duration of 31h as infinity (0x3FFF)". HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues calls correctInfiniteDuration on the raw parameter set for every paramset write; #migrateDurations is reached only from #convertCombinedParameter. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDurationValueParameter declares DURATION_VALUE / RAMP_TIME_VALUE as INTEGER, WRITE-only, default 0, min 0, max 16343; #createDurationUnitParameter declares the enum as {"S","M","H"} (oldFormat) or {"S","M","H","10MS"}. Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json — DURATION_VALUE INTEGER MIN 0 MAX 16343 DEFAULT 0 in all 95 declarations, RAMP_TIME_VALUE identical in all 72; DURATION_UNIT VALUE_LIST ['S','M','H'] on 23 devices and ['S','M','H','10MS'] on 72.
all.firmwareValue: truncation via Java (int) narrowing — but at thresholds 1 s / 16000 s / 960000 s, with a 10MS bucket below 1 s, and on the COMBINED_PARAMETER surface only. On our surface the firmware performs no promotion, and instead rewrites any (value>=31, H) pair to (16383, H) = infinite.
all.ourValue: truncation via int32 cast, thresholds 16343 in both units, no 10MS bucket, sentinel (111600, H)
all.finding: The rounding claim itself holds and can now be grounded: where the CCU does promote a duration into a (value, unit) pair it truncates — `(int)(onTime / 60.0)` and `(int)(onTime / 3600.0)`, Java narrowing, toward zero — so 16373 s → 272 M is what the firmware would produce too. mixins.go:133-135's admission that float_configtime does not govern this is correct; the governing code is DeviceUtil, not HSSTypeConversionFloatConfigtime. Three ways the surrounding claim is false one step wider, and the boundary is the surface. (1) SURFACE: #migrateDurations is called only from #convertCombinedParameter, i.e. it decodes the COMBINED_PARAMETER string the WebUI builds (`L=..,DU=..,DV=..,RTU=..,RTV=..,R=..,SL=..`, www/webui/webui.js:19831). Our Siren and Light write DURATION_VALUE/DURATION_UNIT directly into a VALUES paramset (siren.go:328-336, light.go:873-877), which reaches #validateAndConvertValues, where no promotion happens at all. So on OUR path the firmware supplies no rounding rule — that half is genuinely tier-1-silent and the port is the only authority, as the comment says. (2) THRESHOLDS: the firmware's own promotion switches at 16000 s and 960000 s; ours at 16343 in both units. 16100 s → ours (16100, S), firmware (268, M). Between 960000 s and 980580 s → ours (16000..16343, M), firmware (266..272, H). Both encodings are in range and denote the same duration to within the firmware's own truncation loss, so neither is broken — but our threshold is not the firmware's, and mixins.go:126-129's "Promoting only once the value would exceed the declared maximum is therefore the field's rule" describes the parameter's MAX (16343, confirmed at Tier 1 by #createDurationValueParameter), not the CCU's promotion rule. (3) THE ONE THAT BITES, and it is on our surface: #correctInfiniteDuration runs on every VALUES paramset we send, and turns any DURATION_VALUE >= 31 carrying DURATION_UNIT=H into 16383, which the firmware's own log calls infinity. Our encoder reaches unit H only when the minutes value already exceeds 16343, i.e. for durations above 980580 s — so the smallest hours value it can ever emit is 272, and 272 >= 31. Every single duration our encoder promotes to hours is therefore silently converted by the CCU into "run forever". A requested 20-day siren (1728000 s → our (480, H)) becomes infinite. So does the TimerNotUsed sentinel: our (111600, H) is rewritten to (16383, H), which happens to be the right outcome but not for the reason mixins.go:141-144 gives — the comment says "the value stays unchanged and the unit is forced to hours", and on this path the value does not stay unchanged. 111600 does appear in the firmware, but as the seconds-side infinity threshold in the reverse mapping (`if (onTime >= 111600.0) onTime = 8580000.0`), not as an encodable DURATION_VALUE; 111600 also exceeds the declared MAX of 16343. Fourth, smaller: we have no 10MS bucket, so a sub-second duration truncates to (0, S) and is lost — the firmware would send (50, 10MS) for 0.5 s, and 72 of 95 DURATION_UNIT declarations carry 10MS.
all.negativeControl: Had our rounding been wrong — had the port rounded to nearest — the firmware's promotion would read `(int)Math.round(onTime / 60.0)` or `(int)(onTime / 60.0 + 0.5)`; it reads `(int)(onTime / 60.0)`, and the same scan does show the firmware using a different form where it means something different (`(int)(onTime * 100.0)` for the 10MS bucket), so the check distinguishes rounding from truncation. For the 31 h finding the control is arithmetic on a firmware constant rather than a second reading: our encoder's minimum hours value is 16344/60 = 272, and correctInfiniteDuration's guard is >= 31 — had our promotion threshold been low enough to emit small hour counts, values below 31 would pass through untouched and the finding would not stand.
all.challengeNote: THE HEADLINE SUB-FINDING IS CONTRADICTED. The prior report's item (3), presented as 'THE ONE THAT BITES, and it is on our surface' — every hours-unit duration we send is silently rewritten by the CCU to 16383 = infinite, a 20-day siren running forever — does not follow, and the refutation is one type coercion deep. #correctInfiniteDuration gates on `"2".equals(x) || "H".equals(x)`, i.e. String.equals(Object). It runs on the RAW parameter set, before any enum conversion. We send DURATION_UNIT as an integer ordinal: hmenum.TimerUnitHours = 2 (pkg/hmenum/timer.go:35), staged as int32 by EncodeTimerDuration, converted by goToXMLRPCValue (internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:73) to xmlrpc.IntValue, marshalled as `<int>2</int>` (value.go:104), and decoded by the CCU's own XML-RPC parser via Integer.parseInt into a java.lang.Integer. `"2".equals(Integer.valueOf(2))` is false; so is `"H".equals(Integer.valueOf(2))`. The rewrite cannot fire on any write this daemon makes. The same disproves the prior claim that our (111600, H) sentinel 'is rewritten to (16383, H)' — it is not; 111600 goes through as sent. The disjunction `"0".equals(x) || "S".equals(x)` throughout #migrateDurations shows what the firmware expects when it wants an ordinal: the STRING "2", not the integer 2. This is a latent condition, not a live bug — and worth recording as such, because it inverts: the day anyone changes DURATION_UNIT to be written as the label "H" or the string "2" (which is how we write other enums, e.g. the siren's acoustic selection), every hours-unit duration WOULD become infinite. WHAT I UPHELD. The surface analysis is right and I re-traced the whole call graph rather than taking it: #migrateDurations reaches only COMBINED_PARAMETER, so the firmware supplies no promotion rule on our VALUES-paramset path, and mixins.go:133-135's admission that float_configtime does not govern this is correct — the governing code is DeviceUtil, not HSSTypeConversionFloatConfigtime. The truncation transcription is exact, including `(int)` Java narrowing toward zero, so 16373 s -> 272 M is what the firmware would produce on its own surface. MAX 16343 is Tier-1 confirmed by #createDurationValueParameter, so timeUnitThreshold is not an invented constant — but the prior agent is right that mixins.go:126-129 describes the field's MAX and calls it 'the field's rule', which the firmware's own 16000/960000 promotion contradicts. Both encodings denote the same duration within truncation loss, so neither is broken. ONE CORRECTION to sub-finding (4): the missing 10MS bucket does not apply to the siren. #createDurationUnitParameter is registered for the siren channel with oldFormat = true, whose enum is {"S","M","H"} with no 10MS at all; the 72-of-95 figure is fleet-wide, not siren-wide. A sub-second siren duration truncating to (0, S) is still a real loss, but the firmware would not have sent 10MS there either. Route note: the siren batches DURATION_VALUE and DURATION_UNIT through one PutParamset (siren.go:317-323 collector; internal/model/generic/collector.go:219-221 collapses same-order same-channel writes), so #putParameterSet -> #validateAndConvertValues really is our path — the refutation is the value type, not the surface.

all.finding: I opened our site: SetPosition is a pure 3-way switch on the caller's 0..1 target that then writes the DOOR_COMMAND string. The CCU does not decide the thresholds, because it never models the door as a position at all. Both parameters are enumerations; the ventilation stop is a named enum member (VENTILATION_POSITION / PARTIAL_OPEN), not a percentage. I grepped all 212 channel-type definitions shipped in ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/HMIPServer.jar and all 130 ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml: no garage/door channel declares a LEVEL, and no BidCos device type declares DOOR_STATE or DOOR_COMMAND at all (the drive is HmIP-only). Our code should keep following the enum (Tier 1); the 0.50/0.10 split is our own presentation policy and should be documented as such rather than as CCU behaviour. Secondary: aiohomematic bounds the OPEN branch (`50 < position <= 100`); our Go drops the upper bound, so a target above 1.0 also opens — harmless but a divergence from the cited source.

No Kelvin, no mired, no unit beyond "100%". Direction and curve are MASTER-configurable: CHARACTERISTIC_COLOURASSIGNMENT ∈ {CHARACTERISTIC_LOW_IS_WARM (default), CHARACTERISTIC_LOW_IS_COLD}; CHARACTERISTIC_LINSQUARETYPE ∈ {CHARACTERISTIC_LINEAR, CHARACTERISTIC_SQUARE (default)}; CHARACTERISTIC_BASETYPE ∈ {CHARACTERISTIC_CROSSFADE (default), CHARACTERISTIC_DIM2WARM, CHARACTERISTIC_DIM2HOT}.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_dw.xml:602-614 (DUAL_WHITE_COLOR LEVEL in `color_valueset`), :342-349 (CHARACTERISTIC_BASETYPE), :351-358 (CHARACTERISTIC_LINSQUARETYPE), :367-373 (CHARACTERISTIC_COLOURASSIGNMENT, default CHARACTERISTIC_LOW_IS_WARM); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/dual_white_controller.fn:118-141 and :181 (renders the value as a % slider and a % readout only); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseDualWhiteColor.js:144-152 (picks the transfer-curve diagram from those four MASTER parameters); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:357 ("Colour value") and :115-116 ("low is cold white" / "low is warm white"); contrast HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createColorTemperature; Tier-3 witness for provenance: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:32-37 and :544.
all.finding: Our site is the RF tunable-white branch (l.colorLevel), so the surface is HM-LC-DW-WM's DUAL_WHITE_COLOR channel — I checked the firmware is on that same path before citing. The CCU declares that channel's LEVEL as a dimensionless 0..1 "colour value" with unit "100%" and a 0..200 integer wire scale; the WebUI shows it only as a percentage. Deciding what Kelvin 0.0 and 1.0 mean requires the colour temperatures of the two white LED strips wired to the PWM outputs — hardware the CCU never sees. That input exists in no Tier-1 or Tier-2 source, so the measurement is not performable and the endpoint values 2000 K / 6535 K cannot be grounded (they are HA's own default mired range, arriving via light.py). Two further firmware facts bear on the rule and are worth recording even though they do not settle the endpoints: (1) the warm↔cold *direction* is per-device configurable and only agrees with ours at the CHARACTERISTIC_LOW_IS_WARM default — on a CHARACTERISTIC_LOW_IS_COLD device our mapping is inverted for every value; (2) the transfer curve defaults to CHARACTERISTIC_SQUARE, not linear, so no single fixed linear mapping is universally right. Where the CCU *does* model colour temperature — the HmIP UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER channel — it declares COLOR_TEMPERATURE as an INTEGER in Kelvin with min 1000, max 10200, step 20; our l.kelvin branch writes Kelvin directly there and is unaffected.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU carried the mapping, it would have appeared as a unit or logical range on the parameter (the way HmIP's COLOR_TEMPERATURE carries min 1000 / max 10200 / step 20), or as a Kelvin/mired conversion in the WebUI control. Both checks demonstrably react: the same reads found an explicit Kelvin range on the HmIP colour-temperature parameter and an explicit % rendering on the DUAL_WHITE control. For DUAL_WHITE_COLOR they returned "100%" and a percent slider — the CCU carries no colour-temperature semantics for this channel.
all.missingInput: the colour temperature of the two white LED strips at LEVEL 0.0 and 1.0 (a property of the installation, not of the CCU), plus the per-device CHARACTERISTIC_COLOURASSIGNMENT and CHARACTERISTIC_LINSQUARETYPE settings that decide direction and curve

all.finding: The firmware settles the contradiction in favour of light.go and against color.go, and the family split light.go documents is exactly right. resolveOnTimeParams's premise — that no light carries ON_TIME_VALUE / ON_TIME_UNIT — is confirmed outright: those two literals occur nowhere in the CCU. Its family mapping is confirmed parameter-for-parameter: signal lights and RGBW/DALI carry DURATION_VALUE + DURATION_UNIT, plain dimmers carry a bare seconds ON_TIME. TurnOnFixedColor is contradicted: its doc-comment asserts "HmIP-BSL expects ON_TIME_VALUE / ON_TIME_UNIT (not DURATION_*)", and the BSL channel definition says the opposite in the same breath — DURATION_VALUE / DURATION_UNIT, subtype withColor. One correction to the damage note in the bundle: the CCU does not fault the put_paramset. validateAndConvertValues looks the key up in the channel's state parameters, gets null, and passes the value through unconverted into the backend command, so the two keys are silently discarded — the LED lights with the right colour and level and simply never times out. Mitigating: TurnOnFixedColor has no production caller today (only light tests), so this is latent rather than live; severity is raised over the bundle's medium because the fix is a two-name change on a device-reaching payload and the wrong names are additionally asserted in a doc-comment other code may copy. A further note for the write path: the CCU rewrites an incoming DURATION_UNIT=H with DURATION_VALUE ≥ 31 to 16383 ('infinite') before dispatch (DeviceUtil#correctInfiniteDuration), and requires DURATION_UNIT and DURATION_VALUE to travel together (DeviceUtil#checkRequiredValues) — our stageTimerPair already sends them as a pair.
all.negativeControl: Had ON_TIME_VALUE / ON_TIME_UNIT been real CCU names, the greps would have found them. They demonstrably react: over the 212 extracted channel_type XMLs, `DURATION_VALUE` hits 21 files and `<parameter>ON_TIME</parameter>` hits 16, while `ON_TIME_VALUE` and `ON_TIME_UNIT` hit 0. The same two literals return zero across ../OpenCCU-Base/src, opt and www, whereas DURATION_VALUE returns hits in legacy-parameter-definition.config and ON_TIME returns hits in 72 rftypes XMLs.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD on the headline, with three attached sub-claims demoted. What I checked independently: (1) the fleet-wide negative — I extracted all 212 channel_type definitions and grepped them, plus the whole of ../OpenCCU-Base and the whole pydevccu descriptor corpus; ON_TIME_VALUE/ON_TIME_UNIT occur nowhere. (2) The family split — confirmed parameter-for-parameter on Tier 1 (channel-type state blocks) and independently on Tier 2 (per-device paramset descriptors). (3) color.go is contradicted, and I found the exact provenance the bundle did not name: in the Python reference Field.ON_TIME_VALUE is a profile SLOT name that resolves per-profile to Parameter.DURATION_VALUE for fixed-colour/RGBW and to Parameter.ON_TIME for dimmers. color.go promoted the slot name to a wire parameter name — the classic wrong-surface substitution. color.go:808-809 is the only production use of those two literals in the repo. DEMOTED — (a) Device attribution. The bundle labels OPTICAL_SIGNAL_RECEIVER "HmIP-BSL notification light". The channel_type XML carries a channel type, not a device; nothing in it names HmIP-BSL. The descriptor corpus places OPTICAL_SIGNAL_RECEIVER only on HmIPW-WRC6 (:7-:13) and types HmIP-BSL's notification channels DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER carrying COLOR/COLOR_BEHAVIOUR/DURATION_*. The firmware carries branches for BOTH shapes (DeviceUtil#checkRequiredValues has a DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER-with-COLOR branch and a separate OPTICAL_SIGNAL_RECEIVER branch), so both exist; which one a given BSL firmware reports is not settled by the cited source. Fortunately both carry DURATION_* and neither carries ON_TIME_*, so the parameter conclusion is unaffected. (b) 'requires DURATION_UNIT and DURATION_VALUE to travel together (checkRequiredValues) — our stageTimerPair already sends them as a pair'. Wrong surface and wrong reassurance. checkRequiredValues has exactly one call site and it is inside DeviceUtil#setValue, not DeviceUtil#putParameterSet; the put_paramset path never reaches it. And stageTimerPair sends them as a pair only on the collector path — its fallback issues two separate w.SetValue calls, which IS the setValue path. There the firmware buffers the incomplete first write in a static DeviceChannelValuesCommandDTO, returns false without dispatching, and merges it into the next setValue on the same device+channel. So the first SetValue legitimately returns false; our code inspects only the error, not the boolean. (c) 'the two keys are silently discarded — the LED lights and simply never times out'. Half verified: convertParameterValue's pass-through is verbatim, so the CCU does not fault the call. What happens after the values are handed to the HmIP backend over the event bus is not readable in these sources — the 'never times out' tail is inference, not measurement. SEVERITY demoted from the bundle's raise back to medium: TurnOnFixedColor has no production caller (only light_behavior_test.go), and even when called the CCU does not reject the payload, so the worst case is a missing timeout on a latent path plus a doc-comment that states the wrong names and invites copying.

all.title: Timer.Max publishes 16343 as a maximum in seconds, though 16343 is DURATION_VALUE's per-unit INTEGER maximum
all.ourValue: Max() returns 16343 with the doc-comment "the upper-bound seconds threshold" — i.e. 4 h 32 min 23 s presented as the data point's maximum in seconds
all.firmwareValue: DURATION_VALUE is INTEGER, default 0, min 0, max 16343 *counts*, paired with DURATION_UNIT ∈ {S, M, H} (older channels) or {S, M, H, 10MS} (default S). The count's seconds meaning is value × {1, 60, 3600, 0.01}. The legacy surface's own seconds-domain limits are different numbers again: DURATION_UNIT=H with DURATION_VALUE ≥ 31 is rewritten to 16383 (0x3FFF, the 'infinite' marker) on the way in, and on the read-back path any unit×value ≥ 111600 s is reported as ON_TIME = 8580000 s.
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDurationValueParameter (LogicalType.INTEGER, default 0, min 0, max 16343 — the single factory used for DURATION_VALUE on the withColor, uniLight, siren and withRoom groups and for RAMP_TIME_VALUE / RAMP_TIME_TO_OFF_VALUE / MANUAL_SELF_CALIBRATION_DURATION_VALUE) and #createDurationUnitParameter (LogicalType.ENUM over {"S","M","H"} or {"S","M","H","10MS"}, default "S"); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createDurationValueParameter (same literal 16343); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#correctInfiniteDuration and #migrateDurations.
all.finding: I read our site: Max() hands out float64(timerUpperBoundSeconds) unconditionally, and the constant's own comment two files over (timer.go:25-27) correctly calls it "the threshold above which seconds are re-expressed as minutes" — so the package already contradicts itself, and the firmware sides with timer.go and projection.go against data_point.go. 16343 is the wire integer's maximum per unit, not a duration. Three consequences worth separating. (1) The uniformity claim in internal/model/custom/mixins.go:115-120 is confirmed: 16343 is a single literal in one factory method that every DURATION_VALUE-bearing channel goes through, so no channel declares a different max. (2) projection.go's "~678 days at the hours unit" is arithmetically right about the integer but is not a reachable duration: the CCU coerces DURATION_UNIT=H with value ≥ 31 to the infinite marker before dispatch, so at the hours unit the largest *finite* duration is 30 h. (3) There is therefore no single seconds number to publish — the honest Max() is unit-dependent, and if one number is wanted, the reachable finite ceiling below the infinity coercion is 111600 s (31 h), not 16343 s and not 678 days. Also worth recording: the CCU's own encoder promotes seconds→minutes at 16000 s and minutes→hours at 960000 s (DeviceUtil#migrateDurations), whereas our RecalcUnit promotes at 16343 and 16343 min. Both stay inside the declared integer max, so both are legal writes; the divergence is not a defect but it is a divergence. reachesDevice is false for Max() itself (a read-side metadata accessor that only over-restricts a slider or validator), though the same constant does drive RecalcUnit on the write path.
all.negativeControl: Had 16343 been a seconds cap, the firmware would have had to enforce it in the seconds domain — a check on unit×value against 16343, or a DURATION_VALUE max that varied with the unit. It does neither: the max is a constant argument in one factory that never sees the unit, and the only seconds-domain thresholds in the legacy surface are 111600 and 8580000. The check reacts: the same reading located real seconds-domain limits (111600 / 8580000) and the real unit enum, so it would have surfaced a seconds cap had one existed.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD on the headline and re-verified two ways: 16343 is DURATION_VALUE's per-unit INTEGER maximum (Tier 1 factory literal, Tier 2 descriptor MAX with TYPE INTEGER and a paired unit ENUM), so Max()'s doc-comment 'upper-bound seconds threshold' is wrong and the package already contradicts itself — timer.go:25-27 correctly calls the same constant a unit-promotion threshold. The uniformity claim is confirmed: 16343 is one literal in one factory method per server and nothing else in the corpus carries it. BUT three of the bundle's supporting statements are WRONG SURFACE and must not be used as the fix. (1) 'on the read-back path any unit x value >= 111600 s is reported as ON_TIME = 8580000 s'. That code is in DeviceUtil#migrateDurations, whose only caller is DeviceUtil#convertCombinedParameter — the COMBINED_PARAMETER decoder on the way IN. It is not a read-back path at all, and the branch fires only when the target channel declares an ON_TIME state parameter. Our Timer writes DURATION_VALUE/DURATION_UNIT directly, so this clamp never touches it. (2) Consequently 'the reachable finite ceiling below the infinity coercion is 111600 s (31 h)' is wrong twice over: the number comes from a surface we do not use, and it is self-inconsistent — correctInfiniteDuration coerces at value >= 31.0, so 31 h is precisely the first coerced value, making 30 h the largest finite hours-unit duration. On the path we actually write, the coercion applies only at unit H, so the largest finite duration reachable through a direct DURATION_* write is 16343 minutes (about 11.35 days), not 111600 s. Whether the device accepts it is valve/actuator firmware and is not readable here. (3) 'the CCU's own encoder promotes seconds->minutes at 16000 s and minutes->hours at 960000 s, whereas our RecalcUnit promotes at 16343 — a divergence'. Same wrong surface: those thresholds live in the else-branch of migrateDurations, which runs only when a caller sends ON_TIME inside a COMBINED_PARAMETER to a channel that declares no ON_TIME. Our RecalcUnit emits DURATION_VALUE/DURATION_UNIT directly and never passes through that encoder, so there is no divergence to record. What survives on our path: correctInfiniteDuration is genuinely on it (it runs at the head of validateAndConvertValues for every VALUES write), so unit=H with value >= 31 becomes 16383/infinite whether we intended it or not. FURTHER DEMOTION the bundle did not make: the title says Timer.Max 'publishes' 16343. I could find no production call site of Max() on a Timer anywhere in the repo — the method exists to satisfy a data-point interface and nothing in internal/north or internal/payload invokes it; the HA number bound comes from projection.go's independent timerMaxSeconds = 86400. So today this is a wrong constant and a wrong doc-comment in an unconsumed accessor, not a published value. Severity accordingly low.

all.title: The switch-to-sensor demotion list (HmIP-eTRV / HmIP-HEATING LEVEL) overrides the descriptor's own OPERATIONS on a case-insensitive model-prefix match
