all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/HMIPServer.jar!de/eq3/cbcs/devicedescription/channelspecification/channel_type_heating_climatecontrol_transceiver_trv.xml, !…_trv2.xml, !…_trv3.xml, !…_trv_cooling.xml, !…_trv_bosch.xml (`LEVEL` in ``, no subtype attribute) versus !…_transceiver_wth.xml, !…_wth2.xml, !…_scthd.xml, !…_rbga.xml (no LEVEL); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.ChannelTypeReader#getParameterMapKeyFromNode (a `` with no subtype attribute maps to subtype "default"), de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLevel and #getReadWriteEventIOOperation (READ|EVENT|WRITE), de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations (READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4), de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (the legacy descriptor's OPERATIONS is that value verbatim) and #getParamsetId (the label keys in the config file are device TYPE labels); ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config:10-25 (the eTRV-family label list) and :410 (HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER.LEVEL.Control=HEATING_CONTROL_HMIP.LEVEL, not Disabled); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/heating_control.fn:216 and :363-372 (LEVEL rendered as a read-only `…%`; the only writable control on that page is the SETPOINT slider); HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.hmip.service.internal.HmIPGroupDefinitionProvider (HMIP_HEATING_GROUP_TYPE = "HmIP-HEATING"; the group's thermostat channel state is the merge of the WTH and TRV channel-1 state descriptions, so it inherits LEVEL, and no aggregation is registered for LEVEL).
all.finding: Two halves, and they land differently. The *semantic* half is confirmed: the descriptor really does advertise LEVEL as READ|WRITE|EVENT on the eTRV climate channel — our comment's premise is exact — and the CCU's own operator surface never writes it, rendering it as a bare percentage readout while the page's only writable control is SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE. That is the read/write-direction answer the descriptor alone cannot give, and it backs the demotion. The *scope* half is narrower than the firmware's own family. The CCU keys eTRV-family membership off the device TYPE label, and its list includes "Thermostat AA", an OEM-branded label the CCU maps to the eTRV paramset and which does not begin with "HmIP-eTRV"; our prefix match therefore leaves its LEVEL writable. The channel-type catalogue also carries a `..._transceiver_trv_bosch` variant that declares LEVEL, consistent with an OEM radiator thermostat under a non-HmIP label. The list also shows why case-insensitivity is load-bearing rather than incidental: the CCU itself ships "HMIP-eTRV-2" alongside "HmIP-eTRV-2". Nothing suggests the rule is too *wide*: only radiator-thermostat channel versions declare LEVEL at all, and "HmIP-HEATING" is the exact group type string with no wider HmIP type sharing that prefix. One limit I will not paper over: whether a LEVEL write is *rejected* by the device is not decided by these sources — DeviceUtil#checkRequiredValues only requires SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE companions on that channel type and does not block the key, and an unrecognised or unsupported write is forwarded to the HmIP backend, so the outcome is valve-firmware behaviour I cannot read here. The demotion is justified by the CCU's own UI treatment, not by a proven write rejection.
all.negativeControl: Had the descriptor genuinely made LEVEL read-only — the alternative explanation for the demotion — the channel definition would have carried `<parameter subtype="READ_ONLY">LEVEL</parameter>`, binding createReadOnlyLevel (READ|EVENT). That subtype exists and is used elsewhere, so the check reacts; here the attribute is absent, giving subtype "default" and READ|WRITE|EVENT. Conversely, had the family been exactly our two prefixes, the CCU's own membership list would have contained only HmIP-eTRV*/HmIP-HEATING labels; reading it produced "Thermostat AA" and "HMIP-eTRV-2", which is how the boundary was found rather than assumed.
all.missingInput: the device-label → channel-type-version binding (which model uses …_trv_bosch), which none of the readable CCU sources carries — so I can name "Thermostat AA" as a family member our prefixes miss, but cannot state from firmware that its channel declares LEVEL
all.challengeNote: UPHELD on the semantic half, NARROWED FURTHER than the bundle on the scope half, and one of the bundle's scope arguments demoted to inference. Verified end to end: the map-key chain (unsubtyped <parameter> -> subtype "default" -> ParameterMapKey("LEVEL") -> createLevel -> READ|EVENT|WRITE) is complete and verbatim, and Tier 2 independently reports OPERATIONS 7 with MIN 0.0 / MAX 1.01, matching createLevel's constructor arguments exactly. So the comment's premise is exact: the descriptor really does advertise LEVEL as writable, and the CCU's own operator page never writes it. I also confirmed the WebUI answer survives the distribution patch that rewrites that very block — a step the bundle did not report and the one that could most easily have inverted the finding. I found one channel-type version the bundle's list omitted, _wth_cooling_optimized (tv 10); it declares no LEVEL, so the conclusion is unchanged. The group half is now settled on two tiers: HMIP_HEATING_GROUP_TYPE is verbatim "HmIP-HEATING", the thermostat channel state is an unfiltered merge of the WTH and TRV channel-1 state descriptions with no LEVEL aggregation, and the descriptor corpus shows the resulting group device really does expose LEVEL with OPERATIONS 7. DEMOTED — (a) The bundle says 'the only writable control on that page is the SETPOINT slider'. heating_control.fn also writes ACTIVE_PROFILE via setDpState (:460) alongside the setpoint input and slider. Immaterial to LEVEL, but it is an overstatement. (b) The 'Thermostat AA' scope gap is INFERENCE, not measurement, and I decline to promote it. What the source carries is a line in a section headed '# Mapping of the paramset id' mapping the string 'Thermostat AA' to 'hmip-etrv'. That maps a paramset id used for Control/Unit label lookup; it does not say the device declares HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER at a trv typeversion, and therefore does not establish that such a device has a LEVEL to demote. The same section maps 'ALPHA-IP-RBG' to 'hmip-wth-2' — a wall-thermostat paramset whose channel types declare no LEVEL — which shows the mapping does discriminate but also shows it is a paramset-id mapping, not a channel-type mapping. That the key is a runtime device model string is supported only by a Tier-3 witness. Treating the config key as a device TYPE our matcher sees is exactly the kind of convention this audit exists to catch, so the gap is credible but unverified. (c) The bundle's citation 'DeviceUtil#getParamsetId' is a wrong symbol: DeviceUtil declares no such method; getParamsetId lives on the legacy service handler and the virtual-remote-control component. (d) 'trv_bosch consistent with an OEM radiator thermostat under a non-HmIP label' is speculation the source does not support — the channel-type file names a typeversion, not a manufacturer. CONFIRMED SCOPE: case-insensitivity is load-bearing, not incidental — the config ships 'HMIP-eTRV-2' next to 'HmIP-eTRV-2'; and the rule is not too wide, since only radiator-thermostat typeversions declare LEVEL at all and no other HmIP type shares the 'HmIP-HEATING' prefix. The bundle's own limit stands and I add nothing to it: whether a LEVEL write is rejected at the valve is not decided by these sources — DeviceUtil#checkRequiredValues imposes no LEVEL guard on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER, and an unrecognised or unsupported write is forwarded to the HmIP backend. The demotion is justified by the CCU's operator surface, not by a proven write rejection.

all.title: TIME_OF_OPERATION is assumed to be seconds and is divided by 86400 for display
all.ourValue: raw value is seconds; ×(1/86400) → days, label forced to "d"
all.firmwareValue: raw value published on the legacy XML-RPC surface is seconds (unit selector already applied by the CCU); no UNIT declared on the parameter
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler — the StatusDataType.TIME_OF_OPERATION branch; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.protocol.hmip.application.StatusDataType (TIME_OF_OPERATION = id 12, 2 payload bytes); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createTimeOfOperationParameter. Label only (no unit): ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/stringtable_de.txt:2011 and www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:837 ("Time of operation").
all.finding: Our site is right, and for a reason the reader's summary did not carry: the CCU does not forward a raw device counter — it *normalises* one. The 2-byte status payload carries a 2-bit unit selector in the top bits of byte 0 and a 14-bit magnitude in the remaining 14 bits; the handler multiplies the magnitude by 1 (selector 0), 60 (1), 3600 (2) or 86400 (3) and publishes the product as TIME_OF_OPERATION. Whatever resolution the device reports in, the value that reaches an XML-RPC client is seconds. Two corroborating facts from the same tree: the magnitudes 16383 and 16382 are reserved (they raise TIME_OF_OPERATION_STATUS to UNKNOWN / OVERFLOW and the value is suppressed), and the state parameter is declared INTEGER with min 0 and max 1415491200 — which is exactly 16383 × 86400, i.e. the 14-bit ceiling taken at day resolution and expressed in seconds. A max of 16383 would have meant the CCU passes the raw magnitude through. Separately: the parameter is constructed with no unit, and opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config carries no TIME_OF_OPERATION.Unit entry, so the descriptor's UNIT arrives empty and our fixUnitByParam "d" is the only label there is — self-consistent with the 1/86400 multiplier, but it does mean a consumer that reads the unit without applying Multiplier() renders seconds under a "d" label. That coupling is our risk, not a firmware disagreement.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU reported days, the TIME_OF_OPERATION branch would publish the 14-bit magnitude unscaled with no unit-selector switch, and createTimeOfOperationParameter would declare max 16383 rather than 1415491200. Both discriminators point the same way, so the check can distinguish the two readings.
all.challengeNote: Upheld, and every step of the chain re-read rather than taken on report. What I checked: (1) the enum really is TIME_OF_OPERATION(12, 2); (2) the handler branch decodes exactly as claimed — a 2-bit selector `valueData[0] >> 6 & 3` and a 14-bit magnitude `(valueData[0] & 0x3F) << 8 | valueData[1] & 0xFF`, then a switch multiplying by 60 / 3600 / 86400 for selectors 1 / 2 / 3 and leaving selector 0 unscaled, i.e. seconds in every case; (3) magnitude 16383 raises TIME_OF_OPERATION_STATUS=UNKNOWN and 16382 raises OVERFLOW, and both branches pass null as the parameter data so no value is published; (4) createTimeOfOperationParameter really builds INTEGER/INTEGER with min 0 and max 1415491200 = 16383 x 86400, which only makes sense if the published quantity is the day-resolution ceiling expressed in seconds. Two things I extended beyond the candidate. First, the "no unit" claim is stronger than stated: StateParameter/AbstractParameter carry no unit field at all, so the legacy UNIT can only come from legacy-parameter-definition.config, and that file has no TIME_OF_OPERATION entry — the descriptor's UNIT is necessarily empty. Second, the last link (seconds computed -> seconds published) was unread in the candidate and I closed it: the parameter is constructed with a null converter, AbstractParameter substitutes DefaultTypeConverterFactory.createDefaultTypeConverter(INTEGER, INTEGER), and tryConvertParameter feeds it the 4-byte big-endian seconds value — no scaling in between. One transcription slip to record: in the OVERFLOW branch the handler computes value *= 86400 and then still passes null, so that multiplication is dead; "the value is suppressed" is right, but nothing publishes an overflow magnitude. Scope: Tier 2 is silent — TIME_OF_OPERATION appears in no rftypes/hs485types XML and in no pydevccu descriptor, so this is an HmIP-only parameter and the grounding rests entirely on the HmIP side. Our own coupling risk stands as the candidate wrote it: a consumer reading Unit() ("d") without applying Multiplier() renders seconds under a days label.

all.title: The unit string '100%' is taken to mean the wire value is a 0..1 fraction (multiplier 100)
all.ourValue: unit "100%" ⇒ wire value is 0.0..1.0, display value = wire × 100, unit rendered "%"
all.firmwareValue: identical: value × 100, unit set to "%"
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/programs.fn:606-610 — `var unit = oDP.ValueUnit(); if( unit == "100%") { value = value * 100; unit = "%"; }`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/uiElements.tcl:129-132 — `if {($unit == "100%") && ($max <= 1)} { set min [format %.0f [expr $min * 100]]; set max [format %.0f [expr $max * 100]] }`, and getUnit at :184-186 — `if {$unit == "100%"} { set unit "%" }`. Write direction: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/msg/insertValue.htm:186-189 — `convertValue = function(value, unit) { if (unit == "100%") { value = parseInt(value,10); value = value/100.0; } ... }`. Tier 2 corroboration: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml declare unit="100%" 542 times and every one of them carries a logical range of min="0.0" max="1.0" (the only variants are the default, plus one min="0.3", one min="0.01" and one max="0.2" — all inside 0..1).
all.finding: Both halves of our rule match the firmware exactly, and both directions of the conversion are in Tier 1. ReGa's programs.fn multiplies by 100 and relabels to "%" — the same formula and the same replacement unit our two tables encode. uiElements.tcl scales the declared MIN/MAX by the same factor before showing them (guarded additionally by `$max <= 1`, i.e. the firmware also treats the 0..1 range as the discriminator, not just the spelling). insertValue.htm divides the operator's percentage by 100 on the way back to the device, so the inverse holds too. One boundary worth naming, since it is our risk and not a disagreement: our MultiplierForUnit is applied only on the read path (generic.DataPoint.Multiplier → DisplayValue); we have no write-side inverse keyed on the unit, so anything that lets a caller supply a percentage would have to divide by 100 itself. Nothing in the candidate's two sites does that today.
all.negativeControl: Had "100%" meant a value already in 0..100, four independent places would read differently: programs.fn would not multiply, uiElements.tcl would not scale MIN/MAX (and its `$max <= 1` guard would never fire), insertValue.htm would not divide the entered value, and the device XMLs would declare max="100" rather than max="1.0". All four say the opposite of that, so the check is tethered.
all.challengeNote: Upheld. What I checked, rather than accepting: I re-read all four cited sites verbatim and reproduced the Tier-2 census myself (the 515/27 split and the three range variants are my own counts, matching the candidate's 542). I also found a fifth site the candidate missed — programs.fn:270-275 applies the same x100 and the same relabel to both bounds of a value-range condition — which makes the read-side rule independently attested inside one file. The write-side inverse at insertValue.htm is real and is the half that matters for the boundary note: our MultiplierForUnit has no inverse anywhere. I verified that by enumerating every consumer of Multiplier()/MultiplierForUnit in the tree (calculated_data_points.go:94, devices.go:1063, ws/custom_data_points.go:331, payload.go:136, channel.go:568, uischema_adapter.go:483, eventbridge.go:1426) — all display/read-side, none on a write path. So a caller that accepted a percentage would have to divide by 100 itself; nothing in this rule's two sites does. One correction to the candidate's summary column, not to the rule: getUnit's K / degC -> degC branch is guarded by `[string equal $ch_descr(TYPE) "UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER"] != 1` (uiElements.tcl:192-196); the candidate presented it unconditionally. Also worth naming for precision: uiElements.tcl's range scaling adds the `$max <= 1` guard, so the firmware treats spelling AND declared range as jointly discriminating; our table keys on spelling alone. No firmware-declared unit of "100%" violates the range condition, so the two agree on the shipped corpus — that is scope, not disagreement.

all.title: ON_TIME is written as raw seconds and ON_TIME=0 is assumed to cancel the timer
all.site: internal/model/generic/switch.go:127 (the ON_TIME=0 comment) and :79-86 (SetOnTime writes d.Seconds(), clamped at 0)
all.ourValue: ON_TIME written as raw seconds (float, negative clamped to 0); ON_TIME=0 carried through as an explicit "timer-cancel"
all.firmwareValue: seconds — confirmed on both stacks. But 0 is not an opcode: BidCos omits the field from the radio frame (`omit_if="0"`), HmIP removes the key from the paramset. There is no distinct cancel value.
all.citation: BidCos, Tier 2 descriptor + Tier 1 frame layout: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_s_644.xml:276 `<logical type="float" min="0.0" max="85825945.6" default="0.0" unit="s"/>` with `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="10"/>` + `<conversion type="integer_tinyfloat" mantissa_start="5" mantissa_size="11" exponent_start="0" exponent_size="5"/>` at :278-279; the LEVEL_SET frame at :230 `<parameter type="integer" index="14.0" size="2.0" PARAM="ON_TIME" omit_if="0"/>`; STATE at :270 `<reset_after_send param="ON_TIME"/>`. Same shape in rf_dim_1l_644.xml:320-326. HmIP declared unit: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config:691 `SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER.ON_TIME.Unit=s` (also :271 DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, :688 SWITCH_TRANSCEIVER, :772 WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, :806 WINDOW_DRIVE_RECEIVER). HmIP zero-handling and the seconds proof: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#migrateDurations and #correctInfiniteDuration.
all.finding:
The unit half is confirmed outright and on both stacks. BidCos declares ON_TIME `unit="s"`, float, 0.0..85825945.6, and the CCU owns the encoding (×10, then an 11+5-bit tinyfloat) — so writing raw seconds is correct and we must not pre-encode. HmIP declares ON_TIME.Unit=s on every switch/dimmer receiver, and migrateDurations proves the unit by construction: it converts between ON_TIME and DURATION_VALUE using factors 1.0 (S), 60.0 (M), 3600.0 (H) and 0.01 (10MS), which only balances if ON_TIME is seconds.

The zero half is where our comment is wrong, though our behaviour is not. Neither stack has a cancel opcode. On BidCos the LEVEL_SET frame carries `omit_if="0"` on the ON_TIME field: an encoded 0 makes the field vanish from the radio frame, so what the device receives is a plain unbounded switch-on. On HmIP, migrateDurations removes the ON_TIME key and — when no RAMP_TIME accompanies it — puts nothing in its place; when a RAMP_TIME is present it substitutes DURATION_UNIT="H", DURATION_VALUE=16383, which correctInfiniteDuration documents as infinity (0x3FFF, applied to any H-duration ≥ 31 h). So ON_TIME=0 means "no time limit", reached by dropping the value, not by signalling a cancel.

Where the boundary runs: the observable result is identical to our alternative path. Sending {STATE:true, ON_TIME:0} and sending {STATE:true} alone produce the same frame on BidCos (the field is omitted either way, and `reset_after_send` clears the stored ON_TIME after every STATE write so a stale timer cannot leak) and the same paramset on HmIP (the key is removed before dispatch). So switch.go:126-131 is safe as written; the justification "the CCU interprets ON_TIME=0 as a timer-cancel, so we must carry it through" is the part that is not what the firmware does — carrying it through is a no-op, not a necessity. Unrelated bound worth noting while the file is open: SetOnTime clamps only the lower end; BidCos declares max 85825945.6 s and the HmIP path saturates anything ≥ 111600 s to 8580000 s inside migrateDurations, so a very large duration is silently reshaped rather than rejected.
all.negativeControl: Unit: had ON_TIME been in tenths of a second or in minutes, the logical attribute would read something other than unit="s" (the ×10 scale is a separate <conversion>, not the unit), and migrateDurations could not reconcile ON_TIME with DURATION_UNIT S/M/H/10MS using factors 1/60/3600/0.01. Zero: had 0 been a distinct cancel value, the LEVEL_SET frame would encode it rather than carry omit_if="0", and migrateDurations would emit a specific DURATION pair for onTime==0.0 instead of falling through every `onTime > 0.0` branch with the key already removed. Both discriminators are present and both point away from our comment's mechanism.
all.challengeNote:
The unit half is upheld and I strengthened it. The zero half is upheld for BidCos and DEMOTED for HmIP, because the candidate cited the wrong surface.

What I verified on BidCos. The descriptor line, the two conversions and the frame field are all verbatim as cited. I then closed two gaps the candidate left open. (a) The frame field spells the attribute uppercase, `PARAM="ON_TIME"`, while FrameDescription.cpp reads `node.getAttribute("param")`; that only binds because xmlParser compares attribute names case-insensitively (_tcsicmp) — had it been case-sensitive the whole omit argument would have collapsed. (b) omit_if is documented nowhere in device.xsd (the annotation is literally "???"), so the semantics had to come from the C++: FrameDescription.h:60 states them and FrameDescription.cpp:235 implements them. reset_after_send is SetToDefault, and ON_TIME's default is 0.0, so a stale timer genuinely cannot leak. BidCos conclusion stands: {STATE:true, ON_TIME:0} and {STATE:true} produce the same frame, and 0 is not a cancel opcode.

Where the candidate is wrong. Its entire HmIP argument rests on migrateDurations. That method has exactly one caller — convertCombinedParameter — which is reached only when the written value key is COMBINED_PARAMETER. Our code never writes COMBINED_PARAMETER (grep over the repo: zero occurrences); SetOnTime writes hmenum.ParameterOnTime as a plain VALUES key. On that path the legacy layer runs convertParameterValue, which for a FLOAT parameter passes the value straight through — no key removal, no DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE substitution, no infinity sentinel. So "on HmIP the key is removed before dispatch" and the H/16383 substitution describe a surface we are not on. The 111600 -> 8580000 saturation the candidate attributed to our writes is worse: it sits in the OTHER branch of migrateDurations, the DURATION_* -> ON_TIME direction, so it is misattributed twice over.

The right-surface HmIP grounding, which I did find and which the candidate did not: createOnTimeParameter declares ON_TIME as FLOAT with default 0.0, min 0.0, max 8580000.0 and the converter DoubleToDirectExecutionTime. That converter is the same tinyfloat shape BidCos declares (x10, then 11-bit mantissa + 5-bit exponent) with a stated 0.1 granularity, so ON_TIME is seconds on the path we actually use, proven without migrateDurations. It also fixes the bound: HmIP's declared ceiling is 8 580 000 s, not "saturated above 111600 s", and BidCos's is 85 825 945.6 s. Our SetOnTime clamps only the lower end, so an oversized duration is silently reshaped or rejected downstream on both stacks; that part of the candidate's note survives, its mechanism does not.

What is now unverified: ON_TIME=0 on a plain HmIP write encodes to 0x0000 and is transmitted. Whether the device treats a zero direct-execution time as "no timer" is device firmware and is not in any readable source — tier-1 silent. So "there is no cancel opcode on either stack" is established for BidCos only. Our comment at switch.go:126-131 remains wrong as written and the behaviour remains safe, but the HmIP leg of that argument does not stand.

The only parameters that declare unit="degree" are WIND_DIRECTION and WIND_DIRECTION_RANGE — rf_hm-wds100-c6-o-2.xml:155,163 and rf_ks550.xml:148,156.
all.finding:
The doc claim at :42-44 ("substring-matching replacements") describes a normalisation strategy the CCU does not use, and the corpus it is applied to contains the exact counterexamples the candidate predicted.

Compound units exist and we mangle them. `unit="m3/Imp."` is declared on METER_CONSTANT_GAS in two BidCos device XMLs, and the HmIP legacy parameter definition declares GAS_FLOW as `m3/h`. Both contain "m3", so CleanupUnit returns "m³" for both — a meter constant in cubic metres per impulse and a flow in cubic metres per hour both come out naming a plain volume. The firmware does the opposite: getUnit never matches on a substring; it reaches the per-impulse spelling by keying on the *parameter* (METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME → "m³/Imp"), which is a reading our unit-keyed table structurally cannot produce.

The "degree" entry is a second, independent contradiction, and it is worse than a lost suffix: we map it to "°C" (Celsius) while the firmware maps it to "°" (programs.fn:611-614 sets °, and getUnit maps HmIP's "_Grad_" to ° likewise). The only two parameters that declare unit="degree" are WIND_DIRECTION and WIND_DIRECTION_RANGE — angles. We are saved from shipping that today only because fixUnitByParam:38-39 overrides both to "°" before the replace table is consulted, so the entry is unreachable for the parameters that trigger it. That is a latent trap, not a correct rule: any future parameter declaring a unit containing "degree" would be labelled a temperature.

The damage extends past presentation, because CleanupUnit's output is also a *lookup key*: quantity.go:54 and :86 feed it into parameter.MetadataByUnit to derive Quantity and ValueBehavior. A meter constant collapsed to "m³" is therefore not only mislabelled but classified as a volume measurement.

On the map-iteration nondeterminism the candidate also raises: I could not reproduce it from the firmware's unit corpus. Across all 148 rftypes/hs485types XMLs and the HmIP legacy config, no declared unit string contains two of our six table keys (the only near-miss, `Unit=""` in the legacy config, matches the `"` key alone). So the ordering hazard is real in the code but currently unreachable from firmware-declared data — I am reporting that as measured, not as safe by design.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware normalised units by substring, getUnit would be built from `string match`/`regsub` rather than a chain of `==` tests, and it would not need the two per-parameter escapes (METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME, METER_CONSTANT_ENERGY) that exist precisely because whole-string matching cannot reach a compound spelling. Had no compound unit containing a table key existed, the grep over every declared unit= attribute and every .Unit= line would have returned only atomic spellings; it returned m3/Imp., m3/h, L/min, 1/cm, m3/h and x 200Hz among others.
all.challengeNote:
Contradiction upheld, but on a cleaner counterexample than the candidate's, and with its damage claim cut back.

What I checked. getUnit really is equality-only — I read all 43 lines; every test is `==` or `string equal`, on the unit or on the parameter name. The compound units really exist, in both stacks. And I reproduced the candidate's non-collision claim properly rather than trusting it: I enumerated the complete distinct unit corpus on both sides — 40 distinct `unit="..."` strings across all rftypes + hs485types XMLs, and 30 distinct `.Unit=` values in the HmIP legacy config — and confirmed no declared unit contains two of our six table keys. The map-iteration hazard in CleanupUnit is therefore real in code but unreachable from firmware-declared data. Measured, not safe by design.

Where I improve on the candidate. Its headline example relates two differently-named parameters: getUnit keys on METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME, but the parameter that actually declares `unit="m3/Imp."` is METER_CONSTANT_GAS. METER_CONSTANT_VOLUME and METER_CONSTANT_ENERGY appear in no rftypes/hs485types XML and in no legacy-config line — they are HmIP names. The stronger reading needs no such bridge: METER_CONSTANT_GAS matches none of getUnit's branches, so the firmware renders `m3/Imp.` verbatim, while we return `m³`. Same for GAS_FLOW (`m3/h`), which no firmware surface normalises at all — programs.fn only handles "100%" and "degree".

Where the candidate overstates. "A meter constant collapsed to m³ is not only mislabelled but classified as a volume measurement" is false. sensorMetadataByUnit (internal/parameter/metadata.go:266-271) has exactly four keys — "%", "bar", "°C", "g/m³". "m³" is not among them, so the collapsed unit yields QuantityNone / ValueBehaviorNone, identical to what the raw string would yield. And GAS_FLOW never reaches the unit fallback at all: it is classified one stage earlier by parameter (metadata.go:77, QuantityVolumeFlowRate). The damage is a wrong displayed unit, not a wrong classification.

Reachability, which I checked because a presentation-only defect still has to reach a surface: CleanupUnit is called from MQTT discovery (internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:753 and :820) for VALUES parameters — that is where m3/h lands — and from internal/central/adapter/uischema_adapter.go:456 for the config-UI schema, which is where METER_CONSTANT_GAS, a MASTER parameter, lands. Both are live.

The "degree" -> "°C" entry is a second, independent contradiction and I confirm the candidate's reading including the shadowing: the only four parameters declaring unit="degree" are WIND_DIRECTION and WIND_DIRECTION_RANGE, and fixUnitByParam:38-39 overrides both to "°" before the replace table is consulted, so the wrong entry is unreachable today. Latent, not shipped. One gap the candidate named in its summary column but did not pursue: HmIP declares `_Grad_` (and `Grad`) as units and getUnit maps `_Grad_` to °; we have no entry, so `_Grad_` reaches the operator literally. `${lblReadings}` is another declared HmIP unit we pass through raw.

all.title: The auto-generated sysvar table asserts a unit and a cumulative flag no source in the repo carries
all.ourValue: substring match, longest wins: any name containing svEnergyCounter → Wh/energy/cumulative; svHmIPRainCounter* → mm; svHmIPSunshineCounter* → min; all eight Cumulative=true
all.firmwareValue: the sysvar itself carries no unit at all; the unit is the source datapoint's — Wh for svEnergyCounter/svEnergyCounterFeedIn, mm for the rain counters, min for the sunshine counters, but kWh for svEnergyCounterIEC and m³ for svEnergyCounterGas (and for svEnergyCounter on an HmIP-ESI gas channel); the *Yesterday variables are assigned, not accumulated
all.citation: Creation, with no unit argument: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/views/newdevices.htm:780-792 — `CreateSysVar = function (name, type, value, chnID) { … case "float": … homematic("SysVar.createFloat", {"name": name, "minValue": minVal, "maxValue": maxVal, "internal": 1, "chnID": chnID}, …)`. Source datapoints: :859-860 `chn.DPByControl('POWERMETER.ENERGY_COUNTER')` (BidCos, unit="Wh" at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_es_pmsw.xml:196); :1472 `chn.DPByControl('POWERMETER_PSM.ENERGY_COUNTER')` (HmIP, `ENERGIE_METER_TRANSMITTER.ENERGY_COUNTER.Unit=Wh`, opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config:342, feed-in at :345); :1676 `chn.DPByControl('WEATHER_TRANSMIT.SUNSHINEDURATION')` (legacy config:793 `Unit=min`); :1791 `chn.DPByControl('WEATHER_TRANSMIT.RAIN_COUNTER')` (legacy config:790 `Unit=mm`); :1390 `chn.DPByControl('POWERMETER_IEC1.IEC_ENERGY_COUNTER')` written into svEnergyCounterIEC_* (:2005-2007 getSysVarEnergyCounterIECIds) — unit="kWh" at rf_es_tx_wm_ge_v2_0.xml:253; :944-948 `var sysVarIds = (sensorType == "CURRENT") ? getSysVarEnergyCounterIds(chn) : getSysVarEnergyCounterGasIds(chn); … var counter = (sensorType == "CURRENT") ? "ENERGY_COUNTER" : "GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER";` — GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER declares unit="m3" at rf_es_tx_wm.xml:324; :1579 `chn.DPByControl('POWERMETER_PSM.GAS_VOLUME')` written into getSysVarEnergyCounterIds(chn) i.e. svEnergyCounter_* on an HmIP-ESI (legacy config:355 `GAS_VOLUME.Unit=m3`). Daily rollover: :1907-1916 `oSysVarSunshineCounterYesterday.State(oSysVarSunshineCounterToday.Value()); … oSysVarSunshineCounterToday.State(0); … oSysVarRainCounterYesterday.State(oSysVarRainCounterToday.Value()); … oSysVarRainCounterToday.State(0);`. Corroboration on the sunshine unit: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/weather_sensor.fn:161 renders it through `convertMin2Hour(svHmIPSunshineCounter.Value())`.
all.finding:
Two separate answers, and only one of them is what the candidate expected.

First, the premise. The CCU creates these variables through SysVar.createFloat with name, min, max, internal and chnID — and no unit. So there is no sysvar-side unit for our table to have consulted; Sysvar.Unit arrives empty and the table is legitimately the only source. The candidate's framing ("the CCU's own sysvar descriptor carries a unit field … and this table does not consult it") does not hold: consulting it would yield nothing.

Second, the values. Traced to the datapoint each ReGa program accumulates, the three units in our table are right for the exact tokens they name. svEnergyCounter accumulates the delta of POWERMETER.ENERGY_COUNTER (BidCos, unit="Wh") or POWERMETER_PSM.ENERGY_COUNTER (HmIP, Unit=Wh); svEnergyCounterFeedIn accumulates ENERGY_COUNTER_FEED_IN (Unit=Wh); the rain counters accumulate WEATHER_TRANSMIT.RAIN_COUNTER (Unit=mm); the sunshine counters accumulate WEATHER_TRANSMIT.SUNSHINEDURATION (Unit=min), and weather_sensor.fn independently confirms minutes by calling convertMin2Hour on the value. "Plausible convention" turned out to be measurably correct here.

Where it is false is one step wider, and the mechanism is our own substring matching. The CCU generates more auto-sysvars than our eight tokens, and three families collide with svEnergyCounter:
• svEnergyCounterIEC_<id>_<addr> accumulates POWERMETER_IEC1.IEC_ENERGY_COUNTER, declared unit="kWh". ClassifyAutoSysvar's longest match is svEnergyCounter (svEnergyCounterFeedIn does not match), so we publish kWh as Wh — exactly the 1000× energy-dashboard error the candidate's damage note describes, arrived at from the other direction.
• svEnergyCounterGas_<id>_<addr> accumulates GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER, unit="m3". Same collision: published as Wh with HA device_class "energy".
• On an HmIP-ESI, CreateSysVarGasCounterScriptESI writes POWERMETER_PSM.GAS_VOLUME (Unit=m3) into the *plain* svEnergyCounter_ id, so even the exact token is not unconditionally watt-hours — the unit depends on the channel the CCU attached the program to, which the name does not carry.
• The scratch variables svEnergyCounterOldVal*, svHmIPRainCounterOldVal_, svHmIPSunshineCounterOldVal_ all contain a base token and are classified as the counter itself. (svEnergyCounterOldValFeedIn contains svEnergyCounter but not svEnergyCounterFeedIn, so a feed-in scratch value is classified as consumption.) These are the previous-reading holders the update scripts subtract against, not readings.
svCounter_ (water flow, litres) is the one that escapes: no token matches, so ClassifyAutoSysvar declines and the raw name survives.

The cumulative flag is a second narrowing, and it is decidable from the same script. Today's counters reset to 0 at the daily rollover — consistent with our struct's own "(modulo a reset)" wording and with HA's total_increasing. The *Yesterday* variables are not counters at all: State() assigns them yesterday's daily total outright, so they step up and down freely from one day to the next. Marking them Cumulative=true (autosysvar.go:62-63) describes a monotone series that the firmware demonstrably does not produce; internal/north/mqtt/sysvar_names.go:41-46 then declares total_increasing for them, under which every downward step reads as a counter reset and adds the full new value into the long-term sum. Note that AutoSysvarClass.Cumulative currently has no consumer anywhere in the tree — the MQTT table hard-codes state_class — so fixing the flag alone would change nothing; the state_class is the line that has to move.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU carried a unit on these variables, SysVar.createFloat would take one alongside minValue/maxValue — it does not, and the ReGa weather control has to borrow `oActualRainCounter.ValueUnit()` from the *device* datapoint to render the rain sysvar (weather_sensor.fn:210), which is only necessary because the sysvar has none. Had the sunshine counter been in hours, weather_sensor.fn:161 would not wrap it in convertMin2Hour. Had the token families not collided, the grep for the CCU's sysvar-id builders would have returned only our eight names; it returned svCounter, svEnergyCounterGas, svEnergyCounterIEC and four *OldVal* families as well. Had the Yesterday variables been accumulators, the rollover script would add into them rather than call State() with today's value and zero today.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, including the part that reverses the candidate's premise. Every citation re-read; two line-number slips corrected (the IEC helper is at :2015-2017, not :2005-2007; the rain/sunshine helpers at :1983-2009).

The premise-check is the strongest part and I confirmed it on a source the candidate did not open: SysVar.createFloat's own ReGa implementation. createfloat.tcl builds an OT_VARDP and sets ValueType, Name, ValueMin, ValueMax, State, Internal and Channel — ValueUnit() is never called. So there is no sysvar-side unit for our table to have consulted; the original objection ("the CCU's sysvar descriptor carries a unit and this table does not consult it") is refuted at the source, not merely argued around.

The three units are right for the exact tokens. I traced each ReGa program to the datapoint it accumulates and read that datapoint's declared unit: Wh, Wh, mm, min. weather_sensor.fn independently corroborates minutes by feeding the sunshine value to convertMin2Hour.

The narrowing is where our own substring matching over-reaches, and I re-derived each collision by hand against ClassifyAutoSysvar's longest-match rule rather than accepting the list: (1) svEnergyCounterIEC_ accumulates IEC_ENERGY_COUNTER (kWh) — "svEnergyCounterFeedIn" does not match, so the longest match is "svEnergyCounter" and we publish Wh, a 1000x understatement; (2) svEnergyCounterGas_ accumulates GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER (m3) — same collision, published as Wh with device_class energy; (3) CreateSysVarGasCounterScriptESI writes GAS_VOLUME (m3) into the plain svEnergyCounter_ id, so even the exact token is not unconditionally watt-hours and the name does not carry which; (4) the scratch holders svEnergyCounterOldVal*, svHmIPRainCounterOldVal_, svHmIPSunshineCounterOldVal_ all classify as the counter itself, and svEnergyCounterOldValFeedIn classifies as consumption because it contains "svEnergyCounter" but not "svEnergyCounterFeedIn"; (5) svCounter_ escapes cleanly — no token is a substring of it.

I also confirmed the two repo-side claims the damage rests on. internal/north/mqtt/sysvar_names.go:67 does `pres.unit = domain.Unit`, so the domain's Wh really does become HA's unit_of_measurement alongside device_class "energy" and state_class "total_increasing" — the mislabel reaches HA. And AutoSysvarClass.Cumulative has no production consumer anywhere in the tree (the only other "Cumulative" identifiers are the Matter fail-safe timers), so the MQTT table's hard-coded state_class is indeed the line that would have to move; correcting the flag alone would change nothing. The rollover reading is confirmed verbatim: the *Yesterday variables are assigned yesterday's total with State(), so they step down as freely as up and total_increasing misreads every downward step as a counter reset.

all.title: First-match substring ordering makes two UI-hint rows unreachable (FILLING_LEVEL, GAS_ENERGY)
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_sen_wa_od.xml:235-237 — `<parameter id="FILLING_LEVEL" operations="read,event" control="CAPACITIVE_FILLING_LEVEL_SENSOR.FILLING_LEVEL">` / `<logical type="integer" min="0" max="100" unit="%"/>`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_es_tx_wm.xml:322-329 — `<parameter id="GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER" … control="POWERMETER_IEC1.GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER">` / `<logical type="float" min="0.000" max="2147483.647" unit="m3"/>`, and :340-342 `<parameter id="ENERGY_COUNTER" … control="POWERMETER_IEC1.ENERGY_COUNTER">` / `<logical type="float" min="0.0" max="838860.7" unit="Wh"/>`. HmIP names: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config — `ENERGIE_METER_TRANSMITTER.GAS_VOLUME.Unit=m3`, `ENERGIE_METER_TRANSMITTER.GAS_FLOW.Unit=m3/h`.
all.firmwareValue: FILLING_LEVEL = relative fill level, integer 0..100, unit "%", on its own channel type CAPACITIVE_FILLING_LEVEL_SENSOR. GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER = gas volume, float, unit "m3" — a different physical quantity from ENERGY_COUNTER (unit "Wh") and from IEC_ENERGY_COUNTER (unit "kWh") on the same channel.
all.ourValue: FILLING_LEVEL → the LEVEL row wins: Icon mdi:percent, Semantic "level". GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER → the ENERGY_COUNTER row wins: Icon mdi:counter, Semantic "energy". The FILLING_LEVEL and GAS_ENERGY rows are never reached.
all.finding: I extracted the full shipped parameter-name space — 2,015 distinct `<parameter id="…">` values from ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml plus 631 HmIP names from opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config (2,318 unique) — and ran every name through the real first-match loop as written at pkg/hmui/quantity.go:100-105. Exactly two names are routed to a row that a longer, later row also matches: FILLING_LEVEL (LEVEL at :159 beats FILLING_LEVEL at :167) and GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER (ENERGY_COUNTER at :148 beats GAS_ENERGY at :150). No other name in the catalogue is shadowed, so the comment at :98-99 ("more specific tokens come first") is wrong for exactly these two rows and right for the other 44. Both shadowed rows are unreachable for every catalogue name, i.e. dead code. The firmware disagrees with the winning classification in both cases: it declares FILLING_LEVEL on a dedicated channel type (CAPACITIVE_FILLING_LEVEL_SENSOR) as a percentage fill level, not a dimmer LEVEL; and GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER in m³ — a gas volume — while ENERGY_COUNTER on the very same POWERMETER_IEC1 channel is Wh. So our "energy" bucket for a gas meter is contradicted by the CCU's own unit declaration, which is the distinction internal/north/mqtt/entity_description_rules_sensors.go:243 (device class gas, unit m³) already gets right. Four further rows are unreachable for a different, harmless reason: PRESSURE (only AIR_PRESSURE exists in the catalogue, and its row precedes it with the same hint), and CO2_CONCENTRATION, VAPOR, ACCELERATION (no name in this catalogue contains those tokens at all — the catalogue carries MASS_CONCENTRATION_PM_* / NUMBER_CONCENTRATION_PM_* but no CO2 or vapor parameter, so those rows target devices this shipped catalogue does not describe; that is a scope limit of the source, not evidence the rows are wrong). Note also that GAS_VOLUME is reachable and correct — it exists only on the HmIP side (POWERMETER_PSM.GAS_VOLUME, unit m3).
all.negativeControl: Had our table really been ordered most-specific-first for the shipped fleet, the same sweep over all 2,318 catalogue names would have reported zero names whose winning row is shorter than another matching row, and zero substring rows unreachable by shadowing. It reported two of each, naming them. Had the firmware agreed that GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER is an energy quantity, its `<logical>` element would carry unit="Wh" or "kWh" like its two siblings on the same channel; it carries unit="m3".
all.challengeNote:
MECHANICAL HALF UPHELD, INDEPENDENTLY RE-RUN. I re-extracted the shipped name space myself (2,012 distinct `<parameter id=…>` from rftypes+hs485types, 646 parameter names from the HmIP legacy-parameter-definition.config; 2,330 unique — the candidate reported 2,015/631/2,318, an immaterial parsing difference) and replayed the loop exactly as written at :100-105 including the parameterExact short-circuit. My run reproduces the candidate's result exactly: unreached rows are {GAS_ENERGY, FILLING_LEVEL, VAPOR, CO2_CONCENTRATION, PRESSURE, ACCELERATION}, and the only two names routed to a row that a LATER, LONGER row also matches are FILLING_LEVEL and GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER. All nine other shadowings resolve to the intended (earlier) row.

SURFACE CHECK PASSED. `HintFor` (quantity.go:48-58) calls `parameterHint` FIRST, before the unit table — so the unit string never rescues either name. The two rows are genuinely dead for every shipped catalogue name and both hints are served verbatim to the SPA (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:1083).

DEMOTED TO NARROWED FOR TWO REASONS.
(1) The firmware contradiction is real for GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER only. The CCU declares it in m³ on the same POWERMETER_IEC1 channel where ENERGY_COUNTER is Wh, so bucketing a gas volume as semantic "energy" groups it with a different physical quantity — that is a Tier-2 contradiction. For FILLING_LEVEL the firmware declares unit="%", 0..100, which CORROBORATES the winning row's mdi:percent rendering. What differs is only our own semantic token ("level" vs "fill_level"), and the firmware does not define our taxonomy. The firmware does carry a control-class distinction (CAPACITIVE_FILLING_LEVEL_SENSOR vs DIMMER.LEVEL/WINDOW.LEVEL), so the intended row is the better one — but "contradicted by the firmware" overstates what the source says. Unreachable: yes. Contradicted: only for GAS_ENERGY.
(2) Scope. Unreachability is proven over the SHIPPED catalogue only. A CUxD-fronted or third-party device is free to name a parameter anything; the rows are not provably dead for names outside this corpus. The candidate stated this correctly for the four other unreached rows but not for the two headline ones.

One correction to the candidate's prose: it says ACCELERATION appears nowhere in the catalogue. ACCELERATION appears as a CHANNEL type (ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER.*) in the HmIP config but never as a parameter name — the conclusion is right, the wording is loose.

all.title: Wire-DTO comments state CCU encoding constants that nothing validates
all.site: pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:361, :377-380, :398, :402-404, :425, :432-434; enforced at internal/model/schedule/simple.go:197-198, :311 channelPattern, :329 SimpleMaxSlot; emitted at internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:832-841

Slots per channel: 75 on most models, 69 on HmIP-BSL, HmIP-HDM1, HmIP-HDM2, HmIP-MP3P, HmIPW-WRC6. TARGET_CHANNELS: INTEGER, MIN 0, MAX 16777215 (2^24-1) on 43 models; STRING, MIN '0', MAX '281474976710655' (2^48-1) on HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-LSC, HmIP-RGBW. DURATION_BASE: ENUM, VALUE_LIST ['BASE_100_MS','BASE_1_S','BASE_5_S','BASE_10_S','BASE_1_M','BASE_5_M','BASE_10_M','BASE_1_H'] → index 7 = BASE_1_H; DURATION_FACTOR: INTEGER 0..31, DEFAULT 31. all.ourValue: AstroOffsetMinutes -720..+720 (rest_contract.go:398, enforced simple.go:197 and rawconvert.go:832). "Up to 24 such slots per channel" (rest_contract.go:361). TargetChannels "X_Y" with X=1..8, Y=1..3 (rest_contract.go:402-404, channelPattern `^[1-8]_[123]$`). DURATION forced to "(HOUR_1, 31)". ColorType discriminator 0/1/2, ColorValue packed 20-bit.
all.finding:
Five sub-claims, three outcomes.

CONTRADICTED — astro offset. Every one of the 47 models in the descriptor corpus declares 01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET as INTEGER MIN -128 MAX 127. We accept and emit -720..+720. The CCU's own editor does not carry a constant at all: HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1128-1134 reads ASTRO_OFFSET_MIN/MAX out of the paramset description (hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:39-46 fills them from `$psDescr(01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET)` MIN/MAX) and clamps the input field to them. So the firmware answer is "whatever the channel declares", and what every channel declares is ±128, not ±720. rawconvert.go:832-835 lets anything in ±720 through to the wire, so a value between 128 and 720 is written and the device either rejects the putParamset or stores a clipped switching time. The unit is confirmed as minutes (`'ASTRO_OFFSET_UNIT' : 'min'`).

CONTRADICTED — the 24-slot comment at rest_contract.go:361. It contradicts SlotNo 1..75 three lines below and both the firmware and the descriptors: `_getMaxEntries` returns 69 or 75, and every model in the corpus declares NN_WP_* keys up to exactly 69 or 75. The 75/69 constant at simple.go:329 and its existing citation to `_getMaxEntries` are verbatim correct, including the 69-model list (HmIP-MP3P, HmIPW-WRC6(-A), WRC6-230, water switches, HmIP-BSL fw 2.x); the descriptors add HmIP-HDM1/HDM2 to the 69 group. `default: return -1` means the switch does not bound a lock / access-transmitter channel — for those the descriptor is the only bound, which is what the SlotNo comment already says.

NARROWED — target channels. The firmware field is not an "X_Y" grammar at all: it is an integer bitmask, MAX 16777215 = 2^24-1, addressed by the device's own virtual-receiver channel number minus one (the derivation at internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:940-985 already cites HmIPWeeklyProgram.js correctly and takes the bit from the device, so the write path is sound). What is narrowed is the DTO's grammar: HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-LSC and HmIP-RGBW declare TARGET_CHANNELS as STRING with MAX '281474976710655' = 2^48-1, i.e. 48 addressable bit positions. `channelPattern` `^[1-8]_[123]$` can express at most 24 keys and rejects anything past `8_3`, and internal/central/adapter/week_profile_filter.go:237-247 mints keys as `<group index+1>_<member index+1>` with no upper bound, so a device with more than 8 schedule-relevant groups produces a key its own validator rejects. Separately, those three models declare the field STRING while rawconvert.go:840 writes a Go int — I did not establish what the legacy API does with an int for a STRING-typed config parameter, so that part is unverified.

CONFIRMED with a naming correction — the lock DURATION pair. DURATION_BASE index 7 is BASE_1_H and DURATION_FACTOR's max and default are both 31, so (7, 31) is the CCU's own "maximum duration" encoding. That the wire value of an ENUM is the VALUE_LIST index is read from HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:96-110, not assumed. The name "HOUR_1" in the comment is not a CCU name — it appears nowhere in the descriptors or the CCU editor; it is the Python reference's enum (../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:2550 `HOUR_1 = 7`, a witness). The CCU calls it BASE_1_H.

CONFIRMED — the colour field. NN_WP_HUE_SATURATION_COLOR_TEMPERATURE_EFFECT_VALUE declares MAX 1048575 = 2^20-1 on all three universal-light models, so "packed 20-bit" is exact; the TYPE discriminator declares MAX 2, so the acceptance set {0,1,2} is exact for these devices. One caveat: the CCU's own editor offers five options for that select — 0 hue/saturation, 1 colour temperature, 2 effect, 3 Switch, 4 Dimmer (HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1676-1682) — so 3 and 4 exist in the editor but exceed every shipped device's declared MAX. Because we carry the field as an opaque int, the round-trip is lossless either way; the comment's enumeration is simply not the editor's full list.
all.negativeControl: Had ±720 been the real astro bound, at least one of the 47 models in the descriptor corpus would declare MIN/MAX beyond ±128 — none does, all 47 declare exactly -128/127 — and the CCU editor would have carried a literal rather than reading psDescr. Had 24 been the slot bound, no channel would declare an NN_WP_* key above 24 and `_getMaxEntries` would return 24; every model declares up to 69 or 75 and the function returns 69 or 75. Had (7,31) been wrong, DURATION_BASE's VALUE_LIST would put a different symbol at index 7 or DURATION_FACTOR's MAX would not be 31. Had the colour field not been 20 bits, its declared MAX would not be exactly 2^20-1.
all.challengeNote:
EVERY SUB-CLAIM REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY. I re-derived the descriptor corpus myself rather than trusting the candidate's counts: 01_WP_ASTRO_OFFSET is INTEGER -128..127 DEFAULT 0 on all 44 files that carry it (candidate said 47 — an overcount, substance unaffected); max NN_WP_WEEKDAY index is 69 on exactly {HmIP-BSL, HmIP-HDM1, HmIP-HDM2, HmIP-MP3P, HmIPW-WRC6} and 75 on the other 40; 01_WP_TARGET_CHANNELS is INTEGER 0..16777215 on 42 files and STRING '0'..'281474976710655' on exactly {HmIP-DRG-DALI, HmIP-LSC, HmIP-RGBW} (candidate said 43/3); DURATION_BASE VALUE_LIST is the 8-element list ending BASE_1_H on 38 files, DURATION_FACTOR INTEGER 0..31 DEFAULT 31 on 38; colour VALUE 0..1048575 and TYPE 0..2 on 3. The two contradictions therefore stand, and the write path is the right surface (rawconvert.go:801 mints `%02d_WP_`, i.e. the HmIP MASTER keys the editor edits).

ONE CITATION DEMOTED — WRONG SURFACE. The candidate grounded "an ENUM's wire value is the VALUE_LIST index" on ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:96-110. That code is verbatim as quoted, but libhsscomm is the BidCos stack (rfd / hs485d); 01_WP_DURATION_BASE is an HmIP MASTER parameter served by HMIPServer's legacy XML-RPC surface. The two demonstrably differ: HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDescription emits MIN=int(0), MAX=int(size-1), DEFAULT=int, whereas the captured HmIP descriptor for 01_WP_DURATION_BASE emits MIN="BASE_100_MS", MAX="BASE_1_H", DEFAULT="BASE_1_H" — strings. The cited code is not the code that produced this descriptor.

I FOUND THE RIGHT-SURFACE GROUNDING AND IT REACHES THE SAME ANSWER, WITH A NEW CAVEAT. On the HmIP legacy surface the ordinal substitution is a configuration-gated behaviour: DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue converts an ENUM value to its VALUE_LIST ordinal outbound and back to the string inbound ONLY when `replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal` is set; the field defaults to false in code (set from property `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal`, default false, in both LocalServer and HMIPServer startup), and the shipped CCU config turns it ON at crRFD.conf:47. So (7, 31) is correct on a stock CCU — but it is correct BECAUSE of a config line, not because the protocol says so. On a deployment where that property is false the legacy surface passes ENUM values as strings, and rawconvert.go's `toInt(val)` read would yield 0 while its int write would hand an Integer to a String-typed parameter. That conditionality is not stated anywhere in our code or in the candidate's finding; it is a real, previously-unnamed fragility. The "HOUR_1" naming correction is upheld: HOUR_1 appears nowhere in the firmware tree or the descriptors, and is aiohomematic's enum name at const.py:2550 (verified). The CCU calls it BASE_1_H.

TARGET-CHANNELS NARROWING UPHELD AND SHARPENED. `channelPattern` `^[1-8]_[123]$` (simple.go:158) admits at most 24 keys, while internal/central/adapter/week_profile_filter.go:246-248 mints keys as `fmt.Sprintf("%d_%d", actorIdx+1, subIdx+1)` with no upper bound on either index — verified verbatim — so a device with more than 8 schedule-relevant groups, or more than 3 members in one, produces a key its own validator rejects. The three STRING-typed models declare 48 addressable bit positions. Whether the legacy API accepts a Go int for a STRING-typed config parameter remains unverified in those words; the DeviceUtil path I read converts only ENUM and LONG, and leaves other types untouched, which suggests but does not establish that an Integer would reach the parameter unconverted.

all.title: RX_MODE bit layout is a bare literal block decoded straight into a REST field
all.site: pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:138-145; decoded at internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:161-172; populated for every interface at internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:594
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDeviceDescription.h:42-46 — `RX_ALWAYS=(1<<0)`, `RX_BURST=(1<<1)`, `RX_CONFIG=(1<<2)`, `RX_WAKEUP=(1<<3)`, `RX_LAZY_CONFIG=(1<<4)`; :50 `RX_BURST_AND_WAKEUP=0x0A`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDeviceDescription.cpp:110-121 — the `rx_modes` XML attribute is parsed with `strstr` onto exactly those bits, and `TRIPLE_BURST` also sets `RX_BURST`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:250 — `dev_desc["RX_MODE"]=GetDeviceDescription()->GetRxMode();` (the raw mask is what getDeviceDescription/listDevices returns). Descriptor example: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:3 `rx_modes="CONFIG,WAKEUP,BURST" rx_default="BURST"` → 14. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getDeviceDescriptions sets the legacy RX_MODE from `device.getListenerMode().getValue()`, and de.eq3.cbcs.protocol.hmip.networkmanagement.ListenerMode is a sparse enum.
all.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF (rfd): ALWAYS=1, BURST=2, CONFIG=4, WAKEUP=8, LAZY_CONFIG=16 — a bitmask, reported verbatim. HmIP-RF: RX_MODE is the ListenerMode ordinal — PERMANENT_LISTENER=0, SINGLE_BURST_LISTENER=1, TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER=3, EVENT_LISTENER=4, EVENT_LISTENER_WITH_POWER_SAVE=5, CYCLIC_LISTENER=8, CYCLIC_AND_SINGLE_BURST_LISTENER=9, CYCLIC_AND_TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER=11, PERMANENT_LISTENER_WIRED=12, PERMANENT_LISTENER_BACKBONE=14 — an enum, not a bitmask.
all.ourValue: One bitmask applied to every interface: 1/2/4/8/16, decoded at devices.go:166-171 into Always/Burst/Config/Wakeup/LazyConfig, and 0 rendered as "no rx mode" (rxModeInfo returns nil).
all.finding:
The five bit values are exactly right for BidCos-RF and are settled at Tier 1: the enum is written as `(1<<0)`…`(1<<4)` and the CCU parses the device XML's `rx_modes` attribute straight onto them, then hands the raw integer to clients unmodified. Two BidCos details our block does not carry: `strstr(temp, "CONFIG")` also fires on the token `LAZY_CONFIG`, so a device declaring only LAZY_CONFIG reports CONFIG|LAZY_CONFIG = 20 — our decode reproduces that, matching the CCU; and `TRIPLE_BURST` is folded into RX_BURST, so triple-burst devices are indistinguishable from single-burst on this field. BidCos-Wired is silent: no RX_MODE, rx_modes or RX_* token appears anywhere under src/hs485d.

The rule is false one step wider. internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:594 assigns `hmenum.RxMode(dd.RXMode)` for every interface, and on HmIP-RF the CCU fills that same field from a different vocabulary entirely: DeviceUtil#getDeviceDescriptions sets it from ListenerMode's ordinal, a sparse enum with values 0,1,3,4,5,8,9,11,12,14 whose `getByValue` masks with 0xF. Consequences, each a real fleet value (pydevccu descriptor corpus, parent entries only): an HmIP mains device reporting PERMANENT_LISTENER=0 makes rxModeInfo return nil, so an always-listening device is rendered as having no receive mode; HmIP-eTRV-2/B/B1/C-2 report 11 = CYCLIC_AND_TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER and we render Always+Burst+Wakeup for a battery TRV; HmIP-ASIR/ELV-SH-WSM report 3 = TRIPLE_BURST_LISTENER and we render Always+Burst; HmIP battery sensors reporting 4 = EVENT_LISTENER are rendered as Config. Where the boundary runs: the bitmask is correct for every device delivered by rfd (BidCos-RF, including CUxD-fronted BidCos), and wrong for every device delivered by the HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface.

One adjacent, unrelated observation while reading the write path: rfd's putParamset/setValue accept only "WAKEUP" and "BURST" as the rx_mode argument and throw XmlRpcException(-5) otherwise (RFManager.cpp:105-113 and :181-189). pkg/hmenum/device.go:102 also defines CommandRxModeLazyConfig, which BidCos-RF would reject; I did not check whether anything sends it.
all.negativeControl: Had the five bit values been wrong, RFDeviceDescription.cpp:113-117 would OR the ALWAYS/BURST/CONFIG/WAKEUP/LAZY_CONFIG tokens onto different powers of two than 1/2/4/8/16, or RFDevice.cpp:250 would transform the mask before publishing it — neither is the case. Had HmIP used the same bitmask, DeviceUtil would compose RX_MODE from an OR of mode flags; instead it assigns a single ListenerMode ordinal, and that enum's declared values (0,1,3,4,5,8,9,11,12,14) skip 2, 6, 7 and 10 — a pattern no five-bit OR can produce.
all.challengeNote:
CORE CLAIM UPHELD AT TIER 1 ON BOTH SURFACES. Every C++ and every HmIP citation reproduced verbatim, including the ListenerMode ordinal list and the 0xF mask. The strstr overlap is real (both `strstr(temp,"CONFIG")` and `strstr(temp,"LAZY_CONFIG")` fire on a LAZY_CONFIG token), and the write-path restriction to WAKEUP/BURST is verbatim. pkg/hmenum/device.go:102 does define CommandRxModeLazyConfig; I found no non-test caller for it, so nothing currently sends the value rfd would reject.

MATERIAL DEMOTION OF THE FLEET EVIDENCE. The candidate's consequence paragraph is sourced to "the pydevccu descriptor corpus, parent entries only". That corpus is NOT faithful for RX_MODE on BidCos. I counted 172 parent entries reporting RX_MODE=0, of which 104 are BidCos-RF types (HM-*, and the ELV order-number types '263 130'…'263 147', which rf_s.xml:50 declares as BidCos Schueco switch actuators). rfd cannot report 0 for those: the ctor sets rx_modes=RX_ALWAYS (RFDeviceDescription.cpp:29) and InitFromXml overwrites it only when the `rx_modes` attribute is present — and only 73 of 127 shipped rftypes XMLs carry that attribute; rf_s.xml and rf_es_pmsw.xml do not. A real CCU therefore reports 1, not 0, for HM-LC-Sw1-Pl and HM-ES-PMSw1-Pl. The corpus's 0 is an artefact of not applying the firmware default. So RX_MODE=0 in that corpus cannot be attributed to HmIP PERMANENT_LISTENER without knowing the device's interface.

WHAT SURVIVES ANYWAY. The HmIP examples do not need the corpus: PERMANENT_LISTENER=0 is what ListenerMode gives for an HmIP mains device, read directly from the enum, and rxModeInfo returns nil for 0 — so an always-listening HmIP device is rendered as having no receive mode. Values 3 and 11 occur in the corpus only on HmIP types (HmIP-ASIR/ELV-SH-WSM; HmIP-eTRV-2/B/B1/C-2) and are decoded by us as Always+Burst and Always+Burst+Wakeup respectively.

A COLLISION THE CANDIDATE DID NOT NAME. Value 12 is legal in BOTH vocabularies: on BidCos it is CONFIG|WAKEUP, declared by 28 shipped XMLs as rx_modes="CONFIG,WAKEUP" (I verified '263 135' = HM-PB-2-WM55 and ASH550 are BidCos devices reporting 12); on HmIP it is PERMANENT_LISTENER_WIRED. 14 collides the same way (BidCos CONFIG|WAKEUP|BURST on HM-CC-RT-DN vs HmIP PERMANENT_LISTENER_BACKBONE), and 4 (BidCos CONFIG vs HmIP EVENT_LISTENER). The field is therefore not merely mis-decoded on HmIP — it is undecodable from the value alone. Any fix must key on the delivering interface, which device_pipeline.go:594 has in scope and discards.

BOUNDARY: correct for every device delivered by rfd (BidCos-RF, incl. CUxD-fronted BidCos); wrong for every device delivered by the HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface. hs485d is silent — no RX_MODE, rx_modes or RX_* token anywhere under src/hs485d (re-verified), so the corpus's 0 for HMW-* devices is absence, not a value.

all.title: HM-ES-PMSw1-Pl ENERGY_COUNTER unit 'Wh' is injected when the descriptor carries none
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_es_pmsw.xml — the file whose <supported_types> block (:9-40) lists id="HM-ES-PMSw1-Pl" (and -DN-R1..R5, -DR, -SM); :194-203 `<parameter id="ENERGY_COUNTER" operations="read,event" control="POWERMETER.ENERGY_COUNTER">` / `<logical type="float" min="0.0" max="838860.7" unit="Wh"/>` / `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="10"/>`. Siblings on the same channel: POWER unit="W" factor 100 (:204-213), CURRENT unit="mA" factor 1, VOLTAGE unit="V" factor 10, FREQUENCY unit="Hz" factor 100 offset -50.00. Cross-check ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_es_tx_wm.xml:340-342 — the same ENERGY_COUNTER on HM-ES-TX-WM declares `unit="Wh"`, min 0.0 max 838860.7, while its IEC_ENERGY_COUNTER (:358-360) declares unit="kWh" and GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER (:322-324) unit="m3".
all.firmwareValue: unit="Wh", logical float 0.0..838860.7, conversion float_integer_scale factor=10 (physical integer / 10 → Wh, i.e. 0.1 Wh resolution).
all.ourValue: pd.Unit = "Wh" when the CCU sends an empty UNIT.
all.finding:
The patched value is exactly what the CCU's own device XML for HM-ES-PMSw1-Pl declares. The unit is "Wh", not 0.1 Wh and not kWh: the 0.1 factor lives in the conversion, so the logical value the CCU delivers over XML-RPC is already in Wh, and a consumer that scales by 1 is right. The neighbouring value_ids on the same POWERMETER channel each carry their own unit and factor (W/100, mA/1, V/10, Hz/100 with offset -50.00), which rules out a shared or implied unit. The disambiguation matters for this model family in particular: the same channel type on HM-ES-TX-WM carries three counters with three different units — ENERGY_COUNTER Wh, IEC_ENERGY_COUNTER kWh, GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER m³ — so "Wh" is a per-parameter fact, not a device-wide one, and the patch is correctly keyed on the parameter.

What I did not settle: the patch's premise. Whether some CCU firmware actually drops the UNIT annotation for this parameter is not decidable from these sources — the device XML always carries it, and I found no code path in src/rfd or src/libhsscomm that would omit a declared unit from getParamsetDescription. So the value the patch writes is confirmed; the condition under which it fires (`pd.Unit == ""`) is unverified in those words. That is harmless in direction — the patch is a no-op whenever the CCU does send the unit — but it means the Reason string is a claim with no source behind it. No Python or ccu-jack witness carries an equivalent patch, so the rule appears to be ours alone.
all.negativeControl: Had the device counted in something other than Wh, its own type XML would say so in the ENERGY_COUNTER `<logical>` element — the file distinguishes five units across six parameters on that one channel, and the sibling file distinguishes Wh from kWh from m³ on a single channel, so the source demonstrably does record a different answer when there is one. It records unit="Wh".
all.challengeNote:
THE VALUE IS UPHELD, THE PREMISE IS NOW CONTRADICTED — a stronger result than the candidate's "unverified".

Value: confirmed. rf_es_pmsw.xml declares unit="Wh" and the 10× factor lives in the conversion, so the logical value XML-RPC delivers is already in Wh and a consumer scaling by 1 is right. The per-parameter keying is right for the reason the candidate gives: the same POWERMETER_IEC1 channel on HM-ES-TX-WM carries Wh, kWh and m³ counters.

Premise: the candidate reported the trigger condition as unverified. It is worse than that. `HSSLogicalType::GetDescription` writes UNIT unconditionally into every parameter description, populated from the logical node's `unit` attribute, and it is the ONLY UNIT assignment in libhsscomm (`grep -a UNIT src/libhsscomm/*.cpp *.h` returns exactly that one line). Since the shipped device XML always carries unit="Wh" for this parameter, no shipped rfd build can deliver an empty UNIT for it, and the patch's `pd.Unit == ""` guard is unreachable against any current CCU. The Reason string is not merely unsourced — it is contradicted for the firmware in this tree. Historical firmwares and non-rfd fronts (a CUxD- or Homegear-presented device) are outside this tree, so I cannot say the patch was never justified; I can say it is dead code against the shipped stack.

A SECOND DEFECT THE CANDIDATE MISSED. Patch matching is exact and case-insensitive (patches.go:105 `strings.EqualFold(p.Model, model)`), and the patch keys only "HM-ES-PMSw1-Pl". The very same rf_es_pmsw.xml ships eight further ids under the identical ENERGY_COUNTER declaration — HM-ES-PMSw1-Pl-DN-R1…R5, -DR, -SM, and the generic HM-ES-PMSwX. If the premise were ever real, the patch would cover one of nine affected models. That is the half-fix pattern, independent of whether the premise holds.

No Python or ccu-jack witness carries an equivalent patch — upheld; the rule appears to be ours alone.

all.title: The cached MASTER paramset is never invalidated by anything the CCU says
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:73-89 — `RFChannel::PutParamsetValues` writes the paramset, calls `CommitToDevice`, and on failure sets `config_data_dirty` and calls `GetDevice()->CheckConfigPendingEvent()`; it emits no callback. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:786, :793, :805, :817, :1177 — the complete set of asynchronous callbacks rfd makes: `newDevices`, `replaceDevice`, `deleteDevices`, `readdedDevice`, `updateDevice`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.h:47 — `enum{UPDATE_HINT_ALL=0, UPDATE_HINT_LINKS=1};` is the entire hint vocabulary. The only `ReportUpdate` call sites in rfd are RFChannel.cpp:756 and :868 (both UPDATE_HINT_LINKS, on link removal/creation) and RFDevice.cpp:1618-1620 (UPDATE_HINT_ALL after an OTAU rebuild, and only when the config option "Call UpdateDevice On OTAU Device Rebuild" is set — RFManager.cpp:219-220 defaults it to false, otherwise ReportNewDevice is used). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:480, :535 — the wired daemon's updateDevice calls likewise carry UPDATE_HINT_LINKS. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp CheckConfigPendingEvent — emits CONFIG_PENDING as an internal VALUES event only on a 0↔1 transition. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.IBackendApi declares the client callback surface (event, listDevices, newDevices, deleteDevices, updateDevice, replaceDevice, readdedDevice, system.multicall, firmwareUpdateStatusChanged); de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyNotificationHandler#handleCommonNotification dispatches DEVICE_EXCLUDED / DEVICE_INCLUDED / DEVICE_REINCLUDED / RECEIVED_STATUS_DATA(_TRANSACTION) / RECEIVED_ACCESS_POINT_STATUS_DATA / DEVICE_CONFIGURATION_PENDING_CHANGED / DEVICE_READY_FOR_UPDATE / DUTY_CYCLE_EVENT / CENTRAL_DEVICE_COMMAND / OEM_CONTAINER_EVENT / REPORT_DEVICE_TEST_* / EMC_DATA_EVENT, and #handleConfigurationPendingChanged turns the config-pending notification into a channel-0 CONFIG_PENDING value event.
all.firmwareValue: No callback carries a MASTER paramset change. updateDevice's only hints are ALL=0 and LINKS=1, and rfd emits LINKS only for link add/remove and ALL only after an over-the-air firmware rebuild behind a config flag that defaults off. There is no generation counter or timestamp on a MASTER paramset: getParamsetId returns the static description id from the device XML (e.g. "switch_dev_master"), which does not change when values change.
all.ourValue: The SQLite row is the cache; the only removals are channel/device/interface deletion.
all.finding:
The concern is confirmed at Tier 1, and it is stronger than the candidate states. A MASTER write from another source — the WebUI's device-configuration page, hmcli, any second XML-RPC client — goes through RFChannel::PutParamsetValues, which stores the values and pushes them to the device and then returns. It emits nothing. The one client-visible side effect is conditional: `CheckConfigPendingEvent()` is called only when `CommitToDevice` fails, i.e. only when the device could not be reached immediately. For a mains-powered RX_ALWAYS device the commit succeeds inline, config_pending never leaves 0, and a WebUI MASTER write produces literally zero traffic to any registered callback. For a battery device the daemon sees CONFIG_PENDING go 1 then 0 on the maintenance channel — an edge that names neither the channel nor the parameter that changed, and which our store does not act on. The HmIP legacy surface behaves the same way: its notification switch has no "configuration changed" case, and its config-pending path emits CONFIG_PENDING on channel 0 exactly like BidCos. (`LegacyBackendClient#updateDevice` exists on the HmIP side but I found no caller for it in that tree; that tree can hide a reflective or event-bus dispatch, so treat "HmIP never emits updateDevice" as unverified — "HmIP emits no notification that carries changed MASTER values" is what the notification switch does settle.)

So what our rule rests on: nothing the CCU says. The signals that do exist and could bound the staleness are the device-lifecycle callbacks — newDevices, readdedDevice (RFManager.cpp:786, :817, fired on re-pair), replaceDevice, deleteDevices — plus updateDevice(hint=0) after a firmware update if the CCU is configured to send it. Of the four causes the damage note lists, a re-pair and a firmware update are therefore detectable at the callback level; a WebUI configuration write and a direct device write are not detectable at all, by any means short of re-reading getParamset(MASTER). There is also no cheap comparand: getParamsetId is the paramset's static XML id, not a version, so a poll cannot be made cheap by comparing a generation counter.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU notified on MASTER change, RFChannel::PutParamsetValues (or RFParamset::Put beneath it) would reach one of rfd's five XmlRpcCallAsync sites, or ReportUpdate would appear with a third hint constant. rfd has exactly five async callbacks and exactly two hint values, and grep for ReportUpdate across src/rfd returns three call sites, none of them on the paramset-write path — the check would have named the emitting line had one existed, the way it named RFChannel.cpp:756 for links.
all.challengeNote:
THE FIRMWARE HALF IS FULLY UPHELD AT TIER 1. Every citation reproduced verbatim, including the conditional nature of CheckConfigPendingEvent (called only when CommitToDevice fails), the two-value hint enum, the OTAU config default of false, and the HmIP notification switch. The candidate's caveat that LegacyBackendClient#updateDevice has no caller in that tree is also correct as stated — I re-checked and found the interface declaration and the client method, no invoker.

BUT THE FINDING MAKES A FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT OUR OWN CODE, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. The candidate writes that the daemon sees CONFIG_PENDING go 1 then 0 "and which our store does not act on". It does act on it. internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:77-130 installs `wireConfigPendingHook` on the central's EventCoordinator (wired at internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:472); on the CONFIG_PENDING True→False settle it reloads week profiles, re-applies operation-mode gating, waits `configPendingSettleDelay` = 10 s, then issues a targeted getParamset(MASTER) per channel of the affected device and persists the result into the very MasterValuesStore under audit (`refreshDeviceMasterCache`). That IS invalidation driven by something the CCU says, so the rule as titled is false for the interfaces that reach it.

BOUNDARY, NAMED. The settle path is gated by `hmenum.PushesConfigPendingFor(iface, productGroup) || iface.PushesConfigPending()` (auto_refresh.go:110-113), whose set is HmIP-RF + HmIP-Wired plus HmIP/HmIPW product groups on VirtualDevices. So:
- HmIP devices whose config write raises the CONFIG_PENDING edge: the cache IS refreshed, whoever wrote — including a WebUI write. The rule is FALSE here.
- BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, VirtualDevices, CUxD: `newMasterPollerForInterface` returns nil for pushing interfaces and otherwise builds a MasterPoller whose OnRefresh is scheduled POST-WRITE from our own putParamset (auto_refresh.go:262-300, device/channel_set.go:284-286). A poll of our own write detects nothing a third party did. The rule is TRUE here, and the candidate's central point — a WebUI MASTER write on a BidCos mains device produces literally zero traffic to any registered callback, because CommitToDevice succeeds inline and CheckConfigPendingEvent is never reached — survives intact and is the real defect.
- HmIP mains devices whose write commits without ever raising CONFIG_PENDING are uncovered too, but I did not establish from the HmIP tree when the pending flag is and is not raised; that part is unverified.

The rest of the reasoning is upheld: getParamsetId is the static XML paramset id, not a generation counter, so there is no cheap comparand; and of the four staleness causes, re-pair (newDevices/readdedDevice) and a firmware update (updateDevice hint 0, only if the CCU is configured to send it) are detectable at the callback level while a WebUI write and a direct device write are not.

all.title: The 5-minute straggler sweep loads every visible readable VALUES DP, on the unstated assumption that a getValue does not wake a sleeping device
all.ourValue: the sweep's wire call is a getValue that may reach the radio and queue a wake-up on a sleeping battery device (the visibility gate is described as the protection against that)
all.firmwareValue: on every interface the sweep can actually reach, the wire call is getParamset(VALUES) and the CCU answers it from its own in-memory model without emitting a frame: DEVICE_VALUE_GET → handleGetValueCommand walks the channel's StateDescription, reads IChannel#getParameterValue for each parameter, skips the ones with no value, and replies RESPONSE_STATUS_DATA — it queues no HmipTransaction
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleGetValueCommand and #handleAskValueCommand; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getParameterSet; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#getValue; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.cpp:147-176; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.h:23; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1311-1321; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/ValueStore.cpp:55-63; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485PhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.cpp:83-115
all.finding:
Two corrections to the premise, both from our own code before the firmware is even consulted. (1) The sweep does not issue getValue: LoadValue on a VALUES key routes to runLoadValuesParamset, which calls loader.GetParamset(channel, "VALUES") (internal/model/device/value_cache.go:333). (2) BidCos-RF and VirtualDevices are short-circuited to a sentinel with no wire call at all (value_cache.go:329-332), so the one interface where the CCU would send a frame is excluded by construction.

Firmware, HmIP (the interface family the sweep does reach): getParamset(addr,"VALUES") → DeviceUtil#getParameterSet sends BackendCommandType.DEVICE_VALUE_GET; DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleGetValueCommand answers it from IChannel#getParameterValue for each StateDescription parameter and sends RESPONSE_STATUS_DATA. It queues no transaction. The radio path is the sibling DEVICE_VALUE_ASK → handleAskValueCommand → TransactionTaskFactory#createRequestStatusTransaction + TransactionManagement#queueTransaction. So the sweep never wakes an HmIP device; a parameter with no value is simply omitted from the response.

Where the worry IS true, one step in each direction:
• The method our comment names — getValue — does reach the device on HmIP for exactly two keys: LegacyServiceHandler#getValue special-cases INSTALL_TEST and CURRENT_ILLUMINATION and routes both through DeviceUtil#askValue → DEVICE_VALUE_ASK, unconditionally, cached value or not. CURRENT_ILLUMINATION is declared OPERATIONS 5 / FLAGS 1 on HmIP-SMI, SMO, SPI, SLO and passes our visibility+readable gate. Our sweep escapes this only because it uses getParamset.
• BidCos-RF, if the value_cache.go:329 skip were ever removed: RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand::GetData serves from the store while GetAge(value_id) < VALUE_CACHE_TIME (=2000 ms, RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.h:23), and ValueStore::GetAge returns (uint32_t)-1 for a key that was never stored — precisely the unobserved case — so it falls through to the frame path every time: RxNeedsWakeup() devices get the frame pushed into after_wakeup_queue (capped at 10, oldest dropped, RFDevice.cpp:1311-1321) and getValue fails; others get a synchronous SendFrame.
