As measured, the rule happens to hold on both, but not for the stated reason: ScheduleRelevantChannelGroups (internal/model/custom/schedule_targets.go:83-86) narrows to groups whose profile sets ScheduleChannelNo, and only the IPLock profile does (profiles.go:848-864 for hmip-dld ch1/schedule 10; :884-891 for hmip-dlp ch12/schedule 14). So on HmIP-DLD the available target set is the single key '1_1' — the eight ACCESS_RECEIVER permission channels the CCU offers are never exposed at all, the write-side '2_1' default resolves to no bit and TargetChannelsListToBitmask returns ok=false so TARGET_CHANNELS is withheld entirely, and a CCU-authored permission slot targeting channel 3 decodes to an empty channel list that DetectLockMode then classifies as user_permission by falling through rather than by matching '2_'. The rule is therefore resting on an accident of a filter, doubled by the '1_1'/'2_1' write defaults in schedules.go:920-933 that restate the same unanchored convention. The sound re-grounding is available and needs no new source: classify by the resolved target channel's TYPE (DOOR_LOCK_* vs PERMISSION_TRANSCEIVER/ACCESS_RECEIVER), which both tiers carry. One further note: the neighbouring citation at internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:940-962 attributes the bit formula to `www/config/easymodes/js/HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:2918` (`Math.pow(2, (self.virtualChannels[index] - 1))`) and `:394` (`getWPVirtualChannels`). Neither symbol, nor the string `Math.pow(2`, nor `virtualChannels`, exists in that file in this OpenCCU-Base checkout (3519 lines) or anywhere in ../OpenCCU; that citation could not be reproduced here.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware encoded an ordinal lock/permission split, TARGET_CHANNELS would carry a type converter or a per-bit semantic in its ConfigurationParameter definition — the factory demonstrably can attach one, as the neighbouring LEVEL parameter does with DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0) — and it carries null. And had 'the lowest lock-relevant channel is the actuator' been the firmware's rule, HmIP-DLP would place DOOR_LOCK_TRANSCEIVER at channel 1; the descriptor check can return that answer, and does return it for HmIP-DLD (channel 1), but returns channel 12 for HmIP-DLP.
all.missingInput: The mapping from our '<group>_<member>' key to a device channel, and from that channel to its lock/permission role. The firmware carries the second half (channel TYPE) but nothing anywhere carries the first — it is generated by our own registry ordering, so the rule as written cannot be grounded in any source; it has to be replaced by a type lookup.

all.title: The optical alarm pattern defaults to the LAST entry of the device's light value list — a position, not a declared property
all.site: internal/alarm/outputs/manager.go:475 (`p = lights[len(lights)-1]`) and internal/alarm/outputs/testfire.go:80 (same expression). `AvailableLights()` (internal/model/custom/siren/siren.go:213) returns the OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION VALUE_LIST verbatim, in declaration order.
all.citation: Tier 1, ordering: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SignalOptical — the enum is declared, in order: DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL, BLINKING_ALTERNATELY_REPEATING, BLINKING_BOTH_REPEATING, DOUBLE_FLASHING_REPEATING, FLASHING_BOTH_REPEATING, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_0, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_1, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2. Tier 1, the same order on the operator surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/msg/asir_setAlarm.htm:33-40 maps ordinal 0→DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL … ordinal 7→${stringTableAlarmConfirmingSignal2}, and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js:95 writes that ordinal as `{name:'OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION', type:'int', value: opticalSignal}`. Tier 1, semantics of the last entry: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:30 "stringTableAlarmConfirmingSignal2" : "Confirmation signal 2 - long short short" (:25 "Alternating slow flashing", :26 "Simultaneous slow flashing", :36 "Simultaneous fast flashing", :41 "Simultaneous short flashing"). Tier 2, per-device declaration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/{HmIP-ASIR,HmIP-ASIR-2,HmIP-ASIR-O}.json, channel :3 VALUES OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION — TYPE=ENUM, OPERATIONS=2, DEFAULT='DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL', MIN='DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL', MAX='CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2', VALUE_LIST identical to the enum above on all three. The same file's LINK paramset shows the firmware's own choice of an alarm pattern: LONG_SIGNAL_SELECTION_OPTICAL DEFAULT='BLINKING_ALTERNATELY_REPEATING' (index 1), SHORT_SIGNAL_SELECTION_OPTICAL DEFAULT='FLASHING_BOTH_REPEATING' (index 4) — never the last entry.
all.finding: The firmware fixes the order and it is stable across HmIP-ASIR, HmIP-ASIR-2 and HmIP-ASIR-O (identical 8-entry VALUE_LIST, identical MIN/MAX). Our rule therefore resolves deterministically to the last entry, CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2 — the third of three one-shot confirmation signals ("long short short"), not an alarm pattern. Every repeating optical alarm pattern the device offers is one of the four *_REPEATING entries at indices 1-4; the three CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_* entries at indices 5-7 are the only members whose names do not carry REPEATING, and the firmware's own LINK-paramset defaults for a signalling optical link pick index 1 and index 4. So the positional convention picks the entry furthest from what an optical alarm needs: an optical-only activation or optical test fire writes a confirmation blink pattern, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE goes true, the watchdog is satisfied, and the sustained alarm flash never happens. Scope note: the rule cannot misfire on HM-Sec-Sir-WM — that device declares no OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION at all (../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-Sec-Sir-WM.json: channels :1..:3 VALUES carry only ERROR_SABOTAGE, INHIBIT, INSTALL_TEST, LOWBAT, ON_TIME, STATE, WORKING; :4 carries ARMSTATE), so AvailableLights() is empty and `len(lights) > 1` is false. HmIP-ASIR-B1 is not present in the descriptor corpus; the HmIP-side enum is device-independent, so its VALUE_LIST can only be a prefix/subset of the same order. The sound fix is the one the acoustic half already uses: answer it in the model from the descriptor, choosing a declared *_REPEATING member (or refusing when none exists), not from a position in the flattened projection.
all.ourValue: lights[len(lights)-1] = "CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2" (ordinal 7)
all.firmwareValue: the alarm patterns are ordinals 1-4: BLINKING_ALTERNATELY_REPEATING, BLINKING_BOTH_REPEATING, DOUBLE_FLASHING_REPEATING, FLASHING_BOTH_REPEATING; ordinal 7 is "Confirmation signal 2 - long short short"
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, the last member of SignalOptical / of the declared VALUE_LIST would have been a *_REPEATING flash pattern, and the firmware's own optical LINK defaults would have pointed at the tail of the list. Both checks return the opposite: the tail is the third confirmation signal, and the firmware defaults sit at indices 1 and 4. The check can distinguish the two cases — it did.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD, with two attached claims demoted. I re-read every cited file: SignalOptical, asir_setAlarm.htm, iseAlarmSirenHMIP.js, the English string table and all three ASIR descriptors are verbatim as reported, and I confirmed AvailableLights() is the OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION VALUE_LIST copied without reordering. The positional rule therefore resolves deterministically to CONFIRMATION_SIGNAL_2 — a one-shot confirmation blink, not one of the four *_REPEATING alarm patterns the firmware's own LINK defaults pick (indices 1 and 4). Wrong-surface check passed: the WebUI writes OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION into the VALUES paramset, which is the same parameter and paramset our alarm write targets, not a LINK-paramset twin. I also grepped the two other readable Tier-1 HmIP surfaces named in the firmwareQuestion — ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/ — both are silent on OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, so no substitute source was available and none was invented. Two demotions. (a) The consequence narrative "OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE goes true, the watchdog is satisfied" is device behaviour: no CCU source says a confirmation signal raises OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE. The grounded damage is narrower and sufficient — the daemon writes a confirmation blink where an alarm pattern was intended. (b) The HmIP-ASIR-B1 scope note ("its VALUE_LIST can only be a prefix/subset of the same order") is an inference, not a reading; and it is the weaker form of a true statement — SignalOptical#getNames takes no size argument, so any list generated from this enum is the full eight in this order, and a device declaring a different list would not be using this enum. I checked the whole descriptor corpus: exactly three files declare OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION (the three ASIRs), all identical. HM-Sec-Sir-WM re-verified: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-Sec-Sir-WM.json channels :1..:3 VALUES = ERROR_SABOTAGE, INHIBIT, INSTALL_TEST, LOWBAT, ON_TIME, STATE, WORKING and :4 adds ARMSTATE — no OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, so AvailableLights() is empty there and the rule cannot fire.

all.title: The WKP CODE_STATE known-code enum index (1) rests on a comment that states the value list, not on the descriptor
all.site: internal/alarm/intents.go:100 (`const wkpCodeStateKnownIndex = 1`) and intents.go:484 (`case hmtypes.ValueKindInt: return v.Int == wkpCodeStateKnownIndex`), reached from intents.go:143 for hmenum.ParameterCodeState.
all.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/maintenanceWKP.fn:88-95 decodes the WKP's CODE_STATE ordinals directly — `if (codeState == 0) {curState = "${codeIdle}";}` / `if (codeState == 1) {curState = "${lblUser}: "#objCodeID.Value();}` / `if (codeState == 2) {curState = "${codeUnKnownCodeIDReceived}";}` (continuing 3..7 for the learn-mode and erase states). Tier 1, the enum itself: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.CodeState declares, in order, IDLE, KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED, UNKNOWN_CODE_DETECTED, LEARN_MODE_FOR_CODE_ID_STARTED, LEARN_MODE_EXIT_FOR_CODE_WITH_SUCCESS, LEARN_MODE_EXIT_FOR_CODE_WITH_TIMEOUT, LEARN_MODE_EXIT_FOR_CODE_WITH_ERROR_DUPLICATE_CODE, CODE_ERASED, and CodeState#getNonOptionalNames returns exactly the first three names — the short list a device that has no learn-mode reporting declares. Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-WKP.json, VCU4273771:0 VALUES CODE_STATE — TYPE=ENUM, OPERATIONS=5, DEFAULT='IDLE', MIN='IDLE', MAX='UNKNOWN_CODE_DETECTED', VALUE_LIST=['IDLE','KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED','UNKNOWN_CODE_DETECTED'].
all.finding: Index 1 is KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED, and it is index 1 in both declared variants — the WKP's 3-entry list and the 8-entry list HmIP-FWI declares (../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-FWI.json, VCU4820995:0 VALUES CODE_STATE, VALUE_LIST=['IDLE','KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED','UNKNOWN_CODE_DETECTED','LEARN_MODE_FOR_CODE_ID_STARTED',…,'CODE_ERASED']). The firmware guarantees this structurally rather than per device: CodeState#getNonOptionalNames takes a prefix of the same enum, so a shorter list can only truncate the tail, never reorder or insert ahead of index 1. The ReGa control is the independent confirmation on the CCU's own operator path — it hard-codes the same ordinals and renders ordinal 1 as "user: <CODE_ID>", i.e. exactly the "a known code identified user N" meaning our correlation relies on. The comment's asserted list is correct verbatim for the WKP. The string branch (wkpCodeStateKnownLabel) is also correct: 'KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED' is the declared label.
all.ourValue: wkpCodeStateKnownIndex = 1
all.firmwareValue: CodeState ordinal 1 = KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED (ReGa: ordinal 1 renders as "user: <CODE_ID>")
all.negativeControl: Had our index been wrong, maintenanceWKP.fn would have decoded ordinal 1 as something other than a recognised user (it decodes 0=idle, 2=unknown code), or CodeState would have declared a different member at position 1, or the WKP descriptor's VALUE_LIST would have carried an extra member ahead of KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED. All three checks were run and all three agree on index 1; the FWI list shows what a divergent declaration looks like (it extends the tail, and index 1 is unchanged), so the check demonstrably reacts to list shape.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD. I read CodeState in full — the enum order and getNonOptionalNames' 3-element prefix loop are exactly as reported, so a device declaring the short list can only truncate the tail and can never move a member ahead of index 1. I re-read maintenanceWKP.fn (the ordinal decode is at :88-97, matching the cited :88-95 span) and both descriptors; the WKP's 3-entry and the FWI's 8-entry lists agree at index 1. Wrong-surface check passed: maintenanceWKP.fn reads MAINTENANCE.CODE_STATE (:88, via `cObj.DPByControl("MAINTENANCE.CODE_ID")` at :13 for the companion), which is channel :0 VALUES — the same datapoint our router subscribes to via hmenum.ParameterCodeState (intents.go:143). The string branch is also grounded: 'KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED' is the declared label in both descriptors and in the CCU's own string table. Nothing here rests on a convention — the ordinal is written down twice independently (the enum's declaration order and ReGa's hard-coded `codeState == 1`).

all.title: The WKP channel-to-user-slot layout (channels 1..16, odd=lock, slot=(ch+1)/2) is asserted in a comment, not read from the device
all.site: internal/alarm/intents.go:467 (`wkpPairIndex`: `if err != nil || ch < 1 || ch > 16 { return 0, false }` / `return (ch + 1) / 2, true`) and intents.go:242 (`correlated := c != nil && known && codeID >= 1 && codeID <= 8 && codeID == pairIdx && now.Sub(at) <= wkpCorrelationWindow`). Routing is by parameter, not by model: intents.go:145-148 dispatches on hmenum.ParameterPressLock / ParameterPressUnlock.
all.citation: Tier 1, the pairing formula verbatim: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/control/function.fn:159-169 — `if (chn.HssType() == "ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER") { if (chn.Label() == "HmIP-FWI") { … ${chType_ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER} "#chNumber#" … } if (chn.Label() == "HmIP-WKP") { integer tmpChn = (chNumber + 1) / 2; … ${chType_ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER} "#tmpChn#" … } }`, with chType_ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER = "Access Control" / "Benutzer" (../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/{en,de}/translate.lang.channelDescription.js:7). Tier 1, the pairing on the config surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:7026-7028 — for HmIP-WKP, a channel that does NOT carry NUMERIC_PIN_CODE renders `${lblPinOfChannelLockA} [expr $chn / 2] ${lblPinOfChannelLockB}` = "The PIN code of the channel 'User <chn/2> Lock' is used." (labels at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.label.js:225-226). Tier 2, the channel list and the alternation: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-WKP.json declares VCU4273771:1 … :16 all TYPE=ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER, DIRECTION=1, with :0 MAINTENANCE, :17 ALARM_COND_SWITCH_TRANSMITTER, :18 SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE. ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-WKP.json: every odd channel 1,3,…,15 declares VALUES ['ACCESS_AUTHORIZATION','PRESS_LOCK'], every even channel 2,4,…,16 declares VALUES ['ACCESS_AUTHORIZATION','PRESS_UNLOCK']; MASTER NUMERIC_PIN_CODE exists only on the odd channels. Tier 2, the slot count: VCU4273771:0 VALUES CODE_ID — TYPE=INTEGER, OPERATIONS=5, DEFAULT=1, MIN=1, MAX=8, alongside USER_AUTHORIZATION_01 … USER_AUTHORIZATION_08.
all.finding: All four assertions in the comment are grounded, and the pairing formula is character-for-character the one ReGa uses: `(chNumber + 1) / 2` with integer division, on the same 1-based channel index, for exactly HmIP-WKP. The 1..16 bound is the declared ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER channel span; the odd=lock / even=unlock alternation is declared per channel (PRESS_LOCK vs PRESS_UNLOCK) rather than assumed, and the PIN lives on the odd channel of each pair, which is why the config dialog tells the even channel it borrows `chn/2`'s PIN. The 1..8 CODE_ID bound is the WKP's declared MIN/MAX and matches USER_AUTHORIZATION_01..08. Two scope notes. (1) The router keys on the parameter, not the model, so wkpPairIndex would be applied to any device firing PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK; in the descriptor corpus only HmIP-WKP declares them, and HmIP-FWI — the other ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER device, which does have CODE_ID with MAX=21 and a 1:1 channel-to-user mapping (function.fn:161 uses chNumber, not (chNumber+1)/2) — declares STATE on its access channels, never PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK, so it cannot reach this path. Deriving the bounds from the device rather than the constants 16/8 would make that safety structural instead of incidental. (2) One predicate our code applies is NOT settled by any CCU source: the equality `codeID == pairIdx`, i.e. that the keypad fires the press on the channel pair whose index equals the CODE_ID of the PIN just entered. The CCU only relays the two events; which channel the WKP raises is device firmware. What the CCU does show is that both numbers live in one "User N" namespace with N in 1..8 — ReGa names channel pair (chNumber+1)/2 "Access Control N" and renders CODE_STATE=1 as "user: <CODE_ID>" (../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/maintenanceWKP.fn:91) — which is consistent with the predicate but does not prove it.
all.ourValue: channels 1..16, pair = (ch+1)/2, codeID accepted in 1..8
all.firmwareValue: ReGa for HmIP-WKP: tmpChn = (chNumber + 1) / 2; descriptor: 16 ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER channels, PRESS_LOCK on odd / PRESS_UNLOCK on even, NUMERIC_PIN_CODE on odd only, CODE_ID MIN=1 MAX=8
all.negativeControl: Had the layout been wrong, ReGa's WKP branch would have carried a different formula (it carries a distinct one for HmIP-FWI — plain chNumber — so the file demonstrably distinguishes layouts), the config dialog would have named a different pair for an even channel, or the descriptor would have shown PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK in a different arrangement or a channel span other than 1..16. Each of those was checked against the source and none holds. For the `codeID == pairIdx` predicate the check cannot produce a different answer either way — no CCU source decides it — which is why that half is reported as unsettled rather than confirmed.
all.challengeNote: NARROWED. Every one of the layout citations checks out verbatim — I read function.fn:159-170 (the formula is `(chNumber + 1) / 2` with ReGa integer division, guarded on exactly `chn.Label() == "HmIP-WKP"`), hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:7028 (`[expr $chn / 2]`, Tcl integer division, on the branch where NUMERIC_PIN_CODE is absent, i.e. the even/unlock channel), both label catalogues, the device description's 16 ACCESS_TRANSCEIVER channels, and the per-channel PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK alternation with NUMERIC_PIN_CODE on odd channels only. The two firmware formulas are mutually consistent: (2n-1+1)/2 = n and (2n)/2 = n. The FWI containment argument also holds — HmIP-FWI declares STATE on its access channels, never PRESS_LOCK/PRESS_UNLOCK, so it cannot reach wkpPairIndex even though the router keys on the parameter rather than the model (intents.go:145-148). So the title's rule — the layout — is grounded on Tier 1. I demote the id from confirmed because the predicate the production path actually turns on is not the layout. intents.go:242 requires `codeID == pairIdx`, and no CCU source states that the keypad fires the press on the channel pair whose index equals the CODE_ID of the PIN just entered. I searched the CCU tree for every use of CODE_ID and USER_AUTHORIZATION outside the string tables: only maintenanceWKP.fn:13/16-24 (which reads them for display) and maintenanceFWI.fn:14. Nothing binds a CODE_ID to a channel. The structural correspondence is suggestive — CODE_ID MIN=1 MAX=8, USER_AUTHORIZATION_01..08 and eight channel pairs all live in one "User N" namespace, and ReGa names pair n "Access Control n" while rendering CODE_STATE=1 as "<user>: <CODE_ID>" — but suggestive is not read from the source. Treat `codeID == pairIdx` as not-performable from CCU material and name it in the comment as an untested device-behaviour assumption; if it is wrong, no keypad press ever correlates and every arm/disarm silently lands in journalKeypadUnmatched. Secondary observation, not a defect claim: the 16 and 8 bounds are hard-coded constants rather than read from the declared channel span and CODE_ID MIN/MAX, so the FWI safety above is incidental rather than structural.

all.title: reportValueUsage is classified as a read although the daemon uses it to mutate the CCU
all.site: internal/client/reliability/classifier.go:63 (`"reportvalueusage": {}` inside readMethods, whose header at :49-51 reads "readMethods enumerates every method that returns CCU state without / Mutating it…") and internal/central/adapter/central_links.go:224 (`if err := caller.ReportValueUsage(ctx, ch.Address, valueID, refCounter); err != nil && chErr == nil {`, called per channel with refCounter 1 to create and 0 to tear down, the teardown also zeroing PRESS_LONG).
all.citation: Tier 1, BidCos: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:700-723 — the method's own documentation block states verbatim: "Diese Methode teilt dem Interfaceprozeß mit, wie oft ein Wert innerhalb der Logikschicht verwendet wird. Dadurch kann der Interfaceprozeß die Verbindung mit der entsprechenden Komponente herstellen bzw. löschen. Diese Funktion sollte bei jeder Änderung aufgerufen werden. Der Rückgabewert ist true, wenn die Aktion sofort durchgeführt wurde. Er ist false, wenn die entsprechende Komponente nicht erreicht werden konnte und vom Benutzer zunächst in den Config-Mode gebracht werden muß. Der Interfaceprozeß hat dann aber die neue Einstellung übernommen und wird sie bei nächster Gelegenheit automatisch an die Komponente übertragen. In diesem Fall ist dann auch der Wert \"CONFIG_PENDING\" im Kanal \"MAINTENANCE\" der Komponente gesetzt." The implementation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1425-1449 — `value_usage_map[value]=count;` then, on a non-zero total, `AddLinkPeer(central_device->GetListenerChannel()->GetSerial(), false); central_device->GetListenerChannel()->LowLevelAddLinkPeer(GetDevice()->GetAddress(), GetIndex());` and, on a zero total, `LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(central_address, central_channel); central_device->GetListenerChannel()->LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(...)`, returning `!(config_data_dirty || link_peers_dirty)`. Wired: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:680 and src/hs485d/HS485Channel.cpp:409 carry the same method. Tier 1, HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage — it reads the per-address metadata record whose id is the constant META_DATA_ID_REPORT_VALUE = "reportValueUsageData", writes the (valueId → refCounter) entry back via MetadataUtil#setMetaData, sums the entries, and then calls DeviceUtil#createCentralLink when the sum is > 0 or DeviceUtil#deleteCentralLink when it is 0, waiting on the device's response and raising a transmission-pending fault when the device cannot be reached.
all.finding: reportValueUsage is a write on both south-bound stacks, and it is a write in two senses at once: it persists per-channel state (the BidCos `value_usage_map` / the HmIP `reportValueUsageData` metadata record, which is the very record we read back through getMetadata to compute the links' active state) and it performs radio configuration on the device — adding or removing the direct link peer between the channel and the central. The BidCos return value is explicitly a transmission verdict, not a query result: false means the device could not be reached, the setting is queued, and CONFIG_PENDING is now set on the device's MAINTENANCE channel. The classifier's own header says readMethods holds methods that return state "without mutating it", so the entry contradicts its own contract, and TestClassifyMethod pins the table rather than the semantics. Consequence as the reader described: link create/teardown bursts are paced on the read pool. Note this is not a hypothetical burst — central_links.go issues one call per press-capable channel and two per channel on teardown, each one a device configuration frame. The neighbouring entries in the firmwareQuestion could not be settled here: getSearchResults, getServiceInformation and clientServerInitialized appear nowhere in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd or src/hs485d, and only reportValueUsage among them appears on the HmIP legacy surface; classifying those three is a separate measurement I did not perform.

all.finding: The positional rule is right, and right by construction rather than by luck: the firmware generates every REPETITIONS list from one formula in which the index IS the number formatted into the label, with NO_REPETITION pinned at index 0 and INFINITE_REPETITIONS pinned at the last index whatever the size. So slot 0, slot n and slot len-1 mean exactly what sound.go says, sound.go and mixins.RepetitionsLabel agree for every n a device declares, and no leading sentinel is possible — the OLD_VALUE / DO_NOT_CARE entries that motivated the concern belong to SOUNDFILE, and even there they sit at the TAIL, not the head (HmIP-MP3P.json VCU1543608:2 VALUES SOUNDFILE, 256 entries ending ['RANDOM_SOUNDFILE','OLD_VALUE','DO_NOT_CARE']). The declared LINK and MASTER variants (SHORT_PROFILE_REPETITIONS, LONG_PROFILE_REPETITIONS, POWERUP_PROFILE_REPETITIONS, 256 entries ending REPETITIONS_254, INFINITE_REPETITIONS) follow the same formula, so even a list resolved from the wrong paramset would not shift the meaning of a slot. One real defect surfaces from the same reading, on the bound rather than the ordering: maxRepetitionsIndex = 18 in sound.go while the MP3P and WRCD both declare a 16-entry list topping out at REPETITIONS_014. For index 15..18 the guard `if slot >= len(availableRep) { slot = len(availableRep) - 1 }` clamps to the last slot — INFINITE_REPETITIONS. A caller asking for 15 repetitions gets an unbounded playback, silently, and the clamp is exactly the failure shape the candidate feared, arriving through the ceiling rather than through the ordering. mixins.RepetitionsLabel has the same 18 but fails safe: it emits REPETITIONS_015, which the device's value list rejects. On the semantic half of the question ("3 more times" vs "3 times total"), the firmware names index 0 NO_REPETITION — the file still plays once — so REPETITIONS_003 is three repetitions on top of the first playback, i.e. our comment's "play N+1 times". That reading rests on the member names, which is all the CCU source carries; the WebUI never renders these labels (no REPETITIONS entry in ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/stringtable_de.txt).

all.firmwareValue: Repetitions#getNames: names[0]=NO_REPETITION, names[i]=REPETITIONS_%03d(i), names[size-1]=INFINITE_REPETITIONS; MP3P/WRCD declare size 16, so the highest countable value is REPETITIONS_014

That makes sound.go's slot arithmetic sound independently of which paramset the list was resolved from — I confirmed the 16-entry VALUES list and the 256-entry LINK/MASTER lists in the descriptors, and both obey the formula. The leading-sentinel worry is genuinely absent: OLD_VALUE and DO_NOT_CARE belong to SOUNDFILE and sit at the tail (HmIP-MP3P.json VCU1543608:2 VALUES SOUNDFILE, 256 entries beginning ['INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE','SOUNDFILE_001',…] and ending [… 'SOUNDFILE_252','RANDOM_SOUNDFILE','OLD_VALUE','DO_NOT_CARE']). (a) The ceiling defect is real but mis-mechanised for one value: with a 16-entry list, index 15 needs no clamp — `slot >= len(availableRep)` is false at 15 — it lands directly on availableRep[15] = INFINITE_REPETITIONS; only 16, 17, 18 are clamped there. The outcome is the same for all four: a caller asking for 15 or more repetitions gets unbounded playback silently. The twin at mixins.go:191 fails safe by emitting REPETITIONS_015, which the device rejects, and its own comment already records that both captured devices stop at REPETITIONS_014. (b) The semantic half ("REPETITIONS_003 plays the file four times") is inferred from the member name NO_REPETITION at index 0 and nothing else; no CCU source renders these labels — I confirmed ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/stringtable_de.txt carries no REPETITIONS row. Report that reading as unverified rather than as part of the grounding. One residual assumption I could not close: that the CCU builds each device's declared VALUE_LIST by calling Repetitions#getNames. It is not written anywhere I could read; what supports it is that two independently declared sizes (16 and 256) both match the formula exactly, including the index-equals-count invariant. Since our conversion selects a label by slot and never a raw ordinal, the invariant is what matters and it holds in the observed data at both sizes.

all.finding: Confirmed for every family the CCU ships a definition for, and the table is exactly right there: HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM, HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU (Tier 2 device XMLs) and the HM-CC-VG-1 virtual heating group (Tier 1 groupdefinitions.xml) all declare AUTO-MODE, MANU-MODE, PARTY-MODE, BOOST-MODE at 0..3, and libhsscomm settles that the exported VALUE_LIST is the XML option order and that the wire value is the index into it. It does not bite today only because internal/model/custom/profiles.go routes rfControlModeLabel exclusively through the climate profiles; ST6-SH is not registered there. (2) internal/model/custom/profiles.go:96-124 also registers RfThermostat for device types bc-rt-trx-cyg, bc-rt-trx-cyn and bc-tc-c-wm; no device XML for those exists anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base (grep for BC-RT-TRX over the whole tree hits nothing outside the compiled jars), so their CONTROL_MODE list is unverified and the hard-coded table is an unchecked assumption for those three. all.negativeControl: Had the option order differed, the same extraction would have shown it: the option blocks are read verbatim from the XML, and the `index=` override that HSSLogicalTypeOption::InitFromXml honours is genuinely in use in this same corpus — e.g. the ERROR parameters declare <option id="NO_ERROR" index="0"/> and <option id="LOAD_FAILURE" index="3"/>, producing a deliberately sparse list with empty slots 1 and 2. So the check distinguishes dense-document-order lists from sparse ones, and it returned dense with no index= for all four CONTROL_MODE blocks. Had our rule been wrong, either an index= attribute or a different label sequence would have appeared.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed; I re-derived rather than re-read. Extracting every CONTROL_MODE parameter block in src/devicetypes by regex (not by spot check) yields exactly six declarations in six files, and they partition cleanly into the four PARTY/BOOST climate families and the one HOLIDAY/INACTIVE switch family — no third variant hides in the tree. The table is exactly right for all four climate families. Both narrowing edges survive, and I tightened each.

Edge (1) — keying on the parameter name rather than the channel type — does not bite today, and I checked this properly rather than trusting the original claim, because profile lookup is prefix-based, not exact (registry.go:434-447: exact match first, then longest-prefix-wins). Prefix matching is what makes HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM pick up hm-cc-rt-dn's RfThermostat, which is benign since rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml:2268 carries the identical list. It is also what could have let an unrelated device type slip into a climate profile. I enumerated all 19 Climate-category registrations and confirmed none is a prefix of "st6-sh" (ST6-SH's own type id, from its supported_types block at rf_st_6_sh.xml:8), so the HOLIDAY/INACTIVE list is unreachable from rfControlModeLabel. SimpleRfThermostat devices (hm-cc-tc, zel stg rm fwt) are KindSimpleRF and the Subscribe switch wires CONTROL_MODE only under KindRF, so they never reach it either.

Edge (2) is the stronger one and it holds under a harder search than the original: bc-rt-trx-cyg, bc-rt-trx-cyn and bc-tc-c-wm have no CONTROL_MODE definition anywhere the firmware can be read. Case-insensitive grep for BC-RT-TRX and BC-TC-C-WM over the whole of ../OpenCCU-Base returns nothing; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/replaceMap/rfReplaceMap.xml — the mechanism that would alias an OEM clone onto an existing type XML, and the obvious way this edge could have collapsed — contains no BC-RT entry; and no pydevccu descriptor or paramset carries the type. For those three registrations the hard-coded table is an assumption with no firmware behind it. This is a Tier-1-and-Tier-2-silent input, not a contradiction: the honest statement is that the rule is confirmed for four families and not performable for three.

The remedy named in the original stands, and I confirmed the precedent is real and on the same subscription path: climate.go:1857 and :1873 already resolve TEMPERATURE_OFFSET and HEATING_COOLING through custom.EnumWireLabel (internal/model/custom/replay.go:65). Routing CONTROL_MODE the same way would close both edges without changing behaviour on the four verified families, because for those four the descriptor VALUE_LIST is byte-for-byte the hard-coded table.

all.finding: Both bases are exactly as the comment claims, and the write path is consistent with the read path in both directions. RF: the pointer is an option-typed MASTER parameter on the device root (matching resolveWeekProgramPointer's MASTER+root walk), its ordinals run 0..2 with 0 meaning week program 1, and the firmware docu states the base in words rather than leaving it to convention. numWeekPrograms' MIN/MAX read (climate.go:2358-2364) therefore yields 3 for HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU / HM-CC-VG-1, which is correct. The RF write emits the label "WEEK PROGRAM 1" for profileWeekIndex 0, and HSSLogicalTypeOption::EnforceConstraints resolves a label to its position, so read and write agree on slot 0. IP: ACTIVE_PROFILE is an INTEGER whose logical range starts at 1 (MIN=1, DEFAULT=1) with an IntegerToInteger(factor 1.0, offset -1.0) converter sitting between the logical 1-based value and the device's 0-based physical one — the CCU already does the shift, so a client must not shift again; our read uses the value as-is and our write sends idx+1, both correct. One observation for the future: the descriptor MIN is the field that settles this on the IP side (MIN=1), but it cannot settle it on the RF side, because GetDescription forces MIN=0 for every option type regardless of meaning — reading MIN there would prove nothing, and the option order is what carries the answer.
all.negativeControl: The extraction reports MIN/MAX/DEFAULT and VALUE_LIST verbatim per parameter and it does return different answers for the two families from the same script run: MIN=0/DEFAULT=0 with a three-entry VALUE_LIST for RF WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER, MIN=1/DEFAULT=1 with no VALUE_LIST for IP ACTIVE_PROFILE. Had RF been 1-based, its docu would read <ol start="1"> and its first option would not be "WEEK PROGRAM 1"; had IP been 0-based, createActiveProfileParameter would pass 0 as default and min and carry no -1.0 offset. Both counter-shapes are what the check would have printed.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as confirmed. Both bases are as the comment claims, in both directions, and I checked the two legs the original left implicit.

The converter direction is the load-bearing fact on the IP side, and I read the arithmetic rather than accepting the summary. With factor 1.0 and offset -1.0, physical→logical is (p - (-1.0))/1.0 = p+1 and logical→physical is l*1.0 + (-1.0) = l-1. So physical 0 is logical 1: the CCU performs the shift, and a client that shifted again would be off by one. Our read uses the value as-is and our write sends idx+1. Correct in both directions.

The RF write surface was the other thing worth proving rather than assuming, since "EnforceConstraints resolves a label to its position" is only useful if putParamset actually reaches it. It does — the full chain is in the citation. Two details that chain exposes and that the original did not state: the walk goes through RFDevice, not RFChannel, which is what makes a device-root MASTER parameter reachable at all and matches masterConfigWriteTarget; and HSSParamset::Put drops parameters failing IsWriteable(), which WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER passes only because device.xsd defaults operations to "read,write" in the absence of the attribute. So emitting the label "WEEK PROGRAM 1" for profileWeekIndex 0 lands on ordinal 0, agreeing with the read.

numWeekPrograms (climate.go:2358-2364) computes max-min+1 and is right on both sides for the same reason: RF gives 2-0+1 = 3, IP gives 6-1+1 = 6 or 3-1+1 = 3.

The original's closing observation is correct and worth keeping: descriptor MIN settles the base on the IP side (MIN=1) but proves nothing on the RF side, because HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDescription forces MIN=0 for every option type regardless of meaning. On RF the option order is what carries the answer, and rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml is unusual in stating the base in prose (<ol start="0">) rather than leaving it to convention — which is exactly why this rule is groundable and not another not-performable.

all.negativeControl: The extraction reads each parameter's option list verbatim and it does return divergent lists from the same sweep — FAULT_REPORTING's option lists differ per device family in the same files (VALVE_TIGHT / ADJUSTING_RANGE_TOO_LARGE… on HM-CC-RT-DN vs SENSOR_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPT… on ST6-SH), and the ERROR parameters use explicit sparse index= slots. A DIRECTION list that started with a different entry, or one family that reordered UP and DOWN, would have printed differently; all 38 printed the same dense NONE/UP/DOWN/UNDEFINED. On the HmIP side, had the ordinal not been the exported value, DeviceUtil would lack the ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal branch or crRFD.conf would set it false — the config file was read, not assumed.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as confirmed, and I strengthened the evidence rather than re-reading the original's. Both option lists are unanimous across the entire corpus, not merely across the three blind types the original named: 40 RF declarations and 124 Tier-2 DIRECTION declarations, 166 Tier-2 ACTIVITY_STATE declarations, zero variants. A device family with a different ordering would have shown up in that sweep and none did.

The comment's secondary claim — that both are read-only ENUMs — is also exactly right, and I checked it rather than letting it ride: all 40 RF declarations carry operations="read,event", and ACTIVITY_STATE is built by #createReadEventEnumerationParameter, i.e. READ|EVENT with no WRITE.

The original's chain was sound but stopped one step short, so I closed it: the ordinal reaches us on the push path as well as the poll path. DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue is called with out=true not only from #getParameterSet but from LegacyNotificationHandler and LegacyBackendNotificationHandler, so a pushed ACTIVITY_STATE event arrives as the position in getEnumStrings(), which is the int32 our Sensor receives. Had only getParamset converted, the rule would have been right on replay and wrong on every subsequent event.

One boundary the rule's phrasing glosses, named here so a later reader does not have to rediscover it. The two lists coincide at 1 and 2 — the indices the code actually depends on — but not at 0 and 3. DIRECTION 0 is NONE, a definite "not moving"; ACTIVITY_STATE 0 is UNKNOWN, an absence of information; toCoverDirection maps both to DirectionNone. And HmIP's real "not moving" is STABLE(3), which casts to CoverDirection(3), matching no constant and reaching directionString's default. The effect is cosmetic in both directions — directionString's default returns "stopped", which is right for STABLE and wrong-but-harmless for UNDEFINED — and IsMoving() (cover.go:493) tests only for Up/Down, so movement detection is unaffected. Nothing here is a defect; it is the edge at which "the two lists coincide" stops being true, and it is worth the comment saying so.

I also ruled out the wrong-surface trap this series keeps catching. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.objects.DeviceDescription carries an @RpcMember("DIRECTION") — the device-description link-direction field, an entirely different quantity from the VALUES-paramset DIRECTION. It does not collide, because resolveDirectionDP resolves a channel parameter data point rather than a description field, but the name reuse is real and worth having excluded explicitly.

HmIP-BBL remains outside the descriptor corpus. The original's reason for covering it anyway is correct and I verified it: grep for "ACTIVITY_STATE" across the HmIP side finds exactly one registration, an unqualified ParameterMapKey with no per-device or per-variant override, so the Tier-1 definition is the only one any HmIP drive can carry.

all.title: Garage DOOR_STATE / DOOR_COMMAND labels are compared and written verbatim with no descriptor or firmware source
all.ourValue: DoorStateUnknown = "UNKNOWN"
all.firmwareValue: "POSITION_UNKNOWN" — there is no DOOR_STATE label spelled "UNKNOWN"
all.citation: Tier 1: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDoorState — with ventilation, enumStrings = {"CLOSED", "OPEN", "VENTILATION_POSITION", "POSITION_UNKNOWN"} paired with enumValues = {0, 1, 2, 7}; without ventilation, {"CLOSED", "OPEN", "POSITION_UNKNOWN"} / {0, 1, 7}; built as LogicalType.ENUM with a read+event IOOperations. #createDoorCommand — with ventilation, enumStrings = {LinkJumpTarget.NOP.name(), "OPEN", "STOP", "CLOSE", "PARTIAL_OPEN"} / enumValues = {0, 2, 3, 5, 8}; without, {NOP, "OPEN", "STOP", "CLOSE"} / {0, 2, 3, 5}; IOOperations.WRITE only. Registered in #initialise under ParameterMapKey("DOOR_STATE", "ventilation") / ("DOOR_STATE") and the same pair for DOOR_COMMAND. Export path: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#createParameterDescription sets VALUE_LIST from the converter's enum strings, and #convertParameterValue replaces the label with its position in that list (and an inbound Number with values[intValue]) because ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 sets Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true. Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MOD-HO.json — VCU3574044:1 VALUES DOOR_STATE {TYPE ENUM, MIN 'CLOSED', MAX 'POSITION_UNKNOWN', DEFAULT 'CLOSED', VALUE_LIST ['CLOSED','OPEN','VENTILATION_POSITION','POSITION_UNKNOWN'], OPERATIONS 5}; DOOR_COMMAND {TYPE ENUM, MIN 'NOP', MAX 'PARTIAL_OPEN', DEFAULT 'NOP', VALUE_LIST ['NOP','OPEN','STOP','CLOSE','PARTIAL_OPEN'], OPERATIONS 2}; identical on HmIP-MOD-TM.json (VCU6166407:1). Tier 3 witness on provenance: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:456-463 also spells it POSITION_UNKNOWN, so the divergence was introduced in our port rather than inherited.
all.finding: Eight of the nine labels are verbatim correct — CLOSED, OPEN, VENTILATION_POSITION on DOOR_STATE, and NOP, OPEN, STOP, CLOSE, PARTIAL_OPEN on DOOR_COMMAND, all matching the firmware's enumStrings exactly. The ninth is wrong: our DoorStateUnknown is "UNKNOWN" and the firmware label is "POSITION_UNKNOWN". The consequence is smaller than the bundle's damage note assumes, and I checked rather than assumed: DoorStateUnknown is never matched against a wire value on any live path. Position() (garage.go:214-223) has no case for it and falls through to the same (zero, false) it would return anyway; closureStateFor (matter_closure.go:60-63) has `case DoorStateUnknown: return nil` immediately followed by `default: return nil`. The doorMode EnumSelect (garage.go:184-188) lists only CLOSED / VENTILATION_POSITION / OPEN, all correct. So today the wrong spelling is a dead constant plus one test (internal/model/custom/cover/matter_test.go:268) that drives a label no device ever sends — a bracketing test that will keep passing whatever the constant says. It should still read POSITION_UNKNOWN before something starts comparing it. Two further facts worth recording while the source is open. (a) The physical byte for POSITION_UNKNOWN is 7 and for PARTIAL_OPEN is 8, but the value the daemon sees is the ordinal into VALUE_LIST (3 and 4 respectively), not the physical value — DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue with the crRFD.conf flag does the translation, so custom.EnumLabelValue's positional resolution is on the right surface. (b) On a drive without the ventilation option the list is only three long and PARTIAL_OPEN does not exist at all, so Vent() must stay gated on Capabilities.SupportsVent as it is.
all.negativeControl: The extraction prints each parameter's VALUE_LIST verbatim from two independent surfaces, and it does return different spellings for different parameters in the same run — ACTIVITY_STATE comes back with a bare 'UNKNOWN' as its first entry while DOOR_STATE comes back with 'POSITION_UNKNOWN' as its last. Had our spelling been right, 'UNKNOWN' would have appeared in the DOOR_STATE list from both the firmware factory and the descriptor corpus; it appeared in neither. The ventilation/non-ventilation split is likewise a value the check produced rather than assumed.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as contradicted, and the original's damage assessment survives a harder look — which is the part I most expected to break, since "the wrong constant is harmless" is exactly the claim that usually turns out to be optimistic.

Eight of nine labels are verbatim correct: CLOSED, OPEN, VENTILATION_POSITION on DOOR_STATE, and NOP, OPEN, STOP, CLOSE, PARTIAL_OPEN on DOOR_COMMAND. The ninth is wrong — ours is "UNKNOWN", the firmware's is "POSITION_UNKNOWN".

It is genuinely dead, and I established that from the read path rather than by grepping for the constant. DOOR_STATE arrives as an ordinal and is resolved to a label through custom.EnumLabelValue before OnState sees it (garage.go:365-366: `if label, ok := custom.EnumLabelValue(g.doorStateDp); ok { g.OnState(DoorState(label)) }`). So a real drive in that state produces DoorState("POSITION_UNKNOWN"), which is unequal to DoorStateUnknown and falls to the default arm everywhere. The two arms it could have reached both already return the same thing: closureStateFor's `case DoorStateUnknown: return nil` sits immediately above `default: return nil`, and Position() has no case for it and returns (zero, false) either way. The whole-repo usage set is three sites — the declaration, that one Matter case, a nolint comment — plus internal/model/custom/cover/matter_test.go:268, which drives a label no device can send and will therefore stay green whatever the constant says. A textbook bracketing test.

The write path cannot carry the wrong spelling either: command() writes string(c) where c is a DoorCommand, and the doorMode EnumSelect (garage.go:184-188) lists only CLOSED / VENTILATION_POSITION / OPEN, all correct.

It should still be corrected before something starts comparing it, and the fix is a one-token rename with no behavioural surface.

Two facts worth recording while the source is open, both of which I confirmed independently. (a) The physical byte for POSITION_UNKNOWN is 7 and for PARTIAL_OPEN is 8, but what the daemon sees is the ordinal into the value list (3 and 4), because the two-array StringEnumToInteger maps physical→label and DeviceUtil then maps label→position; so custom.EnumLabelValue's positional resolution is on the correct surface, and a client decoding the physical value directly would be wrong. (b) On a drive without the ventilation option the list is three long and PARTIAL_OPEN does not exist at all, so Vent() must stay gated on Capabilities.SupportsVent as it is. I also checked for an RF-side counterpart that would narrow the rule: there is none — DOOR_STATE and DOOR_COMMAND appear nowhere in src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}, so this is HmIP-only, and the descriptor corpus confirms the parameter pair exists on exactly two device types.

all.title: Garage SECTION motion codes 2 and 5 are bare literals
all.ourValue: SECTION == 2 means the door is opening; SECTION == 5 means it is closing
all.firmwareValue: SECTION is declared as an unlabelled 4-bit INTEGER, min 0, default 0, max 15, with no type converter and no value list; the only value the CCU gives meaning to is 15, which it reports as SECTION_STATUS=UNKNOWN instead of a SECTION value
all.missingInput: The garage drive's own section numbering — which travel phase each of the section values 0..14 denotes. It is device-firmware data; it is not carried by the CCU sources, by the shipped device type XMLs (SECTION is an HmIP parameter and has no rftypes declaration), by the HmIP StateParameter definition, or by the descriptor corpus.
all.citation: Tier 1 declaration: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#initialise registers ParameterMapKey("SECTION") through #createReadEvent4bitIntegerParameter, which builds StateParameter(identifier, LogicalType.INTEGER, PhysicalType.INTEGER, read+event IOOperations, null converter, 0, 0, 15) — a null type converter, so no StringEnumToInteger and therefore no VALUE_LIST is ever published for it (contrast #createReadEventEnumerationParameter, which is what ACTIVITY_STATE, DOOR_STATE and DOOR_COMMAND get). Tier 1 semantics: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler#handleProfileInformation takes the profile-information byte, publishes PROCESS from bit 7, ACTIVITY_STATE from bits 4-5 (masked & 3) when the channel has one, and SECTION from the low nibble (& 0xF); when that nibble is 15 it notifies SECTION_STATUS = StateParameterStatus.UNKNOWN and converts SECTION with null data, otherwise SECTION_STATUS = NORMAL and the raw nibble. That is the entire treatment of SECTION in the CCU — an opaque section number plus a 15 = unknown sentinel. ReGa/WebUI is silent too: the only SECTION strings anywhere under ../OpenCCU-Base/www are the three label rows in www/config/stringtable_de.txt:1690, :1692, :1693 (SECTION, SECTION_STATUS=NORMAL, SECTION_STATUS=UNKNOWN); no CCU code assigns a travel phase to any numeric value. Tier 2 agrees the field is unlabelled: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MOD-HO.json VCU3574044:1 and :2 VALUES SECTION {TYPE INTEGER, MIN 0, MAX 15, DEFAULT 0, VALUE_LIST None, OPERATIONS 5}, identical on HmIP-MOD-TM.json (VCU6166407:1, :2). Tier 3 witness, provenance only: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:438-442 — class GarageDoorActivity(IntEnum): CLOSING = 5; OPENING = 2, consumed at ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/cover.py:603-611. That is where our two literals came from; it is an independent implementation's conclusion, not the CCU's statement.
all.finding: The measurement the candidate asks for cannot be performed against any source in the witness hierarchy, and the honest answer is to say so rather than to promote the Python constant. The CCU deliberately models SECTION as an opaque profile-section index: the StateParameter is built with a null converter (so it publishes no VALUE_LIST at all, unlike every neighbouring enum on the same channel), and the frame handler forwards the low nibble untouched except for turning 15 into SECTION_STATUS=UNKNOWN. Nothing in rfd, hs485d, libhsscomm, ReGa, the WebUI, the OpenCCU patch set or the descriptor corpus says that 2 is the opening phase and 5 the closing one. Two collateral results are worth carrying back. First, the firmware's own motion indicator sits in bits 4-5 of the very same profile-information byte as ACTIVITY_STATE (UP/DOWN/STABLE, the same enum the cover path already resolves) — but HmIP-MOD-HO and HmIP-MOD-TM channel 1 do not declare ACTIVITY_STATE at all in the descriptor corpus (HmIP-DLP does), so there is no in-CCU substitute signal for these drives and SECTION is the only thing available. Second, the guard named in the bundle, TestGarageSectionReachesTheClusterServer, asserts through g.OnSection(sectionOpening) — the constant, not the number — so it is structurally incapable of detecting a wrong value; it is a bracketing test for this rule. Grounding these two literals needs a live drive: observe SECTION across a full open and a full close on a real HmIP-MOD-HO or HmIP-MOD-TM. That is a read-only observation and would settle it outright; until then the constants stay unverified and should be commented as an empirical mapping with no firmware authority behind them, not as a firmware fact.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU carried the mapping, it would have surfaced in one of two shapes the same extractions do produce elsewhere: a StringEnumToInteger value list on the SECTION StateParameter (which is exactly what the identical extraction returns for ACTIVITY_STATE, DOOR_STATE and DOOR_COMMAND in the same factory file), or labelled string-table rows of the form SECTION=<token> (which is what the same www grep returns for SECTION_STATUS=NORMAL and SECTION_STATUS=UNKNOWN). Both came back empty for SECTION's numeric values while both came back populated for their neighbours in the same run, so the check is tethered — it can distinguish a labelled parameter from an unlabelled one, and it says this one is unlabelled.

all.title: The WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE value list is a comment, not a source
all.site: internal/model/safety/classify.go:42-44 (waterStateActiveValues), consumed at :77-81 and narrowed by internal/model/safety/activation.go ActiveFromRaw
all.citation: Tier 2 (device XML the firmware ships): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_wds_v1_1.xml, channel index=1 type="WATERDETECTIONSENSOR", paramset VALUES id="wds_ch_values": `<parameter id="STATE" operations="read,event"><logical type="option"><option id="DRY" /><option id="WET"/><option id="WATER"/></logical>` with `<conversion type="option_integer"><value_map device_value="0" parameter_value="0"/><value_map device_value="100" parameter_value="1" mask="0x00"/><value_map device_value="200" parameter_value="2"/></conversion>`; identical in rf_wds_v1_0.xml (there DRY carries default="true"). Both files declare supported_types HM-Sec-WDS and HM-Sec-WDS-2. Tier 1 (operator-facing semantics): ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/stringtable_de.txt:2143 `WATERDETECTIONSENSOR|STATE=DRY`, :2144 `…=WATER`, :2165 `…=WET` — exactly three keys, no others; resolved at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:914-916 `"stringTableWDSStateDry":"Dry"`, `"stringTableWDSStateWater":"Water level detected"`, `"stringTableWDSStateWet":"Humidity detected"`.
all.ourValue: VALUE_LIST [DRY, WET, WATER]; active = {WET, WATER}
all.firmwareValue: VALUE_LIST [DRY, WET, WATER] in that order; DRY="Dry", WET="Humidity detected", WATER="Water level detected"
all.finding: Both the declared list and its order match our comment exactly, on both firmware revisions of the device (v1_0 and v1_1), and the CCU's own operator strings confirm the semantics: WET is moisture detected and WATER is a detected water level — both mean water present — while DRY (index 0) is the idle state. The active set {WET, WATER} is therefore right and complete. The wire values are 0/100/200 but the CCU's option_integer conversion maps them to parameter values 0/1/2 before XML-RPC, so ActiveFromRaw's index narrowing against the device's declared VALUE_LIST reads index 1 -> WET and index 2 -> WATER correctly. Worth noting for the comment: order is a per-parameter property, not a global one — the same device's MASTER parameters spell the same tokens in three different orders (MSG_FOR_POS_A [NO_MSG, DRY], MSG_FOR_POS_B [NO_MSG, DRY, WATER, WET], MSG_FOR_POS_C [NO_MSG, WATER, WET]), so the rule is safe only because ActiveFromRaw resolves the index against the device's own list rather than against this constant.
all.negativeControl: Had the list been e.g. [DRY, WET] or used different spellings, the `<logical type="option">` block in rf_wds_v1_0/v1_1.xml would have carried different or fewer `<option id=…>` tokens, and the stringtable would have carried a different set of `WATERDETECTIONSENSOR|STATE=` keys. I enumerated every such key in the tree: exactly DRY, WATER, WET and nothing else. Had WET meant something other than water present, translate.lang.stringtable.js would have given it a non-water label; it says "Humidity detected".
all.challengeNote: Upheld on the half the title names, and demoted on the half that actually fires an alarm. What I checked and confirms: the declared list and its order are identical on both shipped revisions of the device (v1_0 and v1_1) and in the runtime descriptor, and the CCU's own three operator strings carry the semantics the comment assumes. I also closed the gap the previous pass left open by assumption: it asserted "the CCU's option_integer conversion maps them to parameter values 0/1/2 before XML-RPC, so index narrowing reads index 1 -> WET" without citing where position-equals-value is written down. It is written down — HSSLogicalTypeOption::InitFromXml/GetDescription build VALUE_LIST positionally and pad sparse option indices with empty strings — so ActiveFromRaw's index narrowing against the device's own list is grounded, not conventional. Two corrections to the previous citation: (a) v1_0 declares only supported_type HM-Sec-WDS; only v1_1 declares HM-Sec-WDS and HM-Sec-WDS-2 (rf_wds_v1_0.xml:8-13 vs rf_wds_v1_1.xml:8-17), so "both files declare" is wrong; (b) nothing in the firmware classifies WET or WATER as an ALARM state. The CCU's alarm handling for this channel is per-installation link/program configuration; the only firmware statement about these values is what the labels mean. So {WET, WATER} = active is our product reading of two operator strings, correct and defensible but not a firmware fact, and the comment should not read as though the CCU declared an active set. Boundary: WATERDETECTIONSENSOR is declared in exactly two shipped device XMLs (rf_wds_v1_0.xml, rf_wds_v1_1.xml) and in one descriptor model; the rule is verified for HM-Sec-WDS / HM-Sec-WDS-2 only. The HmIP water sensor takes the separate WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER boolean path in the same table and is untouched by this.

all.title: The two ISE IDs that make a system variable invisible come from the Python reference, not from the CCU
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/bin/hm_autoconf:233-241 — `sv=dom.GetObject(40); dom.GetObject(ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES).Add(sv.ID()); sv.Name("${sysVarAlarmMessages}"); sv.DPInfo("${sysVarAlarmMessagesCount}"); sv.Internal(0);` and `sv=dom.GetObject(41); … sv.Name("${sysVarServiceMessages}"); sv.DPInfo("${sysVarServiceMessagesCount}"); sv.Internal(0);` (identical copy at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/bin/hm_autoconf:233-241). Label resolution: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/webui/js/lang/de/translate.lang.extension.js:298-301 `"sysVarAlarmMessages":"Alarmmeldungen"`, `"sysVarAlarmMessagesCount":"Anzahl Alarmmeldungen"`, `"sysVarServiceMessages":"Servicemeldungen"`, `"sysVarServiceMessagesCount":"Anzahl Servicemeldungen"`. Second, independent use of the same literals: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/bin/hm_autoconf:158 `create_sysvar_to_value_prg $ch_id SERVICE_COUNT 41 "Servicemeldungen anzeigen"` and :162 `create_sysvar_to_value_prg $ch_id ALARM_COUNT 40 "Alarmmeldungen anzeigen"`, whose body (:249-256) does `object sv=dom.GetObject(sv_id)`. Our fetch path's CCU-side implementation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/getall.tcl — `foreach(id, svList.EnumIDs())` with no ID filter, emitting `INTERNAL {sv.Internal()}` and `VISIBLE {sv.Visible()}` per variable (documented as `isInternal` / `isVisible`).
all.ourValue: IDs "40" and "41" are alarm-message / service-message pseudo-variables and must never enter the hub model
all.firmwareValue: ID 40 = the system variable named "Alarmmeldungen" (Anzahl Alarmmeldungen); ID 41 = "Servicemeldungen" (Anzahl Servicemeldungen) — and the CCU explicitly sets Internal(0) on both and Adds them to ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES
all.finding: The identity half of our rule is confirmed by the CCU's own auto-configuration: 40 and 41 are hard-coded literals (not named ID_ constants, and not CreateObject — the objects are pre-seeded in the ReGa DOM), and hm_autoconf names them exactly the alarm-message and service-message counters. Both copies in the tree are unconditional; nothing branches on hardware or firmware version, so within this tree the pairing is fixed. What is contradicted is the second half — that they are pseudo-variables the CCU hides. hm_autoconf sets `sv.Internal(0)` on both and adds them to the system-variable collection, i.e. the CCU deliberately publishes them as ordinary, non-internal system variables. And SysVar.getAll, the method our fetch path uses, applies no ID filter at all; it enumerates every ID and hands the caller a per-variable `isInternal` / `isVisible` flag. So the firmware's own mechanism for "do not treat this as an ordinary variable" is those two flags, not an ID list — and by that mechanism 40 and 41 are ordinary. Our exclusion is a product decision (the daemon surfaces them as dedicated hub singletons), not a firmware fact; the code comment should say so. Scope limit I could not settle: CCU2-era and pre-RaspberryMatic firmware is not in this tree, so "fixed across firmware versions and hardware" is verified only for the OCCU/OpenCCU line these two copies come from.
all.negativeControl: Had 40/41 been arbitrary or allocation-order-dependent, hm_autoconf would have had to look them up by name or create them — as it does for its siblings, which use named constants (ID_PRESENT, ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES, ID_PROGRAMS) or dom.CreateObject. It instead does dom.GetObject(40) / dom.GetObject(41) on pre-existing objects and then names them. Had the CCU regarded them as internal, the same lines would read `sv.Internal(1)`; they read `sv.Internal(0)`. Had SysVar.getAll filtered them out, our filter would be redundant rather than wrong — its script has no filter and I read it end to end.
all.challengeNote: Upheld as narrowed, with the previous pass's own framing corrected. Identity: confirmed verbatim and twice over — 40 and 41 are bare literals (no named ID_ constant, and reached with GetObject not CreateObject, so the objects are pre-seeded in the ReGa DOM), named by the CCU's own auto-configuration as the alarm-message and service-message counters. Mechanism: also confirmed — I searched the WebUI, ReGa pages, tcl and js trees for any special-casing of sysvar IDs 40/41 and found none, and SysVar.getAll applies no ID filter, so the firmware's only "do not treat this as ordinary" mechanism is the isInternal/isVisible pair, and by that mechanism 40/41 are ordinary. Three corrections to the previous pass. (1) It reports as "contradicted" a claim our comment does not make: sysvar.go:165-173 says the daemon surfaces these "through dedicated hub singletons instead of as ordinary system variables" and already attributes the ID list to the reference stack — it never says the CCU hides them. So the code is already honest; what is left to add is the positive statement that the CCU publishes them as non-internal. (2) `sv.Internal(0)` is inside `create_sysvars`, which hm_autoconf calls only when the sysvar collection is empty (:553-556) — it is the CCU's seeding intent at first setup, not a per-boot enforcement, so "the CCU explicitly sets Internal(0)" holds for a freshly configured CCU and is not re-asserted afterwards. (3) The two copies are not literally identical: `diff ../OpenCCU-Base/bin/hm_autoconf ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/bin/hm_autoconf` reports one whitespace-only difference at line 131; the 40/41 block is byte-identical. The comment's product rationale checks out on our side: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1182 is the single production caller of hub.IsExcludedSysvar, and internal/model/hub does carry dedicated AlarmMessages / ServiceMessages aggregates (NewAlarmMessagesWithCentral / NewServiceMessagesWithCentral), so nothing is silently dropped. Boundary, unchanged and real: CCU2-era and pre-RaspberryMatic firmware is not in this tree, so "fixed across firmware versions and hardware" is verified only for the OCCU/OpenCCU line these two copies come from.
