all.finding: Four points, three of them wrong. (1) Endpoint /config/cp_security.cgi — correct on the older stand; on the OCCU stand the OpenCCU distribution patches, the upload form already posts to /config/fileupload.ccc and passes the CGI back as `url=`, so the endpoint is version-dependent. (2) `@`-wrapping of the sid — CORRECT and required: the canonical session id literally contains the delimiters (session.tcl:464 `set sid "@$sid@"`), and the query parser only accepts an @-wrapped value (:312), so a bare sid is rejected. (3) The action value is wrong: the firmware verb is `backup_upload`; `restore_backup` does not appear anywhere in OpenCCU-Base or in the ~200 OpenCCU patches. Because the CGI dispatches by string concatenation (`action_$action`, :1601) an unknown action raises a Tcl "invalid command name action_restore_backup" rather than a clean error. (4) The file field is wrong: the firmware reads `import_file -client backup_file`, i.e. the field must be named `backup_file`, not `file`. Two further contract facts our code does not model: the CGI requires user level 8 (`session_requestisvalid 8`), and upload is only step one of three — `backup_upload` merely stores /tmp/new_config.tar; `backup_restore_check` validates the archive signature and `backup_restore_go` performs the restore and needs the system security key. So even with the field and action fixed, a single POST would upload and never restore, which is exactly the silent-acceptance failure the candidate feared. Sending `action` in both the query and the body is not itself fatal (cgi_input merges both), but it is redundant — the firmware sends it once, as a POST field on the older stand and as a query parameter on the newer one.
all.negativeControl: Had `restore_backup` and `file` been the firmware's names, a tree-wide grep for those literals would have hit in cp_security.cgi or in the patch set. It returns nothing for `restore_backup` anywhere, while `backup_upload` hits at cp_security.cgi:1027 and :1510 and in 0007/0163 of the patch set, and `backup_file` hits at :1027 and :1515. Had the sid needed to be bare, session.tcl:312's regexp would not require the @ delimiters and :464 would not add them.
all.challengeNote: Upheld as contradicted; every cited line verifies verbatim, and I re-ran the decisive negative search myself. `restore_backup` appears exactly once anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base plus ../OpenCCU, in an unrelated file — the recovery-system's own upload form (../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/package/recovery-system/external/package/hm-platform/rootfs-overlay/www/index.cgi:74, `action="cgi-bin/restore_backup.cgi"`), which is the separate recovery boot mode, not the CCU's config CGI our restorer posts to. So: the action verb is wrong (firmware: `backup_upload`), the multipart field name is wrong (firmware: `backup_file`, read by `import_file -client backup_file`), and the endpoint is stand-dependent (cp_security.cgi on the OpenCCU-Base stand, /config/fileupload.ccc on the newer OCCU stand the distribution patches — fileupload.ccc does not exist in OpenCCU-Base, so the newer stand's receiver cannot be read here). The one point our code has right is the `@`-wrapping: the canonical sid literally contains the delimiters and the query parser only accepts an @-wrapped value. Two claims in the previous pass I could NOT confirm and am demoting to inference: (a) "the CGI requires user level 8" — `session_requestisvalid` has no definition anywhere in either tree, only call sites, whose arguments are 0 and 8; the literal is there, the meaning of 8 is not read from any source; (b) "an unknown action raises a Tcl 'invalid command name' rather than a clean error", and by extension that the CCU answers HTTP 200 — `cgi_eval` is likewise not defined in this tree, so the status code an undefined `action_*` produces cannot be established here. What IS readable and sufficient: no `action_restore_backup` proc exists, so the upload is never processed. Additional defect on the same surface that the previous pass did not name: the doc comment at backup_restorer.go:36-39 ("The CCU runs the restore asynchronously and reboots when done; the HTTP response only confirms that the upload was accepted") is false in a second way — even a correctly-formed backup_upload only writes /tmp/new_config.tar; the restore requires backup_restore_check and then backup_restore_go with the system security key, neither of which our code sends.

all.title: The ENUM label fallback assumes the VALUE_LIST position equals the easymode option ordinal
all.site: internal/central/adapter/valuelabels.go:38-53 (ValueListLabel, step 2), reached from internal/central/adapter/uischema_adapter.go:754-765 (valueList) and from ValueListLabels/MqttParameterLabelAdapter
all.citation: Tier 1, what the N actually is: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/options.tcl:18-62 — the option arrays are keyed by the parameter's RAW value, not by a position: the "DELAY" case is `set options(0) …; set options(5) "5$s"; set options(10) "10$s"; set options(30); set options(60); set options(120); set options(300); set options(600); set options(1800); set options(3600); set options(99999999) "${enterValue}"`. Contiguous ENUM cases in the same file (TIMEBASE_SHORT 0..3, TIMEBASE_LONG 0..7) and in ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl:5872-5915 (ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SIGNAL 0..9, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_TIMING 0..3, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_TRIGGER 0..3) are contiguous only because those parameters' values are. Tier 1, the numeric keys are parameter-scoped, not global: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/stringtable_de.txt:153-158 pairs `ANALOG_INPUT_TRANSMITTER|VOLTAGE_STATUS=NORMAL`/`=0`, `=OVERFLOW`/`=2`, `=UNDERFLOW`/`=3` (no `=1`), while :798-803 pairs `ENERGIE_METER_TRANSMITTER|POWER_STATUS=NORMAL`/`=0`, `=UNKNOWN`/`=1`, `=OVERFLOW`/`=2`. Tier 2 cross-check of one concrete case: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-BROLL.json, channel VCU8537918:3 (SHUTTER_TRANSMITTER) VALUES LEVEL_STATUS TYPE=ENUM VALUE_LIST [NORMAL, UNKNOWN, OVERFLOW, UNDERFLOW, ERROR] — matches stringtable_de.txt:220-228 `BLIND_TRANSMITTER|LEVEL_STATUS=0..4` = Normal/Unknown/Overflow/Underflow/Error one-for-one.
all.ourValue: the key `<parameter>=<N>` names the token at index N of the descriptor's VALUE_LIST
all.firmwareValue: `options(N)` keys the parameter's raw value under a channel-qualified key; equal to the VALUE_LIST index only for an ENUM whose option list was authored against that same list. The DELAY list is keyed 0,5,10,30,60,120,300,600,1800,3600,99999999.
all.finding: The narrow claim holds: for an ENUM parameter, under its own `<channelType>|<parameter>=N` key, N is the raw value and therefore the VALUE_LIST index — the BLIND_TRANSMITTER/LEVEL_STATUS case above matches on all five entries. One step wider it is false, in two ways, and the boundary runs at the key that answers the lookup. (a) The same digit under a different parameter's key means something else: `voltage_status=1` is Uberlauf while `analog_input_transmitter|voltage_status=2` is Uberlauf, so a bare `<param>=N` hit is not the channel-qualified answer, and INTEGER parameters (DELAY, the ON_TIME_LIST_* families) contribute raw-value keys into the same flat namespace. (b) More seriously, our index probe does not consult the channel-qualified key alone: it calls the full ParameterValue chain (internal/ccudata/translations.go:365-405), whose stage 2 is a bare `<param>=N` lookup and whose stage 4 is a VALUE-ONLY reverse index (valueIndexLookup :428, built by buildValueIndices :448, keeping the shortest label per value across all parameters). Feeding that chain a bare digit means it essentially always hits stage 4. Measured against the shipped archive (go-openccu-data v0.1.3 translation_extract.json.gz plus the curated translation_custom overlay, exactly as LoadTranslationsEmbedded assembles it), the de digits resolve to: 0 'aus' (long_dim_step=0), 1 'Ja' (output_swap=1), 2 'Ein' (adaptive_regulation=2), 3 'RGB', 4 'RGBW' (dali_dt8_config_number_primary_colors), 5 'Tage' (interval_unit=5), 6 'HSV', 7 'TW', 8 'TW/RGB', 9 'Ver-/Entriegeln'. Replaying the chain over the whole pydevccu descriptor corpus, 214 distinct (channel type, parameter, index) triples in VALUES ENUM paramsets take that path and get a foreign label — e.g. HmIP-ESI ENERGIE_METER_TRANSMITTER.CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE=SENSOR_ES_IEC -> 'RGB', HmIP-MP3P MAINTENANCE.ERROR_CODE_STATUS=ERROR_FILE -> 'RGB', HmIP-HDM1 SHADING_RECEIVER.LEVEL_STATUS=UNUSED -> 'HSV', HmIP-DRG-DALI MAINTENANCE.ERROR_DALI_BUS=BUS_OK -> 'aus'. Without the curated overlay the same replay yields 630 triples (e.g. DIMMER.DIRECTION=UNDEFINED -> 'RGB' on 52 models), so the overlay is currently masking most of it by hand. The wrong label appears identically on the UI schema, the REST data-point views and MQTT discovery, as the file's own doc comment says it would. Separately, ValueListLabel's contract that it "never returns the empty string for a non-empty value" does not hold: the curated overlay carries `direction=none` -> "", which is != the value and is returned as-is. The firmware-grounded fix is to scope the index probe to the channel-qualified key (and at most the bare-parameter key), never to the value-only index.
all.negativeControl: Two directions. If N were a display position rather than the raw value, options.tcl's DELAY case would be keyed 0..10 rather than 0,5,10,30,…,99999999 — it is the latter. If our index probe were scoped to the parameter, feeding it the string "3" would find no key for the 214 measured cases and ValueListLabel would fall through to humanizeRaw ("Effect 02 End Current Profile"); the replay instead returns 'RGB', and the same replay returns the correct label for every case where the channel-qualified `=<token>` key exists, so the check does distinguish the two hypotheses.
all.challengeNote: Upheld as narrowed, strengthened on the firmware side and re-measured on ours. The narrow claim now has a Tier-1 grounding rather than a coincidence: HSSLogicalTypeOption pads sparse option indices with empty strings and emits VALUE_LIST positionally with MAX = size-1, so for a BidCos ENUM the list position IS the integer value — the previous pass asserted this from the stringtable/descriptor agreement alone, which is the kind of inference this audit exists to catch. Everything one step wider stays false, and I reproduced the concrete failure independently rather than taking it on report. Loading the shipped archive exactly as LoadTranslationsEmbedded assembles it (go-openccu-data v0.1.3 translation_extract.json.gz plus translation_custom/parameter_values_de.json) and replaying buildValueIndices, the de digits resolve to: 0 'aus' (long_dim_step=0), 1 'Ja', 2 'Ein', 3 'RGB', 4 'RGBW', 5 'Tage', 6 'HSV', 7 'TW', 8 'TW/RGB', 9 'Ver-/Entriegeln' — identical to the previous pass's table, and identical with and without the curated overlay (the overlay changes how many triples fall through to stage 4, not which label a bare digit wins). Since ValueListLabel's step 2 hands a bare decimal string into the full ParameterValue chain, any index not covered by a channel-qualified or bare-parameter key lands on stage 4 and is answered with a foreign label. I did NOT re-run the corpus replay, so the counts "214 triples with the overlay, 630 without" and the named examples (HmIP-ESI CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE, HmIP-MP3P ERROR_CODE_STATUS, HmIP-HDM1 LEVEL_STATUS, HmIP-DRG-DALI ERROR_DALI_BUS) remain the previous pass's measurement, unverified here; the mechanism that produces them is confirmed. Also confirmed independently: translation_custom/parameter_values_de.json carries `"direction=none": ""`, which stage 2 returns because "" != "none" — so the file's contract that ValueListLabel "never returns the empty string for a non-empty value" is false, and via stage 2, not stage 4. One new Tier1/Tier2 disagreement worth recording, because it decides which source our code should follow: rf_rhs.xml declares `<parameter id="ERROR" …><option id="NO_ERROR" index="0" default="true"/><option id="SABOTAGE" index="7"/>` (../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_rhs.xml:188-198, byte-identical in ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/rf_rhs.xml), which by HSSLogicalTypeOption yields an 8-entry VALUE_LIST with six empty strings and MAX=7 — while the descriptor fixture ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-Sec-RHS.json VCU0000216:1 carries VALUE_LIST [NO_ERROR, SABOTAGE] with MAX=1. Our code should follow Tier 1 (position = wire value, holes possible); any check that rests on the pydevccu list lengths is measuring the fixture. Scope: all of this is the BidCos path through libhsscomm. Sparse option indices occur in 18 shipped declarations, every one of them named ERROR (indices (0,3) on the dimmer family, (0,7) on the shutter-contact / motion / RHS / EM8 family) — so no ENUM our label chain shows the operator today is sparse, but the padding rule is what makes that safe rather than luck. The HmIP path does not go through libhsscomm and is not settled by this citation.

all.title: The ERROR/SENSOR_ERROR and SEQUENCE_OK suppression sets decide whether a data point exists at all
all.citation: Tier 1, the firmware's own criterion: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:63-70 — `FLG_NONE=0, FLG_VISIBLE=(1<<0), FLG_INTERNAL=(1<<1), FLG_TRANSFORM=(1<<2), FLG_SERVICE=(1<<3), //!< Dieser Parameter soll von der Oberflaeche als Servicenachricht behandelt werden, FLG_STICKY=(1<<4)`, documented there as the values of the FLAGS field in the XML-RPC parameter description. Set from the descriptor at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:75-83 `temp=node.getAttribute("ui_flags"); … if(strstr(temp, "service"))flags |= FLG_SERVICE;` and acted on at :318, :354, :377 `if(flags&FLG_SERVICE)inst->ReportServiceMessage(id, val);`. Allowed spellings: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/device.xsd, simpleType Paramset.Parameter.UIFlagsAttribute = {service, "service,sticky", internal, transform, invisible}. Tier 2 enumeration over ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml: every distinct ERROR* parameter id — ERROR, ERROR_ALARM_TEST, ERROR_BATTERY, ERROR_M1/M2/M3, ERROR_OVERHEAT (17 files), ERROR_OVERLOAD (10), ERROR_POWER, ERROR_REDUCED (17), ERROR_SABOTAGE, ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER — is declared operations="read,event" and carries ui_flags="service", except one ERROR with ui_flags="internal" (rf_resc_win_pcb_sc.xml) and a second channel variant in rf_sec_sfa.xml where ERROR_POWER/ERROR_SABOTAGE/ERROR_BATTERY are declared with no ui_flags at all. SENSOR_ERROR* is declared in none of those XMLs; on the HmIP side it exists — ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/{HmIP-SAM,HmIP-ESI,ELV-SH-TACO}.json VALUES SENSOR_ERROR TYPE=BOOL OPERATIONS=5 FLAGS=9, i.e. VISIBLE|SERVICE. SEQUENCE_OK: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_sen_ep.xml declares it once — `operations="write,event" loopback="true" control="EVENT_INTERFACE.TRIGGER"` with `<logical type="action"/>`; descriptor side ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/{HM-Sen-EP,HM-Sen-X}.json VALUES SEQUENCE_OK TYPE=ACTION OPERATIONS=6 FLAGS=1.
all.ourValue: suppress by name: strings.HasPrefix(parameter, "ERROR") || strings.HasPrefix(parameter, "SENSOR_ERROR"); ImpulseEvents = {SEQUENCE_OK}
all.firmwareValue: suppress by flag: FLAGS & FLG_SERVICE (bit 3, 0x08), declared as ui_flags="service" and delivered on the wire in the parameter description; the C++ routes exactly those parameters to ReportServiceMessage instead of ordinary value handling
all.finding: Both sets are right about the outcome and wrong about the authority. The CCU does have a first-class notion of "this parameter is a service message, not readable state", and it is FLG_SERVICE — a per-parameter flag the device XML declares as ui_flags="service", which HSSParameter.cpp turns into a bit in the FLAGS field of the parameter description and then uses to route the value to ReportServiceMessage. It is not a name prefix; the C++ never inspects the parameter id. Measured over the shipped RF and wired device XMLs, every ERROR* parameter is in fact flagged service (or internal), so our prefix agrees with the firmware on every model in the corpus — the rule is true in our scope. It is false one step wider, in both directions: a parameter can be service-flagged without starting with ERROR (UNREACH, STICKY_UNREACH, CONFIG_PENDING, LOWBAT all carry ui_flags="service" and we deliberately do surface them), and an ERROR-prefixed parameter can be declared without the flag — rf_sec_sfa.xml has a channel variant declaring ERROR_POWER/ERROR_SABOTAGE/ERROR_BATTERY with no ui_flags, which the firmware would treat as ordinary state and which our prefix suppresses anyway. The comment's own record that four lock-family devices needed an un-ignore exception is the same boundary showing up from the other side. Note the input is already available to us: pkg/hmproto/parameter.go:96 exposes IsService() over hmenum.FlagService — the value the source carries is being substituted by a convention. On SENSOR_ERROR: it is absent from every BidCos device XML, so that half of the prefix pair matches nothing on the wired/RF side; it exists only on the HmIP side (4 models), where the CCU declares FLAGS=9 = VISIBLE|SERVICE, i.e. the firmware does classify it as a service message. On SEQUENCE_OK: confirmed, and the strongest of the three. It is declared exactly once, as an ACTION with operations="write,event" (no read), loopback="true", control="EVENT_INTERFACE.TRIGGER", FLAGS=1 — it carries no state semantics at all, so treating it as an impulse event rather than a data point matches the descriptor.
all.negativeControl: If the firmware classified by name, HSSParameter.cpp would test the parameter id somewhere on the path to ReportServiceMessage; the only gate at :318/:354/:377 is `flags & FLG_SERVICE`, and the only writer of that bit is the ui_flags parse at :81. If SENSOR_ERROR carried ordinary state semantics its four HmIP declarations would have FLAGS=1 (VISIBLE) rather than 9 (VISIBLE|SERVICE) — I read the FLAGS value of each. If SEQUENCE_OK had state semantics its declaration would carry OP_READ (operations would include "read", OPERATIONS bit 1); it is write,event only on both the XML and the descriptor side.
all.challengeNote: Upheld as narrowed, with the boundary drawn considerably wider than the previous pass drew it. Every firmware citation verifies verbatim, including the FLG_SERVICE comment text and the three ReportServiceMessage call sites, and the point stands: the CCU's notion of "service message, not readable state" is a per-parameter flag, never a name prefix, and the value is already parsed on our side (hmproto IsService over hmenum.FlagService = 8) — so this is a case of a convention standing in for a field we hold. Two corrections to the previous enumeration. (1) The un-flagged ERROR* declarations are in TWO files, not one: rf_sec_sfa.xml (three ids) and rf_sec_sir_wm.xml (ERROR_SABOTAGE, twice, at :343 and :580). (2) The claim "a parameter can be service-flagged without starting with ERROR" is far larger than the four ids named. Counting every service-flagged declaration across the shipped RF and wired XMLs: UNREACH 138, CONFIG_PENDING 138, STICKY_UNREACH 137, LOWBAT 90, DEVICE_IN_BOOTLOADER 73, UPDATE_PENDING 73, DUTYCYCLE 59, ERROR 22, ERROR_REDUCED 18, ERROR_OVERHEAT 18, ERROR_OVERLOAD 10, FAULT_REPORTING 4, ERROR_M1/M2/M3 2 each, ERROR_BATTERY 2, ERROR_SABOTAGE 2, STICKY_SABOTAGE 2, ERROR_ALARM_TEST 1, ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER 1, ERROR_POWER 1, STICKY_POWER 1, STICKY_BATTERY 1 — plus a whole ERR_* family our prefix does not match at all (ERR_WINDOW_NOT_FOUND, ERR_DETECT_EIA485_SERVICE, ERR_TTM_INTERNAL/OVERVOLT/UNDERVOLT and their STICKY_ twins, sixteen ERR_TTCU_* ids, ERR_FREE_TO_USE_2, FREE_TO_USE, ERR_WIN_STAY_IN_INITIAL_OPERATION). So `HasPrefix("ERROR")` agrees with the firmware on every ERROR-named parameter in the corpus except six declarations across two files, and disagrees on roughly 700 service-flagged declarations under other names. Also confirmed: the previous pass's count of ERROR_OVERHEAT / ERROR_REDUCED as "17 files" is 18 declarations each in my count, and its SENSOR_ERROR model list is missing HmIP-STV (four descriptor models, not three). The surface caveat that keeps this at narrowed rather than contradicted: FLG_SERVICE answers "the operator surface should treat this as a service message", which is the WebUI's routing question — the firmware says nothing about whether a bridge should mint a data point. Adopting IsService() wholesale as the suppression rule would drop UNREACH, STICKY_UNREACH, CONFIG_PENDING, LOWBAT, DUTYCYCLE, UPDATE_PENDING and DEVICE_IN_BOOTLOADER, all of which we deliberately surface; so the flag is the right authority for classification and not, by itself, the right rule for our decision. SENSOR_ERROR: confirmed absent from every shipped BidCos XML, so that half of the prefix pair matches nothing on the RF/wired side and exists only on the HmIP side, where the CCU does classify it as a service message (FLAGS=9). SEQUENCE_OK: confirmed and the strongest of the three — declared exactly once, ACTION, write+event with no read, loopback, control=EVENT_INTERFACE.TRIGGER, FLAGS=1, i.e. no state semantics, so treating it as an impulse event matches the descriptor. One process note: my first greps for SEQUENCE_OK under src/devicetypes returned nothing because the device XMLs are ISO-8859-1 and grep treated them as binary — the previous pass's citation is correct, and I re-read the file with an explicit encoding before concluding anything.

all.title: ASTRO_TYPE wire value 1 = sunset is a bare literal
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1104-1121 (_getAstroType); labels ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/MASTER_LANG/HmIPWeeklyDeviceProgram.js:45-46 and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.option.js:141-142; editor entry point ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:4,64-66
all.ourValue: 0 = sunrise, 1 = sunset
all.firmwareValue: 0 = optionSunrise (Sonnenaufgang / Sunrise), 1 = optionSunset (Sonnenuntergang / Sunset)
all.finding: The CCU's own week-program editor settles this on the same surface our code is on — the `<NN>_WP_ASTRO_TYPE` field of the HmIP week-profile MASTER paramset. `_getAstroType` builds `var arOptions = [translateKey("optionSunrise"), translateKey("optionSunset")];`, reads `var sel = parseInt(this.ps[number + "_WP_ASTRO_TYPE"]);`, and emits `"<option value='" + loop + "' " + selected + ">" + arOptions[loop]` with `selected = (sel == loop)`. The loop index is written into the form field verbatim AND compared against the paramset value, so the index is the wire value — this is read from the source, not inferred from array order. optionSunrise = "Sonnenaufgang"/"Sunrise", optionSunset = "Sonnenuntergang"/"Sunset". Our read site (astroTypeWire == 1 -> AstroSunset) and our independently-stated write site (AstroSunset -> astroID = 1) both match. Note this is the HmIP simple-schedule editor, the same paramset shape our rawconvert.go parses (`<NN>_WP_*`), not the climate `P<n>_*` schema — the right surface.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been inverted, arOptions[0] would be translateKey("optionSunset"), or the loop would emit a `value` other than its own index (e.g. a lookup table). Both are visible in the same 18 lines, so the check discriminates.
all.challengeNote: Upheld, and the one gap the previous grounding left open is now closed. What I checked. (1) The quote is exact — note the file is ISO-8859, so plain grep reports it as binary; with grep -a, HmIPWeeklyProgram.js:1104-1121 contains arOptions = [translateKey("optionSunrise"), translateKey("optionSunset")], sel = parseInt(this.ps[number + "_WP_ASTRO_TYPE"]), and <option value='loop'> with selected = (sel == loop). `number` is addLeadingZero()'d, so the field is <NN>_WP_ASTRO_TYPE — the same MASTER shape rawconvert.go parses with prefix %02d_WP_. Right surface. (2) The previous grounding rested the ordinal on the editor's round-trip alone, which is one step short of the rule this project keeps enforcing: index-equals-value was still being read off an array. It is now read from the source. WP_ASTRO_TYPE_ENUM is WeekProgramAstroType.getNames(); createAstroTypeParameter passes it to the SINGLE-argument StringEnumToInteger constructor — no explicit enumValues array, offset 0 — and convertLogicalToPhysical writes b[0] = (byte)(i + offset), convertPhysicalToLogical returns enumStrings[physical]. The firmware states the ordinal; it is not inferred. (3) The link from that ordinal to what we see on the wire: DeviceUtil fills VALUE_LIST from the very same getEnumStrings() array and, when Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal is set, replaces an outgoing ENUM string with its index in that array and maps an incoming number back through values[n]. The shipped CCU config turns it on (crRFD.conf:47 Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true); the Java default is false. (4) Tier 2 agrees across 20+ HmIP descriptors. Both our sites match. One robustness defect I found while verifying, not a grounding defect: rawconvert.go:910 toInt() returns 0 for a non-numeric string and carries no int32/int64 case. Were that service property ever off, ASTRO_TYPE would arrive as "SUNSET" and read silently as sunrise. mapToProfileKey in the same subsystem does handle int32/int64; toInt does not.

all.title: The RF profile pointer is read as 0-based only when it arrives as a string
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:72-94 (EnforceConstraints), :96-112 (GetDescription), :115-118 (GetDefault); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:381-401; HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createActiveProfileParameter; Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU.json and HM-CC-VG-1.json (WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER), HmIP-BWTH.json / HmIP-eTRV-B1.json (ACTIVE_PROFILE)
all.ourValue: wire Go type is the discriminator: `case string` -> RF, 0-based, accepts 0..5; `case int/int32/int64/float64` -> IP, 1-based, accepts 1..6
all.firmwareValue: WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER is TYPE=ENUM, MIN=0, MAX=2, DEFAULT=0, VALUE_LIST=["WEEK PROGRAM 1","WEEK PROGRAM 2","WEEK PROGRAM 3"], in the MASTER paramset (physical `interface="config" list="7" index="16"`), OPERATIONS=3 (READ|WRITE, no EVENT). The CCU normalises it to an INTEGER index in both directions. ACTIVE_PROFILE is LogicalType.INTEGER, default 1, min 1, max 3 or 6 (converter IntegerToInteger(1.0,-1.0)), in VALUES.
all.finding: Two halves, one confirmed and one contradicted. (a) 0-based for RF is CORRECT: rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:382-393 documents `<ol start="0">` with `WEEK PROGRAM 1` first, and `<logical type="option">` lists the three options in that order; HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDescription sets `MIN=int(0)`, `MAX=int(options.size()-1)` and `VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i]`, so the VALUE_LIST index IS the wire value. 1-based for ACTIVE_PROFILE is also correct (min 1, default 1). (b) The TYPE discriminator is WRONG. For an option-typed parameter the CCU returns an int: `GetDefault()` returns `(int&)default_option`, and `EnforceConstraints` (:78-91) takes any incoming string, matches it against the option labels and REPLACES it with `*val=(int)i`, falling back to `atoi(s_val.c_str())` otherwise. So WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER never reaches us as a numeric string; it reaches us as an int and hits our 1-based branch, mapping firmware 0 -> nothing, 1 -> P1 (should be P2), 2 -> P2 (should be P3). Two further mismatches: our string branch accepts 0..5 where the firmware declares MAX=2 (three programs on both devices that carry the parameter), and the parameter is MASTER/no-EVENT, so `Channel.Parameter` (internal/model/device/channel.go:392-396, VALUES-only) returns nil and `subscribeProfilePointer` never installs the subscription at all — the defect is latent, not live, which is why no round-trip has caught it. The separate climate path (internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:1936, resolveWeekProgramPointer + toInt + MasterParameter walk) is correct and matches the firmware.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU exposed the RF pointer as a string, HSSLogicalTypeOption::GetDefault would return a std::string and EnforceConstraints would leave the string form intact rather than overwriting it with `(int)i`; and the descriptor TYPE would be STRING rather than ENUM with a VALUE_LIST. Both checks read differently in that world.
all.challengeNote: Contradiction upheld and strengthened; one sub-claim narrowed. What I checked. (a) The 0-based half is right and the source carries the ordinal explicitly: InitFromXml stores options[index]=id (honouring an explicit index= attribute when present, sequential otherwise — WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER declares none), and GetDescription sets MIN=int(0), MAX=int(options.size()-1), VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i]. rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:381-401 is verbatim as cited, including <ol start="0"> and <physical type="integer" interface="config" list="7" index="16" size="1.0"/>. (b) The type discriminator is contradicted, and I closed a hole in the previous citation. EnforceConstraints alone does not say which direction it runs; HSSParameter::GetValue:220-249 does — the read path goes physical_type->Get, PhysicalToLogical, then EnforceConstraints(inst, &log_temp, OP_READ). Physical type is integer, so log_temp enters the TypeInt branch, which only clamps. The value handed to getParamset is TypeInt. There is no read path on which the CCU emits this parameter as a numeric string, so our `case string` branch is unreachable and an RF pointer would take the 1-based branch: firmware 0 -> nothing, 1 -> P1 (should be P2), 2 -> P2 (should be P3). The 0..5 acceptance range also exceeds the declared MAX=2. (c) Latency confirmed independently: subscribeProfilePointer (week_profile_filter.go:538, reached only from :455) is the sole production caller of SyncProfilePointer, and it resolves DPs through Channel.Parameter, which reads c.valuePoints — VALUES only (channel.go:392-396). Tier 2 shows WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER in MASTER only with OPERATIONS=3 on both carrying devices, so the DP is never found and the branch never executes. (d) The ACTIVE_PROFILE citation is verbatim: IntegerToInteger(1.0, -1.0), min 1, max 3 for subtype "default" and 6 for "wth2". (e) New: the ORIGIN of the wrong rule is a Tier-3 witness read as fact. aiohomematic week_profile_data_point.py:512 and :539 carry exactly the comments 'RF: WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER is str ("0", "1", ...)'. That is a Python implementation's reading, ported into our code as a wire fact. Tier inflation at source. NARROWING of the previous finding: its blanket 'it reaches us as an int' is proven only for the rfd/BidCos path. HM-CC-VG-1 is a virtual heating group served by HMServer (address INT0000001), and its descriptor declares MIN/MAX/DEFAULT as the STRINGS "0"/"2"/"0" where HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU declares ints — a different description path. WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER does not occur anywhere in the HMServer tree I could read, so whether that virtual-group path returns a string VALUE is unverified. It does not change the verdict (still MASTER-only, still unreachable through Channel.Parameter), but the claim should be scoped to rfd.

Our "valve" bucket strips ramp_time (schedules.go:719), so a SERVO schedule round-trips without its travel time. WATER_SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:20 passes 'switch' where we say "valve" — no consequence, both buckets strip the same fields. SHADING_WEEK_PROFILE does not exist in this firmware at all (HmIP-HDM1/HDM2 absent); it is a Tier-2-only type, so its "cover" bucket is not firmware-grounded. Lock precedence is confirmed on a different discriminator: the firmware also refuses to decide from the channel type — SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:21,47 passes 'switch' for an HmIP-DLD, and the JS then branches on DEVICE TYPE (`isDoorLockDrive` :317 for HmIP-DLD/-A/-S, `isDLP` :285 for HmIP-DLP) to render the lock pickers (:1899-2014). Our "any DOOR_LOCK*/KEYMATIC channel wins" is a different but same-axis rule; note the firmware treats DLD and DLP as two distinct encodings, where we have one "lock" bucket. On climateScheduleChannelTypes: a sweep of src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types} finds only five XMLs with a weekly climate profile. rf_cc_rt_dn(.bom) put bare ENDTIME_/TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_<N> (182 params) in the DEVICE master `cc_rt_dev_master`, rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu puts P1_..P3_ prefixed ones (546) in `tc_it_dev_master` — never on the CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER channel, so that entry's stated justification is wrong (harmless: Path 2 probes the paramset and Path 3 catches the device root). rf_cc_tc(.le_v1_9) DO put a profile on the CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR channel's MASTER `cc_tc_ch_master`, but named TIMEOUT_/TEMPERATUR_ — neither matches slotPattern's (ENDTIME|TEMPERATURE), so that candidate can never resolve. all.negativeControl: Had SERVO belonged to the firmware's switch family, SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl would pass 'switch' and chnType SERVO would be absent from the ramp-time branch at JS:687 and the level branch at :695/:708 — the same two greps return the opposite result. all.challengeNote: Most of the contradiction survives and I strengthened it; but one of its sub-claims is itself refuted and one is softer than stated, so the finding is narrowed. UPHELD, with new Tier-1 support the previous grounding did not have. Every family argument is verbatim as cited (I re-read all seven easymode .tcl files). SERVO_WEEK_PROFILE.tcl:18 passes 'dimmer'; hmipWeeklyProgramDevice.tcl:33-35 dereferences psDescr(01_WP_RAMP_TIME_FACTOR) for exactly that family, a tcl array read that errors if the key is absent — so the firmware asserts a SERVO week-profile MASTER carries WP_RAMP_TIME_FACTOR, on the same paramset our rawconvert parses. Independently, DeviceUtil handles SERVO_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER exactly as DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (RAMP_TIME, ON_TIME, LEVEL) while grouping WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER with SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER on ON_TIME + STATE. So SERVO belongs in a ramp-carrying bucket and our 'valve' bucket strips ramp_time (schedules.go:719); WATER_SWITCH is 'switch', with no field consequence (both buckets strip exactly {level_2, ramp_time}). REFUTED sub-claim: 'SHADING_WEEK_PROFILE does not exist in this firmware at all ... it is a Tier-2-only type, so its cover bucket is not firmware-grounded.' It is Tier 1. ChannelType declares SHADING_RECEIVER(74) and SHADING_WEEK_PROFILE(75), and ShadingCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory builds its parameter set as fillBasicAstroParameter + WP_LEVEL + WP_LEVEL_2 — byte-for-byte the same shape as BlindCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory, and with no WP_RAMP_TIME_* or WP_DURATION_* (which DimmerCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory does add). Tier 2 agrees: HmIP-HDM1 VCU3560967:2 and HmIP-HDM2 VCU1111390:2 MASTER carry exactly WP_{WEEKDAY,CONDITION,FIXED_HOUR,FIXED_MINUTE,ASTRO_TYPE,ASTRO_OFFSET,TARGET_CHANNELS,LEVEL,LEVEL_2}. Our 'cover' bucket (strip ramp_time + duration, keep level_2) is therefore exactly the declared field set — grounded, not a guess. Also, the finding's 'the firmware's own set is exactly seven' is the WEBUI's set: an exhaustive grep over OpenCCU-Base returns those seven, but the HmIP server's ChannelType enum carries eight (SHADING has no easymode shipped). SOFTENED sub-claim: the SERVO round-trip consequence. all.title: The CCU mirror sysvar's German ENUM labels and their order rest on a "CCU convention" comment with no cited source
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createenum.tcl (SysVar.createEnum ReGa body); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:838-844 (istEnum branch), :813-821 (istAlarm branch), :462-465 (type classification); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/de/translate.lang.extension.js:290-291 (sysVarAlarmZone1), :608-610 (iconProtection*); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.extension.js:608-610; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/webui/js/dialog/statusdisplaydialogacousticepaper.js:35-37
all.ourValue: a 7-member ENUM sysvar [Unscharf, Hüllschutz, Vollschutz, Nachtschutz, Urlaub, Benutzerdefiniert, Alarm], index 0..6, presented as "the CCU convention so existing programs read naturally"
all.firmwareValue: The CCU defines no canonical alarm-state value list. Its built-in alarm variable is a different TYPE: ivtBinary + istAlarm, two states (ValueName0/ValueName1, AlType(atSystem), AlArm(true)), shipped as "Alarmzone 1". Of our seven labels only three occur anywhere in the firmware, and only as e-paper status-display icon names: iconProtectionOff="Unscharf", iconProtectionExternal="Hüllschutz", iconProtectionInternal="Vollschutz" (EN: "Protection deactivated" / "Presence mode" / "Absence mode").
all.finding: Two things the firmware DOES settle, and one it does not. Settled: the enum mechanism our CreateSysvarEnum uses is exactly right — SysVar.createEnum's ReGa body does `sv.ValueType( ivtInteger ); sv.ValueSubType( istEnum ); sv.ValueList( valList ); sv.State(0);` with valList documented as `Enum "Wert1;Wert2;Wert3;...."`, matching system.fn:838-844, so position in the list is the 0-based index and index 0 is the initial state. Our transport comment at internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods.go:441-444 is accurate. Also settled: "Unscharf", "Hüllschutz" and "Vollschutz" are genuine CCU wording, and the EN gloss ("Presence mode" for Hüllschutz, "Absence mode" for Vollschutz) matches our perimeter/full semantics. NOT settled: the seven-member list, its membership and its order. There is no built-in ENUM alarm sysvar; the built-in one ("Alarmzone 1") is ivtBinary/istAlarm and structurally cannot carry seven levels. "Nachtschutz" returns zero hits across ../OpenCCU-Base and ../OpenCCU; "Urlaub", "Benutzerdefiniert" and "Alarm" appear only in unrelated contexts, never as protection levels. And the three that do exist are on a different surface — an e-paper display icon picker — not a variable value list, so citing them would answer the wrong question. So the interoperability claim ("existing programs read naturally") is unverified: there is no CCU-side list for a third-party program to have been written against. What our rule actually rests on is our own notes/concepts/alarm-concept.md §13.5 plus three CCU words borrowed from the e-paper catalogue.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU defined a canonical list, it would surface either as a ValueList string literal in a ReGa/Tcl seed or as a contiguous block of translate keys alongside iconProtectionOff/External/Internal. The grep discriminates: it returns the iconProtection* entries for "Hüllschutz" and nothing at all for "Nachtschutz" — a list containing the latter would have been found by the same command.
all.missingInput: A CCU-side definition of an alarm protection-level value list. None exists in the firmware; the daemon is the sole author of this variable's value list, and that is what the comment should say.

all.title: The state-parameter -> reset-action mapping names device families in a comment but cites no descriptor
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory (registers ParameterMapKey("RESET_MOTION","default") and ParameterMapKey("RESET_PRESENCE","default"), each via createStop) and de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterIdentifier; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_sec_mdir.xml (and rf_sec_mdir_v1_5.xml, rf_sen_mdir.xml, rf_sen_mdir_v1_5.xml, rf_sen_mdir_wm55.xml); Tier 2 co-location sweep over ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json joined to ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json
all.ourValue: MOTION -> RESET_MOTION and PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE -> RESET_PRESENCE on the same channel; comment cites HmIP-SMO, HM-Sec-MDIR and HmIP-SPI as the evidence
all.firmwareValue: The pairing and the same-channel co-location hold, but only on HmIP channels. RESET_MOTION appears on MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (8 devices: HmIP-SMI, SMI55, SMO, SMO-2, …) and MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SMO230-A), always beside MOTION. RESET_PRESENCE appears on PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SPI, HmIPW-SPI), always beside PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE. HM-Sec-MDIR declares MOTION on a MOTION_DETECTOR channel and no RESET_MOTION; the string RESET_MOTION does not occur anywhere under src/devicetypes/.
all.finding: The mapping itself is right and the two families are genuinely distinct: the HmIP server registers RESET_MOTION and RESET_PRESENCE as two separate stop-shaped state parameters, so they are not synonyms. The descriptor sweep confirms strict co-location — every channel carrying RESET_MOTION also carries MOTION, every channel carrying RESET_PRESENCE also carries PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE, and never the cross pairing. Completeness also holds: no other latching alarm-sensor state parameter has a reset action. SMOKE_DETECTOR carries only SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS; there is no RESET_WATER on any channel; ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SAM, HmIP-STV) carries MOTION with no reset, and so does the classic MOTION_DETECTOR channel. That last point is where the boundary runs and where the comment is wrong: RESET_MOTION is HmIP-only. HM-Sec-MDIR, named in the comment as a RESET_MOTION device, declares MOTION and nothing else (rf_sec_mdir.xml), as do all 11 classic MOTION_DETECTOR devices in the corpus. The behaviour is still correct — resetParameterFor returns the parameter name, the channel lookup finds no such DP, and the sensor is reported Supports=false — so a classic BidCos detector is correctly non-resettable. Only the comment's cited evidence is refuted; replacing HM-Sec-MDIR with a real HmIP motion detector (HmIP-SMI, HmIP-SMO-2) and noting that classic BidCos MOTION_DETECTOR channels have no reset would make it accurate.
all.negativeControl: Had RESET_MOTION existed on the classic side, `grep -rl RESET_MOTION ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/` would list rf_sec_mdir.xml; it lists nothing, while the same string does resolve in the HmIP server tree — so the check produces different answers on the two sides and is not untethered. Likewise, had the pairing been cross-wired on any device, the co-location sweep would have printed a channel type carrying MOTION together with RESET_PRESENCE; it printed none.
all.challengeNote: Narrowing upheld; every number in it reproduces. What I checked, independently rather than by re-reading the previous agent's sweep. (1) The registration is verbatim: StateParameterFactory puts ParameterMapKey("RESET_MOTION","default") and ParameterMapKey("RESET_PRESENCE","default"), each from createStop, and StateParameterIdentifier declares both constants — two separate parameters, not synonyms, so keying the reset off the parameter rather than off the sensor type is right. (2) I re-ran the co-location sweep from scratch, joining each paramset file's VALUES key set to the channel TYPE from the device description. RESET_MOTION appears on exactly 9 (device, channel) pairs — HmIP-SMI, SMI55, SMO, SMO-2, SMO-A, SMO230-A, UDI-SMI55, HmIPW-SMI55 on MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER, plus HmIP-SMO230-A on MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER — and MOTION is present on every one of them, PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE on none. RESET_PRESENCE appears on exactly 2, both PRESENCEDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SPI, HmIPW-SPI), with PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE present and MOTION absent. No cross pairing anywhere. (3) Completeness holds and I widened the test: RESET_MOTION and RESET_PRESENCE are the ONLY parameters beginning with RESET in any VALUES paramset in the whole corpus — there is no RESET_WATER, no smoke reset. ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER carries MOTION with no reset on 3 devices (HmIP-SAM, HmIP-STV and also ELV-SH-TACO, which the previous finding omitted), and the classic MOTION_DETECTOR channel carries MOTION with no reset on 11 devices. (4) The comment's evidence is refuted as stated: grep over the whole of src/devicetypes/ returns no file containing RESET_MOTION, and rf_sec_mdir.xml:121 declares channel index=1 type="MOTION_DETECTOR" whose only relevant parameter is id="MOTION" operations="read,event" at :227. HM-Sec-MDIR cannot be a RESET_MOTION device. (5) The 'behaviour is still correct' claim is verifiable and correct: motionResetter.action resolves the reset DP through Channel.Parameter and returns an error when it is nil, and Supports is literally `_, err := m.action(row); return err == nil` — so a classic BidCos detector reports Supports=false rather than misbehaving. Only the comment is wrong; the boundary is that RESET_MOTION is HmIP-only.
