all.ourValue: 11 channel types; on an intrusion-role channel only {STATE, MOTION, PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE} are enrollable, described as "a plain boolean with no security classification of its own"
all.firmwareValue: All 11 names are real CCU channel types and the carrier-parameter split is exactly right (STATE / MOTION / PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE). But two sub-claims do not survive: (a) STATE is NOT a plain boolean on the intrusion channels the firmware builds in HmIP — SHUTTER_CONTACT STATE is ENUM {CLOSED,OPEN} and ROTARY_HANDLE_TRANSCEIVER STATE is ENUM {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN} (and BidCos ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR STATE is `<logical type="option">` with the same three options); only SHUTTER_CONTACT/TILT_SENSOR on BidCos are `<logical type="boolean"/>`. (b) The set is not complete for "unambiguous" detection-state channels: ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SAM) declares STATE=ENUM{CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN} plus MOTION=BOOL — byte-for-byte the rotary-handle shape — and DOOR_STATE_TRANSCEIVER declares STATE=ENUM{CLOSED,OPEN}; on the BidCos side SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEAM and SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEAM_V2 declare STATE with control="DANGER.STATE", the group-level fire signal.
all.finding:
Confirmed in scope: every one of the eleven channel types exists in the firmware, and each one's detection-state parameter is exactly the one the second half accepts — no misspelling, no wrong parameter. The rule is false one step wider in two places, and the boundary runs at the shape of STATE and at the edge of the table.

Shape: the code comment asserts the intrusion state parameter is "a plain boolean". The firmware builds HmIP window/handle STATE as an ENUM — GeneralStateParameterFactory#createStateWindowOpenClosed uses enumStrings {CLOSED,OPEN} over physical values {0,200}, #createStateWindowOpenTiltedClosed uses {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN} over {0,100,200}. BidCos ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR is the same three-option enum (rf_rhs.xml:170). Only rf_sc.xml:154 and rf_tis.xml:139 are genuinely `<logical type="boolean"/>`. The code itself is unharmed — sensorCandidateFor copies ParameterData().ValueList and safety.ActiveFromRaw handles the enum — so this is a wrong comment on correct code, not a defect. Fix the comment, not the code.

Completeness: the table omits three detection-state channel types the CCU declares. ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SAM, the window/garage vibration-and-tilt sensor) declares STATE with the identical {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN} vocabulary and a MOTION boolean, yet is neither in sensorTypeByChannelType nor in safety.byChannelAndParameter, so it never becomes a candidate at all. DOOR_STATE_TRANSCEIVER (STATE={CLOSED,OPEN}) is likewise absent. SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEAM / SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEAM_V2 carry the team-level fire STATE (control="DANGER.STATE") and are absent from both tables, so a HM-Sec-SD team channel — the channel that reports the group alarm — cannot be enrolled.

One structural note on the site itself: the hazard entries in sensorTypeByChannelType (SMOKE_DETECTOR, WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER, WATERDETECTIONSENSOR) are dead weight. sensorCandidateFor only consults the map inside the safety.Classify branch, where the fallback is already AlarmSensorTypeHazard, and the intrusion branch explicitly skips role==Hazard. Removing those three rows changes no behaviour.
all.negativeControl: Had the table been wrong, this check produces a different answer in two directly observable ways, and it did produce one of them. (1) A misspelled or invented channel type would not appear in the `<channel type="…">` set extracted from ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml nor among the 127 channel TYPEs in the descriptor corpus — I enumerated both and all eleven appear. (2) A wrong carrier parameter would show as a channel type whose VALUES paramset contains none of {STATE,MOTION,PRESENCE_DETECTION_STATE} — the per-type VALUES listing would have shown it; none did. The completeness half is the direction that did fire: enumerating detection-state channel types from the firmware rather than from the table produced three names the table does not carry, which is exactly the result a complete table would not have produced.
all.challengeNote:
Demoted from tier 1 to tier 2, and one supporting sub-claim is contradicted.

UPHELD. All eleven channel types are real and each one's carrier parameter is exactly the one the intrusion branch accepts — I re-derived this from the corpus rather than reading it back, and got the same set. The "plain boolean" comment at sensor_candidates.go:155-157 is wrong: STATE is an ENUM on every HmIP intrusion channel and on BidCos ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR; only rf_sc.xml:156 and rf_tis.xml:141 are genuinely boolean. The code is unharmed (ParameterData().ValueList is copied and safety.ActiveFromRaw resolves the ordinal), so this is a wrong comment on correct code. I also confirmed by reading both tables that ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER, DOOR_STATE_TRANSCEIVER and SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEAM/_V2 appear in neither sensorTypeByChannelType nor safety.byChannelAndParameter, and that the three hazard rows are dead weight: sensorCandidateFor consults the map only inside the Classify branch whose fallback is already AlarmSensorTypeHazard, and the intrusion branch returns false for role==Hazard, so deleting them changes no outcome for any parameter.

TIER INFLATION. The bundle's Tier-1 label rests on two legs and neither carries the load. (i) The BidCos device XMLs are labelled "Tier 1 (BidCos device XMLs)"; the witness hierarchy places src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml in Tier 2. (ii) The genuine Tier-1 leg answers an adjacent surface: the HmIP factory methods are keyed by the feature qualifier WINDOW_OPEN_CLOSED, and the qualifier→channel binding is read from a device-description resource that is not in the readable material. The same HmIP component names that channel SHUTTER_CONTACT_TRANSCEIVER, and no legacy remap to SHUTTER_CONTACT exists in legacy-parameter-definition.config, which is where DeviceUtil#getChannelType looks. So "the channel our table calls SHUTTER_CONTACT carries this ENUM" is established by the descriptor corpus, not by the firmware code. Tier 2.

CONTRADICTED. "ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SAM) declares STATE=ENUM{CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN} plus MOTION=BOOL — byte-for-byte the rotary-handle shape" does not survive. HmIP-SAM's ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER channel declares MOTION and nothing else; so does HmIP-STV; HmIP-DLP declares an empty VALUES set on that channel. The single device carrying STATE on that channel type is ELV-SH-TACO, and it carries four parameters, not the rotary-handle pair. No device in the corpus shows the shape attributed to HmIP-SAM. The structural gap the sub-claim was raised to support does stand — the channel type is absent from both tables, so HmIP-SAM's MOTION never becomes a candidate — but it stands on our own code, not on the firmware sentence given for it.

SCOPE NOTE. SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEAM / _V2 exist only in the shipped XMLs; the corpus has no device declaring them, so the enrollment gap there is asserted from Tier 2 device XMLs alone and cannot be confirmed against a runtime descriptor.

all.title: "Active unless the value sits at index 0" is the default activation rule for every enumerated alarm sensor, with no source for index 0 meaning idle
all.citation: Tier 1 (HmIP, the quoted list): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus — `public enum SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus { IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM; }` with `getNames()` filling the array from `values()` in ordinal order; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createSmokeDetectorAlarmStatusParameter — `String[] enumStrings = SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus.getNames(); new StateParameter("SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS", LogicalType.ENUM, PhysicalType.INTEGER, …, new StringEnumToInteger(enumStrings), enumStrings[0], enumStrings[0], enumStrings[enumStrings.length - 1])`. Tier 1 (index==value on the legacy wire): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#createParameterDescription sets VALUE_LIST from `converter.getEnumStrings()`, and #convertParameterValue returns the ordinal within getEnumStrings() when replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal is set; ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true`. Tier 1 (BidCos): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:49-58 (`options[index]=id` when the XML carries an index, else append) and :100-107 (`MIN=0`, `MAX=options.size()-1`, `VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i]`). Tier 1 (per-family idle at 0): rf_rhs.xml:170-175 {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN}; rf_wds_v1_1.xml:149-154 {DRY,WET,WATER}; rf_sc.xml:164-169 ERROR {NO_ERROR@0, SABOTAGE@7}.
all.ourValue: Default rule: "active unless the value sits at index 0"; quoted list SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS = [IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM]
all.firmwareValue: The quoted list is exact, in that order, from the firmware's own enum declaration. The positional premise underneath the rule is also exact: the legacy XML-RPC integer IS the VALUE_LIST index on both stacks. What the firmware nowhere states is "index 0 is idle" — the strongest general statement it makes is DEFAULT = MIN = enumStrings[0] for the HmIP state-parameter enums, which is a default, not an idle semantic.
all.finding:
Two separable inputs; they land differently.

(a) The quoted value list is confirmed verbatim at Tier 1. SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus declares IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM in that order, getNames() preserves ordinal order, and createSmokeDetectorAlarmStatusParameter feeds that array straight into the StateParameter. So INTRUSION_ALARM really does sit at index 2 inside a smoke-detector status, and the comment's reasoning — that "not index 0" reads the installation's own siren command as a fire — is sound.

(b) The positional premise our runtime silently depends on is also confirmed, and it is worth recording because it is the part nobody wrote down. safety.ActiveFromRaw maps an integer wire value onto a label by scanning valueList positionally. On HmIP that holds because DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue converts an ENUM to its ordinal in getEnumStrings() and crRFD.conf:47 ships ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true — note the *physical* radio bytes are not the ordinals at all (createStateWindowOpenTiltedClosed maps {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN} onto {0,100,200}), so without that flag the positional read would be wrong. On BidCos it holds because HSSLogicalTypeOption places each option AT its declared index and emits VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i] with MIN=0, MAX=size-1.

(c) "Index 0 is idle" is not a firmware rule. It is a per-enum property that happens to hold across every ENUM an alarm sensor can currently be enrolled on: STATE on SHUTTER_CONTACT {CLOSED,OPEN}, ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR / ROTARY_HANDLE_TRANSCEIVER / ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER {CLOSED,TILTED,OPEN}, DOOR_STATE_TRANSCEIVER {CLOSED,OPEN}, WATERDETECTIONSENSOR {DRY,WET,WATER}, RAINDETECTOR {DRY,RAIN}, ERROR {NO_ERROR,…}, ERROR_ALARM_TEST / ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER {NO_ERROR,…}, and SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS {IDLE_OFF,…} — I enumerated every ENUM VALUE_LIST carried by a classifiable parameter and index 0 is the inactive state in all of them. The boundary runs where the firmware's own statement stops: it guarantees only DEFAULT=MIN=first entry for the HmIP enums, and nothing at all for BidCos option lists. So the rule is true in our scope and unbacked one step wider; it is safe today and it is exactly the kind of rule that must be re-checked when a new ENUM family becomes enrollable, because a firmware that ships an alarm state at position 0 would break it silently.

One caveat on inputs, recorded because it touches the same premise: for SHUTTER_CONTACT/MOTION_DETECTOR/ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR ERROR, the shipped device XML declares SABOTAGE at index="7" (rf_sc.xml:168, and the same in firmware/rftypes/rf_sc.xml), which per HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:53 must yield an eight-entry VALUE_LIST with six empty-string fillers and MAX=7 — while the recorded descriptor corpus consistently shows a two-entry list with MAX=1. The corpus does contain firmware-shaped fillers elsewhere (HM-CC-RT-DN FAULT_REPORTING carries an empty entry at position 5, matching rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:2340's `<option id=""/>`). I could not reconcile the two for the sparse-index case and am not asserting either; it does not move this verdict, since both readings put NO_ERROR at 0.
all.negativeControl: Had our list or our index-0 premise been wrong, three distinct checks would have said so. (1) A wrong list: the firmware enum declares its constants in source order, so a reordered or renamed entry (say IDLE_OFF not first, or SMOKE_ALARM instead of PRIMARY_ALARM) would read straight off SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus — it did not. (2) A wrong positional premise: if the legacy surface delivered the physical byte instead of the ordinal, crRFD.conf would carry ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=false and DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue would return the raw value, and a HmIP window contact would report 200 for OPEN rather than 1 — the config template says true, and StringEnumToInteger's {0,100,200} table shows exactly what a false setting would have produced. (3) A wrong idle-at-0 claim: enumerating every ENUM VALUE_LIST on a classifiable parameter would have produced at least one list whose first entry is an alarm state; across the whole corpus it produced none.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed at tier 1. This is the strongest grounding in the bundle and every load-bearing quote survived transcription check.

(a) The value list is exact — enum order, getNames() ordinal fill, and the factory call that hands the array to the StateParameter all read as claimed. INTRUSION_ALARM really is at index 2 inside a smoke-detector status, so the reasoning behind ActiveValues holds.

(b) The positional premise our runtime silently depends on is confirmed on both stacks, and I verified it independently rather than accepting it. On HmIP the description's value list and the wire ordinal are produced from one and the same getEnumStrings() array, and the inbound direction indexes it directly — so scanning valueList positionally in safety.ActiveFromRaw is exactly right. Worth keeping visible: the physical radio bytes are NOT the ordinals (CLOSED/TILTED/OPEN map to 0/100/200), so without ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal the positional read would be silently wrong; crRFD.conf ships it true. On BidCos, HSSLogicalTypeOption honours a declared index attribute and emits VALUE_LIST[i]=options[i] with MIN 0 and MAX size-1.

(c) The boundary is drawn honestly and I could not push it further. The firmware's strongest general statement is DEFAULT=MIN=first entry for the HmIP state-parameter enums — a default, not an idle semantic — and nothing at all for BidCos option lists. My independent sweep reproduces the empirical claim: every ENUM value list a classifiable parameter carries has its inactive value at index 0. So the rule is true in our scope and unbacked one step wider, which is exactly what "narrowed" should mean.

CORRECTIONS, neither load-bearing. (i) The "per-family idle at 0" citations to rf_rhs.xml / rf_wds_v1_1.xml / rf_sc.xml are labelled Tier 1; those are Tier-2 device XMLs. The Tier-1 half (HmIP enum, HmIP ordinal wire, libhsscomm) stands on its own, which is why the tier survives. (ii) The finding lists ACCELERATION_TRANSCEIVER, DOOR_STATE_TRANSCEIVER and RAINDETECTOR among enums "an alarm sensor can currently be enrolled on"; per its own sibling finding none of those channel types is enrollable, and RAINDETECTOR appears in neither table. Scope creep in the prose, not in the measurement — my sweep was restricted to what classify.go and sensor_candidates.go can actually reach and the conclusion is unchanged. (iii) The unreconciled sparse-index observation is real and reproduced; it does not move the verdict since both readings put NO_ERROR at 0, and ERROR is not a classifiable parameter in the first place.

all.title: The sysvar wire encodings (bool as int 0/1, enum list as ';'-joined string, chnID -1) are bare literals
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods.conf:865-903 — `SysVar.createBool { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name init_val internal chnID} }`, `SysVar.setBool { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name value} }`, `SysVar.createEnum { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name valList internal chnID} }`, `SysVar.createFloat { … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_ name minValue maxValue internal chnID} }`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/setbool.tcl:14-22 — `set val $args(value)` / `if {($val != 0) && ($val != 1) } { if {$val >= 1} { set args(value) 1 } else { set args(value) 0 } }`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createenum.tcl:7 — `#   valList: Enum "Wert1;Wert2;Wert3;...."` and :26 `sv.ValueList( valList );`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/getall.tcl:27 — `#     valueList: [string] Werteliste (Separator: ";")`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/msg/newSysVar.htm:196 (the WebUI's own new-sysvar form) — `pb += "string sValList = '"+$("txVals").value.replace(/(?:\r\n|\r|\n)/g,';')+"';";`, consumed at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:842 `sv.ValueList(system.GetVar("sValList"));`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createbool.tcl:9 / createenum.tcl:9 / createfloat.tcl:10 — `chnID: [integer] ID des Kanals … Wenn an kein Kanal gebunden werden soll, ist -1 zu übergeben`, enforced at createbool.tcl:15 `if (chnID != -1) {`. createbool.tcl:4 — `init_val: [bool] Initialer Status`, applied at :28 `sv.State(init_val);`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/hmscript.tcl:17 — every argument is injected into the ReGa script as `var $name = "…";`, i.e. as a string literal.
all.ourValue: SysVar.setBool value = int 0/1; createBool init_val = int 0/1; createEnum valList = strings joined by ";"; chnID = -1
all.firmwareValue: setBool value: the handler's fast path is literally "is 0 or 1", and anything else is coerced numerically — int 0/1 is the encoding it is written for. valList: ";" verbatim, in the method's own header, in SysVar.getAll's return documentation, and in the WebUI form that joins the operator's textarea lines with ";". chnID: -1 verbatim as "no channel binding". init_val: documented `[bool]`, and the only in-tree caller (www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/views/newdevices.htm:795) sends the JSON boolean `false`, not 0.
all.finding:
Three of the four encodings at this site are confirmed against the CCU's own handler, not against a convention.

setBool: setbool.tcl normalises before touching ReGa — `if {($val != 0) && ($val != 1)}` — so an integer 0 or 1 takes neither branch and is passed through untouched, and the method echoes it back (`jsonrpc_response $args(value)`). Our int 0/1 is precisely the value the handler is written around; a JSON boolean would fall into the else branch and be decided by a Tcl string comparison of "true" against 1, which is not a path to rely on.

valList: ";" is stated three independent times — the method header, the SysVar.getAll return-shape documentation, and the WebUI's own new-sysvar form, which joins the textarea's lines with ";" and hands the result to `sv.ValueList()`. (Note that newdevices.htm:801 passes the literal "val1,val2,val3" to createEnum, but that is a throwaway placeholder immediately overwritten by SysVar.setEnum with the real list; it is not a counter-example to the separator.)

chnID = -1: verbatim in the header of all three create methods and enforced by the `if (chnID != -1)` guard that skips the channel lookup.

The boundary is init_val. The firmware types it `[bool]`, and the CCU's own caller sends JSON `false`. Because hmscript.tcl:17 injects every argument as a ReGa *string* literal, the script receives `var init_val = "0";` from us and `var init_val = "false";` from the WebUI, and `sv.State()` then decides. Whether ReGa coerces "0" to false is not readable — ReGaHss is a binary in this tree — so our integer encoding for init_val is unverified in that word, and the worst case is a freshly created boolean sysvar starting true. Aligning init_val with the documented type (and with the CCU's own caller) is the cheap fix; the same applies to internal, which the OpenCCU distribution has already had to patch for exactly this coercion (see client-transports-c008).

Two adjacent claims at the same site, checked while here: the doc comment "CCU defaults: 0–65000" on CreateSystemVariableFloat is a WebUI *form pre-fill*, not a firmware default — newSysVar.htm:290 `loadIntEdit(0, 65000)` pre-fills that range in the operator dialog, while createfloat.tcl applies no default at all and methods.conf declares minValue/maxValue as required arguments. And the create* response we decode into `map[string]any` is emitted by unpatched firmware as single-quoted pseudo-JSON (`Write("{'name':'"#sv.Name()#…")`, embedded verbatim by jsonrpc.tcl:87 `"result": $result`), which is not valid JSON; OpenCCU's patch 0157-WebUI-Fix-WrongJSONQuotes is what makes it parseable. Against a stock eQ-3 CCU the create* result decode fails.
all.negativeControl: Had any of the three encodings been wrong, the check produces a visibly different answer. A boolean-not-integer setBool would show as a handler branching on `true`/`false` rather than on 0 and 1 — setbool.tcl branches on the integers. A different enum separator would show as a different character in createenum.tcl's header, in getall.tcl's documented return shape, and above all in the WebUI form's join — a comma there would have settled it against us; all three say ";". A different no-channel sentinel would show as a different constant in the `if (chnID != …)` guard, or as an absent guard. The direction that did fire is init_val: the firmware's declared type and its own caller both disagree with our integer, which is exactly the output this check produces when a convention has been substituted for the documented type.
all.missingInput: Whether ReGa's sv.State() coerces the string "0" to false — ReGaHss is a compiled binary in this tree, so createBool's acceptance of integer 0/1 for init_val cannot be settled from source.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed at tier 1, with corrected line numbers. Three of the four encodings are grounded on the CCU's own handler, not on convention, and I re-read each one.

setBool: setbool.tcl normalises before touching ReGa, and an integer 0 or 1 takes neither branch — the handler is written around exactly our encoding. The onward claim about what a JSON boolean would do is correctly left as reasoning rather than asserted; I did not verify Tcl's coercion of "true" and neither should the note.

valList: ";" is stated three times independently — the method header, the getAll return-shape documentation, and the WebUI's own new-sysvar form, which joins the operator's textarea lines with ";" and hands the result to sv.ValueList(). The disposal of newdevices.htm:801's "val1,val2,val3" as a placeholder immediately overwritten by SysVar.setEnum is correct: I read the surrounding callback and it does exactly that.

chnID = -1: header text in all three create methods and the `if (chnID != -1)` guard that skips the channel lookup.

The init_val boundary is drawn correctly and is the honest part of this grounding: the firmware types it [bool], the CCU's own caller sends JSON false, hmscript.tcl:17 injects every argument as a ReGa string literal so our integer arrives as "0", and what sv.State("0") does is decided inside ReGaHss, which is a binary in this tree. Unverified in those words is right.

The two adjacent claims also check out. "CCU defaults: 0–65000" is indeed only a WebUI form pre-fill (newSysVar.htm:290); createfloat.tcl applies no default and methods.conf declares minValue/maxValue as required arguments — and the CCU's own programmatic caller uses 0 .. 1.7e308-1 instead, which is a second, independent refutation of "CCU default". The single-quoted pseudo-JSON claim is exact: the create* Write() emits `{'name':'…'}` and jsonrpc.tcl:87 embeds $result verbatim into the envelope, so on unpatched firmware the whole response body is invalid JSON and our map[string]any decode fails on the envelope, not just on the result.

Only defect: several createbool.tcl line numbers are 1-3 off. Content is present in the named file each time, so this is citation hygiene, not a wrong surface.

all.title: Sysvar creation hard-codes chnID -1 and internal 0 with no source
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/createbool.tcl:5,9 — `#   internal: [integer]  Variable sichtbar / Variable intern` and `#   chnID: [integer] ID des Kanals, an dem die Variable gebunden werden soll. Wenn an kein Kanal gebunden werden soll, ist -1 zu übergeben`; :15 `if (chnID != -1) {`; :30 `sv.Internal(internal);`. Same header text at createenum.tcl:8-9 and createfloat.tcl:9-10. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods.conf:865-895 — ARGUMENTS lists confirming the parameter names. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/sysvar/getall.tcl:20 — `#     isInternal: [bool]   Gibt an, ob die Systemvariable intern verwendet wird`; :17 `#     channelId : [string] Id des zugeordneten Kanals (ungültig bei "0" und "65535")`. Working caller: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/views/newdevices.htm:781-801 — `CreateSysVar = function (name, type, value, chnID) { if (typeof chnID === "undefined") { chnID = -1; } … homematic("SysVar.createBool", {"name": name, "init_val": false, "internal": 1, "chnID": chnID} …)`. Visibility semantics: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/device/listalldetail.tcl:46 `if (false == channel.Internal())`, www/rega/esp/devices.fn:72 `if( !chn.Internal() )`. Distribution: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0157-WebUI-Fix-WrongJSONQuotes.patch — replaces `sv.Internal(internal);` with `if((internal == "true") || (internal == 1)) { sv.Internal(true); } else { sv.Internal(false); }` in createbool.tcl, createenum.tcl and createfloat.tcl.
all.ourValue: chnID: -1 (no channel assignment); internal: 0 (operator-visible)
all.firmwareValue: chnID -1 = "no channel binding", stated verbatim in all three method headers and enforced by the `if (chnID != -1)` guard; the CCU's own JS helper defaults the argument to -1 for exactly that case. internal: 1 (or "true") = internal/hidden, everything else = visible — but that mapping is explicit only on the OpenCCU distribution, which patches it in; upstream the raw argument goes straight into sv.Internal().
all.finding:
chnID = -1 is confirmed twice over, and the second witness is the one that matters: the CCU's own WebUI helper (newdevices.htm:781-783) defaults chnID to -1 whenever no channel is given, which is the repo's working caller for this exact API. The method headers state the same in words, and createbool.tcl:15 enforces it — with chnID -1 the channel lookup is skipped entirely, so nothing binds. There is a read-side asymmetry worth knowing about but not acting on: SysVar.getAll documents the *returned* channelId as invalid at "0" and "65535", not at -1, so a created-unbound variable does not read back as -1. Our code only writes, so nothing depends on it.

internal = 0 meaning operator-visible is confirmed on the distribution we ship against and not decidable upstream. OpenCCU's patch 0157 rewrites `sv.Internal(internal)` into an explicit `if((internal == "true") || (internal == 1)) { sv.Internal(true); } else { sv.Internal(false); }` in all three create methods — so on OpenCCU our 0 lands on the else branch and the variable is visible, definitively. On unpatched firmware the argument reaches ReGa as the string "0" (hmscript.tcl:17 injects every argument as a string literal) and `sv.Internal("0")` is decided inside ReGaHss, a binary. The existence of the patch is itself evidence that the unpatched coercion was not reliable. The surrounding semantics are not in doubt in either direction: SysVar.getAll documents isInternal as "intern verwendet", every WebUI listing gates on `Internal() == false` to show an object, and the CCU's own caller passes internal: 1 precisely because it is creating hidden bookkeeping variables. So 1 = hidden, 0 = visible is the intent; only the upstream coercion of the integer is unverified.

Same-file note, since it hits every create* call here: the response our `map[string]any` decode expects is single-quoted pseudo-JSON on unpatched firmware (`Write("{'name':'"#sv.Name()#…")`, embedded verbatim by www/api/eq3/jsonrpc.tcl:87), and only patch 0157 makes it valid JSON. Against a stock eQ-3 CCU the create succeeds but the result decode does not.
all.negativeControl: Had -1 not been the sentinel, the check produces a different constant in the `if (chnID != …)` guard and a different default in the CCU's own CreateSysVar helper — both would have shown immediately; both say -1. Had internal been inverted, the OpenCCU patch would read `if(internal == 0) { sv.Internal(true); }` and the WebUI's hidden bookkeeping variables would be created with internal: 0 rather than internal: 1, and every listing would gate on `Internal() == true` to display — all four indicators point the other way. The direction that did fire is the upstream half: the patch exists at all, which is the result you get when the unpatched coercion of this argument was not dependable.
all.missingInput: Whether unpatched ReGaHss coerces the string "0" passed to sv.Internal() to false — ReGaHss is a compiled binary, so the upstream (non-OpenCCU) behaviour of internal: 0 cannot be read from source.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed at tier 1, with one wrong-surface correction that I was able to replace with better evidence rather than demote.

chnID = -1 is confirmed twice over and the second witness is the decisive one: the CCU's own WebUI helper defaults chnID to -1 when no channel is given — that is the repo-external working caller for this exact API, which is the specification for the parameter. The guard at createbool.tcl:15 makes it operative: with -1 the channel lookup is skipped and nothing binds. The read-side asymmetry noted (getAll documents the returned channelId as invalid at "0"/"65535", not -1) is real and correctly judged irrelevant, since our code only writes.

WRONG SURFACE in the visibility evidence. The two citations offered for "Internal means hidden" — listalldetail.tcl:46 and devices.fn:72 — are present at exactly those lines but they gate `channel.Internal()` and `chn.Internal()`. A channel's Internal flag is a different object class from a VARDP's, and there is no Internal() gate anywhere under www/api/methods/sysvar/. Cited as written, they are a correct quotation answering a different surface.

The conclusion nevertheless survives, on evidence the bundle did not use: the admin sysvar list enumerates `EnumEnabledIDs()`, and OpenCCU's ShowInternalSysvars patch has to add a separate `EnumEnabledInternalIDs()` enumeration to surface internal sysvars — which is only necessary if the enabled enumeration excludes them. That is the sysvar surface, and it settles the direction: Internal(true) hides, Internal(false) shows. Combined with patch 0157, on the distribution we ship against our 0 lands on the else branch and the variable is visible, definitively.

A precision point the finding should carry: getall.tcl reports VISIBLE and INTERNAL as two independent properties, and our create* calls set only Internal, never Visible. "internal: 0 = operator-visible" is therefore accurate about the internal flag alone.

The upstream boundary stands exactly as stated: unpatched, sv.Internal("0") is decided inside ReGaHss, a binary, and the existence of patch 0157 is itself evidence the raw coercion was unreliable. Unverified in that word is correct. Only defect otherwise: the `internal:` header is createbool.tcl:8, not :5.

all.title: listInterfaces field mapping rests on one observed payload, not on the handler
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/listinterfaces.tcl:8-12 — `# Rückgabewert: [array]` / `#   Für jedes Interface wird ein Objekt mit den folgenden Feldern angegeben:` / `#     name: [string]  Bezeichnung der Schnittstelle` / `#     port: [integer] Portnummer des zugehörigen XML-RPC Servers` / `#     info: [string]  Kurzbeschreibung der Schnittstelle`; :18-27 the emitter itself — `foreach interfaceName [array names INTERFACE_LIST] { array set interface $INTERFACE_LIST($interfaceName) … append result "\"name\":[json_toString $interfaceName]" ; append result ",\"port\":$interface(PORT)" ; append result ",\"info\":[json_toString $interface(INFO)]" … }`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods.conf:241-246 — `Interface.listInterfaces { LEVEL GUEST … ARGUMENTS {_session_id_} }`. ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/ipc.tcl:65 — `set interfaces($name) [list PORT $port URL $url INFO $info]`, from `/etc/config/InterfacesList.xml`'s `<name>` element (:60). Identifier identity: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/dispatch.tcl:156-160 — `set interfaceName $args(interface)` / `if { [catch { array set interface $INTERFACE_LIST($interfaceName) }] } then { jsonrpc_error 500 "unknown interface ($interfaceName)" }`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/device/haslinksorprograms.tcl:16-19 — `"BidCos-RF" {array set ifaceList $INTERFACE_LIST(BidCos-RF)}`, `"BidCos-Wired"`, `"HmIP-RF"`, `"HmIP-Wired"`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/tools/HomeMatic-API.html:6-8 — `<option value="HmIP-RF">`, `<option value="VirtualDevices">`, `<option value="BidCos-RF">`.
all.ourValue: Real firmware answers with name/port/info and reports neither `type` nor `address` nor `url`; `name` is the interface identifier that configured_interfaces is keyed on
all.firmwareValue: The handler emits exactly three keys — name, port, info — and nothing else. URL is present in the internal INTERFACE_LIST record (ipc.tcl:65 stores PORT, URL, INFO) and is deliberately not emitted. The `name` is the INTERFACE_LIST array key, i.e. the same token Interface.* dispatch requires in its `interface` argument, and the CCU's own code spells those keys "BidCos-RF", "BidCos-Wired", "HmIP-RF", "HmIP-Wired", "VirtualDevices".
all.finding:
The comment's claim is exactly right, and it is now grounded on the handler rather than on one observed payload. listinterfaces.tcl builds the JSON by hand, key by key: name, port, info. There is no branch that could ever add type, address or url — and the omission is not accidental, since ipc.tcl:65 keeps URL in the very record the handler iterates and simply does not append it. So the defensive arms in our decoder that let an explicit `type`/`address`/`url` win are dead against any CCU built from this source; they are harmless and can stay as forward-compatibility, but they should not be described as covering a firmware that supplies them, because none in this tree does.

The identifier half is confirmed by two independent uses. dispatch.tcl:156-160 looks `$args(interface)` up directly in INTERFACE_LIST and faults with "unknown interface" otherwise, so the key emitted as `name` is precisely the token every Interface.* call must pass. haslinksorprograms.tcl:16-19 hard-codes those keys as "BidCos-RF", "BidCos-Wired", "HmIP-RF", "HmIP-Wired", and the CCU's own API test page offers "HmIP-RF", "VirtualDevices", "BidCos-RF" — the same strings as pkg/hmenum's Interface values, which is what configured_interfaces is keyed on. Seeding both Type and Address from `name` is therefore correct.

Two qualifications worth recording. First, the InterfaceEntry.Address doc comment says "same as the interface ID the CCU uses in XML-RPC callbacks" — that is a different thing. The interface_id in a callback is whatever the client passed to init(), which the daemon composes itself; the token confirmed here is the CCU-side interface *selector*. The two coincide by convention, not by firmware rule. Second, the emission order is `[array names INTERFACE_LIST]`, i.e. Tcl hash order — unspecified and not stable. Nothing in our decoder depends on order, and nothing should.

On blast radius, the bundle's damage note overstates it: this result is consumed only at internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:258 into unit.SetCCUInterfaces, which feeds the REST /system/ccu status view. Which per-interface clients come up is decided by configured_interfaces, not by this call, and a failure here is already downgraded to a warning. A wrong mapping mislabels a status page; it does not stop an interface.
all.negativeControl: Had the mapping been wrong, the handler would show it directly: a firmware emitting `type`, `address` or `url` would append those keys in listinterfaces.tcl's builder — it appends exactly three and skips the URL it already holds. Had `name` not been the interface identifier, dispatch.tcl would key INTERFACE_LIST on some other field, or haslinksorprograms.tcl would switch on tokens other than "BidCos-RF"/"HmIP-RF"/…; both do the opposite. And had our claim been about a firmware-version artefact, the source would carry a version-conditional branch — there is none; the three-key shape is unconditional.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, and I could not break it. This is the one grounding in the bundle that fully replaces an observed payload with the handler, and every leg checks out on re-reading.

The emitter is short enough to be exhaustive and I read it end to end: three appends, no branch, no path that could ever add type, address or url. The omission is demonstrably deliberate — ipc.tcl keeps URL in the very record listinterfaces.tcl iterates and simply never appends it. So the conclusion that our decoder's type/address/url arms are dead against any CCU built from this source is not an inference from absence; it is a reading of the only code that can produce the field set. I additionally checked that no distribution patch modifies the handler, which the bundle did not state and which was the obvious remaining way for the grounding to be wrong.

The identifier half is confirmed by two independent uses and I widened the check: dispatch.tcl looks $args(interface) up directly in INTERFACE_LIST and faults otherwise, and methods.conf routes essentially every Interface.* method through that one script — so the key emitted as `name` really is the token the whole Interface.* family requires, not just one method. haslinksorprograms.tcl hard-codes those keys and the CCU's own API test page offers the same strings, which match pkg/hmenum's Interface values. Seeding both Type and Address from `name` is correct.

Both qualifications the bundle raises are correct and I verified each: the InterfaceEntry.Address doc comment does say "same as the interface ID the CCU uses in XML-RPC callbacks", and that is a different object — a callback interface_id is whatever the client passed to init(), which the daemon composes; and the emission order really is `[array names INTERFACE_LIST]`, Tcl hash order, which nothing in our decoder depends on.

The blast-radius correction is right and if anything understated. I traced the single production path: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:258 -> unit.SetCCUInterfaces (internal/central/central.go:807) -> cmd/openccu-loom/system_ccu_adapter.go:80 -> the REST /system/ccu view. There is exactly one production reader; a failure is already downgraded to a `hub.ccu_interfaces.fetch_failed` warning, and which per-interface clients come up is decided by configured_interfaces. A wrong mapping mislabels a status page.

One boundary the bundle does not name, worth recording: INTERFACE_LIST keys are read from the `<name>` elements of /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml, i.e. from configuration, not from a firmware constant. The identity between emitted `name` and dispatch selector is structural and survives any renaming, since both read the same array — but haslinksorprograms.tcl's four literals are a hard-coded expectation about that file's content, not a guarantee about it.

all.title: 'The first entry of the icon VALUE_LIST is the no-icon entry' is a position convention, applied on every write
all.ourValue: iconValue = availableIcons[0] when Row.Icon == "", else the literal "NO_ICON"
all.firmwareValue: DEFAULT == MIN == VALUE_LIST[0] == "NO_ICON", by construction
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createDisplayDataColorParameter (registered for DISPLAY_DATA_ICON under the "epaper" subtype with enumStrings = TextIcon.getNames()); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.TextIcon; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.StateParameter (constructor argument order). Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-WRCD.json, VCU4243444:3 VALUES DISPLAY_DATA_ICON — DEFAULT "NO_ICON", MIN "NO_ICON", MAX "CLOCK", VALUE_LIST 32 entries beginning "NO_ICON".
all.finding:
Confirmed, and confirmed more strongly than the comment claims. The firmware does not read the icon list from a device: it builds the parameter as ENUM over TextIcon.getNames(), and TextIcon declares NO_ICON(0) as its first constant. createDisplayDataColorParameter passes enumStrings[0] for BOTH the defaultValue and the minValue argument of StateParameter (whose ctor order is defaultValue, minValue, maxValue), so DEFAULT, MIN and VALUE_LIST[0] are the same string on every device that declares this parameter — there is no device on which the head of the list is not the no-icon entry. Our static fallback defaultIcons (textdisplay.go:75-107) reproduces TextIcon exactly: same 32 names, same order, including the firmware's own misspelling CLOUD_AND_MOOON. So availableIcons[0] and the DEFAULT the sibling siren package would read are the same value here; the comment's hedge ("conventionally") understates it.

Two scope notes, both real results rather than caveats. (1) The confirmation covers the ENUM form only. The firmware registers a second DISPLAY_DATA_ICON under no subtype via createDisplayDataNibbleParameter — LogicalType.INTEGER, min 0, max 15, no VALUE_LIST at all. A channel of that shape carries no icon list, SetAvailableIcons is never called, and our code then writes the string "NO_ICON" onto an INTEGER parameter. Nothing in the profile registry restricts the textdisplay profile to the epaper form, so that is the one way this write path can produce an illegal value — and it is not the failure the candidate describes. (2) The reader's question also asked about ACOUSTIC_NOTIFICATION_SELECTION, and there the answer is the opposite: the firmware builds it from SignalAcoustic.getNotificationNames(), which starts at the enum's index 10, so the list is LOW_BATTERY, DISARMED, INTERNALLY_ARMED, EXTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_INTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_EXTERNALLY_ARMED, EVENT, ERROR, and DEFAULT is LOW_BATTERY (HmIP-WRCD.json confirms DEFAULT=LOW_BATTERY, 8 entries). There is no disable entry in that list. The SoundOptions doc comment at textdisplay.go:224-227 ("e.g. \"DISABLE_ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL\", \"SOUND_SHORT\", \"SOUND_LONG\"") names three labels that this parameter cannot take; DISABLE_ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL belongs to ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION (SignalAcoustic.getNames(), the full 18-entry list, whose head IS the disable label — which is the pair the siren package resolves, and that half is confirmed: HmIP-ASIR/-2/-O all declare ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION DEFAULT=DISABLE_ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL and OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION DEFAULT=DISABLE_OPTICAL_SIGNAL, each equal to its list head). No code writes from that doc string, so it is a wrong comment, not a wrong write.
all.negativeControl: Had the head of the list not been the clearing value, TextIcon's first constant would have been something other than NO_ICON, or createDisplayDataColorParameter would have passed a defaultValue other than enumStrings[0] — and the descriptor would then show DEFAULT != VALUE_LIST[0]. The check does produce that distinguishing result elsewhere in the same bundle: for ACOUSTIC_NOTIFICATION_SELECTION the same two reads return DEFAULT=LOW_BATTERY with no disable member at all, i.e. a list whose head is not a clearing value.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, and I closed the one gap the prior grounding left open. Their chain stopped at the factory; the step that actually matters for our code is the emission path, because our availableIcons is the VALUE_LIST as delivered over legacy XML-RPC (init.go:66 → dp.ParameterData().ValueList), not the factory's array. I read that path: DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter copies the converter's enumStrings array into VALUE_LIST unmodified, and the only subsequent mutator, #fillLegacyParameter, touches TabOrder/Unit/Control alone. So VALUE_LIST[0] is TextIcon's first constant on the wire, not merely in the JVM. Our static fallback defaultIcons (textdisplay.go:75-107) reproduces TextIcon's 32 names in order including the firmware's misspelling CLOUD_AND_MOOON, so the fallback and the runtime head agree.

One correction to the prior finding. Its scope note (1) claims 'Nothing in the profile registry restricts the textdisplay profile to the epaper form', and calls the INTEGER/nibble DISPLAY_DATA_ICON (createDisplayDataNibbleParameter, LogicalType.INTEGER, min 0 max 15, no VALUE_LIST) a live way to write "NO_ICON" onto an INTEGER parameter. It is not reachable: internal/model/custom/profiles.go:1429-1438 registers IPTextDisplay for DeviceType "hmip-wrcd", channel 3 only, and that channel carries the epaper ENUM form (Tier 2 above). Every other DISPLAY_DATA_ICON channel in the fleet is outside this profile. The hazard is a latent one that would open if the profile were extended to a second device type — worth a comment, not a defect.

Their ACOUSTIC_NOTIFICATION_SELECTION note is correct and I re-read the source: SignalAcoustic declares DISABLE_ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL at index 0 and getNotificationNames() copies indices 10..17, so the notification list is LOW_BATTERY…ERROR with no disable entry, and HmIP-WRCD.json shows DEFAULT LOW_BATTERY over 8 entries. The SoundOptions doc at textdisplay.go:224-227 names three labels this parameter cannot take. No code writes from that doc string, so it is a wrong comment, not a wrong write.

all.title: Soundfile index ceiling 252 rests on a comment, and the type's own doc says 189
all.ourValue: maxSoundfileIndex = 252 (const block) vs "a sound-file selector (1..189)" (SoundPlayer doc comment) — the two disagree
all.firmwareValue: SOUNDFILE_001 .. SOUNDFILE_252; VALUE_LIST is INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE, SOUNDFILE_001..SOUNDFILE_252, RANDOM_SOUNDFILE, OLD_VALUE, DO_NOT_CARE (256 entries)
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SoundFile (enum constants, declaration order); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createSoundFileParameter (SOUNDFILE built as ENUM over SoundFile.getNames(), default/min = enumStrings[0], max = last entry). Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MP3P.json, VCU1543608:1 and :2 VALUES SOUNDFILE — VALUE_LIST 256 entries, DEFAULT "INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE", tail RANDOM_SOUNDFILE, OLD_VALUE, DO_NOT_CARE.
all.finding:
The const is right and the type doc is wrong; the candidate's framing ("neither cites a source, and the two cannot both be right") resolves in favour of 252. The firmware's SoundFile enum carries exactly 252 numbered constants (a literal count of the SOUNDFILE_ constants in the enum body is 252), running SOUNDFILE_001 through SOUNDFILE_252, with INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE at index 0 and RANDOM_SOUNDFILE, OLD_VALUE, DO_NOT_CARE at the tail — 256 members total. createSoundFileParameter builds SOUNDFILE as an ENUM over SoundFile.getNames() with no truncation, so every device carrying SOUNDFILE gets the whole list; the MP3P descriptor confirms 256 entries on both channel 1 and channel 2. maxSoundfileIndex = 252 and ConvertSoundfileIndex's "SOUNDFILE_%03d" grammar both match the firmware exactly.

The 189 in the SoundPlayer doc has no counterpart in the firmware's soundfile material. The only 189 near it is a register address (list index) in the POWERUP_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR config parameter that happens to be enumerated over the same SoundFile.getNames() — a different field entirely. Nothing supports 189 as a selector ceiling; the fix is to correct the doc comment at :64-65 to 1..252, not to lower the const. Two related observations from the same read: nonPlayableSoundfiles (:48-51) correctly names OLD_VALUE and DO_NOT_CARE as the non-playable tail, and it is complete — those are the only two sentinel members after RANDOM_SOUNDFILE, which is playable. And PlaySound's index branch (:356-361) still writes without a membership check against availableSF, but with the ceiling at 252 that can no longer produce a label outside the firmware's list on any device declaring the full enum.
all.negativeControl: Had 252 been wrong, the enum's numbered run would end at a different constant — the tail of SoundFile would read ...SOUNDFILE_189, RANDOM_SOUNDFILE if the doc comment were right, and the MP3P descriptor's VALUE_LIST length would be 193 rather than 256. Both reads return the 252/256 shape, and the two independent sources (firmware enum, runtime descriptor) agree on it.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld: the const is right, the type doc is wrong, and 252 is now sourced. Two independent counts agree — 252 numbered constants in the enum body, and 1 + 252 + 3 = 256 members matching the descriptor's 256-entry VALUE_LIST exactly. Both createSoundFileParameter and createSoundFileSelectionListParameter pass the unmodified getNames(), so no device carrying SOUNDFILE gets a truncated list. ConvertSoundfileIndex's "SOUNDFILE_%03d" grammar matches the enum's own spelling.

I replace the prior finding's provenance guess for the 189. It suggested the only nearby 189 is the register address of POWERUP_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR — that address does exist (GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory registers POWERUP_OUTPUT_BEHAVIOUR at address 189 in four subtype variants, one of them over SoundFile.getNames()), but it is a coincidence, not a source. The actual origin is the Python reference this profile was ported from: aiohomematic bounds the same selector at 189 and its own test asserts the 1-189 message. Our const was corrected to 252 during the port and the doc line was left behind. The fix is to correct the doc at :64-65 to 1..252, not to lower the const.

Standing defect, unchanged by this grounding: PlaySound's index branch (sound.go:356-361) writes ConvertSoundfileIndex's label without checking membership in availableSF, while the label branch (:352-355) does check via offersSoundfile. With the ceiling at 252 the index branch cannot exceed the firmware enum, so the gap is now inert on any device declaring the full list — but it is an asymmetry between two branches of the same switch, and a dropped SOUNDFILE replays the previous file and looks like success (the comment on ErrUnknownSoundfile says exactly this). nonPlayableSoundfiles is complete: OLD_VALUE and DO_NOT_CARE are the only sentinel members after RANDOM_SOUNDFILE in the enum body.

all.title: REPETITIONS label grammar caps at 18 with no source
all.ourValue: MaxRepetitions = 18, i.e. REPETITIONS_001..REPETITIONS_018 accepted (siren/sound.go:257 carries the same 18 as maxRepetitionsIndex)
all.firmwareValue: On the VALUES-paramset REPETITIONS state parameter: 16 entries, NO_REPETITION, REPETITIONS_001..REPETITIONS_014, INFINITE_REPETITIONS — highest numbered REPETITIONS_014. On the MASTER/LINK *_PROFILE_REPETITIONS config parameters: 256 entries, highest numbered REPETITIONS_254.
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.Repetitions#getNames (names[0]=NO_REPETITION, names[i]=String.format("REPETITIONS_%03d", i) for 1<=i<size-1, names[size-1]=INFINITE_REPETITIONS); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createRepetitionParameter (calls Repetitions.getNames(16); registered for both the plain "REPETITIONS" key and the "interval" subtype); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory and ...configparameter.LinkConfigurationParameterFactory (POWERUP_PROFILE_REPETITIONS, SHORT_/LONG_PROFILE_REPETITIONS built over Repetitions.getNames(256)). Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-MP3P.json and HmIP-WRCD.json — REPETITIONS in VALUES: 16 entries, DEFAULT NO_REPETITION, MIN NO_REPETITION, MAX INFINITE_REPETITIONS, last numbered REPETITIONS_014; SHORT_/LONG_PROFILE_REPETITIONS in LINK and POWERUP_PROFILE_REPETITIONS in MASTER: 256 entries, last numbered REPETITIONS_254.
all.finding:
Two halves of the rule, opposite verdicts.

The grammar is confirmed verbatim. The firmware's own format string is "REPETITIONS_%03d", NO_REPETITION sits at index 0 and INFINITE_REPETITIONS at the last index — exactly the three constants and the zero-padded three-digit form mixins.go declares. That part is now sourced.

The ceiling 18 is contradicted, and it matches no surface. The parameter our code writes is the VALUES-paramset REPETITIONS state parameter (textdisplay.go:722 and siren/sound.go:368 both stage hmenum.ParameterRepetitions into a ParamsetKeyValues put_paramset), and the firmware builds that one with getNames(16): 16 slots, so the numbered run stops at REPETITIONS_014. The comment at mixins.go:180-184 already observed "the captured HmIP-MP3P and HmIP-WRCD descriptions both end at REPETITIONS_014" and treated that as a per-device narrowing — it is not. It is the firmware's fixed list for that parameter on every device. The only place a higher number is legal is the MASTER/LINK profile-repetition config parameters, built with getNames(256), which top out at REPETITIONS_254; no path in this repo writes those. So 18 is neither 14 nor 254.

The consequence is live on one of the two writers. internal/model/custom/light/sound_led.go:321 calls custom.RepetitionsLabel(cfg.Repetitions) and stages the result with no membership check, so cfg.Repetitions in 15..18 produces REPETITIONS_015..REPETITIONS_018 — labels absent from the device's VALUE_LIST — and the CCU rejects or drops the parameter. TextDisplay.WriteWithSound does check against availableRepetitions, so it fails those counts client-side. A third variant: siren/sound.go's ConvertPlayRepetitionsIndex uses the index as a slot into the device list and then clamps (`if slot >= len(availableRep) { slot = len(availableRep)-1 }`), so RepetitionsIndex 15..18 against the real 16-entry list silently resolves to the last slot — INFINITE_REPETITIONS. Asking for 15 repeats starts an unbounded one. Lowering the shared ceiling to 14 removes all three.
all.negativeControl: Had 18 been the firmware's ceiling, createRepetitionParameter would call Repetitions.getNames(20) and the MP3P/WRCD descriptors would carry 20-entry VALUE_LISTs ending REPETITIONS_018, INFINITE_REPETITIONS. The measurement does distinguish: the same two reads return 16/REPETITIONS_014 for the state parameter and 256/REPETITIONS_254 for the config parameters, i.e. the check separates the two surfaces and returns a different number for each.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld in both halves, and I verified the surface question the prior finding turns on rather than taking it on trust.

Grammar: confirmed verbatim. The firmware's own format string is "REPETITIONS_%03d", NO_REPETITION is index 0 and INFINITE_REPETITIONS is the last index — exactly the three constants and the zero-padded three-digit form mixins.go declares.

Ceiling: contradicted, and 18 matches no surface. I traced all three writers to their paramset: light/sound_led.go:344 stages hmenum.ParameterRepetitions into a map put through custom.PutOrSet(…, hmenum.ParamsetKeyValues, …) at :355; textdisplay.go:722-724 into a ParamsetKeyValues PutParamset; siren/sound.go:368 into a ParamsetKeyValues PutOrSet. All three hit the VALUES parameter, which the firmware builds with getNames(16) — numbered run stops at 014. The comment at mixins.go:180-184 reads the two captured descriptors as a per-device narrowing; it is not one, it is the firmware's fixed list for that parameter on every device. The 254 surface exists only on MASTER/LINK profile parameters, and `grep -rn PROFILE_REPETITIONS internal/ pkg/ assets/` returns nothing — no path in this repo writes those. So 18 is neither 14 nor 254.

The three consequences the prior finding names all check out in the code: sound_led.go:321 calls custom.RepetitionsLabel(cfg.Repetitions) and stages the result with no membership check, so 15..18 emit labels absent from the device list; TextDisplay.WriteWithSound (textdisplay.go:677-678) does check slices.Contains(t.availableRepetitions, …) and fails client-side; and ConvertPlayRepetitionsIndex (sound.go:278-296) sets slot = index then clamps `if slot >= len(availableRep) { slot = len(availableRep)-1 }`, so against the real 16-entry list every index in 15..18 resolves to slot 15 — INFINITE_REPETITIONS. Asking for 15 repeats starts an unbounded siren. Lowering the shared ceiling to 14 removes all three; the clamp should become an error rather than a silent slide to the last slot.

all.title: ScheduleChannelNo 999 is a bare sentinel for the two group thermostats
all.ourValue: ScheduleChannelNo = 999
