Tier 2 is silent: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_wds_v1_1.xml:79-88 declares both as `<logical type="integer"/>` with no min, max or special_value.
all.finding: Our two claims that matter are confirmed, and one boundary is one unit too tight. Confirmed: 128 (0x80) is the CCU's own no-signal marker — HMIPApplicationHandler tests `(getRssiValue() & 0xFF) != 128` before publishing RSSI_PEER — and it must be dropped client-side because the same method publishes RSSI_DEVICE with no such test, so a raw 128 (from the signed byte -128 negated) does reach us. Confirmed: the two encodings our bands straddle are real. BidCoS negates an UNSIGNED byte (`-1*GetByteData(13)`, `-Data().GetUInt8Value(2)`), giving [-255,-1] where the magnitude is the dBm figure; HmIP negates a SIGNED byte, giving mostly positive values (+70 meaning -70 dBm). Our band 3 (`-256 < v < -129 -> -v-256`) is exactly the two's-complement reinterpretation of a BidCoS byte >= 130, and band 2 (`1 < v < 127 -> -v`) is exactly the HmIP case. Narrowed: the firmware's rejected set is {128} plus BidCoS's INVALID_RSSI_VALUE = -65535 and the `if(receiver && rssi)` suppression of 0; our strict inequalities additionally discard -129, -127, 1 and 127, which the firmware publishes as ordinary readings — HmIP byte -127 negated is exactly 127 and passes every firmware guard; BidCoS bytes 127 and 129 yield -127 and -129. The boundary runs at |128| exactly, not at the exclusive |127|/|129| our bands use. -65535 is correctly dropped by our fall-through, but by no named rule. Which source to follow: Tier 1, not the descriptor — the shipped device XMLs declare RSSI as a bare integer with no bounds and no special values, so a per-device MIN/MAX read at runtime carries nothing here.
all.negativeControl: Had 128 not been a sentinel, HMIPApplicationHandler would publish RSSI_PEER unconditionally like it does RSSI_DEVICE; the `& 0xFF != 128` test is present and is the only value-dependent guard in that method. Had the wire value been plain dBm rather than a negated byte, there would be no `* -1` in IncomingHMIPFrameHandler and no `-1*GetByteData(13)` in RFDevice.cpp — both are present, on both stacks.
all.ourValue: reject -127, 0, 1, 127, 128, 129 and |v| >= 256; accept everything else via the four bands
all.firmwareValue: reject 128 only (HmIP, and only enforced by the CCU for RSSI_PEER); BidCoS emits [-255,-1] with 0 suppressed at source and -65535 (INVALID_RSSI_VALUE) for 'never measured'; declared HmIP logical range is min -128 / max 127
all.challengeNote: UPHELD as narrowed, with two corrections to the prior narrowing itself. (1) OVERSTATED: 'BidCoS emits [-255,-1] with 0 suppressed at source' holds only for RSSI_DEVICE on the ACK/INFO_STATUS path (RFDevice.cpp:505). The two paths that set RSSI_PEER — BidcosInterfaceConcentrator.cpp:382 (response frames) and :854 (received frames) — guard only against INVALID_RSSI_VALUE, so a frame byte of 0 becomes RSSI_PEER = 0 and reaches our client. Our rejection of 0 is therefore load-bearing, not redundant, and the prior agent's account would have let it be removed as dead. (2) NOT PERFORMABLE, and it is one of our four bands: band 4 (`129 < v < 256 -> v-256`) is unreachable from either firmware stack. BidCoS negates an unsigned byte and so publishes only [-255, 0]; HmIP negates a signed byte and so publishes at most 128. Nothing in Tier 1 produces 130..255 on RSSI_DEVICE or RSSI_PEER, so no firmware evidence can confirm or refute that band's transformation — it can only be grounded on a source neither tree carries (CUxD or Homegear descriptors). (3) A limit the prior agent stated as fact but did not ground: band 3's transformation `-v-256` reinterprets the CCU's own `-1 * unsigned char` result as a signed char. The firmware never does that reinterpretation anywhere; what Tier 1 establishes is only that values in [-255,-130] arrive, not what they mean. Call the arrival measured and the meaning unverified. Confirmed unchanged: 128 is the CCU's no-signal marker and does reach us on RSSI_DEVICE (the &0xFF test guards RSSI_PEER alone), so dropping it client-side is required; -65535 is correctly dropped, though by fall-through rather than a named rule; our extra exclusions of -129, -127, 1 and 127 discard values both stacks can publish, the firmware's own boundary sitting at |128| exactly. Which source to follow: Tier 1. The HmIP descriptor declares min -128/max 127 yet the same server publishes 128 on RSSI_DEVICE, and the BidCoS XMLs declare no bounds at all, so a per-device MIN/MAX read at runtime carries nothing here.

all.title: FixedColorLight `slot` is cast straight to a FixedColor ordinal on the strength of an uncited claim about the descriptor's COLOR value order
all.site: internal/central/adapter/custom_dp_dispatcher.go:373-388 (`light.FixedColor(slot)`), with internal/model/custom/light/color.go:451-458 (the ordinals) and :576-581 (`Color()` casting the CCU's raw enum index)
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/DIMMER_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/getColorElement.tcl:10-17 `set options(0) "${BLACK}" / options(1) "${BLUE}" / options(2) "${GREEN}" / options(3) "${TURQUOISE}" / options(4) "${RED}" / options(5) "${PURPLE}" / options(6) "${YELLOW}" / options(7) "${WHITE}"` (identical files under easymodes/UNIVERSAL_ACTOR/ and easymodes/UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER_PWM/); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/msg/setDimmerVirtualReceiverCombinedParam.htm:11,13 (`<option value="3">TURQUOISE`, `<option value="5">PURPLE`); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/controls/dimmer.fn:89 and opticalsignalreceiver.fn:65 (`"${lblOff}\t${optionColorBLUE}\t${optionColorGREEN}\t${optionColorTURQUOISE}\t${optionColorRED}\t${optionColorPURPLE}\t${optionColorYELLOW}\t${optionColorWHITE}"`). HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SimpleRGBColor — BLACK(0), BLUE(1), GREEN(2), TURQUOISE(3), RED(4), PURPLE(5), YELLOW(6), WHITE(7), RANDOM(253), OLD_VALUE(254), DO_NOT_CARE(255) — whose #getNames(false) supplies the first eight names, in that order, as the legacy VALUE_LIST.
all.finding: The comment's claim is confirmed verbatim by Tier 1 on both stacks: the CCU's COLOR value list is the RGB bit pattern (bit0 blue, bit1 green, bit2 red) — 0 BLACK, 1 BLUE, 2 GREEN, 3 TURQUOISE, 4 RED, 5 PURPLE, 6 YELLOW, 7 WHITE. The cast it justifies is nevertheless wrong in both directions. Our light.FixedColor ordinals are 0 BLACK, 1 RED, 2 GREEN, 3 YELLOW, 4 BLUE, 5 MAGENTA("PURPLE"), 6 CYAN("TURQUOISE"), 7 WHITE: only 0, 2, 5 and 7 coincide; 1<->4 (RED/BLUE) and 3<->6 (YELLOW/TURQUOISE) are transposed. So `set_color {"slot": 4}` from any caller holding the CCU's own index writes "BLUE" where the firmware means RED. The read path has the same defect and no documentation: FixedColorLight.color is a generic.Select whose Value() is the raw VALUE_LIST index the CCU pushed, and color.go:576-581 casts it straight to FixedColor, so a device reporting the firmware's BLUE(1) surfaces as RED through Color()/ColorName() — while ChannelHsColor() (color.go:672-688) resolves CHANNEL_COLOR by NAME via custom.EnumLabelValue and gets it right, so the two accessors disagree about the same colour. SetColor's optimistic `l.color.OnEvent(int32(c))` (color.go:606) writes our ordinal into that same index-valued DP, so the disagreement persists until the CCU echo arrives. One further hazard the source carries and our enum does not: SimpleRGBColor's extended set is sparse (RANDOM 253, OLD_VALUE 254, DO_NOT_CARE 255), so on any device declaring the extended list the VALUE_LIST index and the wire value diverge above 7 as well.
all.negativeControl: Had the descriptor list matched our enum, the CCU's own colour selectors would read BLACK, RED, GREEN, YELLOW, BLUE, ... — four independent firmware sites (three easymode getColorElement.tcl files, dimmer.fn, opticalsignalreceiver.fn, setDimmerVirtualReceiverCombinedParam.htm) instead all read BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, TURQUOISE, RED, PURPLE, YELLOW, WHITE, and SimpleRGBColor assigns those same ordinals explicitly rather than by declaration order.
all.ourValue: FixedColor: 0 BLACK, 1 RED, 2 GREEN, 3 YELLOW, 4 BLUE, 5 PURPLE, 6 TURQUOISE, 7 WHITE
all.firmwareValue: COLOR: 0 BLACK, 1 BLUE, 2 GREEN, 3 TURQUOISE, 4 RED, 5 PURPLE, 6 YELLOW, 7 WHITE (+ RANDOM 253, OLD_VALUE 254, DO_NOT_CARE 255)
all.challengeNote: UPHELD for the read path, which is the half that is a live defect; the other two halves of the prior finding need correcting. CONFIRMED: FixedColorLight.color is a generic.Select bound to the raw COLOR wire parameter (color.go:481, custom.SelectField), its Value() is the VALUE_LIST index, and crRFD.conf:47 plus DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue prove the CCU sends exactly that index. Color() at color.go:576-581 casts it straight to FixedColor, so a device reporting BLUE(1) surfaces as RED and TURQUOISE(3) as YELLOW; only 0, 2, 5 and 7 coincide. ColorName() inherits it, while ChannelHsColor() (color.go:676-688) resolves CHANNEL_COLOR by NAME through custom.EnumLabelValue and gets it right — the two accessors disagree about the same colour, and the fix is one line (l.color.Label(), which generic.Select already provides). CONFIRMED: SetColor's optimistic `l.color.OnEvent(int32(c))` at color.go:604 writes our ordinal into an index-valued DP, so the disagreement persists until the CCU echo lands. OVERSTATED — the write path: the prior agent presents `set_color {"slot": 4}` writing BLUE-for-RED as a defect. It is a documented contract. custom_dp_dispatcher.go:373-376 says in as many words that the descriptor's value list is ordered by the RGB bit pattern and that a caller holding only the descriptor must use "label"; SetColorByName (color.go:610-621) is that path, and it resolves through fixedColorNames to the string the CCU parses. The write path is correct for a caller that reads its own API. REFUTED — the 'one further hazard': the prior agent claims that on a device declaring the extended list, VALUE_LIST index and wire value diverge above 7 because SimpleRGBColor is sparse at 253/254/255. Wrong surface. Those are the HmIP-internal physical bytes; StringEnumToInteger converts them to the enum NAME, and DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue then converts the name to a dense ordinal into getEnumStrings() before it reaches legacy XML-RPC. The observed Tier-2 VALUE_LIST is 10 dense entries with no gap. Nothing sparse crosses our wire.

all.title: Event sources are attached for VALUES only, on an unread assertion that no MASTER parameter carries the EVENT operation
all.citation: Bit semantics: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:53-59 `OP_NONE=0, OP_READ=1, OP_WRITE=2, OP_EVENT=4, OP_DETERMINE=8`; parsing and default at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:30 `operations=(OP_READ|OP_WRITE);` and :55-61 (`if(strstr(temp,"event"))operations|=OP_EVENT;`), matching the schema default at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/device.xsd:1079 `<xsd:attribute name="operations" type="xsd:string" default="read,write" use="optional">`; the OPERATIONS word is emitted from the parameter alone, with no paramset-type input (HSSParameter.cpp:209 `(*val)["OPERATIONS"]=operations;`). Corpus measurement over all 142 shipped device XMLs (../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml + hs485types/*.xml), resolving every `<subset ref=...>` into `paramset_defs`: MASTER 3273 parameters, 0 with event; LINK 6947, 0 with event; VALUES 2536, of which 1956 carry event. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getParamsetDescription routes MASTER to getConfigurationDescription() and adds the EVENT-carrying synthetic parameters only under `parameterSetType.equals("VALUES")` — DeviceUtil#addSpecialParameter (UPDATE_PENDING, READ|EVENT), #addLongPressParameter (PRESS_LONG_START / PRESS_LONG_RELEASE, EVENT), #createParameterDescriptionForExtendedServiceParam (EVENT); every one of the 292 de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.ConfigurationParameter constructions in the tree is built with AbstractParameterFactory#getRWIOOperations (READ|WRITE) or #getReadIOOperations (READ).
all.finding: The claim holds on both stacks, though our code's stated reason for it does not. Not one MASTER-paramset parameter in the shipped BidCoS/wired device XMLs declares the event bit, and none can acquire it implicitly: the schema default when `operations` is absent is read,write, and the firmware parses it by substring on the parameter element alone. On the HmIP side the MASTER description is assembled from ConfigurationParameters, which are only ever READ|WRITE or READ, and every EVENT-carrying parameter HMIPServer synthesises is gated behind an explicit VALUES check. Two side notes for the same block. First, the comment's supporting argument is genuinely circular as the reader suspected — the OPERATIONS=0 fix-up says nothing about an incoming EVENT bit — but the conclusion it defends is right for an independent reason: the firmware never sets that bit outside VALUES. Second, no paramset_def in the corpus is referenced from more than one paramset type, so the shared-definition route by which an event parameter could leak into MASTER is closed as well.
all.negativeControl: The same scan reports 1956 VALUES parameters carrying `event` (the KEY PRESS_* family among them), so it demonstrably reacts to the bit it is looking for; a MASTER parameter with event would have been printed by name and file. On the HmIP side the check would have shown a ConfigurationParameter built with IOOperations.EVENT, or an addSpecialParameter/addLongPressParameter call outside the VALUES branch — neither exists.
all.ourValue: event sources attached only when key == ParamsetKeyValues && Operations.IsEvent()
all.firmwareValue: OPERATIONS bit 4 (event) appears on VALUES parameters only; MASTER 0/3273 and LINK 0/6947 in the shipped XMLs, and every HmIP ConfigurationParameter is READ|WRITE or READ
all.challengeNote: DEMOTED from confirmed to narrowed. The measurement holds and I reproduced it end to end on two independent corpora, one of which (the pydevccu capture, 129k parameters including HmIP) the prior agent did not use: no MASTER, LINK or SERVICE parameter anywhere carries the event bit, and none can acquire it implicitly, since the schema default is read,write and the firmware parses `operations` by substring on the parameter element alone. The HmIP side closes independently — MASTER is assembled from ConfigurationParameters, which are only ever READ|WRITE or READ, and every synthetic EVENT parameter is behind a VALUES gate. The prior agent's precision slips slightly ('every one of the 292 constructions is built with getRWIOOperations or getReadIOOperations' — 58 use an inline IOOperations instead, though none carries EVENT), which does not move the conclusion. What does move it is scope. This project treats CUxD as a first-class interface over BIN-RPC (CLAUDE.md, TestCuxdUsesBINRPCBackend), and CUxD is a third-party daemon whose device descriptions live in neither OpenCCU-Base nor HMIPServer; the same is true of HomegearBackend. device_pipeline.go is interface-agnostic, so the code's claim 'No MASTER parameter carries EVENT in practice' is asserted over a device population wider than any source measured. That is exactly the input the sources do not carry, so the honest verdict is narrowed with the boundary named, not confirmed. The comment's own supporting argument remains circular as the reader suspected: the OPERATIONS==0 fix-up two lines above only rewrites a zero word and says nothing about an incoming EVENT bit. The conclusion is right for the CCU's own two stacks, for a reason the comment does not give.

all.title: The click-parameter button/event split rests on an OPERATIONS-bit claim about specific channel types
all.citation: Bit values: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:53-59 (OP_READ=1, OP_WRITE=2, OP_EVENT=4) and HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations, whose #toString maps 5 -> "read,event", 6 -> "write,event", 7 -> "read,write,event". Corpus measurement of PRESS_* parameters in VALUES paramsets over ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml + hs485types/*.xml (subsets resolved): channel type KEY — PRESS_SHORT `write,event` (6) in 29 RF XMLs (e.g. rf_4dis.xml, rf_dis_ep_wm55.xml), `event,write` (6) in 5 wired XMLs (hmw_io12_sw7_dr.xml, hmw_io_sr_fm.xml, hmw_lc_bl1_dr.xml, ...), `event,read,write` (7) in 3 wired XMLs (hmw_io12_sw7_dr_V3_02.xml, hmw_lc_bl1_dr_V3_02.xml, hmw_lc_sw2_dr_V3_02.xml); KEY PRESS_LONG same distribution (25 x 6 RF, 5 x 6 wired, 3 x 7 wired); KEY PRESS_CONT `event` (4) 20x; KEY PRESS_LONG_RELEASE `event` (4) 19x; CENTRAL_KEY PRESS_SHORT/LONG/CONT/LONG_RELEASE all `event` (4) (rf_rc_19.xml); VIRTUAL_KEY PRESS_SHORT/PRESS_LONG `write,event` (6) (rf_central.xml, hmw_central.xml); INPUT_OUTPUT 6 or 7; SWITCH_INTERFACE PRESS 6; ecoKEY PRESS_SHORT 6. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory#createEventActionIntegerParameter builds PRESS_SHORT, PRESS_LONG, PRESS_LOCK and PRESS_UNLOCK with `byte ops = IOOperations.EVENT` alone, and it is the sole definition of PRESS_SHORT in that tree, registered under the "default" ParameterMapKey so it applies to every HmIP channel type including KEY_TRANSCEIVER and MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER.
all.finding: The rule the code actually implements — writable press becomes a button, non-writable stays an event — is confirmed by both stacks, and the two headline numbers are right: a BidCoS KEY channel's PRESS_SHORT is 6 (29 of 37 declarations; the remainder are the same bit pattern written in a different order), and every HmIP press parameter is 4, from a single definition that no channel type overrides. Three corrections to the enumeration in the comment. (1) 6 is write|event, not read+write — the CCU's own IOOperations#toString renders 6 as "write,event"; the code's phrasing ('carries the WRITE bit') is right, but any downstream reading of 6 as read+write is not. (2) 'OPS=6' is not exhaustive for KEY: the three HMW V3_02 device XMLs declare 7 (read,write,event). Both still set the WRITE bit, so the button verdict is unchanged; the comment's number is what narrows. (3) The comment groups 'the central/long-press parameters' with the event-only OPS=4 set. That holds for PRESS_CONT (4, 20x), PRESS_LONG_RELEASE (4, 19x) and every CENTRAL_KEY parameter (4), but NOT for PRESS_LONG on a KEY channel, which is 6 in 30 of 33 declarations and 7 in the rest — i.e. writable, and a button. If 'long-press' there is read as PRESS_LONG, the boundary runs one parameter wider than the comment says; if it means PRESS_LONG_RELEASE, the comment is exact. VIRTUAL_KEY presses are 6 as well, but applyClickEventMarks skips IsVirtualRemote() devices, so they never reach this test.
all.negativeControl: The same corpus scan separates OPS values per (channel type, parameter) and does report 4 for CENTRAL_KEY, PRESS_CONT and PRESS_LONG_RELEASE, so it distinguishes 4 from 6 rather than reporting one value throughout; had KEY PRESS_SHORT been event-only it would have appeared in that 4-valued group. On the HmIP side, a writable transmitter press would show as a second PRESS_SHORT definition or a non-"default" ParameterMapKey; grepping the whole tree yields exactly one definition, and it is EVENT-only.

all.title: The reachability parameter set is a bare string literal list that includes CONFIG_PENDING, which the model's own reachability rule does not read
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.h:45 `FLAG_UNREACH=(1<<0), //!< Gerät ist aktuell nicht erreichbar`; :46 `FLAG_STICKY_UNREACH=(1<<1), //!< Gerät war nicht erreichbar`. Sole producer of both events: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1351 `void RFDevice::UpdateUnreachFlags(BidcosFrame* frame)` — :1359-1362 clears FLAG_UNREACH and fires `SendInternalValueEvent("UNREACH")` on a received frame, :1371-1380 sets FLAG_UNREACH+FLAG_STICKY_UNREACH and fires both events when called with NULL (from :627 `case TIMER_CYCLIC_TIMEOUT: unreach_reason = BidcosFrame::UNREACH_CYCLIC_TIMEOUT; UpdateUnreachFlags(NULL);`). CONFIG_PENDING is a disjoint concept: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:771-781 `bool RFDevice::IsConfigPending()` reads only the AES-key mismatch, `config_data_dirty`, `delete_deferred_flags` and the per-channel `IsConfigPending()`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1026-1040 `CheckConfigPendingEvent` emits `SendInternalValueEvent("CONFIG_PENDING", val)` only when that verdict itself changed, and never reads `maintenance_flags`. Wired mirrors the split: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Device.cpp:57-65 (CONFIG_PENDING) vs :92-105 (UNREACH/STICKY_UNREACH on send failure/success). HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.VertxNotificationUtil#setDeviceToUnreach sets channel-0 `UNREACH`=Boolean.TRUE and publishes it; #createAndSendConfigPending sets channel-0 `CONFIG_PENDING` from de.eq3.cbcs.devicemanagement.IDevice#isAnyConfigurationTransmissionPending — no reachability input. Tier 2: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_s_644.xml:156 declares `<parameter id="STICKY_UNREACH" operations="read,write,event" ui_flags="service,sticky">`.
all.finding: Our model's rule is right; the adapter's set is not. Firmware carries exactly two reachability signals, UNREACH (current) and STICKY_UNREACH (latched), both produced only by RFDevice::UpdateUnreachFlags. CONFIG_PENDING is computed from pending configuration transfer and never consults the unreach flags, on rfd, on hs485d and on the HmIP server alike. So including CONFIG_PENDING in isReachabilityParameter is contradicted: it runs refreshDeviceAvailability for an event that cannot have changed IsReachable(), and — because the set is also what bypasses the "only ever flip online" guard at eventbridge.go:1665 — a CONFIG_PENDING event on an offline device can drive the offline branch of markAvailability with a verdict no reachability signal produced. Two boundary facts our code should follow. (1) STICKY_UNREACH exists only on BidCoS: the HmIP state model has no such parameter (the only STICKY_UNREACH strings in the HmIP server are in de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.bidcos.DefaultBidCosGroupDefinitionProvider, a BidCoS group definition). Our fallback chain is therefore BidCoS-only in effect — harmless, since it is a fallback, but it means HmIP reachability rests on UNREACH alone. (2) UNREACH/STICKY_UNREACH are not booleans on BidCoS: RFDevice.cpp:678-700 returns `unreach_reason == 0 ? 1 : unreach_reason`, i.e. one of BidcosFrame.h:32-36 UNREACH_FALSE=0, UNREACH_NO_RESPONSE=1, UNREACH_CYCLIC_TIMEOUT=2, UNREACH_INTERFACE_DUTYCYCLE=3, UNREACH_RF_BUSY=4 — any non-zero means unreachable. On HmIP the same parameter is Boolean. Separately, the reader's third claim is hearsay and wrong: internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:1223 is not a third copy of the reachability set — it is the HA device-class map, where UNREACH/STICKY_UNREACH map to "connectivity" and CONFIG_PENDING/UPDATE_PENDING map to "problem" a few lines below (:1231). There are two copies of the set, not three.
all.negativeControl: Had CONFIG_PENDING been a reachability signal, RFDevice::IsConfigPending would read `maintenance_flags` (or UpdateUnreachFlags would touch the config-pending state) — instead the two functions share no state, and CheckConfigPendingEvent is reached from CommitPendingConfig and from GetLinks, never from the unreach path. Had UNREACH/STICKY_UNREACH not been the pair, RFDevice.h:45-46 would not comment them "currently not reachable"/"was not reachable", and a search for the producer of those two events would return something other than the single function UpdateUnreachFlags.
all.ourValue: isReachabilityParameter = {UNREACH, STICKY_UNREACH, CONFIG_PENDING}
all.firmwareValue: reachability signals = {UNREACH, STICKY_UNREACH} (BidCoS) / {UNREACH} (HmIP); CONFIG_PENDING = pending-configuration flag, orthogonal
all.challengeNote:
The firmware half is confirmed: CONFIG_PENDING is computed from pending configuration transfer and never reads the unreach flags, on rfd, hs485d and the HmIP server alike. So the comment at eventbridge.go:1322 calling CONFIG_PENDING one of "the three parameters that carry reachability" is contradicted, and CONFIG_PENDING does not belong in the set on its stated grounds. But TWO of the reader's supporting claims fail and the finding must be demoted from a delivery defect to a comment/naming defect.

(1) The delivery consequence is refuted. refreshDeviceAvailability (eventbridge.go:1660) computes `online := dev.Available()`, and internal/model/device/device.go:350 is `func (d *Device) Available() bool { return d.availability.IsReachable() }` — which reads only the forced override, UNREACH and STICKY_UNREACH (availability.go:126-140). CONFIG_PENDING can never contribute to the verdict; it can only act as an extra TRIGGER to re-evaluate, and markAvailability's transition cache turns a re-evaluation with an unchanged verdict into a no-op. "a CONFIG_PENDING event ... can drive the offline branch of markAvailability with a verdict no reachability signal produced" is wrong on its load-bearing clause: every verdict markAvailability ever sees was produced by a reachability signal.

(2) Boundary fact (2) is a wrong-surface claim and is refuted outright. The reader read the INTERNAL C++ value (RFDevice.cpp:678-700, `(int&)(*val)= unreach_reason == 0 ? 1:unreach_reason;` — that quote IS verbatim) and reported it as what the XML-RPC client sees. It is not. Every shipped descriptor declares UNREACH/STICKY_UNREACH `<logical type="boolean"/>` over `<physical type="integer">` with no explicit conversion, so HSSParameter::InitFromXml (src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:174-191) synthesises the default `type_conversion_boolean_integer`, whose PhysicalToLogical is `(bool&)*out=(((int&)in>=lower_threshold) && ((int&)in<=upper_threshold)) != invert;` with constructor defaults lower_threshold=1, upper_threshold=INT_MAX, invert=false (src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionBooleanInteger.cpp). PhysicalToLogical runs on the event path before delivery (HSSParameter.cpp:366). The CCU therefore folds "any non-zero means unreachable" into a Boolean ITSELF, before the wire. Our `channel0Bool`'s `raw.(bool)` assertion is correct, not fragile; acting on the reader's advice would have been a change against a value our client never receives.

Boundary fact (1) — STICKY_UNREACH is BidCoS-only — I uphold on Tier 1 (the HMIPServer grep above). Tier 2 corroboration was not performable: ../pydevccu/paramsets_db.json is an empty JSON object in this checkout, so no descriptor corpus carrying HmIP VALUES paramsets was available.

The reader's rebuttal of the third claim is confirmed: internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:1223 is the HA device-class map (UNREACH/STICKY_UNREACH -> "connectivity", CONFIG_PENDING/UPDATE_PENDING -> "problem" at :1231), not a copy of the reachability set. Correct on that point.

LONG 0..0xFFFFFFFFFFFF; the write targets are #createWeekProgramTargetChannelLockParameter and #createWeekProgramTargetChannelLocksParameter, both `IOOperations.WRITE` only. Sole producer of the value: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler#handleStatusData, cases FLAG_REGISTER_24 and FLAG_REGISTER_48, each calling de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationFrameHandlingUtil#tryConvertParameter with "WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS". Change gate, verbatim from #tryConvertParameter: `if (notificationSettings.isNotifyUnchangedStatusEnabled() || oldValue == null || oldValue.getValue() == null || !oldValue.getValue().equals(logicalValue))`. Write path: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#convertCombinedParameter maps `WPTCL` → WEEK_PROGRAM_TARGET_CHANNEL_LOCK and `WPTCLS` → WEEK_PROGRAM_TARGET_CHANNEL_LOCKS, and #getParameterSetForChannelType pairs both into one paramset. Bit semantics: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleRestoreWeekProfile reads WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS as `channelsInManuMode` and iterates `for (int i = 0; i < 48; ++i) { long bitValue = 1 << i; ... }`. Enum ordinals: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.WeekProgramTargetChannelLock = MANU_MODE(0), AUTO_MODE_WITH_RESET(1), AUTO_MODE_WITHOUT_RESET(2).
all.finding: The 3-second number cannot be settled from any source: no CCU source carries a pre-write echo duration for WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS. The five HmIP-server compilation units that mention the parameter contain no timer, timeout or delay bound to it; the value is set only when a device status frame (FLAG_REGISTER_24/48) is converted. The quantity the constant models — how long a device keeps reporting the old bitfield after a radio write — is a device+radio round-trip property, not a firmware constant. Deciding it needs a timed wire capture of a real write, which no static source substitutes for. What the firmware does settle, and where our comment is off: (1) the CCU never synthesises this event from our own write — every WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS notification our daemon sees carries a value a device reported, so a "pre-write echo" can only be an in-flight device status frame that crossed the write, not a CCU-side echo; the comment's mechanism is not the firmware's. (2) "the CCU only pushes the parameter on change" is right by default but is a setting, not a law: #tryConvertParameter suppresses the notification only while `Notify.Unchanged.Status` is off; with it on, every status frame re-delivers the value. (3) "nothing re-delivers it" is narrower than the truth — the parameter is READ|EVENT, so getValue/getParamset on VALUES re-reads it at any time; nothing pushes it, but a pull exists and would be the sound recovery from a dropped update. Two adjacent values at the same site are confirmed: our COMBINED_PARAMETER rendering "WPTCLS=<bit>,WPTCL=<0|2>" hits the right keys and the right ordinals (0 = MANU_MODE, 2 = AUTO_MODE_WITHOUT_RESET), and the bitfield is `1 << i` over 48 channels with a set bit meaning MANU (schedule disabled).
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware carried an echo duration, it would appear as a timer or timeout constant on the WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS path — a delay before the state readback, or a command-confirmation window. Every file that names the parameter was read; none holds one, and the only writer of the parameter value is the received-status-frame branch. The check therefore returns the same "no constant" answer whether 3 s is right or wrong, which is exactly why the measurement is not performable rather than confirmed. Had claim (2) been wrong, #tryConvertParameter would put the value into changesStatusValues unconditionally; it does not. Had claim (3) been wrong, the parameter would be declared EVENT-only like SELF_CALIBRATION_RESULT; it is declared READ|EVENT.
all.missingInput: The elapsed time between a COMBINED_PARAMETER (WPTCL/WPTCLS) write being accepted and the device's next WEEK_PROGRAM_CHANNEL_LOCKS status frame carrying the new bit — a radio round-trip measurement. No CCU source carries it; only a timestamped wire capture against a real device can supply it.
all.ourValue: scheduleWriteHoldWindow = 3 * time.Second
all.firmwareValue: no such constant exists in any CCU source

all.title: Un-ignore candidates require both READ and EVENT on VALUES, which excludes every event-only parameter
all.citation: Bit values: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:54-58 `OP_NONE=0`, `OP_READ=1`, `OP_WRITE=2`, `OP_EVENT=4 //!< Parameter kann über die XmlRpc-Schnittstelle ein Ereignis auslösen`, `OP_DETERMINE=8`. Parsing: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:55-61 — `temp=node.getAttribute("operations"); operations=OP_NONE; if(strstr(temp,"read"))operations|=OP_READ; if(strstr(temp,"write"))operations|=OP_WRITE; if(strstr(temp,"event"))operations|=OP_EVENT; ...`. Emission gate, verbatim: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:361-363 `void HSSParameter::ReportEvent(LogicalInstance* inst, XmlRpc::XmlRpcValue& phys_val) { if(!(operations & OP_EVENT))return;` — the only test is OP_EVENT; READ is never consulted. Reported to callers verbatim at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:209 `(*val)["OPERATIONS"]=operations;`. Tier 2 inventory over ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml, VALUES paramsets only, parameters whose operations contain event and not read: 64 total — INSTALL_TEST `operations="event"` in 37 files (e.g. rf_wds_v1_1.xml), PRESS_SHORT / PRESS_LONG `operations="event"`, `"write,event"` and `"event,write"` (e.g. rf_central.xml, rf_rc_19.xml, hmw_io_sr_fm.xml, hmw_lc_bl1_dr.xml), PRESS_CONT and PRESS_LONG_RELEASE `operations="event"` (rf_rc_19.xml), PRESS `operations="write,event"` (rf_swi.xml). HmIP side, same bits and the same shape: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations (`READ = 1`, `WRITE = 2`, `EVENT = 4`) and de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createEventEnumerationParameter, which builds `byte ops = IOOperations.EVENT` — used for SELF_CALIBRATION_RESULT and ACCESS_POINT_KEYPRESS.
all.finding: The justifying comment states the opposite of what bit 4 means, and the filter it justifies drops real parameters. The firmware emits a VALUES event on OP_EVENT alone (HSSParameter.cpp:363); READ plays no part. The shipped device XMLs declare 64 VALUES parameters with event set and read clear — OPERATIONS=4 or OPERATIONS=6 — and they are precisely the operator-interesting ones: every PRESS_SHORT / PRESS_LONG / PRESS_CONT / PRESS_LONG_RELEASE variant that carries a button press, plus INSTALL_TEST on 37 device types. Requiring `OperationsRead|OperationsEvent` on VALUES excludes all of them from GetUnIgnoreCandidates and from the grouped picker, so an operator can never un-ignore a suppressed button-press datapoint. The failure is silent — the picker just shows fewer rows. The firmware-faithful filter for VALUES is OPERATIONS & EVENT; if the intent is "can be surfaced at all", READ or EVENT (not READ and EVENT). The MASTER arm is untouched by this: MASTER parameters are read/written through paramsets, and requiring READ there is consistent with HSSParameter.cpp:209 exposing the same field. Note the two tiers agree here rather than diverge, which is worth stating: the daemon's rule (Tier 1) and what devices declare (Tier 2) both say event-without-read is a normal, supported shape, so our code should follow the descriptor's OPERATIONS verbatim and not impose an extra READ requirement of its own.
all.negativeControl: Had event-without-read not occurred in practice, the inventory over the shipped device XMLs would have returned zero VALUES parameters with `event` and without `read`; it returns 64, across 40-odd device types and both transports. Had OP_EVENT not been bit 4, HSSParameter.h:57 would carry a different value and OPERATIONS=4 would not be reachable by the parser at HSSParameter.cpp:60. Had READ been required for event delivery, HSSParameter::ReportEvent would test `operations & OP_READ` as well; its single guard is `if(!(operations & OP_EVENT))return;`.
all.ourValue: VALUES candidate iff ops.Has(OperationsRead|OperationsEvent)  — OPERATIONS=4 and OPERATIONS=6 rejected
all.firmwareValue: event delivery gated on OP_EVENT (4) alone; 64 shipped VALUES parameters declare OPERATIONS=4 or 6
all.challengeNote:
Upheld in full, and the effect is real, not hypothetical. I checked the one thing the reader asserted but did not demonstrate — that a real parameter is actually stranded. INSTALL_TEST is declared `operations="event"` (OPERATIONS=4) on 37 device types AND is a hard entry in our own suppression table at internal/store/visibility/rules.go:240 (`"INSTALL_TEST": {}`, with the explanatory comment at :237). A parameter that is forced-Ignored is precisely a candidate under GetUnIgnoreCandidates, and operationsMatchParamset then rejects it for lacking READ. That closes the loop: there is at least one shipped, actually-suppressed, actually-event-emitting parameter no operator can ever un-ignore, and it fails silently — the picker simply shows fewer rows.

Two corroborations worth recording. First, the tiers agree rather than diverge, which is unusual and strengthens the case: the daemon's own event resolver already encodes the correct rule at internal/central/adapter/datapoint_resolver.go:182-186 — "Click-event parameters (PRESS_SHORT / PRESS_LONG / …) are EVENT-only on the wire (OPERATIONS bit 4, no READ, no WRITE)" — and device_pipeline.go:1189-1192 names OPS=4 and OPS=6 explicitly. So queryfacade.go is the outlier inside our own codebase, not a considered divergence. Second, one refinement the reader missed that makes the case stronger, not weaker: HSSParameter::ReportEvent is the internal-value path; the FRAME path at HSSParameter.cpp:345-359 (ProcessIncomingFrame) gates delivery on `if(!hidden)` and does not test OP_EVENT at all. Neither path consults READ, on either surface.

The firmware-faithful filter for VALUES is `ops.Has(OperationsEvent)`; if the intent is "can be surfaced at all", it is READ OR EVENT, never READ AND EVENT. The MASTER arm is untouched — requiring READ there is consistent with HSSParameter.cpp:209 and with MASTER being a paramset read/write surface. Our bit values (pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:77-79: 1/2/4) match the firmware exactly, so the defect is purely the conjunction, not the encoding.

all.title: getLinks flags=0 rests on an unsourced claim about what bit 0 selects
all.site: internal/client/backends/ccu.go:270-278 (comment + call); internal/client/backends/homegear.go:198 (same literal, no comment)
all.citation: Bit layout, verbatim from ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/LogicalInstance.h:31-39: `//! Flag-Bits für die Parametrierung, was bei GetLinks() zurückgegeben werden soll` / `GL_FLAG_GROUP=0x01`, `GL_FLAG_SENDER_PARAMSET=0x02`, `GL_FLAG_RECEIVER_PARAMSET=0x04`, `GL_FLAG_SENDER_DESCRIPTION=0x08`, `GL_FLAG_RECEIVER_DESCRIPTION=0x10`, `GL_FLAG_CHECK_PEER=0x4000`. Same list in the method's own doc comment, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:362-388, which also states `flags ist optional. Defaultwert ist 0x00.` and lists the returned struct fields SENDER, RECEIVER, NAME, DESCRIPTION, SENDER_PARAMSET, RECEIVER_PARAMSET, SENDER_DESCRIPTION, RECEIVER_DESCRIPTION. Implementation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:637-638 fills the metadata unconditionally — `if(((std::string&)link["NAME"]).empty())link["NAME"]=it->second.name;` / `if(((std::string&)link["DESCRIPTION"]).empty())link["DESCRIPTION"]=it->second.description;` — with no flags test, while :666, :675, :686 and :692 gate SENDER_PARAMSET, RECEIVER_PARAMSET, SENDER_DESCRIPTION and RECEIVER_DESCRIPTION on GL_FLAG_SENDER_PARAMSET / GL_FLAG_RECEIVER_PARAMSET / GL_FLAG_SENDER_DESCRIPTION / GL_FLAG_RECEIVER_DESCRIPTION respectively, and :698-705 folds in the paired channel's links only `if(flags & GL_FLAG_GROUP)`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:627 ORs GL_FLAG_CHECK_PEER into the caller's flags whenever the address is non-empty.
all.finding: Both halves of the comment are wrong. Bit 0 is GL_FLAG_GROUP — "if address names a channel that is part of a group (a key pair), return the links of every channel in the group" — it has nothing to do with metadata. And flags=0 is not "full detail": it is the minimum, requesting neither paramset nor channel description. NAME and DESCRIPTION are returned regardless of flags (RFChannel.cpp:637-638), so the four fields we actually parse — SENDER, RECEIVER, NAME, DESCRIPTION, FLAGS — all arrive under flags=0. The literal is therefore harmless for the fields we read today, but it is right by accident, and the stated reason would mislead the next edit in both directions: someone "turning metadata off" would set bit 0 and silently start receiving the paired channel's links folded into the same result; someone wanting a link's parameter set would find flags=0 does not deliver it. One real behavioural gap follows from the correct reading: with flags=0 a getLinks on one half of a key pair does not return the partner channel's links, so the SPA's direct-link view is incomplete for grouped channels — GL_FLAG_GROUP=1 is the flag that fixes that, the opposite of what the comment implies. FLAGS validity is unaffected either way, because RFManager::GetLinks ORs GL_FLAG_CHECK_PEER in for any non-empty address (RFManager.cpp:627) whatever the caller passed. The Homegear copy is a Tier-3 surface — Homegear is not this firmware — so it is unverified here; it repeats the literal with no comment at all.
all.negativeControl: Had bit 0 been a metadata toggle, LogicalInstance.h:32 would name it so rather than GL_FLAG_GROUP with the comment about group members, and RFChannel::GetLinks would gate the NAME/DESCRIPTION assignments on it; those two assignments (RFChannel.cpp:637-638) sit outside every flags test, while the four fields that are flag-gated each carry an explicit `flags & GL_FLAG_*` condition. Had flags=0 meant full detail, XmlRpcMethods.cpp:378-380 would not describe 0x02/0x04/0x08/0x10 as the switches that cause those fields to be filled.
all.ourValue: flags = 0, documented as "bit 0 toggles link metadata; 0 = full detail"
all.firmwareValue: bit 0 = GL_FLAG_GROUP (0x01); NAME/DESCRIPTION always returned; 0 = least detail (no paramsets, no descriptions)
all.challengeNote:
Upheld: both halves of the comment are contradicted. Bit 0 is GL_FLAG_GROUP and concerns key-pair grouping, not metadata; flags=0 is the minimum request, not "full detail". NAME and DESCRIPTION arrive regardless of flags, so all five fields we parse (SENDER, RECEIVER, NAME, DESCRIPTION, FLAGS at ccu.go:287-300 — the reader wrote "four" and listed five) are delivered under flags=0. The literal is right by accident and the stated reason would mislead the next edit in both directions.

But the reader's "one real behavioural gap" is refuted and must not be carried forward. The claim was that flags=0 leaves the SPA's direct-link view incomplete for grouped channels. It does not, for two independent reasons I checked in our callers. First, of our four call sites, two pass a device address (internal/central/coordinators/link.go:149,183) and one passes "" (internal/central/adapter/links.go:192); both route through RFDevice::GetLinks, whose FIRST statement is `flags &= ~GL_FLAG_GROUP;` (../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1240) — the firmware strips bit 0 on any device-scoped query, so setting it there would change nothing at all. Second, the one per-channel call site, internal/central/adapter/links.go:77, sits inside `for _, ch := range dev.Channels()` and dedupes on `link.Sender + "->" + link.Receiver` (links.go:75-89) — we already fetch every channel of the device individually, so the pair partner's links are collected by the partner's own query. Setting GL_FLAG_GROUP would produce duplicates the dedup map discards, not new rows. There is no incompleteness to fix; the correct remedy is to correct the comment and leave the literal alone.

The homegear.go:198 copy stays unverified as the reader said — Homegear is not this firmware and its getLinks contract is not settled by OpenCCU-Base. It repeats the literal with no comment at all.

all.title: Two CCU-behaviour claims on the device-admin port have no source: the deleteDevice bitmask and the channel-rename cascade
all.site: pkg/interfaces/rest_ports.go:109-116; constants at internal/client/backends/backend.go:61-69; rename at internal/central/central.go:1062-1089
all.citation: (a) Bitmask, verbatim from ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:51-56: `//! Flags für DeleteDevice()` / `DELETE_FLAG_RESET=(1<<0), //!< Gerät in Werkszustand zurücksetzen` / `DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=(1<<1), //!< Löschen erzwingen, auch wenn Gerät nicht erreichbar` / `DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=(1<<2) //!< Wenn Gerät nicht erreichbar, bei nächster Gelegenheit löschen`. Same three in the XML-RPC doc comment ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:115-117 as 0x01 / 0x02 / 0x04. Semantics, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:913-931: `if (flags & DELETE_FLAG_RESET) { success = dev->FactoryReset(); } else { success = dev->UnpeerCentral(); }` then `if (!success) { if (flags & DELETE_FLAG_DEFER) { dev->ScheduleDelete(flags & ~DELETE_FLAG_DEFER); return true; } if (!(flags & DELETE_FLAG_FORCE)) return false; }`. Wire acceptance, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:126-130: booleans in params[1]/params[2] map to RESET/FORCE, and `if(params[1].getType()==XmlRpcValue::TypeInt)flags=params[1];` — the integer form overwrites, so our two-argument integer call is the documented path. (b) Rename: the OpenCCU distribution patch ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0099-WebUI-Add-DeviceRenameAllChannels.patch adds `DeviceConfigDialog.renameChannels`, which builds `var chNumber = channel.address.split(':')[1];` and `var chName = $(this.NAME_ID).value + $(this.SEPARATOR_ID).value + chNumber;` where the separator is a text input declared in the same patch as `<input id="DeviceConfigDialog_DeviceChannelsRenameSeparator" size="2" type="text" value=":"/>`; it also treats `this.device.name+":"+chNumber` as the un-renamed default name and skips channels that differ from it unless "including own names" is ticked. Corroborating the same convention inside the shipped firmware: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/pages/GroupEditPage.ftl:449 `homematic("Channel.setName", {id: channel.id, name: groupName+":"+parseInt(index + channelOffset)}, ...)`. Neither ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/webui/js/webui.js nor ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/webui.js contains renameChannels or the separator field.
all.finding: (a) is confirmed exactly and needs no change: DeleteFlagReset=1 and DeleteFlagForce=2 in internal/client/backends/backend.go:64,68 match DELETE_FLAG_RESET=(1<<0) and DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=(1<<1), with the right meanings — RESET selects FactoryReset() over UnpeerCentral(), FORCE decides only whether a failed unpair still removes the device. One narrowing worth writing down, because it changes what FORCE does: a third bit, DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=4, is checked before FORCE, and when set it swallows the failure, schedules the delete for the device's next contact and returns success. We never set it, so our FORCE semantics hold; but "the reset and force booleans map onto the bitmask" understates a surface that has three bits, and abortDeleteDevice (XmlRpcMethods.cpp:145-155) exists solely to cancel a deferred delete we cannot currently create. (b) is where the claim narrows. The pattern is right and the channel number is right — we compose `name + ":" + ch.Number` from the real channel number, matching the patch's `channel.address.split(':')[1]` rather than a list index — and the firmware's own HmIP group editor writes channel names the same way. But "matching the CCU WebUI behaviour" is true only one step in: the rename-all-channels dialog is an OpenCCU distribution patch, absent from the OCCU WebUI sources entirely, so on stock eQ-3 firmware there is no WebUI behaviour to match. Even on OpenCCU the separator is an operator-editable field whose default — not whose fixed value — is ":", and the dialog by default leaves manually renamed channels alone, which we do not: our loop renames every channel unconditionally. The boundary: our string is what the CCU produces with default settings, and it is what the CCU itself treats as a channel's default name, so a name catalogue we write stays consistent with one the CCU wrote. It is not what an operator who changed the separator, or who kept custom channel names, will see.
all.negativeControl: (a) Had the bits been swapped, RFManager.h:53-54 would read FORCE=(1<<0)/RESET=(1<<1) and RFManager::DeleteDevice would branch FactoryReset() on `flags & (1<<1)`; it branches on DELETE_FLAG_RESET, the (1<<0) constant. Had the integer form not been accepted, XmlRpcMethods.cpp:128 would have no `TypeInt` branch and our two-argument call would land on the boolean path with params[1] unmatched, sending flags=0. (b) Had the WebUI used a different pattern, the patch would build the name from something other than device name + separator + `address.split(':')[1]`, and GroupEditPage.ftl would not concatenate with a literal colon. Had the feature been stock, renameChannels would appear in the OCCU webui.js — searching both copies returns nothing, which is the different result the check was able to produce.
all.ourValue: DeleteFlagReset=1, DeleteFlagForce=2; channel name = name + ":" + ch.Number, applied to every channel
all.firmwareValue: DELETE_FLAG_RESET=1, DELETE_FLAG_FORCE=2, DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=4 (checked before FORCE); WebUI channel name = deviceName + <operator separator, default ":"> + channelNo, custom-named channels skipped by default, and only on OpenCCU-patched firmware
all.challengeNote:
Upheld with the reader's own narrowing intact, plus three corrections.

(a) confirmed exactly. Our two constants and their meanings match, RESET selects FactoryReset() over UnpeerCentral(), FORCE decides only whether a failed unpair still removes the device, and the third bit DELETE_FLAG_DEFER=4 is genuinely tested before FORCE and swallows the failure. We never set it, so our FORCE semantics hold; abortDeleteDevice exists solely to cancel a deferred delete we cannot currently create. I additionally checked the wire shape the reader asserted was "the documented path": XmlRpcMethodDeleteDevice::execute touches params[1] and params[2] unconditionally before the type tests, so a two-argument integer call is accepted and the integer form overwrites any boolean mapping. Confirmed.

(b) narrowed, as claimed, and our composition is sound: internal/central/central.go:1080 builds `name + ":" + strconv.Itoa(ch.Number)` where ch.Number comes from internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:2296 `channelNumber(addr)`, which parses the address suffix — the same derivation as the patch's `channel.address.split(':')[1]`, NOT an array index. We do not commit the ordinal-convention error here.

Three corrections to the reader. (i) The citation is wrong in form: the `.patch` file does not contain the JS quoted against it; the expanded directory does. A reader chasing the given path finds only translation strings and a CSS height change. (ii) GroupEditPage.ftl:449 is weaker corroboration than presented — it composes `groupName+":"+parseInt(index + channelOffset)`, an ARRAY-INDEX-derived number with a per-type offset (0 for HmIP-HEATING, else 1), not a parsed channel number. It corroborates the `<name>:<n>` shape only; on the number derivation it is an instance of exactly the convention this project bans, and must not be cited as authority for ch.Number. (iii) The reader called this a WebUI-behaviour claim and stopped at the patch. I looked for a stock Tier-1 source establishing `<devicename>:<channelno>` as the CCU's own default channel name at pairing and found none — no ReGa/tclrega naming site, and the only stock witness is the patch's own `origChName` treating that string as the un-renamed default. So the boundary is: our string is what an OpenCCU CCU produces at default settings and what the patched WebUI itself treats as a channel's default name; that it is the STOCK eQ-3 default is tier1-silent in this corpus. The divergence the reader named stands and is real — the dialog skips manually renamed channels by default, our loop at central.go:1080-1087 renames every channel unconditionally with no equivalent opt-in.

Tier 1 (BidCos-Wired): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485ChannelDescription.h:36 `enum{DIRECTION_NONE=0, DIRECTION_SENDER=1, DIRECTION_RECEIVER=2};`, emitted at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Channel.cpp:312. Tier 1 (HmIP): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil — the switch on the channel's LinkRole sets NONE→setDirection(0), SENDER→setDirection(1) with linkSourceRoles filled and linkTargetRoles cleared, RECEIVER→setDirection(2) with the reverse; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.VirtualRemoteControl sets 1 for a virtual-remote key channel and 0 for its maintenance channel. Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M.json — device root and MAINTENANCE carry DIRECTION 0, HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER / HEATING_ROOM_TH_TRANSCEIVER carry 1, every *_RECEIVER channel carries 2.
all.finding: The mapping is exactly right, and it is right on all three stacks — rfd, hs485d and the HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface all use the same three ordinals, so no interface-specific caveat is needed. Two things the comment gets wrong or leaves open. (1) `DIRECTION` is built as a bitmask internally (`direction|=DIRECTION_SENDER`), but rfd refuses to load a channel description that ends up with both bits set, so the wire value is always exactly one of {0,1,2}; treating it as an enum is safe, and a value of 3 would be a firmware bug, not an input to handle. (2) "Used for LINK paramset routing" is not true in this repo today: `hmproto.DeviceDescription.Direction` has no production reader. Every non-test `.Direction` in internal/ and pkg/ is something else — Matter's `req.Direction`, `cover.Direction()`, `lock.Direction()`, and `coordinators.DeviceLink.Direction`, which is the string "outgoing"/"incoming" derived from comparing SENDER/RECEIVER addresses (internal/central/coordinators/link.go:25,192), not this int. So the stated damage (inverted link routing) is not reachable from this field as wired; it is a correct value with no consumer. Bundle's related question, LINK FLAGS (pkg/hmproto/link.go:18, "CCU-internal flags (bitmask; typically 0)"): the bits are declared at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/LogicalInstance.h:42-45 — LINK_FLAG_SENDER_INVALID=0x01 (link broken on the sender side), LINK_FLAG_RECEIVER_INVALID=0x02, LINK_FLAG_SENDER_UNKNOWN=0x04 (sender device unknown to the CCU), LINK_FLAG_RECEIVER_UNKNOWN=0x08. "Typically 0" is right — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:653,655 sets FLAGS=0 for an intact link — but the four bits are named, meaningful and worth documenting: 0x01/0x02 are exactly the "broken link peer" condition the distribution patches around (../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0067-WebUI-Fix-BrokenLinkPeerList.patch).
all.negativeControl: Had the ordinals been inverted, RFChannelDescription.h would have read `DIRECTION_SENDER=2` / `DIRECTION_RECEIVER=1`, the HmIP DeviceUtil switch would have set 2 under `case SENDER`, and the pydevccu descriptors would have shown DIRECTION 2 on the *_TRANSCEIVER channels and 1 on the *_RECEIVER ones. All five independent readings gave the opposite, so the check can and does distinguish the two hypotheses.
all.challengeNote:
The ordinal mapping is upheld — I opened all three cited sites and the values are literal, not inferred. Two demotions from `confirmed`.

(1) The rule's own second clause is false and I confirmed it independently: `hmproto.DeviceDescription.Direction` has no production reader. A repo-wide `.Direction` grep outside tests returns only Matter's `req.Direction` (cluster/wire/colorcontrol.go:152, bridge/fields_reader.go:145), `lock.Direction()`, `cover.Direction()`, and `coordinators.DeviceLink.Direction` — a *string* "outgoing"/"incoming" (internal/central/coordinators/link.go:25,192). `sameDescription` (internal/central/coordinators/device.go:509-527) deliberately excludes it. Nothing that touches a LINK paramset consults it: internal/central/adapter/uischema_link.go asks the backend for `GetLinkParamsetDescription(ch.Address, peer)` and never reads DIRECTION. Beware a near-miss: `hmenum.ParameterDirection = "DIRECTION"` (pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:51) is a VALUES parameter on sirens, RGBW and locks — a different field with the same name, and it *is* read. A future reader following the comment will land on the wrong one.

(2) "the value 3 can never appear" is Tier-1 guaranteed on rfd only. hs485d builds `direction` with the identical `|=` bitmask but has no equivalent of RFChannelDescription.cpp:219-221 — a wired channel declaring `direction="sender receiver"`, or carrying both link_source_roles and link_target_roles, would emit 3. That no shipped wired device does is a Tier-2 fact (I parsed all 18 files under src/devicetypes/hs485types/ for a channel with both a `<source>` and a `<target>` under `<link_roles>`: none), not a firmware guarantee. Treating the field as a closed enum is still safe today; "can never" overstates it.

all.title: INT000 and CUX address prefixes classify a CCU address family from bare literals
all.ourValue: internalAddressPrefix = "INT000" (matches INT + 4-or-fewer significant digits); cuxdAddressPrefix = "CUX"
all.firmwareValue: The CCU builds the address as "INT" + the group id decimal, left-zero-padded to EXACTLY 7 digits (and truncated to the last 7 when longer). The firmware's own family discriminator is the 3-character prefix "INT", not "INT000".
all.citation: Tier 1 (HmIP/ReGa virtual-device side): HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.GroupDeviceAddressHelper#getVirtualDeviceAddressFromGroup — takes `Integer.toString(groupDevice.getId())`, truncates to the trailing 7 characters when longer than 7, otherwise left-pads with "0" in a `while (length != 7)` loop, and returns `"INT" + <that 7-char string>`; the inverse HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.GroupDeviceAddressHelper#getGroupIdFromVirtualDeviceAddress strips the channel suffix at ":", then `deviceAddress.substring("INT".length())` and `Integer.parseInt`. The CCU's own dispatcher test is HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.GroupDeviceDispatcher#isResponsible → `return address.startsWith("INT");`. Id allocation: HMServer de.eq3.lib.groupadministration.GroupAdministrationService#createGroupInternally → `group.setId(this.biggestUsedGroupId + 1)`, with `biggestUsedGroupId` initialised to 0 and raised to the maximum id found in the persisted group list at load — a monotone counter starting at 1, not a bounded pool. Tier 1 for CUxD: the CUxD add-on itself is in neither ../OpenCCU-Base nor ../OpenCCU, so the generator is unavailable; the CCU-side consumer is ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0027-WebUI-Fix-EmptyTableCUxDDevices.patch:8 — `(oEName.Find("CUxD.CUX") == -1)` in WebUI/www/rega/esp/datapointconfigurator.fn, i.e. the CCU's own WebUI discriminates CUxD datapoints on the literal address prefix "CUX". Tier 3 witness for where our rule came from: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/support.py:66-71 and :517 carry the same two literals with a near-identical comment.
all.finding: The CUX half is sound: the CCU's own WebUI keys on "CUxD.CUX", CUxD addresses observed across the corpora are uniformly CUX + 7 digits (CUX0000001, CUX2800001, CUX2801001, CUX0300001, CUX1234567 in ../aiohomematic), and our test is a bare 3-character prefix with no width assumption, so nothing can outgrow it. The INT half is where the rule is narrower than it looks. The firmware's grammar is INT + exactly 7 digits, and our constant hard-codes three of those seven as zeros. That is correct for every group id from 1 to 9999 — the whole realistic range for a household CCU — and wrong from id 10000 upward, where the address is INT0010000 and `strings.HasPrefix(address, "INT000")` returns false. Ids are handed out by a strictly increasing counter (biggestUsedGroupId + 1) that is only recomputed downward across a restart, so a CCU that creates and deletes groups repeatedly in one uptime reaches 10000 without ever holding 10000 groups. Past that boundary an INT address stops being central-scoped, two CCUs bridged into one Home Assistant declare the same unique_id, and per the file's own comment the loss is permanent once the retained payload lands. The boundary is worth naming even though it is unlikely to be crossed, and the fix is one character: match "INT" — the same test the CCU's own dispatcher uses — which is strictly safer, not merely equivalent. Also note the doc comment's example, `INT0001234`, is itself INT + 7 digits and therefore consistent with the firmware grammar; it is the constant, not the example, that is short. One residual I could NOT settle from Tier 1: whether a real BidCos/HmIP device serial could ever begin "CUX" or "INT" and be mis-scoped by the over-broad direction. Nothing in rfd or hs485d constrains the letter triple of a serial, so this stays unverified; the mitigation is that the CCU firmware itself accepts the same risk by dispatching on `startsWith("INT")`.
all.negativeControl: Had the numeric part been fixed at 4 digits (or the prefix been a literal "INT000" in the firmware), GroupDeviceAddressHelper would have padded to 4 and `getGroupIdFromVirtualDeviceAddress` would have sliced 6 characters, and grepping ../OpenCCU-Base for the literal "INT000" would have hit. Neither: the pad loop is `while (length != 7)`, the inverse strips only `"INT".length()`, and the literal "INT000" appears nowhere in the CCU sources. So the check does distinguish a 7-digit grammar from a shorter one.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, and the boundary the prior agent named is real: `strings.HasPrefix(address, "INT000")` is false from group id 10000 (address INT0010000) onward, and the counter is monotone within an uptime, so repeated create/delete reaches it without ever holding 10000 groups. I re-read all four cited symbols; the padding loop and both `startsWith("INT")` tests are literal.

What I demote is the prescription, not the measurement. "The fix is one character: match INT — strictly safer, not merely equivalent" is wrong for this file. This package is one side of a cross-implementation contract, and the contract is pinned as data: tests/contract/testdata/routing_key/unique_id_golden.json states in its own description field that "aiohomematic and py-openccu-loom-client MUST produce bit-identical output" and spells the rule as "hub / install_mode / program / sysvar / INT000* / CUX* / virtual-remote addresses are prefixed with the central_id". Widening our test alone desynchronises the backends for exactly the addresses in question, and for a real CCU past the boundary it also *changes* an existing unique_id from unprefixed to prefixed — which is the retained-payload entity loss the file's own doc comment warns about, arriving via the fix rather than the bug. The honest write-up is: the constant is narrower than the firmware grammar; correcting it is a coordinated change across the golden fixture, aiohomematic and the Python client, not a local one.

Second, smaller narrowing: "the firmware's own family discriminator is the 3-character prefix" is right, but the ambiguity it buys is real and unmeasured in both directions. `startsWith("INT")` is also what makes the prior agent's own residual (a device serial beginning INT) reachable; the CCU accepting that risk for its group dispatcher is not evidence that a routing-key namespace should.

all.title: PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT field layout and the -11 h/-10 h/12 °C cancellation code are ported values that reach the device verbatim
all.ourValue: "%.1f,%d,%s,%d,%s" with start.Format("02,01,06") / end.Format("02,01,06") → temp, start_minutes_of_day, dd, mm, yy, end_minutes_of_day, dd, mm, yy; cancellation = partyModeCode(now-11h, now-10h, 12.0)
all.firmwareValue: Nine comma-separated tokens in exactly that order: PARTY_TEMPERATURE, PARTY_START_TIME, PARTY_START_DAY, PARTY_START_MONTH, PARTY_START_YEAR, PARTY_STOP_TIME, PARTY_STOP_DAY, PARTY_STOP_MONTH, PARTY_STOP_YEAR. Temperature ×2 with +0.5 rounding into 6 bits (≤31.5 °C); both time fields integer-divided by 30 (truncating) into 6 bits; days 5 bits, months 4 bits, years 7 bits.
all.citation: Tier 1 — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSTypeConversionCCRTDNParty.cpp, `HSSTypeConversionCCRTDNParty::LogicalToPhysical`, which tokenises the string on ',' via the local `getNextToken` and packs 9 bytes. Each token is preceded by the firmware's own copy of the device-XML parameter line it feeds, in this order: `//<parameter type="integer" index="11.0" size="0.6" param="PARTY_TEMPERATURE"/>` with `//float integer scale factor 2` then `d = (d * (double)2); ... unsigned int uintValue = (int)(d + (double)0.5); byte = (unsigned char)(uintValue & BITMASK_LS_6_BIT);`; `//<parameter ... size="0.6" param="PARTY_START_TIME"/>` with `//<conversion type="integer_integer_scale" div="30"/>` then `uintValue = uintValue / 30; byte = (unsigned char)(uintValue & BITMASK_LS_6_BIT);`; `param="PARTY_START_DAY"` (`& BITMASK_LS_5_BIT`); `param="PARTY_START_MONTH"` (`(uintValue << 4) & BITMASK_MS_4_BIT`); `param="PARTY_START_YEAR"` (`& BITMASK_LS_7_BIT`); then PARTY_STOP_TIME (/30, 6 bits), PARTY_STOP_DAY (5 bits), PARTY_STOP_MONTH (4 bits), PARTY_STOP_YEAR (7 bits). A missing token aborts with `"Too few arguments (N)."` and returns false; `in.size()==0` returns false before any parsing. Tokens are parsed with `strtol(..., 10)` and `strtod`, so zero-padded "08"/"09" are decimal, not octal. Tier 1 for ranges and direction — ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml:590-744, the HEATING_CONTROL virtual-device channel that maps 1:1 onto HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU channel 2 and HM-CC-RT-DN channel 4: PARTY_TEMPERATURE `type="FLOAT" min="5.0" max="30.0" default="20.0" unit="°C" operations="3"`; PARTY_START_TIME and PARTY_STOP_TIME `type="INTEGER" min="0" max="1410" unit="minutes" operations="3"`; *_DAY `min="1" max="31"`; *_MONTH `min="1" max="12"`; *_YEAR `min="0" max="99" unit="year"`; and PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT `control="NONE" default="" operations="2" type="STRING"`.
all.finding: Field order, count, units and widths are all confirmed against the CCU's own converter — our nine tokens sit in exactly the nine slots it reads, minutes-of-day is the right unit for the two time fields, and two-digit year is right (declared 0..99, packed into 7 bits). The write-only claim is confirmed too: operations="2" and the DP's DEFAULT is the empty string, which the converter rejects outright (`in.size()==0` → return false), so our comment that the empty string cannot cancel a running party is exactly right for the reason stated. Three things the comment does not carry. (1) The CCU truncates both time fields to a 30-minute grid — `uintValue / 30` on an unsigned integer, no rounding — and the descriptor's max of 1410 (= 23:30) states the same grid. Our `startMOD`/`endMOD` are the exact minute, so any window not landing on :00 or :30 is silently snapped BACKWARD by up to 29 minutes at both ends. For SetAway that means a party that ends earlier than the operator asked; for the cancel path it is harmless. (2) A real range hazard on the SetAway path, not the cancel path: `SetAway` documents "pass 0 for the device default", and the KindIP branch honours that with `if away > 0`, but the KindRF branch passes `away` straight into `partyModeCode` unguarded (climate.go:1337). With away == 0 the first token is "0.0", the converter computes 0×2 = 0 and packs a 0 — a 0 °C setpoint, below the firmware's own declared minimum of 5.0 °C. There is no clamp anywhere on this path, and because PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT is a STRING the CCU applies no per-field range check either; the converter's masks only wrap (30.0 °C → 60 fits 6 bits, but 32.0 °C → 64 → wraps to 0). (3) The cancellation convention itself is NOT settled by any source available here, and this is the honest limit of the exercise. The CCU converter is a pure packer: it validates nothing about the window and takes `abs()` of a negative temperature. Whether a window already in the past cancels a running party, and what 12.0 °C means, are decided by the HM-CC-RT-DN's own radio firmware, which is in neither ../OpenCCU-Base nor ../OpenCCU nor the descriptor corpora. Tier 1 is silent on that half; our rule there rests on the Python reference's disable_away_mode RF override alone (Tier 3), and 12.0 in particular has no firmware meaning — it is simply an in-range value the converter accepts. A separate surface caveat worth recording: the shipped ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml carries no PARTY_* parameters at all and no device XML in the tree references `type_conversion_ccrtdn_party`, so this converter is reached through the HmIP heating-group virtual device rather than through a shipped RF device description. The channel mapping in groupdefinitions.xml (HM-CC-RT-DN ch4 / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU ch2) is the firmware's statement of where this parameter lives.
all.negativeControl: Had the field order been anything else — say temp last, or mm before dd, or seconds instead of minutes-of-day — the converter's nine inline `param="PARTY_*"` comments would have appeared in that other order, or the START_TIME token would not have been divided by 30, or the descriptor would not have declared max=1410 minutes. Had the year been full four-digit, PARTY_*_YEAR would not be `min="0" max="99"` masked to 7 bits. Each of those would have produced a visibly different reading; they did not. For the 12.0 °C half the control fails by construction: no source in the trees produces a different answer depending on whether 12.0 is meaningful, which is precisely why that half is reported as not settled rather than as verified.
all.missingInput: The HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU on-device radio firmware, which is what decides whether a window lying in the past terminates a running party and whether PARTY_TEMPERATURE carries any sentinel. No tree available here contains it; the CCU-side converter only packs the nine fields.
all.challengeNote:
The nine-token layout, both units, the two-digit year and the write-only shape are CONFIRMED on the right surface — and more strongly than claimed, because the CCU's own WebUI emits the identical token order for the same parameter on the same devices. Our `partyModeCode` output maps token-for-token onto the converter's nine `getNextToken` reads.

The prior agent's headline caveat is a measurement error, and it inverted the surface question. It reported that rf_cc_rt_dn.xml "carries no PARTY_* parameters at all" and that "no device XML in the tree references type_conversion_ccrtdn_party", concluding the converter is reached only through the HmIP heating-group virtual device. Both files declare it; the XMLs are ISO-8859-1 and a plain `grep -n` silently suppresses matches in them. The consequence matters: the converter is squarely on the KindRF path our code takes, and the grounding is on-surface rather than adjacent. Related: the ranges were cited from opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml — the HmIP group virtual device, which is a *different* surface that happens to carry the same numbers by mapping. The authority for an RF setValue is the RF device XML, and it agrees.

Three things I confirm and carry forward. (i) The 30-minute truncation is real (`uintValue / 30`, no rounding, and max=1410 = 23:30 declares the same grid), so a SetAway window not on :00/:30 is snapped backward by up to 29 minutes at both ends. (ii) The away==0 hazard is real and unguarded: SetAway's doc says "pass 0 for the device default", the KindIP branch honours it with `if away > 0` (climate.go:1328), and the KindRF branch at climate.go:1337 passes `away` straight into `partyModeCode`; "0.0" packs to 0, i.e. a 0 °C setpoint against a declared min of 5.0. Because PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT is a STRING, no per-field range check runs anywhere; the masks only wrap. (iii) The empty-string claim in DisableAway's comment is right for the reason given — `if(in.size() == 0) return false` at :81, and DEFAULT is the empty string.

What stays open is the half the id names second. Both trees are silent on whether a window already in the past cancels a running party, and 12.0 has no firmware meaning — the converter validates nothing, takes `abs()` of a negative temperature, and packs whatever it is given. The WebUI writes only forward windows. That half rests on ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/climate.py:567-577 alone, which is a Tier-3 witness.

all.title: 'Some CCU firmware variants reject a raw setValue' is an uncited comment steering a write path
all.ourValue: "Some CCU firmware variants reject a raw setValue for parameters they accept inside put_paramset — HmIP CONTROL_MODE=0 (AUTO) is the canonical case."
all.firmwareValue: The asymmetry is real, unconditional and channel-type-driven (not variant-driven): setValue gates on checkRequiredValues, putParameterSet does not. But on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER the gated key is SET_POINT_MODE, not CONTROL_MODE — a bare setValue of CONTROL_MODE passes the gate and is dispatched.
all.citation: Tier 1 — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#setValue builds a DeviceChannelValuesCommandDTO for the single key and then guards the dispatch with `if (!DeviceUtil.checkRequiredValues(device, channelIndex, valueKey, commandDTO)) { return false; }` — no event-bus send, no fault, and the incomplete DTO is parked in the class's `storedDeviceChannelValuesCommandDTO` static to be merged into the next setValue on the same device+channel. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#putParameterSet has no such call: for parameterSetType "VALUES" it goes straight from #validateAndConvertValues to the event-bus send. #checkRequiredValues builds a per-channel-type required set and decides with `if (paramSet.size() > 0 && (!paramSet.contains(valueKey) || paramSet.contains(valueKey) && paramSet.size() == commandDTO.getValues().size())) { ret = true; }`. Its HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER branch adds SET_POINT_MODE only when the write already carries it, then unconditionally adds SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE. Parameter shape: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.ClimateStateParameterFactory#createControlModeParameter — `byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE;` and a StateParameter("CONTROL_MODE", LogicalType.INTEGER, PhysicalType.INTEGER, IOOperations(ops), null, 0, 0, 3, ...), i.e. write-only, default 0, range 0..3; IOOperations values are READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4 (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations). Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M.json, channel :1 VALUES — CONTROL_MODE `"OPERATIONS": 2, "MIN": 0, "MAX": 3, "DEFAULT": 0, "TYPE": "INTEGER"`; SET_POINT_MODE `"OPERATIONS": 7`; ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M.json gives channel :1 TYPE = HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER. BidCos side for contrast: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:318-330 forwards setValue straight to RFManager::SetValue with no companion-parameter gate at the RPC layer.
all.finding: The mechanism the comment gestures at exists and is exactly the shape claimed — the CCU's HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface really does accept inside put_paramset writes it refuses as a bare setValue, and the refusal is the worst kind: setValue returns false with no XML-RPC fault and no frame sent, so the caller sees success-shaped silence. PutParamsetForce is therefore defensible. But three parts of the sentence are wrong or wider than the firmware. (1) "Some CCU firmware variants" — it is not a variant question. checkRequiredValues is an unconditional branch on the channel's ChannelType, present on every build of this surface; the outcome is deterministic per (channel type, key set). (2) CONTROL_MODE is the wrong canonical case. On HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER the required set is {SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE} (plus SET_POINT_MODE when the write already carries it), and the final predicate short-circuits to ret=true for any valueKey NOT in that set — CONTROL_MODE is not in it, so a bare setValue(CONTROL_MODE, 0) is dispatched normally. The key on that channel that setValue actually refuses alone is SET_POINT_MODE: it lands in the required set, the set has 2 entries against a 1-entry write, the predicate fails, and nothing is sent. That is a striking result because the neighbouring comment in setIPMode (climate.go:1493-1499) already claims writing SET_POINT_MODE "has no effect on most CCU firmwares" — that claim is the one the firmware backs, and it backs it through this gate rather than through read-only-ness (SET_POINT_MODE is declared OPERATIONS 7, fully writable). The two comments have the right facts attached to the wrong parameters. (3) The genuinely gated cases on other channel types are worth naming instead of a vague "some parameters": DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE and RAMP_TIME_UNIT/RAMP_TIME_VALUE (each pair required whole, on any channel type); IDENTIFY_TARGET_LEVEL with IDENTIFY_DURATION and the IDENTIFICATION_MODE_* pair; WEEK_PROGRAM_TARGET_CHANNEL_LOCK(S); STATE on SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER/BACKLIGHTING_RECEIVER/WATER_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER; LEVEL on SERVO_/DIMMER_/BLIND_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and SHADING_RECEIVER (which also injects LEVEL=1.01 when only LEVEL_2 is given); the COLOR/COLOR_BEHAVIOUR pair; the DISPLAY_DATA_* set on ACOUSTIC_DISPLAY_RECEIVER; and on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the four-way {DURATION_UNIT, DURATION_VALUE, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION} — which is directly relevant to the siren path and means a bare setValue of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION alone is silently dropped. Net effect on our code: PutParamsetForce is not needed for the CONTROL_MODE-only ModeAuto write it was justified by, and is needed for cases the comment does not mention. Nothing is broken today — PutParamsetForce is strictly safe, and the two multi-key ModeHeat/ModeOff writes would take put_paramset regardless — but the justification should be rewritten around checkRequiredValues and the ALARM_SWITCH/siren cases, not around CONTROL_MODE and "firmware variants".
all.negativeControl: Had CONTROL_MODE genuinely been gated, it would have had to appear inside the HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER branch of checkRequiredValues (the way SET_POINT_MODE and SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE do) or in isLegacyParameterDisabled; it appears in neither, and the final predicate's `!paramSet.contains(valueKey)` clause explicitly lets an unlisted key through. Conversely, had there been no asymmetry at all, putParameterSet would have called the same guard — it does not, which is what makes the general claim survive while the example fails.
all.challengeNote:
Demoted from `narrowed` to `contradicted`, because both load-bearing assertions in the comment are false against Tier 1 and I verified each by opening the method.

"Some CCU firmware variants" — #checkRequiredValues is an unconditional branch on the channel's ChannelType. The outcome is a pure function of (channel type, key set); there is no build flag, no version gate. A reader who believes "variants" will conclude the risk is probabilistic and untestable, which is the opposite of true.

"CONTROL_MODE=0 (AUTO) is the canonical case" — I traced the predicate by hand for the exact write our code makes. For a bare {CONTROL_MODE} on HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER, paramSet = {SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE}: size > 0 and `!paramSet.contains("CONTROL_MODE")` is true, so ret = true and the DTO is sent. For a bare {SET_POINT_MODE}: paramSet = {SET_POINT_MODE, SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE}, valueKey IS contained and 2 != 1, so the condition fails, ret stays false, the DTO is parked and setValue returns false. So `PutParamsetForce` at internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:1530 is not needed for the ModeAuto write it is justified by, and the ModeHeat/ModeOff writes carry two keys and would take put_paramset regardless. Nothing is broken — PutParamsetForce is strictly safe — but the comment's example is the one case that does not need it.

One narrowing of the prior report, which I checked because it read as too clean. It says SET_POINT_MODE is "declared OPERATIONS 7, fully writable", making the gate the whole story for the neighbouring comment at climate.go:1493 ("writing SET_POINT_MODE has no effect on most CCU firmwares — the value is read-only on the wire"). ClimateStateParameterFactory registers two SET_POINT_MODE variants; the "READ_ONLY" one really is READ|EVENT.
