So the old comment's read-only claim is correct for channels bound to that variant and wrong for those bound to "default" (the eTRV-B-2 R4M shows 7), where the gate is the operative mechanism. Which variant a given channel gets is a per-channel-type binding I did not enumerate, so "the gate, not read-only-ness" is right for the devices in the corpus and not proven in general.

The siren consequence the prior report surfaced is real and I confirm it verbatim: on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the branch adds all four of DURATION_UNIT, DURATION_VALUE, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION as soon as any one is present, so a bare setValue of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION is dropped silently. That, not CONTROL_MODE, is what the comment should point at.

all.title: The actuator-feedback exclusion list decides which parameters can never raise an alarm, from seven literals
all.ourValue: "Every entry is a parameter the alarm engine or an operator *writes* — reading it back as a cause turns the domain's own output into an input" — asserted over all seven entries
all.firmwareValue: Only three of the seven are writable. ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION and SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND are OPERATIONS 2 (write-only). ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE and EMERGENCY_OPERATION are OPERATIONS 5 (read+event) — device-reported, never written. INTRUSION_ALARM is not a parameter identifier on any CCU surface.
all.citation: Tier 1 — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory registers ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE and OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE through #createReadEventBooleanParameter, whose body is `byte ops = GeneralStateParameterFactory.getReadEventIOOperation();` — no WRITE bit. The same class's #createAcousticAlarmSelectionParameter, #createOpticalAlarmSelectionParameter and #createSmokeDetectorCommandParameter each open with `byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE;` (SELECTION parameters are ENUMs over SignalAcoustic/SignalOptical names, SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND over SmokeDetectorCommand names). EMERGENCY_OPERATION is registered through HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory#createReadEventBooleanIntegerParameter, whose body is `byte ops = IOOperations.READ; ops = (byte)(ops | IOOperations.EVENT);`. Bit values: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations — READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4. INTRUSION_ALARM appears in the firmware only as an enum MEMBER, never as a parameter id: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.SmokeDetectorCommand (alongside INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF), SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus, and SmokeDetectorEvent (ordinal 2); the only INTRUSION_ALARM-prefixed parameter is the SERVICE parameter INTRUSION_ALARM_COUNTER (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.serviceparameter.StatisticParameterFactory). None of the seven appears in any ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml — they are HmIP-only. Tier 2 confirmation across the whole descriptor corpus (../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json joined to channel TYPE from ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json): ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER VALUES carries ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE OPERATIONS 5, ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION 2, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE 5, OPTICAL_ALARM_SELECTION 2, DURATION_UNIT 2, DURATION_VALUE 2 — and nothing else; SMOKE_DETECTOR VALUES carries SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND 2 and, read-only at 5 or 4, DIRT_LEVEL, ERROR_ALARM_TEST, ERROR_CODE, ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER, INSTALL_TEST, LOWBAT, SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS, SMOKE_DETECTOR_TEST_RESULT, SMOKE_LEVEL, STATE; EMERGENCY_OPERATION appears only on CLIMATECONTROL_FLOOR_TRANSCEIVER / _PUMP_TRANSCEIVER / _DIRECT_TRANSMITTER at OPERATIONS 5; and no paramset anywhere declares a parameter named INTRUSION_ALARM.
all.finding: The list's stated rationale is false for four of its seven entries, which matters because that rationale is what a future reader will use to decide whether a new entry belongs. ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE and EMERGENCY_OPERATION are read+event on every surface that declares them — the device reports them and nothing in the system can write them, so they are not "the domain's own output" in the sense the comment claims. They are feedback the device produces, which is a perfectly good reason to exclude them from causal classification (a siren reporting that it is sounding is not evidence of an intrusion) but a different reason, and the comment states the wrong one. EMERGENCY_OPERATION is doubly mis-scoped: it lives on the underfloor-heating actuator channels (CLIMATECONTROL_FLOOR_*), so the entry has nothing to do with the siren/smoke families the block is organised around. The fourth is inert rather than wrong: "INTRUSION_ALARM" is keyed as an `hmenum.Parameter`, but the CCU has no parameter by that name — it is a VALUE of SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS and of the SmokeDetectorCommand enum, which our own contract tests already treat correctly as a value (tests/contract/safety_classifier_test.go:214 asserts it is excluded from ActiveValues, not from parameters). The map entry can never match a lookup key and is dead. On the bundle's second question — write-capable VALUES parameters on the siren/smoke channel types the list omits — the answer is short and reassuring: on ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER the only writable parameters beyond the two SELECTIONs are DURATION_UNIT and DURATION_VALUE (the siren's own on-time, which nothing would classify as a fault cause anyway, though note from candidate c009 that the firmware requires all four to be written together); on SMOKE_DETECTOR there is nothing beyond SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND. There is no channel type literally named SIREN — the HmIP siren channel is ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER, and the adjacent ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (HmIP-MP3P) carries a much larger writable set (LEVEL 7, SOUNDFILE 7, STOP 2, REPETITIONS 2, OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE 2, SOUNDFILE_LIST_1..12 at 2) that the list does not cover at all. Impact today is nil: none of ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE or EMERGENCY_OPERATION appears in byParameter or byChannelAndParameter (they occur nowhere else in classify.go), so the exclusions are belt-and-braces and removing them would change no output. The defect is entirely in the recorded reason, which is the load-bearing part of a hand-maintained list whose completeness the file says rests on the comment.
all.negativeControl: Had all seven genuinely been written parameters, each factory would have opened with `byte ops = IOOperations.WRITE;` the way the three SELECTION/COMMAND ones do, and the descriptor corpus would have reported OPERATIONS 2 (or a value with bit 2 set) for all seven instead of 5 for three of them; a real INTRUSION_ALARM parameter would have surfaced as a key in some paramset or as a StateParameterIdentifier constant. The scan reports 2 for exactly three, 5 for exactly three, and no key at all for the seventh — three distinguishable outcomes from one mechanism, so the check is tethered.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as contradicted. I re-ran every leg rather than accepting it, including the negative Tier-1 claim, because the same tree's ISO-8859-1 encoding produced a false negative elsewhere in this bundle — here the absence is real.

The recorded rationale is false for four of seven entries, and the rationale is the load-bearing part: the file's own comment tells a future reader to keep the list ahead of every lookup, so the stated reason is the admission test for new entries. ACOUSTIC_ALARM_ACTIVE, OPTICAL_ALARM_ACTIVE and EMERGENCY_OPERATION are read+event on every surface that declares them — nothing in this system or any other can write them, so they are not "the domain's own output". They are device-reported feedback, which is a good reason to exclude them (a siren reporting that it is sounding is not evidence of an intrusion) but a different one. EMERGENCY_OPERATION is doubly mis-scoped: the Tier-2 join puts it only on underfloor-heating actuator channels, so it has nothing to do with the siren/smoke families the block is organised around, and its inline comment ("a fallback mode an actuator enters on command loss") is the accurate description sitting under the wrong heading.

The fourth entry is inert rather than wrong: "INTRUSION_ALARM" is keyed as an hmenum.Parameter but the CCU has no parameter by that name, so the map entry can never match a lookup key. Our own tests already treat it correctly as a *value* (internal/model/safety/classify_test.go:111 asserts it is absent from ActiveValues; :118 asserts Classify(SMOKE_DETECTOR, INTRUSION_ALARM) is not ok — which passes via this dead entry rather than via absence from the tables).

I confirm the impact assessment independently: none of the seven appears anywhere else in internal/model/safety/classify.go, so all seven exclusions are belt-and-braces and removing them changes no output today. The defect is entirely in the recorded reason.

One addition the prior report gestured at without pinning: there is no channel type literally named SIREN, and the adjacent ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER (HmIP-MP3P) carries a large writable set the list does not cover. That is a completeness gap in the list, not a defect in the entries present.

all.title: The enum-index narrowing rests on the declared value list being exhaustive and index-ordered
all.site: internal/model/safety/activation.go:56 (ActiveFromRaw), :78-80 (positional scan); classification set in internal/model/safety/classify.go:50-113
all.citation: BidCos/rfd: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:49-58 (option `index` attribute: `if(options.size()<=index)options.resize(index+1); options[index]=id;` else `index=options.size(); options.push_back(id);`), :100-107 (`(*val)["TYPE"]="ENUM"; (*val)["MIN"]=int(0); (*val)["MAX"]=int(options.size()-1); XmlRpcValue& values=(*val)["VALUE_LIST"]; for(i…) values[i]=options[i];`), :74-77 (out-of-range int coerced to default_option). Schema: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/device.xsd:887-909 (`Paramset.Parameter.Logical.Option` — `index` is xsd:optional). Descriptor: ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/rftypes/rf_sec_sd_2.xml:1 (HM-Sec-SD-2 ch1 SMOKE_DETECTOR: ERROR_ALARM_TEST `<option id="NO_ERROR" index="0" default="true"/><option id="ALARM_TEST_FAILED" index="1"/>`; ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER NO_ERROR=0 / DEGRADED_SMOKE_CHAMBER=1); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_wds_v1_1.xml:149-165 (WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE: options DRY, WET, WATER with no index → 0,1,2; `<conversion type="option_integer"><value_map device_value="0" parameter_value="0"/>…parameter_value="2"/>`). HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus (enum constants in order IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM) and GeneralStateParameterFactory#createSmokeDetectorAlarmStatusParameter (LogicalType.ENUM with `new StringEnumToInteger(SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus.getNames())`); de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (`parameterDescription.setValueList(converter.getEnumStrings())`) and DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue (out: scans getEnumStrings() and returns the 0-based ordinal; in: `values[numberValue.intValue()]` guarded by `< values.length`, else logs "invalid parameter value … (out of range)"), gated on `replaceEnumValueWithOrdinal`, which the CCU ships enabled: ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:47 `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal=true`. Event path also converted: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyNotificationHandler and LegacyBackendNotificationHandler both call DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue with out=true. ERROR_JAMMED is not an ENUM at all: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory registers it via createReadEventBooleanBit0Parameter.
all.finding: Confirmed on both transports. The integer a classified ENUM carries on the XML-RPC surface IS a 0-based position in that parameter's VALUE_LIST, and the two firmware paths build VALUE_LIST from exactly the array they index. BidCos: HSSLogicalTypeOption stores each option AT its declared index (resizing the vector), and GetDescription emits the vector positionally — so a sparse enum (rf_rhs.xml ERROR: NO_ERROR index=0, SABOTAGE index=7; rf_d.xml LOAD_FAILURE index=3) produces a VALUE_LIST with EMPTY-STRING placeholders at the gaps, not a compacted list. Position i therefore still equals wire integer i. HmIP: the legacy surface converts the enum string to its ordinal in getEnumStrings() and publishes the same array as VALUE_LIST; this holds even for converters constructed with explicit enumValues/offset (e.g. SMOKE_DETECTOR_EVENT), because the legacy conversion is purely positional. None of the classified parameters is a bit mask, a count or a 1-based index. Specifics: SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS ordinals are IDLE_OFF=0, PRIMARY_ALARM=1, INTRUSION_ALARM=2, SECONDARY_ALARM=3 — exactly the order pkg/hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go declares, so excluding INTRUSION_ALARM at index 2 is grounded. WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE is [DRY,WET,WATER] = 0,1,2, matching waterStateActiveValues. ERROR_ALARM_TEST and ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER are two-entry options with NO_ERROR at index 0, so classify.go:104-108's claim is exact. ERROR_JAMMED is BOOLEAN on HmIP, not an ENUM — it never enters the index path, and our bool arm handles it. Two narrowings worth recording, neither breaking the rule: (a) 'exhaustive by construction' is true positionally but the list can contain empty strings at gap indices, so any consumer that filters empty VALUE_LIST entries before handing the slice to ActiveFromRaw would silently shift every label past the gap — the exhaustiveness lives in the SLICE INDEX, not in the entry count; (b) out-of-range handling differs: we return inactive, the firmware coerces to default_option (HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:76-77) or passes the number through with a debug log (HmIP). For every parameter this domain classifies default_option is index 0 (NO_ERROR/IDLE_OFF), which is inactive too, so the verdicts agree.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong I would have found one of: a compacting VALUE_LIST builder (options pushed back only when non-empty, so declared index ≠ emitted position); a legacy conversion keyed on StringEnumToInteger#getEnumValues() or #getOffset() rather than the loop index; `Legacy.Parameter.ReplaceEnumValueWithOrdinal` absent or false in crRFD.conf, which would make HmIP emit the enum STRING and our int path unreachable; or a classified parameter declared with a bitmask conversion (`option_integer` value_map with mask semantics binding several bits). I found the opposite in each case, and rf_rhs.xml/rf_d.xml prove the sparse case is real and handled by index, not by position-in-file.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld for every parameter this domain actually classifies; demoted because the sparse case, which the prior pass asserted as settled, is not.

What I checked and confirmed. The surface is right: `VALUE_LIST` is written in exactly one place in the entire firmware C++ tree (grep over --include=*.cpp --include=*.h returns only HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:104), and HSSParameter.cpp:118 builds the factory tag as "logical_type_" + the XML `type` attribute, so `<logical type="option">` really does reach this class. The formula is transcribed exactly, including that resize()-then-assign stores each option AT its declared index. On the HmIP side I read DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue and confirmed the outbound conversion is a plain 0-based scan with no offset applied — this matters, because StringEnumToInteger has a (enumStrings, offset) constructor that would have broken the rule had the legacy path used it, and it does not. SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus's ordinals are not a convention I supplied: Java values()/ordinal() is declaration order by definition, and the declaration order is IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM, matching pkg/hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go, so excluding INTRUSION_ALARM at index 2 is grounded. I also confirmed our side does not disturb the list: internal/security/index.go:267 and internal/alarm/resolver.go:187 hand ParameterData().ValueList straight to ActiveFromRaw with no filtering of empty entries.

What breaks the prior verdict. The prior finding states as fact that a sparse enum yields a placeholder-padded VALUE_LIST so 'position i still equals wire integer i', and cites rf_rhs ERROR (SABOTAGE index=7) and rf_d LOAD_FAILURE (index=3) as the examples. That is what Tier 1 computes. It is not what the descriptor corpus reports: those same parameters come back compacted, two entries, MAX=1, in 6 RHS descriptors and 20 dimmer descriptors. I checked the obvious escape — that the distribution patches the XMLs or the option class — and neither rf_rhs nor HSSLogicalTypeOption is touched by any patch under ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu. So which shape a real CCU puts on the wire for a sparse option list is not settled by the material available to me, and I will not pick one by convention.

Why the demotion is narrow rather than fatal. All four parameters this domain classifies are dense and carry their idle label at index 0 (SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS, WATERDETECTIONSENSOR STATE, ERROR_ALARM_TEST, ERROR_SMOKE_CHAMBER), and Tier 1 and Tier 2 agree on all four; classify.go:104-108's claim about NO_ERROR at index 0 is exact. ERROR_JAMMED never enters the index path — HMIPServer GeneralStateParameterFactory registers it via createReadEventBooleanBit0Parameter, so it is BOOLEAN and our bool arm handles it. The unresolved case is the operator-enrolment path at internal/alarm/resolver.go:187, which hands ActiveFromRaw an arbitrary enrolled parameter's ValueList: enrol HM-Sec-RHS ERROR with ActiveValues [SABOTAGE] and the wire value 7 resolves correctly under the Tier-1 shape and returns ActivationIndexOutOfRange -> inactive under the Tier-2 shape. That is the direction that loses a sabotage alarm rather than raising a false one, which is the safer failure, but it is a failure. The prior finding's narrowing (b) about out-of-range handling I confirmed and it stands: HSSLogicalTypeOption.cpp:76-77 coerces to default_option, HmIP logs and passes through, and for every parameter this domain classifies default_option is index 0, so the verdicts agree.

all.title: The low-battery flag is searched on exactly channels 0, 1 and 2 — a channel set nothing in the source states
all.citation: BidCos-RF/Wired descriptors: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml and ../OpenCCU-Base/firmware/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml — 176 device XMLs declare LOWBAT; parsing every `<channel index=… count=…>` and expanding `count`, the minimum channel carrying LOWBAT is 0 in ALL 176. Channel 0 declarations are `<channel index="0" type="MAINTENANCE" ui_flags="internal" class="maintenance" count="1">` with `<parameter id="LOWBAT" operations="read,event" ui_flags="service"><logical type="boolean"/><physical … interface="internal" value_id="LOWBAT"/>`. Duplicates on functional channels exist but never alone: rf_sec_sd_2.xml (ch0 + ch1 SMOKE_DETECTOR), rf_sc.xml / rf_sc_e_v1_7.xml / rf_sc_le_v1_6.xml / rf_sci_3.xml / rf_sec_sco.xml (ch0 + ch1 SHUTTER_CONTACT), rf_rhs.xml / rf_rhs_e_v1_7.xml / rf_rhs_le_v1_6.xml (ch0 + ch1 ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR), rf_tis.xml / rf_tis_le_v1_0.xml (ch0 + ch1 TILT_SENSOR), rf_wds_v1_0.xml / rf_wds_v1_1.xml (ch0 + ch1 WATERDETECTIONSENSOR), rf_em_8.xml (ch0 + ch1 KEY), and the one device that goes above 2: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_wds30_ot2.xml — ch0 MAINTENANCE, ch1 WEATHER count=4 (channels 1-4), and ch5 WEATHER. No device XML declares LOWBAT/LOW_BAT/LOWBAT_SENSOR only above channel 2. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler — the status-frame handler binds `byte channelIndex = 0; IChannel channel0 = device.getChannel(channelIndex);` and writes `channel0.setParameterValue("LOW_BAT", timestamp, statusFrame.isLowBat())`, notifying under that same channelIndex 0; the parameter itself is registered as BOOLEAN by de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.StateParameterFactory (createReadEventBooleanIntegerParameter("LOW_BAT")).
all.finding: Our three-channel scan is a strict superset of what the firmware requires, so it produces no wrong answer — but the damage the reader posited does not exist, and the widening is not what makes the code correct. Channel 0 alone is sufficient on every shipped device: BidCos always declares LOWBAT on the MAINTENANCE channel (ui_flags="service", interface="internal" — rfd derives it itself), and duplicates it on the functional channel only as an additional copy fed from the same frame bit (`param="LOWBAT"` in the EVENT/INFO_LEVEL frames, e.g. rf_sec_sd_2.xml). HmIP writes LOW_BAT to channel 0 exclusively. The boundary the reader was reaching for is real but one step further out: HM-WDS30-OT2-SM (rf_wds30_ot2.xml) does declare LOWBAT on channel 5, above the {:0,:1,:2} window — and the scan would still be right there, because the same device declares it on 0 and 1-4 as well. So: our rule is true in our scope, and the reason it is true is the channel-0 MAINTENANCE invariant, not the 0/1/2 widening. The ordering worry is also moot — the extra copies are the same device bit, so 'first hit in ascending channel order' cannot pick a contradicting value. Our type guard matches too: both firmware sides declare the parameter BOOLEAN, and we only accept raw.(bool). What our code SHOULD follow is the channel-0 rule that internal/central/adapter/relevant_init.go:34-36 already states for the other device-meta parameters; the :1/:2 arms are dead weight rather than a defect, and no device in the shipped set makes them load-bearing.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong I would have found at least one device XML whose only LOWBAT declaration sits at channel index ≥ 3 after expanding `count`, or an HmIP path writing LOW_BAT to a non-zero channel. The scan was built to surface exactly that (it prints every file whose minimum LOWBAT channel exceeds 2, and it did print the ch5 declaration on rf_wds30_ot2.xml when not filtered by minimum) — it produced no such file, and the HmIP handler binds the literal 0.
all.challengeNote:
Verdict upheld, boundary confirmed by re-running the census rather than accepting it, and one defect added that the prior grounding missed.

What I checked. I re-derived the census independently with an XML parser over all four directories, expanding `count` attributes, and reproduced the prior pass's numbers exactly: 176 files, minimum channel 0 in every one, one device (rf_wds30_ot2.xml, HM-WDS30-OT2-SM) reaching channel 5 and also declaring channel 0. So the {:0,:1,:2} window is a strict superset of what the firmware requires, no shipped device makes the :1/:2 arms load-bearing, and the rule is true in our scope for the reason the prior pass named — the channel-0 MAINTENANCE invariant, not the widening.

What I upgraded from inference to grounding. The prior finding asserted that the duplicate copies on functional channels are 'fed from the same frame bit' and therefore cannot contradict channel 0. That was an inference; it is now read from the source. RFDevice::UpdateDeviceFlags extracts the LOWBAT bit from the frame and routes it through SetInternalValue, which sets the device-level maintenance_flags FLAG_LOWBAT; the channel-0 read returns that same flag; and the functional-channel parameter is populated from the frame field the decoder names "LOWBAT", which BidcosFrame.h places at exactly the bit positions UpdateDeviceFlags reads. First-hit-in-ascending-order therefore cannot pick a contradicting value, and our fall-through when a channel has no value yet is safe.

What the prior grounding missed. The comment being grounded is itself wrong. availability.go:249-250 reads 'LOW_BAT (HM/BidCos) and LOWBAT (HmIP)'. The two are inverted. Every BidCos device XML spells it LOWBAT — all 176 in the census, on the MAINTENANCE channel with interface="internal" — and HmIP spells it LOW_BAT, in the frame handler, the state-parameter factory and the group definitions alike. Tier 2 agrees at 224-to-65. The code is unharmed because it tries both names, but this is precisely the class of comment the project's own rule targets: a property of a data source asserted without having been read from it. The fix is one line, and the code should follow the channel-0 rule that internal/central/adapter/relevant_init.go:34-36 already states for the other device-meta parameters.

One boundary the prior pass named loosely. LOWBAT_SENSOR does appear outside the window — ST6-SH channels 3 and 4 — but that device carries LOWBAT on channel 0 too, and lowBattery() does not look for that alias at all (only hmenum.ParameterLowBat and ParameterLowbat), so it is not a gap on this surface. It is a gap on internal/model/safety/classify.go's lowBatAliases, which does list LOWBAT_SENSOR; that is a different site and outside this rule.

all.title: "Two groups with more than one member each" is an invented threshold for the sub-device split
all.site: internal/model/device/aggregate.go:496-512 (HasSubDevices); groupChannels populated only from internal/model/custom/materialize.go:278-281 via Device.AddChannelToGroup (aggregate.go:344)
all.citation: Searched for a firmware-side sub-structure notion and found none. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/device.xsd:290-395 defines the full `<channel>` attribute set: index, type, ui_flags, class, count, hidden, physical_index_offset, autoregister, pair_function, function, paired, aes_default, count_from_sysinfo, direction, aes_always, has_team, team_tag — there is no group/subdevice attribute. Inventorying every `<channel>` across ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml (428 channel elements) yields only: class ∈ {maintenance:144, central:2}, ui_flags ∈ {internal:143}, function ∈ {A:29, T:4}, pair_function ∈ {BA:19, AB:1}, paired:33, team_tag ∈ {smoke_detector:6}. `function`/`pair_function`/`paired` express a two-channel A/B PAIR on a single control (e.g. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_rc_12.xml:82 `<channel autoregister="true" index="1" type="KEY" count_from_sysinfo="23.0:1.0" pair_function="BA" function="A" paired="true" …>`), not a partition of a device into logical devices. ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/groups/groupdefinitions.xml is about groups ACROSS devices (`<allowed_member_types>` of HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-Sec-SC, … under `<group_type><id>HomeMatic.heating</id>`), not within one. Grepping the whole of ../OpenCCU-Base for `CHANNEL_GROUP` returns nothing, and the WebUI sources under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/webui/ carry no sub-device/child-device concept. HmIP is equally silent: grepping the HMIPServer component for channelGroup / ChannelGroup / groupIndex / GROUP_INDEX returns nothing.
all.finding: Tier 1 does not decide this, and it cannot: the input the threshold reads does not come from the CCU at all. `d.groupChannels` is populated exclusively by internal/model/custom/materialize.go:278-281 from OUR hand-maintained device profiles (ADR 0063) — the CCU never sends a channel grouping. So there is no firmware value to compare 'at least two groups with at least two members each' against; the check would be measuring our own registry against itself. What the CCU actually expresses about a multi-channel device's internal structure is three unrelated things, none of them a split: a maintenance channel marked class="maintenance"/ui_flags="internal" (channel 0), A/B channel PAIRS on a single physical control (function/pair_function/paired), and team membership (team_tag, e.g. smoke_detector). The CCU's own operator surface renders a device as one flat channel list; it has no notion of presenting one device as several. Our rule therefore rests on the profile registry plus the worked HmIP-WRC6-230 example, and nothing in the firmware either supports or refutes the 2-of-2 shape. Consequence for the code: the honest framing is that HasSubDevices is a presentation policy over OUR grouping, not a device property — the comment should not read as if it were describing the device. Because the whole input is repo-owned, the right guard is a fixture over the profile registry (what shape does each registered profile's group map take, and which devices flip the verdict), not a firmware citation.
all.negativeControl: Had a firmware sub-structure source existed I would have found it in one of four places I checked and would then have compared its partition against ours: a `<channel>` attribute in device.xsd naming a group or parent (the attribute inventory enumerates every attribute actually used, so a grouping attribute could not hide), a `CHANNEL_GROUP`-shaped key anywhere in OpenCCU-Base, a within-device grouping in groupdefinitions.xml (it is cross-device by construction — its members are device TYPES), or a channelGroup/groupIndex accessor on the HmIP channel description. All four came back empty, which is what makes 'silent' a measurement rather than a failure to look.

all.title: The allow-list of INTERNAL-flagged parameters that may still surface
all.citation: HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter — the FLAGS assignment is a single if/else chain: UNREACH → 25; ERROR_CODE and service-message parameters → 1 or 9; `parameter.getName().equals("REPETITIONS") || parameter.getName().equals("OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE") || parameter.getName().startsWith("COLOR_LIST_") || parameter.getName().startsWith("ON_TIME_LIST_") || parameter.getName().startsWith("SOUNDFILE_LIST_")` → setFlags(2); everything else → setFlags(1). DeviceUtil#fillLegacyParameter, the only later mutator, sets TAB_ORDER, UNIT and CONTROL only — never FLAGS. CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE is a configuration parameter (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.ConfigurationParameterIdentifier#CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE, built by GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory#createEnumeration) and matches no branch above, so it takes the else → FLAGS=1. BidCos: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/ declares DIRECTION 12 times, every one of them `<parameter id="DIRECTION" operations="read,event" ui_flags="internal">` (e.g. rf_d.xml:274, rf_winmatic.xml:198, rf_dim_1l_644.xml:360); rfd emits FLAGS from HSSParameter.cpp:210 `(*val)["FLAGS"]=flags;`. ON_TIME_LIST_*, REPETITIONS and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE do not appear in rftypes/ or hs485types/ at all — they are HmIP-only. Tier 2 corroboration, ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json (FLAGS as actually declared at runtime): CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE FLAGS=1 TYPE=ENUM in 105 descriptors (e.g. HmIP-STV.json, VCU3432945:1 MASTER); DIRECTION FLAGS=3 TYPE=ENUM in 124 (e.g. HMW-LC-Bl1-DR.json, VCU0000011:3 VALUES); REPETITIONS FLAGS=2 in 5 (HmIP-WRCD.json, VCU4243444:3 VALUES); ON_TIME_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 in 3 (HmIP-MP3P.json, VCU1543608:6 VALUES); plus COLOR_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 (3), SOUNDFILE_LIST_1 FLAGS=2 (1), OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE FLAGS=2 (4).
all.ourValue: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE listed as an INTERNAL-flagged parameter needing an exemption to surface
all.firmwareValue: CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE carries FLAGS=1 (VISIBLE, no INTERNAL bit) — the firmware never flags it internal, on either transport
all.finding: Three of the four entries are grounded; the fourth is not, and it is precisely the one the comment presents as the Go-side addition. DIRECTION, REPETITIONS and ON_TIME_LIST_1 do carry the INTERNAL bit (DIRECTION: ui_flags="internal" in all 12 BidCos declarations, FLAGS=3 = VISIBLE|INTERNAL at runtime; REPETITIONS and ON_TIME_LIST_* : the HmIP legacy surface sets FLAGS=2 by name-match), so exempting them is doing real work. CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE does not: the HmIP FLAGS chain has no branch for it and the else yields FLAGS=1, and 105 real descriptors agree. The entry is therefore inert — the exemption at internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:401 and reason.go:206 can never fire for it, because the guard those sites sit behind only asks about INTERNAL-flagged parameters. That is harmless in behaviour but wrong as documentation: the comment asserts a property of the descriptor ('their Flags field includes FLAG.INTERNAL') that the firmware contradicts for that name, and the stated reason for the entry ('the operation-mode gating pipeline reads it directly') is a claim about our pipeline, not about the CCU. Second, smaller result: the firmware's INTERNAL-by-name set is wider than our allow-list — OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE, COLOR_LIST_* and SOUNDFILE_LIST_* are also FLAGS=2. That is a deliberate difference in the safe direction (an allow-list is what we want visible), not a gap, but it means 'ported verbatim from the Python sibling's field map' is not the same set the firmware flags, and the two should not be conflated.
all.negativeControl: Had the CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE claim been true I would have found either a name-match for it in the DeviceUtil FLAGS chain (the chain is exhaustive — every parameter takes exactly one branch, so an INTERNAL classification could not come from anywhere else in that method), a later FLAGS mutation in fillLegacyParameter, or descriptors carrying FLAGS 2/3/6 for it. The same scan that returned FLAGS=1 for CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE returned FLAGS=2 for REPETITIONS/ON_TIME_LIST_1 and FLAGS=3 for DIRECTION in the same pass, so the check demonstrably distinguishes the two outcomes.
all.challengeNote:
Contradiction upheld, verified independently on both tiers rather than accepted.

What I checked. I opened the FLAGS chain and transcribed it rather than trusting the summary — it is a single if/else with four arms, and CHANNEL_OPERATION_MODE matches none of them, so it lands on the else and takes FLAGS=1. I then closed the escape the prior pass asserted without showing: fillLegacyParameter really does touch only TabOrder, Unit and Control, and the properties file it reads from carries no FLAGS key anywhere in its 1092 lines and no entry for this parameter at all, so nothing downstream can set the bit. I confirmed the parameter is absent from every BidCos device XML in both trees, and I re-ran the descriptor census myself: 105 real descriptors report FLAGS=1 for it. The three genuine entries hold up: DIRECTION carries ui_flags="internal" in all 31 BidCos declarations and comes back FLAGS=3 at runtime, and REPETITIONS / ON_TIME_LIST_1 are set to 2 by the name-match arm, so exempting those three is doing real work.

One count corrected. The prior finding said DIRECTION appears 12 times in rftypes; it appears 31 times across src/devicetypes/rftypes and firmware/rftypes together. All 31 carry ui_flags="internal", so the conclusion is unchanged, but the number should not be repeated as given.

Why this is documentation and not behaviour. I read both consumers. Each tests Flags.IsInternal() before consulting the map — reason.go:205-209 and operation_mode.go:397-401 — so a FLAGS=1 parameter never reaches the allow-list and the entry can never fire. The cost is entirely in what the comment claims: it asserts a property of the descriptor ('their Flags field includes FLAG.INTERNAL') that the firmware contradicts for that one name, and it justifies the entry with a claim about our own pipeline ('the operation-mode gating pipeline reads it directly') rather than about the CCU. The prior finding's second result also stands and is worth keeping: the firmware's INTERNAL-by-name set is wider than our allow-list — OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE, COLOR_LIST_* and SOUNDFILE_LIST_* are FLAGS=2 as well — so the comment's provenance line, that this set was ported verbatim from the Python sibling's field map, describes a different set from the one the firmware flags. Leaving them out is the safe direction for an allow-list; conflating the two sets is not.

all.title: The default pairing window and the CCU's clamp are stated as facts with no source
all.site: internal/model/hub/install_mode.go:214 (DefaultInstallModeDuration = 60s), :199-208 (Press); internal/model/hub/writers.go:42-44 (InstallModeWriter contract); default applied at internal/north/rest/handlers/system_hub.go:325
all.citation: Default, BidCos-RF: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:598-634 (XmlRpcMethodSetInstallMode) — `if(params.size()>=2)time=params[1]; else time=60;` at :608-609, with the method's own doc comment at :594-595 verbatim: "Der Parameter \"seconds\" ist optional und gibt die Zeit in Sekunden an, die der Install-Mode aktiv bleiben soll. \"seconds\" darf maximal 600 sein. Defaultwert ist 60." Default, HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#setInstallMode and #setInstallModeWithWhitelist — both open `int internalTime = 60; if (time != null) { internalTime = time; }` before calling AccessPointUtil#setInclusionMode. Operator surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_add_device.cgi:903 `xmlrpc $RFD_URL setInstallMode [list bool $activate]` — the WebUI's BidCos teach-in passes NO seconds argument and so runs on the firmware default; the HmIP teach-in dialog in the same file (:918-940, hmip_install_mode_start) hard-codes `installTime = 60` and posts it as `'time' : installTime`. Clamp, BidCos-RF: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:580-597 and :599-616 (both SetInstallMode overloads) `if (seconds > INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME) seconds = INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME;` with ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:562 `enum{INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME=600};`; there is no lower bound — `if (seconds)` then arms the timer, and the else branch (`seconds == 0`) sets install_mode = INSTALL_OFF. Clamp, HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.AccessPointUtil#setInclusionMode passes the value straight through — `long timeoutTimestamp = System.currentTimeMillis() + (long)time.intValue() * 1000L; long timerID = vertx.setTimer((long)time.intValue() * 1000L, new InclusionTimeoutHandler(accessPoint, vertx));` — with no bound check anywhere on the path.
all.ourValue: "duration is clamped by the CCU (typically 60 s min, 3600 s max); the writer does not clamp itself" (writers.go:43)
all.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF: no minimum at all (0 means OFF), maximum 600 s (RFManager.h:562 INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME=600). HmIP: no minimum and no maximum — the value is used verbatim as the inclusion timer.
all.finding: Split verdict, and the two halves point in opposite directions. The 60-second default is confirmed three times over and is genuinely a property of the pairing behaviour rather than of any one surface: the BidCos daemon substitutes 60 when the caller omits `seconds`, the HmIP legacy handler substitutes 60 in both its setInstallMode entry points, and the CCU's own teach-in dialog relies on the first and hard-codes the second. DefaultInstallModeDuration = 60s at install_mode.go:214 is right, and so is the comment's framing of it. The clamp claim at writers.go:43 is wrong on both bounds and on both transports, and it is the load-bearing half — it is the stated reason the writer does not validate. There is no 60 s minimum anywhere; on BidCos-RF a `seconds` of 0 does not become 60, it turns install mode OFF, and the maximum is 600 s, a factor of six below the 3600 s the comment asserts. On HmIP nothing clamps at all: a caller-supplied 3600 really does open a one-hour pairing window, while the same request against BidCos-RF silently becomes ten minutes. So the operator-visible behaviour our comment describes as uniform is in fact transport-dependent and unbounded on one of the two. What our code should follow is the firmware's own ceiling per transport, not a single invented pair of bounds: if the daemon wants to keep not clamping, the contract should say the CCU truncates to 600 s on BidCos-RF and does not bound HmIP at all — and a duration above 600 s should not be reported back to the operator as if it had been honoured. Our lower guard (duration <= 0 → ErrInstallModeInvalidDuration, install_mode.go:225) is a divergence from the firmware's 0-means-off, but a safe one.
all.negativeControl: Had the comment been right I would have found a lower-bound raise (a `if (seconds < 60) seconds = 60`-shaped line, or a 60 substituted for a non-null small value) and a 3600 ceiling constant on at least one of the two paths. I read both SetInstallMode overloads in RFManager.cpp end to end and the whole AccessPointUtil inclusion path, and grepped INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME across ../OpenCCU-Base/src — it resolves to exactly one enum, 600, referenced only by the two clamp sites. The check plainly distinguishes: the same reading produced a confirmed 60 for the default in the very same functions where it produced a refuted 3600/60-min for the clamp.
all.challengeNote:
Contradiction upheld on the clamp, and extended: the half the prior pass reported as confirmed is also wrong at our surface. The severity is higher than recorded.

The clamp half — upheld, verified verbatim. I read all four sites. There is no 60 s minimum anywhere: on BidCos-RF a `seconds` of 0 does not become 60, it takes the else branch and turns install mode OFF; the only bound is the 600 s ceiling in both RFManager::SetInstallMode overloads, a factor of six below the 3600 s our contract asserts. On HmIP nothing clamps at all — AccessPointUtil multiplies the value by 1000 and hands it to the timer. So the same requested 3600 opens a one-hour window on HmIP and is silently truncated to ten minutes on BidCos-RF, while writers.go:43 describes one uniform pair of bounds. That comment is the stated reason the writer does not validate, which is what makes it load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

The default half — the prior pass called this 'confirmed three times over' and 'genuinely a property of the pairing behaviour rather than of any one surface'. That framing is the wrong-surface failure this audit exists to catch, and I found the surface it missed. Our HmIP-RF path does not call the legacy XML-RPC setInstallMode the prior grounding cites. It calls JSON-RPC Interface.setInstallModeHMIP, and that method's Tcl implementation defaults `time` to 30, not 60, then forwards an explicit time onward so HMIPServer's 60 is unreachable from here. Three surfaces, two defaults. The default is a property of the surface, exactly as the comment denies.

What is still safe, and what is not. The constant's value survives, because no firmware default is ever exercised from this daemon: Press() at install_mode.go:202 passes 60 explicitly, the REST handler substitutes hub.DefaultInstallModeDuration for a zero at system_hub.go:323-326, and ccu_extended.go always puts a `time` on the wire. So DefaultInstallModeDuration = 60s is a defensible choice of our own; its justification is not. What is not safe is the missing ceiling: validateInstallModeRequest (system_hub.go:362-376) rejects only Seconds < 0, so an operator asking for 3600 on BidCos-RF is told the request succeeded and gets 600. If the daemon keeps not clamping, the contract should say the CCU truncates to 600 s on BidCos-RF and does not bound HmIP at all, and a duration above 600 s should not be reported back as honoured. Our own lower guard — duration <= 0 -> ErrInstallModeInvalidDuration at install_mode.go:225 — diverges from the firmware's 0-means-off, but in the safe direction; I would keep it.

all.title: FLAGS STICKY is 10 decimal, which overlaps INTERNAL|SERVICE, and the comment itself says firmware documents 0x10
all.ourValue: FlagSticky = 10 (0b1010); Flag.Has is an all-bits test, so IsSticky() == (FLAGS & 10) == 10
all.firmwareValue: FLG_STICKY = (1<<4) = 16 = 0x10
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:69 — `FLG_STICKY=(1<<4)  //!< Servicenachricht setzt sich nicht selbst zurueck, wenn der Grund fuer die Nachricht entfaellt`; the same enum block gives FLG_VISIBLE=(1<<0):65, FLG_INTERNAL=(1<<1):66, FLG_TRANSFORM=(1<<2):67, FLG_SERVICE=(1<<3):68. Parsed at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:82 `if(strstr(temp, "sticky"))flags |= FLG_STICKY;` over an accumulator initialised at :32 `flags=FLG_VISIBLE;`, and emitted verbatim onto the XML-RPC paramset description at :210 `(*val)["FLAGS"]=flags;`. HmIP legacy surface, same bit: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter sets FLAGS to 25 for the parameter named UNREACH (= 1|8|16 = VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY) and to 9 (VISIBLE|SERVICE) for every other service-message parameter. Tier 2 corroboration: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json, 129,195 parameter descriptions carrying FLAGS+OPERATIONS+TYPE — observed FLAGS values are {0,1,2,3,5,9,11,25}; FLAGS=25 occurs 168 times (UNREACH x156, STICKY_UNREACH x12, e.g. HmIP-STV.json VCU3432945:0/VALUES/UNREACH), FLAGS=10 occurs zero times. Provenance of our value (Tier 3 witness): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:1243 `STICKY = 10  # This might be wrong. Documentation says 0x10 # not used`.
all.finding: Contradicted. The CCU builds FLAGS as an OR of single bits and STICKY is bit 4 (0x10 = 16), not 10. Our constant is not a bit at all, and because Flag.Has is an all-bits-set test the rule is effectively inverted on real data: FLAGS=25 (VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY — the genuinely sticky HmIP UNREACH, 168 occurrences in the descriptor corpus) gives 25&10 = 8 != 10, so IsSticky() returns false for a sticky parameter; FLAGS=11 (VISIBLE|INTERNAL|SERVICE, 268 occurrences, mostly BidCos STICKY_UNREACH and ERR_TTCU_*) gives 11&10 = 10, so IsSticky() returns true for a parameter whose sticky bit is clear. The code comment ("documented as 0x10 ... a known eQ-3 documentation bug") has it backwards: 0x10 is what the firmware implements; 10 is the Python family's own flagged-uncertain guess. Fix is FlagSticky = 16, and pkg/hmenum/bitmask_test.go:52 (TestFlagStickyKeepsAiohomematicEncoding) is the guard that has to change. Latent today — IsSticky has no production caller — but the sibling bits from the same enum are live in internal/store/visibility.
all.negativeControl: Had our value been right, HSSParameter.h would define FLG_STICKY as the literal 10 or as (1<<3)|(1<<1), and sticky parameters in the descriptor corpus would carry FLAGS with bits 1 and 3 set and bit 4 clear. The check discriminates: it returned a different answer for the four sibling flags, whose declared bits (1,2,4,8) match our constants exactly, and it found a concrete FLAGS value (25) that our test misclassifies and a concrete value (11) that it misclassifies the other way.
all.challengeNote: Upheld as contradicted, and strengthened. STICKY is bit 4 (16); 10 is not a bit at all but INTERNAL|SERVICE, and because Flag.Has is an all-bits-set test the predicate is inverted on real descriptor data: FLAGS=25 gives 25&10=8 != 10 → IsSticky() false for the 168 genuinely sticky rows, while FLAGS=11 gives 11&10=10 → IsSticky() true for 268 rows whose bit 4 is clear. The code comment has the direction backwards: 0x10 is what the firmware implements, 10 is the Python family's own flagged-uncertain guess. Two corrections to the original: (a) the descriptor count is 129,395, not 129,195; (b) the finding paraphrases our comment as calling 0x10 'a known eQ-3 documentation bug' — the actual text at paramset.go:100-104 and the guard comment at bitmask_test.go:50-51 are both truncated mid-sentence and no longer parse ('STICKY is documented as 0x10 but / the value stays faithful to that encoding for wire parity'), so the comment defect is worse than reported, not different. Latency confirmed independently: grep across the repo shows IsSticky/FlagSticky have zero production callers — only pkg/hmenum/bitmask_test.go and tests/contract/hmenum_constants_test.go:48. Fix is FlagSticky = 16; the guard that has to change is TestFlagStickyKeepsAiohomematicEncoding at pkg/hmenum/bitmask_test.go:49-55, which asserts the wrong value by name.

all.title: The 70-name IGNORED_PARAMETERS deny list and its 13 wildcard patterns rest on the Python port alone
all.ourValue: INHIBIT, SPEED, BOOST_TIME, BOOST_STATE, ADAPTION_DRIVE, RELOCK_DELAY, SELF_CALIBRATION, USER_PROGRAM, WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER, INSTALL_TEST all suppressed unconditionally; plus every VALUES parameter ending in _STATUS/_RESULT/_REPORTING/_SUBMIT/_OVERFLOW/_OVERRUN or starting with HANDLE_/IDENTIFY_/ADJUSTING_/ERR_TTM_/PARTY_START_/PARTY_STOP_/STATUS_FLAG_
all.firmwareValue: INSTALL_TEST is the only one the firmware declares internal (ui_flags="internal"; FLAGS 2 or 3 on all 829 descriptor occurrences). The other nine are declared FLAGS=1 (VISIBLE set, INTERNAL clear, SERVICE clear); INHIBIT is operations="read,write,event" on 268 channels; LED_STATUS, caught by the _STATUS$ suffix rule, is operations="read,write,event" on 16 channels of HM-OU-LED16 with VALUE_LIST [OFF,RED,GREEN,ORANGE]
all.citation: Device XMLs (the type descriptions the firmware ships): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_s.xml:240 `<parameter id="INHIBIT" operations="read,write,event" control="NONE" loopback="true">` (27 identical declarations across rftypes, none carrying ui_flags); rf_winmatic.xml:177 `<parameter id="SPEED" operations="write" control="NONE">`; rf_winmatic.xml:170 and rf_keymatic.xml:176 `<parameter id="RELOCK_DELAY" operations="write" control="NONE">`; rf_ou_led16_le_v1_0.xml:173 `<parameter id="LED_STATUS" operations="read,write,event" control="NONE">`. Contrast, the one entry that holds: every INSTALL_TEST declaration is `ui_flags="internal"` (23x operations="write", 22x operations="event", 1x "write,event"). Operator-facing labels in the CCU's own parameter string table ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/stringtable_de.txt: INHIBIT:1031-1033, BOOST_STATE:286, BOOST_TIME:287, KEYMATIC|RELOCK_DELAY:1073-1074, WINMATIC|RELOCK_DELAY:2256-2257, SELF_CALIBRATION=START/STOP:1698-1699, USER_PROGRAM:2051, LED_STATUS=GREEN/OFF/ORANGE/RED:1126-1129, ACTOR_WINDOW|HANDLE_LED_MODE:95-97, ACTOR_WINDOW|HANDLE_LOCK:98-99. The distribution adds a WebUI control that reads LED_STATUS: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0091-WebUI-Add-HM-OU-LED16-LedStatus.patch:31 `integer objValue = cObj.DPByHssDP("LED_STATUS").Value();`. Tier 2 runtime descriptors, ../pydevccu/pydevccu/paramset_descriptions/*.json, VALUES paramsets only, as (OPERATIONS, FLAGS, TYPE) x count: INHIBIT (7,1,BOOL)x267 + (6,1,BOOL)x1; BOOST_TIME (5,1,INTEGER)x21; BOOST_STATE (5,1,INTEGER)x2; SPEED (2,1,FLOAT)x3; RELOCK_DELAY (2,1,FLOAT)x7; ADAPTION_DRIVE (2,1,ACTION)x1; SELF_CALIBRATION (2,1,ENUM)x2; USER_PROGRAM (2,1,STRING)x2; INSTALL_TEST (3,2,BOOL)x124 + (4,3,ACTION)x437 + (2,3,ACTION)x251 + (6,3,ACTION)x17; LED_STATUS (7,1,ENUM)x17 + (2,1,INTEGER)x2 (HM-OU-LED16.json VCU0000158:1..16, HM-OU-X.json); HANDLE_LOCK (7,1,BOOL)x1; HANDLE_LED_MODE (7,1,ENUM)x1. WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER appears only in MASTER, never in VALUES: (3,1,ENUM)x2.
all.finding: Contradicted for nine of the ten names the reader asked about, and for two of the thirteen wildcard prefixes/suffixes. Only INSTALL_TEST matches the justification written next to it — it is the sole entry the firmware declares ui_flags="internal", and its descriptor FLAGS carry the INTERNAL bit on all 829 occurrences. The other nine carry FLAGS=1: VISIBLE set, INTERNAL and SERVICE clear, i.e. exactly the shape the CCU's own visible-parameter test (../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParamset.cpp:70, `(param->GetFlags() & (FLG_INTERNAL|FLG_VISIBLE))==FLG_VISIBLE`) accepts. They would NOT have been filtered anyway. Five of them (INHIBIT, BOOST_STATE, BOOST_TIME, RELOCK_DELAY, SELF_CALIBRATION) plus USER_PROGRAM carry operator labels in the CCU's own parameter string table. INHIBIT is read+write+event on 268 channels — a live device write path our list removes fleet-wide. The widest damage is in the wildcards, as the bundle predicted: the `_STATUS$` suffix suppresses LED_STATUS, a read/write/event ENUM on all 16 channels of HM-OU-LED16 with a four-value list and its own string-table entries, for which the OpenCCU distribution ships a dedicated WebUI control; the `HANDLE_` prefix suppresses HANDLE_LOCK and HANDLE_LED_MODE (both OPERATIONS=7, FLAGS=1, both labelled under ACTOR_WINDOW in the string table). Of the 82 distinct wildcard-matched VALUES parameters in the descriptor corpus, 23 are writable (OPERATIONS bit 2 set): LED_STATUS, HANDLE_LOCK, HANDLE_LED_MODE, IDENTIFY_DURATION, IDENTIFY_TARGET_LEVEL, PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT and the eight PARTY_START_*/PARTY_STOP_* pairs. Separately: WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER never occurs in a VALUES paramset in the corpus (MASTER only), so that entry appears inert on the surface the list documents itself as governing. Not audited here: the remaining ~60 names on the list.
all.negativeControl: Had the list's stated basis been right, each name would carry ui_flags="internal" or "service" in src/devicetypes and its descriptor FLAGS would set bit 2 (INTERNAL) or bit 3 (SERVICE), and none would appear in the CCU's operator string table. The check demonstrably produces that other answer: INSTALL_TEST came out with ui_flags="internal", FLAGS 2/3, and no string-table label, on the same measurement that put the other nine at FLAGS=1 with labels.
all.challengeNote: Narrowed hard. Five bites. (1) The headline damage claim is false against our own code: LED_STATUS on HM-OU-LED16 is explicitly carved out at internal/store/visibility/rules.go:341, inside `unIgnoreParametersByDevice` (declared :316), consumed by `deviceUnIgnoresByPrefix` (decider.go:309-320) in the step-0 early exit at decider.go:237 — one line above the :243 the finding cites — so it returns not-ignored before the `_STATUS$` wildcard is ever evaluated. Pinned by internal/store/visibility/rules_test.go:184 `{"HM-OU-LED16", hmenum.ParameterLEDStatus, true}`. The surviving remnant is HM-OU-X VCU0000159:1, one channel, not sixteen. (2) 'Suppressed unconditionally' is false for all ten names: step 0 and the required-parameter whitelist (`custom.DefaultRegistry().RequiredParameters()`, wired at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:105) both bypass the list, and the effect is a forced DataPointUsageIgnored mark, not DP removal — internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline_visibility_test.go:82-88 asserts the INHIBIT DP IS created ('every wire parameter becomes a DP under the new architecture'). So 'a live device write path our list removes fleet-wide' is not established. (3) Wrong surface on the load-bearing inference: HSSParamset.cpp:70 is not a visible-parameter test, it is a TAB_ORDER assignment (`param->SetTabOrder(tab_order++)`) — every parameter is inserted into `params` regardless, and GetDescription emits every one with no FLAGS gate, so 'they would NOT have been filtered anyway' rests on a line that filters nothing. FLAGS answers what the descriptor declares; our list governs a northbound entity surface, whose CCU counterpart is template-driven per channel type (www/rega/esp/controls/*.fn), and INHIBIT appears nowhere in the whole WebUI/ReGa tree except stringtable_de.txt. (4) Each verbatim quote carries contrary evidence the finding did not address: control="NONE" on INHIBIT, SPEED, RELOCK_DELAY and LED_STATUS, where the operator-facing siblings in the same paramsets carry a real control (rf_s.xml:219 STATE control="SWITCH.STATE"; rf_ou_led16_le_v1_0.xml:163 PRESS_SHORT control="BTN_SHORT_ONLY.SHORT"). CONTROL is emitted on the wire at HSSParameter.cpp:212. (5) Tier inflation: six of the ten names — BOOST_TIME, BOOST_STATE, ADAPTION_DRIVE, SELF_CALIBRATION, USER_PROGRAM, WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER — have ZERO declarations in any of the 142 shipped device XMLs; their FLAGS=1 is Tier 2 only, plus Tier 1 on the HmIP side by construction (HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter assigns 1 to everything outside its UNREACH / ERROR_CODE / service-message / REPETITIONS+OUTPUT_SELECT_SIZE+COLOR_LIST_*/ON_TIME_LIST_*/SOUNDFILE_LIST_* branches), which the finding did not cite. It reads as if all nine were BidCos Tier 1. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is real: INSTALL_TEST is the one entry whose written justification is Tier-1 grounded (46/46 ui_flags="internal"), and the `HANDLE_` prefix does over-reach — HANDLE_LOCK and HANDLE_LED_MODE, OPERATIONS=7 FLAGS=1, one channel each on HM-ReSC-Win-PCB-xx, labelled at stringtable_de.txt:95-99, with no un-ignore entry. That is the boundary: a one-device over-reach, not a fleet-wide one. Counts corrected: 67 names not 70, 14 writable wildcard-matched parameters not 23 (the finding's own list enumerates exactly 14). Separately true and worth keeping: the doc comment at rules.go:198-200 ('parameter names for which no data points are created') is refuted by our own test at device_pipeline_visibility_test.go:86.

all.title: "All alarm messages are unconditionally acknowledgeable" clears the local set with no per-entry gate
all.ourValue: AlarmMessages.AcknowledgeAll clears the entire local map; ServiceMessages.AcknowledgeAll deletes only Quittable entries; the ReGa script internal/client/rega/scripts/acknowledge_all_alarm_messages.fn calls AlReceipt() on every ALARMDP under ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES with AlState()==1, while acknowledge_all_service_messages.fn gates on `oTrigger.Operations() & 2`
all.firmwareValue: Same asymmetry, in the CCU's own two pages: the alarm list renders an enabled Confirm on every row and its ackAll loops unconditionally; the service-message list gates both the per-row button and ackAll on the trigger's OPERATION_WRITE bit
all.citation: Alarm side — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/tabs/statusviews/alarmMessages.htm:23, the list is seeded as `if( oTmp.IsTypeOf( OT_ALARMDP ) && ( oTmp.AlState() == asOncoming ) )` over ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES; :248 every row gets `<input type="button" name="btnConfirm" ... onclick="ReceiptAlarm('#oSV.ID()#');" ...>` with no gate and no disabled variant anywhere in the file; :328-333 `ackAll = function() { for (var i = 0; i < arAlarms.length; i++) { ReceiptAlarm(arAlarms[i]['id']); } }`. Service side, same tree — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/tabs/statusviews/serviceMessages.htm:325-326 `boolean bWrite = (oLastTrigger.Operations() & OPERATION_WRITE); if( oLastTrigger.Operations() & OPERATION_WRITE )` → enabled button, else :339 the same button with `disabled="disabled"`; :429-437 `ackAll = function() { ... if( arServices[i]['write'] ) { ReceiptAlarm( arServices[i]['id'], false ); } ... }`.
all.finding: Confirmed, on the surface our code is on. The CCU carries no per-alarm quittable property: the alarm list has no equivalent of the service list's OPERATION_WRITE test, no disabled-button branch, and its confirm-all loop is unconditional — while the service-message page in the same directory implements exactly the per-entry gate our ServiceMessages side mirrors. The two different answers in messages.go are the two different answers the firmware's own two pages give, and our alarm script's selection (ALARMDP under ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES in the oncoming state) matches alarmMessages.htm:23 exactly. Two residuals, both narrower than the claim: (a) whether ReGaHss's AlReceipt() itself can fail for an individual alarm is inside a stripped binary (../OpenCCU-Base/bin/*/ReGaHss) and is not decidable from source — our optimistic local clear would then drop an alarm the CCU still holds until the next full refresh; (b) our script hardcodes `AlState() == 1` for asOncoming, and the ordinal value of asOncoming is not carried by any readable source (the ReGaHss string table lists asNone/asOncoming/asReceipted in that order, but list order is not an ordinal and I will not treat it as one). (b) is a separate not-performable item, not part of this candidate.
all.negativeControl: Had alarms carried a per-entry acknowledgeable flag, alarmMessages.htm would render a disabled Confirm for non-acknowledgeable rows and filter its ackAll on a per-row property — the exact shape serviceMessages.htm:326/:339/:433 uses. The check discriminates because that other answer was produced, by the sibling page, on the same measurement.
all.challengeNote: Confirmed, with the boundary named. The alarm page is not missing the gate for want of the data: it fetches the last-trigger object, tests it for OT_HSSDP, and declines to test its Operations — while the service page in the same directory does exactly that test on the same object type. That is a deliberate asymmetry in the firmware, and messages.go reproduces it on both sides: AlarmMessage has no Quittable field to gate on (the struct carries ID/Name/Description/timestamps/Counter/DisplayName only), ServiceMessage does (:302). Our alarm script's selection matches alarmMessages.htm:23 exactly. BOUNDARY, which I hold tighter than the original did: what the readable sources settle is the WebUI presentation surface and its two ackAll loops, not the alarm engine's acceptance rule. `functions.fn::ReceiptAlarm()` is dispatched at src/webui/rega/www/esp/functions.htm:2 but is present in no readable file — grep for ReceiptAlarm across OpenCCU-Base returns only the two statusview pages, the dispatch line, and one commented-out line at esp/system.fn:370 — and `AlReceipt` occurs nowhere in the ReGa/WebUI sources, only as a symbol in the stripped bin/*/ReGaHss alongside strings such as 'Alarm is not receipted until now!' and 'AlAutoReceipt'. So the chain from button to AlReceipt is unreadable at two points, not one; 'the CCU carries no per-alarm quittable property' is safe as a statement about what the CCU presents and about what our model can populate, and remains open as a statement about the engine. Residual (b) from the original stands and I could not close it: asOncoming's ordinal is not carried by any readable source — the three names asNone/asOncoming/asReceipted appear as adjacent strings in ReGaHss with no values beside them, no numeric AlState comparison exists anywhere in OpenCCU-Base or the OpenCCU patch set, and the only AlState()==1 occurrences outside our repo are copies of our own scripts. Our hardcoded 1 is therefore an ungrounded ordinal — but it is used identically by both scripts, so it cancels out of the asymmetry claim; it is a separate not-performable item against acknowledge_all_alarm_messages.fn and acknowledge_all_service_messages.fn, not against this one.

all.title: "A deactivated program refuses to run" is a comment, and it gates a control
all.ourValue: ProgramExecuteAvailable(active) = active; feeds ProgramState.ExecuteAvailable (REST internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:432, WS internal/north/rest/ws/hub_events.go:339) and the MQTT execute-role availability topic (internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go:1013)
all.firmwareValue: Not decidable from source: the accept/refuse decision lives in ReGaHss (dom object method ProgramExecute), which ships only as a stripped binary. What IS readable: no caller on any execution path tests Active(), and the CCU's own control page offers the Execute button for an inactive program.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/system.fn:1190-1196 `function ExecuteProgram() { object obj = dom.GetObject( system.GetVar("dpid") ); if (obj) { obj.ProgramExecute(); } }` — no Active() test. Control-page rendering, same file :1277-1283: the Start/Execute div is written whenever `system.GetVar("iStatusOnly") == 0`, and Active() is passed only as the second constructor argument at :1282 `Write("new iseButtonProg("#pid#", "#objProg.Active()#");")`; in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www_source/ise/js/iseButtonsSwitch.js:208-226 that argument is used solely at :215 `if ( progActive ) { ControlBtn.on(this.actBtn); }` to light the "Aktiv" tile, while :225 `ExecuteProgram(this.id)` runs unconditionally. JSON-RPC surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/api/methods/program/execute.tcl — `var program = dom.GetObject(id); Write(program.ProgramExecute());`, i.e. the CCU does report a boolean result to the caller, but the script adds no gate. Same shape at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/pda/eq3/program.tcl:31. Distribution behaviour: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0122-WebUI-ProgramExecutionWithConditionCheck.patch adds a second button and re-labels the first, keeps both ungated by Active(), and documents the two verbs — `ExecuteProgram = function(dpid, thenOnly) { ... pb += (thenOnly === true) ? "  o.ProgramExecute();" : "  o.State(1);"; }`, with `o.State(1)` = "Executes the program including all condition checks" and `ProgramExecute()` = "Executes only the actions of the first THEN part ... without considering any condition check whatsoever". ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0070-WebUI-ProgramList-InactiveProgramsMod.patch greys an inactive program's row text and touches no button.
all.finding: Tier-1 silent on the claim as written. Whether ReGaHss declines to run a program with Active()==false cannot be read: ProgramExecute and State(1) are dom methods implemented inside the stripped ReGaHss binary, and the readable sources contain no such guard on any path. What the readable firmware does settle is the surface our rule actually governs — execute-availability offered to an operator — and there it points the other way: the CCU's own Status-und-Bedienung page renders the Execute button for an inactive program and only dims the separate "Aktiv" indicator, and the same codebase disables a button when it means to (serviceMessages.htm:339 uses disabled="disabled" for a non-acknowledgeable service message). So our rule makes the MQTT/REST/WS execute control unavailable in a case where the CCU's own UI keeps it live. Two further facts worth carrying: the CCU exposes two distinct execution verbs with different semantics (State(1) with condition checks, ProgramExecute() first-THEN-only), and Program.execute returns ProgramExecute()'s boolean — so if a refusal exists it is reported to the caller, which our execute path could observe directly instead of predicting it from the flag. What our rule rests on today: the comment at payload.go:86, plus the Python family; no firmware source was found behind it.
all.missingInput: The body of ReGaHss's dom ProgramExecute / State setter for OT_PROGRAM objects. Only ../OpenCCU-Base/bin/{i686,arm,aarch64,x86_64}-*/ReGaHss carries it and all four are stripped; the readable tree holds only HMScript callers. Settling it needs either an unstripped/annotated build or a live CCU probe (execute an inactive program and observe Program.execute's boolean plus ProgramLastExecuteTime).
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU refused, the readable path would show it the way this codebase shows every other refusal: `if( obj.Active() )` around the ProgramExecute call, or a disabled Execute button on the control page. The check does produce that other answer elsewhere — serviceMessages.htm:326/:339 gates and disables its Confirm button on a per-entry property — so a gate would have been visible had one existed on the program path. It cannot, however, distinguish "no gate, and ReGaHss runs it" from "no gate, and ReGaHss silently refuses"; that is why the verdict is tier1-silent and not contradicted.

all.title: The 255-character limit on a string system variable comes from the Python reference
all.ourValue: SysvarTextMaxLength = 255, enforced as `if len(text) > limit` — i.e. UTF-8 bytes — and the over-long write is rejected locally before any CCU call
all.firmwareValue: Not found. No length constant, no maxlength attribute and no length test exists anywhere in the readable CCU sources for a string system variable.
all.citation: Absence, measured across the readable Tier-1 surface: `grep -rn -i maxlength ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/` returns nothing, so no sysvar input carries one — including the create/edit dialog ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/tabs/admin/msg/newSysVar.htm and the admin list ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/pages/tabs/admin/systemvars.htm, whose string branches (:171-174, :181-182, :281-283) carry no bound at all, unlike the numeric branch which writes ValueMin/ValueMax (:287-288). The two OpenCCU patches that touch sysvar input validation add no length test: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0178-WebUI-Fix-ValidateSaveSysvarInput.patch adds only `isTextAllowed(...)`, and 0097-WebUI-SetSysvarValueByUser.patch adds none. The CCU's JSON-RPC sysvar surface has no string setter at all — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/api/methods/sysvar/ contains createBool/createEnum/createFloat/setbool/setenum/setfloat and no string variant — which is why our write goes through ReGa (internal/client/rega/runner.go:543 SetSystemVariableString). The declared subtype is ISO-8859-1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/rega/www/esp/system.fn:847-848 `sv.ValueType(ivtString); sv.ValueSubType(istChar8859);`. Provenance of our 255 (Tier 3 witness, not authority): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/support.py:208-210 `if isinstance(value, str) and len(value) > 255:` followed by a warning and truncation to 255 — note the witness truncates where we reject.
all.finding: Tier-1 silent, and none of the three sub-questions is answerable. The object that owns ivtString/istChar8859 variables is ReGaHss, which ships only as a stripped binary (../OpenCCU-Base/bin/*/ReGaHss); the source tree holds only its Tcl bridge (src/tclrega/tclrega.cpp, no length constants) and HMScript callers. Nothing in rfd, hs485d, libhsscomm, tclrega, tclrpc, the WebUI or the ReGa pages declares a maximum length for a string system variable, rejects an over-long one, or truncates one. So: the value 255 is unsourced against the firmware; whether the CCU rejects or truncates is unsourced; and the unit is worse than unsourced — the CCU declares the subtype as ISO-8859-1, so a CCU-side character count and our `len(text)` (UTF-8 bytes) are different units for every non-ASCII character. A 200-character German string with 60 umlauts is 260 bytes and our check rejects it, whichever way the real limit falls. Our rule currently rests on aiohomematic/model/support.py alone, and diverges from it in behaviour: that witness truncates with a warning, we return an error. Making this measurable requires extending the source: a live CCU write of increasing-length ASCII and Latin-1 strings, reading back through SysVar.getValue, is the only path I can see.
all.missingInput: The maximum length ReGaHss enforces for an ivtString/istChar8859 variable value, its unit (ISO-8859-1 characters vs bytes), and its over-length behaviour (reject vs truncate). No readable source carries any of the three; the enforcing component is a stripped binary.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU declared a 255 limit, the sysvar string input would carry `maxlength="255"` or the save path a length test — the same file set does carry maxlength where a limit exists (e.g. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/remote4dis_ch_master.tcl:94 uses maxlength="12" for the RC-19 display TEXT1 field), so the grep discriminates. It cannot distinguish "no limit exists" from "the limit lives inside ReGaHss and is never surfaced", which is exactly why the value is reported as unsourced rather than as absent.

all.title: HmIP-FWI CODE_ID MAX widened from 21 to 31 on the claim that CODE_ID is a 5-bit field with 31 = idle
all.ourValue: MAX=31, justified as "5-bit field, 31 = no active code"; the CCU's MAX=21 asserted to be wrong
all.firmwareValue: HmIP-FWI CODE_ID: MIN=1, MAX=21, DEFAULT=1 (deliberate, channel-type-specific); CODE_ID is decoded as valueData[0] & 0x1F; idle is CODE_STATE=0 (CodeState.IDLE), not CODE_ID=31; CODE_ID=21 = bell button
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createCodeId — registered three times: default key CODE_ID → createCodeId(0, 30); key (CODE_ID, "fwi") → createCodeId(1, 21); key (CODE_ID, "wkp") → createReadOnlyCodeId(1, 8, -1.0). createCodeId builds StateParameter("CODE_ID", LogicalType.INTEGER, PhysicalType.INTEGER, read|write|event, null, default=minvalue, min=minvalue, max=maxvalue, …) — no bit-width field. · HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler, CODE_STATUS case: CODE_STATE is decoded as (valueData[0] & 0xFF) >> 5 and CODE_ID as valueData[0] & 0x1F. · HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.CodeState — IDLE is the first constant (ordinal 0), followed by KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED. · ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/controls/maintenanceFWI.fn:80-91 — `if (codeState == 0) {curState = "${codeIdle}";}` and, only under `codeState == 1`, `if ((objCodeID.Value() == 21) || (objCodeID.Value() == "21")) { curState = "${lblBellButton}"; }`. Tier 2 is silent: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-FWI.json carries the device/channel descriptions only, and ../pydevccu/paramsets_db.json contains no CODE_ID entry at all.
all.finding:
Both premises of the patch comment fail, in opposite ways.

(1) "the CCU declares MAX=21 … [wrongly]" is contradicted. 21 is not a stale or generic bound the CCU got wrong: the firmware registers CODE_ID three times under distinct channel-type keys, and the HmIP-FWI variant is deliberately (1, 21) — narrower than the generic (0, 30) and wider than the keypad (1, 8). The WebUI then gives 21 a name: on the FWI maintenance control, CODE_ID == 21 renders as the bell button, i.e. 1..20 are the twenty finger codes and 21 is the doorbell. So MAX=21 is the firmware's considered answer for exactly this device.

(2) "5-bit field" is confirmed — CODE_ID is the low five bits of the CODE_STATUS byte (`valueData[0] & 0x1F`), CODE_STATE the top three (`>> 5`) — so the wire can indeed carry 0..31 and a 31 observation is physically possible. But nothing in the firmware names 31 as an idle/no-active-code sentinel; that half of the comment is Tier-1 silent. The firmware's idle indicator is a different parameter: CODE_STATE = 0 = CodeState.IDLE, and the WebUI reads CODE_ID *only* when CODE_STATE == 1 (KNOWN_CODE_ID_RECEIVED), ignoring it in every other state.

Consequence for our code: the patch widens a bound the firmware set on purpose, and does so with a sentinel meaning the firmware does not assign. CODE_ID carries read|write|event on the fwi variant, so the widened MAX also admits writes of 22..31 that the declared range rejects. The reported symptom ("the entity never returned to 31 after a recognized code") is better served by following CODE_STATE — which is what the CCU's own operator surface does — than by re-interpreting an out-of-range CODE_ID. If the raw 31 must be kept, the honest framing is "the wire field is 5 bits wide, so values above the declared MAX are observable", not "31 means idle".
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, createCodeId for the "fwi" key would have carried max=31 (or the generic 0..30 registration would have applied to FWI with no fwi-specific override), and either the CODE_STATUS decode or the WebUI control would special-case 31 the way it special-cases 21. Instead the fwi override exists and pins 21, and the only value the WebUI singles out is 21. The check discriminates: the same file proves the mechanism can express per-device bounds (fwi 1..21 vs wkp 1..8 vs generic 0..30), so an idle sentinel or a wider FWI bound would have been visible in the same place I looked.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld, and the case is stronger than the first pass made it, but one link in its stated chain was unread and I close it differently.

Premise 1 — "the CCU declares MAX=21 [wrongly]" — is contradicted. 21 is the firmware's considered answer: the generic registration is (0,30), the keypad one is (1,8), and only the fwi-keyed one is (1,21). The WebUI then gives 21 a meaning on exactly our surface: the FWI maintenance control reads MAINTENANCE.CODE_ID, lists twenty CODE_USED_01..20 slots, and renders CODE_ID == 21 as the bell button. Twenty finger codes plus the doorbell is 21.

Premise 2 — "5-bit field, 31 = no active code" — splits. The bit layout is confirmed verbatim, and I added the leg that makes the observation credible: the event path applies no range check, so a raw 31 is deliverable and the reported symptom is physically consistent. But nothing in the firmware assigns 31 any meaning. The firmware's idle indicator is a different parameter — CODE_STATE = 0 = CodeState.IDLE — and the CCU's own operator surface reads CODE_ID only while CODE_STATE == 1, ignoring it in all seven other states. "31 = no active code" is a convention supplied by us, sitting behind a firmware citation. Under the project's own rule that half of the comment is not confirmable — it is Tier-1 silent, and the honest framing is "the wire field is 5 bits wide, so values above the declared MAX are observable".

Correction to the first pass's reasoning (not its verdict): it asserted that the (CODE_ID, "fwi") registration is the one HmIP-FWI receives. The second element of ParameterMapKey is a parameterSubtypeID, not a channel or device type, and it is assigned from a `subtype` attribute in a channel-type XML that is not readable here. That mapping was presented as read; it was not. It survives by elimination — (1,21) is the only registration in the whole firmware that can produce MAX=21, and our own patch records observing MAX=21 — plus the FWI-specific WebUI evidence above. Conclusion unchanged, chain repaired.

Consequence for our code: the patch widens a deliberate bound on a parameter that carries WRITE on this variant (ops = 7), so it also admits writes of 22..31 that the CCU's declared range rejects — that half is an inference about our validation path, not a firmware measurement. Following CODE_STATE, which is what the CCU's own surface does, addresses the reported symptom without re-interpreting an out-of-range CODE_ID.

all.title: HmIP-RGBW SATURATION gets the EVENT operations bit set by hand
all.ourValue: "HmIP-RGBW sometimes reports SATURATION without the EVENT bit" — patch ORs OperationsEvent into SATURATION's OPERATIONS when IsEvent() is false
all.firmwareValue: SATURATION OPERATIONS = 7 (read,write,event) unconditionally; identically HUE and COLOR_TEMPERATURE
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory — the VALUES-paramset registry contains exactly one SATURATION entry, `new ParameterMapKey("SATURATION")` → createLevel("SATURATION", 144, 1), with no channel-type variant; createLevel, createHue and createColorTemperature all take their ops from #getReadWriteEventIOOperation, which is #getReadEventIOOperation (READ|EVENT) OR'ed with WRITE. · HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations — READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4, so the emitted OPERATIONS byte is 7. · HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter — `parameterDescription.setOperations(parameter.getIoOperations().getValue())`, i.e. the byte is copied verbatim into the legacy XML-RPC ParamsetDescription; the only post-processing, #fillLegacyParameter, sets TabOrder, Unit and Control and never touches OPERATIONS. · ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HmIP/legacy-parameter-definition.config (1092 lines) contains no OPERATIONS key of any kind, and no SATURATION, HUE, COLOR_TEMPERATURE or RGBW entry. · HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.framehandling.HMIPApplicationHandler pushes SATURATION status through handleLevelStatus(..., "SATURATION_STATUS", "SATURATION") on the HUE_SATURATION_LEVEL_WITH_PROFILE status data type, so the device does event the value.
all.finding:
There is no path in this firmware by which the CCU emits a SATURATION descriptor without the EVENT bit. SATURATION is registered once, with read|write|event; the legacy XML-RPC descriptor copies that byte unchanged; the one override file that could rewrite a parameter description (legacy-parameter-definition.config, consumed by #fillLegacyParameter) can only set TabOrder, Unit and Control, and carries no RGBW or SATURATION entry at all.
