The device-side frame handling does deliver SATURATION as a status update, so the event source the patch restores is real — the patch is therefore a no-op against a current CCU (its Apply returns false) rather than a corruption, but its stated condition cannot be reproduced from the firmware.

The patch names neither a firmware version nor a CCU version, so the "sometimes" it rests on is unfalsifiable and the patch can never be retired on evidence. Either it was written against an older HMIPServer build, or the observation had a different cause (e.g. a descriptor read that raced device bring-up, or a channel where SATURATION is absent rather than event-less). Recommendation: either date the observation to a firmware version so it can be re-measured, or drop the patch — the descriptor is the authority here and it already says 7.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, I would have found a second SATURATION registration under a channel-type-qualified ParameterMapKey (the mechanism the same file uses for CODE_ID's "fwi" and "wkp" variants) built from #getReadEventIOOperation-without-EVENT or a write-only factory, or an OPERATIONS override in #fillLegacyParameter / legacy-parameter-definition.config. Both mechanisms exist and are exercised elsewhere in the same two files, so a per-device EVENT-less SATURATION would have been visible exactly where I looked; neither shows one.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld on every leg, with one addition and one boundary the first pass understated.

Addition: the first pass said the override file can only set TabOrder, Unit and Control. There is a fourth lever — .Disabled — and it is worth knowing because it strengthens the alternative explanation the first pass floated. A disabled parameter is dropped from the descriptor entirely; it never appears with reduced operations. So the two shapes a real CCU can produce for SATURATION are "present with OPERATIONS=7" and "absent". "Present without EVENT" is not among them.

Boundary: the patch names no firmware version, so "sometimes" cannot be falsified for builds not in this tree. What is measured is that the condition cannot arise on this firmware; that older builds behaved differently is neither shown nor excluded. Because Apply returns false against a current CCU the patch is inert rather than harmful, but it can never be retired on evidence as written. Either date the observation to a firmware version so it can be re-measured, or drop it — the descriptor is the authority and it already says 7.

I also checked the thing that would have made this a wrong-surface finding: whether HmIP-RGBW's colour channels are described by a second producer (a virtual universal-light service) rather than by the legacy path cited. They are not.

all.title: PONG correlation depends on the CCU echoing the caller_id verbatim, sourced only to the Python sibling
all.ourValue: The CCU echoes the ping caller_id as the PONG value unmodified and broadcasts PONGs to every registered logic-layer client; correlate only when the caller_id's '#'-prefix equals this client's WireBoundaryID
all.firmwareValue: Same: ReportEvent("CENTRAL", "PONG", callerId) with callerId passed through untouched, delivered to every entry in the handler map; the only validation is a string type check
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1206-1217 — XmlRpcMethodPing: `if(params[0].getType() != XmlRpcValue::TypeString) throw XmlRpcException("Parameter callerId must be of type string");` then `RFManager::GetSingleton()->Ping(params[0]);` — no length or character validation. · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:539-542 — `void HSSManager::Ping(XmlRpcValue& callerId) { ReportEvent("CENTRAL", "PONG", callerId); }` — the value is forwarded by reference, unmodified. · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:93-116 — ReportEvent iterates the whole `xmlrpc_handlers` map (`for (it = xmlrpc_handlers.begin(); it != xmlrpc_handlers.end(); ++it) … *dispatcher << message;`), i.e. every registered client, skipping only handlers already marked unreachable. · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSXmlRpcEventDispatcher.cpp:51-56 — `params[0] = m_id; params[1] = …GetAddress(); params[2] = …GetValueKey(); params[3] = …GetValue();`, so the event's interface_id is the *receiving* client's own registered id while params[3] is the untouched caller_id. · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:601-612 — the wired daemon's ping is the same shape, routing into the same HSSManager::Ping. · HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#ping → de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.AccessPointUtil#sendPong, which puts the callerID verbatim under the key "PONG" on a CENTRAL/channel-0 notification and *publishes* it on the event bus. · Virtual devices: HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.rega.VirtualDeviceHandlerRega#ping calls #event("CENTRAL", "PONG", callerID), which loops over every key in its registered-client map and sends one event per client with that client's own interface_id and the callerID as the value.
all.finding:
Both premises hold on all four CCU-side surfaces our clients speak to, and the fault modes the reader worried about are absent.

Echo fidelity: the caller_id crosses from the ping method to the event value without a copy, a trim, a case fold or a length cap. The only thing rfd checks is that the argument is a string; hs485d routes into the same HSSManager::Ping; the HmIP legacy surface stores the Java String unchanged under the "PONG" key; the ReGa virtual-device surface passes it straight into its event payload. So our '#'-token split is safe: whatever we send comes back byte-for-byte.

Broadcast: rfd/hs485d deliver every event, PONG included, to every registered XML-RPC handler; the HmIP path publishes (not sends point-to-point) on the notification bus; the virtual-device path explicitly iterates all registered clients. A second daemon on the same CCU therefore does see our PONGs and we see theirs — the exact condition the prefix guard exists for.

One firmware detail worth pinning in our comment, because it is what makes the guard necessary rather than merely prudent: the event's first argument is *not* the pinger's id, it is `m_id` — the id the receiving client itself registered at init(). A co-located daemon's PONG therefore arrives on our interface_id, so interface_id can never discriminate; only the echoed value can. Our design already does the right thing, but for the right reason only by accident of the reference port. Note also that the address is "CENTRAL" and the value key "PONG" (uppercase) on every path — a further discriminator we do not currently use. CUxD/BIN-RPC is outside these trees and stays unverified for this rule.
all.negativeControl: Had the echo not been verbatim, Ping would have rebuilt or normalised the string (a substr, a truncation to some id length, a re-registration lookup) before handing it to ReportEvent, and the value would have been reconstructed rather than forwarded by reference — none of that is present on any of the four paths. Had the delivery been caller-only, ReportEvent would have looked the sender's handler up by url or id instead of iterating the whole map, and VirtualDeviceHandlerRega#event would not loop over every registered client. Both checks can produce the opposite answer and both came back the same way.
all.challengeNote:
Every leg the first pass claimed holds, and I added the one it was missing: the HmIP path's broadcast-with-receiver-own-interface_id, which previously rested only on the rfd dispatcher. Echo fidelity survives on all four surfaces — no copy, trim, case fold, length cap or type coercion touches the caller_id anywhere between the ping method and the event value. Broadcast holds on all four: rfd and hs485d fan out over the whole handler map, the HmIP legacy handler fans out over backendClients, the ReGa virtual-device handler fans out over regaClients. And the detail that makes our guard necessary rather than merely prudent is now confirmed on two independent surfaces, not one: the event's interface_id is the receiver's own registered id, so a co-located daemon's PONG arrives stamped with OUR interface_id and interface_id can never discriminate. Only the echoed value can.

I demote from confirmed to narrowed on scope, not on doubt. Our correlation closure is installed per interface and runs for every interface whose backend declares PingPong — and the CUxD backend declares it true. CUxD is an add-on daemon speaking BIN-RPC; its sources are in neither reference tree, and nothing here establishes that it echoes the caller_id verbatim or broadcasts at all. That is a live boundary rather than a formality: if CUxD returns anything but our exact `<instance>-<central>-<interface>#<token>` string, the prefix test fails closed and every CUxD pong is silently discarded, so CUxD ping/pong health would read as permanently unmatched with no error anywhere. The comment should say which surfaces it was measured on and name CUxD as unverified, rather than saying "the CCU" as though it covered all five.

One further discriminator the firmware offers and we do not use: the address is "CENTRAL" and the value key "PONG" (uppercase) on every one of the four verified paths.

all.title: The `.nobackup` tag name and the `--exclude-tag` semantics are asserted about the CCU's own backup producers without a path:line
all.ourValue: Both producers — the WebUI `create_backup` CGI and `/bin/createBackup.sh` — tar `/usr/local` with GNU tar's `--exclude-tag=.nobackup`
all.firmwareValue: Exactly that, on both producers — but the WebUI producer applies it only on the `[getProduct] >= 3` branch; below it the tar carries no exclusions at all
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/backup.tcl:8 `proc create_backup {}`; :15 `if {[getProduct] < 3 } {`; :16 `catch { exec tar czf /tmp/usr_local.tar.gz usr/local }` (no exclusions); :18 `catch { exec tar --owner=root --group=root --exclude=usr/local/tmp --exclude=/usr/local/.firmwareUpdate --exclude=usr/local/lost+found --exclude=usr/local/eQ-3-Backup --exclude-tag=.nobackup --one-file-system --ignore-failed-read -czf /tmp/usr_local.tar.gz usr/local }`. Reached from ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_security.cgi:1506 `proc action_create_backup {}` → `[create_backup]` (the `action=create_backup` link is built at :1008) and from ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_maintenance.cgi:1286. Identical copies under ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/. · ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base-openccu/bin/createBackup.sh:67 `/bin/tar -C / --owner=root --group=root --exclude=usr/local/tmp --exclude="usr/local/.*" --exclude=usr/local/lost+found --exclude="${BACKUPDIR}" --exclude=usr/local/eQ-3-Backup --exclude-tag=.nobackup --one-file-system --ignore-failed-read --warning=no-file-changed -czf "${TMPDIR}/usr_local.tar.gz" usr/local 2>/dev/null`. · /bin/tar is GNU tar, not busybox: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/Buildroot.config:72 `BR2_PACKAGE_TAR=y`. · Corroborating uses of the same tag by the distribution itself: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base-openccu/bin/cronBackup.sh:72-75 and ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/init.d/S62HMServer:74-75 both `touch` a `.nobackup` in their own storage directory. · No patch under ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/ changes the exclude list: 0007-WebUI-Enhanced-FirmwareUpdate.patch:61 carries the same line as context.
all.finding:
Every load-bearing detail of the comment checks out against Tier 1: the tag file is named `.nobackup`, both named producers exist and are the ones the operator actually reaches, both use `--exclude-tag=` and not `--exclude-tag-all=` or `--exclude-tag-under=`, and both tar `usr/local`. The dangerous direction the reader flagged — that `--exclude-tag-all` would silently drop the daemon's SQLite database and at-rest key from the CCU backup — does not arise.

The comment's claim about surviving sibling state is also right, though for a reason worth stating precisely: `--exclude-tag` drops the *contents of the directory that holds the tag*, so the tag has to sit one level below the state that must survive. It does — cmd/openccu-loom/audit_wiring.go:59-63 puts the tag in `<DataDir>/<ccuBackupsDirName>` (or cfg.Backup.Dir), a child of the data directory, while the database and key live in the data directory itself. Move the archive store to be the data directory and the comment's guarantee inverts.

Where the rule narrows: the WebUI producer is version-gated. `backup.tcl:15` takes an unfiltered `tar czf … usr/local` when `[getProduct] < 3`, so on those products the tag is inert and a WebUI backup does contain every downloaded .sbk. `createBackup.sh` has no such branch. `getProduct` is not defined anywhere in the checked-out sources (it comes from a Tcl extension outside this tree), so I can state the branch but not the numeric product mapping — I have deliberately not guessed it. The narrowing does not touch the two claims the comment makes about flag and tag name, both of which are unconditional where the flag is used at all.

One semantics caveat to keep labelled: that `--exclude-tag` keeps the directory (and the tag file) while dropping the rest of its contents is GNU tar's documented behaviour, not something the CCU source states. The firmware citation settles the tag name and the flag choice; the flag's meaning rests on GNU tar, which BR2_PACKAGE_TAR confirms is the binary in play.
all.negativeControl: Had the tag name or the flag been wrong, the grep for `exclude-tag` and `nobackup` across both trees would have returned a different tag name, a different flag spelling (`--exclude-tag-all` / `--exclude-tag-under`), or no hit in a backup producer at all. It returned `--exclude-tag=.nobackup` in exactly the two places the comment names, and nowhere else in a tar invocation — and the same sweep did surface a real discrepancy the comment omits (the `getProduct < 3` unfiltered branch), so the check demonstrably reports differences when they exist rather than confirming what it was asked to confirm.
all.challengeNote:
The tag name and the flag are upheld. The first pass's headline narrowing is not — it answers a file the target distribution does not ship, which is exactly the recurring failure this series exists to catch.

There are two different files named backup.tcl. The 38-line one in OpenCCU-Base tars inline and gates the exclusions on `[getProduct] >= 3`. The one the OpenCCU firmware actually ships is 56 lines, delegates to /bin/createBackup.sh, and contains no tar at all — established from occu.mk (the image pulls OpenCCU/occu 3.89.8-2 and patches it) together with patch 0118's unchanged context, which shows the delegating shape in the file being patched. So on OpenCCU: one tar producer, one exclude list, `--exclude-tag=.nobackup` unconditional, and a WebUI backup honours the tag by delegation rather than by having its own tar. The `getProduct` branch, and with it the "below product 3 the tag is inert" caveat, is a property of the OpenCCU-Base WebUI source — relevant to an eQ-3-firmware CCU, not to the distribution this daemon is packaged for.

Net effect on our comment: its conclusion survives on both firmwares (a WebUI-triggered backup does honour the tag), but its stated mechanism — "both producers tar /usr/local" — is false for OpenCCU and only conditionally true for the base source. The fix is to cite createBackup.sh as the single producer and say the WebUI reaches it, rather than naming two tars.

The placement guarantee holds and is worth restating precisely: `--exclude-tag` drops the contents of the directory holding the tag, so the tag must sit one level below the state that must survive. It does — the tag goes into the backup storage directory, a child of the data directory. That guarantee inverts the moment an operator sets `backup.dir` to the data directory itself, which the config permits; the database and the at-rest key would then be inside the tagged directory and would vanish from every CCU backup, silently.

One claim I demote outright rather than narrow: "/bin/tar is GNU tar, not busybox: BR2_PACKAGE_TAR=y". That setting proves GNU tar is built into the image; it does not prove which binary answers to the path /bin/tar. Busybox's own tar applet is enabled (../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/Busybox.config:181 CONFIG_TAR=y, :182 CONFIG_FEATURE_TAR_LONG_OPTIONS=y) and busybox tar has no --exclude-tag; the config sets no BR2_ROOTFS_MERGED_USR and no post-build script in the tree resolves the collision, and buildroot's own package logic is not vendored here. The strongest honest statement is circumstantial: the CCU's only backup producer passes GNU-only flags to /bin/tar and backups work, so /bin/tar must be GNU tar — inference, not measurement.

all.title: Write-only data points are excluded from the self-reload on the strength of an uncited error code (-5, "Unknown Parameter")
all.ourValue: getValue on a parameter without the Read operations bit "returns `Unknown Parameter` (code -5)"
all.firmwareValue: Interface-dependent. BidCos-RF: fault -1, message "Parameter is not readable". BidCos-Wired: no readability check at all — no fault. HmIP: fault -5, message "Unknown Parameter …for value key: <name>". On BidCos-RF, -5 "Unknown parameter" means the name is absent from the VALUES paramset, which is a different condition.
all.citation: BidCos-RF, the whole path: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:285-296 (XmlRpcMethodGetValue → RFManager::GetValue) → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:152-162 (`return inst->ReadValue(name,mode, val);`) → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:132-152. In ReadValue: :136-138 `throw XmlRpcException("Unknown paramset", -3);` if VALUES is missing; :140-142 `if (!param) { throw XmlRpcException("Unknown parameter", -5); }`; :144-147 `if(!param->IsReadable()) { throw XmlRpcException("Parameter is not readable", -1); }`. IsReadable is `(operations & OP_READ)!=0` with OP_READ=1, OP_WRITE=2, OP_EVENT=4 — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:55-57, :85. That a write-only parameter *is* present in VALUES (so it reaches the readability check, not the -5 branch) is Tier 2: e.g. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_rc.xml:146 declares `<parameter id="PRESS_SHORT" operations="write,event" …>` inside the channel's VALUES paramset; rf_pb-2-wm55_le_v1_3.xml:120, rf_pbi.xml:121 and rf_ou_led16_le_v1_0.xml:163 are identical. · BidCos-Wired: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:217-226 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:202-208 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Channel.cpp:80-88, which has no IsReadable check and simply `return param->GetValue(this, val);`; an unknown name returns false, which the method turns into `XmlRpcException("Failure")` — default code -1 per ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcException.h:27 (`XmlRpcException(const std::string& message, int code=-1)`). · HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#getValue throws NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException when the channel holds no IParameterValue for the key; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException sets faultCode = -5 with message "Unknown Parameter for value key: <key>" (or "Unknown Parameter value for value key: <key>" when a StateParameter exists but no value is stored).
all.finding:
The branch's *predicate* is exactly right and better grounded than the comment claims: rfd's own readability gate is `(operations & OP_READ) != 0`, the identical test our code performs, with the identical bit weights (READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4 — and HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations uses the same three values). Skipping the reload for a non-READ parameter is what the firmware would force anyway.

The cited *fault* is wrong for the interface where the named examples actually live. PRESS_SHORT and friends are BidCos-RF remote parameters, declared `operations="write,event"` inside VALUES — so they pass rfd's name lookup and fail the readability check one line later, producing fault **-1 "Parameter is not readable"**, not -5. On rfd, -5 "Unknown parameter" is reserved for a name that is not in the VALUES paramset at all, which is a different situation with a different remedy. BidCos-Wired is a third answer: hs485d omits the readability check entirely, so getValue on a write-only wired parameter faults only if the name is unknown, and then with the generic "Failure"/-1. Only the HmIP surface produces the -5 "Unknown Parameter …" the comment quotes, and it does so on a different condition (no stored value / no StateParameter), not on the READ bit.

Boundary, stated plainly: the claim is true on HmIP-RF/HmIP-Wired, false on BidCos-RF (-1, different message), false on BidCos-Wired (usually no fault at all). Consequence for the branch: it stays correct in effect on all three — a fault is a fault, whatever its code, and on wired the reload would return a stale-or-absent value that is worthless anyway. Nothing needs changing but the comment, which should either cite ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:144 for the BidCos case or drop the fault code and cite the Operations gate itself, since that is the invariant it actually relies on. CUxD/BIN-RPC is not in these trees and stays unverified.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, RFChannel::ReadValue would have reached the -5 throw for a non-readable parameter — i.e. either write-only parameters would be absent from the VALUES paramset (making `!param` true), or the IsReadable branch would carry code -5. Neither holds: the rftypes XMLs declare PRESS_SHORT inside VALUES with operations="write,event", and the readability branch three lines below the -5 branch carries -1 with a distinct message. The check also produced a *different* answer on the HmIP path, where -5 is genuinely what comes back — so it is not returning "-1" indiscriminately.

all.title: The BIN-RPC type tags and message types carry no source at all
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:55-62 (STREAM_TAG_INTEGER=0x001, BOOLEAN=0x002, STRING=0x003, DOUBLE=0x004, DATETIME=0x005, BINARY=0x006, ARRAY=0x100, STRUCT=0x101); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:35 (BINARY_SIGNATURE[]="Bin"), :96-100 (header = sig + 1 type byte + ntohl u32 length, body at sig+5), :356-362 (response appends type byte 1), :405-411 (fault appends type byte 0xff); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:334-361 (request appends type byte 0), :475-479 (client reads the type byte, 0xff = fault)
all.firmwareValue: marker 'Bin'; msgType request=0, response=1, fault=0xff; tags 0x001 int / 0x002 bool / 0x003 string / 0x004 double / 0x005 datetime / 0x006 binary / 0x100 array / 0x101 struct; big-endian throughout
all.ourValue: marker {'B','i','n'}; msgTypeRequest=0x00, msgTypeResponse=0x01, msgTypeFault=0xFF; typeInt=0x01, typeBool=0x02, typeString=0x03, typeDouble=0x04, typeArray=0x100, typeStruct=0x101
all.finding: Every constant in wire.go matches the CCU's own BIN-RPC codec exactly, and so do the payload shapes our encoder writes: int is a 4-byte big-endian word (XmlRpcValue.cpp:539-547), bool is a single 0/1 byte (:461-468), string is a u32 length followed by the raw bytes with no terminator (:709-719), double is mantissa then exponent as two big-endian int32 (:605-616, matching our value = mantissa * 2^exp / 2^30). The request framing our WriteRequest builds is the firmware's, verbatim: 8-byte header, then a length-only method name with no type tag, then a u32 parameter count, then each parameter as a self-tagged value — note the top-level parameter list carries no 0x100 array tag, which is what our writeParamArray also does (XmlRpcClient.cpp:335-352, and the server's matching parseRequest at XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:259-266 reads stringFromStream then arrayFromStream). Two narrowings worth recording rather than fixing blind: the firmware codec also accepts DATETIME (0x005) and BINARY (0x006), which our readValue rejects with "unknown value type tag", and the firmware's client treats any header byte other than 0xff as a non-fault rather than requiring exactly 0x01. Neither is wrong for the CUxD path we drive, but wire.go states the tag set as if it were complete, and it is a strict subset. CUxD itself is a closed add-on present in neither reference tree, so this grounds the framing our client speaks, not CUxD-specific behaviour.
all.negativeControl: Had a tag been wrong, the firmware's constant block would have shown a different number against the same name — the check reads eight named constants and compares each to ours, so a single mismatched value (e.g. bool at 0x03) would have surfaced as a named disagreement rather than the eight-for-eight agreement observed. The bundle correctly notes the existing round-trip test cannot produce that result, since it encodes and decodes with the same constants; reading the firmware's own definitions is the only check that can.
all.challengeNote: I re-read every cited line. All eight constants, the 8-byte header, the request framing (tagless method name, u32 parameter count, no top-level 0x100 array tag) and all four payload shapes are exactly as claimed; the double formula matches in both directions (firmware frexp + int() truncation vs our math.Trunc; firmware ldexp(mant/2^30, exp) vs our 2^exp*mant/2^30). I demote from confirmed to narrowed for three reasons the grounding either understated or missed. (1) The tag set in wire.go is a strict subset — DATETIME 0x005 and BINARY 0x006 are refused by readValue with "unknown value type tag"; the grounding names this but still reports the rule confirmed. (2) Missed: our ReadRequest rejects any header type byte other than 0x00, while XmlRpcServerConnection never inspects that byte on the read path at all — it branches on the "Bin" signature alone (:96-101) — so our server is strictly stricter than the CCU's, in the same way our client is stricter than XmlRpcClient's 0xff-or-not fault test. (3) Scope: our BIN-RPC peer is CUxD, a closed add-on present in neither reference tree. What is grounded is that our codec matches the CCU's own BIN-RPC codec, which is strong evidence for the protocol family and no evidence at all about CUxD-specific behaviour. Separately verified as a scope note: rfd and hs485d never construct a TypeDateTime or TypeBase64 value (0 hits), so the two unsupported tags are a codec capability, not something the CCU emits.

all.title: HSColor's 0..1 wire range and x100 exposure are asserted in a comment, not read from the SATURATION descriptor
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createLevel and #createHue (SATURATION registered via createLevel, HUE via createHue in #initializeStateParameterList); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.StateParameter (constructor argument order: name, logicalType, physicalType, ioOperations, typeConverter, defaultValue, minValue, maxValue, ...); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.AbstractParameterFactory#PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_MIN / #PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_MAX / #PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_OLD_VALUE / #PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_DON_T_CARE; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (publishes MIN/MAX verbatim from the parameter). Tier 2 corroboration of scope: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml and hs485types/*.xml declare neither HUE nor SATURATION on any device (0 files each), so both parameters are HmIP-only.
all.firmwareValue: SATURATION: LogicalType.FLOAT, DEFAULT 0.0, MIN 0.0, MAX 1.01 (physical conversion DoubleToInteger(200.0, 0.0)). HUE: LogicalType.INTEGER, DEFAULT 0, MIN 0, MAX 361, with 0..359 the real hue range, 360 = OLD_VALUE and 361 = DON'T_CARE.
all.ourValue: SATURATION clamped to [0.0, 1.0] on read (hscolor.go:205-211) and written as sat/100.0 from a [0,100] input (hscolor.go:241). HUE folded ((v%360)+360)%360 on both read (hscolor.go:255) and write (hscolor.go:234).
all.finding: Both halves of the comment are off, and the HUE half mis-decodes real device values. SATURATION's declared MAX is 1.01, not 1.0 — a one-ulp-class difference in exactly the sense the brief asks about, so our read clamp truncates the top of the declared range. HUE's declared MAX is 361, and the two values above 359 are named constants, not slack: 360 is OLD_VALUE and 361 is DON'T_CARE. Our modulo maps them to hue 0 and hue 1, so a light reporting "don't care" (the value the config-side POWERUP_ON_HUE and SHORT_ON_HUE parameters use to mean "leave hue alone") is published as a real red hue with nothing anywhere indicating a sentinel was swallowed. The write path is unaffected in practice: we send hue in [0,359] and saturation in [0,1], both inside the declared bounds, so no out-of-range value reaches a device. The bundle's worry about a device declaring SATURATION as 0..100 or 0..255 does not arise — the corpus is uniform because these parameters exist only on the HmIP side and are built from one factory method. The structural criticism stands regardless: Subscribe already holds the DP at hscolor.go:127 and never reads Descriptor.Min/Max, so the code cannot notice any of this. The right fix is to consult the descriptor and treat HUE values above the declared real maximum as sentinels rather than folding them.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, createHue would have carried maxValue 359 and createLevel maxValue 1.0, and AbstractParameterFactory would not have named 360 and 361 at all. The check reads the declared MIN/MAX triple straight out of the factory call and compares it to our clamp bounds, so agreement and disagreement produce visibly different results; here it produced 1.01 vs 1.0 and 361 vs 359, plus two named sentinel constants our code has no branch for.
all.challengeNote: Half of this grounding holds and half is a wrong-surface transfer. Upheld: the declared ranges contradict our comment. createLevel gives SATURATION maxValue 1.01, not 1.0, and createHue gives HUE maxValue 361, not 359; both are published verbatim over the legacy XML-RPC surface (addDesriptionOfParameter copies min/max off the parameter, and fillLegacyParameter can only set TabOrder/Unit/Control, so nothing downstream rewrites them). The structural criticism is also upheld: hscolor.go contains no reference to Descriptor at all. Demoted: the claim that 360/361 are live sentinels on the state HUE, so that our modulo publishes a "don't care" as a red hue, is not grounded. PARAMETER_VALUE_HUE_OLD_VALUE and _DON_T_CARE are declared and then used nowhere in HMIPServer or HMServer; the 361 default appears only on POWERUP_ON_HUE (MASTER) and SHORT_ON_HUE / LONG_ON_HUE (LINK), built by a different factory method, while the state HUE's declared default is 0. Reading the config-paramset sentinel meaning onto the VALUES parameter because both stop at 361 is exactly the convention this audit exists to catch, and it is the half a reader would later cite as a device fact. Two smaller corrections: the grounding's line numbers are wrong (read fold is :189 not :255, write fold :230 not :234, Subscribe :124 not :127), and Tier 2 is silent in both directions — no HUE or SATURATION appears in the shipped device XMLs or in the pydevccu descriptor corpus, so nothing outside the HmIP server says what a real device declares.

all.title: A STRING parameter's descriptor MAX is read as a character-length cap, and an over-length write is only logged
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalTypeString.cpp:57-66 (GetDescription sets TYPE="STRING", MIN="", MAX=""), :51-54 (EnforceConstraints checks only that the value is a string); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:205-218 (GetDescription merges the logical type's fields into the published parameter description). HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.GeneralConfigurationParameterFactory, .TileConfigurationParameterFactory, .MaintenanceConfigurationParameterFactory and .stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory (STRING parameters constructed with maxValue "[0x20-0x7E]{16}", "[U+00-U+FF]{16}", "[0-9]{8}", "[0x00-0x7E]{127}", "2255_12_31 23:55", "255.255.255" or ""); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.typeconversion.converter.AsciiStringToInteger#convertLogicalToPhysical; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter
all.firmwareValue: BidCos/wired: MAX is the empty string for every STRING parameter, and no length is enforced. HmIP: MAX is a character-class regex (e.g. "[0x20-0x7E]{16}") or a maximum lexical value (e.g. "2255_12_31 23:55", "255.255.255"), never a number. The actual length lives in the converter constructor (AsciiStringToInteger(16), UnicodeStringToInteger(16), AsciiStringToInteger(127)) and is not published in the paramset description. An over-long value is silently truncated to the converter's fixed byte length in ISO-8859-1, with no error.
all.ourValue: textMaxLen(t.Descriptor.Max) is treated as a character count; when len(v) exceeds it the daemon logs a warning and writes anyway.
all.finding: MAX on a STRING parameter is not a length on either transport. On BidCos the CCU publishes MAX as the empty string and its only constraint check is that the value is a string at all. On HmIP the same field carries either a character-class regex whose {n} suffix happens to contain the length, or a maximum lexical value for date- and version-shaped strings; DeviceUtil publishes it verbatim, so that is exactly what arrives on the wire. Neither form is an integer. Traced through textMaxLen, every real descriptor value returns 0: "" yields 0, "[0x20-0x7E]{16}" stops on '[', "2255_12_31 23:55" stops on '_', "255.255.255" stops on '.'. So the guard is inert in production — it neither fires falsely nor ever fires, and the comment describes a check that cannot run. The bundle's byte-vs-character concern is real in principle (len(v) counts UTF-8 bytes while the firmware converter counts ISO-8859-1 bytes, so an umlaut costs 2 against a budget measured in 1) but moot while maxLen is always 0. On the second half of the question: the CCU does not refuse an over-long value, it truncates it into the fixed-size byte array, so nothing surfaces as an error either way. Deriving a real cap is not possible from the descriptor — it would need the converter's length argument, which the paramset description never exposes.
all.negativeControl: Had MAX been a length cap, HSSLogicalTypeString::GetDescription would have written a number rather than the empty string, and the HmIP factories would have passed an integer maxValue for STRING parameters instead of a regex or a date literal. The check reads the published MAX for both transports and inspects its type, so a numeric MAX would have been directly visible; what appeared instead was "" on one side and character-class regexes on the other.
all.challengeNote: Upheld, and I widened the enumeration rather than sampling it. On BidCos the STRING logical type writes MAX="" unconditionally and its constraint check is a type test — no length is enforced or published. I additionally checked the shipped device corpus: zero rftypes and zero hs485types XMLs declare a logical_type_string at all, so the BidCos STRING path has no device behind it in the firmware's own device set. On HmIP I enumerated every LogicalType.STRING construction site plus every DISPLAY_DATA_STRING regex actually passed in; each maxValue is "", a regex beginning '[' or '(', or a lexical bound ("2255_12_31 23:55", "255.255.255", "0.0.0"). Tracing each through textMaxLen: the empty string yields 0 (empty loop), every regex yields 0 on its first non-digit, "2255_12_31 23:55" yields 0 at '_', "255.255.255" yields 0 at '.'. So the guard is inert for every descriptor value I can enumerate — it neither fires falsely nor ever fires, and the comment describes a check that cannot run. The truncation half is also upheld verbatim: AsciiStringToInteger allocates a fixed-size array and copies min(length, input) bytes in ISO-8859-1, so the CCU neither rejects nor reports an over-long write. Two boundaries the grounding did not name. (a) HSSDescription::Describe lets a device XML override any published field, MAX included, after the logical type has written "" — no shipped XML does so (0 hits), but "MAX is never numeric" is therefore a property of the shipped corpus, not a firmware invariant. (b) Our Text data point is built from whatever descriptor an interface returns, and CUxD's descriptors are in no reference tree; a CUxD STRING with a numeric MAX would wake the guard, and nothing here says what it would then do. Tier 2 is silent throughout: the pydevccu corpus contains no STRING parameter at all (0 of them), and openccu-data ships translations and semantics, not paramset descriptions.

all.title: The OPERATIONS DETERMINE bit and the FLAGS projection are restated in DTO comments, away from their definition and without a firmware citation
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:54-58 (OP_NONE=0, OP_READ=1, OP_WRITE=2, OP_EVENT=4, OP_DETERMINE=8 — "Werte fuer das Feld OPERATIONS in der Parameterbeschreibung an der XmlRpc-Schnittstelle"), :64-69 (FLG_NONE=0, FLG_VISIBLE=(1<<0), FLG_INTERNAL=(1<<1), FLG_TRANSFORM=(1<<2), FLG_SERVICE=(1<<3), FLG_STICKY=(1<<4)), :91 (IsDeterminable = operations & OP_DETERMINE); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:209-210 ((*val)["OPERATIONS"]=operations; (*val)["FLAGS"]=flags); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFParamset.cpp:251-265 (Determine refuses unless IsDeterminable, then calls DetermineValue on the device); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:258-265 (XML-RPC method "determineParameter"); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/tools/devconfig.cgi:902-903 (renders the "Determine" link exactly when $operations & 8), :950-956 (that link calls determineParameter). HmIP corroboration of the STICKY bit: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter stamps UNREACH with FLAGS 25 = 1|8|16 = VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY. Tier-3 witness for provenance only: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:1243 "STICKY = 10  # This might be wrong. Documentation says 0x10 # not used".
all.firmwareValue: OPERATIONS: READ=1, WRITE=2, EVENT=4, DETERMINE=8. FLAGS: VISIBLE=1, INTERNAL=2, TRANSFORM=4, SERVICE=8, STICKY=16 (1<<4).
all.ourValue: OPERATIONS identical (pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:77-80). FLAGS: FlagVisible=1, FlagInternal=2, FlagTransform=4, FlagService=8 identical — but FlagSticky=10 (pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:113), where the firmware says 16.
all.finding: The two claims the bundle names are both right, and a neighbouring constant in the same definition block is wrong. DETERMINE is 0x08, and its meaning is exactly what the DTO comment says: RFParamset::Determine refuses the request unless IsDeterminable and then reads the value off the device, reachable over XML-RPC as determineParameter. The surface matches too — the CCU's own device-configuration tool renders a "Determine" link on precisely the condition $operations & 8, on any paramset, so our MASTER-editor button is on the same path the firmware is on and not a different surface wearing the same name. VISIBLE/INTERNAL/SERVICE are 1/2/8, so the three-field projection in UISchemaParameterFlags is faithful as far as it goes; the comment "mirrors the OCCU FLAGS bitmask" overstates it, since TRANSFORM (4) and STICKY (16) are dropped and unnamed, leaving a client unable to distinguish "flag absent" from "flag not projected". The contradiction is FlagSticky = 10 against the firmware's (1<<4) = 16. Because Has() requires every bit of the mask, the constant is wrong in both directions: a parameter genuinely carrying FLAGS 16 reports IsSticky() false, and a parameter carrying FLAGS 10 (INTERNAL|SERVICE) reports IsSticky() true. The in-repo comment asserts the opposite of what I found — it calls 0x10 "a known eQ-3 documentation bug" and keeps 10 "for wire parity" — but 0x10 is what eQ-3's own source says, not merely its documentation, and the HmIP server independently emits 25 for UNREACH, which only decomposes as VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY if STICKY is 16. The value traces to aiohomematic, a Tier-3 witness that flags its own uncertainty in the same line. Nothing in production reads FlagSticky or IsSticky today (only bitmask_test.go), so this is latent rather than live — but the test TestFlagStickyKeepsAiohomematicEncoding currently pins the wrong value in place.
all.negativeControl: Had our values been right, HSSParameter.h would have shown OP_DETERMINE at some value other than 8 (making the DETERMINE claim fail) and FLG_STICKY at 10 rather than (1<<4). The check reads all nine named constants and compares each: eight agreed and one did not, which is the differential result the control asks for. The independent HmIP confirmation is a second, structurally different check on the same bit — FLAGS 25 for UNREACH decomposes uniquely as 1|8|16 and is impossible if STICKY were 10.
all.challengeNote: Upheld on every point, and I closed the one hole that could have sunk it. DETERMINE is 0x08 and means what the DTO comment says: RFParamset::Determine refuses with fault -6 unless the parameter carries the bit, then reads the value off the device, reachable as determineParameter. The surface matches ours — devconfig.cgi renders its "Determine" link on precisely $operations & 8, on any paramset, and that link invokes determineParameter, so our MASTER-editor button sits on the firmware's own path rather than a different surface wearing the same name. Because that is WebUI behaviour, I checked the distribution patch layer the firmware map warns about: patch 0037-WebUI-DevConfig touches devconfig.cgi but no line mentioning operations or Determine, so the condition survives into the shipped image. VISIBLE/INTERNAL/SERVICE are 1/2/8, so the three-field projection is faithful as far as it goes, while "mirrors the OCCU FLAGS bitmask" overstates it — TRANSFORM (4) and STICKY (16) are dropped unnamed, leaving a client unable to tell "flag absent" from "flag not projected". The contradiction stands: FLG_STICKY is (1<<4) in eQ-3's own header, not 10, so our in-repo comment asserts the opposite of the source — 0x10 is what the firmware's code says, not merely its documentation. Because Has() requires every bit of the mask, FlagSticky=10 is wrong in both directions: a parameter carrying FLAGS 16 reports IsSticky() false, and one carrying FLAGS 10 (INTERNAL|SERVICE) reports it true. The HmIP side corroborates independently: UNREACH is stamped FLAGS 25, whose only decomposition is 1|8|16 = VISIBLE|SERVICE|STICKY, and STICKY's firmware comment ("a service message that does not reset itself when its cause goes away") is exactly UNREACH's behaviour. Correction to the grounding's blast radius: FlagSticky and IsSticky are read in two test files, not one — pkg/hmenum/bitmask_test.go and tests/contract/hmenum_constants_test.go:48 — and in no production file, so the defect is latent, with TestFlagStickyKeepsAiohomematicEncoding pinning the wrong value in place.

all.title: The HmIP indoor/outdoor siren split and the smoke-sounder alarm class are named as device facts with no cited source
all.citation: Outdoor: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.deviceDescription.js:191 ("HmIP-ASIR-O": "Homematic IP Alarm Siren - outdoor") — a product-name catalogue entry; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:24 ("stringTableAlarmAllSensArmed": "Outdoor sensors armed, (presence mode)") and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/ARMING/localization/en/SHUTTER_CONTACT.txt:7 ("armOutdoorSensors") — both about sensors, not sirens; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/easymodes/etc/hmipAlarmPanel.tcl:26-45 (the CCU's HmIP alarm configuration is ALARM_MODE_ZONE_1..7 plus ALARM_MODE_TYPE, numbered zones with no indoor/outdoor and no output classes); HMIPServer de.eq3.* carries no "outdoor" token anywhere. Smoke sounder: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createSmokeDetectorCommandParameter (SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND: LogicalType.ENUM, IOOperations.WRITE); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.SmokeDetectorCommand (RESERVED_ALARM_OFF, INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF, INTRUSION_ALARM, SMOKE_TEST, COMMUNICATION_TEST, COMMUNICATION_TEST_REPEATED); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.SmokeDetectorAlarmStatus (IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#setParamset (rewrites SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND to SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND_GROUP when the device is a new smoke detector and its groups are configured); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/config/stringtable_de.txt:1886-1887 (INTRUSION_ALARM / INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF are operator-visible commands)
all.firmwareValue: Outdoor: no channel attribute, no paramset field, no group role — the words appear only as product-description text in the WebUI name catalogue (HmIP-ASIR vs HmIP-ASIR-O) and, separately and about sensors rather than sirens, in the BidCos ARMING easymode. The CCU's own HmIP alarm panel models numbered zones ALARM_MODE_ZONE_1..7 only. Smoke sounder: SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND is a real write-only ENUM whose value list includes INTRUSION_ALARM and INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF; the CCU applies no protection-level restriction to it.
all.ourValue: ExcludeOutdoor documented as "the HmIP indoor/outdoor split"; SmokeSounders documented as "HmIP 'Rauchwarnmelder-Alarm' parity — typically full protection only".
all.finding: Three claims, three different answers. (a) The smoke-detector sounder is a real driveable output: SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND is declared write-only with INTRUSION_ALARM and INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF in its value list, both surfaced to the CCU operator, and our SmokeSiren drives exactly that parameter. Enrolling the class does something. Confirmed. (b) The indoor/outdoor distinction is not something the CCU models. It is a product-line distinction visible only in the WebUI's device-name catalogue — HmIP-ASIR-O is named "outdoor" the way HmIP-STHO is; there is no device or channel attribute, no paramset field and no group role carrying it, and the HmIP server contains no "outdoor" token at all. That is where the boundary runs: true as a fact about product names, false as a fact the daemon could read off a device. Our Outdoor flag is an operator-set field in our own alarm_outputs config, which is the correct design given the firmware; the parenthetical attributing it to HmIP is what is wrong, and it is the kind of comment that later gets cited as a device fact. (c) "typically full protection only" has no counterpart in the CCU: its HmIP alarm configuration is seven numbered zones plus an unreachability policy, with no notion of output classes or of protection levels restricting which sounders enrol. That sub-claim is Tier-1 silent — it describes Homematic IP app convention, not CCU behaviour, and our rule rests on the alarm-concept note alone. One adjacent observation, not part of the candidate but worth recording: our SmokeAlarmStatus constants are declared in the order IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM while the firmware enum orders them IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM. This is harmless only because we resolve the ENUM by label through custom.EnumLabelValue rather than by index; anything that starts treating that Go const block as ordinal would be wrong from the third entry on.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU modelled an indoor/outdoor siren split, it would have appeared as a parameter, a device-attribute or a group role — the check searched the rftypes and hs485types descriptors, the HmIP state and configuration parameter factories, the group definitions and the WebUI's alarm configuration, any of which would have produced a named field. What it produced instead was two unrelated uses of the word (a product name and a sensor-arming label), which is a visibly different result from the one a real split would have given. The smoke-sounder half is symmetric: had the class not corresponded to a driveable output, SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND would have been absent or read-only, and it is neither — it is IOOperations.WRITE with an intrusion command in its value list.
all.challengeNote: The three-way split is upheld, and I strengthened the middle claim rather than resting on the grounding's sample. (a) Confirmed: SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND is declared write-only with INTRUSION_ALARM and INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF in its value list, and our SmokeSiren writes exactly those two labels (internal/model/custom/siren/smoke.go:206 and :218), so enrolling the class drives a real device output. (b) Narrowed as stated: I swept both HmIP server components for the token "outdoor" and found zero occurrences, and swept the CCU sources outside the language catalogues, where it survives only inside product names (the BidCos HM-Sen-MDIR-O in the device replace map) and in an ARMING easymode string about sensors. So indoor/outdoor is a product-line fact, never a device or channel attribute the daemon could read. Our own design is right — Outdoor is an operator-set field in alarm_outputs — and it is only the parenthetical attributing it to HmIP that is wrong, which is precisely the comment that would later be cited as a device fact. (c) Tier-1 silent as stated: the CCU's HmIP alarm panel is numbered zones plus ALARM_MODE_TYPE, with no output classes and no protection-level gating, so "typically full protection only" describes app convention and rests on our alarm-concept note alone. Two corrections to the adjacent observations. First, the ordering claim needs its file: it is true of internal/model/custom/siren/smoke.go:24-29, whose block runs IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM against the firmware's IDLE_OFF, PRIMARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM; the other block, pkg/hmenum/smoke_alarm_status.go:22-32, is in firmware order and its "in VALUE_LIST order" comment is accurate. Second, a finding neither the grounding nor the guards caught: the fixture at tests/contract/wire_snapshots/reference_compare_test.go:548 declares SMOKE_DETECTOR_ALARM_STATUS's VALUE_LIST as IDLE_OFF, IDLE_ON, PRIMARY_ALARM, SECONDARY_ALARM, INTRUSION_ALARM — five labels in a non-firmware order, including an IDLE_ON that appears nowhere in either server component and nowhere in aiohomematic either. It is inert only because resolution goes through custom.EnumLabelValue by label; as a fixture it misrepresents what the device declares.

all.title: The updateDevice hint and the weekday bitmask are bare literals with no source and no current consumer
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.h:47 — "//! Enum fuer den Parameter \c hint der XmlRpc-Methode updateDevice" / "enum{UPDATE_HINT_ALL=0, UPDATE_HINT_LINKS=1};"; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1620 (the only emitter of 0, inside RFDevice::Rebuild); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:655 — "If true, Device->Rebuild() calls XmlRpc method updateDevice instead of newDevices. Default is false."; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:219 (config key "Call UpdateDevice On OTAU Device Rebuild", default "false"); emitters of 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:756, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:868, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:480, ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:535. Weekday mask: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.AbstractParameterFactory#WP_WEEKDAY_SUNDAY..WP_WEEKDAY_SATURDAY (also in HMServer); parameter shape: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.CalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#createWeekdayParameter.
all.ourValue: UpdateDeviceHintFirmware = 0 ("0 means a firmware change"); UpdateDeviceHintLinks = 1. WeekdayInt: Sunday=1, Monday=2, Tuesday=4, Wednesday=8, Thursday=16, Friday=32, Saturday=64.
all.firmwareValue: hint enum: UPDATE_HINT_ALL = 0, UPDATE_HINT_LINKS = 1. WP_WEEKDAY bits: WP_WEEKDAY_SUNDAY=1, WP_WEEKDAY_MONDAY=2, WP_WEEKDAY_TUESDAY=4, WP_WEEKDAY_WEDNESDAY=8, WP_WEEKDAY_THURSDAY=16, WP_WEEKDAY_FRIDAY=32, WP_WEEKDAY_SATURDAY=64; parameter declared INTEGER, RW, min 0, max 127, 7 bits.
all.finding:
Two sub-claims, two different outcomes.

(b) WEEKDAY bitmask — CONFIRMED, exactly, all seven bits. The CCU's HmIP server declares the seven bit values as independently named constants (Sunday=1 through Saturday=64), so this is not an array-order inference: each day carries its own literal. Our pkg/hmenum/schedule.go WeekdayInt block matches value for value, and so does the production duplicate in internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:490-509 (which is the code that actually reaches a device). The parameter itself is declared INTEGER RW with MIN 0 / MAX 127 over 7 bits, consistent with all-days = 127.
  Tier-1 boundary worth recording: `WP_WEEKDAY` does not exist anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base (grep for "WP_WEEKDAY" over the whole tree returns nothing) — it is an HmIP-only parameter, so the BidCos C++ side is silent on it by construction and the HmIP server is the only Tier-1 witness.
  Side finding on the production site: the comment at internal/model/weekprofile/rawconvert.go:494-497 attributes the bit order to "`_getWeekDay` in `WebUI/www/config/easymodes/js/HmIPWeeklyProgram.js`". That file exists (3520 lines) but contains no `_getWeekDay`, no `_get*` function at all, and zero case-insensitive matches for weekday/wochentag/monday/montag. The cited authority is not there; the mapping is nonetheless correct, and its real Tier-1 source is the HmIP symbol cited above. Rewriting that comment to the real source is the fix.

(a) updateDevice hint — NARROWED, and this is why the overall verdict is narrowed. Value 1 is confirmed verbatim: the firmware's own name is UPDATE_HINT_LINKS and every emitter of 1 is a link add/remove (two in RFChannel, two in HS485Manager). Value 0 is numerically right but semantically mislabelled: the firmware calls it UPDATE_HINT_ALL, not "firmware". Our narrower reading happens to hold inside rfd today — the single emitter of 0 is RFDevice::Rebuild(), reached after an OTA firmware-version change — but it is false one step wider, in two ways. First, the declared contract is "all": Rebuild() swaps the device description, clears `channels` and calls CreateChannels() before reporting, and RFManager.h:655 states the call is made "instead of newDevices", so the reaction the CCU expects to hint 0 is a full device re-read, exactly as for newDevices — not a firmware-version refresh. A consumer wired against our label would under-refetch. Second, that emitter is behind a non-default option: `callUpdateDeviceOnOTAUDeviceRebuild` initialises to false (RFManager.cpp:48) and is only enabled by the rfd.conf key "Call UpdateDevice On OTAU Device Rebuild" = "true"; on a stock CCU, rfd sends newDevices instead and hint 0 is never seen from rfd at all. hs485d emits only UPDATE_HINT_LINKS. On the HmIP side the legacy XML-RPC surface declares updateDevice(interfaceId, address, hint) and forwards a hint received from BidCos, but no HmIP code path originates one with a literal value — HmIP is not a third source of hint semantics.
  Recommendation: keep both ordinals; rename the 0 constant to match the firmware ("All" / full-description-changed) and document that the correct reaction is a complete device re-read, plus the note that stock rfd sends newDevices on OTAU rebuild.

Damage scope, measured not assumed: `grep -rn "UpdateDeviceHint" --include=*.go` and the same for `WeekdayInt` return only the declarations in pkg/hmenum — no production or test reader of either. Both are latent today.
all.negativeControl: (a) Had our hint rule been wrong, HSSManager.h:47 would have read `enum{UPDATE_HINT_LINKS=0, UPDATE_HINT_ALL=1}` and the four link-mutation call sites (RFChannel.cpp:756/868, HS485Manager.cpp:480/535) would pass 0; they pass UPDATE_HINT_LINKS, and the sole 0-emitter sits in RFDevice::Rebuild. The check did in fact produce a different answer than expected for the *name* of 0 (ALL, not firmware) — it bit. (b) Had the weekday mask been the ISO order our code does not use, AbstractParameterFactory would have declared WP_WEEKDAY_MONDAY=1 and WP_WEEKDAY_SUNDAY=64; it declares the reverse. Because all seven constants are named individually and read individually, any permutation — not just a whole-week rotation — would have shown up as a mismatch; no bit position was inferred from list position anywhere in this check.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed, but on a corrected basis and with the prior report's impact assessment reversed.

(b) WEEKDAY bitmask — values confirmed, scope narrower than stated. All seven constants reproduce verbatim and each carries its own literal, so this is not an array-order inference and our WeekdayInt matches value for value. The production form at rawconvert.go:499-509 is bit-position rather than value form ({0,Sunday},{1,Monday},...) applied as mask&(1<<bit); that is arithmetically the same mapping, and it is the live one (read at :693, written at :793). I verified the surface independently instead of trusting it: fillBasicAstroParameter creates WP_WEEKDAY next to WP_FIXED_HOUR and WP_FIXED_MINUTE, and getParameterName formats "%02d_%s", together reproducing our file header's "01_WP_WEEKDAY"/"01_WP_FIXED_HOUR"/"01_WP_FIXED_MINUTE" key for key. MAX 127 over 7 bits independently confirms a seven-bit mask. Two boundaries the prior report did not draw. First, the constants are dead declarations — zero consumers in either server, and createWeekdayParameter passes a null converter — so "CONFIRMED exactly" overstates what is executed; the executed content is only the 7-bit 0..127 shape. Second, the rule is HmIP-simple-weekly-program only: I re-ran the silence check broadly rather than on the HmIP symbol name, and case-insensitive "weekday" across OpenCCU-Base, pydevccu and openccu-data yields no WP_WEEKDAY parameter at all, so Tier 2 is silent too and nothing here extends to any BidCos-RF weekly program. The prior side finding holds and is worse than reported: WebUI/www/config/easymodes/js/HmIPWeeklyProgram.js contains no _getWeekDay and no occurrence of the string WEEKDAY whatsoever, on either copy in the tree.

(a) updateDevice hint — narrowing upheld verbatim; ordinal 0 is right, the label is not. The firmware's own name is UPDATE_HINT_ALL, the gate and the default reproduce exactly, and hs485d emits only LINKS. But the prior report's closing claim that both constants are latent is wrong, and wrong in the specific way this project keeps catching: it measured damage by grepping the identifier UpdateDeviceHint. callback_handlers.go:658 consumes the hint semantics while re-declaring `const hintFirmware = 0` locally and documenting it as "a firmware-update notification (hint=0)" — a live, shipped instance of the same mislabel that no enum-name grep can see. Offsetting that, the predicted under-refetch is milder than claimed: the handler already invalidates the firmware cache and runs RefreshDeviceDescriptionsAndCreateMissingDevices. The real residual gap is that Rebuild clears `channels` and calls CreateChannels(), so hint 0 can carry a changed channel set, while the handler re-fetches descriptions and leaves the paramset registry merely invalidated.

all.title: MASTER OPERATIONS=0 is rewritten to READ|WRITE on a ported claim about CCU firmware behaviour
all.ourValue: OPERATIONS=0 on MASTER -> 3 (READ|WRITE)
all.firmwareValue: 3 (OP_READ|OP_WRITE) is the firmware's own default for a parameter that declares no operations attribute; the firmware never emits 0 in a paramset description
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:31 `operations=(OP_READ|OP_WRITE);` (constructor default) and :55-61 `temp=node.getAttribute("operations"); if(temp){ operations=OP_NONE; if(strstr(temp,"read"))operations|=OP_READ; ... }` — the attribute is the ONLY thing that can clear it. Bit values: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.h:53-59 `OP_NONE=0, OP_READ=1, OP_WRITE=2, OP_EVENT=4, OP_DETERMINE=8`. Sole emitter of the field: HSSParameter.cpp:209 `(*val)["OPERATIONS"]=operations;`. Visibility gate on the description: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParamset.cpp:207 `if(!param->IsVisible())continue;` with HSSParameter.h:93 `inline bool IsVisible(){return !hidden;}`. HmIP side: OPERATIONS is written verbatim from the parameter's IOOperations — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#addDesriptionOfParameter (`setOperations(parameter.getIoOperations().getValue())`); the class default is READ=1 and IOOperations#toString maps 0 to "undefined" — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.IOOperations. Tier 3 witness for where our rule came from: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/__init__.py:144-146 (comment "required to fix hm master paramset operation values", no source).
all.finding: The SUBSTITUTE VALUE IS EXACTLY RIGHT: 3 is the firmware's own default, not a guess — HSSParameter's constructor initialises operations to OP_READ|OP_WRITE, and only an explicit `operations=` attribute can lower it. But the PREMISE ("some CCU firmwares return OPERATIONS=0 for MASTER parameters") is not reproduced anywhere in Tier 1. Where the boundary runs: (a) in the shipped device XMLs, `operations="none"` (the only spelling that yields 0) occurs 28 times, ALL in LINK paramsets on wired devices (hmw_lc_dim1l_dr, hmw_lc_bl1_dr[_V3_02], hmw_lc_sw2_dr[_V3_02], hmw_io_4_fm[_V3_02]), ZERO in MASTER; (b) every one of those 28 also carries `hidden="true"`, and GetDefinition skips non-visible parameters — so getParamsetDescription cannot emit OPERATIONS=0 at all on BidCos-RF/Wired; (c) on HmIP no IOOperations is ever constructed with 0. What our rule actually fires on is a DESCRIPTOR that dropped the default: pydevccu records OPERATIONS=0 for e.g. HMW-LC-Bl1-DR MASTER INPUT_TYPE/INPUT_LOCKED/LONG_PRESS_TIME and HM-LC-Bl1-FM MASTER AES_ACTIVE — and each of those parameters carries NO operations attribute in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes (hs485types/hmw_lc_bl1_dr.xml:144,154; rftypes AES_ACTIVE declarations), i.e. a real CCU reports 3 for them (210 of 376 pydevccu device files carry MASTER OPERATIONS=0; MASTER histogram over that corpus: 0x2942, 1x495, 3x69214). So our code should follow Tier 1 (3), which it does; the rewrite is correct but is a corpus repair, not a firmware workaround, and it would be WRONG if a MASTER parameter ever genuinely declared `operations="none"`. Consequence side: rfd/hs485d does not fault a write to a non-writable parameter — HSSParamset::Put silently `continue`s (HSSParamset.cpp:190), and the HmIP legacy surface enforces nothing at all, so a wrongly-offered MASTER write is dropped, not rejected. Sibling claim at :1995 ("no MASTER parameter carries EVENT") is CONFIRMED at Tier 1: zero MASTER parameters in any of the 148 rftypes/hs485types XMLs declare an operations string containing `event`, and neither firmware default grants EVENT.
all.negativeControl: Had our value been wrong I would have found the constructor initialising `operations` to OP_READ (1) or OP_NONE, or a getParamsetDescription path that emits 0 for a visible MASTER parameter. The constructor reads OP_READ|OP_WRITE, and the 28 zero-valued parameters are all LINK and all filtered out by IsVisible() before the description is built — a different result in both directions.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD as narrowed, with two corrections and one scope gap the prior pass missed.

What I re-checked and confirm verbatim: the constructor default (HSSParameter.cpp:30), the attribute branch as the only path to a lower value (:55-61), the single emitter (:209), the bit values (HSSParameter.h:53-59), and the visibility gate in GetDefinition (HSSParamset.cpp:210). I additionally grepped all of src/rfd, src/hs485d and src/libhsscomm for any other assignment to `operations` and found exactly two — lines 30 and 57 of HSSParameter.cpp — so no rfd/hs485d code path can inject 0 outside the XML attribute. Same for HmIP: every `new IOOperations(...)` call site in the HMIPServer channelspecification factories passes RW, READ, or a local `ops` byte initialised from READ/WRITE/EVENT; none passes 0. The substitute value 3 is therefore the firmware's own default, not a convention.

CORRECTION 1 — the corpus scan was undercounted. The prior pass reported 28 occurrences of `operations="none"` in 4 device families. That number comes from a grep that silently skipped four latin-1-encoded XMLs as binary. Re-scanned in Python with explicit latin-1 decoding: 44 occurrences across 11 files (hmw_io_sr_fm, hmw_io_12_fm, hmw_io12_sw7_dr, hmw_io12_sw7_dr_V3_02 are the four that were dropped). The conclusion survives the correction and is strengthened: all 44 sit in a paramset with type="LINK" and all 44 carry hidden="true", so GetDefinition skips every one. Zero in MASTER, zero in rftypes. Had one of the four skipped files carried a non-hidden or MASTER instance the conclusion would have flipped, so this was a real hole, not a rounding error.

CORRECTION 2 — the file count. 142 device XMLs (124 rftypes + 18 hs485types), not 148.

SCOPE GAP the prior pass did not name. The rewrite lives in `hydrateParamset`, which is called for every channel of every interface through the generic `backends.Operations` — I read the call site: `hydrateChannel` invokes it once for VALUES and once for MASTER with no interface discrimination. Tier 1 covers rfd, hs485d and the HmIP legacy surface; it says nothing about CUxD (BIN-RPC, a third-party addon) or Homegear, both of which our pipeline runs this rewrite against. A CUxD MASTER descriptor that genuinely means "neither readable nor writable" would be rewritten to read+write and the parameter offered as writable in the UI and over MQTT. That half of the rule is not performable against Tier 1 and should be recorded as such rather than left implied.

TIER 2 vs TIER 1, restated sharply. I reproduced the pydevccu histogram exactly: over 399 paramset-description files, MASTER OPERATIONS is 3 in 69214 cases, 0 in 2942, 1 in 495, with 210 of 399 files carrying at least one 0. I then chased one of the recurring names: AES_ACTIVE is declared in the rftypes XMLs as `<parameter id="AES_ACTIVE" ui_flags="internal">` with no operations attribute, so a live rfd must emit 3 for it. The descriptor corpus and the firmware disagree, and Tier 1 wins: our code should keep writing 3. The rewrite is a repair of a lossy descriptor corpus, not a firmware workaround, and the comment should say so.

SIBLING CLAIM at :1995 ("No MASTER parameter carries EVENT in practice") — CONFIRMED at Tier 1 by a binary-safe scan: 2645 MASTER parameters across all 142 XMLs, zero declaring an operations string containing `event`; and neither firmware default grants EVENT (BidCos default 3, HmIP default 1).

all.title: The two XML-RPC write-formatting rules that reach every device write rest only on a comment claiming fault -5
all.ourValue: "<i4> is silently rejected with xml-rpc fault -5"; "<double>1</double> is rejected with fault -5, <double>1.0</double> is accepted"; both attributed to "the CCU firmware (eQ-3 ReGaHss)"
all.firmwareValue: <i4> and <int> are synonyms in all three CCU-side XML-RPC parsers; <double>1</double> parses fine (strtod / Double.parseDouble); fault -5 in rfd is "Unknown parameter", and the string "Invalid parameter or value" belongs to the HmIP legacy surface and is raised for an unknown parameter or an out-of-domain value, never for a tag or literal form
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcValue.cpp:260-261 `else if (typeTag == I4_TAG || typeTag == INT_TAG)\n      result = intFromXml(valueXml, offset);` — and libXmlRpc itself EMITS <i4>: :515-519 `xml += I4_TAG;` in `XmlRpcValue::intToXml`. Double: :577-584 `bool XmlRpcValue::doubleFromXml(...) { ... double dvalue = strtod(valueStart, &valueEnd); if (valueEnd == valueStart) return false; ...}`. Tcl surface: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrpc/tclrpc.cpp:111 `}else if(strstr(type, "int")==type || strstr(type, "i4")==type){//int`. HmIP legacy XML-RPC: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcParser#parseValue — `case 3307: case 104431:` (the hashCodes of "i4" and "int", declared as TYPE_INTEGER_4_BYTE and TYPE_INTEGER) fall through to the same `Integer.parseInt` branch, and the double branch is `Double.parseDouble(this.reader.getText())`. Fault -5 in rfd: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:128,140,163 and :1738 `throw XmlRpcException("Unknown parameter", -5);`. The exact string "Invalid parameter or value" with faultCode -5: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException (cases UNKNOWN_PARAMETER / INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE).
all.finding: Both stated reasons are false on both CCU-side XML-RPC surfaces our transport actually reaches. (1) <i4>: libXmlRpc (rfd, hs485d) dispatches I4_TAG and INT_TAG to the identical intFromXml, and it serialises its OWN integers as <i4> — a client that rejected <i4> could not talk to the CCU at all. tclrpc accepts both. The HmIP legacy parser (HmIP-RF, HmIP-Wired, VirtualDevices) puts "i4" and "int" in the same switch case. (2) <double>1</double>: libXmlRpc converts with strtod and the HmIP parser with Double.parseDouble; both accept "1", and both discard the literal text at that point — the value is a C++ TypeDouble / Java Double before any putParamset type check runs, so NO downstream validator can distinguish "1" from "1.0". (3) The fault attribution is doubly wrong: -5 in rfd reads "Unknown parameter", and the message our comment quotes comes from the HmIP legacy surface (raised when the backend reports UNKNOWN_PARAMETER or INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE — a parameter-identity or value-domain failure), not from ReGaHss and not from value formatting. What our code DOES is harmless: emitting <int> and forcing at least one fractional digit are both accepted everywhere. The defect is the recorded reason — it names a constraint that does not exist, and an operator who "simplifies" the formatter on that basis will change nothing, while one who trusts it will look for -5 in the wrong place. Scope caveat: I checked the three CCU-side parsers only; CUxD is BIN-RPC (no value tags) and Homegear is third-party, so an observation behind the original comment may have come from a non-CCU peer — that possibility is unverified.
all.negativeControl: Had the claims been right I would have found a tag whitelist that maps only INT_TAG to the integer branch (each of the three parsers could trivially have done so — they all enumerate tag names explicitly), and a double path that kept the literal string for a later validator. All three parsers accept both integer tags in one branch, and both double paths call strtod/parseDouble immediately — the opposite result in each case.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted. I opened every cited line and each contains what was claimed, transcribed exactly.

The decisive point is one I re-verified independently: libXmlRpc does not merely tolerate <i4>, it EMITS it. `XmlRpcValue::intToXml` at :517 appends I4_TAG. rfd and hs485d serialise every integer they send us as <i4>. A CCU that rejected <i4> on input would be rejecting its own wire form, and our transport — which parses incoming <i4> — could not have worked at all. That single fact settles rule (1) without needing the parser dispatch, and the parser dispatch (:260-261) settles it a second time.

Rule (2) is equally dead. Both surfaces convert the literal before any validator sees it: strtod in C++ (:580-584), Double.parseDouble in the HmIP parser. Neither preserves the text "1" vs "1.0", so no downstream putParamset check can distinguish them — the distinction our comment asserts is not merely unenforced, it is unrepresentable at the point where enforcement would happen.

I add a THIRD independent wrongness the prior pass gestured at but did not state as a finding: the attribution names a peer this transport never addresses. `internal/client/transport/xmlrpc` speaks to the interface processes — rfd, hs485d (both libXmlRpc) and HMIPServer's legacy surface. ReGaHss is reached over JSON-RPC (`internal/client/transport/jsonrpc`), never over this codec. So the comment attributes a constraint to a component that is not on the path, in addition to describing a constraint that does not exist on the components that are.

What our code does is harmless — <int> and a forced fractional digit are accepted everywhere — so this is a documentation defect, not a delivery bug. The cost is directional: an operator debugging a -5 will look in ReGaHss and at value formatting, when -5 from rfd means the parameter name is unknown and -5 from the HmIP legacy surface means unknown parameter or out-of-domain value.

I keep the prior pass's scope caveat and endorse it: only the three CCU-side parsers were read. CUxD is BIN-RPC and carries no value tags at all; Homegear is third-party. Whatever observation originally produced this comment may have come from a non-CCU peer, and that remains unverified — it is not a reason to keep the comment as written, but it is a reason not to assert the comment was invented.

all.title: setInstallMode is always sent with mode=1 on the strength of a comment alone
all.ourValue: mode=1 = "normal"; "mode=2 means ready for re-pairing"
all.firmwareValue: INSTALL_OFF=0, INSTALL_NORMAL=1, INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG=2, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST=3
all.finding: The value we send is CORRECT: mode=1 is INSTALL_NORMAL, the ordinary teach-in that registers the CCU as central. The GLOSS of mode=2 is wrong and dangerous: 2 is INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG, which resets the device to the default configuration from its device/channel description AND deletes all existing links — not "ready for re-pairing". "Ready for re-pairing / known device only" is mode 3, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST, and rfd's int range check is `0 <= mode <= INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG(2)`, so passing 3 as an int is rejected with fault -1; the whitelist mode is reachable ONLY by putting the serial as a STRING in params[2]. Our device-scoped path already does exactly that (ccu_extended.go:104 `b.xml.Call(ctx, "setInstallMode", on, duration, deviceAddress)`), so it matches the firmware — and installModeNormal is simply unused on that branch and on the HmIP branch. Second, unrelated-site defect found while grounding this: internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods.go:163-165 documents the same argument as "mode selects the learning mode (0 = normal, 1 = set, 2 = unset)", which matches neither the enum nor the adapter's comment; and the CCU's JSON-RPC wrapper discards both extra arguments — ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/setinstallmode.tcl reads only `interface` and `on` and calls `xmlrpc $interface(URL) setInstallMode [list bool $on]`, so duration and mode sent through Interface.setInstallMode never reach rfd (the window silently becomes the 60 s default).
all.negativeControl: Had mode=1 not been "normal" the enum would have ordered the constants differently (e.g. INSTALL_NORMAL=0), or RFDevice's switch would have taken a non-teach-in branch for it; instead INSTALL_NORMAL is the first non-zero ordinal and its case performs the central-address write. Had mode=2 meant re-pairing, RFDevice.cpp's INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG case would not call InitDefault()/SetDefaultConfig() — it does, so the check produced a different answer for the half of the claim that is false.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD as narrowed. Every citation opened and matched, including the enum's implicit ordinals and the exact fault string. One transcription note: the prior pass rendered the rfd source comment as "bestehenden"; the file reads "besehenden" (a typo in eQ-3's source). Immaterial to the finding, but a quote is a quote.

The value we send is CORRECT and the gloss is WRONG and dangerous, exactly as reported. Mode 2 is INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG: it calls InitDefault on config list 0 and SetDefaultConfig on the device description, which the source itself says deletes all existing links. It is not "ready for re-pairing". The re-pairing/known-device flavour is mode 3, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST, and rfd's int range check tops out at 2, so an integer 3 is refused with fault -1 — the whitelist mode is reachable only by passing the serial as a STRING in params[2].

I CORRECT one statement in the prior finding. It says installModeNormal "is simply unused on that branch and on the HmIP branch". That reads as though the constant never reaches the wire. It does: install_mode.go:59 passes installModeNormal on the broadcast path (empty deviceAddress), and ccu_extended.go:107 sends it as the third argument to the XML-RPC setInstallMode. So mode=1 IS live on the broadcast pairing path — which is fine, since 1 is INSTALL_NORMAL. It is unused only on the device-scoped path (install_mode.go:69 also passes it, but ccu_extended.go:104 takes the deviceAddress branch and drops it). The correct statement is: the constant is sent, its value is right, and its comment is wrong.

Second-site defect, re-verified: internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods.go:163-165 documents the mode argument as "0 = normal, 1 = set, 2 = unset", which matches neither the enum nor the adapter comment nor each other. I add the severity qualifier the prior pass omitted: `SetInstallModeBidCos` has NO production caller — grep across internal/ and cmd/ finds only its own declaration and one test. It is a dead method carrying a wrong comment, which lowers urgency but not the case for fixing it, since a future caller would inherit the error. And the wrapper it names would discard the argument anyway: setinstallmode.tcl reads only `interface` and `on` and forwards a single bool, so duration and mode sent through Interface.setInstallMode never reach rfd and the window silently falls back to the 60 s default.

BOUNDARY (why narrowed rather than confirmed): the enum, the range check and the mode-2 semantics are rfd-only. Our SetInstallMode also serves HmIP-RF, where ccu_extended.go:92-99 takes an entirely different route (`Interface.setInstallModeHMIP` with an installMode/address/key/keymode struct) that carries no numeric mode at all, and CUxD/Homegear, for which Tier 1 says nothing. The grounded rule is "mode=1 is INSTALL_NORMAL on the rfd XML-RPC surface", not "on every interface".

all.title: Interface reachability is inferred from a `connected` field that may not exist
all.ourValue: "one entry per *currently active* interface"; absence = down; optional per-entry `connected` boolean honoured
all.firmwareValue: one entry per CONFIGURED interface, with exactly the members name, port, info; no connected member; entries are read from /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml and cached, never from live process state
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/listinterfaces.tcl — header: "Fuer jedes Interface wird ein Objekt mit den folgenden Feldern angegeben: name [string], port [integer], info [string]"; body: `foreach interfaceName [array names INTERFACE_LIST] { array set interface $INTERFACE_LIST($interfaceName) ... append result "\"name\":[json_toString $interfaceName]" ; append result ",\"port\":$interface(PORT)" ; append result ",\"info\":[json_toString $interface(INFO)]" ... }`.
