Source of the list: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/homematic.cgi:53 `array set INTERFACE_LIST [ipc_getInterfaces]` and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/ipc.tcl:14,20,25-35,40-72 — `set IPC_INTERFACES_FILE "/etc/config/InterfacesList.xml"`, `set IPC_CACHE_FILE "/var/tmp/api_ipc.cache"`, `proc ipc_getInterfaces` returns the cache when present else parses the XML (name/url/info per <ipc> node, PORT derived from the URL). Where liveness does live: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/listbidcosinterfaces.tcl — "isConnected: [boolean] true, falls das Interface gerade verbunden ist", `append result ",\"isConnected\":[toJSONBoolean $gateway(CONNECTED)]"`, fed by ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:1269 `(bool&) descr["CONNECTED"] = (iface->IsConnected());`.
all.finding: Both halves of the comment are false, and the consequence is the one the reader feared. Interface.listInterfaces is a CONFIGURATION listing: it walks /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml (via a /var/tmp cache), so an interface process that is dead still appears, and no member reports liveness. Concretely, on stock firmware our decoder always takes `reachable := true` (the `connected` lookup at :70-74 is dead code — the response literally appends only three keys), and the Reconciler's membership diff never shrinks, so ConnectivityChangedEvent can never carry an unreachable transition from this probe; a total interface outage reads as fully reachable. The `connected`/`isConnected` field the comment half-remembers belongs to a DIFFERENT method: Interface.listBidcosInterfaces reports address, description, dutyCycle, isConnected, isDefault, fwVersion, type per BidCoS gateway (from rfd's listBidcosInterfaces struct) — i.e. per radio gateway, not per interface process. That method, or Interface.getLGWConnectionStatus, or a per-interface XML-RPC ping/init round trip, is what would actually settle reachability. Tier 2 cannot help here: this is a firmware-generated response, not a device declaration, so Tier 1 is the only authority and it is unambiguous.
all.negativeControl: Had our reading been right the tcl would either have appended a fourth member (a `connected` key) or built INTERFACE_LIST from live process state rather than from a file plus a cache. It appends exactly three keys and reads a static XML through ipc_getInterfaces — a different result in both directions.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted, and I found nothing that rescues it.

Every cited line opened and matched. listinterfaces.tcl emits three keys and only three; there is no conditional branch that could add a fourth. The list comes from a file on disk via a cache in /var/tmp, so a dead interface process still appears — and worse, a genuine configuration change does not appear until the cache file is cleared. The `connected` lookup at connectivity_probe.go:70-74 is dead code against stock firmware: `reachable` is always true, so ConnectivityChangedEvent can never carry an unreachable transition from this probe, and a total interface outage reads as fully reachable.

I ran the check the prior pass did not: the firmware map warns that a WebUI/ReGa rule read from the sources may be overridden by the ~200 distribution patches. I grepped all of ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/ for listinterfaces / listInterfaces and got zero hits. So the OCCU source text is what ships on OpenCCU, and there is no patched variant that adds a liveness member. That closes the one escape route the citation had.

The half-remembered field belongs to a different method on a different granularity: Interface.listBidcosInterfaces reports address, description, dutyCycle, isConnected, isDefault, fwVersion and type per BidCoS radio GATEWAY, sourced from rfd's own listBidcosInterfaces struct — not per interface process. That method, Interface.getLGWConnectionStatus, or a per-interface XML-RPC round trip is what would actually settle reachability.

Tier 2 cannot speak here and it is worth being explicit about why: this is a firmware-generated response shape, not something a device declares, so no descriptor corpus is authority over it. Tier 1 is the only witness and it is unambiguous.

all.title: The central-link create/remove asymmetry rests on a claim about the CCU WebUI with no path citation
all.ourValue: create raises PRESS_SHORT only; remove zeroes PRESS_SHORT and PRESS_LONG
all.firmwareValue: create: reportValueUsage(addr, PRESS_SHORT, 1). remove: reportValueUsage(addr, PRESS_SHORT, 0) AND reportValueUsage(addr, PRESS_LONG, 0)
all.citation: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0171-WebUI-Add-HmIPKeyTransceiverCentralLinkConfiguration.patch:81-107 (post-patch text at ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0183-WebUI-ImprovedFirmwareupdateDialog/occu/WebUI/www/webui/webui.js:15619-15647): `createCentralLink: function(channeltype) { ... homematic("Interface.reportValueUsage", {"interface": "HmIP-RF", "address": addr, "valueId": "PRESS_SHORT", "refCounter":"1"}); ... }` and `removeCentralLink: function(channeltype) { ... {"valueId": "PRESS_SHORT", "refCounter":"0"}); ... {"valueId": "PRESS_LONG", "refCounter":"0"}); ... }` — interface chosen by channelType: KEY_TRANSCEIVER / MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER -> HmIP-RF, KEY -> BidCos-RF. Why the asymmetry is required: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1425-1449 `bool RFChannel::ReportValueUsage(const std::string& value, int count) { if(!GetDescription()->GetAutoregisterCentral())return true; value_usage_map[value]=count; int total_count=0; for(...){ if(it->second > 0)total_count+=it->second; } ... if(total_count && !IsLinkedTo(central_address, central_channel)){ AddLinkPeer(...); }else if(!total_count && IsLinkedTo(...)){ LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(...); ... } }`. HmIP equivalent: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage — reads channel metadata "reportValueUsageData" as a Map, `dataMap.put(valueId, refCounter)`, writes it back, `newRefCounter = dataMap.values().stream().mapToInt(Integer::valueOf).sum()`, then createCentralLink when `Math.max(0, newRefCounter) > 0` else deleteCentralLink. RPC entry point and semantics: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:700-724 (returns false when the device must first be put into config mode; CONFIG_PENDING is then set on MAINTENANCE) and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/reportvalueusage.tcl:19.
all.finding: Confirmed verbatim, on both the operator surface and the mechanism beneath it. The WebUI's create path issues one reportValueUsage with PRESS_SHORT/1; the remove path issues two, PRESS_SHORT/0 and PRESS_LONG/0. More than a UI convention: the interface process keys the counters per value-id and gates the device-internal peering on the SUM, so zeroing PRESS_SHORT alone leaves the link standing whenever PRESS_LONG was ever raised, while raising PRESS_SHORT alone is sufficient to establish it. Our implementation matches on both paths. On the metadata question in the brief: reportValueUsageData is a map valueId -> integer refCounter stored per channel address; a value-id absent from the map simply contributes nothing to the sum, so "absent means zero" is correct — but note it means "absent from the sum", and reading the map back is the right way to determine the active state. Two details worth carrying: rfd sums only POSITIVE counters (`if(it->second > 0)`) whereas the HmIP side sums all values and then clamps with max(0, sum) — irrelevant for the 0/1 values we send, but a negative counter would behave differently on the two interfaces; and reportValueUsage returns false (not an error) when the device could not be reached, meaning the setting is queued and CONFIG_PENDING is raised on MAINTENANCE — our adapter treats only a transport error as failure, which matches. Scope note: the WebUI applies this only to channelTypes KEY (BidCos-RF) and KEY_TRANSCEIVER / MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER (HmIP-RF); our eligibility rule lives in device.CentralLinkEligibility and was not compared against that set here.
all.negativeControl: Had the asymmetry been the other way round, webui.js would show a PRESS_LONG call inside createCentralLink or a single call inside removeCentralLink; and had the counters not been summed across value-ids, RFChannel::ReportValueUsage would test only the just-written entry rather than accumulating total_count over the whole map, in which case zeroing PRESS_SHORT alone would suffice and the second call would be pointless. Both checks read the opposite of the alternative.
all.challengeNote:
DEMOTED from confirmed to narrowed. The quote itself is exact — I opened patch 0171 and both functions read verbatim as cited, create with one call and remove with two, on both interface branches. The rfd mechanism is exact too, including the positive-only sum. So the rule under grading is grounded. What I am demoting is its reach, by settling the question the prior pass explicitly left open ("our eligibility rule lives in device.CentralLinkEligibility and was not compared against that set here").

I compared it, and the gap is real and measurable. The firmware gates the ENTIRE mechanism on one flag: `if(!GetDescription()->GetAutoregisterCentral())return true;` — identically in rfd (RFChannel.cpp:1425) and hs485d (HS485Channel.cpp:411). When the flag is unset the call is a no-op that returns TRUE, indistinguishable at our transport from a successful link. Our eligibility (aggregate.go:551-561) admits any non-virtual-remote device on BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired or HmIP-RF, filtered per channel only by channelHasPressEvents (central_links.go:277-287, PRESS_SHORT or PRESS_LONG present in VALUES). Measured against the shipped device XMLs:

- BidCos-Wired: ZERO channels in any of the 18 hs485types XMLs carry an `autoregister` attribute, and HS485ChannelDescription defaults it false. Yet 12 hs485types files declare PRESS_SHORT/PRESS_LONG. So every central-link create or remove we issue on BidCos-Wired passes channelHasPressEvents, reaches hs485d, does nothing, and returns true — which our adapter counts as a channel touched and reports to the operator as a created link.
- BidCos-RF: 32 of 34 KEY channels carry `autoregister`; the two that do not are rf_ou_led16_ge_v1_1.xml and rf_ou_led16_le_v1_0.xml (HM-OU-LED16), whose KEY channels do declare PRESS_SHORT. Same silent-success shape on a real, shipping device.

The WebUI's own scope is narrower still: it offers the control only for channelType KEY on BidCos-RF and KEY_TRANSCEIVER / MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER on HmIP-RF. It never offers it on BidCos-Wired at all.

Two further details from the prior pass that I re-checked and confirm: reportValueUsageData on the HmIP side is a map valueId -> refCounter, so "absent contributes nothing to the sum" is right and reading the map back is the correct way to determine active state; and reportValueUsage returning false is not an error but "queued, device must enter config mode, CONFIG_PENDING raised on MAINTENANCE" — our adapter treating only a transport error as failure matches. I also confirm the divergence in summation the prior pass noted: rfd and hs485d both sum only counters `> 0`, while the HmIP handler sums all values then clamps with max(0, sum) — immaterial for the 0/1 values we send.

all.title: The paramset-consistency check is gated on HmIP-RF alone, on an unsourced claim that HmIP-Wired devices are served by the same CCU service

all.firmwareValue: one HMIPServer process, one legacy XML-RPC endpoint (Legacy.Port=32010); shipped interface names are BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, VirtualDevices, HmIP-RF — no component in either tree writes an `HmIP-Wired` ipc entry
all.ourValue: iface != hmenum.InterfaceHmIPRF → skip the device
all.finding: True as shipped, false one step wider. On OpenCCU the HmIP family really is one service: a single HMIPServer daemon with a single legacy XML-RPC API, and the InterfacesList that ReGa and the WebUI index by name never gains an `HmIP-Wired` entry — hs485dLoader.cpp:238 is the only place any daemon adds an ipc entry at runtime, and it adds BidCos-Wired. So on this firmware an HmIPW-* device arrives on the interface named `HmIP-RF` and our gate does cover it. The boundary runs at the InterfacesList: eQ-3's own operator layer is written for `HmIP-Wired` to be a distinct interface NAME (haslinksorprograms.tcl:19 indexes INTERFACE_LIST by it; ReGa functions.fn:583 compares a channel's interface object Name() against it; ic_ifacecmd.cgi resolves iface_url for it). Those branches are dormant on this distribution, not absent from the firmware. Note also that hmenum has no HmIP-Wired Interface constant at all, so a CCU that did expose one could not be connected in the first place — the gate is not the only thing that would have to change. Second, weaker point: the comment's other half — 'only HmIP devices are affected by the HmIPServer stale-files bug' — is not decidable from the CCU sources; nothing in rfd, hs485d or the HmIP side names that symptom. Our rule there rests on the Python sibling alone, and aiohomematic expresses it on the product-group axis (device.py:1149), which is the axis that survives an InterfacesList change. Our port moved it to the interface axis without saying so.
all.negativeControl: Had the rule been wrong, hs485dLoader.cpp's insertion pattern (a daemon that writes its own `<ipc><name>…</name>` block when its bus is present) would have had a counterpart writing `<name>HmIP-Wired</name>`, and monitrc would have monitored a second HmIP process or a second Legacy.Port. A grep for `>HmIP-Wired<`, `<name>HmIP`, and `Legacy.Port` across both trees returns only the single HmIP-RF entry and the single port 32010 — a different result from the one a two-interface firmware would give.
all.challengeNote: The grounding survives, and I moved it in two places. (1) Every citation is verbatim, and the step the previous agent left as inference - that the WebUI's HmIP-Wired branches are dormant rather than reachable - is now measured: dispatch.tcl:158 answers `unknown interface (HmIP-Wired)` for any interface name absent from INTERFACE_LIST, which is built from ipc_getInterfaces (homematic.cgi:53) over InterfacesList.xml. The boundary the previous agent named is the right one. Two supports it did not have: HMIPServer carries the wired MAC/OTAU subsystem itself, and its legacy XML-RPC parameter filter names SUPPORTING_WIRED_OPERATION_MODE - wired HmIP is served by the one legacy API, not merely by one process. Also confirmed: internal/config/config.go:112-119 already rejects an interface literally named "HmIP-Wired" with that reasoning, so the rule is enforced one layer above the gate, not only at it. (2) I BREAK the previous agent's second claim. It reported the comment's other half - 'only HmIP devices are affected' - as 'not decidable from the CCU sources'. It is decidable, and it decides in our favour for the structural question: on BidCos the description and the values are two filters over ONE parameter map (HSSParamset.cpp:162/:204), and Tier 2 shows no shipped MASTER parameter is non-readable, so the symptom our check looks for cannot arise there; on HmIP the two sides read two different sources (channel-type spec vs the backend's value set), so it can. What remains Tier-3-only is the specific mechanism word 'stale files' - no CCU source names that symptom; only the aiohomematic comment does. (3) NEW narrowing the previous agent missed, and it cuts against the gate. HmIP has a false-positive source our check does not exclude and that is not a stale file: MULTICAST_ROUTER_MODULE_ENABLED enters the MASTER description when the channel-type spec declares ROUTER_MODULE_ENABLED (DeviceUtil#getParamsetDescription), but enters the MASTER values only when the returned values actually contain ROUTER_MODULE_ENABLED (DeviceUtil#addVirtualConfigurationParameter). Different gates on the same parameter, so a legitimate divergence gets reported as an inconsistency. (4) SECOND boundary, on the axis question the previous agent raised but did not close: the interface axis and the product-group axis diverge at VirtualDevices, not only at HmIP-Wired. aiohomematic derives product_group model-first (interface_client.py:636), so an HmIP-model device reached over VirtualDevices gets ProductGroup.HMIP and the Python check runs on it; our interface gate skips it. Whether HmIP-model devices appear on VirtualDevices on this firmware I did not settle - unverified, and I will not fill it with a convention. (5) Precision, not a defect: the gate sits inside the per-device loop but is loop-invariant (iface never changes), so it is a whole-call skip written as a per-device skip.

all.title: The Homegear-vs-CCU classification rests on three unsourced string signatures and defaults to CCU
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:35 `const char XmlRpcServerConnection::BINARY_SIGNATURE[] = "Bin";` and :98-101 `if((_header.length()>=BINARY_SIGNATURE_SIZE+5) && (strncmp(hp, BINARY_SIGNATURE, BINARY_SIGNATURE_SIZE)==0)){ _isBinary=true; …}` — one listening socket, protocol chosen per request · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/CMakeLists.txt:95 and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/CMakeLists.txt:57 both `target_link_libraries(… XmlRpc …)` · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1206 `XmlRpcMethodPing(XmlRpcServer* s):XmlRpcServerMethod("ping", s){};` and :1274 registers it; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:601 the same · ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/config_templates/InterfacesList.xml:5 `<url>xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001</url>` (BidCos-RF) and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485dLoader/hs485dLoader.cpp:238 `<url>xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:` (BidCos-Wired) — the CCU's own clients address rfd and hs485d over BIN-RPC · Homegear signatures: `grep -rai "homegear"` over ../OpenCCU-Base returns nothing, and no device type in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types} or in ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/ begins with `HG-` (Tier 2).
all.firmwareValue: rfd and hs485d both serve BIN-RPC on their ordinary XML-RPC socket (auto-detected by the 3-byte "Bin" signature) and both implement `ping`; the CCU addresses them as `xmlrpc_bin://…`
all.ourValue: `// Step 1 — try BIN-RPC ping (CUxD uses BIN-RPC exclusively).` → any endpoint that answers a BIN-RPC ping is classified KindCUxD
all.finding: The CUxD half is contradicted outright. BIN-RPC is not a CUxD discriminator on a CCU: libXmlRpc's server sniffs the first three bytes of every request and switches to the binary framing on the same socket, rfd and hs485d both link that library, both register `ping`, and the CCU's own InterfacesList addresses BidCos-RF with `xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001`. rfd's ping handler accepts exactly one string parameter (XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1208-1217), which is precisely the shape we send (`Call(ctx, "ping", cfg.InterfaceID)`), so a BIN-RPC probe pointed at rfd returns success and the endpoint is classified KindCUxD with no further check. The Homegear half is a different result and should not be reported as the same one: whether `TYPE` starting `HG-` or a FIRMWARE string containing `homegear` identifies Homegear is a Homegear question, and the CCU sources are silent on it by construction. What Tier 1 + Tier 2 do settle is the false-positive risk against stock firmware: neither string occurs anywhere in the OCCU sources, in the shipped device-type XMLs, or in the pydevccu descriptor corpus, so stock firmware cannot trip the Homegear branch. Mitigating fact discovered while reading: DetectBackend has no production caller (only detection_test.go), so nothing on a running daemon depends on either branch today.
all.negativeControl: Had 'CUxD uses BIN-RPC exclusively' been right, the CCU's own interface list would address rfd over `xmlrpc://` like it addresses VirtualDevices, and the shared server library would carry no binary path. It addresses it `xmlrpc_bin://` and the library carries the path at XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:98 — a different result from the one the rule predicts. For the Homegear half the control is `grep -rai homegear ../OpenCCU-Base` plus a `HG-` scan of both descriptor corpora: a hit would have shown the sniff can fire against stock firmware; there is none.
all.challengeNote: The CUxD half is contradicted and I confirm it end to end: BIN-RPC is not a CUxD discriminator on a CCU. libXmlRpc switches to binary framing on the same listening socket from the first three bytes, rfd and hs485d both link it, both register `ping`, the handler accepts exactly the one-string shape our probe sends, and the CCU's own InterfacesList addresses BidCos-RF as xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001 - so a BIN-RPC probe pointed at rfd returns success and the endpoint is labelled KindCUxD with no further check. I ALSO BREAK the previous agent's treatment of the Homegear half. It reported that half as Tier-1-silent-by-construction and stopped there, which reads as 'ungrounded but ordinary'. It is worse: the three signatures have no witness at ANY tier. The Python family we ported from does not use them - aiohomematic decides Homegear from the getVersion string (`"homegear" in version_lower`), probed only when system.listMethods advertises getVersion. So sniffHomegear's TYPE-prefix/FIRMWARE rules were invented at the port, not carried over, and the doc comment's confident 'Homegear encodes a TYPE field that starts with HG-' asserts a property of a data source that was read from nowhere - the exact tell this project's rule names. That should be recorded as unverified-with-no-witness, not as Tier-1 silence. The constructive half: the mechanism aiohomematic uses IS groundable against this firmware - rfd implements getVersion and libXmlRpc serves system.listMethods, so a version-string discriminator can be built and negative-controlled against a real CCU, while the listDevices sniff cannot be checked against anything. Two things I upheld from the previous agent, both re-measured: stock firmware cannot trip the Homegear branch (0 hits for "homegear", no HG- type, both with negative controls), and DetectBackend has no production caller - grep over *.go finds it only in internal/client/backends/detection_test.go. One consequence the previous agent did not name: internal/client/interface_client.go:158 and :163 carry comments saying the client 'populates this after [backends.DetectBackend] completes'. Nothing calls DetectBackend, so those two comments are false as well - a comment-claims item, not a wire item.

all.title: installFirmware-then-updateFirmware fallback: the doc claims a device-family split and 'any error', the code branches only on an XML-RPC fault
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1092 `XmlRpcMethodUpdateFirmware(XmlRpcServer* s):XmlRpcServerMethod("updateFirmware", s){};` — rfd registers `updateFirmware` and no `installFirmware` (grep -ra over src/rfd) · ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:486 the same for hs485d · unknown-method behaviour: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:240-242 `if ( ! executeMethod(…) && ! executeMulticall(…)) generateFaultResponse(methodName + ": unknown method name");` with the default code from XmlRpcServerConnection.h:78 `void generateFaultResponse(std::string const& msg, int errorCode = -1);` — an XML-RPC fault, faultCode -1, never a transport error · HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.IServiceApi declares both `@RpcMethod("updateFirmware")` and `@RpcMethod("installFirmware")`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#updateFirmware throws a NotImplementedException RPC remote exception, while #installFirmware is the real implementation and returns boolean `false` when `DeviceUtil.isUpdateInstallable` is false or the transaction result is unsuccessful, faulting only for DeviceNotFound / AccessPointNotFound / transmission-pending · the CCU's own caller: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368 branches on the interface (`if {($iface != $HmIPIdentifier) && ($iface != $HmIPWiredIdentifier)} { … updateFirmware … } else { … installFirmware … }`) and :371 checks `if { $result == 1 }`.
all.firmwareValue: rfd/hs485d: `updateFirmware` only, unknown method → XML-RPC fault, faultCode -1, faultString "installFirmware: unknown method name". HMIPServer: `installFirmware` is real and returns boolean false on a legitimate refusal; `updateFirmware` exists but throws NotImplemented. The CCU's own WebUI never probes — it selects by interface and then checks the boolean.
all.ourValue: try installFirmware; fall back to updateFirmware only when errors.As(err, *hmerr.XMLRPCFault); return value discarded
all.finding: The probe mechanism is sound where the doc says it matters, and false one step wider. The described danger — 'a transport-level failure (not a fault) is what an old rfd returns for an unknown method' — does not occur: libXmlRpc answers an unregistered method with a real XML-RPC fault (faultCode -1), so `errors.As(callErr, &fault)` fires and the BidCos fallback runs. The comment's 'fall back on any error' is the half that is wrong, and the code is the half that is right. Two boundaries the rule does not cover. (1) The CCU's own caller does not probe at all: ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368 picks the method from the interface — HmIP-RF/HmIP-Wired → installFirmware, everything else → updateFirmware. Our probe costs every BidCos update one guaranteed round trip that ends in a logged fault. (2) The boolean is load-bearing and we drop it. HMIPServer's installFirmware returns `false` — not a fault — when the update is not installable or the transaction fails; `_, callErr := b.xml.Call(...)` sees callErr == nil and we return success for an update that never started. The WebUI checks `$result == 1` at :371 precisely for this. The bundle's other worry (a fault on HmIP fires a second update at the same device) is real but harmless in effect: HMIPServer's updateFirmware immediately throws NotImplemented, so no second update starts — it only converts a specific fault into a misleading one.
all.negativeControl: Had rfd answered an unknown method with a transport error rather than a fault, the shared server would have had no `generateFaultResponse(methodName + ": unknown method name")` path — it would have closed the connection or returned nothing. XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:240-242 shows the fault path and XmlRpcServerConnection.h:78 shows the code it carries, which is a different observation from the one the damage note predicts. Had 'installFirmware fails only by faulting' been right, LegacyServiceHandler#installFirmware would have had no `return false` branches; it has two before any throw.
all.challengeNote: The previous agent's core result stands and I re-measured every leg of it: libXmlRpc answers an unregistered method with a real XML-RPC fault (code -1), not a transport error, so errors.As fires and the BidCos fallback runs; the comment's 'fall back on any error' is the wrong half and the code is the right half; and the CCU itself never probes, it branches on the interface at ic_ifacecmd.cgi:363-368. I BREAK one framing and add one boundary. (1) The finding presents the dropped return value as an HmIP problem ('HMIPServer's installFirmware returns false ... we return success for an update that never started'). It is both families. rfd's updateFirmware also returns a boolean: XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1096 assigns the result of RFManager::UpdateFirmware into the reply, and the WebUI's `$result == 1` at :371 sits AFTER the if/else, so eQ-3 checks the boolean on the BidCos branch too. Our `_, err := b.xml.Call(ctx, "updateFirmware", address)` discards it identically. Reported as an HmIP-only defect it would get an HmIP-only fix. (2) NEW narrowing the previous agent missed, and it matters for any fix: the two BidCos daemons do not return the same SHAPE. rfd writes a scalar `(bool&)result` from params[0] only; hs485d loops over all params and writes `(bool&)result[i]` - a one-element array for our single-address call. Code that starts reading the return has to handle bool and []bool, or it will silently mis-read BidCos-Wired. (3) Quote precision, not a defect: the grounding gives faultString as the literal `"installFirmware: unknown method name"`. The firmware constructs it as `methodName + ": unknown method name"` - the rendered string is right, but it is a concatenation, and presenting a constructed string as a verbatim constant is the kind of transcription that later gets matched against literally. (4) I confirm the finding's own narrowing about the second update: a fault on HmIP's installFirmware makes us call updateFirmware, which throws NotImplemented immediately, so no second update starts - the damage is a misleading error, not a duplicate write.

all.title: The virtual-remote device addresses are bare literals with no cited source

all.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF → address "BidCoS-RF", TYPE HM-RCV-50 · BidCos-Wired → address "BidCoS-Wir", TYPE HMW-RCV-50 · HmIP-RF → address "HmIP-RCV-1" (HmIP-RCV-<n>, n starts at 1), TYPE HmIP-RCV-50

all.finding: Both halves the reader flagged are wrong, and the third definition in the repo is right. (1) `interface_client.go:1085` returns "HmIP-RF" as the HmIP virtual-remote address. The firmware address is `HmIP-RCV-1` — DEVICE_ID_BASE "HmIP-RCV-" plus a counter that starts at 1, with one instance constructed per LegacyServiceHandler. "HmIP-RF" is the INTERFACE name, not a device address; no device with that address exists. (2) The doc comment at :1079-1081 says wired interfaces have no virtual-remote concept. hs485d constructs one unconditionally: HS485Central.cpp:37 `serial="BidCoS-Wir"`, type HMW-RCV-50. (3) The capitalisation the reader doubted is right: `BidCoS-RF` with a capital S, verbatim from RFCentral.cpp:37. So `internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:38-44` — "BidCoS-RF", "BidCoS-Wir", "HmIP-RCV-1" — matches the firmware on all three entries, and `pkg/hmenum/device_model.go:21-25` — HM-RCV-50, HMW-RCV-50, HmIP-RCV-50 — matches the three TYPE strings exactly. The wrong definition is the one in interface_client.go, and it is the one with no citation. One narrowing on the routingkey entry: `HmIP-RCV-1` is only the first VRC's address; the counter is static and increments per constructed instance, so a second LegacyServiceHandler in one JVM would yield HmIP-RCV-2. On a CCU one handler is built, so HmIP-RCV-1 is correct in our scope. Consequence today: `VirtualRemote()` has no production caller (only interface_client_test.go:186 and interface_client_deep_test.go:559), so the wrong address is latent — but it is a device-addressing datum that would go on the wire the moment it is wired up, and its two neighbours prove the repo already knows the right answer.
all.negativeControl: Had "HmIP-RF" been the HmIP virtual remote's address, the HmIP component would have had a constant carrying it and no `DEVICE_ID_BASE` counter; instead the address is composed from a base plus an instance number and the TYPE is a separate constant. Had BidCos-Wired had no virtual remote, hs485d would have had no HS485Central with a `serial=` assignment, mirroring rfd's RFCentral; it has one, at the same line, with a different literal — the check returns a different string for each of the three families, so it is not echoing our input.
all.challengeNote: Upheld, and I strengthened it in the one place it was thin. All three firmware values are verbatim, and the step the previous agent left implicit - that rfd's `serial` is the XML-RPC ADDRESS - is now cited (RFDevice.cpp:242). interface_client.go:1085 returns "HmIP-RF", which is the INTERFACE name; the firmware address is HmIP-RCV-1, and I closed the one escape route the previous agent did not test: VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching is exact-equality against DEVICE_ID_BASE+vrcNr, so "HmIP-RF" matches nothing and would be resolved as an ordinary device id, raising DeviceNotFound. The doc comment's claim that wired interfaces have no virtual-remote concept is refuted by HS485Central.cpp:36-37, which constructs one unconditionally. The capitalisation the reader doubted is right (`BidCoS-RF`, capital S). The two neighbouring definitions match the firmware exactly on all three entries. ONE CITATION DEFECT I found in the grounding, and it is the kind this audit exists to catch. It writes the VRC channel range as though crRFD.conf carried it - 'gated by Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.Enabled (=true in crRFD.conf) with channel indices Legacy.VirtualRemoteControl.ChannelIndex.First=0 ... .Last=50'. crRFD.conf sets only three VRC properties: Enabled, MigrationGate.Enabled, MigrationGate.File (grep over ../OpenCCU-Base/etc and /opt returns exactly those). 0 and 50 are the CODE defaults in VirtualRemoteControl's constructor (ServiceProperties.getInt with fallback 0 and 50) - a firmware default, not a shipped configuration value, and this project's own rule separates those two tiers. It does not change the address, so the verdict stands, but a later reader following that citation into crRFD.conf will not find the numbers. The address narrowing the previous agent gave is correct and I re-derived it: vrcNr is static and increments per constructed instance, so HmIP-RCV-1 is only the first; on a CCU one LegacyServiceHandler is built, so it is the right value in our scope. Consequence today is latent - VirtualRemote() has no production caller - but it is a device-addressing datum that goes on the wire the moment it is used, and its two neighbours already hold the right answer.

No PING TTL and no mismatch count exist anywhere in the CCU sources. The one comparable constant is 10 consecutive failed event deliveries before rfd/hs485d drop a client.
all.ourValue: PingPongTTL = 300 s; defaultPingPongMismatchThreshold = 15; unknown PONG recorded at Error severity as "ping/pong: unknown PONG (CCU restart?)"
all.finding: The CCU source does not decide either number. `ping` is not a device round trip: rfd's handler calls HSSManager::Ping inline, which calls ReportEvent immediately, so the only latency between PING and PONG is one XML-RPC event dispatch back to our callback server. Nothing in rfd, hs485d or libhsscomm expires a pending ping or counts mismatches — those are our policy, and the TTL rests on the Python sibling's const.py while the threshold 15 rests on nothing at all. Two firmware facts that do bear on the surrounding claims. (a) The callerId is echoed verbatim (`ReportEvent("CENTRAL", "PONG", callerId)`) and the event address is the literal "CENTRAL", not the central serial — the doc comment at XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1198 says centralSerial and the implementation passes "CENTRAL"; our BIN-RPC fixtures already use "CENTRAL". (b) ReportEvent fans out to every registered handler, so a PONG carrying a callerId we never sent is emitted by design whenever another registered client (ReGa, another daemon) pings the same rfd — not only after a restart. Our production wiring already handles that correctly: internal/central/adapter/pingpong_wiring.go:89-92 drops any callerId whose prefix is not this client's own WireBoundaryID, so the Error-severity "CCU restart?" incident can only fire for one of our own tokens. The comment there is confirmed by the firmware. (c) For sizing: rfd removes a client after 10 consecutive failed event deliveries, after which no PONG can arrive at all — a threshold of 15 outstanding pings sits past the point where the CCU has already dropped us as a handler. That is the firmware's own number on the same channel, but it counts a different quantity (failed pushes, not unanswered pings), so it cannot be substituted for 15; naming it as the source would be exactly the convention-for-a-missing-input substitution this audit exists to catch.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU carried a ping TTL or a mismatch bound, it would live beside the ping handler or in the dispatcher, next to the one constant that IS there — `m_clientSendFailureCount >= 10`. Greps for a timeout, a TTL or a counter around ping/PONG across src/rfd, src/hs485d and src/libhsscomm return only that failure counter, a different result from the one a firmware-derived 300 s / 15 would have produced. Had PONG been unicast to the pinging client, ReportEvent would have taken a target URL like XmlRpcCallSync does; it takes none and loops the whole handler map.

all.title: HmIP pairing mode sends 'on' as a string while BidCos sends a bool - only one of the two can be right by accident
all.firmwareValue: setinstallmodehmip.tcl: `if { ($on != "") && (($on == "true") || ($on == 1) || ($on == "1"))}` — string and JSON-boolean are indistinguishable. `Interface.setInstallMode` is NOT registered in methods.conf. rfd InstallModes enum: INSTALL_OFF=0, INSTALL_NORMAL=1, INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG=2, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST=3; accepted int range for params[2] is 0..2, default when omitted is INSTALL_NORMAL(=1); seconds clamped to 600, default 60.

all.finding: Four separate results. (1) The string form is ACCEPTED but not REQUIRED: the CCU's own JSON parser maps the bare literal `true` to the Tcl string "true", so a JSON boolean and the string "true" reach `$args(on)` identically. The value we send works; the stated justification is wrong. (2) installMode "ALL" is correct — it is the branch that forwards to XML-RPC `setInstallMode [bool on] [int time]`; "LOCAL" forwards to setInstallModeWithWhitelist; anything else falls into a STOP branch that drops `time`. Confirmed. (3) key/keymode may be empty STRINGS but the KEYS must be present — checkArguments rejects a missing name with error 402. Our payload is correct. (4) The asymmetry is not an asymmetry, it is a dead method: `Interface.setInstallMode` is not in methods.conf on any variant I read (base tree, src/webui tree, and seven patched copies under ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/**/methods.conf), so the CCU answers `jsonrpc_error 401 "method not found"`. The orphan script www/api/methods/interface/setinstallmode.tcl exists but is unreachable and reads only `$args(on)` — it ignores `duration` and `mode` entirely. jsonrpc.Client.SetInstallModeBidCos could never work against a CCU; it has no production caller (only methods_test.go:253). The live BidCos path, CcuBackend.SetInstallMode at ccu_extended.go:100-108, goes over XML-RPC and matches the firmware. (5) Additional contradiction on the same doc comment: methods.go:163-164 documents mode as "0 = normal, 1 = set, 2 = unset". The firmware enum is OFF=0, NORMAL=1, PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG=2, DEVICE_WHITELIST=3. A caller following our doc and passing 0 for "normal" selects INSTALL_OFF. This one does reach the radio, because CcuBackend.SetInstallMode passes the same `mode` straight into the XML-RPC call at ccu_extended.go:107.

It returns neither. The same grep does return the HMIP entry and the getInstallMode entry, so the read is not blind; and the enum read does discriminate — it returns four distinct ordinals, not a uniform answer.
all.challengeNote: The Tier-1 core is upheld; the reachability clause is not. UPHELD, re-read verbatim: (a) JSON `true` and the string "true" are indistinguishable at $args(on) — json_parseValue:116 hands "t" to json_parseConstant, which returns $const, the token itself; the accepted set in the Tcl is {"true", 1, "1"}. Our value works; the doc's "as required by the CCU wire protocol" is wrong, and only the justification is wrong. (b) `Interface.setInstallMode` is not registered. METHOD_LIST is built solely from methods.conf (homematic.cgi:54-55), and I re-ran the sweep myself with grep -a over nine copies — www/api/methods.conf, src/webui/www/api/methods.conf, and all seven patched methods.conf under ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/**: every one carries `Interface.setInstallModeHMIP` and none carries `Interface.setInstallMode`. all.title: The stale-session code set admits two codes whose only authority is the test simulator
all.firmwareValue: 400 is emitted from exactly one site in the firmware: `jsonrpc_error 400 "access denied (\"$method(LEVEL)\" needed $upl)"` inside checkPrivilegeLevel. -32001 and -32002 appear nowhere in the CCU tree.
all.ourValue: const ccuAccessDeniedCode = 400, documented as "both for an invalid/expired session and for a privilege mismatch"; -32001/-32002 documented as non-CCU backend codes.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/homematic.cgi:104-118 (checkPrivilegeLevel; the 400 emission is :115) — `grep -ran "jsonrpc_error 400" www/ src/webui/` returns that line and its src/webui/www twin and nothing else, while the same sweep returns 30 sites for 500 and 14 for 501; www/api/eq3/getupl.hms (verbatim: `var upl = 0; if ( system.IsVar("_session_id_") ) { var id = system.GetVar("_session_id_"); var s = system.GetSessionVarStr(id); if (s) { upl = s.StrValueByIndex(";", 1); } } Write(upl);`); www/api/eq3/jsonrpc.tcl:44-70 (jsonrpc_error writes only CONTENT-TYPE plus the body — no Status header, so the CGI answers HTTP 200); www/api/homematic.cgi:196-210 (the published code table: 400 = "Privilegstufe reicht nicht"). Codes actually emitted across www/ and src/webui/www/: 100, 102, 103, 200, 400, 401, 402, 500-507, 599, 601-604.
all.finding: Our rule is right on every clause I could test. 400 carries both meanings and only those two: getupl.hms returns upl = 0 whenever the session variable is absent or GetSessionVarStr yields empty — i.e. an invalid, expired or unpresented session — so checkPrivilegeLevel fires the identical 400 for a dead session and for a genuine privilege shortfall, on every method whose LEVEL is not NONE. It is emitted under HTTP 200, as our comment says. It is used for nothing else: one call site in the whole tree. The two negative codes are correctly labelled as non-CCU: neither -32001 nor -32002 occurs anywhere in the firmware, so admitting them cannot mis-trigger against a real CCU. One adjacent fact worth keeping: `Session.login` answers 501 for "invalid credentials or too many sessions" (www/api/methods/session/login.tcl:51), and dispatch.tcl reuses 501 for "XML-RPC: general error" (www/api/methods/interface/dispatch.tcl). We do NOT treat 501 as stale — correct, because a re-login loop on 501 is exactly the session-slot burn the candidate worries about, and 501 is the code a too-many-sessions condition actually uses.
all.negativeControl: Had 400 been a general-purpose rejection code, `grep -ran "jsonrpc_error 400" www/ src/webui/` would have returned several call sites scattered through www/api/methods/**, the way the same grep returns 30 sites for 500 and 14 for 501. It returns one (plus its src/webui duplicate). Had the two negative codes been CCU codes, the enumeration of emitted codes would have contained them; it contains no negative value at all.
all.challengeNote: Upheld on every clause I could test, and I tried to break each one separately. 400 carries both meanings and only those two: getupl.hms yields upl = 0 whenever the session variable is absent or GetSessionVarStr returns empty — an invalid, expired or unpresented session — so checkPrivilegeLevel fires the identical 400 for a dead session and for a genuine privilege shortfall. There is one emission site in the entire tree; I re-ran the sweep rather than trusting the count, and calibrated it against 500 (30 sites) and 501 (14 sites) so a zero result could not be a broken grep. The two negative codes are correctly labelled non-CCU: zero occurrences across www/, src/webui/ and src/, so admitting them cannot mis-fire against a real CCU. Not treating 501 as stale is right and load-bearing: 501 is what a too-many-sessions condition actually uses (login.tcl:51), so admitting it would build exactly the re-login loop that burns the remaining session slots. Two scope facts our comment does not state, neither a defect: checkPrivilegeLevel is skipped entirely when $central is false (a config-tool document root, not a CCU), and a method whose LEVEL is NONE never reaches the check at all — so a stale session on a NONE-level method produces no 400 and no re-login. One clause is inference rather than reading: "under HTTP 200" rests on jsonrpc_error emitting no Status header, which I did read, plus CGI protocol semantics, which are not in this tree. The conclusion is right; our comment states it more flatly than the source supports.

all.title: The CGI session form sid=@<session>@ and the endpoint-suffix base URL are both unverified and gate backup + firmware download
all.firmwareValue: Query-string session id: `regexp "$sidname=(@\\[A-Za-z0-9\\]*@)" $queryparams dummy querysid` — the @-delimiters are mandatory and are kept in the captured value. cp_security.cgi has `proc action_create_backup`. cp_maintenance.cgi has NO `action_download_firmware` and accepts no `url` parameter; its remote source is the fixed REMOTE_FIRMWARE_SCRIPT and its local source is a multipart `firmware_file` upload.
all.ourValue: DownloadBackup: `?sid=@" + url.QueryEscape(sid) + "@&action=create_backup` — correct. DownloadFirmware: POST form {sid: <bare>, action: "download_firmware", url: <firmwareURL>} — no such action, and the bare sid is never read.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/tcl/eq3_old/session.tcl:291-329 (session_urlsid; the regexp is :312, the empty-QUERY_STRING early return :299), :334-342 (session_urlsid_short strips with `^@([a-zA-Z0-9]*)@$`), :768 (`set sid [session_urlsid]`), :902 (REGA_SESSION(REGASID)); www/config/cp_security.cgi:1008 (the WebUI's own `…?sid=$sid&action=create_backup`) and :1506 (proc action_create_backup) → www/config/backup.tcl:8-39 (streams application/x-download, .sbk); www/api/methods/session/create.tcl:43 and login.tcl:52 (`regexp {sid=@([^@]*)@}` — the JSON-RPC API hands back the INNER value, so re-wrapping is right); www/config/cp_maintenance.cgi:1-8 (session.tcl sourced before cgi_eval) and :1393-1408 (`if {[session_requestisvalid 8] > 0} then action_$action`), :42/:44 (REMOTE_FIRMWARE_SCRIPT), :1021 (action_firmware_upload, multipart), :1372 (action_download_logfile — the only action_download_*); www/api/homematic.cgi:28 (DOCUMENT_ROOT is /www/), with www/api/homematic.cgi and www/config/cp_*.cgi as siblings under it. Witness (Tier 3, and equally wrong): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/client/json_rpc.py:781,791-794.
all.finding: Split result. CONFIRMED, on Tier 1: (a) the @-delimited form is not a convention, it is the CGI's extraction regexp — session_urlsid captures `@…@` inclusive and session_urlsid_short strips the delimiters for the ReGa lookup; the WebUI builds byte-for-byte the URL we build, and `action=create_backup` really is a proc that streams the .sbk archive; (b) `url.QueryEscape(sid)` is a harmless no-op, since the sid alphabet is [A-Za-z0-9] per that same regexp; (c) stripping `/api/homematic.cgi` to get the base is right, established structurally by the firmware's document root — the JSON-RPC entry point and the two CGIs are siblings under /www/. CONTRADICTED, twice, on DownloadFirmware: (1) no `download_firmware` action exists anywhere — grep over the whole OpenCCU-Base www/ and src/webui/ trees and over the ../OpenCCU patch tree returns zero hits; the dispatcher calls `action_$action`, so an unknown name is an undefined Tcl command, and there is no `url` parameter for a firmware source on that CGI at all. (2) The bare `sid` form field is never seen: session.tcl is sourced at cp_maintenance.cgi:4, before cgi_eval/cgi_input parses the POST body, and session_urlsid reads $env(QUERY_STRING) and returns "" immediately when it is empty — so a POST with no query string yields sid = "" and session_requestisvalid rejects the request before any action would run. Both failures produce an HTML page under HTTP 200, and DownloadFirmware returns nil on 200 — a silent success for an operation that did not happen. The unexplained asymmetry therefore resolves the other way round from the reader's guess: the wrapped call is the correct one and the bare one is broken.
all.negativeControl: Had `download_firmware` been a real action, the sweep that finds `action_download_logfile` at cp_maintenance.cgi:1372 and `action_create_backup` at cp_security.cgi:1506 would have found it in the same pass — that sweep does return the full action inventory of both CGIs, so it is not blind. Had the query-string sid been accepted bare, session.tcl:312's regexp would have read `"$sidname=(\\[A-Za-z0-9\\]*)"` without the @ literals; it does not, and the complementary read (session_urlsid_short) exists precisely to remove them again.
all.challengeNote: Split result upheld, and the contradicted half is worse than reported. CONFIRMED: the @-delimited form is the CGI's extraction regexp, not a convention — session_urlsid captures the delimiters inclusive and session_urlsid_short strips them for the ReGa lookup; session_generatesid builds the id from [A-Za-z0-9] and wraps it in @…@ itself, so the WebUI's own URL at cp_security.cgi:1008 is byte-for-byte ours and url.QueryEscape is a provable no-op over that alphabet; action=create_backup is a real proc that streams the .sbk. The base-URL derivation is right, established structurally by the document root. CONTRADICTED on DownloadFirmware, and I attacked both legs rather than accepting them. (1) `grep -ran "download_firmware"` over the whole OpenCCU-Base tree and the whole ../OpenCCU tree returns zero lines; cp_maintenance.cgi defines 19 action_ procs and I listed all of them in the base file and in every patched copy under buildroot-external/patches/occu — none is action_download_firmware, and none of the update actions takes a `url`. The dispatcher calls `action_$action`, so the name is an undefined Tcl command. (2) The bare `sid` form field is unreachable, and the obvious counter-argument is worth stating because it nearly rescues the call: session_urlsid DOES have a POST fallback at :315-319. It is dead here, because the empty-QUERY_STRING early return at :299 fires first, and because session_requestisvalid reads the globals fixed at source time (:762-768), before cgi_input has parsed the body at :1395. So sid is "" and the request is rejected before any action would run. NEW, and the reason I raise severity: the prior grounding measured the wrong function. The live path is not jsonrpc.Client.DownloadFirmware but CcuBackend.DownloadFirmware (ccu_extended.go:1083-1128), wired at ccu_wiring.go:885 and reachable from REST via handlers/ccu_maintenance.go:286 -> adapter/ccu_maintenance.go:188. It builds the identical form and returns nil on HTTP 200. Both failure legs produce an HTML page under HTTP 200, so an operator-triggered firmware download reports success for an operation that never started — on the production path, not only in the transport helper.

all.title: "The CCU's putParamset handler crashes on a bare /" is a bare comment claim that drives a hard rejection
all.firmwareValue: rfd/hs485d: the request URI is never parsed — readHeader scans only for "Content-length: ", "Connection: " and the header terminator. HmIP-RF legacy API: a single requestHandler, no router, no path inspection. VirtualDevices: routes /bidcos and /groups, catch-all `.*` → HTTP 404, body "404 - page no exist", connection closed.
all.ourValue: config.go:153-155 — "the bare \"/\" is not usable — the CCU's putParamset handler crashes on it"; config.go:71-74 — "POSTing to it crashes the CCU's putParamset handler".
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:103-112 (readHeader's only header scan) and :231-278 (executeRequest/parseRequest work off the body alone — no URI member, no path compare anywhere in the file); src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:67,74,96,117 ("/RPC2" exists in this library only as the CLIENT-side default URI, never as a server route); src/hs485d/hs485d.cpp:71-75 (hs485d instantiates the same XmlRpcServer); src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp (the rfd method table registers by method NAME only). HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyApiServerUtil#startHttpServer (installs BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler as the sole requestHandler on Legacy.Port, default 2010) and de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle (does not read the request path); HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.server.BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer (routes "/bidcos" and "/groups", then a `.*` catch-all that sets status 404 and ends the response) and de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT.
all.finding: The claim is false on every interface this validator governs, and the failure it names does not exist. On BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired the daemons serve XML-RPC through src/libXmlRpc, whose server discards the request line entirely: readHeader looks for Content-length, Connection and the blank line, and nothing else; the URI is not stored, not compared, not logged. A bare "/" is therefore byte-for-byte equivalent to "/RPC2" for every method including putParamset. On HmIP-RF the legacy XML-RPC server is created with one request handler and no router, so every path is served. VirtualDevices is the single interface where the path is routed at all, and an unmatched path there yields a plain HTTP 404 with the body "404 - page no exist" and a closed connection — the server keeps running. So: no crash, no daemon abort, and no putParamset-specific path handling anywhere, because there is no path handling for it to be specific about. Keeping the rejection is still defensible as a guard against a mis-set VirtualDevices path (where "/" gives a 404 on every call), but both the field doc and the operator-facing message state a firmware behaviour the firmware does not have, and the message misdirects the next reader away from the one interface that actually cares. On the surface question: I answered the surface remote_path sits on — how each interface daemon dispatches a request by URI — and confirmed the answer is "three of four never look at it".
all.negativeControl: Had the claim been right, XmlRpcServerConnection would have had to parse the request line: there would be a URI/path member on the connection, or a strncmp against "/RPC2" in readHeader, or a fault path keyed on the URI. There is none — the class's only header fields are _contentLength and _keepAlive. And BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer's unmatched-path branch would have thrown or exited rather than answering 404. The same reads DO find real path routing where it exists ("/bidcos" and "/groups" on the VirtualDevices server), so the check discriminates rather than reporting "no routing" uniformly.
all.challengeNote: Upheld, and I went after the two ways it could have been wrong. First, wrong surface: our remote_path governs the URL path our XML-RPC client POSTs to per interface, and I confirmed the daemons on the other end are the ones cited — rfd.cpp:64 and hs485d.cpp:71 both instantiate the same libXmlRpc XmlRpcServer whose connection class contains no URI member and no path comparison, so a bare "/" is byte-for-byte equivalent to "/RPC2" for every method, putParamset included. Second, an omitted variant: "/RPC2" occurs in the whole src tree only as the client-side default in XmlRpcClient.cpp, so there is no second server implementation I missed. On HmIP the legacy XML-RPC server installs one handler with no router and that handler reads only the body. VirtualDevices is the single interface that routes at all, and its unmatched path yields a plain 404 with a closed connection — the server keeps running. So: no crash, no daemon abort, and no putParamset-specific path handling anywhere, because there is no path handling for it to be specific about. I also looked for the claim's provenance and could not find it in any tier, including the Python family the field was ported from. Keeping the rejection is still defensible as a guard against a mis-set VirtualDevices path, where "/" gives a 404 on every call — but both the field doc and the operator-facing message assert a firmware behaviour the firmware does not have, and the message points the next reader away from the one interface that actually cares about the value.

all.title: SimpleRF temperature bounds 6.0–30.0 are attributed to a MASTER descriptor the code never reads
all.firmwareValue: HM-CC-TC channel 2 CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR, VALUES paramset: `<parameter id="SETPOINT" operations="read,event,write" control="TEMP.SETPOINT">` with `<logical type="float" min="6.0" max="30.0" default="21.0" unit="°C">`, two special values `VENT_CLOSED` = 0.0 and `VENT_OPEN` = 100.0, and `<conversion type="float_integer_scale" factor="2"/>`. MASTER TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE: `<logical type="float" min="6.0" max="30.0" default="21.0" unit="°C"/>`.
all.ourValue: MinTemperature 6.0, MaxTemperature 30.0, TemperatureStep 0.5 — frozen in simpleRfCapabilities; setSimpleRFMode writes MaxTemperature for HEAT and MinTemperature for OFF, bypassing MinTemp()/MaxTemp().
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_tc.xml:185 (channel index 2, type CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR), :269 (paramset type="VALUES"), :271 (the SETPOINT parameter), :286 (the logical min/max/default), :287-288 (special_value VENT_CLOSED 0.0 / VENT_OPEN 100.0), :293 (float_integer_scale factor 2 → the 0.5 step), :424+:434 (MASTER TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE), :449 (TEMPERATUR_LOWERING_VALUE), :533 (TEMPERATUR_PARTY_VALUE), :606 (a weekly TEMPERATUR_SATURDAY_1) — all 6.0/30.0; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_tc_le_v1_9.xml:267-268 (same SETPOINT block on the LE variant). Our side: internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:831-852 (SimpleRfThermostat primary channel 1, ChannelFields[1] → FieldSetpoint: Bare(ParameterSetpoint)), internal/model/custom/profiles.go:287-296 and :1629-1638 (hm-cc-tc and "zel stg rm fwt"), internal/model/custom/climate/climate.go:638-663 and :672-693 (MinTemp/MaxTemp read c.setpoint.DescriptorMin/Max BEFORE the capability fallback), :1022-1033 (SetTemperature's range validation), :1073-1086 (SetMode dispatches on Kind and never consults SupportsOff).
all.finding: The numbers are right, and right for a better reason than the comment gives. The comment's premise is false: the SimpleRF family DOES ship a writable setpoint descriptor — it is named SETPOINT, not SET_TEMPERATURE, it lives in the VALUES paramset of the very channel we write to (device channel 2, CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR), and it declares min=6.0 max=30.0 default=21.0 with a factor-2 integer scale that is also where our 0.5 step comes from. Our own profile writes exactly that DP. The named source, MASTER TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE, happens to carry the same bounds, as do TEMPERATUR_LOWERING_VALUE, TEMPERATUR_PARTY_VALUE and every weekly TEMPERATUR_<day>_<n>; but calling it a "weekly-schedule descriptor" is wrong — it is the comfort-temperature config parameter, and the weekly entries are a separate family. Where the rule is false one step wider: the device's acceptance set for SETPOINT is NOT [6.0, 30.0]. Two special values sit outside it — VENT_CLOSED (0.0), which fully closes the linked valves, and VENT_OPEN (100.0), which fully opens them. SetTemperature rejects anything outside [MinTemp, MaxTemp], so neither is reachable through our climate DP, and setSimpleRFMode(ModeOff) writes 6.0 — the lowest regulating setpoint, not the device's actual off. SetMode reaches that path even though simpleRfCapabilities.SupportsOff is false, because SetMode dispatches on Kind alone. Second boundary: the verification covers HM-CC-TC only. The firmware device-type set carries no ZEL_STG_RM_FWT XML (grep over src/devicetypes returns nothing), and it is absent from ../pydevccu and ../openccu-data as well; our profile registers "zel stg rm fwt" as an alias of hm-cc-tc at profiles.go:1629-1638. Today the two agree exactly, so nothing is mis-written — the defect is that the code takes the frozen copy where the live descriptor is one call away.

TIER: rf_cc_tc.xml is a device-type XML, which this audit's own map places at Tier 2, not Tier 1. The bounds are a descriptor fact. The only Tier-1 leg is the step, which I added below. BOUNDARY REMOVED: the prior grounding reported ZEL STG RM FWT as unverified because "the firmware device-type set carries no ZEL_STG_RM_FWT XML; grep over src/devicetypes returns nothing". The firmware id is space-separated — `ZEL STG RM FWT` — and it is declared in rf_cc_tc.xml's own `<supported_types>` at :13, beside HM-CC-TC at :9. One XML, one channel-2 SETPOINT descriptor, serving both models; our alias registration at profiles.go:1629-1638 reproduces the firmware's own grouping exactly. A grep for the underscore form finds nothing, which is presumably how the boundary was invented — a boundary asserted from a grep miss reads exactly like one read from the source. SURFACE, traced end to end rather than assumed: the profile registers primary channel 1, ChannelFields keys are relative offsets rebased by groupNo (`rebased[ch+groupNo]`), so ChannelFields[1] resolves to absolute channel 2 — the CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR channel that carries SETPOINT — and ParameterSetpoint is literally "SETPOINT". So we do bind to that descriptor, and the comment's "no SET_TEMPERATURE DP whose descriptor would otherwise drive these" is false; the DP is simply named SETPOINT. The "weekly-schedule descriptor" label is also wrong: TEMPERATUR_COMFORT_VALUE is `docu brief="Konforttemperatur"`, a config parameter on list 5, and the weekly TEMPERATUR_<day>_<n> entries are a separate family that merely shares the range. CORRECTION to the prior reading of our own code: setSimpleRFMode does NOT bypass MinTemp()/MaxTemp(). It calls SetTemperature, which validates against both at :1023-1033. What it bypasses is the descriptor as the SOURCE of the value — it writes the frozen capability constant. A descriptor/capability disagreement would therefore surface as ErrTemperatureOutOfRange, not as a silently wrong write; the defect shape reported was more severe than the code supports. STEP, now grounded on Tier 1 and worth recording because nothing else names it: `float_integer_scale` is handled by HSSTypeConversionFloatInteger, which rfd links, and LogicalToPhysical is a C cast — it TRUNCATES. At factor 2 the logical grid is 0.5 and an off-grid setpoint goes toward zero, not to nearest. SURVIVING BOUNDARY: the device's acceptance set for SETPOINT is [6.0,30.0] plus {0.0, 100.0}; VENT_CLOSED and VENT_OPEN are unreachable through Climate.SetTemperature, and setSimpleRFMode(ModeOff) writes 6.0 — the lowest regulating setpoint, not the device's valve-closed value — over a path SetMode reaches although simpleRfCapabilities.SupportsOff is false, because SetMode dispatches on Kind alone. Which source to follow: Tier 2, the per-device descriptor read at runtime; MinTemp()/MaxTemp() already do, and setSimpleRFMode is the one place that takes the frozen copy where the live descriptor is one call away.

all.firmwareValue: Polarity and paramset: exactly as we say. true = lock activated = device input ignored, on BOTH stacks; it is a config/MASTER parameter on both, never a VALUES parameter (no stateparameter class of that name exists on the HmIP side; no rftypes XML declares it in a VALUES paramset). Address: HmIP places it on the MAINTENANCE channel (channel 0) MASTER, so `:0` is right there; HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU — the only device the RFButtonLock profile targets (internal/model/custom/profiles.go:729-737) — declares it in the DEVICE-level MASTER paramset `tc_it_dev_master` (rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:14), which rfd serves at the bare device address, not at `:0`; channel 0's own MASTER is `maint_ch_master` (:5053) and does not contain it.
all.finding: Both audited claims hold. Polarity is confirmed three ways and none of them is the Python port: the shipped RF device XML states that setting it true activates the lock and that inputs at the device are then ignored; the HmIP configuration-parameter identifier documents it as the "activation state of the global button lock"; the WebUI renders it as a checkbox labelled "Globale Bediensperre" whose help says the lock blocks operation at the device. The MASTER/put_paramset claim is confirmed: it is a `<physical interface="config">` parameter on RF and a ConfigurationParameter on HmIP, so a setValue can never reach it (see c012). The narrowing is the third, adjacent claim at lock.go:227-228 — "on ch0" is true for HmIP but false for the one RF device the RFButtonLock profile covers, where the parameter sits in the device-level MASTER paramset addressed without a channel suffix. This matters because HSSParamset::Put silently ignores ids it cannot find and returns true, so a putParamset aimed at `:0` on that device would report success and write nothing.
all.negativeControl: Had the polarity been inverted, rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml:44-45 would have said that true releases the keys (as its sibling BUTTON_LOCK docu at :22-31 says the LOCAL lock can be released at the device), the HmIP @ParameterDocumentation would have named a deactivation or release state, and the WebUI checkbox label/help would have read "Bedienung freigeben" rather than "sperrt die Bedienung am Gerät". All three read the same way, and the German and English help strings agree. Had it been a VALUES parameter, it would have appeared in a `<paramset type="VALUES">` block in some rftypes XML or as a StateParameter on the HmIP side; it appears in neither.
all.challengeNote:
The narrowing is correct and I confirmed its mechanism independently, but it is stated too narrowly in one place and its consequence is not established.

Upheld: polarity holds on both stacks, and none of the evidence is the Python port. The RF device XML says setting it true activates the lock and device-side inputs are then ignored; HmIP documents it as the "activation state of the global button lock". It is a config/MASTER parameter on both — `<physical interface="config">` on RF, a ConfigurationParameter (not a stateparameter) on HmIP — so setValue can never reach it. The addressing narrowing is right, and I verified the mechanism the audited report only asserted: RFChannelDescription::GetParamset (:313) does not fall back to the device paramset — its only fallback is "LINK" — so `<addr>:0` MASTER on HM-TC-IT resolves to `maint_ch_master`, which does not carry GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK.

Widened: the boundary is not "the one device RFButtonLock targets". Three shipping RF device types declare GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK (HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU, HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM) and all three put it in a device-level MASTER paramset, not on channel 0. RFButtonLock currently covers only hm-tc-it-wm-w-eu (internal/model/custom/profiles.go:729-737), but the trap is the parameter's, not the profile's.

Corrected: the stated failure mode — "a putParamset aimed at :0 would report success and write nothing" — is not reachable on RF as our code stands. RFButtonLock resolves its DP with PrimaryChannel 0 (internal/model/custom/profile_configs.go:564-579) against the channel's own descriptor. Since the CCU never exposes GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK in `<addr>:0` MASTER, `custom.SwitchField(...)` at lock.go:232 returns nil, the channel-scoped BUTTON_LOCK fallback at :234 returns nil too, and the profile yields no lock DP at all. The RF consequence is a dead profile, not a silently-lost write. HSSParamset::Put's silent-success behaviour is real and worth knowing (it also silently skips present-but-read-only ids), but it only bites once something puts the parameter on ch0.

One presentation flaw: the audited report calls polarity "confirmed three ways" without saying that the WebUI leg is HmIP-only. GLOBAL_BUTTON_LOCK appears in exactly two files under www/config/easymodes/ — hmipChannelConfigDialogs.tcl and MASTER_LANG/HEATINGTHERMOSTATE_2ND_GEN_HELP.js — and that help file is sourced only by hmip dialogs. For RF the polarity rests on the shipped device XML (Tier 2) alone.

all.title: Per-parameter VALUES reads are suppressed for the whole VirtualDevices and BidCos-RF interfaces
all.citation: OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand.cpp:147-176 `GetData`: `if(get_request_frame.id.empty()){ return inst->GetStoredValue(value_id, param); }` / `if(inst->GetAge(value_id)<VALUE_CACHE_TIME){ return inst->GetStoredValue(value_id, param); }` / `if(channel->GetDevice()->RxNeedsWakeup()){ if(inst->GetStoredValue(value_id, param))return true; channel->GetDevice()->QueueAfterWakeupFrame(frame); return false; }`. OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/ValueStore.cpp:25-38 (`GetStoredValue` returns false when the name was never stored). OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParameter.cpp:220-234 (`if(!physical_type->Get(...)){ if(logical_type->UseDefaultOnFailure()){ ... *val=description["DEFAULT"]; return true; } ... return false; }`); :28 `undefined(true)`; :355 `this->undefined = false;` inside `ProcessIncomingFrame`; :252-279 (mode==1 returns `{VALUE: default, UNDEFINED: true}`). OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSParamset.cpp:162-176 (`Get` returns false on the first parameter whose GetValue fails — no partial struct). OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSLogicalType.cpp:43-44 (`use_default_on_failure` is a per-parameter XML attribute, default false at :25). OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:228-244 + OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcException.h:29 (`Failure` with the default code -1). Descriptor scan: `grep -rn use_default_on_failure ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/` = 21 hits in 20 of 130 files, every one `<logical type="string" default="" use_default_on_failure="true"/>`. `grep -rho 'id="[A-Z_0-9]*_STATUS"' ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/*.xml | sort -u` = ACK_STATUS, LED_STATUS only.
all.ourValue: value_cache.go:314-332: BidCos-RF and VirtualDevices are skipped interface-wide because a per-parameter fallback "cannot return a device-fresh reading — only a CCU-internal placeholder (reported with *_STATUS = NORMAL so the status cannot be used to reject it)" and because "the fallback then returns the paramset default instead of a real reading".
all.firmwareValue: For BidCos-RF: (a) a read that cannot be satisfied does NOT return the paramset default — `HSSParamset::Get` aborts on the first failing readable parameter and the whole getParamset answers fault -1 "Failure". The DEFAULT fallback exists only for parameters whose device XML declares `use_default_on_failure="true"`, which in the shipped rftypes is 21 parameters, all `logical type="string" default=""`. (b) There is no `*_STATUS = NORMAL` sibling convention on BidCos-RF; the only `*_STATUS` ids in the 130 shipped rftypes are ACK_STATUS and LED_STATUS. (c) The suppression is not interface-shaped: the no-active-query branch is gated on `RxNeedsWakeup()`, i.e. on the device's RX_MODE, so a mains BidCos-RF device (RX_ALWAYS) DOES get the get-request frame sent and answered from the device. (d) The CCU already computes the exact flag we want — `undefined`, true from construction and cleared only when a device frame delivered the value — and exposes it through the 3-argument getValue/getParamset (mode==1).
all.finding: The rule's stated firmware basis does not hold for BidCos-RF on any of its three legs. The failure mode is not a plausible-looking default value quietly marked valid; it is a hard fault -1 on the whole paramset, because HSSParamset::Get is all-or-nothing. The `*_STATUS = NORMAL` reasoning is imported from the HmIP surface and has no counterpart in the BidCos-RF descriptors. And the skip keys on the interface while the firmware keys on RX_MODE, which is exactly the over-broad scope the reader flagged: mains-powered BidCos-RF devices are actively queried by rfd and are paying for the battery subset. Most usefully, the input our code is trying to guess at is carried by the source after all — rfd tracks `undefined` per parameter and hands it over on the 3-argument form, so the honest fix is to read that flag rather than to widen or narrow a heuristic. I could not settle the VirtualDevices half: that interface is served by the HMServer group/virtual-device stack, not by rfd, and I did not verify its read path — treat the VirtualDevices leg of this rule as still ungrounded.
all.negativeControl: Had our claim been right, `HSSParamset::Get` would have inserted the logical DEFAULT for an unreadable parameter and continued to the next one, and `use_default_on_failure` would appear on ordinary numeric value parameters across the rftypes corpus rather than on 21 empty-string parameters. It does neither: Get `return false`s on the first failure, and the attribute defaults to false (HSSLogicalType.cpp:25). Had the battery/mains distinction been irrelevant, `RFPhysicalDataInterfaceCommand::GetData` would have had no RX_MODE branch; it has one, and the branch is the only place the get-request frame is skipped.
all.missingInput: The VirtualDevices read path (HMServer group/virtual-device stack) — not examined; the BidCos-RF findings do not transfer to it.
all.challengeNote:
Contradicted, and I reproduced all three legs myself — but the audited report's own leg (c) is over-broad in the same way it accuses our comment of being.

Confirmed by my reading: (a) the failure mode is a hard fault, not a plausible default. HSSParamset::Get (:162-176) aborts on the first readable parameter whose GetValue fails and XmlRpcMethodGetParamset turns that into -1 "Failure" — there is no partial struct and no silently-substituted default. The DEFAULT fallback exists only behind `use_default_on_failure`, which in the shipped descriptors is 21 empty-string parameters. Our code's fallback path is `loader.GetParamset(..., ParamsetKeyValues)`, so this is the right surface. (b) There is no *_STATUS = NORMAL convention in the RF descriptors; the only ids are ACK_STATUS and LED_STATUS. (d) The firmware does carry the flag we are guessing at — `undefined`, true from construction (:28), cleared only in ProcessIncomingFrame (:355), exposed on the 3-argument getValue/getParamset (mode==1, :252-280). Reading it is the honest fix.

Overstated by the audited report: leg (c), "the suppression is not interface-shaped, it is RxNeedsWakeup-shaped, so mains BidCos-RF devices DO get queried". The RxNeedsWakeup gate at :166 is reached only after the guard at :152 — `if(get_request_frame.id.empty()) return GetStoredValue(...)`. Only 76 parameters across 21 of the 127 shipped RF device XMLs declare a `<get request="..."/>` frame at all. For every other BidCos-RF VALUES parameter no active query is issued regardless of RX_MODE; the read returns the stored value or fails. So the firmware's key is (declares a get frame) AND (RX_ALWAYS or already stored) — not RX_MODE alone. Our interface-wide skip is still wrong, but it is less wrong than the audited report implies, and a fix keyed purely on RX_MODE would be a second guess.

The VirtualDevices half stays ungrounded; the audited report says so and I did not close it either.

all.firmwareValue: setValue targets VALUES and only VALUES on every stack — confirmed, and the method signature carries no paramset argument at all. The fault code is interface-dependent: rfd answers -5 with the message "Unknown parameter" (not "Invalid parameter or value"); hs485d answers -1 with the message "Failure". CONFIG_PENDING is NOT an HmIP-only signal: rfd raises it on every True↔False transition for BidCos-RF devices and hs485d does the same for BidCos-Wired.
all.finding: The load-bearing half is confirmed outright: `RFChannel::SetValue` hard-codes `GetParamset("VALUES")` before looking the name up, so a MASTER parameter can never be reached through setValue, and the dangerous branch our comment worries about is real by construction — the lookup is by name inside VALUES, so a MASTER parameter that shares a name with a VALUES parameter gets the VALUES one written silently. Two details are narrower than stated. First, the fault code is not universal: BidCos-Wired returns -1 "Failure", not -5, because hs485d returns a bool where rfd throws; anything that keys recovery on -5 will miss the wired case. Second, the stated reason for the nil master-refresh hook on HmIP is contradicted — CONFIG_PENDING is emitted by rfd and hs485d as well, so it is not what distinguishes the two stacks. The wiring may still be correct, but its written justification is not a firmware distinction and should not be cited as one.
all.negativeControl: Had setValue been paramset-aware, `RFChannel::SetValue` would have taken a paramset key from the call rather than hard-coding "VALUES", and `XmlRpcMethodSetValue::execute` would have accepted a fourth non-rxmode argument; it accepts only an optional rxmode string constrained to "WAKEUP"/"BURST" (RFManager.cpp:181-189). Had CONFIG_PENDING been HmIP-only, `grep -rn CONFIG_PENDING ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/` would have been empty; it returns the emitter, the getter and the header documentation.
all.challengeNote:
Upheld as narrowed, and there is a third fault path the audited report missed — the one that matters for the very parameter class c009 is about.

Confirmed line-exact: `RFChannel::SetValue` hard-codes `GetParamset("VALUES")` before the name lookup, so a MASTER parameter can never be reached through setValue, and the dangerous branch our comment worries about is real by construction — the lookup is by name inside VALUES, so a MASTER parameter sharing a name with a VALUES parameter gets the VALUES one written silently. I also checked the layer above: `RFManager::SetValue` does not catch, so the -5 genuinely reaches the client.

Added: our comment's "-5" holds only for rfd at a CHANNEL address. `RFDevice::SetValue` (RFDevice.cpp:225-228) returns false unconditionally, so a setValue at a bare device address on rfd is turned into -1 "Failure" by XmlRpcMethodSetValue (:322/:327). That is exactly the address a device-level MASTER parameter lives at on HM-TC-IT and HM-CC-RT-DN (see c009), so the three outcomes are: channel/rfd -5 "Unknown parameter", device/rfd -1 "Failure", hs485d -1 "Failure". Anything keying recovery on -5 misses two of the three. The message in our comment is wrong too — rfd says "Unknown parameter", not "Invalid parameter or value".

Confirmed contradiction of the second claim: CONFIG_PENDING is emitted by rfd on every True↔False transition (RFDevice.cpp:1036-1040) and by hs485d identically (HS485Device.cpp:64), so it is not what distinguishes HmIP from classic HM. The wiring may still be correct for other reasons, but its written justification is not a firmware distinction. Note this sentence lives at channel_set.go:284-286, repeated at :531 and channel.go:211-213 — three sites, not the one the audited report named.

Two of the four sets are wrong, both in the direction that sends a call the HmIP daemon refuses: InterfacesSupportingConfigRestore includes HmIP-RF and InterfacesSupportingTeams includes HmIP-RF, and all three of those methods answer with NotImplementedException. The comment's smoke-detector rationale for Teams does not survive — HmIP smoke-detector grouping goes through the HmIP group/virtual-device path, not the legacy team methods.

I verified both method tables line by line rather than trusting the summary; every cited line number was exact, and I confirmed the negative halves directly: rfd contains no searchDevices symbol at all (not just an unregistered class), and hs485d contains no team or config-restore symbol. I also checked ExtendedLegacyServiceHandler's full override list to make sure none of the six is rescued by the subclass, and found the same six throwing in HMServer as well as HMIPServer, so the result does not depend on which server serves a given legacy interface.

The one counter-signal I found, and why it does not overturn: OpenCCU patch 0151-WebUI-Add-DeviceRestoreConfigButton gates the new Restore Config button on `$EASYLINKMODE == "false"` only — it is NOT interface-gated. (The `if {($iface != $HmIPIdentifier) && ($iface != $HmIPWIdentifier)}` line in the same hunk is pre-existing context belonging to the firmware-update block, not the restore gate.) So the OpenCCU WebUI does offer restore-config on HmIP devices.
