That is a WebUI bug, not evidence of support: the call lands on HMIPServer's throwing method, and devconfig.cgi's own `cmd_restore_config` is written to `catch` the failure and render a "failed" page. The daemon is authority over the button.

all.title: The BIN-RPC callback endpoint scheme xmlrpc_bin:// is asserted, not sourced
all.citation: OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/config_templates/InterfacesList.xml:5 `<url>xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001</url>` for BidCos-RF, against `xmlrpc://127.0.0.1:39292/groups` (:10) and `xmlrpc://127.0.0.1:32010` (:15) for the HTTP interfaces. OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485dLoader/hs485dLoader.cpp:238 writes the BidCos-Wired entry as `<url>xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:` + port. These two are the ONLY occurrences of the token in either tree (`grep -rn xmlrpc_bin ../OpenCCU-Base ../OpenCCU`). Scheme semantics: OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:46-50 parses the substring before `://` into `protocol`, and :82 `_isBinary = protocol.find("bin")!=std::string::npos;`. Re-serialisation: :605 `if(_isBinary)url="binary://";` (and :613 `uds_bin://` for the socket form) in `XmlRpcClient::getURL()`. Registration keying: OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:270-272 `if(xmlrpc_handlers.find(url) == xmlrpc_handlers.end()) { ... xmlrpc_handlers[url]= xmlrpcEventDispatcher; ... }` and the deregistration branch :341-347 `HSSXmlRpcEventDispatcher* dispatcher = xmlrpc_handlers[url]; xmlrpc_handlers.erase(url);`.
all.ourValue: cuxd_wiring.go:191-196: "xmlrpc_bin:// is the scheme every CCU-side component uses for a BIN-RPC callback endpoint, and the one the CCU prints in its own handler lists. CUxD itself accepts anything here — it speaks no other protocol — but an unrecognised scheme makes the entry unreadable for an operator comparing handler lists."
all.firmwareValue: `xmlrpc_bin://host:port` is the CCU's form for a BIN-RPC endpoint, but on the interfaces-list (outbound IPC) surface — the two occurrences are both `<ipc><url>` entries, neither is an init() callback registration. The CCU's own client PRINTS a binary endpoint as `binary://host:port`, not `xmlrpc_bin://` (XmlRpcClient::getURL(), :605). And the scheme is not cosmetic in the CCU's own receiving code: any scheme containing the substring "bin" selects BIN-RPC (`_isBinary = protocol.find("bin")!=std::string::npos`), and the handler map is keyed on the verbatim URL string with no normalisation, so init and deinit must present byte-identical URLs.
all.finding: The chosen value is right and the reasoning behind it is half right. `xmlrpc_bin://` is genuinely the CCU's spelling for a BIN-RPC endpoint — but the evidence sits on the interfaces-list surface (where the CCU records how to reach an interface process), not on the init() callback surface our code is on, where the token does not appear in either tree at all. The clause "the one the CCU prints in its own handler lists" is not supported by the code path that prints one: XmlRpcClient::getURL() emits `binary://`. More importantly, the comment's premise that the scheme is decorative is contradicted for the CCU's own daemons on both counts the comment itself worries about: the substring "bin" is what selects BIN-RPC over HTTP, and `xmlrpc_handlers` is keyed on the raw URL, so a scheme that differs between init and deinit leaves the handler registered — precisely the duplicate-delivery shape LegacyInitInterfaceID already works around. Whether CUxD behaves the same way is not decidable here.
all.negativeControl: Had the scheme been cosmetic in the CCU, XmlRpcClient's URL constructor would have discarded `protocol` after splitting on `://`; instead it is the sole input to `_isBinary`, so a `xmlrpc://` callback URL on a BIN-RPC port would make the CCU speak HTTP to it. Had registrations been normalised, `xmlrpc_handlers` would key on host and port; it keys on `const std::string& url` and erases by the same string. Had `xmlrpc_bin://` been the init-callback convention, the token would appear somewhere under src/tclrega, www/ or the rfd init path; `grep -rn xmlrpc_bin ../OpenCCU-Base ../OpenCCU` returns exactly the two `<ipc>` sites.
all.missingInput: CUxD's own parsing, normalisation and registration keying of the callback URL. CUxD source is present in neither ../OpenCCU-Base nor ../OpenCCU (no CUxD package under buildroot-external/package/occu), so the half of the claim that is about CUxD is not performable from these sources; it would need CUxD's own source or a wire capture of an init/deinit pair against a live CUxD.
all.challengeNote:
Demoted from narrowed to tier1-silent, on two grounds — one of which is a wrong-surface citation inside the audited report itself.

First, the audited report's own refutation is on the wrong surface. It says "the CCU's own client PRINTS a binary endpoint as `binary://host:port`, not `xmlrpc_bin://` (XmlRpcClient::getURL(), :605)" and uses that to refute our comment's clause about handler lists. But `getURL()` renders an outgoing client's own URL; it is not what writes a handler list. `HSSManager::SaveXmlRpcHandlers` (HSSManager.cpp:448-462) writes `it->first` — the verbatim string the client registered in init() — and `LoadXmlRpcHandlers` reads it back unchanged. So the CCU's handler-list file echoes whatever scheme the caller sent; the CCU never chooses the spelling there. Our comment's clause is therefore neither supported nor refuted by any code path either report found: it is unverified, and the refutation offered for it repeats the exact failure this audit hunts.

Second, and why the whole item drops rather than narrows: our code is on the init()/callback surface, and no Tier-1 source in either tree carries an `xmlrpc_bin://` on that surface. Both occurrences of the token are `<ipc><url>` entries — the direction in which the CCU reaches an interface process, not the direction in which an interface reaches a callback. The grammar analogy is reasonable and the value is very likely right, but it was measured on a neighbouring surface, which is not a grounding.

The supported observations, kept: `xmlrpc_bin://` is genuinely the CCU's BIN-RPC URL spelling on the interfaces-list surface, and the scheme is not decorative for the CCU's own daemons — `_isBinary` keys on the substring "bin" (XmlRpcClient.cpp:82) and `xmlrpc_handlers` is keyed on the raw URL string (HSSManager.cpp:270-272, :341-347), so a scheme that differed between init and deinit would leave a handler registered. That is a real duplicate-delivery shape, and it is the same shape LegacyInitInterfaceID already works around at cuxd_wiring.go:188-190. But it describes rfd and hs485d. Whether CUxD's parser and registry behave the same way is not decidable from either tree, so "CUxD itself accepts anything here" is also unverified.

What would settle it: CUxD's own source or configuration for its callback registry, or a wire capture of a working CUxD `init()` plus the resulting CUxD handler list.

all.title: The per-interface endpoint path rule (and the 'bare / crashes putParamset' claim) has no source
all.citation: HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT (= "/groups") and #DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT (= 9292); HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer (routes "/bidcos" and "/groups"; a routeWithRegex(".*") catch-all answers 404 "404 - page no exist" and closes the connection); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyApiServerUtil#startHttpServer (ServiceProperties.getInt("Legacy.Port", 2010), requestHandler = BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler, no Router); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle (reads only the body, never request.uri()); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:84-160 (readHeader parses only the BIN-RPC signature, Content-length and the HTTP version — the request URI is never extracted or compared); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:67,74,96,117 (_uri = "/RPC2" as the client-side default); witness ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/central/config.py:284 remote_path="/groups"
all.finding:
The path VALUES are right; the stated REASON is false, and the two halves live on different servers.

(a) /groups for VirtualDevices — CONFIRMED at Tier 1. The 9292 service (HMServer) is the only CCU XML-RPC server that routes by path at all: BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer registers exactly "/bidcos" and "/groups", and Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT is the literal "/groups" with DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT 9292. So our /groups + 9292 pair matches the firmware.

(b) /RPC2 for the rest — CONFIRMED as harmless, not as required. rfd (2001) and hs485d (2000) run libXmlRpc's XmlRpcServerConnection, whose header parser never extracts a request URI (XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:84-160); it looks only for the BIN-RPC signature, "Content-length: " and "HTTP/1.0". The HmIP legacy surface on 2010 installs a bare requestHandler with no Router (LegacyApiServerUtil#startHttpServer) and BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle consumes the body without touching request.uri(). On 2000/2001/2010 the path is ignored entirely. /RPC2 is nonetheless the correct value to send: it is libXmlRpc's own client default (XmlRpcClient.cpp:67,74,96,117).

(c) 'POSTing to the bare "/" causes the CCU's putParamset handler to crash internally (Vert.x NPE or fault -5) while reads still succeed' — CONTRADICTED. On the one server where the path matters (9292), the catch-all route answers HTTP 404 with the body "404 - page no exist" and closes the connection, for every method — putParamset and getParamset alike. Reads do not 'still succeed'. On 2000/2001/2010 nothing dispatches on the path, so a bare "/" cannot select a different handler at all. The comment attributes a crash to a routing mechanism that either 404s uniformly or does not exist.

Boundary: keep the paths explicit — but because the 9422/9292 groups service 404s an unrouted path, not because any handler crashes. The Vert.x/fault -5 sentence is unsourced and should not be repeated as observed CCU behaviour.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong, BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer would have registered a different literal (or none) for the virtual-device surface, and Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT would have held something other than "/groups" — the check reads two independent firmware sites that could each have disagreed. For the crash claim the control is sharper: had the CCU really mishandled writes on "/", the 9292 router would have needed a route that accepts "/" and forwards to a dispatcher; instead the only non-/bidcos, non-/groups route is a 404-and-close terminal handler, which cannot produce 'reads still succeed'.
all.ourValue: /RPC2 for all interfaces, /groups for VirtualDevices; comment: bare "/" crashes putParamset (Vert.x NPE or fault -5) while reads succeed
all.firmwareValue: /groups + port 9292 confirmed (Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT, BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer). Bare "/" on 9292 = HTTP 404 "404 - page no exist" + connection close for every method. On 2000/2001/2010 the request URI is never read, so no path selects any handler.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD on substance, with two corrections; verdict stays narrowed.

I re-read every cited symbol rather than trusting the transcription. All eight check out verbatim: GROUP_CONTEXT is "/groups", DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT is 9292, initializeHttpServer registers exactly two exact-match routes plus a `.*` catch-all that 404s and closes, LegacyApiServerUtil installs a bare requestHandler with no Router, BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle touches only the body, XmlRpcClient defaults _uri to "/RPC2" at all four constructors, and readHeader contains no URI parse.

Correction 1 — the prose carries a port that exists in no source. The boundary sentence says "the 9422/9292 groups service". "9422" appears nowhere in the firmware, nowhere in our DetectionPorts (which pairs 9292 with TLS 49292), and nowhere in the aiohomematic witness. It must not be carried forward; a stray number inside an otherwise-verified grounding is exactly what gets quoted later as fact.

Correction 2 — (b) is stronger than "harmless" and should be stated as such. I verified that rfd's putParamset and getParamset are registered on the same libXmlRpc XmlRpcServer instance whose connection reads headers via XmlRpcServerConnection::readHeader. That parser walks the header buffer looking only for the BIN-RPC signature, "Content-length: ", "Connection: " and the header/body separator. The request line is never tokenised, so "POST / HTTP/1.1" and "POST /RPC2 HTTP/1.1" differ only in bytes that no comparison in the daemon ever touches. On 2000/2001/2010 the path cannot select a different handler, therefore it cannot select a *crashing* one. That is a proof, not an absence of evidence.

(c) stays contradicted, and I add the reason the comment is self-defeating: it claims reads succeed where writes crash. On 9292 the catch-all fires before any method name is decoded — the RPC body is never parsed — so getParamset and putParamset receive the identical 404 and a closed connection. There is no server among the four on which a path can make reads and writes diverge.

Keep the explicit paths. The justification in the comment should be: 9292 routes by path and 404s anything but /bidcos and /groups; 2000/2001/2010 ignore the path entirely and /RPC2 is libXmlRpc's own client default. Drop the Vert.x/NPE/fault -5 sentence — it is unsourced and, on the only path-routing server we talk to, refuted.

all.title: The mixed-case-address rule rests on a comment claiming HmIP-RCV-1 is the only mixed-case address in a CCU's inventory
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFCentral.cpp:37 `serial="BidCoS-RF";` (type="HM-RCV-50" at :36); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Central.cpp:37 `serial="BidCoS-Wir";`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.VirtualRemoteControl (DEVICE_ID_BASE = "HmIP-RCV-", id = DEVICE_ID_BASE + vrcNr with vrcNr starting at 1 and incremented per instance; #isIdMatching uses this.id.equals(serial), a case-sensitive String.equals); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler (new VirtualRemoteControl(ap.getID(), ap.getAddress(), vertx) — one per access point); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException (DeviceNotFoundException -> faultCode -2, faultMessage "Invalid device"); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:591,593 `typedef std::map<std::string, RFDevice*> t_dev_instances; t_dev_instances dev_instances;`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:347-365 (GetInstance does dev_instances.find(dev_address) on that map); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:160,169 `throw XmlRpcException("Unknown instance", -2);`; HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupdevice.service.internal.GroupVirtualDevice (GroupDeviceIdentifier = "INT") and de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.ip.IpVirtualDevice (DEVICE_DESCRIPTION_SERIAL_ADDRESS = "VIP", serial String.format("%s%07d", "VIP", n)) — both upper-case
all.finding:
Two claims in the comment; the mechanism claim holds, the inventory claim does not.

Case sensitivity — CONFIRMED, on both south-bound daemons. rfd looks a device up by serial in a std::map<std::string, RFDevice*> (RFManager.h:591) via dev_instances.find (RFManager.cpp:356), i.e. byte-wise std::less<std::string>; a miss throws XmlRpcException("Unknown instance", -2) from RFManager.cpp:160 (getValue) / :169 (setValue). The HmIP legacy surface matches the virtual remote with this.id.equals(serial) (VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching) and maps the resulting DeviceNotFoundException to faultCode -2 / "Invalid device" (NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException). Note the fault TEXT our comment quotes is the HmIP one; rfd says "Unknown instance" for the same -2.

'HmIP-RCV-1 is the one mixed-case address in a CCU's inventory' — CONTRADICTED. There are at least three mixed-case address roots, one per south-bound daemon:
  • BidCoS-RF   — rfd's own central device (RFCentral.cpp:37)
  • BidCoS-Wir  — hs485d's central device (HS485Central.cpp:37)
  • HmIP-RCV-<n> — the HmIP virtual remote (VirtualRemoteControl.DEVICE_ID_BASE)
And the ordinal is not fixed: vrcNr starts at 1 and is incremented for each VirtualRemoteControl, one of which is constructed per access point in LegacyServiceHandler — a CCU with a second HmIP access point yields HmIP-RCV-2.

The rest of this repository already knows this: internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:41-43 lists all three roots, and internal/central/adapter/devices.go:56 names them too (with a typo, "BidCos-Wir" for the firmware's "BidCoS-Wir"). Only the mqtt_sink comment claims a set of one. The mechanism (case-insensitive registry scan) is unaffected and covers all three when the model knows them; what is wrong is the comment's justification, and by extension any future code that hard-codes {HmIP-RCV-1} as the exhaustive set — pkg-level lists that pin "HmIP-RCV-1" literally will miss HmIP-RCV-2 on a two-AP CCU.

The group/virtual pseudo-devices are not a further exposure: INT<id> (GroupVirtualDevice.GroupDeviceIdentifier) and VIP%07d (IpVirtualDevice) are both all-upper-case.
all.negativeControl: Had the case-sensitivity claim been wrong, rfd's lookup would have used a case-insensitive comparator (a strcasecmp-based map comparator or an upper-casing normaliser before find) and VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching would have used equalsIgnoreCase — the tree does use equalsIgnoreCase elsewhere (DeviceUtil, for "ALL_SMOKE_DETECTORS"), so the check could have come back the other way and did not. Had the 'only mixed-case address' claim been right, RFCentral.cpp and HS485Central.cpp would have assigned all-upper-case serials; both assign mixed-case literals.
all.ourValue: comment: the virtual remote "HmIP-RCV-1" is the one mixed-case address in a CCU's inventory; wrong case faults with "Invalid device"
all.firmwareValue: three mixed-case roots — BidCoS-RF (rfd), BidCoS-Wir (hs485d), HmIP-RCV-<n> (HmIP, n from an incrementing counter, one VRC per access point). Fault on a case mismatch: rfd "Unknown instance" / -2; HmIP "Invalid device" / -2.
all.challengeNote:
The two headline claims hold and I verified them independently. The ORDINAL MECHANISM the previous grounding offered is CONTRADICTED by the source, and its stated consequence does not follow.

What I confirmed. Case sensitivity, on both south-bound daemons: rfd resolves a serial through std::map<std::string,RFDevice*>::find (RFManager.cpp:356 on the map declared at RFManager.h:591-593), i.e. byte-wise std::less<std::string>, and a miss throws XmlRpcException("Unknown instance", -2) from GetValue (:160) and SetValue (:169). On the HmIP legacy surface I traced the actual write path rather than assuming it: LegacyServiceHandler#setValue takes the VRC branch only when isIdMatching passes, so a case-mismatched address falls through to DeviceUtil#setValue -> #getDeviceID, whose lookup is a case-sensitive map get followed by a case-sensitive endsWith scan, and which throws DeviceNotFoundException -> NotificationUtil -> -2 / "Invalid device". So the fault text our comment quotes is reachable, though by the generic device path, not by VirtualRemoteControl#isIdMatching as the previous grounding implied. Three mixed-case roots confirmed at the two C++ sites and the DEVICE_ID_BASE constant. INT/VIP are upper-case, so the pseudo-devices add no exposure.

What breaks. The previous grounding wrote: "one VRC per access point ... a CCU with a second HmIP access point yields HmIP-RCV-2", citing LegacyServiceHandler. The source says otherwise. There is exactly one `new VirtualRemoteControl(...)` in the entire HmIPServer tree, and its argument is AccessPointUtil.getFirstMasterAccessPoint(vertx) — a method that iterates the access-point map, breaks on the FIRST entry whose hasMaster() is false, and returns that one. No loop over access points exists. Adding a second HmIP access point therefore does not create a second virtual remote through this path.

What actually drives the ordinal — and why it is not answerable here. vrcNr is a private static Integer initialised to 1 and incremented once per VirtualRemoteControl construction, i.e. once per LegacyServiceHandler construction. Two workers construct one: LegacyAPIWorker#initializeService (new LegacyServiceHandler) and ExtendedLegacyAPIWorker#initializeService (new ExtendedLegacyServiceHandler, which extends LegacyServiceHandler). So within one process the second handler's virtual remote is named HmIP-RCV-2. Which of those two is reachable on the 2010 legacy port, and whether both workers are deployed on a stock CCU, is verticle-deployment configuration I cannot read out of the readable material. So the question our code actually cares about — "can an address other than HmIP-RCV-1 appear in a CCU inventory?" — is not settled by anything I found. It is not-performable from these sources, and the answer is certainly not "yes, via a second access point".

Tier 2 is silent here and cannot be promoted: I scanned all 2924 entries of ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json for an ADDRESS whose device part is neither all-upper nor all-lower and found zero — the corpus uses synthetic VCU* addresses and carries no real central or virtual-remote address at all.

Standing exposure, unchanged and real: internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go:39-44 hard-codes the literal "HmIP-RCV-1" as an exhaustive member of virtualRemoteRoots. If any CCU ever presents HmIP-RCV-2, that entry silently fails to namespace it per central. The mechanism in mqtt_sink.go is not affected — it scans the registry case-insensitively and covers whatever roots the model knows. Also note internal/central/adapter/devices.go:56 spells the wired root "BidCos-Wir"; the firmware writes "BidCoS-Wir" (HS485Central.cpp:37). That is a comment, not a lookup key, so it is cosmetic — but it is the same class of error the rule is about.

all.title: The auto-generated link name and description are written to the CCU with no length or charset check
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:413-430 (XmlRpcMethodAddLink: AddLink(params[0],params[1]) then, only if params.size()>=3, SetLinkInfo(params[0..3]); no validation of params[2]/params[3]); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:715-726 (RFChannel::SetLinkInfo — `it->second.name=name; it->second.description=description; RequestSave();`, no length or charset check, no truncation); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1154,1156 (SaveToXml: name -> the `link_name` XML attribute, description -> the `description` child node text); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LinkUtil#setLinkInfo (stores a LinkData verbatim into a HashMap keyed "%s:%02d-%s:%02d" and Jackson-serialises it to linkData.conf; no validation); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LinkData (name/description are plain Strings defaulting to ""); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LinkUtil#getLinkInfo and #getDefaultName (on a miss returns new LinkData(getDefaultName(...), "NO_DESCRIPTION") where getDefaultName = String.format("%s:%02d %s:%02d", ...)); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:126 (WebUI cmd_addLink calls addLink with two arguments only) and :150-152 (it calls setLinkInfo only `if { $description != "" || $name != "" }`); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/tools/devconfig.cgi:1040 (addLink with two arguments)
all.finding:
The feared damage does not exist; a different, real divergence does.

Constraints — none, on either surface. rfd's addLink hands name and description straight to RFChannel::SetLinkInfo, which assigns them into the link_peers entry as std::string and requests a save (RFChannel.cpp:719-724). Nothing measures a length, filters a character set, truncates, or rejects. Persistence is XML (link_name attribute + description text node, RFChannel.cpp:1154-1156). The HmIP legacy surface is the same shape: LinkUtil#setLinkInfo puts a LinkData holding the two raw Strings into a map and Jackson-writes linkData.conf. So the hypothesis 'the firmware silently truncates or rejects' is contradicted — there is no code path that could.

What the firmware does differently is that it never writes a default at all. Both firmware-side callers pass addLink two arguments (ic_ifacecmd.cgi:126, devconfig.cgi:1040) and the WebUI reaches setLinkInfo only when the operator actually typed something (ic_ifacecmd.cgi:150-152). With nothing stored, the HmIP side synthesises on READ: LinkUtil#getLinkInfo returns getDefaultName = "%s:%02d %s:%02d" (a space, zero-padded two-digit channel indices, no arrow) and the literal description "NO_DESCRIPTION".

Our AddLink always writes, and writes a different shape: name = `<sender> -> <receiver>` (unpadded channel numbers, an arrow separator), description = `created by openccu-loom`. The consequence is on the same operator-visible surface — what getLinkInfo returns after an unnamed link creation — so a link we create is distinguishable from one the WebUI created, and an operator-blank name is stored as a value rather than left absent. Note the two defaults also differ in kind: ours is persisted (surviving into linkData.conf / the rfd XML), the firmware's is computed per read and disappears the moment a real name is set.

Surface caveat: getDefaultName/"NO_DESCRIPTION" is the HmIP legacy API's read-side synthesis. On rfd there is no equivalent synthesis — an unnamed link's entry simply carries empty strings — so the firmware's two south-bound surfaces are not even consistent with each other. Matching either is a product decision, not a firmware constraint; what is settled is that no constraint exists to violate.
all.negativeControl: Had a length or charset limit existed, RFChannel::SetLinkInfo would have had to compare a size or copy into a fixed buffer before assigning (the same file does exactly that for numeric fields — `char buffer[16]` + snprintf in SaveToXml at RFChannel.cpp:1123), and LinkUtil#setLinkInfo would have had to validate before constructing LinkData. Both assign the caller's string unconditionally, so a limit would have been visible at the one place it could live. Had our concern about the empty-name path been unfounded, ic_ifacecmd.cgi would have computed and sent a name; instead it explicitly skips setLinkInfo when both fields are blank.
all.ourValue: name = "<sender> -> <receiver>" (unpadded channels), description = "created by openccu-loom", always written
all.firmwareValue: no length or charset constraint anywhere; nothing is written when the caller supplies no name. HmIP read-side default: name = String.format("%s:%02d %s:%02d", ...) (space-separated, zero-padded channel indices), description = "NO_DESCRIPTION".
all.challengeNote:
The half that matters for the audited concern is CONFIRMED and I re-verified it end to end. The supporting narrative is CONTRADICTED on the HmIP surface.

Confirmed — no constraint exists to violate. I followed rfd's write path from the RPC method to persistence: XmlRpcMethodAddLink -> RFManager::SetLinkInfo -> RFChannel::SetLinkInfo, which assigns two std::strings into the link_peers entry and requests a save; then SaveToXml writes name as an XML attribute and description as a child text node. There is no length measurement, no character filter, no truncation, no rejection at any of the four hops. The HmIP side is the same shape: LinkUtil#setLinkInfo puts a LinkData holding the raw Strings into a map and Jackson-serialises it. The hypothesis that the firmware silently truncates or rejects a long or non-ASCII link name is refuted — no code path could.

Contradicted — "the firmware never writes a default at all". The previous grounding built its whole divergence story on the premise that both firmware callers pass addLink two arguments, therefore nothing is stored, therefore the HmIP side synthesises getDefaultName/"NO_DESCRIPTION" on read. I checked what a 2-argument call actually becomes on the HmIP legacy surface and the premise fails.

XmlRpcParser#parseParams sizes its argument array from the TARGET METHOD's parameter count, not from the number of <param> elements on the wire, and fills only as many as the document supplies. Omitted trailing parameters arrive as Java null; the reflective invoke in AnnotationAwareRpcHandler#execute therefore succeeds rather than throwing on arity. So the WebUI's two-argument addLink reaches LegacyServiceHandler#addLink as addLink(sender, receiver, null, null) — and that method, on success, calls DeviceUtil.setLinkInfo(..., null, null) with no guard. LinkUtil#setLinkInfo then stores `new LinkData(null, null)` under both directional keys and saves linkData.conf.

Consequence: on HmIP the firmware DOES write on every addLink, and getLinkInfo subsequently finds that entry and returns nulls. getDefaultName and "NO_DESCRIPTION" are reached only for links with NO stored entry — links predating linkData.conf, or ones whose entry removeLinkInfo/removeAllLinkInfo deleted. They are not what an operator sees after creating a link through the WebUI. The "firmware value" column of the original finding is wrong on both halves.

What survives as the real divergence, restated per surface:
  - rfd (2000/2001): the `params.size()>=3` guard means a 2-argument addLink never calls SetLinkInfo, so the link_peers entry keeps its default-constructed empty strings, and GetLinkInfo returns them verbatim — I confirmed rfd has no read-side synthesis at all. Our AddLink always sends four arguments, so we store "A:1 -> B:2" / "created by openccu-loom" where the WebUI would have left ""/"".
  - HmIP (2010): both write. The firmware writes nulls, we write our synthesized strings.
Either way the operator-visible read-back differs, so the boundary conclusion (a link we create is distinguishable from a WebUI one; an operator-blank name becomes a stored value) stands — but not for the reason given, and the getDefaultName shape must not be cited as "what the firmware leaves for an unnamed link".

One further caveat the original left out: RFChannel::SaveToXml passes the name straight into addAttributeConst and the description into addTextConst. Whether that path escapes XML metacharacters is not something I established, so a link name containing a quote or an angle bracket is an open question — irrelevant for our generated name, which is ASCII address text, but relevant for an operator-supplied one that we forward unchanged.

all.title: DefaultBaseTemperature 18.0 is written into the device's unused slots
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:1017-1023 `<parameter id="TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_1">` … `<logical type="float" min="5.0" max="30.0" default="17.0" unit="°C"/>`; same file :1077-1092 `<parameter id="ENDTIME_MONDAY_5">` `<logical type="integer" min="5" max="1440" default="1440" unit="minutes"/>` and `<parameter id="TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_5">` `<logical type="float" min="5.0" max="30.0" default="17.0" unit="°C"/>` (slots 5..13 all default 1440 / 17.0; only the comfort points 2 and 4 default to 21.0); same pattern in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml and rf_cc_rt_dn_bom.xml (TEMPERATURE_*_13 default="17.0"); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.configparameter.ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues — `int endTime = 1440; double temperature = 17.0;` with overrides only for _1 (endTime 360), _2 (21.0 / 540 or 1320), _3 (endTime 1020), _4 (21.0 / 1320); #createWeekProgram builds each ConfigurationParameter with that default and bounds 5.0 / 30.0; witness ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:2579 `DEFAULT_CLIMATE_FILL_TEMPERATURE: Final = 18.0`
all.finding:
CONTRADICTED, on both climate surfaces, by 1.0 K.

Our constant is 18.0 and it does not stay read-side: RawToClimate stores it as the weekday's BaseTemperature, climateWeekdayToSlotsExpand fills every gap with it (rawconvert.go:396, :407) and fillUpWeekdaySlots pads the remaining slots to 13 with EndTime "24:00" and that same temperature (slot.go:121-133). Those padding slots are exactly the case the firmware declares a default for.

Classic BidCos (HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU): the padding slots — ENDTIME_<DAY>_5..13, whose own default is 1440 minutes, i.e. 24:00 — declare `default="17.0"` on TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_5..13, bounds min 5.0 / max 30.0 (rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:1077-1092 and the parallel blocks through slot 13). The factory profile is 17.0 at points 1 and 3, 21.0 at points 2 and 4, then 17.0 for every unused slot.

HmIP: ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues opens with `int endTime = 1440; double temperature = 17.0;` and overrides only points 1..4; every other slot of every weekday of every profile gets 17.0 / 1440, with the same 5.0/30.0 bounds. Byte-for-byte the same rule as the BidCos XML.

So the firmware's fill setpoint for an unconfigured climate slot is 17.0 °C; ours is 18.0 °C. A load-then-save on a weekday the reader could not decode writes 18.0 into slots the device would otherwise hold at 17.0 — a 1 K error written into the thermostat's MASTER paramset, on both transports.

The comment's own justification is accurate about provenance and wrong about authority: 18.0 is the Python reference's DEFAULT_CLIMATE_FILL_TEMPERATURE (aiohomematic/const.py:2579 — Tier 3, a witness), not a CCU value. Tier 1 and Tier 2 agree with each other and disagree with it. Our code should follow 17.0.

One boundary worth stating: the firmware value is a parameter DEFAULT (what the device declares and reverts to), while ours is a runtime fallback for an undecodable weekday. Those are the same role — 'what an unconfigured slot holds' — which is why the comparison is on the right surface; but the honest fix is to prefer the per-device declared DEFAULT read from the paramset description at runtime, and to use 17.0 only as the constant when no descriptor is at hand. Every shipped descriptor I checked declares 17.0, so the constant and the descriptor agree today.
all.negativeControl: Had 18.0 been the firmware's value, TEMPERATURE_MONDAY_5..13 in rf_cc_rt_dn.xml would have read default="18.0" and ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues would have initialised `temperature = 18.0`. The check is capable of returning 18.0 — the same files do carry a second, different default (21.0) for the comfort points, so the extraction distinguishes values rather than reporting one constant everywhere. Both independent sources returned 17.0.
all.ourValue: 18.0 °C (schedule.DefaultBaseTemperature), written into every gap and every padding slot 1..13
all.firmwareValue: 17.0 °C — TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_5..13 default="17.0" (ENDTIME default 1440), bounds 5.0/30.0, in rf_cc_rt_dn.xml / rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml; and `double temperature = 17.0; int endTime = 1440;` in ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory#getDefaultValues on the HmIP side
all.challengeNote:
The firmware number is CONFIRMED — I re-derived it by machine scan rather than trusting the quoted line range, and it is 17.0 at every padding ordinal on both surfaces. But three qualifications shrink the finding, and the middle one matters most.

(1) 18.0 is a failure fallback, not the normal fill. The original states our value as "18.0, written into every gap and every padding slot 1..13". That overstates. DefaultBaseTemperature has exactly two production readers (climate.go:304 and :333), both inside IdentifyBaseTemperature / IdentifyBaseTemperatureFromSegments, and both fire only when the weekday yields no usable stretch. On every normal round-trip the fill is cwd.BaseTemperature = the temperature that actually dominates the day as read off the device, and 18.0 never appears. So the exposure is the degenerate case — an empty or undecodable weekday map — not the ordinary load-then-save the original implies.

(2) The comparand is a DECLARED DEFAULT, not device state. The original's boundary paragraph names this and its own damage sentence then crosses it: "writes 18.0 into slots the device would otherwise hold at 17.0". A `default=` attribute in the type XML, and ClimateCalendarConfigurationParameterFactory's `temperature`, are what getParamsetDescription advertises as DEFAULT and what a factory reset restores. Neither tells us what a given thermostat currently holds in slot 9 — that is whatever was last written to it. The honest statement is: our fallback disagrees with the value the descriptor declares for those slots by 1.0 K. Whether that constitutes a 1 K error written into a device depends on what the device held, which no descriptor can answer.

(3) 17.0 is ordinal-dependent. The original generalises to "the firmware's fill setpoint for an unconfigured climate slot is 17.0". Ordinals 5..13 do declare 17.0 uniformly — 63 parameters on HM-CC-RT-DN, 189 on HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU, all with min 5.0 / max 30.0 — but ordinal 2 declares 21.0 on all seven days and ordinal 4 declares 21.0 on the five weekdays. Our fill is applied to gaps as well as to padding, and a gap fill can land at ordinal 2 or 4. So the comparison is exact for the padding slots and not for a gap that lands early.

One citation hygiene note. "TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_5..13 ... in rf_tc_it_wm-w-eu.xml" is right in substance and wrong as written: the identifiers in that file are P1_/P2_/P3_-prefixed. A reader following the citation with a literal grep finds nothing (I did, first pass). The HmIP factory names them the same way. Also, the original's paraphrase of getDefaultValues ("overrides only for _1, _2, _3, _4") flattens a real branch — SATURDAY/SUNDAY and week programs 2 and 3 override only _1 and _2, which is exactly why the XML shows 17.0 at ordinal 4 on two of seven days.

Provenance is correct and worth keeping: 18.0 is the Python reference's DEFAULT_CLIMATE_FILL_TEMPERATURE (Tier 3, a witness), and Tier 1 and Tier 2 both say 17.0. The recommendation to prefer the per-parameter DEFAULT read from the paramset description at runtime, with a constant only as last resort, is the right shape — and the descriptor does carry DEFAULT, so it is performable.

all.title: sameDescription ignores the CCU's own VERSION field, the descriptor's declared paramset-change signal
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/device.xsd:1480-1484 `<xsd:attribute name="version" type="xsd:int" default="0" use="optional">` with the annotation "Version der XML-Datei. Muss hochgezählt werden, damit Änderungen an die Logikschicht weitergegeben werden."; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDeviceDescription.cpp:34 `version=0;`, :137-138 `temp=node.getAttribute("version"); if(temp)version=strtol(temp, NULL, 0);`, :201 `team_description->version=version;` — the only three assignments in the file, all at parse/copy time; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDeviceDescription.h:123 `inline int GetVersion(){return version;};`, :249 `int version;`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:247 `dev_desc["VERSION"]=GetDeviceDescription()->GetVersion();`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:982 `(*descr)["VERSION"]=GetDevice()->GetDeviceDescription()->GetVersion();`; ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485DeviceDescription.cpp:32,101-102 (identical pattern for BidCos-Wired); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/rftypes/rf_cc_rt_dn.xml:3 `<device version="29" …>`; HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil (device: `deviceDescription.setVersion(device.getDeviceDescription().getVersion())`; channel: `int typeVersion = device.getDeviceDescription().getVersion(); if (channel.getStateParameter("PRESS_LONG") != null) { typeVersion += 10; } channelDescription.setVersion(typeVersion);`); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.VirtualRemoteControl (`this.deviceDescription.setVersion(1)`, `channelDescription.setVersion(1)`); Tier 2: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json — all 2924 description entries carry VERSION, none omits it; values are small integers (0 ×1267, 1 ×849, 2 ×247, 4 ×146, 3 ×91, 11 ×79, …)
all.finding:
The hmproto comment is wrong about what VERSION is; the sameDescription field set is defensible but has one real gap.

What VERSION actually is: the version attribute of the `<device>` root node in the device-type XML the firmware ships. device.xsd:1480-1484 documents it in the CCU's own words — "Version der XML-Datei. Muss hochgezählt werden, damit Änderungen an die Logikschicht weitergegeben werden" (version of the XML file; must be incremented so changes are propagated to the logic layer). rfd reads it once at parse time (RFDeviceDescription.cpp:137-138) into an int that is never reassigned afterwards — the file's only other writes are the constructor's `version=0` (:34) and the team-description copy (:201) — and echoes it into every device and channel description (RFDevice.cpp:247, RFChannel.cpp:982). hs485d is identical (HS485DeviceDescription.cpp:101-102). On the HmIP side DeviceUtil sets the device's VERSION from the device-TYPE description's version, and a channel's to that same type version plus a fixed +10 when the channel exposes PRESS_LONG.

So VERSION is CONSTANT for a given (device type, CCU firmware image). It does not move when a device's paramsets change at runtime — not on re-pair, not on channel reconfiguration, not on a device firmware update (that shows in FIRMWARE, which sameDescription already compares). pkg/hmproto/device.go's 'a per-device schema version bumped by the CCU when paramsets change' is contradicted on both counts: it is per device TYPE, not per device, and it is bumped by eQ-3 shipping a new descriptor XML, not by the CCU observing a change.

The second half of that comment — 'missing for older firmwares' — is unsupported by anything I read: the xsd marks the attribute optional with default 0, so a type XML that omits it yields VERSION 0 rather than an absent key, and across the 2924-entry pydevccu descriptor corpus (Tier 2) not one entry omits VERSION. The most common values, 0 and 1, are what an omitted-or-fresh XML attribute produces, and the 79 entries at 11 are 1+10, matching DeviceUtil's PRESS_LONG rule exactly — an independent cross-check that the corpus really carries the type version and not a counter.

Consequence for sameDescription: because VERSION tracks the shipped descriptor, comparing TYPE + FIRMWARE + PARENT + CHILDREN misses exactly one case — a CCU firmware upgrade that ships a new device-type XML for an already-paired device. TYPE and FIRMWARE are unchanged, CHILDREN usually are too, and VERSION is the one field that moves; that is precisely the propagation signal the xsd annotation describes. Adding VERSION to sameDescription would close it. What it would NOT do is give the coordinator a 'paramsets changed on this device' signal — no field in a DeviceDescription carries that, so a future re-hydrate decision cannot be built on VERSION however the comment is worded.

I could not verify the intended consumer side: ReGaHss is a closed binary and the Tcl layer under src/tclrega / src/tclrpc never reads a description VERSION, so which CCU component acts on the bump is unverified.
all.negativeControl: Had VERSION been a runtime counter, RFDeviceDescription.cpp would have contained at least one increment or assignment outside the constructor and the XML parse (a `version++` on a paramset write, a bump in RequestSave or in the link/config-change paths); grep over the file's `version =` sites returns exactly three, none of them runtime. And had it been per device instance rather than per type, DeviceUtil would have read it from the device object rather than from device.getDeviceDescription() — the same method does read per-instance values right beside it (getFirmwareVersion, getAvailableFirmwareVersion, getUpdateState), so the distinction was observable and came out the other way. For the 'missing for older firmwares' claim the control is the corpus: a single descriptor entry without a VERSION key would have shown it; 0 of 2924 do.
all.ourValue: pkg/hmproto/device.go:94-96 — VERSION is "a per-device schema version bumped by the CCU when paramsets change; missing for older firmwares"; sameDescription compares TYPE, FIRMWARE, PARENT, CHILDREN only
all.firmwareValue: VERSION is the `version` attribute of the device-type XML's `<device>` node (device.xsd:1480-1484: "Version der XML-Datei. Muss hochgezählt werden, damit Änderungen an die Logikschicht weitergegeben werden"), parsed once and never mutated at runtime; HmIP channels report that type version +10 when the channel has PRESS_LONG. Never absent in the descriptor corpus (0/2924 missing); defaults to 0 when the XML omits it.
all.challengeNote:
The primary contradiction STANDS and I re-verified every Tier-1 and Tier-2 citation myself, including the histogram (2924 entries, 0 missing, identical counts). But the grounding's one piece of independent corroboration is FALSE, and one sub-claim is not-performable from these sources.

Upheld. VERSION is the type XML's `version` attribute. device.xsd:1480-1484 documents it in the CCU's own words as the version of the XML FILE, to be incremented so changes propagate to the logic layer. rfd reads it once at parse time into an int with no later reassignment anywhere in the file, and echoes it into both device and channel descriptions; hs485d is identical. So VERSION is constant for a given (device type, CCU firmware image): it does not move on re-pair, on channel reconfiguration, or on a device firmware update — that last one shows in FIRMWARE, which sameDescription already compares. "A per-device schema version bumped by the CCU when paramsets change" is wrong on both halves — per TYPE, not per device; bumped by eQ-3 shipping a new XML, not by the CCU observing anything. The consequential point also stands: no field in a DeviceDescription carries a "this device's paramsets changed" signal, so a re-hydrate decision cannot be built on VERSION however the comment is reworded.

Refuted — the "independent cross-check". The grounding wrote: "the 79 entries at 11 are 1+10, matching DeviceUtil's PRESS_LONG rule exactly — an independent cross-check that the corpus really carries the type version and not a counter." I partitioned those 79 by surface. 56 are HmIP channels (consistent with the +10 rule). 17 are DEVICE-level entries of BidCos types — HM-RC-Sec3, HM-RC-Sec3-B, HM-RC-P1, HM-RC-4, HM-RC-X, HM-PB-4-WM, HM-LC-Dim1PWM-CV, HMW-LC-Dim1L-DR and others — which have no PARENT, so there is no "1" for the +10 to have been added to. The remaining 6 are BidCos channels. DeviceUtil's PRESS_LONG rule lives in HMIPServer and runs only on HmIP channel descriptions; it cannot touch a BidCos device entry at all. Wrong surface for 23 of 79.

And the direct disproof: rf_rc.xml — the type file covering the HM-RC-Sec3 family — opens `<device version="11" rx_modes="CONFIG" peering_sysinfo_expect_channel="false" supports_aes="true">`. The 11 is the XML's own version attribute, read verbatim. The numeric coincidence 11 = 1 + 10 was doing the work of an argument. The conclusion it was offered to support happens to be correct — but it was supported by the Tier-1 parse chain, never by the histogram, and the corroboration should be struck rather than repeated.

Narrowed — "missing for older firmwares". The grounding called this unsupported. That is right for descriptions generated by these two servers: the xsd marks the attribute optional with default 0 so an omitting XML yields VERSION 0, DeviceUtil always calls setVersion, and 0 of 2924 corpus entries omit the key. But hmproto.DeviceDescription is decoded from every south-bound interface we speak to, and neither CUxD nor Homegear is in either reference tree. Whether those emit VERSION is not measurable here, so `Version *int` being a pointer is not thereby shown to be dead defensive typing. The honest scope is: no CCU-generated description omits VERSION; nothing is known about the third-party interfaces.

The recommendation (add VERSION to sameDescription to catch a CCU firmware upgrade that ships a new type XML for an already-paired device) follows from the xsd annotation and is sound as a hypothesis about intent. Its consumer side remains unverified in those words: ReGaHss is a closed binary and nothing under src/tclrega or src/tclrpc reads a description VERSION, so which component acts on the bump is unknown.

all.title: Coalescing key joins arguments with ':' — the same separator CCU channel addresses use
all.ourValue: key = method + ":" + arg1 + ":" + arg2 …; the reader's premise is that ':' appears only as the device/channel separator, so the join is unambiguous
all.firmwareValue: Parameter IDs never contain ':' — but a paramset key legally does: the firmware's own doc for getParamset/putParamset says paramset_key is "MASTER", "VALUES" oder die Adresse eines Kommunikationspartners (a peer channel address, SERIAL:CHANNEL)
all.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:188 and :220 (putParamset / getParamset doc: paramset_key may be a link-peer address); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:299-308 (RFManager::ParseAddress splits on address.find(':') — the FIRST colon, so a serial cannot contain one). Tier 2: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml — 0 of 2181 <parameter … id="…"> declarations contain ':' (and no id= attribute anywhere in either tree does); ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json — 0 of 53792 keys contain ':'. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.StateParameterAbbreviation carries no colon-bearing parameter name.
all.finding: Our code is safe today, but not for the reason the comment implies. Firmware answer to the reader's question, split in two: (a) a CCU parameter ID cannot contain ':' — measured across every shipped device XML and the descriptor corpus, and the address grammar itself forbids it in a serial, since ParseAddress takes everything after the first colon as the channel via atoi(); (b) a paramset key CAN contain ':', because the LINK paramset is addressed by the peer's channel address — that is not folklore, it is written in the firmware's own method documentation at XmlRpcMethods.cpp:188/:220. So the ambiguity source the reader worried about is real in the CCU's argument vocabulary. It is unreachable at the only production call site, which passes exactly one argument (address) to MakeCoalesceKey("getDeviceDescription", …): with one argument the key is method+":"+address, injective in address. The boundary runs at the second argument — the first caller that coalesces getParamset/putParamset/getParamsetDescription by (address, paramsetKey) puts two colon-bearing values on either side of a colon separator. I could not construct a *legal* collision even then (address is SERIAL[:CHANNEL] and key is MASTER|VALUES|SERIAL:CHANNEL, and no re-split of a joined pair yields two legal values), so the correct statement is: no demonstrated collision, and the invariant that prevents one is a property of the address/key grammar, not of the join. If a guard is wanted, it belongs on the arity of the caller, not on the key format.
all.negativeControl: Had a CCU parameter ID contained ':', the grep over the 2181 shipped <parameter id="…"> declarations would have returned a non-zero count and named the device XML; it returned 0. Conversely, had paramset keys been restricted to MASTER/VALUES, XmlRpcMethods.cpp would not name a communication partner's address as a legal paramset_key — it does, twice, so the check does distinguish the two halves of the question.
all.challengeNote:
Grounding upheld as narrowed — every citation reproduces, and both Tier-2 counts re-ran to the same numbers. Two corrections to the finding, one of which moves the boundary.

(1) The comment does not make the claim being graded. coalesce.go:113-120 says only that method and args are joined with ':' separators; it asserts nothing about CCU addresses. So there is no comment claim here to confirm or contradict — the rule grounds a latent hazard, and that should be said plainly rather than attributed to "the reader's premise".

(2) The named boundary is wrong. The prior finding says the hazard opens at "the first caller that coalesces getParamset/putParamset by (address, paramsetKey)". It cannot: our backend contract types the key as `hmenum.ParamsetKey` (backends/backend.go:228, master_poll.go:51), a closed enum of seven colon-free constants (pkg/hmenum/paramset.go:13-19), none of which is a peer address. A colon-bearing paramset key is unrepresentable on the path a coalescing caller would use, at any arity. The real boundary is narrower and different: a caller that passes a raw `string` key (or any other free-form colon-bearing value) instead of the enum. A guard, if wanted, belongs there — not on arity, and not on the key format.

What the firmware genuinely settles: (a) parameter IDs are colon-free across the entire shipped descriptor corpus and the address grammar forbids a colon in a serial; (b) LINK paramsets ARE addressed by a peer channel address — that is the firmware's own documentation at three sites, not folklore. Both stand. No collision is demonstrated, and the derivation that none is constructible from *legal* values is sound but is a derivation, not a reading — label it as such.

all.title: The 3-request concurrency cap on the CCU webserver is an operational observation
all.ourValue: 3 in-flight requests per JSON-RPC client, justified as "3 concurrent sessions is the safe operational limit observed in practice"
all.firmwareValue: No per-connection or per-session request cap exists in the readable CCU source. lighttpd: server.max-connections = 1024, server.max-fds = 2048, server.max-worker commented out, server.max-keep-alive-requests = 50. /api/ is served by mod_cgi (one forked tclsh per request), not proxied, and carries no lock.
all.missingInput: The numeric concurrent-session limit enforced by ReGaHss — the only concurrency cap the firmware documents. ReGaHss ships as a compiled binary; the value is in neither OpenCCU-Base nor the OpenCCU overlays. Also missing: whether the CCU's instability under higher concurrency was ever attributed to a limit at all, rather than to CPU/memory pressure from N forked tclsh processes.
all.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf:132 (#server.max-worker = 4, commented), :220 (server.max-fds = 2048), :238 (server.max-connections = 1024), :253 (server.max-keep-alive-requests = 50); .../conf.d/cgi.conf:2 (cgi.assign ".cgi" => "/bin/tclsh"); .../conf.d/webui.conf:11 (the proxy rule explicitly excludes ^/api/, so homematic.cgi runs locally as CGI); ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/homematic.cgi (215 lines, no flock/lock/semaphore) and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/*.tcl (same); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/tcl/eq3/session.tcl:42-43 and :56-57 — session_login maps HTTP 503 from login.htm to error "create", documented as "falls keine Session-Id erstellt werden konnte (z.B.: zu viele gleichzeitige Sitzungen)".
all.finding: The CCU source does not decide this number. What the firmware does carry is a cap on concurrent *sessions*, enforced by ReGaHss: login.htm answers 503 and the WebUI's own Tcl client turns that into a create failure, with the comment naming "too many concurrent sessions" as the cause. That cap is a different quantity from what DefaultMaxConcurrent bounds — our constant limits in-flight HTTP requests within a single JSON-RPC client, and every one of those requests carries the same _session_id_ (client.go:35-36), so they are one session however many are in flight. The comment's wording "3 concurrent sessions" therefore mislabels the constant on top of resting on an unsourced observation. On the transport itself the firmware is permissive: 1024 connections, 2048 fds, one forked tclsh per request with no serialisation anywhere in the CGI or its helper Tcl. The real ceiling is process/CPU pressure on the CCU from N concurrent tclsh interpreters plus the single ReGaHss behind them — a load property, not a documented limit, and not something these trees quantify. Our 3 rests on operational observation alone; that is a legitimate basis, but the comment should say so and should stop calling them sessions.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware carried a request-concurrency cap on this path, it would appear as a lighttpd directive (server.max-connections, server.max-worker, or a per-host connection limit) or as a lock/serialisation in homematic.cgi. max-connections is 1024 — three orders of magnitude above 3 — max-worker is commented out, and the grep for flock/lock/semaphore/exclusive across homematic.cgi and www/api/eq3/*.tcl returns nothing. The check does produce a different answer when a cap exists: it found one, in session.tcl, for sessions.

all.title: The callback mux answers an unknown CCU probe with the JSON-RPC code -32601 on an XML-RPC surface
all.ourValue: "the CCU treats an absent signature as 'any types accepted' and never inspects the contents" (methodSignature), "the CCU only checks existence, not content" (methodHelp), and -32601 chosen "as the closest standardised codepoint" for a method-not-found probe
all.firmwareValue: The CCU never calls system.methodSignature — the string does not occur anywhere in ../OpenCCU-Base. It never calls system.methodHelp on a callback either. It calls system.listMethods exactly once, at callback registration, and inspects the result solely for the presence of "replaceDevice". No CCU code path reads a fault code returned by a callback.
all.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libhsscomm/HSSManager.cpp:255 (XmlRpcCallSync("system.listMethods", …) inside PlatformInit — the sole caller in the tree), :256/:263-266 (result scanned only for methname.compare("replaceDevice")), :322 (supportReplaceDevice decides replaceDevice vs deleteDevices), :132-144 (XmlRpcCallSync tests only c.isFault() and logs result->toText(); the code number is never extracted); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:575 (parseResponse sets the boolean _isFault and parses the fault struct as a value, no faultCode branch); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServer.cpp:218-219, :271-277 (listMethods/methodHelp exist only as methods the CCU *offers*; no methodSignature at all). Tree-wide grep for "methodSignature" over ../OpenCCU-Base returns zero files. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyBackendClient exposes exactly event, listDevices, newDevices, deleteDevices, updateDevice, replaceDevice, readdedDevice, multicall and firmwareUpdateStatusChanged toward a registered callback — no system.* probe; and HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.InterfaceInitializer#handle registers an interface via DeviceUtil#synchronizedBackendDevices, which goes straight to listDevices, never to listMethods. HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcParser does parse faultCode into an RpcRemoteException, but no caller in the legacy notification path branches on getFaultCode().
all.finding: Both comment claims are contradicted, though the code itself is harmless. (1) -32601 is safe for the stated purpose but not for the stated reason: no CCU path compares a fault code from a callback. rfd/hs485d only test the boolean isFault() and log the fault struct's rendered text; the HmIP side parses faultCode into an exception object that the legacy path never inspects. Any code would do; -32601 is not "what the CCU expects", because the CCU expects nothing. (2) The methodSignature comment asserts a CCU behaviour that does not exist — the CCU never issues that call, on either the BidCos or the HmIP callback surface. Same for methodHelp: it is a method the CCU *implements* on its own surface, never one it calls on ours. (3) The one probe the CCU does make is the one the comments say nothing about, and it has a real consequence: HSSManager::PlatformInit calls system.listMethods on the callback URL during registration and scans the returned array for "replaceDevice"; a missing entry sets supportReplaceDevice=false, after which a replaced device arrives as deleteDevices + newDevices instead of replaceDevice. We do register "replaceDevice" (internal/central/rpcserver/xmlrpc_server.go:415), so this is currently correct — but it is the claim worth pinning, and it is load-bearing in a way -32601 is not. Note the answer must be an array: a fault or any non-array from listMethods silently yields supportReplaceDevice=false and registration continues regardless (HSSManager.cpp:258-270).
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU probed methodSignature, the string would occur somewhere in the CCU sources — the tree-wide grep over ../OpenCCU-Base returns zero files, while the same grep for "system.listMethods" returns exactly two hits and one of them is a live caller. Had a fault code been inspected, XmlRpcCallSync or XmlRpcClient would extract result["faultCode"] and compare it; both only set/inspect a boolean. The check demonstrably distinguishes the two cases: it found the one probe that does exist and the one place the fault is examined, and both fell the other way from our comment.
all.challengeNote:
Contradicted, upheld — and I extended the search past where the prior agent stopped, which strengthened rather than weakened it. Three checks I added:

(a) methodSignature. The prior claim was scoped to ../OpenCCU-Base. I grepped both HmIP server components as well: zero occurrences anywhere. The comment at mux.go:110-111 asserts a CCU behaviour that exists on no surface.

(b) methodHelp. Not merely "implemented, never called" — it IS called, by ../OpenCCU-Base/src/webui/www/tools/devconfig.cgi, but toward `$interfaces($iface)`, i.e. the interface daemon's own XML-RPC surface, not toward a registered callback. That is the wrong-surface trap this series keeps catching, and it lands on the prior finding's side: the call exists, it just is not on our path. The comment at mux.go:105 is still contradicted.

(c) A near-miss I chased and cleared: `RpcClient.listMethods()` exists as a client capability in both HmIP components (`new RpcRequest(method, "system.listMethods")`), and `IRegaServer` declares @RpcMethod("system.listMethods") and @RpcMethod("system.methodHelp") as a proxy toward ReGa. Neither is a callback probe: `grep -rn '\.listMethods()'` finds no invocation of the client method anywhere in either tree, and IRegaServer's target is ReGa, not us. Recording this so a later grep does not appear to overturn the finding.

The prior finding's positive claim also holds and is the one worth pinning: HSSManager::PlatformInit probes the callback URL with system.listMethods and scans the array for "replaceDevice"; a fault, a non-array, or a missing entry all silently yield supportReplaceDevice=false, after which a replaced device arrives as deleteDevices + newDevices. We register it (xmlrpc_server.go:415), so this is correct today and is load-bearing in a way -32601 is not.

One shape constraint the prior finding missed: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRpcParser reads the fault struct as `(Integer) errorStruct.get("faultCode")` with no null guard. The *value* is indeed never inspected — but the *member* must be present and integer-typed or the HmIP side throws while parsing our fault. Our faults always carry an int code, so this is a constraint on the struct shape, not on the number.

all.title: XML-RPC bodies are transcoded to ISO-8859-1 unconditionally, so a non-Latin-1 device name fails the whole call
all.ourValue: charmap.ISO8859_1 encoder on every outbound body, prolog encoding="ISO-8859-1", Content-Type charset=ISO-8859-1; a rune above U+00FF fails at encode time
all.firmwareValue: ISO-8859-1 on all three south-bound XML-RPC surfaces, and the declared encoding is never read: BidCos parses the body as raw bytes; HmIP and VirtualDevices force a configured encoding into the StAX reader, overriding the prolog
all.citation: Tier 1, BidCos (rfd :2001→:32001, hs485d :2000→:32000, both libXmlRpc): ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:24 and :414 (emits <?xml version="1.0" encoding="iso-8859-1"?> and Content-Type: text/xml; charset=iso-8859-1); XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:366, :388, :414 (same on the server side); XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:105-112 (readHeader scans only for "Content-length: ", "Connection: " and the header terminator — the charset parameter and the request URI are never read); XmlRpcUtil.cpp:135-144 and :217 (nextTagIs / xmlDecode operate on std::string bytes; the prolog is skipped as an ordinary tag, its encoding attribute never inspected). Tree-wide grep for "encoding|charset" in libXmlRpc yields three hits, all emission sites, none in a parse path. VirtualDevices (:9292→:39292): HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer constructs both RpcMessageHandlers with the literal "ISO-8859-1". HmIP-RF (:2010→:32010): HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.AbstractLegacyAPIWorker reads the encoding from ServiceProperties key "Legacy.Encoding" (code default "UTF-8") and passes it to HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.communication.rpc.internal.format.xml.XmlRequestResponseProcessor#parseRequest → XmlRpcParser, whose constructor calls XMLInputFactory#createXMLStreamReader(InputStream, String) — the two-argument form, which takes the encoding from the caller and does not consult the XML declaration. The shipped value is pinned by ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:15 "Legacy.Encoding=ISO-8859-1" (same file, :25, pins Legacy.Port=32010, which is exactly the proxy target in ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/lighttpd/conf.d/webui_remoteapi.conf:74).
all.finding: Confirmed, and the firmware is stronger than the comment claims: not one of the three surfaces reads the encoding we declare. On BidCos the parser is a hand-written byte scanner — a UTF-8 body would not be *rejected*, it would be accepted and stored byte-for-byte, then rendered as Latin-1 downstream. That is silent corruption, which is worse than the encode-time error we produce. On HmIP and VirtualDevices the declared encoding is overridden by a configured constant before the first byte is decoded. So sending a UTF-8-declared body buys nothing anywhere and corrupts on one surface; our unconditional transcode is the right behaviour, and the failure on a rune above U+00FF is the CCU's own representational ceiling, not a self-inflicted restriction. Which source to follow: Tier 1, the firmware constant — not any per-request declaration, because none is read. One boundary worth recording: on the HmIP surface alone the encoding is a *configuration* value, not a compiled-in one. Its code default is UTF-8; only the shipped crRFD.conf overrides it to ISO-8859-1. An operator who edits Legacy.Encoding=UTF-8 in /etc/config/crRFD.conf would make our bodies mis-decode for every byte ≥ 0x80 on HmIP-RF while BidCos and VirtualDevices stayed correct. OpenCCU does not ship that, and nothing in our config surface exposes it — but it is the one configuration under which this rule is false, and it belongs in the comment.
all.negativeControl: Had any surface honoured the declared encoding, it would show as an inspection of the prolog or the Content-Type charset in a parse path — libXmlRpc has three encoding/charset occurrences and all three are writes, none a read — and HMIPServer would call the one-argument XMLInputFactory#createXMLStreamReader(InputStream), which lets StAX auto-detect from the declaration; it calls the two-argument form instead. The check distinguishes the cases: the two-argument form is exactly the API shape that ignores the prolog, and the one-argument form is exactly the shape that honours it.
all.challengeNote:
The rule itself is confirmed and every citation reproduces verbatim; I am demoting to narrowed because the finding's stated boundary is half wrong and its load-bearing step is not a firmware reading.

Upheld: the outbound leg. Not one of the three surfaces reads the encoding we declare on a request — BidCos by byte-scanning (readHeader never touches the charset parameter; findTag/nextTagIs skip the prolog as an ordinary tag), HmIP and VirtualDevices by forcing a configured constant into the reader. Our unconditional transcode is right, and the failure above U+00FF is the CCU's representational ceiling.

Narrowing 1 — the leg the finding omits. The response/notification direction is NOT symmetric. HMIPServer's XmlRpcSerializer opens every request and response with `writeStartDocument(encoding, "1.0")`, so the CCU declares its configured encoding on the wire, and our decoder honours declarations (message.go:188-192, `d.CharsetReader = charset.NewReaderLabel`). Inbound is therefore correct under any Legacy.Encoding. The prior finding's operator scenario ("our bodies mis-decode for every byte ≥ 0x80 on HmIP-RF") is true only outbound, and the comment should say which direction it governs.

Narrowing 2 — a convention smuggled into the boundary. "The two-argument form takes the encoding from the caller and does not consult the XML declaration" was not read from any eQ-3 source; it is a property of the StAX implementation. If it were false, an operator setting Legacy.Encoding=UTF-8 would still decode our ISO-8859-1 bodies correctly, because our prolog says ISO-8859-1 — and the boundary would evaporate. That sub-claim is unverified in those words, and only Tier-1 evidence about the shipped JRE's XMLInputFactory, or a wire test against a CCU with Legacy.Encoding=UTF-8, would settle it. The rule's main body does not depend on it.

Two transcription corrections. (i) "Tree-wide grep for encoding|charset in libXmlRpc yields three hits" is wrong: there are five emission sites (client 24, 414; serverconnection 366, 388, 414) plus three unrelated comment hits in XmlRpcValue.cpp:907,1318 and XmlRpcUtil.cpp:207. The conclusion — none in a parse path — is correct. (ii) "a UTF-8 body would be accepted byte-for-byte and rendered as Latin-1 downstream" is an inference from the byte-scanner's shape, not a measurement; it should be labelled as such.

One genuine addition for the comment: the shipped HmIP config also pins the *outbound* encoding — LegacyNotificationHandler reads the same Legacy.Encoding for what it sends us — so a single operator edit moves both legs at once.

all.title: The per-interface XML-RPC default paths (/RPC2, /groups) are documented in config but sourced nowhere
all.site: internal/config/config.go:67-70 (RemotePath doc); the real table is internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:1567-1580
all.ourValue: "/RPC2" for HmIP-RF / BidCos-RF / BidCos-Wired, "/groups" for VirtualDevices, described as the path each interface serves XML-RPC on
all.firmwareValue: /RPC2 is the CCU's XML-RPC *client-side* default URI, not a server route. Three of the four interfaces ignore the request path entirely; only VirtualDevices routes by path, where /groups (and /bidcos) are real routes and anything else gets HTTP 404 with the connection closed. All four external ports are lighttpd reverse proxies selected by $SERVER["socket"] — by port, never by path.
all.citation: Tier 1: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcClient.cpp:67, :74, :96, :117 (_uri = "/RPC2" whenever the target URL carries no path — this is the client default; a tree-wide grep for "RPC2" over ../OpenCCU-Base matches this one file and nothing else); ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:105-112 (readHeader parses only Content-length, Connection and the header terminator; the request URI is never stored or compared — this is the server for both rfd/BidCos-RF and hs485d/BidCos-Wired); HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.LegacyApiServerUtil#startHttpServer (installs a bare requestHandler on Legacy.Port, default 2010, with no Router) feeding HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle (forwards the body on the event bus; the path is not read); HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.BaseHMServer#initializeHttpServer (route("/bidcos") and route("/groups") on the HM server port, plus a routeWithRegex(".*") catch-all returning 404 and closing the connection) with HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.Constants#GROUP_CONTEXT = "/groups", #BIDCOS_CONTEXT = "/bidcos", #DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT = 9292; ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/lighttpd/conf.d/webui_remoteapi.conf:70 (:2010→:32010), :94 (:9292→:39292), :118 (:2001→:32001), :142 (:2000→:32000) — every rule keyed on $SERVER["socket"] with proxy.server = ( "" => … ), i.e. all paths forwarded unchanged.
all.finding: Our table works, and it agrees with the client code it documents (config.go:67-70 matches ccu_wiring.go:1572-1575 exactly — the doc comment is not drifting from the implementation). But the framing — "which URL path each CCU interface serves XML-RPC on" — is only a real constraint for one of the four. /RPC2 is not a route anywhere in the CCU: it is the default URI libXmlRpc fills in when an outbound URL has no path, which is why every Homematic client has used it for twenty years. On BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired the server never looks at the request line's URI at all; on HmIP-RF the legacy XML-RPC server is a bare Vert.x requestHandler with no Router, so any path reaches the handler. VirtualDevices is the exception and the boundary: HMServer registers /groups and /bidcos and terminates everything else with a 404 and a connection close, so a wrong remote_path there takes the interface down hard — which is why reachesDevice is true: nothing written to a group or virtual device reaches the CCU. Two things an operator reading this comment should be told and currently is not: (a) an override on the three /RPC2 interfaces cannot break routing, because there is no routing — the failure mode the comment warns about does not exist there; (b) on VirtualDevices there is a second XML-RPC surface, /bidcos, on the same port, which our table does not mention. Also worth recording for the operator-facing rationale: the CCU already *is* the reverse-proxied case the comment imagines — every port we connect to (2000/2001/2010/9292 and their 4xxxx TLS twins) is lighttpd forwarding to a 3xxxx internal port, and lighttpd selects on the socket, not the path.
all.negativeControl: Had the three /RPC2 interfaces routed by path, a comparison of the request URI against "/RPC2" would exist on a server path; the tree-wide grep over ../OpenCCU-Base finds "RPC2" in XmlRpcClient.cpp only, and LegacyApiServerUtil passes no Router. The control fires the other way for VirtualDevices, which is what makes it a control rather than an absence argument: there the route literal, the Constants entry and the 404 catch-all are all present and all found by the same searches.
all.challengeNote:
Narrowed, upheld — every citation reproduces exactly, including the four lighttpd line numbers and the fact that "RPC2" appears in precisely one file in the whole tree. The framing correction stands: /RPC2 is a client default, not a route; the failure mode the comment warns about exists only on VirtualDevices, where a wrong path yields 404 + connection close and takes the interface down; and /bidcos is a second XML-RPC surface on that same port that our table omits.

What the prior agent missed, and it is the more consequential half of the same comment block: config.go:72-73 also asserts that "the bare '/' is rejected because POSTing to it crashes the CCU's putParamset handler", ccu_wiring.go:1569-1571 elaborates it as "Vert.x NPE or fault -5 while reads still succeed", and config.go:154 ships it to operators as a validation error string ("the CCU's putParamset handler crashes on it; name the real endpoint path"). No Tier-1 surface supports that mechanism. On BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired the request URI is never read (XmlRpcServerConnection.cpp:103-114), so no path can select a different handler and "/" is indistinguishable from "/RPC2". On HmIP-RF the legacy server has no Router at all, so "/" reaches BasicAPIHttpVertxHandler#handle unchanged. On VirtualDevices — the only Vert.x surface that routes, and therefore the only place the named mechanism could live — "/" falls to `routeWithRegex(".*")`, which returns 404 and closes the connection: not a crash, not a fault -5, and reads do not survive it either. So the stated mechanism is contradicted on all four surfaces; whether some empirical crash was once observed I cannot rule out, and that residue is unverified. As written the comment names a cause that cannot occur and a symptom asymmetry (writes break, reads succeed) that the routing surface does not produce. The validator's behaviour may well be worth keeping; its stated reason is not.

Also worth recording for the operator-facing rationale, and correct as the prior agent had it: the CCU already is the reverse-proxied case the comment imagines — 2000/2001/2010/9292 and their 4xxxx TLS twins are all lighttpd forwarding to 3xxxx internal ports, selected on the socket, never the path.

all.title: "HmIP-Wired devices are classified by the model-name prefix hmipw-" is a config-side claim about another package's rule
all.citation: Interface vocabulary: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/ipc.tcl:40-71 (ipc_loadInterfacesFromFile parses only <ipc><name>/<url>/<info> out of /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml) feeding ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/homematic.cgi:53 (`array set INTERFACE_LIST [ipc_getInterfaces]`); every Interface.* call resolves the name there or dies at ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/dispatch.tcl:159 `jsonrpc_error 500 "unknown interface ($interfaceName)"`. Shipped list: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/config_templates/InterfacesList.xml (exactly BidCos-RF xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001, VirtualDevices xmlrpc://127.0.0.1:39292/groups, HmIP-RF xmlrpc://127.0.0.1:32010). Only other writer: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485dLoader/hs485dLoader.cpp:229-240 (inserts `<name>BidCos-Wired</name>`). One HmIP legacy endpoint: ../OpenCCU-Base/etc/config_templates/crRFD.conf:28 `Legacy.Port=32010`; HomeMatic IP Wired is handled inside that same process — HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.lib.hmiptrxcommadapter.HomeMaticIpWiredFrame, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.otau.handler.WiredUnicastHandler, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.lib.hmiptrxcommadapter.internal.LowLevelMacWiredSubsystem. Wired-marker: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/control/function.fn:80 and :93 `chn.Label().Substr(0,6) == "HmIPW-"`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/STATE_RESET_RECEIVER/KEY_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:19 `[string first "HmIPW-" $device] == 0`; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/EnterFreeValue.tcl:267; ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/WGD.js:20 `device.typeName.includes("HmIPW-")`. Descriptor (Tier 2): ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIPW-DRS8.json declares TYPE/SUBTYPE/ADDRESS/CHILDREN/PARENT/INDEX/AES_ACTIVE/PARAMSETS/FIRMWARE/VERSION/FLAGS/LINK_*_ROLES/DIRECTION/GROUP/TEAM*/INTERFACE/ROAMING/RX_MODE — no product-group field. Reserved-name boundary: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_add_device.cgi:271-297,367 and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:26,110,343,649 use "HmIP-Wired" as an iface identifier passed to Interface.isPresent / iface_url($iface).
all.finding: Both halves hold, with one boundary. (a) The CCU's interface names are exactly the <ipc><name> entries of InterfacesList.xml; the shipped template plus hs485dLoader's insertion produce BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, VirtualDevices, HmIP-RF and nothing else, and the HmIP side runs a single legacy XML-RPC port (32010) whose process also carries HomeMatic IP Wired framing and OTAU. So wired HmIP devices are reached through HmIP-RF and "HmIP-Wired" is not an interface our XML-RPC client could connect to — our rejection is right. (b) The device description carries no product-group field; the CCU itself identifies wired HmIP by the device TYPE string prefix "HmIPW-" in at least four independent WebUI/ReGa sites, so a model-name prefix rule is the firmware's own rule. Case differs (firmware tests uppercase "HmIPW-"; we lower-case the model first at pkg/hmenum/backend.go:62-64), same acceptance set.
