Where it narrows: "HmIP-Wired" is not an unknown token to the CCU — it is a reserved WebUI interface identifier with a complete add-device and firmware-update code path (cp_add_device.cgi putSectionHMIPWired, ic_ifacecmd.cgi's HmIPWiredIdentifier branches) that resolves through the same InterfacesList lookup. Nothing in either tree writes such an ipc entry, so that path is dead in this distribution — but the claim is "no HmIP-Wired entry is generated", not "the CCU has no such concept". If a firmware generation did write the entry, the WebUI would light up and dispatch.tcl would accept it.
all.negativeControl: Had HmIP-Wired been a separate interface, InterfacesList.xml (template or a loader) would carry a fourth <ipc><name>HmIP-Wired</name> with its own port and crRFD.conf would define a second Legacy.Port — I read both and found neither; the wired-only writer is hs485dLoader, and it writes BidCos-Wired. Had wired HmIP been marked by a descriptor field rather than the TYPE name, the CCU's own code would branch on that field instead of `Substr(0,6) == "HmIPW-"`, and HmIPW-DRS8.json would carry it.
all.ourValue: model prefix "hmipw-" (lower-cased compare) ⇒ ProductGroup HMIPW; "HmIP-Wired" refused as an interface name
all.firmwareValue: TYPE prefix "HmIPW-" (upper-case compare) is the CCU's own wired-HmIP marker; interface list = BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, VirtualDevices, HmIP-RF
all.challengeNote: Upheld as narrowed; both halves survive re-reading and I closed one hole the prior grounding left open. The interface vocabulary really is exactly the <ipc><name> entries, dispatch.tcl really does die on an unknown one, and I checked the writer side rather than assuming it: the init script S49hs485d and hs485dLoader are the only things in either tree that write /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml, and between them they produce BidCos-RF, VirtualDevices, HmIP-RF and (conditionally) BidCos-Wired — never HmIP-Wired. The classification half is stronger than cited: seven independent WebUI/ReGa sites key on the device TYPE prefix "HmIPW-", and function.fn:80 settles that ReGa's Label() is that same TYPE string, so the firmware's own wired-HmIP test operates on exactly the datum our `model` carries. The descriptor carries no product-group field. Two boundaries stand. (a) "HmIP-Wired" is not an unknown token to the CCU: cp_add_device.cgi renders a complete HmIP-Wired teach-in section unconditionally and hands that literal to Interface.setInstallModeHMIP, which resolves through the same INTERFACE_LIST; in this distribution it takes dispatch.tcl's error branch, so the path is dead here, but the claim is "this distribution generates no such entry", not "the CCU has no such concept". (b) NEW, and the prior grounding did not name it: /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml is a mutable runtime file, and third-party add-ons write it — that is how CUxD becomes an interface at all, a name our own config accepts and no OpenCCU source ever writes. So the two trees can settle what eQ-3 ships, never what the file contains on a given box. Our refusal of the string is a defensible policy for this distribution's own writers; it is not a firmware-derived impossibility, and the error text should not be read as one. Minor: the firmware compares upper-case "HmIPW-" while pkg/hmenum/backend.go:62-64 lower-cases first, making our acceptance set a strict superset — identical for every shipped TYPE, but the case-insensitivity is our convention, not something read from the source.

all.title: The empty-heating-group sentinel is a claim repeated in two files
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/ccu/getheatinggrouplist.tcl:11-21 — `set pathOfFile "/etc/config/groups.gson"` / `set result ""` / `if {[catch {set fp [open $pathOfFile r]}] == 0} { set result [read $fp]; close $fp } else { set result -1 }` / `jsonrpc_response [json_toString $result]`. String encoding: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/json.tcl:203-215 — `return "\"[string map $map $str]\""` (always quoted, so the payload is a JSON string, and "/" is escaped as "\/"). Method registration and level: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods.conf:1001-1006 (`CCU.getHeatingGroupList`, LEVEL ADMIN). The CCU's own consumer guards on the same value: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/js/ic_functions.js:2152-2153 — `groupList = JSON.parse(homematic("CCU.getHeatingGroupList", {}));` then `if (groupList != -1 && typeof groupList == "object")`.
all.finding: Exact match, and it is the same surface: CCU.getHeatingGroupList opens /etc/config/groups.gson, returns its text on success and the literal -1 on failure, and json_toString wraps the result in quotes unconditionally — so the wire value is the JSON string "-1", which is what our string type-assertion plus `trimmed == "-1"` accepts. The empty-payload branch is also covered: a file that exists but is empty yields `set result [read $fp]` = "", which our `trimmed == ""` maps to the same empty slice. One wording narrowing worth fixing in the comments: the firmware produces -1 on ANY failure of `open`, not only a missing file — an unreadable or permission-denied groups.gson yields "-1" too. Both our comments say "does not exist" / "absent", which is narrower than the firmware; the code behaves correctly either way.
all.negativeControl: Had the marker been anything else — a JSON null, an empty object, a JSON-RPC error — the else-branch of getheatinggrouplist.tcl would show that value or the script would call jsonrpc_error instead; it literally reads `set result -1` and falls through to the same jsonrpc_response. And json_toString has no numeric path, so a bare JSON number -1 was never possible.
all.ourValue: sentinel string "-1" (and "") ⇒ empty group list
all.firmwareValue: `set result -1` on any failed `open`, emitted through json_toString ⇒ JSON string "-1"
all.challengeNote: Confirmed, and it is the same surface end to end. I did not stop at the two files the prior grounding cited — the load-bearing question was whether the quotes survive to the wire, so I read jsonrpc_response itself and then checked whether the distribution patches it. It does patch it (0159), and the patch is harmless here. The method opens /etc/config/groups.gson, returns its text on success and the literal -1 on failure, json_toString quotes whatever it is given, and jsonrpc_response splices that quoted text straight into the result member — so the wire value is the JSON string "-1", which is exactly what the `raw.(string)` assertion at ccu_extended.go:529 plus `trimmed == "-1"` at group.go:144 accepts. The empty-payload branch is covered by the same reading: an existing but empty file yields `[read $fp]` = "", json_toString emits "", and our `trimmed == ""` maps it to the same empty slice. One wording narrowing stands, unchanged from the prior finding and worth fixing in the two comments: the firmware emits -1 on ANY failure of `open` — permission denied, a directory in the way, EMFILE — not only on absence. group.go:139-141 says "a missing file yields the sentinel" and ccu_extended.go:518 says "when the file is absent"; the code is correct for all of them, only the prose is narrower than the firmware.

all.title: The central-link eligible-interface set is a comment-justified literal
all.citation: BidCos-RF: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:714-724 registers `reportValueUsage` → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:1132-1139 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:1425-1450, which on total_count>0 does `AddLinkPeer(central_device->GetListenerChannel()->GetSerial(), false)` and on 0 `LowLevelRemoveLinkPeer(central_address, central_channel)`. BidCos-Wired: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:511-520 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Manager.cpp:680-686 → ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Channel.cpp:409-430, same AddLinkPeer/RemoveLinkPeer against the central listener channel. Both gate first on `if(!GetDescription()->GetAutoregisterCentral())return true;` (RFChannel.cpp:1427, HS485Channel.cpp:411). HmIP-RF: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage (persists the per-address metadata key "reportValueUsageData" and forwards to the backend; throws on a null refCounter). VirtualDevices: HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.rega.IRegaServer#reportValueUsage, annotated @RpcMethod("reportValueUsage"), implemented by HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.service.internal.rega.VirtualDeviceHandlerRega#reportValueUsage as an unconditional `return true;`. Virtual remote: LegacyServiceHandler#reportValueUsage short-circuits with `return true` when the VirtualRemoteControl is enabled and the address matches it. Operator surface: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0171-WebUI-Add-HmIPKeyTransceiverCentralLinkConfiguration/occu/WebUI/www/webui/webui.js:198 (buttons rendered only for channelType KEY_TRANSCEIVER, KEY, MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER) and :15625,15627,15639-15643 (KEY_TRANSCEIVER|MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER → interface "HmIP-RF"; KEY → interface "BidCos-RF"; create raises PRESS_SHORT only, remove zeroes PRESS_SHORT and PRESS_LONG). RPC plumbing: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/reportvalueusage.tcl:19.
all.finding: The three interfaces we accept all implement reportValueUsage with real device-side effect — rfd and hs485d both add/remove the central listener channel as a link peer, the HmIP legacy API persists reportValueUsageData and forwards — so the positive half of the set is confirmed on Tier 1. Two corrections to the reason and the justification. (1) VirtualDevices does NOT reject the call: its XML-RPC surface declares reportValueUsage (@RpcMethod on IRegaServer) and the implementation returns true unconditionally. Excluding it yields the right user-visible outcome (nothing would happen), but our token "interface_unsupported" and the comment "VirtualDevices and CUxD do not participate in CCU link management / use a different event dispatch path" state something the firmware contradicts in the letter — the CCU accepts and silently no-ops. (2) CUxD is a third-party add-on and appears nowhere in the CCU source trees; its half of the set is tier1-silent and rests on nothing I could read. Two boundaries the reader should know: the CCU's own central-link UI is one interface narrower than us — it never offers the buttons for BidCos-Wired, hard-coding "BidCos-RF" for channelType KEY and "HmIP-RF" for KEY_TRANSCEIVER/MULTI_MODE_INPUT_TRANSMITTER — although hs485d does implement the call, so our wider set is defensible rather than wrong. And both BidCos daemons short-circuit on the channel description's AUTOREGISTER flag (`GetAutoregisterCentral()`), returning true with no effect; our eligibility filter uses press-event presence only, so CentralLinksStatus can report a channel eligible whose reportValueUsage is a firmware no-op. The virtual-remote conjunct is confirmed for HmIP-RF by the LegacyServiceHandler short-circuit; I found no equivalent guard for HM-RCV-50 / HMW-RCV-50 in rfd or hs485d, so that part of the model filter stays ungrounded.
all.negativeControl: Had BidCos-Wired lacked the concept, src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp would not register a `reportValueUsage` method at all (it registers it at :639) or HS485Channel::ReportValueUsage would be the base-class `return true` stub from HS485LogicalInstance.h:40 — instead it is overridden with a real AddLinkPeer/RemoveLinkPeer body. Had VirtualDevices genuinely lacked it, IRegaServer would carry no @RpcMethod("reportValueUsage") entry — I read the full interface and it does, next to addLink/removeLink/getLinks. For CUxD the check cannot produce a different answer either way: nothing about CUxD exists in these trees.
all.ourValue: eligible = {BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired, HmIP-RF}; VirtualDevices and CUxD → reason "interface_unsupported" ("no concept of CCU press-event link management")
all.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF / BidCos-Wired / HmIP-RF: real link-peer effect (AUTOREGISTER-gated). VirtualDevices: method declared and accepted, `return true;` no-op. CUxD: not present in the CCU sources. CCU's own UI: only BidCos-RF and HmIP-RF, dispatched by channel type.
all.missingInput: CUxD's XML-RPC surface — the add-on is not part of OpenCCU-Base/OpenCCU, so whether it implements reportValueUsage cannot be settled from Tier 1 or Tier 2 here.
all.challengeNote: The prior verdict (narrowed) is right but its boundary is in the wrong place, and its positive half does not survive. Where it holds: BidCos-RF and HmIP-RF do carry real device-side effect, and I re-read every line to confirm the chain — rfd adds/removes the central listener channel as a link peer, and the HmIP legacy handler is stronger than cited, calling DeviceUtil.createCentralLink / deleteCentralLink on the summed ref counter rather than merely persisting metadata. Where it breaks: the prior finding wrote "the three interfaces we accept all implement reportValueUsage with real device-side effect", which takes "implements the method" for "has effect". Both BidCos daemons return true before touching anything when the channel description's `autoregister` attribute is false, and that attribute is not a runtime property — it is a literal in the shipped device-type XML, defaulting to false in the schema and in both daemons' constructors, with no other writer. Counting it: 0 of 40 channel declarations across all 15 shipped hs485types XMLs carry `autoregister="true"`. So on BidCos-Wired, HS485Channel::ReportValueUsage is a no-op for every wired device type this firmware ships. Our set includes an interface on which the operation cannot do anything, and central_links.go will report success. That is exactly why the CCU's own UI never offers the button for BidCos-Wired — the 0171 dispatch hard-codes HmIP-RF and BidCos-RF only — so the WebUI's narrowness is not an oversight to be shrugged off, it matches the descriptors. On BidCos-RF the gate bites too, though far less: 29 of 34 KEY channel declarations are armed, so 5 declarations in 2 files (rf_em_8.xml, rf_em_8_bit.xml, rf_st_6_sh.xml among the armed) sit the other way; our eligibility filter uses press-event presence only and cannot see the attribute at all, because the XML-RPC device description does not export it. Two prior corrections upheld unchanged: VirtualDevices does NOT reject the call (IRegaServer declares it, VirtualDeviceHandlerRega returns true unconditionally), so the token "interface_unsupported" and the comment "do not participate in CCU link management / use a different event dispatch path" are contradicted in the letter even though the user-visible outcome is right; and CUxD is a third-party add-on with no trace in either tree, so its half of the set is tier1-silent and rests on nothing readable. One prior gap I can close in our favour: the virtual-remote conjunct is groundable after all. The virtual remotes ARE the central device — RFCentral.cpp:36 names HM-RCV-50 — and rf_central.xml / hmw_central.xml carry no `autoregister` on any channel, so reportValueUsage on a virtual-remote VIRTUAL_KEY channel returns true with no effect, the same outcome our filter produces; HmIP-RCV-50 is settled independently by the LegacyServiceHandler VirtualRemoteControl short-circuit. The exact three-model set in pkg/hmenum/device_model.go:21-25 is therefore grounded on Tier 1 across all three bus families (hm_autoconf:112-122 and ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi:281-283 enumerate the same three), not just for HmIP.

all.title: A package-private constant named addressSeparator is "-" in the naming path while the same name is ":" everywhere else
all.site: internal/model/device/naming.go:11-13 (const addressSeparator = "-") and :110-124 (normaliseChannelName), reached from Channel.DataPointName / DataPointFullName at :74-106
all.citation: Distribution (Tier 1, applied on top of OCCU): ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0099-WebUI-Add-DeviceRenameAllChannels/occu/WebUI/www/webui/webui.js:314 — the rename dialog's separator field is `<input id=\"DeviceConfigDialog_DeviceChannelsRenameSeparator\" size=\"2\" type=\"text\" value=\":\"/>`; :15689 — `var origChName = this.device.name+":"+chNumber;` (the CCU's own test for "this channel still carries its derived name"); :15694 — `var chName = $(this.NAME_ID).value + $(this.SEPARATOR_ID).value + chNumber;` written back via `homematic("Channel.setName", ...)`. Stock eQ-3 OCCU, a documented real ReGa channel Name(): ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_metadata.tcl:257 — `#HSS;DAA0217858:1 HSS.DAA0217858:1` (the sample row for the `channel.Name()` ReGa script at :212-228), i.e. the channel name is the device-name-shaped prefix joined to the channel index by ":". Tier-3 witness for where our rule came from: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/support.py:98-105 (`if c_name.startswith(ADDRESS_SEPARATOR): c_name = c_name[1:]`) with ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/const.py:269 `ADDRESS_SEPARATOR: Final = ":"`.
all.finding: The separator is a colon, not a dash. When the CCU duplicates the device name into a channel name it joins device name + separator + channel number, and both the derived form the CCU computes for itself and the default of the operator-facing separator field are ":"; the stock ReGa example in ic_metadata.tcl shows the same shape (HSS.DAA0217858 / HSS.DAA0217858:1). The Python function this was ported from strips exactly that colon. Our constant strips "-", so for the common case — a never-renamed channel whose name is "<device name>:<n>" — normaliseChannelName returns ":<n>" instead of "<n>", and the leading colon then travels into DataPointName / DataPointFullName and everything built on them. The comment "addressSeparator is the dash the CCU uses between channel and parameter slugs" describes neither the CCU nor what the function does (the function operates on a device-name prefix, not on a parameter slug), and internal/model/device/naming_test.go:63 pins the dash by constructing "Wohnzimmer Licht-Kanal" — the test was written to the code, so it cannot bite. Note the residual limit: the CCU lets the operator type any separator into that field, so no single constant covers every renamed channel; ":" is the default and the only form the CCU itself derives, which is what the strip should target. The name collision the reader flagged is real and points the same way: internal/model/device/definitionexport/export.go:33 and pkg/hmtypes/address.go:16 both bind the identifier `addressSeparator` to ":".
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU used a dash, the rename dialog's separator input would default to "-" and origChName would read `this.device.name+"-"+chNumber`; both read ":" verbatim. Had ReGa's derived channel name not embedded the device-name prefix at all, ic_metadata.tcl's sample row would show a bare index or a free-form label rather than `HSS.DAA0217858:1`.
all.ourValue: addressSeparator = "-" (internal/model/device/naming.go:13)
all.firmwareValue: ":" — webui.js:15689 `this.device.name+":"+chNumber` and the separator field's default `value=":"` (operator-overridable)
all.challengeNote: The contradiction stands — the separator is a colon — but the prior finding's blast-radius claim does not, and that changes what the defect is. Confirmed: when the CCU derives a channel name from a device name it joins with ":", both in the form it computes for its own "has this been renamed" test and in the default of the operator-facing separator field; the stock ReGa sample shows the same shape; and the Python function ours was ported from strips exactly that colon. Our constant strips "-", so normaliseChannelName("Wohnzimmer Licht", "Wohnzimmer Licht:1") returns ":1" where it should return "1". The comment at naming.go:11-12 ("the dash the CCU uses between channel and parameter slugs") describes neither the CCU nor what the function does — the function strips a device-name prefix, not a parameter slug — and the two tests that would catch it were written to the code. Where the prior finding overreaches: it says the leading colon "travels into DataPointName / DataPointFullName and everything built on them". Nothing production is built on them. Channel.FullName() (internal/model/device/channel.go:1374) has no non-test caller; no interface in the tree declares `FullName() string` that *Channel would satisfy; and DataPointName / DataPointFullName / CustomDataPointName / CustomDataPointFullName are called only from tests/golden/naming_test.go:354-358. Production naming runs through device.BuildDataPointName / BuildCustomDataPointName (internal/model/device/namedata.go), which uses baseChannelName plus stripChannelAddressSuffix — and namedata.go:246 hard-codes ':' correctly, with internal/model/device/namedata_test.go:88-99 pinning the CCU auto-default form "HmIP-eTRV 000ABC:1" to "Schlafzimmer:1". Channel.NameData() (channel.go:1382-1386) delegates to BuildDataPointName, and that is what internal/north/matter/endpoint/helpers.go:51 and internal/model/datapoint/base.go:696 consume. So the wrong constant is real and its comment is wrong, but it lives in a naming family unreachable from the daemon, which is why no operator has ever seen the stray colon — and equally why correcting the constant to ":" would change no output today. The choice is to correct constant and comment together, or to delete the family; what is not defensible is leaving a constant that asserts a CCU property the CCU contradicts. Residual limit, upheld from the prior finding: the separator field is operator-editable, so no single constant covers every renamed channel; ":" is the default and the only form the CCU derives for itself, which is what a strip should target.

all.title: setInstallMode's third positional argument is overloaded between device address and mode on a comment alone
all.ourValue: `setInstallMode(on, time, deviceAddress)` when an address is given, else `setInstallMode(on, time, mode)`; comment claims this holds for "BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired".
all.firmwareValue: rfd: `setInstallMode(bool on [, int seconds [, {int mode | string serial}]])` — exactly as we do it, third slot type-dispatched. hs485d: the method does not exist. HMIPServer legacy: `setInstallMode(Boolean, Integer, String)` — third slot String-only, no int-mode form.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:589 (doc: "void setInstallMode(Boolean on, Integer seconds)"), :602 (registration), :606-609 (`InstallModes mode = INSTALL_NORMAL;`, `if(params.size()>=2)time=params[1]; else time=60;`), :610 `if(params.size()>=3)`, :612-613 (`params[2].getType() == XmlRpcValue::TypeInt` and the range check `>= INSTALL_OFF && <= INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG`), :621-623 (`else if(params[2].getType() == XmlRpcValue::TypeString) { … SetInstallMode(INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST, time, params[2]); return; }`), :634. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:562 `enum{INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME=600};`; RFManager.cpp:565-570 (whitelist branch throws "Device serial number must not be empty." on empty serial), :582-583 (clamp to 600). hs485d method registrations: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:48-601 (26 methods; setInstallMode absent, pairing is :66 `searchDevices`). Working CCU callers: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/setinstallmode.tcl (`xmlrpc $interface(URL) setInstallMode [list bool $on]` — one arg), ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_add_device.cgi:903. HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.IServiceApi#setInstallMode and de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#setInstallMode (signature `(Boolean on, Integer time, String address)`, defaults time to 60 when null), plus #setInstallModeWithWhitelist(Boolean, Integer, RpcStruct[]).
all.finding: The signature the bundle feared — `(on, time, mode, address)` — does not exist anywhere. rfd reads at most params[2] and dispatches on its XML-RPC type: TypeInt selects a mode (range-checked 0..2, anything else faults -1), TypeString is taken as the device serial and forces INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST. Our two branches are therefore exactly right for BidCos-RF, and the security scenario in the bundle (address landing in the mode slot, unrestricted window) is refuted. Two boundaries the comment crosses, though. (1) BidCos-Wired: hs485d registers no setInstallMode at all — the CCU's own wired pairing is `searchDevices` — yet `hmenum.InterfacesSupportingInstallMode` (pkg/hmenum/interface.go:190-194) includes InterfaceBidCosWired, so `WireInstallModeDPs` (internal/central/adapter/install_mode.go:104-106) creates an install-mode DP for it and every enable/disable is an XML-RPC call to a method hs485d does not implement. (2) On the HmIP legacy XML-RPC surface the third slot is declared `String` only; our int-mode branch would not type-map there. Our code never reaches it (HmIP-RF is routed to Interface.setInstallModeHMIP via JSON-RPC, which matches the WebUI's own caller in www/api/methods/interface/setinstallmodehmip.tcl), but the comment's blanket wording does. Two side facts worth carrying: seconds defaults to 60 when omitted and is silently clamped to 600 (INSTALL_MODE_MAX_TIME); with `on == false` rfd ignores params[1]/params[2] entirely and sets INSTALL_OFF.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong I would have found either a read of `params[3]` in XmlRpcMethodSetInstallMode::execute, or a params[2] handled only as TypeInt with the address carried elsewhere. Neither appears; the whole method body is 30 lines and reads params[0..2] only. For the wired half, had hs485d implemented the method it would appear among the 26 `XmlRpcServerMethod("…", s)` registrations in src/hs485d/XmlRpcMethods.cpp — it does not, and a case-insensitive grep for install_mode/installmode over src/hs485d returns nothing.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD on the BidCos-RF surface, with the bundle's own HmIP parenthetical REFUTED. What I re-read line by line and confirm verbatim: rfd reads at most params[2]; TypeInt selects a mode range-checked to 0..2 (anything else faults -1); TypeString is taken as the serial and forces INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST; with on==false params[1]/[2] are never read and time stays 0, which drives SetInstallMode into the INSTALL_OFF branch that also clears the whitelist serial; seconds defaults to 60 and is clamped to 600. The feared `(on, time, mode, address)` form exists nowhere. Boundary (1) UPHELD and strengthened: hs485d registers no setInstallMode (26 methods; the sibling grep in src/rfd finds 51 registrations including it), and the CCU's own Add-Device page pairs BidCos-Wired with `wir_search()` — a search, not an install mode — while `hmenum.InterfacesSupportingInstallMode` (pkg/hmenum/interface.go:190-194) includes InterfaceBidCosWired, so WireInstallModeDPs (internal/central/adapter/install_mode.go:104-106) still mints an install-mode DP whose every enable/disable is an XML-RPC call to a method hs485d does not implement. Boundary (2) is where the bundle's grounding BREAKS. It wrote that our HmIP route "matches the WebUI's own caller in setinstallmodehmip.tcl". It does not. methods.conf requires `address` as an argument, but the wrapper only uses it in the LOCAL branch; our CcuBackend hard-codes `installMode: "ALL"` (ccu_extended.go:92) and in the ALL branch the Tcl calls `setInstallMode [list bool $on] [list int $time]` — two arguments, `address` silently discarded. Consequence: on HmIP-RF, installModeWriter.SetInstallModeForDevice and DeviceAdminDomain.SetInstallMode open an UNSCOPED broadcast pairing window while the operator surface says the window is scoped to one device. The bundle's third boundary is therefore an unqualified "the address never reaches the HmIP daemon", not just "the comment's wording overreaches". Separately, the bundle's "working CCU caller" setinstallmode.tcl is not registered in methods.conf and is unreachable over the JSON-RPC API — the live callers are the CGIs, all one-argument.

all.title: setInstallMode mode=1 / mode=2 semantics rest on a comment with no cited source
all.ourValue: "`mode=1` is the CCU's \"normal\" install mode (mode=2 means \"ready for re-pairing\")", called as `setInstallMode(true, durationSecs, mode=1, address)`.
all.firmwareValue: `enum InstallModes { INSTALL_OFF = 0, INSTALL_NORMAL, INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG, INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST }` — 2 is INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG (write the description's default configuration and delete every existing link), 3 is INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST. There is no 4-argument form, and the per-device call selects mode 3, not 1.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.h:28-34 (the enum, with the inline note on the last member "Only the device with matching serial … only one device with given serial can be installed."). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:353-354 (`case INSTALL_NORMAL: case INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST:` share one branch — central address into list 0 index 10, manual peering disabled, then ScheduleConfig) versus :388-390 (German note "setzt die default Configuration die in der Devicedescription bzw. der Channeldescription hinterlegt sind / auserdem werden alle besehenden Verknüpfungen gelöscht" immediately above `case INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG:`, whose body calls `config_data[0].InitDefault()` and `description->SetDefaultConfig(this)`). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:613 (int modes accepted only in 0..INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG, i.e. 0..2 — mode 3 is not reachable as an integer), :622 (a String third argument is what selects INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST). ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:447-450 (the whitelist filter compares the sysinfo serial and returns early on a mismatch).
all.finding: Both halves of the comment are wrong, while the code is right. (a) mode=2 is not "ready for re-pairing": INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG re-provisions the device from its device/channel description and, per the firmware's own note at RFDevice.cpp:388-389, deletes all existing links — a destructive re-configuration, not a pairing flavour. (b) The signature in the comment, `setInstallMode(true, durationSecs, mode=1, address)`, does not exist; `DeviceAdminDomain.SetInstallMode` passes address non-empty, so `CcuBackend.SetInstallMode` takes the string branch and rfd runs INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST (3). mode=1 is never transmitted on this path — and could not be, since the int branch rejects 3. The behaviour is nonetheless correct: RFDevice.cpp:353-354 gives INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST exactly the INSTALL_NORMAL treatment, and RFManager.cpp:447-450 adds the serial restriction the operator asked for. The only genuinely correct use of `installModeNormal = 1` is the broadcast path in install_mode.go:60 (empty address), where mode 1 does mean INSTALL_NORMAL. What is at risk is future work: a reader following this comment would try to add a 4th argument, or would reach for mode=2 wanting a re-pair and get a link-wiping default-config push instead.
all.negativeControl: Had "mode=2 = ready for re-pairing" been right, the third enum member would carry a re-pairing name and its RFDevice case would re-run the pairing handshake. Instead the member is named INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG and its case calls InitDefault()/SetDefaultConfig(). Had mode=1 actually been sent on the per-device path, RFManager::SetInstallMode(InstallModes, int, const std::string&) would have to accept a mode argument from the wire — it is reached only from the TypeString branch, which hard-codes INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST.
all.challengeNote: CONFIRMED contradicted on both halves, with one addition that makes the bundle's exoneration of the behaviour too generous. Verified verbatim: the enum ordinals; that INSTALL_NORMAL and INSTALL_DEVICE_WHITELIST share a single case body at RFDevice.cpp:353-354, so mode 3 gets exactly the normal treatment plus the serial filter; that INSTALL_PUSH_DEFAULT_CONFIG's body re-initialises config_data[0] and pushes the description's default config, under a firmware comment that says all existing links are deleted — a destructive re-provisioning, not a pairing flavour; and that the integer branch's upper bound is 2, so mode 3 cannot be sent as an int. The comment's 4-argument signature does not exist on any surface. ADDITION the bundle missed: its closing "The behaviour is nonetheless correct" holds only when the resolved device sits on BidCos-RF. `DeviceAdminDomain.SetInstallMode` (device_admin.go:381-387) resolves the backend by address; for a device on HmIP-RF the call takes the JSON-RPC branch (ccu_extended.go:79-98) where the `mode` argument is unused AND the CCU's own wrapper discards `address` in installMode=ALL (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:66-68). So on HmIP-RF a "pair this one device" request opens a broadcast window with no serial restriction at all. `installModeNormal = 1` at install_mode.go:20 is genuinely correct only for the BidCos-RF broadcast path at install_mode.go:60.

all.title: connectivityErrorThreshold = 1 is a bare literal that decides when every north-bound availability surface flips
all.ourValue: connectivityErrorThreshold = 1 — the second consecutive unanswered `ping` leaves CONNECTED. With defaultCheckConnectionSlot = 30 s (internal/central/jobs.go:202) and connectionCheckerInterval = 15 s (internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:62) feeding the same counter, a CCU is declared down roughly 30-60 s after it goes quiet.
all.firmwareValue: No firmware constant bounds how long a healthy rfd/HMIPServer may take to answer an XML-RPC request. The only CCU-side tolerance figures that exist are: monit's 20 cycles × 13 s = 260 s before rfd (port 32001), HMIPServer (39292) or ReGaHss are considered dead and restarted; and, on the HmIP legacy surface only, `Legacy.ResponseTimeout` = 25 s per blocking RPC call.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/rfd.cpp:396-402 (the single main loop: `while(run){ … timeout=TimerTarget::s_timerQueue.TimeBeforeNextDue(); … s.work(timeout); }`) with ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcServer.cpp:137-143 (`XmlRpcServer::work` → `_disp.work(msTime)`) — RF frames, timers and every XML-RPC method share one thread. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFController.cpp:54-63 (`SendFrame` → `msg.WaitUntilSent()`, a blocking wait) and ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFCommMessage.cpp:19 (`SetResponseTimeout(2000)`) — one RF round-trip parks the loop for up to 2 s, and a putParamset issues many. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:1206-1219 (`ping` only calls `RFManager::Ping(callerID)` and returns true; the PONG is delivered asynchronously). Supervisor: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base-openccu/etc/monitrc:2 `set daemon 13`, :291 `if failed port 32001 for 20 cycles then restart` (rfd), :311 same for HMIPServer port 39292, :327-329 same for ReGaHss. HmIP per-call ceiling: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler, field `responseTimeout` initialised from the service property `Legacy.ResponseTimeout` with default 25 (seconds) and used as the poll timeout on every legacy response queue.
all.finding: Tier 1 does not decide this, and it cannot: rfd serves XML-RPC from the same single-threaded select loop that drives the BidCos radio, so the answer to "how long may a healthy CCU legitimately not answer ping" is "as long as whatever RF work is in front of it takes" — there is no timeout, no request queue bound and no service-level constant anywhere in src/rfd, src/hs485d or src/tclrpc. What the CCU does carry is its own patience with an unresponsive interface daemon, and it is 260 s (20 monit cycles of 13 s) before it restarts rfd/HMIPServer/ReGaHss; on the HmIP legacy surface a single blocking call may hold for 25 s by default. Our rule declares an outage 4-9× sooner than the CCU's own supervisor would. That is a defensible product choice — we are detecting a dead link, not deciding to restart a daemon — but it rests on our judgement, not on the firmware, and the doc comment should say so rather than reading as a sourced value. Two things the comment gets right on the evidence: `ping` really is cheap on both surfaces (rfd returns immediately and fires PONG later; HMIPServer's ping does the same via AccessPointUtil.sendPong), so a ping failure is not itself evidence of RF load. One thing the comment does not mention: two independent probe loops (jobs.go:545-551 at 30 s and ccu_wiring.go:1100-1105 at 15 s) increment the same `connectivityErrors` counter, so the effective time-to-declare-down is not derivable from either interval alone.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware carried a bound, it would appear as a service-time or dispatch timeout in rfd's XML-RPC path or as a documented maximum for a method; a grep for timeout constants across src/rfd, src/hs485d, src/libhsscomm and src/tclrpc yields only per-frame RF timeouts (2000 ms default, 500 ms in CommMessage) and the send-inhibit wait — none of them bounding the listener. And had the CCU tolerated a stall as short as ours, monitrc would use a small cycle count; it uses 20 on every homematic daemon.

all.title: Duty-cycle and transmission-pending recovery windows are ported constants, not measured against the CCU
all.missingInput: The transceiver's duty-cycle accounting-window semantics (how the reported percentage decays over time). rfd reads the percentage from the coprocessor's HELLO message and never models its recovery; no readable source carries the decay law, so no honest wait can be derived from it.
all.ourValue: RetryDutyCycleDelay = 40 s on XML-RPC fault -8; RetryTransmissionPendingDelay = 5 s on fault -10; both fixed, jitter-free, and both freezing the exponential schedule, with MaxAttempts = 3.
all.firmwareValue: Fault -8 ("not enough DutyCycle free") is raised at exactly one place in the whole CCU source tree — inside `RFDevice::UpdateFirmware()` — and never by setValue/putParamset; the HmIP legacy surface has no -8 at all. Fault -10 ("Transmission is pending.") exists only on the HmIP side and is emitted when `device.isReachable()` is false; it is cleared by the device becoming reachable, not by elapsed time. Neither daemon defines any recovery interval.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1490-1492 (`if(!… ->DutyCycleForUpdate(this->address,updateFile)) { throw XmlRpcException("not enough DutyCycle free",-8); }`) — the sole `-8` in ../OpenCCU-Base/src. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosInterfaceConcentrator.cpp:1045-1076, whose whole test is instantaneous: verbatim `//450000 Byte entsprechen bei 100k Datenrate 100%` then `if((uint32_t)(450000 - (4500 * dutycycle)) > (bytesToSend + 90000)) // nach dem Update sollen noch mehr als 20% DutyCycle übrigsein`. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosInterface.cpp:38-51 (`DUTYCYCLE_THRESHOLDMAP[] = {0,40,65,80,90,95,98,99,100}`) and :234-247 (`SetDutyCycle` fires a DUTY_CYCLE update only when a threshold band is crossed) — hysteresis for notification, not a budget. ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/BidcosRemoteInterface.cpp:505-506 (`int dutyCycle = msg.GetUIntParam(BidcosInterfaceMessage::PARAM_INDEX_HELLO_DUTYCYCLE); SetDutyCycle(dutyCycle);`) — the percentage arrives from the transceiver. HmIP: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#createTransmissionPendingRpcRemoteException (message "Transmission is pending.", code -10), #getRpcRemoteException (only -1/-2/-5/-10 are produced; no -8), #createDeleteDeviceRpcRemoteException (AP_BUSY, RESPONSE_NAK, TIMEOUT, TRANSMISSION_PENDING, STACK_BUSY and UNREACH all collapse to -10); de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleSetConfigCommand (persists the config as pending, then `if (device.isReachable()) { … } else { sendBackendResponseObject(… BackendNotificationType.TRANSMISSION_PENDING) }`) and #handleExcludeCommand (same reachability test).
all.finding: The trigger mapping is contradicted on both codes, and the durations themselves are not derivable. -8: a CCU never rejects a value write with a duty-cycle fault. The only producer is the firmware-update path, gated by an instantaneous airtime-budget test (does the image fit in the remaining 450000-byte allowance with 20 % to spare). So RetryDutyCycleDelay = 40 s cannot fire on the write path its own doc comment describes ("when a CCU rejects a command with a duty-cycle / RF-throttle error"); against a real CCU it is reachable only from `updateFirmware`. -10: real, but HmIP-only (rfd and hs485d never emit it), and it does not mean "the CCU is busy for a moment" — it means the target device is not currently reachable and the command has been persisted as pending configuration for delivery when the device next talks to the access point. It is cleared by that event, so a fixed 5 s wait re-asks a question whose answer cannot have changed; with MaxAttempts = 3 the chain then gives up 10 s later while the CCU still intends to deliver the write. The duration questions themselves are not performable from any source I can read: rfd holds no duty-cycle recovery model at all (it reads a percentage out of the transceiver's HELLO frame and only re-notifies on band crossings), and the HmIP pending window is bounded by the device's own wake-up cycle, which no CCU source carries. Do not substitute a plausible number: the honest outputs here are (i) re-key the -8 handling to the firmware-update path or drop it, and (ii) treat -10 as "queued at the CCU, stop retrying" rather than as a timed backoff.
all.negativeControl: Had the firmware defined a recovery interval, `DutyCycleForUpdate` or `BidcosInterface::SetDutyCycle` would compute or wait on one; both only compare the instantaneous percentage, and the threshold map is consumed exclusively by `GetDutyCycleLowerBound`/`GetDutyCycleUpperBound` for change notification. Had -8 been produced on the value path, a grep for `-8)` across ../OpenCCU-Base/src would return more than one hit — it returns exactly RFDevice.cpp:1492 — and NotificationUtil's fault mapping would carry an -8 arm; it carries -1, -2, -5 and -10 only. Had -10 been a timed condition, DeviceSubcommandHandler would emit it behind a timer or retry count; it emits it behind `device.isReachable()`.
all.challengeNote: CONFIRMED contradicted on the -8 mapping, and NARROWED FURTHER than the bundle on -10 — the bundle was itself too generous. -8: I re-grepped the whole src tree; RFDevice.cpp:1492 is the only producer, inside UpdateFirmware, and DutyCycleForUpdate is a pure airtime-budget predicate with no time dimension whatsoever, so RetryDutyCycleDelay's own doc comment describes a path on which the fault cannot occur. -10: the bundle wrote that it is real on the write path and means "the device is not reachable". Half right. handleSetConfigCommand (reached by putParamset MASTER) does emit it on !isReachable(), verbatim as cited. But handleSetValueCommand — the setValue path, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.server.core.vertx.backendhandler.DeviceSubcommandHandler#handleSetValueCommand — never emits TRANSMISSION_PENDING: with zero tasks it answers RESPONSE_ACK, otherwise it queues the transaction (or, for a non-permanent listener, defers it into ShareableAccessPointDevicePendingCommands with no notification at all). I grepped every TRANSMISSION_PENDING producer in HMIPServer; they are handleExcludeCommand, handleSetConfigCommand, handleDoUpdateDeviceCommand, handleUpdateListenerModeDeviceCommand, LinkSubcommandHandler, the two RestoreConfiguration response handlers and DeviceBackgroundUpdateSubsystem — none on the value-write result path — and TransmissionPendingException is imported by NotificationUtil but never constructed anywhere, so it is a dead branch. Net: BOTH of our special delays are keyed to faults our value-write path cannot receive. -10 remains reachable on putParamset MASTER, deleteDevice, link operations, restoreConfig and firmware update — and on deleteDevice specifically it does cover genuinely transient AP_BUSY / STACK_BUSY, for which a short timed retry IS defensible, so "treat -10 as queued, stop retrying" is right for setConfig and wrong for deleteDevice. The two durations themselves stay NOT PERFORMABLE from any readable source: rfd carries no duty-cycle recovery model (it reads a percentage out of the HELLO frame and only re-notifies on band crossings), and the HmIP pending window is bounded by the device's own wake-up cycle, which no CCU source states. The 40 s is traceable to aiohomematic/const.py:166 — a Tier 3 witness, which is where the number came from, not evidence about the CCU.

all.title: The 90-second session freshness window has no source, and the documented failure of getting it wrong is CCU session-pool exhaustion
all.ourValue: jsonSessionAge = 90 s, described as "the freshness window for session renewal" and, in the reader's framing, as how long a CCU session stays valid without traffic.
all.firmwareValue: The CCU's session timeout is `SessionTimeout` in /etc/config/rega.conf: an integer, validated to 180 ≤ t ≤ 600 seconds, default 300 s, effective only after the next CCU restart. It is not 90, and it is operator-configurable rather than fixed.
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/cp_security.cgi:899-911 (`proc action_set_session_timeout`, `set REGA_CONF_FILE "/etc/config/rega.conf"`, and at :906 verbatim `if { $timeout != [expr int($timeout)] || 180 > $timeout || 600 < $timeout } then { error "invalid timeout" }`, then `append rega_conf "SessionTimeout=$timeout\n"` at :910). ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.js:529 verbatim "The time out value can be set between 180 and 600 seconds. The default value is 300 seconds." (German twin at www/webui/js/lang/de/translate.lang.js:530). Sliding, not absolute: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/session/renew.tcl fetches `127.0.0.1/pages/index.htm?sid=@$sid@` and answers `true` — it touches the session and mints no new id, which is what our Renew decoder assumes. Pool pressure is real: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/session/login.tcl raises `jsonrpc_error 501 "invalid credentials or too many sessions"` when login.htm returns no sid. Ordinary calls also touch the session: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/homematic.cgi `checkPrivilegeLevel` runs `eq3/getupl.hms` with `_session_id_` for every method whose LEVEL is not NONE, and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/eq3/getupl.hms calls `system.GetSessionVarStr(id)`.
all.finding: As a safety property our rule holds: 90 s sits below the firmware's configurable floor of 180 s, so no operator setting can open a gap in which a session dies inside our freshness window — the margin is 2× at the tightest setting and 3.3× at the default. What is false one step wider is the description: 90 s is not the CCU's inactivity timeout and does not correspond to any firmware value. The boundary runs at 180 s: raising jsonSessionAge to that value or beyond re-creates exactly the failure the surrounding comments fear (calls into the gap fail, the client re-logs in, the abandoned session lingers until it idles out, and login.tcl's "too many sessions" path is what an operator then meets in the WebUI too). Two limits on what I could settle. The session-pool size is not readable: the "too many sessions" text is only the WebUI's inference from a missing sid, and the actual limit lives in the closed ReGaHss binary — our 90 s does not depend on it. And whether an ordinary privileged JSON-RPC call refreshes the CCU-side session is only half-settleable: the call demonstrably reaches ReGa with the sid via getupl.hms, but whether `GetSessionVarStr` bumps the last-activity stamp is inside ReGaHss and is therefore unverified. That does not matter for us, because our own renewal cadence never exceeds 90 s regardless.
all.negativeControl: Had the CCU's inactivity timeout been shorter than our window, cp_security.cgi's validator would accept values below 90 s — it rejects anything under 180 and the operator-facing help text in both catalogues names the same floor. Had the session been absolute rather than sliding, Session.renew would have to mint a new id; renew.tcl issues one authenticated GET carrying the existing sid and returns a bare `true`.
all.challengeNote: Every firmware citation UPHELD verbatim, including the 180/600 bounds and the English help string. The safety claim itself is UPHELD but its stated MARGIN is wrong, and the bundle's closing sentence is refuted. Two corrections. (1) jsonSessionAge is not a renewal cadence, it is a skip threshold: loginOrRenew runs lazily before a Call (client.go:266) and there is no periodic session keepalive anywhere in internal/client — the only "keepalive" in the southbound stack is the XML-RPC PING (internal/central/jobs.go:522-531), which never touches the JSON-RPC session. The effective renewal interval is therefore jsonSessionAge PLUS the caller's inter-call gap. With the default hub refresh of 60 s (schedule_timer.go:53) a refresh at t=0 is skipped at t=60 and renews at t=120, so the real margin to the firmware's 180 s floor is about 1.5x, not the bundle's 2x, and about 2.5x at the 300 s default, not 3.3x. (2) The bundle's "our own renewal cadence never exceeds 90 s regardless" is false as written: if JSON-RPC traffic pauses for longer than the operator's SessionTimeout, no renewal happens at all, the CCU drops the session, and we take the recovery path at client.go:645-647 (logoutStale then Login) — the very leaked-slot failure the Renew doc comment at :528-535 is written to prevent, only recovered rather than avoided. So the honest statement of the rule is conditional: 90 s keeps a session alive under any operator setting ONLY while JSON-RPC calls keep arriving at least every (SessionTimeout - 90 s). The boundary the bundle named still stands — raising jsonSessionAge to 180 s or beyond re-creates the gap even under continuous traffic. I reproduce the bundle's two limits unchanged: the pool size is not readable (login.tcl's message is the WebUI's inference from a missing sid; the real limit is inside ReGaHss), and whether GetSessionVarStr bumps the last-activity stamp is inside ReGaHss and stays unverified.

all.title: Every XML-RPC fault -5 on a schedule putParamset is reported to the operator as a successful save
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/dispatch.tcl:144 `-5 { jsonrpc_error 505 "XML-RPC: unknown argument or value" }` | ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFManager.cpp:112 (in RFManager::PutParamsetValues, :89-121) `throw XmlRpcException("Value not supported at parameter 4. Supported values are WAKEUP and BURST", -5);` | ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:203,208 `throw XmlRpcException("Failure");` with ../OpenCCU-Base/src/libXmlRpc/src/XmlRpcException.h:29 `XmlRpcException(const std::string& message, int code=-1)` | HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException and #getRpcRemoteException, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues, HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#putParameterSet
all.ourValue: fault -5 on a schedule MASTER putParamset is always the documented CCU false positive; log a warning and return success
all.firmwareValue: -5 is the CCU's own "unknown argument or value" error (jsonrpc_error 505). On rfd it is thrown BEFORE the paramset is touched and is the only -5 that surface can produce; on the HmIP legacy surface one of its two producers is thrown before the write command reaches the event bus.
all.finding: Wrong surface first: HmIP-PSM SWITCH_WEEK_PROFILE — the device the read-back observation came from — is served by HMIPServer's legacy XML-RPC surface, not by rfd, yet the filter is applied to every backend. On rfd (the surface our bare-schema climate writes to HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU use) putParamset can emit exactly one -5: RFManager::PutParamsetValues rejects any rx_mode string other than WAKEUP/BURST at RFManager.cpp:112, before `inst->PutParamsetValues(key, set)` is ever reached. Every other rfd putParamset failure is XmlRpcException("Failure") whose default code is -1. So a -5 from a BidCos schedule write provably means nothing was written — and our code reports it as saved. On the HmIP side there are two -5 producers: NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException, thrown from DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues before `vertx.eventBus().send("backend.command.hmip", ...)` (nothing written at all), and NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException(JsonObject), which maps backend notification types UNKNOWN_PARAMETER and INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE to faultCode -5 / "Invalid parameter or value". LegacyServiceHandler#putParameterSet has no branch that returns success after either. Whether the second kind can leave the recognised subset applied on the device is access-point behaviour that HMIPServer does not model — that half is unverified — but it cannot rescue the blanket rule, because the first kind and the whole BidCos surface write nothing. The rule as written cancels exactly the protection that FilterRawScheduleByFields, filterClimateScheduleByDescKeys and the deactivateUpTo bound exist to provide. Side note on the same surface: internal/client/write_options.go:42 documents `LEVEL` as an rx-mode value; rfd accepts only WAKEUP and BURST and answers anything else with -5 before writing. The schedule path passes CommandRxModeUnset so no 4th argument is appended today, but any caller that sets RxMode to LEVEL or LAZY_CONFIG on a BidCos putParamset would produce a -5 that this filter then reports as success.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been right, the firmware's -5 producers would sit after the commit — in rfd after `inst->PutParamsetValues` returned, and in HMIPServer after the DEVICE_CONFIG_SET command was placed on the event bus. Both sit on the pre-dispatch side, and the CCU's own fault catalogue would not have classified -5 as an error at all. It classifies it as jsonrpc_error 505.
all.challengeNote: I re-ran the prior agent's attack and it holds only on a narrower base than claimed. Three corrections. (1) "the only -5 that surface can produce" is true of the putParamset path, not of rfd: a whole-tree grep finds seven -5 throws in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/, five of them on getValue/readValue/setValue/setValueAsUndefined/determineParameter. I traced the actual write path end to end and it is cleaner than the prior agent showed — RFManager::PutParamsetValues -> RFChannel/RFDevice::PutParamsetValues -> RFParamset::Put -> HSSParamset::Put, and HSSParamset::Put skips a key it does not know (`if(it2!=params.end())`, no else) and `continue`s past a non-writable one, then unconditionally returns true. So an undeclared schedule key on BidCos cannot fault at all; nothing below the rx_mode check can produce -5. (2) Reachability kills the operator-harm half of the contradiction. putParamsetViaCaller appends the 4th argument only `if appendRxMode && rxMode != hmenum.CommandRxModeUnset` (internal/client/backends/wire_shared.go:155-160), PutClimateSchedule passes CommandRxModeUnset, and no production caller anywhere in internal/, cmd/ or pkg/ sets a non-unset RxMode. Today's daemon therefore cannot elicit a -5 from rfd on any putParamset. The prior agent's side note named `LEVEL`; LEVEL is only a doc comment at internal/client/write_options.go:26,42 and is not an hmenum constant — the live hazard is hmenum.CommandRxModeLazyConfig = "LAZY_CONFIG" (pkg/hmenum/device.go:102), which rfd also answers with -5 before writing. (3) The HmIP pre-send leg does not cover our payload. DeviceUtil#convertParameterValue returns the value unchanged when the channel declares no such parameter (`if (parameter == null) return value;`), so an undeclared MASTER slot key is NOT rejected before the event-bus send; the only pre-send -5 on the MASTER branch is DeviceUtil#validateAndConvertValues throwing NotificationUtil#getUnknownParameterValueRpcRemoteException for a legacy-disabled parameter. Our schedule payload's characteristic failure (13x7 slot keys, some undeclared) therefore lands on the post-send backend notification, whose UNKNOWN_PARAMETER / INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE -> -5 mapping in NotificationUtil#getRpcRemoteException(JsonObject) says nothing about whether the access point applied the recognised subset. The empirically observed HmIP-PSM false positive sits on exactly that unmodelled branch and is not contradicted by Tier 1. Also: NotificationUtil has a third -5 producer the prior agent missed, #getDeviceExpectedException ("A device address was expected but a chanel address was given"), used by DeviceUtil — not on our channel-address MASTER path, but "two producers" was wrong. Finally, the dispatch.tcl citation is www/api's JSON-RPC error mapping (-5 -> jsonrpc_error 505), a gloss on what -5 means, not a statement about the XML-RPC surface our code calls. Net: the blanket rule is unsound in principle — a -5 from a BidCos putParamset provably means nothing was written — but the demonstrated harm is confined to two legs neither of which the schedule call site reaches today: a future caller that sets RxMode on a BidCos putParamset, and an HmIP write that hits a legacy-disabled parameter.
