The only non-VCU device in the whole capture is BidCoS-RF (type HM-RCV-50), and all 51 of its channels carry the `<device name>:<no>` shape, so there is no never-renamed BidCos channel anywhere in the evidence — the BidCos boundary the reader flagged is real and the capture cannot close it. TIER: the substrate is a recorded, address-shuffled JSON-RPC session living in a Tier-3 tree. It is an observation of a CCU rather than a witness's conclusion, so it is stronger than Tier 3 — but it is not "what a device declares at runtime", so calling it Tier 2 stretches the ladder. Read it as: Tier 1 is silent by construction, Tier 2 does not speak to channel names at all, and the support is a single recorded observation. I re-ran the Tier-1-silence control myself rather than taking it on trust, and it holds. What would settle it: `Device.listAllDetail` on a CCU carrying a freshly taught-in, never-renamed BidCos device, or the ReGaHss device-import path.

all.title: The channel-rename grammar is attributed to the CCU WebUI with no source
all.ourValue: `chName := name + ":" + strconv.Itoa(ch.Number)` for EVERY channel of the device, unconditionally, persisted through renameDeviceFn; documented as "the colon-separated channel-number suffix the CCU WebUI applies"
all.firmwareValue: the WebUI's rename-all-channels handler builds `$(NAME_ID).value + $(SEPARATOR_ID).value + chNumber` where SEPARATOR_ID is an operator-editable text input whose markup is `<input id="DeviceConfigDialog_DeviceChannelsRenameSeparator" size="2" type="text" value=":"/>`; and it SKIPS a channel unless the operator ticked "including own names": `var origChName = this.device.name+":"+chNumber; if (channel.name !== origChName && renameOwnChannelNames === false) return true;` — then calls `homematic("Channel.setName", {id: channel.id, name: chName})`
all.citation: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0099-WebUI-Add-DeviceRenameAllChannels.patch — the hunk against occu/WebUI/www/webui/webui.js adding DeviceConfigDialog.renameChannels, plus the SEPARATOR_ID/RENAME_OWN_ID members and the German/English strings "Die Kanalnamen lauten anschliessend: GeraetenameKanalnummer" / "The new channel names will afterwards look like: device_namechannel_number". Counter-check against the unpatched upstream: `grep -a 'renameChannels\|DeviceChannelsRenameSeparator' ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/webui.js` returns nothing, while `grep -a setName` on the same file returns 13 hits — the file is present and readable, the feature is not in it.
all.finding: Our code does what the reader described, and the pattern matches — but the attribution is wrong in three ways, one of which is a behavioural divergence. (1) It is not "the CCU WebUI": stock eQ-3/OCCU has no rename-all-channels action at all. The feature exists only because the OpenCCU distribution adds it in patch 0099, so the sentence is true for an OpenCCU box and false for a stock CCU. (2) The colon is a default, not a grammar: the separator is a two-character text input the operator can change before pressing the button, so a CCU can legitimately hold `Wohnzimmer-1` or `Wohnzimmer 1` channel names produced by its own UI. Our hard-coded ":" therefore matches the default and only the default. (3) The real divergence: the WebUI renames a channel only when the checkbox is ticked OR the channel's current name still equals `<old device name>:<channel number>` (colon hard-coded in that comparison, independent of the separator field) — i.e. by default it preserves every channel the operator ever named. RenameDeviceWithChannels has no such gate; central.go:1079-1087 rewrites every channel and persists each one, so an operator-chosen channel label is destroyed by a device rename and cannot be recovered daemon-side. If the intent is WebUI parity, the includeChannels flag needs a second dimension (rename own names yes/no) and the skip predicate above. Scope note on "reaches the device": this write lands in ReGa on the CCU, not in the device — it is persisted CCU state rather than device state, which is why I marked reachesDevice false, but it is not merely presentational and it is not undoable from here.
all.negativeControl: Had the WebUI used a different grammar, patch 0099's renameChannels would show a different concatenation than `deviceName + separator + chNumber` — it shows exactly that, and the two translation strings state the shape in words in both languages. Had this been stock behaviour rather than a distribution patch, the grep for `renameChannels` in the unpatched ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/webui.js would have hit; it returns nothing on a file where `setName` hits 13 times, so the grep is live and the absence is real.
all.challengeNote: UPHELD — every quote is verbatim in patch 0099 and the counter-check reproduces exactly. Two additions the reader missed, both Tier 1. (1) The skip predicate is STRICTER than described: it compares against `<OLD device name>:<chNumber>`, so with the checkbox unticked the WebUI skips not only operator-named channels but also NEVER-RENAMED ones, whose name is `<type> <channel address>` (see c014). The default WebUI behaviour therefore rewrites only channels already in the `devname:no` shape; our loop at central.go:1078-1086 rewrites all of them, so it destroys both the operator's labels and the CCU's auto-defaults. If parity is the intent, includeChannels needs the second dimension plus that predicate. (2) A second divergence, not previously named: Channel.setName is documented in the CCU's own API script as ADJUSTING a name that is not unique, and the script returns the name ReGa actually stored. central.go:1080 stamps our own string into the model BEFORE the call, and ccu_wiring.go:904 discards the returned name — so after a cascade our model can report names the CCU does not hold. A cascade mints n names that must be unique CCU-wide, which makes this the likely case rather than the rare one. Caveat stated honestly: the uniqueness enforcement itself lives inside ReGaHss (binary), so it is documented in Tier-1 source but not implementation-verified; the discarded return value is verified in our code. Scope on reach: this write lands in ReGa/CCU state, not in the device — reachesDevice false — but it is persisted and not undoable daemon-side. Callers affected: internal/central/adapter/device_admin.go:136 and :295.

all.title: Two CCU wire conventions about messages are asserted in comments and used to parse
all.site: internal/model/hub/messages.go:282-287 and :22-25; extraction at internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1577-1588 (serviceMessageParameter) and :1497; consumption at internal/model/hub/messages.go:571
all.ourValue: (A) Parameter = rawName[LastIndex(rawName,".")+1:], justified by "Device / channel addresses never contain a dot, so the split is unambiguous" (hub_wiring.go:1579-1580); example given is "LOWBAT"; "" when no dot. (B) "the CCU reports its trigger data point as the 65535 'unknown' sentinel" (messages.go:24-25).
all.firmwareValue: (A) ReGaHss composes the service-alarm object name as the literal "AL-" followed by one runtime string, the single-character literal ".", and a second runtime string — one dot after the address part, and the parameter part is what follows it. (B) 65535 is ID_ERROR, ReGa's invalid-object-reference constant (script-constant table entry: name "ID_ERROR", value 0x0000ffff = 65535), not an alarm-specific "unknown" sentinel.
all.citation: Tier 1 — ../OpenCCU-Base/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu/ReGaHss (the shipped ReGaHss binary, stripped, so cited by content not line): the ReGa script-constant table at load address 0x1f2360 holds {name -> "ID_ERROR", value 0x000000000000ffff}; the neighbouring entries are ID_PRESENT=950, ID_SERVER_DP=945, pppNone=0, pppServer=1, pppClient=2, which identifies the table. The same binary carries a NUL-terminated "AL-" literal at 0x19ab7c and a single-character "." literal at 0x18e5bc; both code sites that reference "AL-" (0x10272f and 0x114de3) do: assign(buf,"AL-"); append(buf, s1); append(buf, "."); append(buf, s2). At the second site the immediately preceding block builds the ReGa data-point name in the CCU's canonical <interface>.<address>.<param> shape from the same operands. || ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/interface/suppressservicemessages.tcl:3-4 ("Suppress service messages for given channel (service parameter). Provide empty parameter string to suppress all service parameters of given channel."), :9 ("parameterId: [string] Optional: Service parameter name / id. Use empty string to supress all service parameters."), :20 (proxies straight to the interface's XML-RPC suppressServiceMessages). || ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp:917-925 registers getServiceMessages; the file's 51 XmlRpcServerMethod("…") registrations contain no suppressServiceMessages and no getSuppressedServiceMessages, and neither does src/hs485d (26 registrations). || ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/statusviews/serviceMessages.htm:211-217 and :258-289 — the CCU's own service-message page never parses the alarm name: it takes LastTriggerID(), falls back to AlTriggerDP() when that == ID_ERROR, and derives the parameter from oLastTrigger.HSSID() (with oLastTriggerChannel.ChnLabel()#"|"#HSSID() as the long key). || ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/statusviews/alarmMessages.htm:162-166 — same LastTriggerID()/ID_ERROR/AlTriggerDP() sequence, guarded by `if(oLastTrigger)` on the resolved object, never by `> 0`. || ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:770-786 — the operator's alarm system variable is created as dom.CreateObject(OT_ALARMDP) + Name + AlSetBinaryCondition + Add to ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES; nothing anywhere in the WebUI/ReGa sources ever sets AlTriggerDP on it. :864 — `sv.Channel( ID_ERROR );` is how ReGa itself writes an unset object reference. || ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/repeater_ch_master.tcl:30 (`dev.Interface() != 65535`) against ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/admin/views/newdevicechannels.htm:35 and newdevicechannelsloader.htm:19 (`iface != ID_ERROR`) — the same accessor, the same "is this a real object" test, written once with the literal and once with the constant. || ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0044-WebUI-DisableDeviceServiceMsg.patch — the distribution's own "disable service messages" feature (Device.setEnabledServiceMsg) walks ID_SERVICES and resolves oAlarm.AlTriggerDP() -> Channel() -> Device(); it too never parses a name. || HmIP side: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.LegacyServiceHandler#suppressServiceMessages, de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.DeviceUtil#setSuppressedServiceParam, de.eq3.cbcs.legacy.bidcos.rpc.internal.ServiceMessage#isServiceMessageParameter / #isExtendedServiceParameterName (same symbols in HMServer). || Tier 2 — ../OpenCCU-Base/src/devicetypes/{rftypes,hs485types}/*.xml: of every distinct id="…" attribute value shipped, 0 contain a dot; ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json: of 2924 distinct "ADDRESS" values, 0 contain a dot. || Tier 3 witness (provenance only) — ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/rega_scripts/get_service_messages.fn:53: `!# Extract address from alarm name (format: "AL-ADDRESS:X.PARAM")`, which is verbatim where our comment and our own internal/client/rega/scripts/get_service_messages.fn came from.
all.finding:
Both claims survive, but each is true for a different reason than the comment gives, and one surface the comment implies does not exist.

(A) The last-dot split. The firmware does compose the name as "AL-" + X + "." + Y with exactly one literal dot, so "the segment after the last dot" recovers Y. But our justification — "device / channel addresses never contain a dot" (hub_wiring.go:1579-1580) — is the wrong invariant and is not asserted anywhere in the firmware. The split is safe iff the PARAMETER contains no dot (X may contain any number). That property is real and measurable: 0 of all id="…" values in the shipped device-type XMLs contain a dot, and the HmIP acceptance set (ServiceMessage#isServiceMessageParameter) is a closed list of [A-Z0-9_] names — LOW_BAT, UNREACH, SABOTAGE, CONFIG_PENDING, VALVE_STATE, plus extended forms built as "%s_%s" (e.g. VALVE_STATE_ERROR_POSITION). Note our comment's example "LOWBAT" is the BidCos spelling; the HmIP name is LOW_BAT, and only the HmIP spelling is in the accepted set.

Three consequences the comment does not carry:
1. Interface.suppressServiceMessages exists only on the HmIP side. rfd (BidCos-RF, BidCos-Wired via hs485d) registers getServiceMessages but no suppressServiceMessages and no getSuppressedServiceMessages; the CCU's tcl (suppressservicemessages.tcl:20) forwards blindly to $interface(URL), so a Disable() on a BidCos channel is an unknown-method XML-RPC fault, not a suppression. Our Disable() at messages.go:571 passes msg.InterfaceID through unconditionally.
2. A wrong non-empty parameter is a SILENT no-op: DeviceUtil#setSuppressedServiceParam only writes the channel's service-message-filter metadata when isServiceMessageParameter or isExtendedServiceParameterName matches; otherwise it falls off the end and returns normally. No fault reaches us, so our suppressed[] map records a suppression that never happened.
3. An empty parameter is not merely "all parameters" — with enable=true it replaces the channel's filter with the single entry "*"; with enable=false it removes the filter metadata entirely, i.e. our Unsuppress with an empty parameter clears every suppression on that channel, including ones we never set. serviceMessageParameter() returns "" for any name without a dot and Disable() does not check, so a name outside the "AL-…" shape silently escalates to channel-wide.

The firmware's own route to the parameter does not go through the name at all: serviceMessages.htm and the distribution's Device.setEnabledServiceMsg both resolve AlTriggerDP() -> the trigger DP object and read HSSID(). Our own get_service_messages.fn already resolves that exact object (for Operations() and Channel()); emitting oTrigger.HSSID() would replace the inherited string convention with the value the CCU itself uses, and would leave Parameter empty only when the trigger DP is genuinely absent.

(B) The 65535 sentinel. Confirmed as a value, narrowed as a name: 65535 is ID_ERROR, ReGaHss's script constant for "no such object", not an alarm-specific "unknown" marker — ReGa writes it itself to clear a reference (system.fn:864). What the firmware does show for our case is that the operator's alarm variable is created without ever setting a trigger DP, and that the CCU's own pages guard the trigger by resolving the object and comparing to ID_ERROR, never by `> 0` — which is exactly the failure our script comment records. What no readable source states is the AlarmDP field's default in so many words; that AlTriggerDP() specifically returns ID_ERROR rather than 0 for such a variable rests on ID_ERROR being ReGa's unset-reference value plus our own live observation, and stays unverified at that last step. Suggested wording: "…so the CCU leaves its trigger data point at ID_ERROR (65535), ReGa's invalid-object-reference constant" — and drop "unknown".
all.negativeControl: For (A): had the firmware composed the name with a different separator, with no separator, or with the parameter first, the two "AL-" code sites would have loaded a different literal than 0x18e5bc (".") between the two appends, or would have ordered the appends differently — the disassembly at 0x10272f-0x102798 and 0x114de3-0x114e3c would have read differently, and I would have reported the split contradicted. Had a parameter id contained a dot, the sweep of every id="…" in the shipped device-type XMLs would have returned a non-zero count instead of 0; had an address contained a dot, the sweep of the 2924 descriptor ADDRESS values would have. Had rfd implemented suppressServiceMessages, it would have appeared among the 51 XmlRpcServerMethod("…") registrations in src/rfd/XmlRpcMethods.cpp alongside getServiceMessages — it does not, while getServiceMessages does, which is the control that the grep was looking in the right file. For (B): had ID_ERROR been any other value, the 8 bytes following the name pointer at 0x1f2360 would not have read 0x000000000000ffff; the control that the table is the constant table (and not a coincidence) is that the adjacent entries decode to ID_PRESENT=950, ID_SERVER_DP=945, pppNone=0, pppServer=1, pppClient=2 — values that would be nonsense if the stride or field order were wrong. What this check cannot produce is a different answer about AlTriggerDP()'s default for an alarm system variable, because no readable source carries that field's initialiser; that sub-claim is therefore reported as unverified above rather than confirmed.
all.challengeNote:
I could not break the claim's citations. Every one of them — the binary offsets, the two constant values, the exact xref count, the tcl line numbers, the 51/26 registration counts, the 2924 ADDRESS values — reproduces exactly when executed independently. No invented source, no tier inflation, no simulator. I am upholding it on that basis, and narrowing it on three points the claim did not reach.

NARROWING 1 — the invariant is about the parameter, and the claim's restatement still smuggles the operand identity. The claim says the firmware composes "AL-" + address + "." + parameter, "one dot after the address part". What the binary actually carries is "AL-" + X + "." + Y with nothing appended after Y. ReGaHss is stripped: X and Y have no names. Calling X "the address" is inference. But Y is better grounded than the claim managed: the AL- name is built inside CreateDPs (../Platform/DOM/iseXmlRpc.cpp) in the loop over a getParamsetDescription response, and Y is assigned from the loop entry's own string field, sibling to the per-entry "FLAGS" and "TYPE" lookups. So Y is a paramset parameter name, read from the firmware rather than assumed. That is exactly and only what the last-dot split needs, and it makes the invariant measurable on the right corpus: 220 distinct <parameter id> values in the shipped device-type XMLs, 0 with a dot; and on the HmIP side a closed acceptance set of [A-Z0-9_] names with "%s_%s" extensions. Our comment's justification — "device / channel addresses never contain a dot" (hub_wiring.go:1579-1580) — is the wrong condition and is asserted by no firmware source; X may contain any number of dots without harming the split. The claim's 2924-ADDRESS measurement is real but measures the operand that does not matter.

NARROWING 2 — (B) splits into a confirmed half and a Tier-1-silent half, and the claim's suggested rewrite still asserts the silent one. Confirmed: 65535 IS ID_ERROR, ReGa's invalid-object-reference constant — I read it out of the .data table myself, and ReGa writes it to clear a reference (system.fn:864) and tests for it on the sibling accessor (Interface(), LastTriggerID()). Not confirmed, and not confirmable from any source I can reach: that AlTriggerDP() specifically returns 65535 rather than 0 for an operator-created alarm variable. I searched the whole www/ tree and the patch set. Nothing anywhere compares AlTriggerDP() to ID_ERROR or to 0 — every consumer resolves the object and guards on the object. The claim's proposed wording ("the CCU leaves its trigger data point at ID_ERROR (65535)") is a firmware-flavoured restatement of an unverified value; adopting it would convert an honest live observation into a false firmware citation, which is the exact failure this series exists to catch. The observation is real (get_alarm_messages.fn records the ScriptRuntimeError that an `if (trigger > 0)` guard let through) and should stay attributed to the live CCU. Note this half touches no live code path at all: get_alarm_messages.fn walks ID_SYSTEM_VARIABLES and never calls AlTriggerDP(); the comment is documentation of why it does not.

NARROWING 3 — one correction against the claim, and one piece of evidence it missed. The claim says our example "LOWBAT" is the wrong spelling and "only the HmIP spelling is in the accepted set". Half right, and the wrong half matters: LOWBAT is the correct BidCos spelling — 29 shipped rftypes XMLs declare id="LOWBAT", none declare id="LOW_BAT". The sharper statement is that a BidCos LOWBAT cannot be suppressed at all, because rfd and hs485d register no suppressServiceMessages. That reinforces the claim's consequence 1 rather than weakening it, and I found independent corroboration the claim did not: the firmware's ONE caller of Interface.suppressServiceMessages, at src/webui/www/config/easymodes/hmip/CLIMATECONTROL_FLOOR_TRANSCEIVER.tcl:40, hardcodes 'interface':'HmIP-RF' and 'parameterId':''. eQ-3 uses this method only on HmIP, and only channel-wide.

All three of the claim's consequences hold on our path. Disable() at messages.go:571 forwards msg.InterfaceID unconditionally into the JSON-RPC Interface.suppressServiceMessages (adapter/hub_wiring.go:2795 -> jsonrpc/methods.go:152), so a BidCos channel yields an unknown-method fault; a wrong non-empty parameter is a silent no-op that our suppressed[] map records as a success; and an empty parameter with enable=false removes the channel's filter metadata outright, clearing suppressions we never set. serviceMessageParameter() has no "AL-" prefix check — unlike our own ReGa script, which does guard with Find("AL-") == 0 — so any non-AL-shaped name silently escalates to channel-wide.

What our code should follow: Tier 1 for the mechanism (the CCU's own route to the parameter never touches the name — serviceMessages.htm and patch 0044 both resolve AlTriggerDP() -> HSSID()), Tier 2 for the dot-freeness of the parameter. Our get_service_messages.fn already resolves that exact trigger object for Operations() and Channel(); emitting oTrigger.HSSID() would replace an inherited string convention with the value the CCU itself uses. I endorse the claim's suggestion there — it is the one change that removes the guessed input rather than re-justifying it.

all.title: The jpages group contract's constants (errorCode 42, 60 s save window, form content-type) are live observations with no firmware citation
all.citation: errorCode 42: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/pages/GroupEditPage.ftl:191 `var sessionTimeoutErrorCode = "42";` (also GroupListPage.ftl:65), and HMServer de.eq3.ccu.http.service.JsonResponseFactory#getSessionInvalidResponse, which builds JsonResponse with errorCode "42"; it is returned for EVERY group command by HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.GroupRequestWorker#handle before dispatch. Other codes: HMServer de.eq3.ccu.groupadministration.http.service.GroupAdministrationController#addDevice / #checkGroupAssignment / #createGroupWithGroupMember return "43" (bad parameters) and #create / #createGroupWithGroupMember return "44" (errorNoGroupDefinitions). Content-Type: ../OpenCCU-Base/opt/HMServer/pages/GroupEditPage.ftl:614 `new Ajax.Request(url,opt)` with only `postBody` set, over the shipped ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/extern/prototype.js:1164-1168 defaults (`method: 'post'`, `contentType: 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'`, `encoding: 'iso-8859-1'`) composed at :1260-1261 as `headers['Content-type'] = this.options.contentType + '; charset=' + this.options.encoding`. Parse anchors: GroupEditPage.ftl:206 `self.groupId = ${object.id};`, :223 `createVirtualDeviceSerialNumber(${object.id})`, :237 `new GroupType("${deviceType.getId()}", translateKey('${deviceType.getLabel()}'))`.
all.firmwareValue: errorCode "42" = session invalid (confirmed, two independent Tier-1 sites). Content-Type the CCU's own WebUI sends: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=iso-8859-1`. Save timeout: none anywhere in the CCU sources.
all.ourValue: jpagesSessionExpiredCode = "42" (matches). Content-Type header `application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8` (charset token differs). jpagesSaveTimeout = 60 * time.Second (no firmware basis).
all.missingInput: The bound on the group-save round trip. HMServer's own path carries no timeout: de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.RouteHandler.RequestHandler#sendEventBusMessage issues the worker request with no DeliveryOptions, and Prototype's Ajax.Request sets no client timeout — the shipped WebUI simply spins on the `groupWillBeSaved` dialog until a reply arrives. Whatever bound exists lives in the Vert.x runtime, which is not part of the eQ-3 sources, so 60 s is not derivable from any source available here.
all.finding:
Three constants, three different outcomes.

(1) errorCode 42 — CONFIRMED at Tier 1, and our comment is exactly right, including its subtlety. HMServer de.eq3.ccu.server.internal.GroupRequestWorker#handle checks the sid BEFORE dispatching any of the eleven group commands and returns the JsonResponseFactory session-invalid response, so even the bare-payload data endpoints (suitableGroupMembers, assignedGroupMembers) fall back to the {isSuccessful,errorCode,content} wrapper on a bad session and only then — which is precisely what SuitableHeatingGroupMembers probes for at ccu_groups.go:262-272. The rest of the code table is 43 = bad/missing parameters and 44 = errorNoGroupDefinitions; neither #save nor #delete has any validation-failure branch at all, so a genuine save rejection carries no errorCode — it surfaces as an exception, not as isSuccessful:false. Mapping every non-42 code to ErrUnsupported is therefore safe.

(2) Content-Type — NARROWED. The value family is firmware-attested: the shipped GroupEditPage does use Prototype's Ajax.Request with a raw postBody and no contentType override, and the shipped prototype.js 1.6.0.2 default is application/x-www-form-urlencoded. But the shipped default charset is iso-8859-1, not UTF-8, so the exact header the CCU's own WebUI emits differs from ours in the charset token. It does not bite: RouteHandler hands the worker `buffer.toString()` off a raw bodyHandler and the controller Gson-parses that string as JSON — nothing on the group route reads the request Content-Type at all. Which is also why the comment's stated MECHANISM ("the save handler hangs on application/json") is not decided by the CCU sources: there is no Content-Type branch to hang on. Keep the header (it is what the WebUI sends), but the rationale is a live observation, not a firmware fact, and the comment should not assert a handler behaviour the firmware does not implement.

(3) The 60 s save window — TIER-1 SILENT, see missingInput. The firmware neither bounds nor documents the save duration on this path. Two corroborating details for the surrounding design: the sid must be in the query string (RouteHandler reads request.params().get("sid"), never a form field), which jpagesURL already does; and the route always answers HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/html, so our non-200 rejection is dead-but-harmless code.

One unasked constant that this pass did settle, because it sits three lines away: the `assignedDevicesIds` JSON-STRING requirement at ccu_groups.go:210-214 is Tier-1 confirmed — GroupAdministrationController#save does `parameter.get("assignedDevicesIds").toString()` and re-parses that with `gson.fromJson(..., List.class)`, i.e. it genuinely expects a stringified array, and the controller URL-decodes groupName/groupDeviceName with ISO-8859-1, which is what makes jsEscape correct.
all.negativeControl: Had 42 been something else, GroupEditPage.ftl:191 would carry a different literal and JsonResponseFactory#getSessionInvalidResponse a different string — the check reads two independent sites that could have disagreed. The check demonstrably discriminates rather than echoing our input: on the very same Content-Type line it returned a DIFFERENT answer from ours (charset=iso-8859-1, not UTF-8), and on the 60 s constant it returned no answer at all instead of the expected one.
all.challengeNote: The rule's three constants survive, with the same split the first pass reported, and I re-read every site rather than trusting the citation. (1) errorCode 42 — CONFIRMED at Tier 1 at three independent sites, including the subtlety our code depends on: GroupRequestWorker#handle rejects a bad sid before dispatch, so even the bare-payload data endpoints fall back to the {isSuccessful,errorCode,content} wrapper only on a bad session — exactly what ccu_groups.go:262-272 probes for. 43/44 exist but never on #save or #delete, so mapping every non-42 code to ErrUnsupported is safe. (2) Content-Type — NARROWED as reported, and I can now state the mechanism claim is refuted rather than merely unsourced: RouteHandler takes the sid from request.params() and the body from a raw `buffer.toString()`, and no class on the group route reads a request Content-Type, so there is nothing for `application/json` to hang on. Our charset token (UTF-8) differs from the shipped WebUI's (iso-8859-1) and is if anything the more honest label, because Vert.x's Buffer#toString decodes UTF-8 regardless. Also worth recording: the route always answers 200 with text/html, so our non-200 branch is dead-but-harmless code. (3) The 60 s save window — TIER-1 SILENT, confirmed by absence: no timeout constant on this path, no eventBus send-timeout override, and the only 60 in the surrounding config is lighttpd's `server.max-keep-alive-idle = 60`, which is not a response deadline. WHERE THE FIRST PASS BROKE: its unasked aside declared the assignedDevicesIds JSON-STRING requirement "Tier-1 confirmed" and repeated our code comment's claim that the WebUI sends it stringified. The shipped template does the opposite — it builds a native JS array and JSON.stringify()s the whole object, in both the OCCU original and the OpenCCU-patched copy. So the comment at ccu_groups.go:210-214 is refuted on its stated evidence. What the firmware does say is only that #save calls .toString() on whatever Gson parsed and re-parses that as a List; whether a native array survives that round trip depends on Gson's lenient unquoted-token handling, which is not readable in this tree — and since member ids are bare device addresses (no ':'), the plausible outcome is that a native array parses fine, i.e. our comment's asserted mechanism ("silently drops a native array, committing an EMPTY group") is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed. Sending the stringified form remains safe either way, because .toString() of a String is the JSON text; only the justification is wrong.

all.title: RGBW secondary-channel suppression is a hard-coded channel-number set (2,3,4 / 3,4)
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/hmip/UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER.tcl:23 `set devMode $dev_ps(DEVICE_OPERATION_MODE); # 0 = RGBW, 1 = RGB, 2 = Tuneable White, 3 = PWM`, then the switch at :33-57 — case 0 `if {$chn == 1}` (:36) else `[getNoParametersToSet]` (:39); case 1 `if {$chn == 1}` (:43) else getNoParametersToSet (:46); case 2 `if {($chn == 1) || ($chn == 2)}` (:50) else getNoParametersToSet (:53); case 3 (:56) unconditional. Device scoping: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/easymodes/linkHmIP_UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER.tcl:12 `if {$dev_descr_receiver(PARENT_TYPE) == "HmIP-RGBW"}` with :18 repeating the same ordinal comment, and separate elseif branches for HmIP-DRG-DALI (:36, keyed on UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_MAX_CAPABILITIES, not DEVICE_OPERATION_MODE) and HmIP-LSC (:61, unconditional). Also :28-30 in UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER.tcl forces devMode 5 for any HmIP-LSC. Tier 2 topology: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/HmIP-RGBW.json declares channels 1-4 UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER + 5 UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_WEEK_PROFILE; HmIP-LSC.json declares one (channel 1); HmIP-DRG-DALI.json declares 48 (channels 1-48). Tier 3 witness (where our rule came from): ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:616-627.
all.firmwareValue: DEVICE_OPERATION_MODE 0 (RGBW) and 1 (RGB): channel 1 only is a functional light receiver, every other channel renders "no parameters to set". Mode 2 (Tunable White): channels 1 AND 2. Mode 3 (PWM): every channel. Scoped by PARENT_TYPE == "HmIP-RGBW"; HmIP-LSC and HmIP-DRG-DALI take separate, ungated branches.
all.ourValue: RGB/RGBW: channels 2,3,4 secondary (⇒ only 1 primary). TunableWhite: channels 3,4 secondary (⇒ 1 and 2 primary). PWM and every other mode: all primary. Identical in all four modes.
all.finding:
Confirmed, and the surface matches. The CCU has no notion of an "entity", so the closest thing to our exposure question is the operator-facing channel-configuration dialog, and that is exactly what the easymode decides: in RGBW and RGB mode the CCU offers configuration for channel 1 alone and answers `getNoParametersToSet` for the rest; in Tunable-White mode it opens channels 1 and 2; in PWM mode it opens all four. Our set {2,3,4} / {3,4} is the exact complement, mode for mode, on a four-receiver device. The mode ordinals never enter our code (we match the wire LABELS "RGBW"/"RGB"/"2_TUNABLE_WHITE"/"4_PWM" in recordMode, rgbw.go:292-303), so the sparse-ordinal trap does not apply here; the Tcl's ordinal comment is corroboration only.

Two scope boundaries worth recording, neither of which currently bites:

(a) The firmware gates on PARENT_TYPE == "HmIP-RGBW" and takes an unconditional branch for HmIP-LSC (devMode forced to 5, UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER.tcl:28-30) and a different parameter entirely for HmIP-DRG-DALI (UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_MAX_CAPABILITIES). Our registry registers IPRGBW — hence this rule — for both hmip-rgbw and hmip-lsc (profiles.go:1110, :1220). For LSC it cannot misfire: the LSC declares a single UNIVERSAL_LIGHT_RECEIVER (channel 1), so the numbers 2/3/4 have nothing to hide, and effectiveMode()'s RGBW fallback for an LSC (which carries no DEVICE_OPERATION_MODE) lands on the branch that suppresses nothing real. DALI is safe by construction: DRGDaliLight composes ColorTempLight, not RGBWLight (dali.go:24-40), so it carries no Usage() at all — which is right, because on DALI the firmware never gates by channel number.

(b) The bundle's worry about HmIP-DRDI3 does not reach this code: our registry classifies hmip-drdi3 as IPDimmer on channels 5/9/13 (profiles.go:949-958), not IPRGBW. The file-header comment at light/init.go:19 and the constructor doc at :271-272, which both name DRDI3 as an IPRGBW device, are refuted by our own registry and should be corrected — a stale comment, not a live defect.

What the rule still is NOT: derived. The literals {2,3,4}/{3,4} happen to equal base channel 1 plus the profile's own SecondaryChannels [1,2,3] (profile_configs.go:260), so the same numbers exist twice, unlinked, and a device with a different base would desynchronise them silently. That is a robustness point, not a correctness finding — for the two models that reach this constructor the firmware says our numbers are right.
all.negativeControl: Had our mapping been wrong, the Tcl switch would gate a different `$chn` set per case — and it demonstrably produces different answers across cases rather than one constant (case 2 admits chn 2, cases 0 and 1 do not, case 3 admits everything), so the check discriminates. Concretely: had we mixed up TW and RGB, mode 2 would have shown `$chn == 1` only and modes 0/1 would have shown `($chn == 1) || ($chn == 2)`.
all.challengeNote: Upheld, and on a stronger surface than the first pass had. Its own framing conceded a gap ("the CCU has no notion of an entity, so the closest thing is the config dialog") — there IS a closer thing, and it agrees exactly: webui.js gates the HmIP-RGBW's channels by mode at three list-filter sites and one control site, keyed on `channel.index` and `typeName == "hmip-rgbw"`, admitting {1} in modes 0/1, {1,2} in mode 2 and everything otherwise. Our {2,3,4} / {3,4} is the exact complement of that on a four-receiver device, mode for mode. The sparse-ordinal trap does not apply — we match wire labels, never positions — and the label↔ordinal correspondence the WebUI relies on is itself readable in the descriptor's VALUE_LIST rather than assumed. The first pass's registry and composition claims all check out as stated: hmip-lsc really is registered as IPRGBW (harmless: it declares one receiver, so 2/3/4 name nothing), hmip-drdi3 really is IPDimmer on 5/9/13 (so the file-header comment at light/init.go:19 and the constructor doc at :271-272 naming DRDI3 as an IPRGBW device are stale prose, refuted by our own registry), and DRGDaliLight really composes ColorTempLight (dali.go:24-40), so it carries no Usage() — right, because on DALI the CCU filters by DALI_ADDRESS, not by channel number. ONE BOUNDARY THE FIRST PASS DID NOT NAME, and it is the only place we diverge from the CCU: webui.js reads the mode from operator-written METADATA, not from the live DEVICE_OPERATION_MODE, so `parseInt(undefined)` is NaN on a device whose mode was never saved through the WebUI and the switch falls to `default:` — the CCU shows ALL channels when the mode is unknown. Our effectiveMode() falls the other way (unknown → RGBW → hide 2,3,4). We read the real MASTER parameter, so we are more accurate rather than wrong, but the two defaults are opposites and that is worth a sentence in the comment. Also a nit on the first pass's numbers: its Tier-2 corpus tally said 102 HmIP-* models; I count 106 of 399.

all.title: Product group is derived from four model-name prefixes, and that derivation decides whether MASTER writes are polled
all.citation: Model name is the CCU's own HmIP-Wired discriminator: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi:155 `if {[string first HmIPW- $devType] != -1}` (over `$dev_descr(TYPE)`), and ../OpenCCU-Base/www/config/ic_ifacecmd.cgi:359 `if { [string first "HmIPW-DRAP" $devDescr(TYPE)] != -1 }`. No separate wired interface is shipped: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/config_templates/InterfacesList.xml declares exactly BidCos-RF (xmlrpc_bin://127.0.0.1:32001), VirtualDevices (:39292/groups) and HmIP-RF (:32010) — there is no HmIP-Wired ipc entry. CONFIG_PENDING on BidCos-RF MASTER writes: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFChannel.cpp:73-89, in particular :81-84 `if(!cd.CommitToDevice(this)){ config_data_dirty=true; GetDevice()->CheckConfigPendingEvent(); }` — and the identical shape in ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:171-187 (:179-182). Edge-triggering: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/rfd/RFDevice.cpp:1036-1040 `if((config_pending == last_config_pending) && !force)return; last_config_pending=config_pending; ... SendInternalValueEvent("CONFIG_PENDING", val);`. BidCos-Wired: ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Device.cpp:57-66 defines `HS485Device::CheckConfigPendingEvent()`, and `grep -rn CheckConfigPendingEvent src/hs485d/` returns that definition and nothing else — no caller in the whole wired daemon; the value is only readable, at ../OpenCCU-Base/src/hs485d/HS485Device.cpp:651 `(int&)(*val)=IsConfigPending();`. Tier 2 corpus for the prefix survey: ../pydevccu/pydevccu/device_descriptions/*.json (197 HM-*, 102 HmIP-*, 15 HmIPW-*, 12 HMW-*, plus ~60 models matching no prefix).
all.firmwareValue: BidCos-RF: CONFIG_PENDING is raised ONLY when the commit to the device fails, and the event fires only on a transition of the flag — a MASTER write that reaches the device emits no CONFIG_PENDING event at all. BidCos-Wired: CONFIG_PENDING is never pushed; the event emitter exists but is dead code, the value is poll-only. HmIP-Wired vs HmIP-RF: the CCU distinguishes them by the device TYPE string containing "HmIPW-", because the shipped interface list has no wired HmIP interface to distinguish them by.
all.ourValue: PushesConfigPendingFor: ProductGroupHM → false, ProductGroupHmW → false, ProductGroupHmIP/HmIPW → true, else the interface fallback. ProductGroupForModel: hmipw- / hmip- / hmw- / hm- prefixes, else the interface.
all.finding:
Both halves confirmed, and the CONFIG_PENDING half comes back stronger than our comment claims.

CONFIG_PENDING. `RFChannel::PutParamsetValues` and `RFDevice::PutParamsetValues` are identical in shape: they call `ps->Put(...)`, then raise CONFIG_PENDING only inside `if(!cd.CommitToDevice(this))`. A MASTER write that actually lands therefore produces NO event — not an unreliable one, none. `CheckConfigPendingEvent` is additionally edge-triggered (RFDevice.cpp:1036), so even a device that was already pending emits nothing on a second failed write. A subscriber waiting for CONFIG_PENDING to confirm a BidCos-RF MASTER write waits forever; polling MASTER, which is what our false verdict selects, is the only sound path. For BidCos-Wired the answer is absolute: hs485d defines the emitter and never calls it, anywhere. Our comment's word "unreliable" understates both cases and could be sharpened to "not emitted on a successful write (BidCos-RF) / never emitted (BidCos-Wired)".

Product group. The CCU carries no product-group field at all — there is nothing better to read, and the CCU's own code solves the same problem the same way: it tests the device TYPE string for "HmIPW-". The premise our comment rests on is confirmed at the distribution level: the shipped InterfacesList.xml has three ipc entries and no HmIP-Wired one, so wired HmIP devices necessarily arrive over HmIP-RF and the model name is the only discriminator available. (The WebUI does carry an `HmIP-Wired` interface identifier — ic_ifacecmd.cgi:26, :110, :343, :649 — but the shipped configuration never instantiates it; it is legacy/defensive, and worth knowing before someone reads that string as evidence of a second interface.)

On the fallback's exposure, which is what the damage note is really about: I surveyed every model in the descriptor corpus that matches none of the four prefixes (~60: HB-*, HBW-*, ELV-SH-*, ALPHA-IP-RBG, ZEL_STG_RM_*, 263_*, WS550*, KS550*, ASH550, atent, RPI-RF-MOD, HSS-DX, OLIGO.smart.iq.HM, …) and none of them is misclassified by the interface fallback. ELV-SH-* and ALPHA-IP-RBG declare HmIP channel types (CLIMATE_TRANSCEIVER, HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_*) and sit on HmIP-RF → HmIP → true, which is correct. HB-*/ZEL_*/263_*/WS*/ASH550 are BidCos-RF → HM → false, correct. HBW-* are homebrew BidCos-WIRED and do NOT match "hmw-", so they fall through to InterfaceBidCosWired → HmW → false — also correct, and worth noting because it is the one case where the prefix list misses and the fallback saves it. Critically, the dangerous direction (a false `true`, skipping the poll) needs a BidCos device whose model name begins "hmip-", or a BidCos device on the HmIP-RF interface; neither exists in the corpus, and the two HmIP flavours both return true, so an HmIPW model spelled without the W is harmless by construction.
all.negativeControl: Had our verdict been wrong for BidCos, `CheckConfigPendingEvent()` would sit unconditionally after `ps->Put(...)` in RFChannel.cpp:79-85 rather than inside the `if(!cd.CommitToDevice(...))` failure branch, and `grep -rn CheckConfigPendingEvent src/hs485d/` would have returned at least one caller alongside the definition — it returns the definition alone. The check discriminates rather than echoing us: it returns a different answer on the same question for the HmIP side (where our verdict is true) and a different answer from our own comment's wording on the wired side (never emitted, not merely unreliable). Had the prefix premise been wrong, InterfacesList.xml would carry a fourth ipc entry named HmIP-Wired and ic_deviceFirmwareOverview.cgi would branch on an interface name rather than on `string first HmIPW- $devType`.
all.challengeNote: Both halves upheld, and I closed the gap the first pass left open. Its negative half is exact and I re-read every line: on BidCos-RF the flag is raised only when CommitToDevice fails, and CheckConfigPendingEvent returns early unless the flag actually transitioned, so a successful MASTER write produces no event at all — not an unreliable one, none; I additionally enumerated all seventeen other call sites to make sure none of them fires on a success path, and none does. On BidCos-Wired the emitter has no caller anywhere in hs485d. Our `false` verdict is therefore the only sound one for both, and "unreliable" in the comment understates it. WHAT THE FIRST PASS DID NOT GROUND, and what a rule of the form "HmIP → true, HM → false" needs, is the TRUE branch: it verified only that HM/HmW must be false. I grounded it on the HmIP side — a config write goes through AbstractPersistency, which flips the device pending flag and calls createAndSendConfigPending on the transition, and SendPendingConfigurationResponseHandler calls it again when the pending configuration has actually been transmitted, so the legacy XML-RPC surface sees CONFIG_PENDING true then false around a successful write. That is the exact inverse of the BidCos-RF path and is what makes the event usable as a settle signal for HmIP and not for HM. Note the symmetric caveat: the HmIP side is transition-guarded too (`oldConfigPending != configPending`), so a config write that changes nothing emits nothing there either; our handler only ever misses a no-op. The classification half stands as reported: the CCU carries no product-group field and solves the same problem the same way (string-match "HmIPW-" on the device TYPE), and the shipped InterfacesList.xml has no wired HmIP ipc entry, so wired HmIP devices necessarily arrive over HmIP-RF. My own re-survey of the 69 prefix-less models finds none misclassified — ELV-SH-* and ALPHA-IP-RBG are HmIP and reach `true` through the HmIP-RF fallback; HB-*/ZEL_*/263_*/WS*/KS*/ASH550 are BidCos-RF and reach `false`; HBW-* do NOT match "hmw-" and are saved by the BidCos-Wired fallback, which is the one case where the prefix list misses. The dangerous direction (a false `true` skipping the poll) needs a BidCos device whose name begins "hmip-", and none exists. Two leftovers: the first pass's HmIP corpus count is 106, not 102; and the VirtualDevices sentence in interface.go:120-124 ("HmIP-flavored virtual devices where CONFIG_PENDING does work") is a separate claim I did NOT ground — I found the CONFIG_PENDING constant in HMIPServer de.eq3.ccu.virtualdevice.ip.IpVirtualDevice but nothing that ties it to an HmIP-HEATING group's MASTER write, so treat that sentence as unverified.

all.title: The CCU readiness marker (path and body) rests on a comment, not on a firmware source
all.ourValue: GET /ise/checkrega.cgi; ready iff HTTP 200 AND strings.TrimSpace(body) == "OK"; asserted to mean "system fully started" uniformly across CCU2/CCU3/OpenCCU
all.firmwareValue: GET /ise/checkrega.cgi; body is exactly "OK" (no trailing newline) iff ReGaHss's script port executed the script; otherwise the Tcl catch's error message, also served as 200/text-plain. What it proves is "ReGaHss serves scripts", not "system fully started"
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/ise/checkrega.cgi:6 `array set result [rega_script {Write("OK");}]`, :10 `puts -nonewline $result(STDOUT)`, :13-15 (catch branch writes $errorMessage as the body, with the same `Content-Type: text/plain` and no status line) | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/error/error-503.html:64 `request.open("GET", "/ise/checkrega.cgi", false);` and :67 `if ("OK" == request.responseText)` (identical at error-500.html:63,66; duplicated at src/webui/www/error/) | ../OpenCCU-Base/src/tclrega/tclrega.cpp:67 `static std::string portRega("8183");`, :225 `Tcl_AppendResult(interp, "Error connecting to peer", NULL);`, :335 Tclrega_Script | ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/base/etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf:399 `server.errorfile-prefix = "/www/error/error-"` | ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/patches/occu/0149-WebUI-ImprovedErrorPages.patch (touches only markup/CSS; the check() body with the CGI path and the "OK" comparison survives verbatim in the patched result) | init order: ../OpenCCU/buildroot-external/overlay/RFD/etc/init.d/S61rfd, base/etc/init.d/S62HMServer, WebUI/etc/init.d/S70ReGaHss
all.finding:
Path and body are exactly right, and they are firmware-grounded rather than folklore. The CGI runs `rega_script {Write("OK");}` through tclrega.so, which POSTs the script to ReGaHss on 127.0.0.1:8183 (/tclrega.exe). Connection refused, a malformed reply, or a missing `<xml><exec>` tag all raise TCL_ERROR, the CGI's `catch` fires, and the error text is written as the body — still with a 200, since the CGI emits no status line. Our probe requires 200 AND the body, so an errored CGI is correctly read as "still booting". Our TrimSpace is one notch more permissive than the firmware's strict `"OK" == responseText`; since the CGI uses `puts -nonewline` there is no whitespace to trim, so the two agree on every body the firmware can produce.

Where the claim narrows: the comment says "system fully started". The CGI tests exactly one thing — that ReGaHss's script engine accepts and executes a script. That is materially stronger than a `pidof` check (the distribution's own S70ReGaHss `waitStartupComplete` only does `pidof`), and it is precisely the right gate for the half of our bring-up that reads names through ReGa. It is silent about rfd / HMIPServer: the CGI never touches them. The distribution's boot order (S61rfd → S62HMServer → S70ReGaHss) means those processes were *started* before ReGa, which is not the same as *serving listDevices*. So the rule is true in our scope for the names half and rests on process ordering, not on the marker, for the listDevices half.

The "uniformly across CCU2/CCU3/OpenCCU" half: measured for OCCU (the shared eQ-3 firmware source both CCU2/CCU3 images are built from) and for the OpenCCU patch stack, which leaves the CGI and the comparison untouched. I did not have a CCU2/CCU3 image to measure directly; that step is inference from the shared source, and I flag it as such rather than asserting it.

One correction to the comment independent of the verdict: the poller is not the "boot page" but lighttpd's 503/500 error-handler page (`server.errorfile-prefix`). `grep -arl checkrega` over the whole of ../OpenCCU-Base finds no other consumer.
all.negativeControl: Had our rule been wrong I would have found a different literal inside the CGI's `rega_script {...}` (it is a one-line Write, so the body is whatever that Write emits — e.g. "READY", or an "OK\n" with a trailing newline had it used plain `puts`), or a different comparison in the error page's check(). The check does discriminate: sibling CGIs under www/ emit entirely different bodies, and `puts -nonewline` vs `puts` is a visible one-character difference in the source that would have changed our TrimSpace verdict. For the narrowing: had the CGI actually tested full-system readiness, its script would have had to touch a device or interface object (e.g. dom.GetObject(ID_DEVICES)) rather than being a bare Write, and the pidof-only waitStartupComplete in S70ReGaHss would not have been the distribution's own idea of "ReGa is up".
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD as narrowed, and I extend the narrowing on two further points.

What I re-checked independently: the CGI is 16 lines and contains exactly one outbound call, `rega_script {Write("OK");}`; it names no other daemon. It is routed as CGI (`cgi.assign ".cgi" => "/bin/tclsh"`), so the path resolves, and it emits no Status line, so lighttpd answers 200 for both the success and the catch branch — meaning the `200 &&` half of our probe does no work and only the body comparison is load-bearing. I traced tclrega's SendRequest end to end: it strips the HTTP head at the first CRLFCRLF and returns only the body, so `$result(STDOUT)` is `OK` with no headers and no newline; both `connect()` failure and a reply without `<xml><exec>` return TCL_ERROR, the catch fires, and the body becomes the error text. So path and body are exactly right and are firmware-grounded, and our TrimSpace is one notch more permissive than the firmware's own strict `"OK" == responseText` with nothing in between (the CGI cannot emit surrounding whitespace).

Where I harden the narrowing beyond the prior report:

1. The comment's "system fully started" is not merely unproven — it is contradicted by Tier-1 text. The firmware's own comment directly above the poller reads "Prüft zyklsich, ob der ReGa Webserver verfügbar ist" (error-503.html:56). eQ-3's own description of this exact check is "is the ReGa webserver available".

2. The comment's "WebUI boot page (the 'CCU is not yet ready' splash)" is wrong on the file's identity: the two consumers are lighttpd's 500 and 503 error-handler pages, reached via `server.errorfile-prefix`. `grep -arli checkrega` over all of ../OpenCCU-Base returns exactly four files — www/error/error-{500,503}.html and their byte-identical copies under src/webui/www/error/ — and nothing else.

3. NEW demotion the prior report did not make: the comment's superlative, "the only manufacturer-sanctioned, SSH-free, cross-variant" signal, is an absence claim. No source can settle it and I did not try to; it is unverified, in those words, and should not be carried in a comment as fact.

4. The CCU2/CCU3 half stays inference. I confirmed no CCU2/CCU3 image exists in any reference tree here — the measurement is over the shared OCCU source plus the OpenCCU patch stack, and I verified the 0149 error-page patch leaves the CGI path and the "OK" comparison verbatim, and that no patch under buildroot-external touches www/ise/checkrega.cgi at all.

5. The listDevices half is tier1-silent, not inferred-from-ordering-and-fine. ReGaHss ships as a binary (../OpenCCU-Base/src has tclrega and webui but no ReGaHss source), so whether ReGaHss serving scripts implies rfd or HMIPServer answering `listDevices` cannot be read anywhere. S70ReGaHss's own readiness wait is `pidof` and nothing more. Our gate therefore covers the names half soundly and rests on nothing measurable for the HmIP listDevices half — a co-booting HmIP CCU can pass this gate with HMIPServer still warming up.

Recommendation: keep the constants; rewrite the comment to say what the CGI proves (ReGaHss's script engine accepts and executes a script), name the consumer as the lighttpd 500/503 error pages, drop the superlative, and note the HmIP gap explicitly.

all.title: The arm/disarm squawk convention (1x vs 2x) is a bare comment claim on a device-facing feedback tone
all.ourValue: ChirpArmSquawk documented as "1x squawk", ChirpDisarmSquawk as "2x squawk convention"
all.firmwareValue: No repetition count exists anywhere on the CCU. The arm/disarm distinction is carried by tone identity: ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION accepts 18 named values including DISARMED, INTERNALLY_ARMED, EXTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_INTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_EXTERNALLY_ARMED
all.citation: HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.SignalAcoustic — 18 constants in declared order: DISABLE_ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL, FREQUENCY_RISING, FREQUENCY_FALLING, FREQUENCY_RISING_AND_FALLING, FREQUENCY_ALTERNATING_LOW_HIGH, FREQUENCY_ALTERNATING_LOW_MID_HIGH, FREQUENCY_HIGHON_OFF, FREQUENCY_HIGHON_LONGOFF, FREQUENCY_LOWON_OFF_HIGHON_OFF, FREQUENCY_LOWON_LONGOFF_HIGHON_LONGOFF, LOW_BATTERY, DISARMED, INTERNALLY_ARMED, EXTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_INTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_EXTERNALLY_ARMED, EVENT, ERROR | HMIPServer de.eq3.cbcs.devicedescription.channelspecification.stateparameter.GeneralStateParameterFactory#createAcousticAlarmSelectionParameter — builds ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION from SignalAcoustic.getNames() (all 18), LogicalType.ENUM over PhysicalType.INTEGER via StringEnumToInteger, IOOperations.WRITE only | HMIPServer …GeneralStateParameterFactory#createAcousticNotificationSelectionParameter — the sibling ACOUSTIC_NOTIFICATION_SELECTION takes only SignalAcoustic.getNotificationNames(), the last 8 | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/webui.js:5028-5045 (the operator label table, same 18 keys) | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/webui/js/lang/en/translate.lang.stringtable.js:35 "Protection deactivated" (DISARMED), :40 "Absence mode" (EXTERNALLY_ARMED), :51 "Presence mode" (INTERNALLY_ARMED)
all.finding:
Tier 1 does not decide this and cannot: no repetition-count concept exists in the CCU at all. `grep -arin 'squawk|quittungston|chirp'` over ../OpenCCU-Base www/ src/ opt/ returns only three hits, all in rf_keymatic.xml's docu for the Keymatic's own Bestaetigungston (a pitch parameter, SIGNAL_TONE — unrelated). The HmIP server carries no arm/disarm confirmation emitter either; arming a zone writes state parameters, it does not schedule chirps. So "1x on arm, 2x on disarm" is an external security-industry convention (car alarms, panel keypads), not a CCU rule, and our comment should say so rather than read as a device property.

What the firmware does decide, and what makes the underlying worry unfounded: the device offers a *named* arm/disarm distinction. ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION is a write-only ENUM over the full 18-value SignalAcoustic set, and three of those values are semantically exactly "armed away", "armed home" and "disarmed" — eQ-3's own English labels are "Absence mode", "Presence mode", "Protection deactivated". A disarm confirmation is therefore not indistinguishable from an arm confirmation; it is a different selection value on the wire.

And our code already works that way. internal/alarm/outputs/chirp.go:95-106 resolves ChirpArmSquawk to inst.cfg.ChirpArmTone and ChirpDisarmSquawk to inst.cfg.ChirpDisarmTone — two independently configured labels — and emitChirp (:79-91) issues exactly ONE TurnOn per chirp with `AcousticSelection: &tone`. There is no loop, no repeat count, nothing that could emit a second squawk. The "1x"/"2x" in the comment is not implemented and is not implementable through this driver; the counts never reach a device. What reaches the device is the operator-configured label, and both labels used in the repo's own fixture (harness_test.go:176: EXTERNALLY_ARMED, EVENT) are members of the firmware's 18-value acceptance set. Scope note: this is the HmIP ALARM_SWITCH_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER surface; BidCos sirens carry a different parameter set that I did not examine.
all.negativeControl: Had a repetition count been a CCU concept, I would have found either a numeric REPEAT/COUNT parameter alongside ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION in GeneralStateParameterFactory's state-parameter table (it registers DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE and the ZONE_n_* family there, so a count parameter would sit in the same map), or a repeat argument in the SignalAcoustic enum, or a squawk/Quittungston string in the WebUI alarm easymodes. All three greps come back empty while the same greps find the duration and zone parameters — so the check discriminates rather than returning silence for want of looking. Had our arm/disarm split been unrepresentable, SignalAcoustic would have carried only the ten FREQUENCY_*/DISABLE values (which is exactly what getAlarmNames() returns, and is NOT what ACOUSTIC_ALARM_SELECTION is built from — I checked which getter the factory calls rather than assuming).

all.title: The com-test completion timestamp is parsed in the daemon's local zone although the CCU's zone is known
all.ourValue: time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02 15:04:05", poll.Completed, time.Local) — the string is interpreted in the DAEMON's zone; the constant's comment attributes the layout to system.Date
all.firmwareValue: The string is the CCU's local wall clock in the CCU's configured zone, carrying no offset; and it comes from LastTestCompletedTime(), not from system.Date. A zone-free Unix-seconds accessor for exactly this value exists: LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds()
all.citation: ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/pages/tabs/startpage.htm:179 `<% Write(system.Date("%H:%M")); %>` and :184 `Write(system.Date("%d.%m.%Y"))` — system.Date IS the operator-facing wall clock, so it renders CCU local time, not UTC | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/api/methods/device/startcomtest.tcl:17-18 `Write(system.Date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")); device.DevStartComTest();` and www/api/methods/device/pollcomtest.tcl:19-21 `if (device.LastTestCompletedTime() >= timestamp) { Write(device.LastTestCompletedTime()); }` — the CCU's own Device.startComTest/pollComTest, the exact pattern our scripts reproduce, and it compares the two as STRINGS and never parses them | ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/system.fn:492-494 (LastTestCompletedTime() → TimeStampToString3) with ../OpenCCU-Base/www/rega/esp/TimeStamp.fn:55-75, whose fixed offsets Substr(0,4)/(5,2)/(8,2)/(11,2)/(14,2)/(17,2) pin the layout to `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` and which renders it verbatim with no zone conversion | ../OpenCCU-Base/bin/{arm-linux-gnueabihf,aarch64-linux-gnu,x86_64-linux-gnu}/ReGaHss — the ReGa script method-name table lists `LastTestCompletedTime` immediately followed by `LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds`, and `DevStartComTest` on the next entry; siblings `LastDPActionTimeSeconds`, `LastTimestampSeconds`, `LastTriggerTimeSeconds`, `AlOccurrenceTimeSeconds`, `ProgramLastExecuteTimeSeconds` follow the same naming convention | our own get_alarm_messages.fn:62 already uses that convention (`oVar.LastTimestampSeconds()`)
all.finding:
Contradicted on two counts.

Zone. `system.Date` is what the CCU prints as its own clock on the WebUI start page (`maintime`, `maindate`), so it renders the CCU's configured local time; there is no UTC path and no format string anywhere in the tree carries %z or an offset. LastTestCompletedTime() is the same wall-clock shape — TimeStamp.fn slices it at fixed offsets and prints the result unchanged, so the operator sees CCU local time. Our code hands that offset-free string to time.ParseInLocation with `time.Local`, which is the *daemon's* zone. A UTC container against a Europe/Berlin CCU therefore reports CompletedAt one or two hours off, and the sign of the error is such that CompletedAt can land *before* StartedAt (StartedAt is a real time.Now()). The rega package already has the correct input: BackendInfo.Timezone carries the CCU's IANA zone (runner.go:368-370), and runner.go:303-306 states the very convention this path breaks.

Surface. The comment at :135-137 attributes the layout to `system.Date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")` "for the start / completed timestamps". Only `started` is system.Date (start_com_test.fn:41). `completed` is `oDev.LastTestCompletedTime()` (poll_com_test.fn:42) — and `completed` is the only one the constant is ever used on, at :194. The layout happens to match, but it is grounded on the wrong accessor; TimeStamp.fn is the source that actually settles the layout of the value we parse.

And the firmware offers the clean way out. `LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds()` exists in ReGaHss's script API, sitting directly beside `LastTestCompletedTime` and `DevStartComTest` in the method-name table, and the repo already uses that naming convention for alarm timestamps. Switching poll_com_test.fn to it removes the parse and the zone question entirely. Note also that the CCU's own pollComTest never converts these strings to a time at all — it only string-compares them, which is exactly what our poll script does at poll_com_test.fn:43; the zone bug is purely on the Go side, in turning the reported string into an absolute instant.
all.negativeControl: Had system.Date rendered UTC, the WebUI start page would be showing UTC as the CCU's clock to the operator, and TimeStamp.fn would have had to apply an offset before display — it applies none, and the check would have surfaced that as a conversion step in the Substr chain. Had no seconds accessor existed, the ReGaHss method-name table would list `LastTestCompletedTime` with no `…Seconds` sibling — which is exactly what the table shows for its neighbours `LastChangeValue`, `LastTriggerID` and `ValueMin`, so the extraction distinguishes presence from absence rather than matching every name. And had our code been right, :194 would have named a zone derived from BackendInfo.Timezone instead of time.Local; the literal `time.Local` is unambiguous in the source.
all.challengeNote:
UPHELD as contradicted on both counts, with one correction to the prior report's reasoning and one demotion of its proposed fix.

Surface, re-checked: the constant is referenced exactly once, at :194, and only on poll.Completed. poll_com_test.fn:42 reads `oDev.LastTestCompletedTime()`; system.Date appears only in start_com_test.fn:41, and `started` is never parsed. So the comment grounds the layout on an accessor that never produces the value the constant is used on. The layout is nevertheless correct, and the source that actually settles it is TimeStamp.fn:55-75: the WebUI slices LastTestCompletedTime() at fixed character offsets 0,4 / 5,2 / 8,2 / 11,2 / 14,2 / 17,2, which can only be `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. One correction to the prior report: TimeStampToString3 does NOT render the value verbatim — it emits only `HH:MM:SS`. What the source proves is the input layout and the absence of any zone conversion, which is what the claim needs; "verbatim" overstates it.

Zone, re-checked and strengthened: the ReGaHss binary carries the literal `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S` and, separately, a logging format `[%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z]`. eQ-3 attaches %Z where they want a zone and omit it here, and the binary links localtime/localtime_r rather than gmtime. Combined with system.Date being the operator clock on the start page and with the test date being rendered straight to the operator, the value is CCU-local wall clock with no offset. Note the contradiction does not even depend on "CCU-local": an offset-free string parsed in the daemon's zone is wrong for any CCU zone that is not the daemon's, and internal/client/rega/runner.go:303-306 already states that convention for the alarm path.

CORRECTION the prior report got wrong: it claims "a UTC container against a Europe/Berlin CCU therefore reports CompletedAt one or two hours off, and the sign of the error is such that CompletedAt can land before StartedAt". The sign is inverted for that example. CCU-local 14:30 CEST is the instant 12:30Z; parsed as UTC it becomes 14:30Z, i.e. roughly two hours in the FUTURE, so CompletedAt lands after StartedAt, not before. CompletedAt precedes StartedAt only in the opposite arrangement (daemon zone ahead of the CCU's — e.g. a Berlin daemon against a UTC CCU). The defect is real either way; the failure mode stated in the report is not the one the common deployment produces. DurationMs is computed from time.Since(startedAt) and is unaffected; the wrong instant is confined to CompletedAt, which is a public DTO field (`completed_at`, pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:781) and therefore reaches REST and WS clients as an RFC3339 stamp with the daemon's offset.

DEMOTION of the proposed fix: `LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds` is proven to EXIST as a symbol, adjacent to two methods that are proven callable (LastTestCompletedTime at system.fn:492, DevStartComTest at startcomtest.tcl:18), on all four shipped architectures; and the *Seconds convention is proven real by four siblings actually invoked in firmware ReGa (system.fn:1222,1227,1232; pda/eq3/program.tcl:8) plus a ReGaHss runtime error message that names LastTimestampSeconds() and LastDPActionTimeSeconds() with call parentheses. But no firmware call site for LastTestCompletedTimeSeconds exists anywhere in www/ or src/webui/. That it is callable and returns Unix seconds is inference from adjacency and naming, not read from a call site — exactly the shape of assumption this audit exists to catch. It is a well-supported hypothesis and the right thing to try, but it must be probed against a live CCU (a read; no write, no approval needed) before poll_com_test.fn is switched to it. The zone-independent fallback that needs no new accessor is to parse with the zone from BackendInfo.Timezone (runner.go:368-370) instead of time.Local.
